entries.zh: 寡人今改名晃，是以天意雅符於明德，日光顯契于瑞文，昭融萬邦，理斯在是。
entries.en: I now take the name Huang—Heaven's will aligns with Bright Virtue, sunlight with the omen in writing, that all under heaven may be illumined; this is the fitting course.
entries.literal: I now change my name to Huang—for thus Heaven's intent elegantly matches Bright Virtue, and sunlight clearly accords with auspicious script, illuminating ten thousand states; reason lies herein.

entries.zh: 庶順昊穹之意，永臻康濟之期。
entries.en: May it satisfy Heaven above and bring lasting peace and plenty.
entries.literal: May it accord with the Supreme Vault's intent and ever reach the season of peace and relief.

entries.zh: 宜令有司分告天地宗廟，其舊名，中外章疏不得更有回避。」
entries.en: Let the proper offices report to Heaven, Earth, and the temples. The old name need no longer be tabooed in memorials at court or abroad."
entries.literal: Let the relevant offices announce it in turn to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples; as for the old name, memorials within and without the court need no longer avoid it."

entries.zh: 時將受禪，下教以本名二字異帝王之稱，故改名。
entries.en: He was on the verge of receiving the mandate; this edict explained that his two-character birth name was unsuitable for an emperor—hence the change.
entries.literal: At the time he was about to receive the abdication; he issued this teaching because his original two-character name differed from an emperor's style—hence the change of name.

entries.zh: 己未，賜文武百官一百六十人本色衣一副。
entries.en: On jiwei he gave one set of plain court robes apiece to one hundred sixty officials, civil and military.
entries.literal: On jiwei he bestowed one set of plain-color robes each upon one hundred sixty civil and military officials.

entries.zh: 戊辰，即位。
entries.en: On wuchen he took the throne.
entries.literal: On wuchen he ascended the throne.

entries.zh: 制曰：
entries.en: His inaugural edict read:
entries.literal: An edict said:

entries.zh: 開平元年正月丁亥，帝回自長蘆，次於魏州。
entries.en: On dinghai in the first month of Kaiping year 1 the Emperor returned from Changlu and stopped at Weizhou.
entries.literal: On dinghai in the first month of Kaiping year 1, the Emperor returned from Changlu and halted at Weizhou.

entries.zh: 節度使羅紹威以帝回軍，慮有不測之患，由是供億甚至，因密以天人之望切陳之。
entries.en: Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei, fearing trouble when the Emperor marched home with his army, supplied provisions lavishly and privately urged that Heaven and men alike expected the transfer of the mandate.
entries.literal: Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei, because the Emperor was returning with his army, feared unforeseen trouble; he therefore supplied provisions on an extraordinary scale and privately urged him in the strongest terms that Heaven and men alike expected his next step.

entries.zh: 帝雖拒而不納，然心德之。
entries.en: The Emperor refused but was inwardly grateful.
entries.literal: The Emperor declined but was inwardly grateful.

entries.zh: 壬寅，帝至自長蘆。
entries.en: On renyin the Emperor arrived from Changlu.
entries.literal: On renyin the Emperor arrived from Changlu.

entries.zh: 是日，有慶雲覆於府署之上。
entries.en: That day auspicious clouds covered the prefectural compound.
entries.literal: That day auspicious clouds spread over the prefectural compound.

entries.zh: 甲辰，天子遣御史大夫薛貽矩來傳禪代之意。
entries.en: On jiachen the Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to convey the plan for abdication.
entries.literal: On jiachen the Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to convey the intention of transferring the mandate.

entries.zh: 貽矩謁帝，陳北面之禮，帝揖之升階。
entries.en: Yiju called on the Emperor, explained the ceremony of a northern vassal, and the Emperor bowed him up the steps.
entries.literal: Yiju called on the Emperor, set forth the rites due a northern vassal, and the Emperor bowed him up the steps.

entries.zh: 貽矩曰：「殿下功德及人，三靈所卜已定。
entries.en: Yiju said: "Your Highness's merit reaches all men; Heaven, Earth, and the spirits have already settled the matter.
entries.literal: Yiju said: "Your Highness's merit reaches all men; the three powers have already decreed the issue.

entries.zh: 皇帝方議裁詔，行舜、禹之事，臣安敢違。」
entries.en: The emperor is drafting the edict to follow Shun and Yu—I dare not refuse."
entries.literal: The emperor is now drafting the edict to do as Shun and Yu did—I dare not disobey."

entries.zh: 既而拜伏於砌下，帝側躬以避之。
entries.en: He then bowed prostrate on the steps, and the Emperor turned aside.
entries.literal: He then bowed prostrate on the steps; the Emperor turned aside to avoid it.

entries.zh: 二月戊申，帝之家廟棟間有五色芝生焉，狀若芙蓉，紫煙蒙護，數日不散。
entries.en: On wushen in the second month five-colored lingzhi sprouted between the rafters of the Emperor's ancestral shrine—lotus-shaped, veiled in purple mist that lingered for days.
entries.literal: On wushen in the second month, five-colored lingzhi grew between the rafters of the Emperor's ancestral temple, shaped like hibiscus, wreathed in purple mist, not dispersing for several days.

entries.zh: 又，是月，家廟第一室神主上，有五色衣自然而生，識者知梁運之興矣。
entries.en: That same month five-colored vestments appeared of themselves on the spirit tablet of the first ancestral chamber—those in the know took it as a sign that Liang's fortune was rising.
entries.literal: Also, in that month, on the spirit tablet of the first chamber of the ancestral temple, five-colored garments naturally formed; those who understood knew the rise of the Liang fortune had come.

entries.zh: 唐乾符中，木星入南斗，數夕不退，諸道都統晉國公王鐸觀之，問諸知星者吉凶安在，咸曰：「金火土犯斗即為災，唯木當為福耳！」
entries.en: In the Qianfu era Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper and held there night after night. Wang Duo, Prince of Jin and overall commander of the circuits, watched it and asked the astrologers what it portended. All agreed: "Metal, fire, or earth in the Dipper means disaster—only wood should mean good fortune!"
entries.literal: During Qianfu of Tang, Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper and for several nights did not withdraw. Wang Duo, Prince of Jin and commander-in-chief of all circuits, observed it and asked star-readers where fortune and misfortune lay. All said: "When metal, fire, and earth invade the Dipper it means calamity; only wood should mean blessing!"

entries.zh: 或亦然之。
entries.en: Others agreed.
entries.literal: Some agreed with this as well.

entries.zh: 時有術士邊岡者，洞曉天文，博通陰陽曆數之妙，窮天下之奇秘，有先見之明，雖京房、管輅不能過也。
entries.en: There was then a diviner named Bian Gang, master of the heavens and of yin-yang calendrics, who knew secrets none could match and saw what was coming—surpassing even Jing Fang and Guan Luo.
entries.literal: At the time there was a technician named Bian Gang who thoroughly understood astronomy, was broadly versed in the subtleties of yin-yang and calendrical reckoning, exhausted the rare secrets of the realm, and had foresight—neither Jing Fang nor Guan Luo could surpass him.

entries.zh: 鐸召而質之，岡曰：「惟木為福神，當以帝王占之。
entries.en: Duo called him in and pressed him. Gang said: "Wood alone is the star of blessing—it must be read as the omen of an emperor.
entries.literal: Duo summoned and questioned him. Gang said: "Only wood is the fortune star; it should be read as concerning an emperor.

entries.zh: 然則非福於今，必當有驗於後，未敢言之，請他日證其所驗。」
entries.en: But the blessing is not for today—it will prove itself later. I dare not say more; let another day show whether I am right."
entries.literal: Yet this is not fortune for the present; there must be verification later. I dare not speak of it—please let another day confirm what comes to pass."

entries.zh: 一日，又密召岡，因堅請語其詳，至於三四，岡辭不獲。
entries.en: Another day Duo summoned him in private and pressed him again and again—three or four times—until Gang could not refuse.
entries.literal: One day Duo again secretly summoned Gang and, pressing firmly for details, three or four times, Gang could not refuse.

entries.zh: 鐸乃屏去左右，岡曰：「木星入斗，帝王之兆也。
entries.en: Duo sent attendants away. Gang said: "Jupiter in the Dipper is the sign of a Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Duo then dismissed those nearby. Gang said: "Jupiter entering the Dipper is an omen of emperorship.

entries.zh: 木在斗中，『朱』字也。
entries.en: Wood inside the Dipper forms the character Zhu.
entries.literal: Wood within the Dipper is the character "Zhu."

entries.zh: 以此觀之，將來當有朱氏為君者也，天戒之矣。
entries.en: By that token a Zhu will rule in time to come—Heaven has given warning.
entries.literal: Viewed thus, hereafter there will be one surnamed Zhu as ruler—Heaven has warned of it.

entries.zh: 且木之數三，其禎也應在三紀之內乎！」
entries.en: And wood's number is three—perhaps the omen will run its course within three twelve-year periods!"
entries.literal: Moreover wood's number is three—perhaps the blessing manifests within three twelve-year periods!"

entries.zh: 鐸聞之，不復有言。
entries.en: Duo heard him out and said nothing further.
entries.literal: Duo heard this and spoke no more.

entries.zh: 天后朝有讖辭云：「首尾三鱗六十年，兩角犢子自狂顛，龍蛇相鬥血成川。」
entries.en: In the reign of Empress Wu a prophecy ran: "Head and tail, three scales, sixty years; the two-horned calf runs wild; dragons and serpents battle until rivers run red."
entries.literal: During Empress Wu's reign a prophecy said: "Head and tail, three scales, sixty years; the two-horned calf goes mad by itself; dragons and snakes fight until the rivers run with blood."

entries.zh: 當時好事者解云：「兩角犢子，牛也，必有牛姓干唐祚。」
entries.en: Contemporaries read it thus: "A two-horned calf is an ox—surely someone surnamed Niu will overturn Tang's mandate."
entries.literal: At the time enthusiasts interpreted: "Two-horned calf—that is niu (ox); surely one surnamed Niu will undermine Tang's mandate."

entries.zh: 故周子諒彈牛仙客，李德裕謗牛僧孺，皆以應圖讖為辭。
entries.en: Hence Zhou Ziliang attacked Niu Senke and Li Deyu vilified Niu Sengru—each invoking the prophecy as proof.
entries.literal: Hence Zhou Ziliang impeached Niu Senke, and Li Deyu slandered Niu Sengru, all citing fulfillment of the prophecy as their argument.

entries.zh: 然「朱」字「牛」下安「八」，八即角之象也，故朱滔、朱泚構喪亂之禍，冀無妄之福，豈知應之帝也。
entries.en: Yet in the character Zhu the element for "ox" stands above "eight"—eight being the sign of horns—so Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci stirred rebellion hoping for a throne that was not theirs, never guessing the omen pointed to the Emperor himself.
entries.literal: But the character Zhu has "ba" (eight) beneath "niu"—eight is the image of horn—so Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci brought calamity of disorder hoping for undeserved fortune, little knowing it foretold the Emperor.

entries.zh: 王者受命於天，光宅四海，祗事上帝，寵綏下民。
entries.en: The ruler receives Heaven's mandate, holds the realm in light, serves the Lord on High, and shelters the people below.
entries.literal: The king receives the mandate from Heaven, dwells in glory over the four seas, reverently serves the Supreme Lord, and cherishes and pacifies the people below.

entries.zh: 革故鼎新，諒歷數而先定，創業垂統，知圖籙以無差。
entries.en: To renew what is old and raise what is new—the turn of fortune was already settled; to found a line and pass it on—the portents left no doubt.
entries.literal: Renewing the old and establishing the new—surely the sequence of fate was fixed beforehand; founding the enterprise and handing down the succession—knowing the charts and registers are without error.

entries.zh: 神器所歸，祥符合應。
entries.en: Where the sacred vessel belongs, omens align.
entries.literal: Where the sacred vessel returns, auspicious tokens answer in accord.

entries.zh: 是以三正互用，五運相生，前朝道消，中原政散，瞻烏莫定，失鹿難追。
entries.en: The three calendars succeed one another; the five phases give birth in turn. Tang's Way faded and the heartland fell apart—no perch for the ravens, no catching the lost deer.
entries.literal: Thus the three orthodoxies alternate in use and the five phases generate one another; the former dynasty's Way waned and government in the Central Plain dissolved—like crows on the wing, none could settle; like the deer lost, none could recover it.

entries.zh: 朕經緯風雷，沐浴霜露，四征七伐，垂三十年，糾合齊盟，翼戴唐室。
entries.en: I have braved storm and frost, fought east, west, north, and south for nearly thirty years, knit alliances together, and upheld the Tang house.
entries.literal: I have woven wind and thunder, bathed in frost and dew, campaigned in four directions and seven punitive expeditions for nearly thirty years, rallied allied states, and supported the House of Tang.

entries.zh: 隨山刊木，罔憚胼胝；
entries.en: I felled forests and opened roads without flinching from toil;
entries.literal: Following mountains to hew wood, I did not shrink from calloused hands;

entries.zh: 投袂揮戈，不遑寢處。
entries.en: I took up arms and scarcely slept.
entries.literal: throwing up my sleeves to wield the spear, I had no leisure to lie down.

entries.zh: 洎上穹之所贊，知廣運之不興，莫諧輔漢之謀，徒罄事殷之禮。
entries.en: When Heaven above lent its aid, I knew the great fortune would not flourish; plans to assist Han came to nothing, and the rites of serving Yin were spent in vain.
entries.literal: When Heaven above came to aid, I knew the broad mandate would not revive; no harmony could be found in the plan to assist Han, and the rites of serving Yin were exhausted in vain.

entries.zh: 唐主知英華已竭，算祀有終，釋龜鼎以如遺，推劍紱而相授。
entries.en: The Tang sovereign knew his glory was spent and his years were up; he set aside the regalia of empire and offered sword and seal.
entries.literal: The Tang ruler knew that splendor was spent and his allotted span had ended; he released the tortoise and tripod as a legacy and pushed sword and seal cord forward to confer them.

entries.zh: 朕懼德弗嗣，執謙允恭，避駿命于南河，眷清風于穎水。
entries.en: I feared I lacked the virtue to succeed and clung to humility, declining the throne at South River and longing for the ease of Ying Stream.
entries.literal: I feared my virtue could not succeed and held to humility and deference, avoiding the august mandate at South River and cherishing the clear wind at Ying Stream.

entries.zh: 而乃列嶽群後，盈廷庶官，東西南北之人，斑白緇黃之眾，謂朕功蓋上下，澤被幽深，宜應天以順時，俾化家而為國。
entries.en: Yet the lords of the mountains, the officials who filled the court, folk from every quarter, gray heads and monks alike, said my merit reached heaven and earth and my grace the depths—that I must answer Heaven, follow the season, and turn a house into a realm.
entries.literal: Yet the peaks in rank and the hosts of officials, people from east, west, south, and north, and the multitude in plain cloth and monastic garb said my merit covered above and below and my grace reached the depths; I should respond to Heaven and accord with the season, transforming the family into a state.

entries.zh: 拒彼億兆，至於再三。
entries.en: I refused the countless pleas, again and again.
entries.literal: I refused those hundred millions, even to a third time.

entries.zh: 且曰七政已齊，萬幾難曠。
entries.en: They said the seven luminaries were in order and the myriad duties could not lie idle.
entries.literal: They said moreover that the seven regulators were aligned and the myriad affairs could not be left vacant.

entries.zh: 勉遵令典，爰正鴻名，告天地神祗，建宗廟社稷。
entries.en: Yielding at last to precedent, I set the great name, reported to Heaven and Earth and the spirits, and founded temples and altars.
entries.literal: Reluctantly following the established canon, I now rectify the great name, announce it to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, and establish ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 是日大酺，賞賜有差。
entries.en: That day the court held a grand feast; gifts varied by rank.
entries.literal: That day there was a great communal feast; rewards were graded.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》：甲辰，唐昭宣帝降御劄禪位於梁。
entries.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 notes: On jiachen Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang issued an imperial decree abdicating to Liang.
entries.literal: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: On jiachen, Tang's Emperor Zhaoxuan issued an imperial decree abdicating the throne to Liang.

entries.zh: 以攝中書令張文蔚為冊禮使，禮部尚書蘇循副之；
entries.en: Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei was made chief envoy for the investiture, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;
entries.literal: Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei was made chief of the investiture rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;

entries.zh: 攝侍中楊涉為押傳國寶使，翰林院學士張策副之；
entries.en: Acting Shizhong Yang She was made chief custodian of the imperial seal, with Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce as deputy;
entries.literal: Acting Shizhong Yang She was made chief custodian of the dynastic seal, with Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce as deputy;

entries.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，尚書左丞趙光逢副之。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made chief custodian of the gold regalia, with Left Assistant Minister Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made chief custodian of the gold regalia, with Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.

entries.zh: 帥百官備法駕，詣大樑。
entries.en: They led the full court with the imperial escort to Daliang.
entries.literal: They led the hundred officials with the imperial carriage to Great Liang.

entries.zh: 甲子，張文蔚、楊涉乘輅自上源驛至，從冊寶諸司各備儀衛鹵簿前導，百官從其後，至金祥殿前陳之。
entries.en: On jiazi Zhang Wenwei and Yang She came in the imperial carriage from Shangyuan Post, regalia and seals borne ahead with full guard, officials following, and arrayed all before the Hall of Golden Auspice.
entries.literal: On jiazi, Zhang Wenwei and Yang She rode the imperial carriage from Shangyuan Post; the offices bearing registers and seals each prepared guards and insignia to go before, the hundred officials following behind, until they arrayed them before the Hall of Golden Auspice.

entries.zh: 王被袞冕，即皇帝位。
entries.en: He assumed the imperial regalia and took the throne.
entries.literal: The king donned the imperial robes and took the emperor's seat.

entries.zh: 張文蔚、蘇循奉冊升殿進讀，楊涉、張策、薛貽矩、趙光逢以次奉寶升殿，讀已，降，帥百官舞蹈稱駕。
entries.en: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun presented and read the register; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng presented the seals in turn; then they led the court in the bowing dance and acclamation.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun bore the register up the hall and read it; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng in turn bore the seals up the hall; when the reading was done they descended and led the hundred officials in ritual dance and acclamation.

entries.zh: 帝遂與文蔚等宴於元德殿。
entries.en: The Emperor then banqueted Wenwei and the others in the Hall of Primordial Virtue.
entries.literal: The Emperor then feasted with Wenwei and the others in the Hall of Primordial Virtue.

entries.zh: 帝舉酒曰：「朕輔政未久，此皆諸公推戴之力。」
entries.en: The Emperor raised his wine and said: "I have governed but briefly—this is entirely your doing in elevating me."
entries.literal: The Emperor raised his cup and said: "I have assisted in government only a short while; this is all the power of your pushing me forward."

entries.zh: 文蔚等慚懼，俯伏不能對，獨蘇循、薛貽矩及刑部尚書張禕盛稱帝功德，宜應天順人。
entries.en: Wenwei and the rest were abashed and speechless on their faces; only Su Xun, Xue Yiju, and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi loudly praised the Emperor's merit as fitting Heaven and the people.
entries.literal: Wenwei and the others were ashamed and afraid, bowed prostrate and could not reply; only Su Xun, Xue Yiju, and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi lavishly praised the Emperor's merit and virtue, saying he should respond to Heaven and accord with the people.

entries.zh: 宋州刺史王皋進兩岐麥，陳州袁象先進白兔一，付史館編錄，兼示百官。
entries.en: Wang Gao of Songzhou offered double-eared wheat; Yuan Xiangxian of Chenzhou a white hare—both were recorded by the Historiography Office and displayed to the court.
entries.literal: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, presented double-eared wheat; Yuan Xiangxian of Chenzhou presented one white hare—both were sent to the Historiography Office for record and shown to the hundred officials.

entries.zh: 詔在京司及諸軍州縣印一例鑄換，其篆文則各如舊。
entries.en: An edict ordered all seals of capital bureaus and of armies, prefectures, and counties recast at once, each keeping its former inscription.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that seals of capital offices and of all army prefectures and counties be recast uniformly; the seal script should each remain as before.

entries.zh: 辛未，武安軍節度使馬殷進封楚王。
entries.en: On xinwei Ma Yin, governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced to King of Chu.
entries.literal: On xinwei, Ma Yin, military governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Chu.

entries.zh: 乙太府卿敬翔知崇政院，翔與帷幄之謀，故首擢焉。
entries.en: Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.
entries.literal: Appointing Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.

entries.zh: 追尊四代廟號：高祖媯州府君上諡曰宣元皇帝，廟號肅祖，太廟第一室，陵號興極陵，祖妣高平縣君范氏追諡宣僖皇后；
entries.en: Four ancestral generations received temple names: the High Ancestor, Lord of Guizhou, posthumous Emperor Xuanyuan, temple Sizu, first chamber, tomb Xingji; Lady Fan of Gaoping, Empress Xuanxi;
entries.literal: Posthumous temple names for four generations were honored: the High Ancestor, Lord of Guizhou Prefecture, was given the posthumous title Emperor Xuanyuan, temple name Sizu, first chamber of the Great Temple, tomb name Xingji, and ancestress Lady Fan of Gaoping County was posthumously titled Empress Xuanxi;

entries.zh: 皇曾祖宣惠王上諡曰光獻皇帝，廟號敬祖，第二室，陵號永安，祖妣秦國夫人楊氏追諡光孝皇后；
entries.en: the great-grandfather, King Xuanhui, posthumous Emperor Guangxian, temple Jingzu, second chamber, tomb Yong'an; Lady Yang of Qin, Empress Guangxiao;
entries.literal: the Emperor's great-grandfather, King Xuanhui, was given the posthumous title Emperor Guangxian, temple name Jingzu, second chamber, tomb Yong'an, and ancestress Lady Yang of Qin was posthumously titled Empress Guangxiao;

entries.zh: 皇祖武元王上諡曰昭武皇帝，廟號憲祖，第三室，陵號光天，祖妣吳國夫人劉氏追諡昭懿皇后；
entries.en: the grandfather, King Wuyuan, posthumous Emperor Zhaowu, temple Xianzu, third chamber, tomb Guangtian; Lady Liu of Wu, Empress Zhaoyi;
entries.literal: the Emperor's grandfather, King Wuyuan, was given the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, temple name Xianzu, third chamber, tomb name Guangtian, and ancestress Lady Liu of Wu was posthumously titled Empress Zhaoyi;

entries.zh: 皇考文明王上諡曰文穆皇帝，廟號烈祖，第四室，陵號咸寧，皇妣晉國太夫人王氏追諡文惠皇后。
entries.en: the father, King Wenming, posthumous Emperor Wenmu, temple Liezu, fourth chamber, tomb Xianning; the mother, Grand Lady of Jin, Lady Wang, Empress Wenhui.
entries.literal: the Emperor's father, King Wenming, was given the posthumous title Emperor Wenmu, temple name Liezu, fourth chamber, tomb Xianning, and the Emperor's mother, Grand Lady of Jin, Lady Wang, was posthumously titled Empress Wenhui.

entries.zh: 以宣武節度副使皇子友文為開封尹，判建昌院事。
entries.en: Prince Youwen, deputy Xuanwu governor and imperial son, was made Prefect of Kaifeng and superintendent of the Jianchang Court.
entries.literal: The Prince Youwen, deputy military governor of Xuanwu and imperial son, was made Prefect of Kaifeng and given charge of Jianchang Court affairs.

entries.zh: 友文，本康氏子也，帝養以為子。
entries.en: Youwen was born to the Kang clan; the Emperor adopted him as his son.
entries.literal: Youwen was originally a son of the Kang clan; the Emperor adopted and raised him as a son.

entries.zh: 顧惟涼德，曷副樂推，栗若履冰，懍如馭朽。
entries.en: My virtue is slight beside what men have urged upon me; I tremble as on thin ice, I drive as over rotten timber.
entries.literal: Looking back on my meager virtue, how can I match what joy has pushed forward? I tremble as if treading on ice, I am wary as if driving rotten wood.

entries.zh: 金行啟祚，玉曆建元，方宏經治之規，宜布惟新之令。
entries.en: Metal begins its reign; the calendar starts anew—it is time to widen governance and proclaim a fresh order.
entries.literal: The Metal phase begins its fortune; the jade calendar establishes a new origin—now is the time to enlarge the rules of governance and proclaim orders of renewal.

entries.zh: 可改唐天祐四年為開平元年，國號大樑。
entries.en: Let Tang's Tianyou year 4 become Kaiping year 1; the realm shall be called Great Liang.
entries.literal: Let the fourth year of Tang's Tianyou be changed to the first year of Kaiping; the state name is Great Liang.

entries.zh: 《書》載虞賓，斯為令範，《詩》稱周客，蓋有明文。
entries.en: The 《Book of Documents》 praises Yu's guest as the model; the 《Classic of Poetry》 honors Zhou's guest—text enough for what follows.
entries.literal: The 《Book》 records the guest of Yu as a fine model; the 《Odes》 praise the guest of Zhou—there is clear text for this.

entries.zh: 是用先封，以禮後嗣，宜以曹州濟陰之邑奉唐主，封為濟陰王。
entries.en: So we enfeoff before we enthrone: Caozhou's Jiyin district shall sustain the Tang ruler as Prince of Jiyin.
entries.literal: Therefore we first enfeoff and only afterward install the successor: let the seat of Jiyin in Caozhou support the Tang ruler, enfeoffing him as Prince of Jiyin.

entries.zh: 凡曰軌儀，並遵故實。
entries.en: Every rite shall follow established usage.
entries.literal: All ceremonial norms shall follow former practice.

entries.zh: 姬庭多士，比是殷臣；
entries.en: Men of the Zhou court served Yin as well;
entries.literal: Many officers of the Zhou court were likewise ministers of Yin;

entries.zh: 楚國群材，終為晉用。
entries.en: and Chu's worthies ended in Jin's employ.
entries.literal: talents of the state of Chu in the end were used by Jin.

entries.zh: 歷觀前載，自有通規，但遵故事之文，勿替在公之效。
entries.en: History offers a constant rule: follow precedent and do not lessen the duty of public service.
entries.literal: Reviewing former records, there has always been a common rule—only follow the language of old stories and do not diminish the effect of serving in office.

entries.zh: 應是唐朝中外文武舊臣，見任前資官爵，一切仍舊。
entries.en: Every Tang official, civil or military, in post or holding former rank, keeps office and title unchanged.
entries.literal: All former civil and military officials of Tang, whether currently serving or holding prior ranks and titles, shall remain as before in every respect.

entries.zh: 凡百有位，無易厥章，陳力濟時，盡瘁事我。
entries.en: Let none among the hundred offices alter his charge; serve the times with all your strength and give your utmost to me.
entries.literal: For the hundred ranks, let none change their statutes; exert your strength to aid the age and exhaust yourselves in serving me.

entries.zh: 古者興王之地，受命之邦，集大勳有異庶方，沾慶澤所宜加等。
entries.en: Anciently the land that raised a king and the state that received the mandate, for uncommon merit, deserved extra grace when rewards were given.
entries.literal: In antiquity the place where a king rose and the state that received the mandate, having gathered great merit unlike other regions, deserved added favor when blessings were bestowed.

entries.zh: 故豐沛著啟祚之美，穰鄧有建都之榮，用壯鴻基，且旌故里，爰遵令典，先示殊恩。
entries.en: Feng and Pei shone as seats of founding; Rang and Deng as places of enthronement—so we honor the cradle of empire and, by ancient right, show favor first to our home.
entries.literal: Thus Feng and Pei showed the beauty of founding fortune, Rang and Deng the glory of establishing the capital—strengthening the great foundation and honoring the old home, following the established canon, we first display special favor.

entries.zh: 宜升汴州為開封府，建名東都。
entries.en: Bianzhou is raised to Kaifeng Prefecture and named the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Bianzhou should be promoted to Kaifeng Prefecture and styled the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 其東都改為西都，仍廢京兆府為雍州佑國軍節度使。
entries.en: The old Eastern Capital becomes the Western Capital; Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished and Yongzhou given a Youguo Army governor.
entries.literal: The former Eastern Capital is changed to the Western Capital, and Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished in favor of a Yongzhou Youguo Army military governor.

entries.zh: 〈《五代會要》：「四月，改京兆府為大安府，長安縣為大安縣，萬年縣為大年縣，仍置佑國軍節度使額。
entries.en: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: "In the fourth month Jingzhao became Da'an Prefecture, Chang'an county Da'an, Wannian county Danian, and the Youguo Army post was created.
entries.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: "In the fourth month Jingzhao Prefecture was changed to Da'an Prefecture, Chang'an County to Da'an County, Wannian County to Danian County, and the Youguo Army governorship was established.

entries.zh: 始命韓建為佑國軍節度使。」〉
entries.en: Han Jian was first named Youguo Army governor."〉
entries.literal: Han Jian was first appointed military governor of the Youguo Army."〉

entries.zh: 十一月丁亥朔，幸廣王第作樂。
entries.en: On dinghai, the first of the eleventh month, he went to the Prince of Guang’s mansion for music.
entries.literal: On dinghai, first day of the eleventh month, he visited the Prince of Guang’s residence for music.

entries.zh: 辛卯，宴文武四品已上于宣威殿。
entries.en: On xinmao he gave civil and military officials of fourth rank and above a feast at Xuanwei Hall.
entries.literal: On xinmao he feasted civil and military officials of fourth rank and above at Xuanwei Hall.

entries.zh: 庚戌，幸左龍虎軍，宴群臣。
entries.en: On gengxu he went to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army and feasted the ministers.
entries.literal: On gengxu he visited the Left Dragon-Tiger Army and feasted the ministers.

entries.zh: 甲寅，幸右龍虎軍，宴群臣。
entries.en: On jiayin he went to the Right Dragon-Tiger Army and feasted the ministers.
entries.literal: On jiayin he visited the Right Dragon-Tiger Army and feasted the ministers.

entries.zh: 戊戌，詔曰：「自朔至今，暴風未息，諒惟不德，致此咎征。
entries.en: On wuxu an edict read: "Since the new moon, violent winds have not stopped. I alone lack virtue and have drawn down this portent.
entries.literal: On wuxu an edict stated: "From the new moon until now violent winds have not ceased—I alone lack virtue and have brought on this ill omen.

entries.zh: 皇天動威，罔敢不懼。
entries.en: Heaven has stirred its might; none may fail to fear.
entries.literal: Heaven has shown its wrath; who would not fear?

entries.zh: 宜遍命祈禱，副朕意焉。」
entries.en: Let prayers be ordered throughout the realm to match my intent."
entries.literal: Prayers should be ordered everywhere to accord with my intent."

entries.zh: 差官分往祠所止風。
entries.en: Envoys were sent to various shrines to pray for the wind to cease.
entries.literal: Officials were dispatched separately to shrines to halt the wind.

entries.zh: 己亥，日南至，帝被袞冕禦朝元殿，列細仗，奏樂於庭，群臣稱賀。
entries.en: On jihai, the winter solstice, the Emperor wore full regalia at Chaoyuan Hall, drew up the detailed guard, had music in the courtyard, and received congratulations from the ministers.
entries.literal: On jihai, the winter solstice, the Emperor donned ceremonial robes and presided at Chaoyuan Hall, arrayed the detailed guard, music played in the courtyard, and the ministers offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 帝畋于伊水。
entries.en: The Emperor hunted along the Yi River.
entries.literal: The Emperor hunted on the Yi River.

entries.zh: 乙巳，詔曰：「關防者，所以識異服、察異言也。
entries.en: On yisi an edict read: "Frontier posts exist to spot foreign dress and foreign speech.
entries.literal: On yisi an edict stated: "Frontier posts exist to recognize alien dress and detect alien speech.

entries.zh: 況下天未息，兵民多奸，改形易衣，覘我戎事。
entries.en: The realm is still unsettled and soldiers and civilians are rife with deceit; they disguise themselves to spy on our armies.
entries.literal: Moreover the realm is not yet at peace and soldiers and people are full of treachery—they change their appearance and clothes to spy on our military affairs.

entries.zh: 比者有諜皆以詐敗，而未嘗罪所過地，叛將逃卒竊其妻孥而影附使者，亦未嘗詰其所經。
entries.en: Lately every spy has been caught by trickery, yet the districts they passed through went unpunished; defecting officers and runaway soldiers stole families and trailed behind envoys, yet no one questioned their route.
entries.literal: Lately spies have all been exposed by fraud, yet the places they passed through were never punished; rebel generals and fugitive soldiers stole away wives and children and shadowed envoys, yet where they traveled was never investigated.

entries.zh: 今海內未同，而緩法弛禁，非所以息奸詐、止奔亡也。
entries.en: The empire is not yet one, yet the law is lax and the gates open—no way to curb deceit or stop desertion.
entries.literal: Now the realm is not yet united, yet laws are slack and prohibitions loose—this is no way to end fraud or stop flight.

entries.zh: 應在京諸司，不得擅給公驗。
entries.en: No capital agency may issue travel passes on its own.
entries.literal: All offices in the capital must not issue official passes on their own authority.

entries.zh: 如有出外須執憑由者，其司門過所，先須經中書門下點檢，宜委宰臣趙光逢專判出給，俾由顯重，冀絕奸源。
entries.en: Anyone leaving the capital with papers must have Gate Office permits checked first by the Secretariat-Chancellery; chief minister Zhao Guangfeng alone should issue them, so the trail is weighty and treachery choked at the source.
entries.literal: If anyone going out must carry credentials, the Gate Office travel permit must first be inspected by the Secretariat-Chancellery; chief minister Zhao Guangfeng should be charged solely with issuing them, so that the route is weighty and the source of treachery cut off.

entries.zh: 仍下兩京、河陽及六軍諸衛、御史台，各加鈐轄。
entries.en: The same order went to both capitals, Heyang, the Six Armies guards, and the Censorate to tighten oversight.
entries.literal: The order was also sent to the two capitals, Heyang, the Six Armies guards, and the Censorate, each to tighten control.

entries.zh: 公私行李，復不得帶挾家口向西。
entries.en: Private and official baggage might no longer take dependents west.
entries.literal: Private and official baggage again must not carry family members westward.

entries.zh: 其襄、鄧、鄜、延等道，並同處分。」
entries.en: The Xiang, Deng, Fu, and Yan circuits received the same rules."
entries.literal: The Xiang, Deng, Fu, and Yan circuits were to be handled the same way."

entries.zh: 以甯國軍節度使王景仁充北面行營都招討使，潞州副招討使韓勍為副，相州刺史李思安為先鋒使。
entries.en: Wang Jingren, Ningguo commissioner, became overall northern campaign commander; Han Qin, Luzhou deputy, his second; Li Si’an, Xiangzhou prefect, vanguard.
entries.literal: Ningguo military commissioner Wang Jingren was made overall northern campaign commander; Luzhou deputy commander Han Qin was his second; Xiangzhou prefect Li Si’an was vanguard commander.

entries.zh: 時鎮州王熔、定州王處直叛，結連晉人，故遣將討之。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Zhenzhou and Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou had rebelled and joined the Jin, so troops were sent against them.
entries.literal: At the time Zhenzhou’s Wang Rong and Dingzhou’s Wang Chuzhi had rebelled and allied with the Jin, so generals were sent to attack them.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》：十一月十四日，司天奏：「月蝕，不宜用兵。」
entries.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: On the fourteenth of the eleventh month the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "There will be a lunar eclipse; it is inauspicious to use arms."
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: On the fourteenth of the eleventh month the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "A lunar eclipse—war should not be waged."

entries.zh: 時王景仁方總大軍北伐，追之不及。
entries.en: Wang Jingren was already at the head of the main northern force; the recall did not overtake him.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Jingren was already leading the great army north; the recall could not reach him in time.

entries.zh: 至五年正月二日，果為後唐莊宗大敗于柏鄉。
entries.en: On the second of the first month of the fifth year he was indeed crushed at Baixiang by Zhuangzong of Later Tang.
entries.literal: By the second of the first month of year five he was indeed routed at Baixiang by Later Tang’s Zhuangzong.

entries.zh: 六月乙卯，命北面都招討使、鎮國軍節度使楊師厚出屯邢、洺。
entries.en: On yimao in the sixth month he sent overall northern commander Yang Shihou, Zhenguo commissioner, to camp at Xing and Mo.
entries.literal: On yimao of the sixth month he ordered overall northern commander and Zhenguo military commissioner Yang Shihou to encamp at Xing and Mo.

entries.zh: 丁巳，鎮、定鈔我湯陰。
entries.en: On dingsi the Zhen and Ding forces raided Tangyin.
entries.literal: On dingsi Zhen and Ding raided our Tangyin.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「常山背義，易水效尤，誘其蕃戎，動我邊鄙，南侵相、魏，東出邢、洺。
entries.en: An edict read: "Changshan broke faith and Yishui copied it, rousing frontier tribes and stirring our borders, pushing south into Xiang and Wei and east toward Xing and Mo.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Changshan turned traitor and Yishui followed suit, enticing the frontier tribes and stirring our borderlands, invading south into Xiang and Wei and east out of Xing and Mo.

entries.zh: 是用遣將徂征，為人除害，但初頒赦令，不欲食言，宥而伐之，諒非獲已。
entries.en: I send generals to clear away harm—but we have just proclaimed an amnesty and I will not break my word; to pardon yet still strike is not what I desire.
entries.literal: Therefore I send generals on campaign to remove harm for the people—but having just proclaimed an amnesty I do not wish to break my word; to spare yet still attack is surely not my wish.

entries.zh: 況聞謀始，不自帥臣，致此厲階，並由奸佞。
entries.en: I hear the plot did not start with the commanders; this disaster came from treacherous advisers.
entries.literal: Moreover I hear the plot did not begin with the commanders themselves; this evil stage was all due to treacherous minions.

entries.zh: 密通人使，潛結沙陀，既懼罪誅，乃生離叛。
entries.en: They sent secret envoys and allied with the Shatuo; fearing punishment, they rebelled.
entries.literal: They secretly sent envoys and quietly allied with the Shatuo; fearing punishment, they turned to rebellion.

entries.zh: 今雖行討伐，已舉師徒，亦開詔諭之門，不阻歸降之路。
entries.en: Though we march to punish them and armies are already raised, the door of edicts stays open and the road of surrender is not blocked.
entries.literal: Though we now march to punish them and have already raised armies, we also open the gate of edicts and do not block the road of surrender.

entries.zh: 矧又王熔、處直未曾削爵除名，若翻然改圖，不遠而復，必仍舊貫，當保前功。
entries.en: Wang Rong and Chuzhi have not been stripped of rank; if they turn back soon, they keep their posts and their past merit.
entries.literal: Moreover Wang Rong and Chuzhi have not yet been stripped of rank and name—if they turn back and return not far off, they shall keep their old posts and preserve their former merit.

entries.zh: 如有率眾向明，拔州效順，亦行殊賞，冀徇來情，免令受弊於疲民，用示維新於汙俗。
entries.en: Whoever leads men to submit, takes a prefecture, and proves loyal will receive special rewards, to spare the people and show renewal to a corrupted land.
entries.literal: If any lead the masses toward the light, seize a prefecture and show loyalty, special rewards will also be granted, hoping to meet their intent, lest the weary people suffer harm and to show renewal to a tainted land.

entries.zh: 宜令行營都招討使及陳暉軍前，准此敕文，散加招諭，將安眾懼，特舉明恩。
entries.en: The campaign commander and Chen Hui at the front should circulate this edict, reassure the fearful, and proclaim mercy openly.
entries.literal: The campaign overall commander and Chen Hui before the army should follow this edict, distribute persuasion widely, calm the people’s fear, and specially proclaim clear grace.

entries.zh: 鎮州只罪李宏規一人，其餘一切不問。」
entries.en: At Zhenzhou only Li Honggui is to be punished; all others go free."
entries.literal: At Zhenzhou only Li Honggui is guilty; all others are not questioned."

entries.zh: 詔修天宮佛寺。
entries.en: An edict ordered the Heavenly Palace Buddhist monastery repaired.
entries.literal: An edict ordered repair of the Heavenly Palace Buddhist monastery.

entries.zh: 又，湖南奏：「潭州僧法思、桂州僧歸真並乞賜紫衣。」
entries.en: Hunan also reported: "The monks Fasi of Tanzhou and Guizhen of Guizhou both request purple robes."
entries.literal: Also, Hunan reported: "Tanzhou monk Fasi and Guizhou monk Guizhen both beg purple robes."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: It was granted.

entries.zh: 十二月，詔以時雪稍愆，命丞相及三省官各詣望祠祈禱。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, with timely snow scarce, the chief minister and Three Departments officials were each sent to the Wang Shrine to pray.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month an edict stated that timely snow was somewhat lacking and ordered the chief minister and Three Departments officials each to go to the Wang Shrine to pray.

entries.zh: 癸酉，臘假，詔諸王與河南尹、左右金吾、六統軍等較獵于近苑。
entries.en: On guiyou, La holiday, princes, the Henan prefect, the Gold Crow commanders, and the six army commanders were ordered to hunt together in the nearby park.
entries.literal: On guiyou, on the La holiday, an edict ordered the princes with the Henan prefect, Left and Right Gold Crow, and the six army commanders-in-chief to compete in hunting in the nearby park.

entries.zh: 命大理卿王鄯使于安南，左散騎常侍吳藹使於朗州，皆以旌節官誥錫之也。
entries.en: Wang Shan, judicial review director, was sent to Annan and Wu Ai, left regular attendant, to Langzhou, each with banners of authority and commission patents.
entries.literal: He appointed Court of Judicial Review director Wang Shan envoy to Annan and Left Regular Attendant Wu Ai envoy to Langzhou—both were granted banners of authority and commission patents.

entries.zh: 又命將作少監薑宏道為朗州旌節官使副。
entries.en: Jiang Hongdao, works vice-director, was made deputy banner envoy to Langzhou.
entries.literal: He also appointed Directorate of Works vice-director Jiang Hongdao deputy banner envoy to Langzhou.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》：舊制，巡撫、黜陟、冊命、吊贈、入蕃等使，選朝臣為之，其宣慰、加官、送旌節，即以中官為之，今以三品送旌節，新例也。
entries.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: By old custom, inspection, promotion and demotion, investiture, condolence, and missions abroad went to court officials; consolation, promotion, and delivery of banners went to eunuchs—now third-rank officials carry banners, a new rule.
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: By old rule, inspection, promotion and demotion, investiture, condolence, and entry to foreign lands envoys were chosen from court officials; consolation, promotion, and delivery of banners of authority were given to eunuchs—now third-rank officials deliver banners, a new precedent.

entries.zh: 延州節度使高萬興奏，領軍於邠州界蒿子谷韋家寨，殺戮甯、慶兩州賊軍約二千餘人，並生擒都頭指揮使及奪馬器甲等事。
entries.en: Gao Wanxing reported a raid at Weijia Stockade in Haozi Valley on the Bin border, killing some two thousand bandits of Ning and Qing and capturing commanders with horses, armor, and gear.
entries.literal: Yanzhou commissioner Gao Wanxing reported leading troops at Weijia Stockade in Haozi Valley on the Binzhou border, killing about two thousand bandit troops of Ning and Qing prefectures, and capturing bandit commanders alive along with seized horses, armor, and gear.

entries.zh: 其入奏軍將使宣召赴內殿賜對，以銀器彩物錫之，宰臣及文武官各奉表賀。
entries.en: The reporting officer was summoned to the inner hall and given silver and silks; chief ministers and officials sent congratulations.
entries.literal: The reporting army officer was announced and summoned to audience in the inner hall and granted silver vessels and colored goods; chief ministers and civil and military officials each submitted congratulatory memorials.

entries.zh: 是月，魏博節度上言，於涇縣北戮殺鎮州王熔兵士七千餘人，奪馬二千餘匹，戈甲未知其數，並擒都將以下四十餘人。
entries.en: That month Weibo reported slaughtering more than seven thousand of Wang Rong’s men north of Jing county, seizing two thousand horses, armor in unknown quantity, and forty-odd commanders.
entries.literal: That month Weibo’s commissioner reported that north of Jing county he slaughtered more than seven thousand of Wang Rong’s Zhenzhou soldiers, seized more than two thousand horses, armor in unknown quantity, and captured more than forty commanders and below.

entries.zh: 兩浙進大方茶二萬斤，琢畫宮衣五百副。
entries.en: The two Zhes sent twenty thousand jin of brick tea and five hundred sets of carved palace robes.
entries.literal: The two Zhes presented twenty thousand jin of large-block tea and five hundred sets of carved palace robes.

entries.zh: 廣州貢犀象奇珍及金銀等，其估數千萬。
entries.en: Guangzhou sent rhinoceros horn, ivory, rarities, and gold and silver estimated in the tens of millions.
entries.literal: Guangzhou offered rhinoceros horn, elephant ivory, rare treasures, and gold and silver worth tens of millions by estimate.

entries.zh: 安南兩使留後曲美，《通鑒》：十二月戊午，以靜海、曲美為節度使。
entries.en: Annan’s envoys and regent Qu Mei—《Zizhi Tongjian》: On wuwu of the twelfth month Qu Mei of Jinghai was made military commissioner.
entries.literal: Annan’s two envoys and regent Qu Mei—《Zizhi Tongjian》: On wuwu of the twelfth month Jinghai’s Qu Mei was made military commissioner.

entries.zh: 進筒中蕉五百匹，龍腦、郁金各五瓶，他海貨等有差。
entries.en: He presented five hundred bolts of tube-rolled plantain, five jars each of borneol and turmeric, and other overseas goods in graded amounts.
entries.literal: He presented five hundred bolts of tube-rolled plantain, five jars each of borneol and turmeric, and other sea goods in graded amounts.

entries.zh: 又進南蠻通好金器六物、銀器十二並乾陁綾花繓棖越啉毛等雜織奇巧者各三十件。
entries.en: He also sent six gold and twelve silver friendship vessels from the south, and thirty each of ganduo brocade, huajiao, bing, yueling, and other exotic textiles.
entries.literal: Also presented six gold vessels and twelve silver vessels for southern barbarian friendship, and thirty each of ganduo brocade, huajiao, bing, yueling, and other exotic woven goods.

entries.zh: 福建進戶部所支榷課葛三萬五千匹。
entries.en: Fujian presented thirty-five thousand bolts of Revenue Ministry monopoly ramie cloth.
entries.literal: Fujian presented thirty-five thousand bolts of monopoly-tax ramie cloth paid by the Revenue Ministry.

entries.zh: 開平四年十月乙亥，東京博王友文入覲，召之也。
entries.en: On yihai in the tenth month of Kaiping 4, Prince of Bo Youwen at the Eastern Capital entered court; he had been summoned.
entries.literal: On yihai, tenth month of Kaiping 4, Prince of Bo Youwen of the Eastern Capital came to audience—it was a summons.

entries.zh: 己卯，以新修天驥院開宴落成，內外並獻馬，而魏博進絹四萬匹為駔價。
entries.en: On jimao, to mark completion of the newly rebuilt Heavenly Steeds Park, court and country presented horses; Weibo sent forty thousand bolts of silk as stud fees.
entries.literal: On jimao, because the newly repaired Heavenly Steeds Park held a feast for its completion, inside and outside alike presented horses, and Weibo sent forty thousand bolts of silk as stud price.

entries.zh: 壬午，以冬設禁軍，幸興安鞠場，召文武百官宴。
entries.en: On renwu, with winter drill for the Palace Army, he went to Xing’an Ball Ground and feasted the full civil and military establishment.
entries.literal: On renwu, because winter was setting in for the Palace Army, he visited Xing’an Ball Ground and summoned civil and military officials to a feast.

entries.zh: 幸開化，大閱軍實。
entries.en: He went to Kaihua and held a grand inspection of arms and stores.
entries.literal: He visited Kaihua and conducted a great review of military stores.

entries.zh: 五月己卯朔，從官文武自丞相而下，並詣行殿起居，親王及諸道籓帥咸奉表來上。
entries.en: On jimao, the first of the fifth month, civil and military attendants from the chancellor down all came to the traveling hall for inquiry; princes and military commissioners of every circuit presented memorials.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jimao, civil and military attendants from the chancellor down all came to the traveling hall for inquiry; princes and military commissioners of every circuit presented memorials.

entries.zh: 庚辰，發自鄭州，至滎陽，河南尹魏王宗奭望塵迎拜；
entries.en: On gengchen he set out from Zhengzhou and reached Xingyang; Henan Intendant Prince of Wei Zongshi met him bowing in the dust;
entries.literal: On gengchen he set out from Zhengzhou, reached Xingyang; Henan Intendant Prince of Wei Zongshi met him bowing in the dust;

entries.zh: 河陽留後邵贊、懷州刺史段明遠等邐迤來迎。
entries.en: Shao Zan, acting Heyang commissioner, Duan Mingyuan of Huai, and others met him in turn along the route.
entries.literal: Heyang Acting Commissioner Shao Zan, Huai Prefecture Inspector Duan Mingyuan, and others came in succession to meet.

entries.zh: 夕次汜水縣，帝召魏王宗奭入對，便於御前賜食，數刻乃退。
entries.en: That night he stopped at Sishui; the Emperor called Prince of Wei Zongshi to audience, fed him before the throne, and after some time sent him away.
entries.literal: That evening he halted at Sishui County; the Emperor summoned Prince of Wei Zongshi to audience and at once bestowed food before the throne; after several quarters he withdrew.

entries.zh: 壬午，駐蹕于汜水，宰臣、河南尹、六學士並于內殿起居，敕以建昌宮事委宰臣於兢領之。
entries.en: On renwu he was at Sishui; chancellors, the Henan intendant, and the Six Academicians attended in the inner hall; Jianchang Palace business was placed in Chancellor Yu Jing's hands.
entries.literal: On renwu he halted at Sishui; chancellors, Henan Intendant, and Six Academicians all made inquiry in the inner hall; an order entrusted Jianchang Palace affairs to Chancellor Yu Jing.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》：其年六月，廢建昌宮，以河南尹、魏王張宗奭為國計使，凡天下金穀兵戎舊隸建昌宮者，悉主之。
entries.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the sixth month Jianchang Palace was abolished and Prince of Wei Zhang Zongshi, Henan intendant, became state comptroller, taking over all grain, funds, and troops formerly held by the palace.
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the sixth month of that year Jianchang Palace was abolished; Henan Intendant Prince of Wei Zhang Zongshi was made State Comptroller; all realm grain, funds, and troops formerly under Jianchang Palace were placed under him.

entries.zh: 癸未，帝發自汜水，宣令邵贊、段明遠各歸所理。
entries.en: On guawei he left Sishui and announced that Shao Zan and Duan Mingyuan should each return to their posts.
entries.literal: On guawei the Emperor set out from Sishui and proclaimed that Shao Zan and Duan Mingyuan should each return to their jurisdictions.

entries.zh: 午憩任村屯，夕次孝義宮。
entries.en: He rested at Rencun Station at noon and lodged at Xiaoyi Palace that evening.
entries.literal: At noon he rested at Rencun Station; that evening he halted at Xiaoyi Palace.

entries.zh: 留都文武禮部尚書孔續而下道左迎拜。
entries.en: Civil and military officials left in the capital, from Minister of Rites Kong Xu down, lined the road to welcome him.
entries.literal: Capital custodian civil and military officials from Minister of Rites Kong Xu down met and bowed on the left of the road.

entries.zh: 次偃師。
entries.en: He stopped at Yanshi.
entries.literal: He halted at Yanshi.

entries.zh: 甲申，至都，文武臣奉迎於東郊。
entries.en: On jiashen he entered the capital; civil and military officials received him at the eastern suburb.
entries.literal: On jiashen he reached the capital; civil and military officials welcomed him at the eastern suburb.

entries.zh: 渤海遣使朝貢。
entries.en: Bohai presented tribute envoys.
entries.literal: Bohai sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 宰臣薛貽矩抱恙在假，不克扈從，宣問旁午，仍命且駐東京以俟良愈。
entries.en: Chancellor Xue Yiju was ill on leave and could not join the tour; the Emperor's inquiries came often, yet ordered him to stay at the Eastern Capital until recovery.
entries.literal: Chancellor Xue Yiju was ill on leave and could not attend the progress; inquiries were frequent, and he was still ordered to remain at the Eastern Capital until fully recovered.

entries.zh: 及薨，帝震悼頗久，命雒苑使曹守璫往弔祭之，又命輟六日、七日、八日朝參，丞相、文武並詣上閣門進名奉慰。
entries.en: At his death the Emperor mourned at length, sent Luoyuan commissioner Cao Shoudang to condole, and cancelled court for the sixth through eighth; chancellor and officials filed condolence at the Upper Gate.
entries.literal: When he died the Emperor mourned a long while, ordered Luoyuan Commissioner Cao Shoucong to go offer condolences, and also ordered court attendance suspended on the sixth, seventh, and eighth; chancellor and civil and military officials all went to the Upper Gate to enter their names in condolence.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以彗星謫見，詔兩京見禁囚徒大辟罪以下，遞減一等，限三日內疏理訖聞奏。
entries.en: On dinghai, after a comet appeared, an edict reduced by one grade the sentences of all prisoners in both capitals down through capital offenses, requiring review within three days.
entries.literal: On dinghai, because a comet had appeared, an edict ordered that in the two capitals all imprisoned convicts down from capital crimes should have their sentences reduced one grade, with review completed and reported within three days.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》：彗星見於靈台之西，至五月始降赦宥罪，以答天譴。
entries.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: A comet showed west of Lingtai; not until the fifth month did the court grant amnesty for crimes to answer Heaven's reproof.
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: A comet appeared west of Lingtai; only in the fifth month was an amnesty granted for crimes, to answer Heaven’s reproof.

entries.zh: 又云：五月壬戌夜，熒惑犯心大星，去心四度，順行。
entries.en: It adds: On renxu night in the fifth month Mars crossed the great star of Heart, four degrees off, moving direct.
entries.literal: It also says: On the night of renxu in the fifth month Mars trespassed the great star of Heart, four degrees from Heart, moving direct.

entries.zh: 司天奏：「大星為帝王之星，宜修省以答天譴。」
entries.en: The directorate reported: "The great star is the sovereign's star—the ruler should cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof."
entries.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "The great star is the star of the Son of Heaven—self-cultivation is fitting to answer Heaven’s reproof."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「生育之人，爰當暑月，乳哺之愛，方及薰風。
entries.en: An edict read: "Living creatures are now in the summer months; the love of suckling meets the warm breeze.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Living creatures are now in the summer months; the love of suckling meets the warm breeze.

entries.zh: 儻肆意于刲屠，豈推恩於長養，俾無殄暴，以助發生。
entries.en: Wanton slaughter cannot square with nurturing life; let killing cease that growth may flourish.
entries.literal: If one recklessly slaughters, how can one extend kindness in nurturing—let there be no extermination, to aid generation.

entries.zh: 宜令兩京及諸州府，夏季內禁斷屠宰及採捕。
entries.en: The two capitals and all prefectures and circuits shall forbid slaughter and hunting for the summer.
entries.literal: Let the two capitals and every prefecture and circuit forbid slaughter and hunting through the summer.

entries.zh: 天民之窮，諒由賦分；
entries.en: The people's want surely lies in fate's decree;
entries.literal: The people’s poverty is surely from allotted fate;

entries.zh: 國章所在，亦務興仁。
entries.en: yet where the state's charge rests, benevolence must still be practiced.
entries.literal: where the state’s regulations lie, one must also practice benevolence.

entries.zh: 所在鰥寡孤獨、廢疾不濟者，委長吏量加賑恤。
entries.en: Where widowers, orphans, the solitary poor, the disabled, and the destitute are found, let chief officials give relief as needed.
entries.literal: Wherever widowers, orphans, the solitary, the disabled, and those in distress are found, commission the chief official to grant relief as appropriate.

entries.zh: 史載葬枯，用彰軫恤；
entries.en: History praises burying the unburied dead as proof of compassion;
entries.literal: History records burying the withered, to show compassion;

entries.zh: 禮稱掩骼，將致和平。
entries.en: ritual demands covering bleached bones to restore peace.
entries.literal: ritual speaks of covering exposed bones, to bring peace.

entries.zh: 應兵戈之地，有暴露骸骨，委所在長吏差人專攻收瘞。
entries.en: Where war has left exposed bones, commission the local chief official to send men to gather and bury them.
entries.literal: Where war has left exposed bones, commission the local chief official to send men specially to gather and bury them.

entries.zh: 國癘之文，尚標七祀；
entries.en: State plague ordinances still prescribe the seven sacrifices;
entries.literal: The state’s plague texts still mark the seven sacrifices;

entries.zh: 良藥之市，亦載三醫。
entries.en: the registry of fine medicines still lists three doctors.
entries.literal: the market of good medicines also records three physicians.

entries.zh: 用憐無告之人，宜征有喜之術。
entries.en: Pity those with none to speak for them—let skilled physicians be sought.
entries.literal: Out of pity for those with no one to plead for them, skilled healing should be sought.

entries.zh: 凡有疫之處，委長吏檢尋醫方，于要路曉示。
entries.en: Wherever plague appears, commission the chief official to search out medical formulas and post them at key roads.
entries.literal: Wherever plague appears, commission the chief official to search out medical formulas and proclaim them at key roads.

entries.zh: 如有家無骨肉兼困窮不濟者，即仰長吏差醫給藥救療之。」
entries.en: If any household lacks kin and is destitute and in distress, the chief official should dispatch a physician to give medicine and treat them."
entries.literal: If any household lacks kin and is also destitute and in distress, the chief official should dispatch a physician to give medicine and treat them."

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔曰：「亢陽滋甚，農事已傷，宜令宰臣於兢赴中嶽，杜曉赴西嶽，精切祈禱。
entries.en: On xinmao an edict read: "Drought grows severe and farming is already harmed—let Chancellor Yu Jing go to the Central Peak and Du Xiao to the Western Peak for earnest prayer.
entries.literal: On xinmao an edict stated: "Drought yang grows severe and farming is already harmed—let Chancellor Yu Jing go to the Central Peak and Du Xiao to the Western Peak for earnest prayer.

entries.zh: 其近京靈廟，宜委河南尹，五帝壇、風師雨師、九宮貴神，委中書各差官祈之。」
entries.en: Shrines near the capital were left to the Henan intendant; the Five Emperors Altar, Wind Master, Rain Master, and Nine Palaces spirits each received Secretariat officers to pray."
entries.literal: Spirit shrines near the capital should be entrusted to the Henan Intendant; the Five Emperors Altar, Wind Master, Rain Master, and Nine Palaces Noble Spirits should each have officials dispatched by the Secretariat to pray."

entries.zh: 《通鑒》：閏月壬戌，帝疾甚，謂近臣曰：「我經營天下三十年，不意太原餘孽更昌熾如此！
entries.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On renxu of the intercalary month the Emperor was gravely ill; he said to his intimates: "Thirty years I have ruled, and never thought the Taiyuan remnant would grow so strong!
entries.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On renxu in the intercalary month the Emperor’s illness was grave; he told close ministers: "I have managed the realm for thirty years and did not expect the Taiyuan remnant to flourish so!

entries.zh: 吾觀其志不小，天復奪我年，我死，諸兒非彼敵也，吾無葬地矣！」
entries.en: Their aim is not small; Heaven again cuts my years—when I die my sons cannot stand against them; I have no grave prepared!"
entries.literal: I see their ambition is no small thing; Heaven again shortens my years—when I die my sons are no match for them; I have no burial ground!"

entries.zh: 因哽咽，絕而復蘇。
entries.en: He sobbed until breath failed, then came back.
entries.literal: He choked with sobs, stopped breathing, and revived.

entries.zh: 帝長子郴王友裕早卒。
entries.en: His eldest son, Prince of Chen Youyu, had died young.
entries.literal: The Emperor’s eldest son Prince of Chen Youyu had died early.

entries.zh: 次假子友文，帝特愛之，常留守東都，兼建昌宮使。
entries.en: Next came the adopted son Youwen, the Emperor's favorite, who often stayed at the Eastern Capital as Jianchang palace commissioner.
entries.literal: Next was the adopted son Youwen, whom the Emperor especially loved; he often remained at the Eastern Capital as Jianchang Palace Commissioner.

entries.zh: 次郢王友珪，其母亳州營倡也，為左右控鶴都指揮使。
entries.en: Next was Prince of Ying Yougui, born of a Bozhou camp singer, commander of the left and right Crane-Controlled Armies.
entries.literal: Next was Prince of Ying Yougui, whose mother was a camp entertainer from Bozhou; he was Commander of the Left and Right Crane-Controlled Armies.

entries.zh: 次均王友貞，為東都馬步都指揮使。
entries.en: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander.

entries.zh: 帝雖未以友文為太子，意常屬之。
entries.en: Youwen was not named crown prince, yet the Emperor's heart was often set on him.
entries.literal: Although the Emperor had not made Youwen crown prince, his intent often rested on him.

entries.zh: 六月丁丑朔，帝命敬翔出友珪為萊州刺史，即命之官。
entries.en: On dingchou, the first of the sixth month, the Emperor ordered Jing Xiang to issue an order posting Yougui as prefect of Laizhou, and at once ordered him to take office.
entries.literal: On dingchou, the first day of the sixth month, the Emperor ordered Jing Xiang to issue an order posting Yougui as prefect of Laizhou, and at once ordered him to take office.

entries.zh: 已宣旨，未行敕。
entries.en: The choice had been announced, but no edict had followed.
entries.literal: The intent had been proclaimed but the edict had not yet been issued.

entries.zh: 時左遷者多追賜死，友珪益恐。
entries.en: Many recently demoted men were hunted down and forced to die; Yougui's fear deepened.
entries.literal: At that time many demoted officials were pursued and granted death; Yougui grew more fearful.

entries.zh: 戊寅，友珪易服微行入 左龍虎軍，見統軍韓勍，以情告之。
entries.en: On wuyin Yougui went in disguise to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, confided in commander Han Qin, and laid bare his fear.
entries.literal: On wuyin Yougui changed clothes and went in secret to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, saw Commander-in-Chief Han Qin, and told him his plight.

entries.zh: 勍亦見功臣宿將多以小過被誅，懼不自保，遂相與合謀。
entries.en: Qin too had seen meritorious officers killed for trifles and feared for himself; they took counsel together.
entries.literal: Qin also saw meritorious generals and veteran officers often executed for small faults and feared he could not preserve himself; they then plotted together.

entries.zh: 勍以牙兵五百人從友珪雜控鶴士入，伏於禁中；
entries.en: Qin brought five hundred guardsmen; Yougui mixed them with the Crane-Controlled troops and hid them inside the palace;
entries.literal: Qin led five hundred guardsmen to follow Yougui mixed among the Crane-Controlled troops into the palace; they lay in ambush within the forbidden precinct;

entries.zh: 夜斬關入，至寢殿，侍疾者皆散走。
entries.en: At night they forced the gate and reached the sleeping hall; attendants scattered.
entries.literal: At night they broke through the gate and reached the sleeping hall; those attending the sick all fled.

entries.zh: 帝驚起，問：「反者為誰？」
entries.en: The Emperor roused himself and cried: "Who rebels?"
entries.literal: The Emperor started up and asked: "Who are the rebels?"

entries.zh: 友珪曰：「非他人也。」
entries.en: Yougui said: "No other."
entries.literal: Yougui said: "It is no other."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「我固疑此賊，恨不早殺之。
entries.en: The Emperor said: "I long suspected this villain—only regret I did not kill him sooner.
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "I always suspected this villain—regret I did not kill him sooner.

entries.zh: 汝悖逆如此，天地豈容汝乎！」
entries.en: You rebel thus—Heaven and Earth will not bear you!"
entries.literal: You are so rebellious—how could Heaven and Earth tolerate you!"

entries.zh: 友珪曰：「老賊萬段！」
entries.en: Yougui cried: "Old thief, ten thousand cuts!"
entries.literal: Yougui said: "Old villain, ten thousand cuts!"

entries.zh: 友珪僕夫馮廷諤刺帝腹，刃出於背。
entries.en: Yougui's groom Feng Tingyu drove a blade into the Emperor's belly until it showed at his back.
entries.literal: Yougui’s servant Feng Tingyu stabbed the Emperor in the belly; the blade came out his back.

entries.zh: 友珪自以敗氈裹之，瘞於寢殿，秘不發喪。
entries.en: Yougui himself wrapped the body in a cast-off rug, buried it in the hall, and concealed the death.
entries.literal: Yougui himself wrapped the corpse in a worn rug, buried it in the sleeping hall, and kept the death secret.

entries.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
entries.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
entries.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

entries.zh: 己卯，矯詔稱：「博王友文謀逆，遣兵突入殿中，賴郢王友珮忠孝，將兵誅之，保全朕躬。
entries.en: On jimao a forged edict read: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted revolt and burst into the hall with troops; Prince of Ying Yougui, loyal and filial, led forces to execute them and saved Us.
entries.literal: On jimao a forged edict stated: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted rebellion and sent troops bursting into the hall; thanks to Prince of Ying Yougui’s loyalty and filial piety, who led troops to execute them and preserved Our person.

entries.zh: 然疾因震驚，彌致危殆，宜令友珪權主軍國之務。」
entries.en: Shock has worsened Our illness—let Yougui govern state and army affairs for now."
entries.literal: Yet the illness from shock grows critical—let Yougui provisionally direct state and military affairs."

entries.zh: 韓勍為友珪謀，多出府庫金帛，賜諸軍及百官以取悅。
entries.en: Han Qin schemed for him, emptying much gold and silk from the treasury to buy the armies and the officials.
entries.literal: Han Qin plotted for Yougui, taking much gold and silk from the treasury to bestow on the armies and the hundred officials to win favor.

entries.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
entries.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
entries.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

entries.zh: 友珪葬太祖于伊闕縣，號宣陵。
entries.en: Yougui buried Taizu at Yique, naming the tomb Xuan.
entries.literal: Yougui buried Taizu in Yique County, titled the tomb Xuan Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 《五代史補》：太祖硃全忠，黃巢之先鋒。
entries.en: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Taizu Zhu Quanzhong was Huang Chao's vanguard.
entries.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Taizu Zhu Quanzhong was vanguard of Huang Chao.

entries.zh: 巢入長安，以刺史王鐸圍同州，太祖遂降，鐸承制拜同州刺史。
entries.en: When Chao took Chang'an, Wang Duo besieged Tongzhou; Taizu surrendered, and Duo, with imperial warrant, made him prefect of Tong.
entries.literal: When Chao entered Chang’an, Wang Duo besieged Tongzhou; Taizu then surrendered and Duo, acting on imperial order, appointed him prefect of Tong.

entries.zh: 黃巢滅，淮、蔡間秦宗權復盛，朝廷以淮、蔡與汴州相接，太祖汴人，必究其能否，遂移授宣武軍節度使以討宗權，未凡滅之。
entries.en: After Huang Chao fell, Qin Zongquan rose again between Huai and Cai; because those regions marched with Bian and Taizu was a native of Bian, the court had to try him and transferred him as Xuanwu commissioner to destroy Zongquan—which he soon did.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao was destroyed, Qin Zongquan revived his strength between Huai and Cai; the court, because Huai and Cai bordered Bianzhou and Taizu was a man of Bian, was bound to test his ability, and so transferred him as Xuanwu Military Commissioner to attack Zongquan; before long he destroyed him.

entries.zh: 自是威福由己，朝廷不能制，遂有天下。
entries.en: Thereafter he held power in his own hands and the court could not restrain him until he possessed the realm.
entries.literal: From then on power and favor were his own and the court could not control him; he then possessed the realm.

entries.zh: 先是，民間傳讖曰：「五公符」，又謂之「李淳風轉天歌」，其字有「八牛之年」，識者以「八牛」乃「硃」字，則太祖革命之應焉。
entries.en: Earlier folk prophecy spoke of "Five Lords' tally," also called Li Chunfeng's Turning Heaven Song, containing "the year of eight oxen"—readers saw eight oxen as the character Zhu, presaging Taizu's rise.
entries.literal: Earlier the people had transmitted a prophecy saying "Five Lords tally," also called the "Li Chunfeng Turning Heaven Song"; its characters had "the year of eight oxen"—those who understood took "eight oxen" as the character Zhu—thus the omen of Taizu’s revolution.

entries.zh: 太祖之用兵也，法令嚴峻，每戰，逐隊主帥或有沒而不反者，其餘皆斬之，謂之：「跋隊斬」。
entries.en: Taizu's armies were ruled by harsh law: when a unit commander fell and did not return, his whole unit was beheaded—this was called "beheading the straggler."
entries.literal: In Taizu’s use of troops the laws were stern; in each battle if a unit commander was lost and did not return, the rest were all beheaded—called "beheading the straggling unit."

entries.zh: 自是戰無不勝。
entries.en: From then on his battles knew no defeat.
entries.literal: From then on in battle there was no not winning.

entries.zh: 然健兒且多竄匿州郡，疲於追捕，因下令文面，健兒文面自此始也。
entries.en: Yet able men often hid among the prefectures, exhausted from pursuit—so he ordered facial brands, and the branding of strong soldiers began.
entries.literal: Yet strong soldiers often hid in prefectures and counties, weary of pursuit; therefore he ordered facial tattooing—facial tattooing of strong soldiers began here.

entries.zh: 《五代史闕文》：世傳梁太祖迎昭宗於鳳翔，素服待罪，昭宗佯為鞋系脫，呼梁祖曰：「全忠為吾系鞋。」
entries.en: 《Lost Passages》: Tradition says that when Liang Taizu welcomed Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang, he wore plain dress to await punishment; Zhaozong feigned a loose shoe-thong and called: "Quanzhong, tie my shoe for me."
entries.literal: 《Lost Passages of the History of the Five Dynasties》: The world transmits that when Liang Taizu welcomed Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang, in plain clothes he awaited punishment; Zhaozong pretended his shoe thong came loose and called Liang Taizu: "Quanzhong, tie my shoe for me."

entries.zh: 梁祖不得已，跪而結之，汗流浹背。
entries.en: Liang Taizu could only kneel to tie it, sweat soaking his back.
entries.literal: Liang Taizu had no choice but to kneel and tie it; sweat streamed down his back.

entries.zh: 時天子扈蹕尚有衛兵，昭宗意謂左右擒梁祖以殺之，其如無敢動者。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven's escort still had guards; Zhaozong hoped those beside him would seize Taizu and kill him—yet none dared.
entries.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven’s progress still had guard troops; Zhaozong’s intent was that those beside him seize Liang Taizu and kill him—but none dared move.

entries.zh: 自是梁祖被召多不至，盡去昭宗禁衛，皆用汴人矣。
entries.en: Thereafter Taizu often ignored summons; he stripped Zhaozong of every palace guard and replaced them with men from Bian.
entries.literal: From then on when Liang Taizu was summoned he often did not come; he removed all Zhaozong’s forbidden guards and used only men of Bian.

entries.zh: 臣謹案：梁祖以天復三年迎唐昭宗於岐下，歲在甲子，其年改天祐，至國初建隆庚申歲，才五十六年矣，然則乾德七十歲人皆目睹其事。
entries.en: This commentator notes: Liang Taizu in Tianfu year 3 welcomed Tang Emperor Zhaozong from below Qi in the jiazi year, then Tianyou; from Jianlong's founding gengshen to our day is only fifty-six years—yet men of seventy in the Qiande era saw it with their own eyes.
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: Liang Taizu in the third year of Tianfu welcomed Tang Emperor Zhaozong from below Qi—year jiazi; that year was changed to Tianyou; from the founding of the state in the gengshen year of Jianlong it was only fifty-six years—yet people of the Qiande era, seventy years old, all witnessed the affair.

entries.zh: 蓋唐室自懿宗失政，天下亂離，故武宗以下實錄，不傳於世。
entries.en: From Tang Yizong's loss of rule the realm shattered; veritable records from Wuzong down no longer circulated.
entries.literal: It is that from Emperor Yizong of Tang the government was lost and the realm torn apart; therefore veritable records from Emperor Wuzong down were not transmitted in the world.

entries.zh: 昭宗一朝，全無記注。
entries.en: Zhaozong's entire reign left no record whatsoever.
entries.literal: For Zhaozong’s entire reign there was no record at all.

entries.zh: 梁祖在位止及六年，均帝朝詔史臣修梁祖實錄，岐下系鞋之事，恥而不書。
entries.en: Taizu reigned only six years; under Emperor Jun historians were ordered to compile his veritable record—yet the shoe-tying at Qi was too shameful to write.
entries.literal: Liang Taizu reigned only six years; in Emperor Jun’s reign an edict ordered historians to compile Taizu’s veritable record—the affair of tying shoes below Qi was shameful and not written.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，史臣張昭重修《唐史》，始有《昭宗本紀》，但雲即位之始，有《會昌》之風，岐陽事蹟，不能追補。
entries.en: In Jin's Tianfu era Zhang Zhao revised the Tang history and added Annals of Emperor Zhaozong, noting only Huichang-era style at his accession—affairs at Qi-yang could not be recovered.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, historian Zhang Zhao revised the 《History of Tang》, and only then was there 《Annals of Emperor Zhaozong》, but it said only that at the beginning of his reign there was the style of the Huichang era; affairs at Qi-yang could not be pursued and supplemented.

entries.zh: 此亦明唐昭宗有英睿之氣，而衰運不振；
entries.en: This shows that Zhaozong had keen spirit, yet declining fortune would not turn;
entries.literal: This also shows that Tang Emperor Zhaozong had keen and discerning spirit, yet the declining fortune did not revive;

entries.zh: 又明左右無忠義奮發之臣，致梁祖得行其志。
entries.en: and that none beside him were loyal enough to strike, so Taizu could do as he pleased.
entries.literal: it also shows that those beside him had no loyal and righteous ministers who would rise up, so Liang Taizu could carry out his will.

entries.zh: 有所警誡，不可不書。
entries.en: There is a lesson here, and it must be written.
entries.literal: There is warning in this—it must not go unwritten.

entries.zh: 乾化二年正月，宣：「上元夜，任諸市及坊市各點彩燈，金吾不用禁夜。」
entries.en: In the first month of Qianhua 2, the court proclaimed: "On Lantern Festival night, every market and ward may hang colored lamps; the Jinwu need not enforce the curfew."
entries.literal: In the first month of Qianhua 2, an announcement stated: "On the Lantern Festival night, let every market and ward hang colored lamps; the Jinwu need not enforce the curfew."

entries.zh: 近年以來，以都下聚兵太廣，未嘗令坊市點燈故也。
entries.en: In recent years, with too many troops concentrated at the capital, the wards had not been allowed to light lamps—that was the reason.
entries.literal: In recent years, because troops massed at the capital were too numerous, the wards had never been allowed to light lamps—that is why.

entries.zh: 甲申，以時雪久愆，命丞相及三省官群望祈禱。
entries.en: On jiashen, with timely snow long overdue, the Emperor ordered the chancellor and officials of the Three Departments to pray at the various altars.
entries.literal: On jiashen, because timely snow had long been lacking, the chancellor and officials of the Three Departments were ordered to pray at the various altars.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「謗木求規，集囊貢事，將裨理道，豈限側言。
entries.en: An edict read: "The slander-wood seeks counsel; the bag gathers reports—all to aid governance. Why limit oneself to oblique speech?
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The slander-wood seeks counsel; the bag gathers matters—this will aid governance; how could it be limited to oblique words?

entries.zh: 應內外文武百官及草澤，並許上封事，極言得失。」
entries.en: Civil and military officials within and without, and commoners alike, may submit sealed memorials and speak freely of what is right and wrong."
entries.literal: All civil and military officials inside and outside, and commoners, are permitted to submit sealed memorials and speak fully of gains and losses."

entries.zh: 以丁審衢為陳州，而審衢厚以鞍馬、金帛為謝恩之獻，帝慮其漁民，復其獻而停之。
entries.en: Ding Shenqu was appointed prefect of Chenzhou; he sent lavish gifts of saddles, horses, and silks in thanks for the appointment. Fearing he would fleece the people, the Emperor returned the gifts and refused them.
entries.literal: Ding Shenqu was appointed to Chenzhou, but Shenqu lavishly offered saddles, horses, and silks as thanks for grace; the Emperor, fearing he preyed on the people, returned the gifts and stopped him.

entries.zh: 封保義節度使王檀為琅琊郡王。
entries.en: Baoyi Military Commissioner Wang Tan was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya.
entries.literal: Baoyi Military Commissioner Wang Tan was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya Commandery.

entries.zh: 命供奉官硃嶠于河南府宣取先收禁定州進奉官崔騰並傔從一十四人，並釋放，仍命押領送至貝。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered Palace Attendant Zhu Qiao to proclaim at Henan Prefecture the release of detained Dingzhou tribute officer Cui Teng and his fourteen attendants, and had them escorted to Bei.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Palace Attendant Zhu Qiao to proclaim at Henan Prefecture the release of the detained Dingzhou tribute officer Cui Teng and fourteen attendants, and still ordered them escorted to Bei.

entries.zh: 騰，唐戶部侍郎潔之子也。
entries.en: He was the son of Tang Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Jie.
entries.literal: Teng was the son of Tang Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Jie.

entries.zh: 廣明喪亂，客于北諸侯，為定州節度使王處存所辟，去載領貢獻至闕。
entries.en: During the Guangming upheaval he had lived among northern lords; Wang Chucun, military commissioner of Dingzhou, had recruited him, and the year before he had led tribute to court.
entries.literal: In the Guangming turmoil he sojourned among northern lords, was recruited by Dingzhou Military Commissioner Wang Chucun, and last year led tribute to court.

entries.zh: 未幾，其帥稱兵，遂縶之。
entries.en: Before long his commander rebelled and had him imprisoned.
entries.literal: Before long his commander raised troops and imprisoned him.

entries.zh: 至是，帝念賓介之來，又已出境，特命縱而歸焉。
entries.en: Now the Emperor, mindful that a guest envoy had come and had already crossed the border, specially ordered his release and return home.
entries.literal: At this time the Emperor, mindful that a guest envoy had come and had already left the border, specially ordered him released and sent home.

entries.zh: 丙戌，有司以孟春太廟薦享上言，命丞相杜曉攝祭行事。
entries.en: On bingxu the court reported on the spring ancestral offering; the Emperor had Chancellor Du Xiao conduct the rite in his stead.
entries.literal: On bingxu the authorities memorialized on the first-spring offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Emperor ordered Chancellor Du Xiao to perform the rites as proxy.

entries.zh: 丙申夕，熒惑犯房第二星。
entries.en: On the night of bingshen, Mars encroached on the second star of the Fang asterism.
entries.literal: On the night of bingshen, Mars trespassed the second star of Fang.

entries.zh: 二月庚戌，中和節，御崇勳殿，召丞相、大學士、河南尹，略封訖，于萬春門外廡賜以酒食。
entries.en: On gengxu in the second month, the Zhonghe Festival, the Emperor presided at Chongxun Hall, summoned the chancellor, Grand Academicians, and Henan Intendant; after the brief audience he bestowed food and drink in the corridor outside Wanchun Gate.
entries.literal: On gengxu in the second month, the Zhonghe Festival, the Emperor presided at Chongxun Hall, summoned the chancellor, Grand Academicians, and Henan Intendant, finished the brief audience, and bestowed food and drink in the corridor outside Wanchun Gate.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》，二月，追封故魏博節度使羅宏信為趙王。
entries.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the second month the court posthumously enfeoffed the late Weibo commissioner Luo Hongxin as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the second month the late Weibo Military Commissioner Luo Hongxin was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 癸丑，敕曰：「今載春寒頗甚，雨澤仍愆，司天監占以夏秋必多霖潦，宜令所在郡縣告喻百姓，備淫雨之患。」
entries.en: On guichou an order read: "This year spring cold is severe and rain still lacking; the Directorate of Astronomy divines heavy rains in summer and autumn—let every prefecture and county warn the people to prepare for floods."
entries.literal: On guichou an order stated: "This year spring cold is quite severe and rain still lacking; the Directorate of Astronomy divines that summer and autumn will see much flood—let every prefecture and county inform the people to guard against excessive rain."

entries.zh: 庚申，禦宣威殿開宴，丞相洎文武官屬咸被召列侍，竟日而罷。
entries.en: On gengshen the Emperor held a banquet at Xuanwei Hall; the chancellor and all civil and military officials were summoned to attend in rows until evening.
entries.literal: On gengshen the Emperor held a banquet at Xuanwei Hall; the chancellor and civil and military officials were all summoned to attend in rows until day’s end.

entries.zh: 壬戌，帝將巡按北境，中外戒嚴，詔以河南尹、守中書令、判六軍事張宗奭為大內留守。
entries.en: On renxu, as the Emperor prepared to inspect the northern border, court and realm went on alert; Zhang Zongshi, Henan intendant, keeper of the Secretariat, and director of the Six Armies, was named Grand Inner Custodian.
entries.literal: On renxu the Emperor was about to tour the northern frontier; court and country were placed on alert; an edict appointed Henan Intendant, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Director of the Six Armies Zhang Zongshi Grand Inner Custodian.

entries.zh: 中書門下奏，差定文武官領務尤切宜扈駕者三十八人。
entries.en: The Secretariat memorialized, naming thirty-eight civil and military officials whose duties were especially urgent and who should attend the imperial progress.
entries.literal: The Secretariat memorialized, fixing thirty-eight civil and military officials whose duties were especially urgent and who should attend the imperial progress.

entries.zh: 詔工部尚書李皎、左散騎常侍孫騭、右諫議大夫張衍、兵部侍郎劉邈、兵部郎中張俊、光祿少卿盧秉彝並令扈蹕。
entries.en: By edict Li Jiao, minister of works, Sun Zhi, left regular attendant, Zhang Yan, right remonstrator, Liu Miao, vice minister of war, Zhang Jun, war bureau director, and Lu Bingyi, vice director of imperial sacrifices, were all ordered on the progress.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Works Li Jiao, Left Regular Attendant Sun Zhi, Right Remonstrance Official Zhang Yan, Vice Minister of War Liu Miao, War Bureau Director Zhang Jun, and Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Bingyi all to attend the progress.

entries.zh: 甲子，發自洛師，夕次河陽。
entries.en: On jiazi he left Luoyang and stopped at Heyang that night.
entries.literal: On jiazi he set out from Luoyang and halted at Heyang that evening.
