entries.zh: 《通鑒》云：至白馬屯，賜從官食，多未至，遣騎趣之于路。
entries.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Reaching Baima Station, he bestowed food on attending officials; many had not arrived, and he sent riders to hurry them along the road.
entries.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Reaching Baima Station, he bestowed food on attending officials; many had not arrived, and he sent riders to hurry them on the road.

entries.zh: 左散騎常侍孫騭、右諫議大夫張衍、兵部郎中張俊最後至，帝命撲殺之。
entries.en: Sun Zhi, Zhang Yan, and Zhang Jun came late; the Emperor had them beaten to death.
entries.literal: Left Regular Attendant Sun Zhi, Right Remonstrance Official Zhang Yan, and War Bureau Director Zhang Jun arrived last; the Emperor ordered them beaten to death.

entries.zh: 乙丑，次溫縣。
entries.en: On yichou he stopped at Wen County.
entries.literal: On yichou he halted at Wen County.

entries.zh: 丙寅，次武陟。
entries.en: On bingyin he stopped at Wuzhi.
entries.literal: On bingyin he halted at Wuzhi.

entries.zh: 懷州刺史段明遠迎拜於境上，其內外所備，咸豐霈焉。
entries.en: Duan Mingyuan, inspector of Huai Prefecture, met him at the border with obeisance; supplies within and without were lavish beyond measure.
entries.literal: Huai Prefecture Inspector Duan Mingyuan met and bowed at the border; all provisions inside and out were abundantly lavish.

entries.zh: 丁卯，次獲嘉。
entries.en: On dingmao he stopped at Huojia.
entries.literal: On dingmao he halted at Huojia.

entries.zh: 戊辰，次衛州之新鄉。
entries.en: On wuchen he stopped at Xinxiang in Weizhou.
entries.literal: On wuchen he halted at Xinxiang in Weizhou.

entries.zh: 己巳，晨發衛州，夕止淇門，內衙十將使以十指揮兵士至於行在。
entries.en: On jisi he left Weizhou in the morning and camped at Qimen that evening; Inner Palace Ten Generals marched their commands to the imperial camp.
entries.literal: On jisi he set out from Weizhou in the morning and halted at Qimen in the evening; Inner Palace Ten Generals led soldiers by the tens to the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 辛未，駐蹕黎陽。
entries.en: On xinwei he encamped at Liyang.
entries.literal: On xinwei he halted at Liyang.

entries.zh: 癸酉，發自黎陽，夕次內黃。
entries.en: On guiyou he left Liyang and camped at Neihuang that night.
entries.literal: On guiyou he set out from Liyang and halted at Neihuang that evening.

entries.zh: 甲戌，次昌樂縣。
entries.en: On jiaxu he stopped at Changle County.
entries.literal: On jiaxu he halted at Changle County.

entries.zh: 丁丑，次於永濟縣。
entries.en: On dingchou he stopped at Yongji County.
entries.literal: On dingchou he halted at Yongji County.

entries.zh: 青州節度使賀德倫奏，統領兵士赴曆亭軍前。
entries.en: He Delun, Qingzhou commissioner, reported that he was marching his forces to Liting.
entries.literal: Qingzhou Military Commissioner He Delun memorialized that he was leading troops to the front at Liting.

entries.zh: 戊寅，至貝州，命四丞相及學士李琪、盧文度、知制誥竇賞等十五人扈從，其左常侍韋戩等二十三人止焉。
entries.en: On wuyin he reached Beizhou and ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend; Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained behind.
entries.literal: On wuyin he reached Beizhou, ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend, while Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained.

entries.zh: 己卯，發自貝州，夕駐蹕於野落。
entries.en: On jimao he set out from Beizhou and camped that evening in the open country.
entries.literal: On jimao he set out from Beizhou and halted that evening in the open country.

entries.zh: 三月庚辰朔，次於棗強縣之西城。
entries.en: On gengchen, the first of the third month, he halted at the west city of Zaoqiang County.
entries.literal: On the first day of the third month, gengchen, he halted at the west city of Zaoqiang County.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》：辛巳，至下博南，登觀津塚。
entries.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On xinsi he came to south of Xiabo and ascended Guanjin Mound.
entries.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On xinsi he reached south of Xiabo and climbed Guanjin Mound.

entries.zh: 趙將符暕引數百騎巡邏，不知是帝，遽前逼之。
entries.en: Zhao general Fu Yan led several hundred horsemen on patrol, did not recognize the Emperor, and suddenly pressed forward.
entries.literal: Zhao general Fu Yan led several hundred horsemen on patrol, did not know it was the Emperor, and suddenly pressed forward.

entries.zh: 或告曰：「晉兵大至矣！」
entries.en: Someone cried: "Jin troops are upon us in force!"
entries.literal: Someone reported: "Jin troops have arrived in great numbers!"

entries.zh: 帝行幄，亟引兵趣棗強，與楊師厚軍合。
entries.en: The Emperor quit his camp, hurried his troops toward Zaoqiang, and united with Yang Shihou's army.
entries.literal: The Emperor left his traveling pavilion, hastily led troops toward Zaoqiang, and joined Yang Shihou’s army.

entries.zh: 丙戌，鎮、定諸軍招討使楊師厚奏下棗強縣，車駕即日疾馳南還。
entries.en: On bingxu Zhen and Ding Pacification Commissioner Yang Shihou memorialized that Zaoqiang County had fallen; the imperial carriage galloped south that same day.
entries.literal: On bingxu Zhen and Ding Pacification Commissioner Yang Shihou memorialized that Zaoqiang County had fallen; the imperial carriage that day galloped south.

entries.zh: 丁亥，復至貝州。
entries.en: On dinghai he was back at Beizhou.
entries.literal: On dinghai he returned to Beizhou.

entries.zh: 庚寅，楊師厚與副招討李周彝等准詔來朝。
entries.en: On gengyin Yang Shihou, deputy pacifier Li Zhouyi, and others presented themselves at court by edict.
entries.literal: On gengyin Yang Shihou and Deputy Pacifier Li Zhouyi and others came to court as ordered.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔丞相、翰林六學士、文武從官、都招討使及諸軍統指揮使等，賜食於行殿。
entries.en: On xinmao an edict ordered the chancellor, Hanlin Six Academicians, civil and military attendants, Grand Pacification Commissioner, and unified army commanders to be feasted at the traveling hall.
entries.literal: On xinmao an edict ordered the chancellor, Hanlin Six Academicians, civil and military attendants, Grand Pacification Commissioner, and unified army commanders to be given food at the traveling hall.

entries.zh: 壬辰，命以羊酒等各賜從官。
entries.en: On renchen he had mutton and wine distributed to each attending official.
entries.literal: On renchen he ordered mutton and wine given separately to attending officials.

entries.zh: 甲午，幸貝州之東闉閱武。
entries.en: On jiawu he went to Beizhou's east gate to review the army.
entries.literal: On jiawu he visited the east gate of Beizhou to review troops.

entries.zh: 乙未，帝復幸東闉閱騎軍。
entries.en: On yiwei he again went to the east gate to review the cavalry.
entries.literal: On yiwei the Emperor again visited the east gate to review the cavalry.

entries.zh: 敕以攻下棗強縣有功將校杜暉等一十一人，並超加檢校官，衙官宋彥等二十五人並超授軍職。
entries.en: An order promoted eleven officers distinguished in taking Zaoqiang, including Du Hui, with supernumerary inspector ranks, and gave twenty-five yamen officers including Song Yan higher military posts.
entries.literal: An order stated that eleven meritorious officers in the capture of Zaoqiang County, including Du Hui, were all given supernumerary inspector ranks, and twenty-five yamen officers including Song Yan were all promoted in military office.

entries.zh: 丙午，次濟源縣。
entries.en: On bingwu he stopped at Jiyuan County.
entries.literal: On bingwu he halted at Jiyuan County.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「淑律將遷，亢陽頗甚，宜令魏州差官祈禱龍潭。」
entries.en: An edict read: "The harmonious pitch is about to shift and drought is severe—let Weizhou dispatch officials to pray at Dragon Pool."
entries.literal: An edict stated: "The harmonious pitch is about to shift and drought yang is quite severe—let Weizhou dispatch officials to pray at Dragon Pool."

entries.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「雨澤愆期，祈禱未應，宜令宰臣各于魏州靈祠精加祈禱。」
entries.en: On wushen an edict read: "Rain is overdue and prayers unanswered—let each chancellor pray with utmost care at the spirit shrines of Weizhou."
entries.literal: On wushen an edict stated: "Rain is overdue and prayers unanswered—let each chancellor at Weizhou spirit shrines pray with utmost care."

entries.zh: 《五代會要》：三月，詔曰：「夫隆興邦國，必本於人民；
entries.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the third month an edict read: "To uplift a state one must be rooted in the people;
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the third month an edict stated: "To uplift a state must be rooted in the people;

entries.zh: 惠養疲羸，凡資於令長。
entries.en: nurturing the exhausted and feeble falls wholly to local magistrates.
entries.literal: to nurture the weary and weak depends entirely on magistrates.

entries.zh: 苟選求之逾濫，固撫理之乖違。
entries.en: If appointments are excessive, governance will surely go astray.
entries.literal: If selection is excessive, governance will surely go astray.

entries.zh: 如聞吏部擬官，中書除授，或緣親舊所請，或為勢要所幹，姑徇私情，靡求才實，念茲蠹弊，宜舉條章。
entries.en: We hear that appointments proposed by the Ministry of Personnel and confirmed by the Secretariat often follow kin or patrons, favor private ties over merit—this abuse must be met with clear rules.
entries.literal: We hear that when the Ministry of Personnel proposes offices and the Secretariat appoints, sometimes through kin and friends’ requests, sometimes through powerful men’s intercession—they indulge private feeling and do not seek real talent; mindful of this corruption, regulations should be promulgated.

entries.zh: 今後應中書用人及吏部注擬，並宜省籓身之才業，驗為政之否臧，必有可觀，方可任用。
entries.en: Hereafter for Secretariat appointments and Ministry nominations, all should examine the candidate’s talent and verify whether his governance was good or bad—only if there is merit may he be employed.
entries.literal: Hereafter for Secretariat appointments and Ministry nominations, all should examine the candidate’s talent and verify whether his governance was good or bad—only if there is something to be seen may he be employed.

entries.zh: 如或尚行請說，猶假貨財，其所司人吏，必當推窮，重加懲斷。」
entries.en: Should solicitation or bribery continue, responsible officials are to investigate fully and punish without mercy."
entries.literal: If anyone still practices solicitation or lends goods and money, the responsible clerks must be thoroughly investigated and punished severely."

entries.zh: 四月己酉，幸魏州。
entries.en: On jiyou in the fourth month he went to Weizhou.
entries.literal: On jiyou in the fourth month he visited Weizhou.

entries.zh: 金波亭，賜宴宰臣、文武官及六學士。
entries.en: At Jinbo Pavilion he feasted the chancellors, the civil and military officials, and the Six Academicians.
entries.literal: At Jinbo Pavilion he gave a feast to chancellors, civil and military officials, and the Six Academicians.

entries.zh: 甲寅夕，月掩心大星。
entries.en: On jiayin night the moon occulted the great star of Heart.
entries.literal: On the night of jiayin the moon occulted the great star of Heart.

entries.zh: 丙辰，敕：「近者星辰違度，式在修禳，宜令兩京及宋州、魏州取此月至五月禁斷屠宰。
entries.en: On bingchen an order read: "Recently the stars have gone out of their courses—rectification lies in ritual prayer; let the two capitals and Songzhou and Weizhou from this month through the fifth month forbid slaughter.
entries.literal: On bingchen an order stated: "Recently the stars have gone out of their courses—rectification lies in ritual prayer; let the two capitals and Songzhou and Weizhou from this month through the fifth month forbid slaughter.

entries.zh: 仍各於佛寺開建道場，以迎福應。」
entries.en: Let each also establish ritual platforms at Buddhist temples to welcome blessings."
entries.literal: Still let each establish ritual platforms at Buddhist temples to welcome blessings."

entries.zh: 己未，次黎陽縣。
entries.en: On jiwei he stopped at Liyang County.
entries.literal: On jiwei he halted at Liyang County.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》：乙卯，博王友文來朝，請帝還東都。
entries.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On yimao the Prince of Bo, Youwen, attended court and urged the Emperor to return east.
entries.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On yimao Prince of Bo Youwen came to court and asked the Emperor to return to the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 丁巳，發魏州。
entries.en: On dingsi he departed Weizhou.
entries.literal: On dingsi he set out from Weizhou.

entries.zh: 己未，至黎陽，以疾淹留。
entries.en: On jiwei he came to Liyang and stayed on, held up by sickness.
entries.literal: On jiwei he reached Liyang and lingered there because of illness.

entries.zh: 東都留守官吏奉表起居，賜丞相、從官酒食有差。
entries.en: Custodian officials at the Eastern Capital sent memorials of greeting; chancellor and attendants received graded gifts of food and drink.
entries.literal: Eastern Capital custodian officials presented memorials of inquiry; the chancellor and attending officials were given food and drink in varying measure.

entries.zh: 己巳，至東都，博王友文以新創食殿上言，並進準備內宴錢三千貫、銀器一千五百兩。
entries.en: On jisi he arrived at the Eastern Capital; Prince of Bo Youwen reported on the new Dining Hall and presented three thousand strings of cash and fifteen hundred taels of silver for an inner banquet.
entries.literal: On jisi he reached the Eastern Capital; Prince of Bo Youwen memorialized on the newly built Dining Hall and also presented three thousand strings of cash and fifteen hundred taels of silverware prepared for an inner banquet.

entries.zh: 辛未，宴於食殿，召丞相及文武從官等侍焉。
entries.en: On xinwei he banqueted at the Dining Hall and summoned the chancellor and civil and military attendants to attend.
entries.literal: On xinwei he banqueted at the Dining Hall and summoned the chancellor and civil and military attendants to serve.

entries.zh: 帝泛九曲池，御舟傾，帝墮溺于池中，宮女侍官扶持登岸，驚悸久之。
entries.en: The Emperor rowed on Nine-Bend Pool; the imperial boat capsized and he fell into the water; palace women and attendants helped him ashore, and he remained shaken for a long time.
entries.literal: The Emperor rowed on Nine-Bend Pool; the imperial boat capsized and the Emperor fell into the pool; palace women and attending officials supported him ashore, and he was shaken for a long time.

entries.zh: 制加建昌宮使、金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、開封尹、博王友文為特進、檢校太保，兼開封尹，依前建昌宮使，充東都留守。
entries.en: By order Youwen, Prince of Bo, Jianchang palace commissioner, golden-seal grand master of splendid happiness, honorary grand mentor, and Kaifeng intendant, was raised to special court attendance and honorary grand guardian, kept Kaifeng intendant, and remained Jianchang commissioner and Eastern Capital custodian.
entries.literal: An order advanced Jianchang Palace Commissioner, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Honorary Grand Mentor, Kaifeng Intendant, and Prince of Bo Youwen to Special Court Attendance and Honorary Grand Guardian, also Kaifeng Intendant, continuing as Jianchang Palace Commissioner and Eastern Capital Custodian.

entries.zh: 戊寅，車駕發自東京，夕次中牟縣。
entries.en: On wuyin the imperial train left the Eastern Capital and camped at Zhongmou that evening.
entries.literal: On wuyin the imperial carriage set out from the Eastern Capital and halted at Zhongmou County that evening.

entries.zh: 己丑，魏博軍亂，囚節度使賀德倫。
entries.en: On jichou Weibo troops rebelled and seized He Delun.
entries.literal: On jichou the Weibo army mutinied and imprisoned Military Commissioner He Delun.

entries.zh: 是時，朝廷既分魏博六州為兩鎮，命劉鄩統大軍屯於南樂，以討王熔為名，遣澶州刺史、行營先鋒步軍都指揮使王彥章領龍驤五百騎先入於魏州，屯於金波亭。
entries.en: The court had split Weibo, sent Liu Yan to Nanle ostensibly against Wang Rong, and Wang Yanzhang with five hundred Dragon-Prancing horse into Weizhou to camp at Jinbo Pavilion.
entries.literal: The court had divided Weibo's six prefectures into two commands, ordered Liu Yan to lead the great army at Nanle in the name of attacking Wang Rong, and sent Cizhou Military Commissioner and campaign vanguard foot commander Wang Yanzhang with five hundred Dragon-Prancing cavalry into Weizhou first, encamped at Jinbo Pavilion.

entries.zh: 詔以魏州軍兵之半隸於相州，並徙其家焉。
entries.en: Half of Weizhou's soldiers were assigned to Xiangzhou and their families moved with them.
entries.literal: An edict placed half of Weizhou's troops under Xiangzhou and moved their families as well.

entries.zh: 又遣主者檢察魏之帑廩。
entries.en: Auditors were sent to inventory Weibo's stores.
entries.literal: Inspectors were also sent to examine Weibo's treasuries.

entries.zh: 既而德倫促諸軍上路，姻族辭決，哭聲盈巷。
entries.en: Delun ordered the troops on the road; families wailed in every street.
entries.literal: Then Delun urged the armies to march; kin took leave with weeping that filled the lanes.

entries.zh: 其徒乃相聚而謀曰：「朝廷以我軍府強盛，故設法殘破，況我六州，歷代藩府，軍門父子，姻族相連，未嘗遠出河門，離親去族，一旦遷於外郡，生不如死。」
entries.en: They muttered: "The court means to break us because we are strong; six generations we held the gate, kin in every company—never sent beyond Hemen—and now they tear us away; death is kinder."
entries.literal: The men then gathered and plotted: "The court, because our command is strong, contrived to ruin us; moreover our six prefectures for generations were a frontier command—fathers and sons in the army, kin by marriage—never far from Hemen, never leaving kin; suddenly to move to outer commands—better dead than alive."

entries.zh: 三月二十九日夜，魏軍乃作亂，放火大掠，首攻龍驤軍，王彥章斬關而遁。
entries.en: On the twenty-ninth of the third month Weibo rose, burned, and looted; they struck Dragon-Prancing first; Wang Yanzhang hacked his way out and escaped.
entries.literal: On the night of the twenty-ninth of the third month the Weibo troops mutinied, set fires, and plundered greatly; they first attacked the Dragon-Prancing Army; Wang Yanzhang cut through the gate and fled.

entries.zh: 遲明，殺德倫親軍五百餘人於牙城，執德倫置之樓上。
entries.en: At dawn they slaughtered five hundred of Delun's guard at headquarters and held him on the tower.
entries.literal: At dawn they killed more than five hundred of Delun's personal guard at the headquarters and seized Delun on the tower.

entries.zh: 有效節軍校張彥者，最為粗暴，膽氣伏人，乃率無賴輩數百，止其剽掠。
entries.en: Zhang Yan, a brutal officer who cowed the host, rallied hundreds of ruffians and halted the sack.
entries.literal: A valiant command officer Zhang Yan, most violent, whose courage subdued men, then led several hundred ruffians and stopped the pillage.

entries.zh: 是日，魏之士庶被屠戮者，不可勝計。
entries.en: That day the dead of Weizhou could not be numbered.
entries.literal: That day the gentlemen and commoners of Wei who were butchered could not be counted.

entries.zh: 末帝，諱瑱，初名友貞，及即位，改名鍠，貞明中又改今諱。
entries.en: The Last Emperor, taboo name Zhen, was originally Youzhen; on accession he took the name Huang, and in Zhenming changed to his present taboo name.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor, taboo name Zhen, was originally named Youzhen; on taking the throne he changed his name to Huang, and in Zhenming again changed to his present taboo name.

entries.zh: 太祖第四子也。
entries.en: He was Taizu's fourth son.
entries.literal: He was Taizu's fourth son.

entries.zh: 母曰元貞皇后張氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Yuanzhen (Zhang).
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang.

entries.zh: 以唐文德元年戊申歲九月十二日生於東京。
entries.en: He was born in the Eastern Capital on the twelfth of the ninth month of the wushen year, Wende 1 of Tang.
entries.literal: On the twelfth day of the ninth month of the wushen year of Tang Wende 1 he was born in the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 帝美容儀，性沉厚寡言，雅好儒士。
entries.en: Handsome and composed, he spoke little and loved the company of scholars.
entries.literal: The Emperor had fine features and bearing; his nature was deep, steady, and sparing of speech, and he esteemed Confucian scholars.

entries.zh: 唐光化三年，授河南府參軍。
entries.en: In Guanghua 3 of Tang he was made aide of Henan Prefecture.
entries.literal: In Tang Guanghua 3 he was appointed aide of Henan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，封均王。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, he was made Prince of Jun.
entries.literal: When Taizu received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jun.

entries.zh: 時太祖初置天興軍，最為親衛，以帝為左天興軍使。
entries.en: When Taizu first formed the Tianxing Army as his personal guard, he made the Emperor commander of the Left Tianxing.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu first established the Tianxing Army as the closest imperial guard, and made the Emperor Left Tianxing Army commander.

entries.zh: 開平四年夏，進位檢校司空，依前天興軍使，充東京馬步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: In the summer of Kaiping 4 he was promoted to honorary Minister of Works, kept command of the Tianxing Army, and became commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: In summer of Kaiping 4 he was advanced to honorary Minister of Works, still serving as Tianxing Army commander, and filled the post of Eastern Capital horse-and-foot commander.

entries.zh: 乾化二年六月二日，庶人友珪弑逆，矯太祖詔，遣供奉官丁昭溥馳至東京，密令帝害博王友文。
entries.en: On the second day of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, the deposed Yougui murdered his sovereign; forging an edict as if from Taizu, he sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu racing to the Eastern Capital with secret orders for the Emperor to kill Prince of Bo Youwen.
entries.literal: On the second day of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, the commoner Yougui committed regicide; he forged an edict in the name of Taizu and dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital, secretly ordering the Emperor to kill Prince of Bo Youwen.

entries.zh: 友珪即位，以帝為東京留守，行開封府尹，檢校司徒。
entries.en: When Yougui acceded, he made the Emperor custodian of the Eastern Capital, acting prefect of Kaifeng, and honorary Minister of Education (Situ).
entries.literal: Yougui took the throne and appointed the Emperor Eastern Capital custodian, acting Kaifeng prefect, and honorary Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 友珪以篡逆居位，群情不附。
entries.en: Yougui ruled by treason, and the realm would not rally to him.
entries.literal: Yougui held power by usurpation, and popular sentiment did not attach to him.

entries.zh: 會趙岩至東京，從帝私宴，因言及社稷事。
entries.en: Zhao Yan came to the Eastern Capital; over a private banquet with the Emperor they spoke of the fate of the dynasty.
entries.literal: When Zhao Yan arrived at the Eastern Capital, he joined the Emperor at a private banquet and the talk turned to affairs of state.

entries.zh: 帝以誠款謀之，岩曰：「此事易如反掌，成敗在招討楊令公之手，但得一言諭禁軍，其事立辦。」
entries.en: The Emperor opened his heart in planning; Yan said: "This is easy as turning the hand; victory rests with Pacification Commissioner Yang—persuade the forbidden army and the thing is settled at once."
entries.literal: The Emperor laid out his sincerity in counsel; Yan said: "This matter is as easy as turning one's palm; success or failure lies in the hands of Pacification Commissioner Lord Yang—one word to the forbidden army and the affair is done at once."

entries.zh: 岩時典禁軍，洎還洛，以謀告侍衛親軍袁象先。
entries.en: Yan held the forbidden army; back in Luoyang he told the plot to Imperial Guard commander Yuan Xiangxian.
entries.literal: Yan then commanded the forbidden army; when he returned to Luoyang he disclosed the plot to Imperial Guard commander Yuan Xiangxian.

entries.zh: 帝令腹心馬慎交之魏州見師厚，且言成事之日，賜勞軍錢五十萬緡，仍許兼鎮。
entries.en: The Emperor dispatched his confidant Ma Shenjiao to Weizhou to win Shihou, promising fifty thousand strings in rewards on success and a second command besides.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent his trusted man Ma Shenjiao to Weizhou to see Shihou, saying that when the deed succeeded he would grant fifty thousand strings in army rewards and still permit him to hold two commands.

entries.zh: 慎交，燕人也，素有膽辨，乃說師厚曰：「郢王殺君害父，篡居大位，宮中荒淫，靡所不至。
entries.en: Shenjiao, a Yan man known for nerve and speech, pressed Shihou: "Prince of Ying slew his sovereign and father, seized the throne, and now wallows in every palace excess.
entries.literal: Shenjiao, a man of Yan, had long been bold and eloquent; he urged Shihou: "Prince of Ying killed his lord and harmed his father, usurped the great throne, and in the palace indulges every debauch.

entries.zh: 洛下人情已去，東京物望所歸，公若因而成之，則有輔立之功，討賊之效。」
entries.en: Luoyang has turned away; all eyes are on the Eastern Capital—act now and you win the credit of raising a ruler and crushing a rebel."
entries.literal: Sentiment in Luoyang is already gone; the Eastern Capital holds the people's hopes—if you seize the moment, you will have the merit of aiding enthronement and the effect of punishing the traitor."

entries.zh: 師厚猶豫未決，謂從事曰：「吾於郢王，君臣之分已定，無故改圖，人謂我何！」
entries.en: Shihou wavered and told his staff: "Prince of Ying and I are already lord and subject; to shift without cause—what would people say!"
entries.literal: Shihou still hesitated and said to his staff: "Between Prince of Ying and me the lord-subject bond is fixed; to change course without cause—what would men say of me!"

entries.zh: 慎交曰：「郢王以子弑父，是曰元凶。
entries.en: Shenjiao replied: "Prince of Ying murdered his father as a son—the chief villain.
entries.literal: Shenjiao said: "Prince of Ying as son slew his father—he is the arch rebel.

entries.zh: 均王為君為親，正名仗義。
entries.en: Prince of Jun stands for sovereign and family—right in name and in arms.
entries.literal: Prince of Jun is ruler and kin; his name is righteous and his cause just.

entries.zh: 彼若一朝事成，令公何情自處！」
entries.en: If he wins overnight, what place will you have, my lord!"
entries.literal: If he succeeds in a morning, how will you, my lord, face yourself!"

entries.zh: 師厚驚曰：「幾誤計耳！」
entries.en: Shihou cried: "I was on the verge of ruin!"
entries.literal: Shihou started and said: "I nearly took the wrong course!"

entries.zh: 乃令小校王舜賢至洛，密與趙岩、袁象先圖議。
entries.en: He sent junior officer Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to conspire quietly with Zhao Yan and Yuan Xiangxian.
entries.literal: He then sent junior officer Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to plot secretly with Zhao Yan and Yuan Xiangxian.

entries.zh: 時有左右龍驤都在東京，帝偽作友珪詔，遣還洛下。
entries.en: The Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies were then at the Eastern Capital; the Emperor forged Yougui's edict and ordered them back to Luoyang.
entries.literal: At that time the Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies were at the Eastern Capital; the Emperor forged an edict in Yougui's name and sent them back to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 先是，劉重遇部下龍驤一指揮於懷州叛，經年搜捕其黨，帝因遣人激怒其眾曰：「郢王以龍驤軍嘗叛，追汝等洛下，將盡坑之。」
entries.en: Earlier a Dragon-Prancing command under Liu Chongyu had mutinied at Huaizhou and been hunted a full year; the Emperor sent agents to stir them: "Prince of Ying means to drag you to Luoyang and slaughter every man, since Dragon-Prancing once rebelled."
entries.literal: Earlier, a Dragon-Prancing command under Liu Chongyu had rebelled at Huaizhou; for a year their partisans were hunted; the Emperor therefore sent men to inflame the troops, saying: "Prince of Ying, because the Dragon-Prancing Army once rebelled, is summoning you to Luoyang and will bury you all alive."

entries.zh: 翌日，乃以偽昭示之。
entries.en: Next day he displayed the forged order.
entries.literal: The next day the forged edict was shown them.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》：《梁太祖實錄》：「丙戌，東京言龍驤軍準詔追赴西京，軍情不肯進發。」
entries.en: (《Zizhi Tongjian: Divergent Accounts》: 《Veritable Record of Emperor Taizu of Liang》: "On bingxu the Eastern Capital reported Dragon-Prancing troops under orders for the Western Capital would not move."
entries.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian: Divergent Accounts》: 《Veritable Record of Emperor Taizu of Liang》: "On bingxu the Eastern Capital reported that the Dragon-Prancing Army, per edict, was to hurry to the Western Capital; the troops refused to march."

entries.zh: 實友珪征之，非友貞偽作，但激怒言坑之耳。）〉
entries.en: Yougui truly summoned them; Youzhen did not forge the edict—only the threat of massacre was invented.)〉
entries.literal: Yougui actually summoned them; Youzhen did not forge it—only the incitement about burial alive.)〉

entries.zh: 諸軍憂恐，將校垂泣告帝，乞指生路。
entries.en: The troops were terrified; commanders wept and pleaded for a path to survival.
entries.literal: The armies were anxious and afraid; officers wept and begged the Emperor to show them a way to live.

entries.zh: 帝諭之曰：「先帝三十餘年，經營社稷，千征萬戰，爾等皆會從行。
entries.en: The Emperor told them: "For thirty years the late Emperor built the realm through endless campaigns—you marched at his side.
entries.literal: The Emperor addressed them: "The late Emperor for more than thirty years tended the altars of state, fought a thousand battles and ten thousand campaigns—you all marched with him.

entries.zh: 今日先帝尚落人奸計，爾等安所逃避。」
entries.en: Today even he was trapped by villains—there was nowhere to run."
entries.literal: Today even the late Emperor fell to traitors' schemes—where can you flee."

entries.zh: 因出梁祖御容以示諸將，帝歔欷而泣曰：「郢王賊害君父，違天逆地，復欲屠滅親軍，爾等苟能自趨洛陽，擒取逆豎，告謝先帝，即轉禍為福矣！」
entries.en: He displayed Taizu's portrait; weeping, he said: "Prince of Ying murdered sovereign and father, defied Heaven and earth, and now would butcher the guard—march on Luoyang, seize the rebel, and appease the late Emperor, and disaster becomes fortune!"
entries.literal: He then brought out Taizu's portrait to show the commanders; the Emperor sobbed and wept: "Prince of Ying as traitor harmed lord and father, defied Heaven and earth, and would again slaughter the imperial guard—if you can yourselves hurry to Luoyang, seize the rebel, and report to the late Emperor, you will turn calamity into blessing!"

entries.zh: 眾踴躍曰：「王言是也。」
entries.en: All cried: "Your Highness is right."
entries.literal: The crowd leapt up and said: "Your Highness speaks rightly."

entries.zh: 皆呼萬歲，請帝為主，時友珪改元之二月十五日也。
entries.en: They shouted long life and begged him to lead them—the fifteenth day of Yougui's second regnal month.
entries.literal: All shouted ten thousand years and asked the Emperor to be their lord—it was the fifteenth day of the second month of Yougui's reign era.

entries.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
entries.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
entries.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

entries.zh: 乙酉，前蔡州刺史董璋權知宣義軍軍州事。
entries.en: On yiyou, Dong Zhang, former prefect of Cai, was given acting charge of Xuanyi Army affairs.
entries.literal: On yiyou, former Cai prefect Dong Zhang was made acting Xuanyi Army military and prefectural commissioner.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以前右羽林軍統軍梁繼業為左衛上將軍。
entries.en: On dinghai, Liang Jiye, former commander of the Right Feathered Forest, became Senior General of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: On dinghai, former Right Feathered Forest commander Liang Jiye was made Senior General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 壬辰，以租庸判官、檢校司徒張紹圭為光祿卿，依前充租庸判官。
entries.en: On renchen, Zhang Shaogui, Rent and Corvée commissioner and honorary Minister of Works, was made Director of the Imperial Banquets while retaining the Rent and Corvée post.
entries.literal: On renchen, Rent and Corvée commissioner and honorary Minister of Works Zhang Shaogui was made Director of the Imperial Banquets, continuing as Rent and Corvée commissioner.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以權知平盧軍軍州事、客省使、知銀台事元湘為檢校司空。
entries.en: On guisi, Yuan Xiang—acting commissioner of Pinglu, Guest Bureau commissioner, and Silver Terrace director—was made honorary Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On guisi, acting Pinglu Army military and prefectural commissioner, Guest Bureau commissioner, and Silver Terrace director Yuan Xiang was made honorary Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 甲午，以飛龍使婁繼英為左武衛大將軍。
entries.en: On jiawu, Lou Jiying of the Flying Dragon office was appointed senior general of the Left Martial Guard.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Flying Dragon commissioner Lou Jiying was made Left Martial Guard senior general.

entries.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
entries.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
entries.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以前天平軍馬步軍都指揮使、檢校太保朱為懷州刺史。
entries.en: On guihai, Zhu Wei, former horse-and-foot commander of Tianping and honorary Grand Guardian, became prefect of Huai.
entries.literal: On guihai, former Tianping Army horse-and-foot commander and honorary Grand Guardian Zhu Wei was made Huai prefect.

entries.zh: 癸酉，以右天武軍使石釗為密州刺史。
entries.en: On guiyou, Shi Zhao of the Right Heavenly Martial Army was appointed prefect of Mi.
entries.literal: On guiyou, Right Heavenly Martial Army commissioner Shi Zhao was made Mi prefect.

entries.zh: 戊寅，以前懷州刺史李建為安州刺史，仍賜名知節。
entries.en: On wuyin, Li Jian, former prefect of Huai, was made prefect of An and granted the name Zhijie.
entries.literal: On wuyin, former Huai prefect Li Jian was made An prefect; he was also granted the name Zhijie.

entries.zh: 己卯，以宣義軍節度副大使、知節度事、北面行營副招討等使、特進、檢校太傅霍彥威為天平軍節度副大使，知節度事。
entries.en: On jimao, Huo Yanwei—deputy commissioner of Xuanyi, acting military commissioner, deputy northern pacification commissioner, specially advanced, and honorary Grand Mentor—was named deputy commissioner of Tianping with charge of military affairs.
entries.literal: On jimao, Xuanyi Army deputy commissioner, acting military commissioner, Northern Line deputy pacification commissioner, specially advanced, honorary Grand Mentor Huo Yanwei was made Tianping Army deputy commissioner, acting military commissioner.

entries.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

entries.zh: 庚申，以左金吾衛大將軍、充街使華溫琪為右龍虎軍統軍，以右龍虎統軍張彥勳為商州刺史，以前西京大內皇牆使李項為右威衛上將軍，以左金吾衛上將軍李周彝權兼左街使。
entries.en: On gengshen, Hua Wenqi became Right Dragon-Tiger commander; Zhang Yanxun, Right Dragon-Tiger commander, was made Shang prefect; Li Xiang, former Western Capital wall commissioner, became Right Awesome Guard senior general; Li Zhouyi, Left Golden Crow senior general, was made acting Left Street commissioner.
entries.literal: On gengshen, Left Golden Crow Guard senior general and street commissioner Hua Wenqi was made Right Dragon-Tiger Army commander; Right Dragon-Tiger commander Zhang Yanxun was made Shang prefect; former Western Capital inner-palace wall commissioner Li Xiang was made Right Awesome Guard senior general; Left Golden Crow Guard senior general Li Zhouyi was made acting Left Street commissioner.

entries.zh: 壬戌，以守太尉、兼中書令、河南尹、判六軍諸衛事、魏王張宗奭為天下兵馬副元帥。
entries.en: On renxu, Zhang Zongshi, Prince of Wei—acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Counselor, Henan prefect, and overseer of the Six Armies and Guards—was named deputy marshal of all armies.
entries.literal: On renxu, acting Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Counselor, Henan prefect, overseer of the Six Armies and Guards, and Prince of Wei Zhang Zongshi was made deputy marshal of all-under-Heaven's armies.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以西面行營馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保、鄭州刺史、充本州防禦使王彥章為檢校太傅。
entries.en: On bingyin, Wang Yanzhang, Western Line horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, and Zheng prefect and defense commissioner, was promoted to honorary Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: On bingyin, Western Line camp horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, Zheng prefect, and Zheng defense commissioner Wang Yanzhang was made honorary Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 丁卯，以西面行營馬步都指揮使、左龍虎軍統軍賀瑰為檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事，充宣義軍節度使、鄭滑濮等州觀察處置等使。
entries.en: On dingmao, He Gui—Western Line horse-and-foot commander and Left Dragon-Tiger commander—was made honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor and named Xuanyi military commissioner over Zheng, Hua, and Pu.
entries.literal: On dingmao, Western Line camp horse-and-foot commander and Left Dragon-Tiger Army commander He Gui was made honorary Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor, and Xuanyi Army military commissioner and observation and disposition commissioner for Zheng, Hua, and Pu.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：時論平慶州功，故賀瑰進秩。）〉
entries.en: The Zizhi Tongjian notes: Contemporary opinion credited the pacification of Qing Prefecture, so He Gui was advanced in rank.
entries.literal: The Zizhi Tongjian notes: At the time, opinion credited the pacification of Qing Prefecture, and therefore He Gui was advanced in rank.

entries.zh: 己巳，帝幸洛陽，為來年有事於南郊也。
entries.en: On jisi the Emperor went to Luoyang to prepare for a Southern Suburban rite the following year.
entries.literal: On jisi the Emperor visited Luoyang, because next year there would be affairs at the Southern Suburban Altar.

entries.zh: 遂幸伊闕，親拜宣陵。
entries.en: He then went to Yique and bowed at Xuanling in person.
entries.literal: He then visited Yique and personally performed obeisance at Xuanling.

entries.zh: 時租庸使趙岩勸帝郊天，且言：「帝王受命，須行此禮，願陛下力行之。」
entries.en: Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged Heaven-sacrifice, saying: "Emperors who receive the Mandate must perform this rite—Your Majesty should see it through."
entries.literal: At the time Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged the Emperor to sacrifice to Heaven, saying: "When emperors receive the Mandate they must perform this rite; Your Majesty should exert yourself to carry it out."

entries.zh: 宰臣敬翔奏曰：「國家自劉鄩失律以來，府藏殫竭，箕斂百姓，供軍不暇，郊祀之禮，頒行賞賚，所謂取虛名而受實弊也。
entries.en: Chancellor Jing Xiang argued: "Since Liu Xun's defeat, the treasury is empty and the people are squeezed dry to supply the armies. The suburban rites would require lavish rewards, taking a hollow name at real cost.
entries.literal: Chancellor Jing Xiang memorialized: "Since Liu Xun lost military discipline, the treasury has been exhausted; the people have been raked for levies, and supplying the armies leaves no respite. The suburban sacrifice would require the distribution of rewards; this is what is called taking an empty name while suffering real harm.

entries.zh: 況晉人壓境，車駕未可輕動。」
entries.en: Jin forces press the frontier; the court must not travel lightly."
entries.literal: Moreover Jin men press the border; the imperial carriage must not move lightly."

entries.zh: 帝不聽，遂行。
entries.en: The Emperor refused and went ahead.
entries.literal: The Emperor would not listen and proceeded.

entries.zh: 是月，晉人陷楊劉城，帝聞之懼，遂停郊禮，車駕急歸東京。
entries.en: That month the Jin seized Yangliu; frightened, the Emperor canceled the suburban rite and raced back to the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: That month the Jin took Yangliu city; the Emperor, hearing, was afraid, halted the suburban rite, and the imperial carriage hurried back to the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：道路訛言晉軍已入大梁，扼汜水矣。
entries.en: The Zizhi Tongjian states: False reports spread along the roads that Jin troops had already entered Daliang and seized the Si River crossing.
entries.literal: The Zizhi Tongjian states: On the roads, false reports said that Jin troops had entered Daliang and seized the Si River ford.

entries.zh: 從官皆憂其家，相顧涕泣，帝惶駭失圖，遂罷郊祀。）〉
entries.en: Courtiers wept for their homes; the Emperor panicked and abandoned the suburban rite.
entries.literal: Attendants all feared for their families, looked at one another and wept; the Emperor was terrified and lost his plan, and so the suburban sacrifice was stopped.

entries.zh: 癸酉，詔文武兩班，除元隨駕人數外，其餘並令御史司憲張袞部署，候車駕離京後一兩日，發赴東京。
entries.en: On guiyou the court ordered that except for essential escorts, the rest of the civil and military ranks were to be staged by Zhang Gun of the Censorate and dispatched to the Eastern Capital a day or two after the Emperor left.
entries.literal: On guiyou an edict ordered that of the civil and military two ranks, apart from those who must accompany the carriage, the rest were all to be deployed by Censorate director Zhang Gun and, one or two days after the carriage left the capital, sent to the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 甲戌，以天下兵馬副元帥、太尉、兼中書令、河南尹、魏王張宗奭為西都留守。
entries.en: On jiaxu, Zhang Zongshi, deputy marshal, Grand Preceptor, Grand Counselor, Henan prefect, and Prince of Wei, was made Western Capital custodian.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, deputy marshal of all armies, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Counselor, Henan prefect, and Prince of Wei Zhang Zongshi was made Western Capital custodian.

entries.zh: 貞明五年春正月，晉人城德勝，夾河為柵。
entries.en: In the first month of Zhenming 5 the Jin fortified Desheng and fenced both banks of the river.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of Zhenming 5, the Jin fortified Desheng and built palisades along the river.

entries.zh: 二月乙巳，以宣徽院副使韋堅權知徐州軍事。
entries.en: On yisi in the second month, Xuanhui Court deputy commissioner Wei Jian was given acting charge of Xu Prefecture's military affairs.
entries.literal: On yisi in the second month, Xuanhui Court deputy commissioner Wei Jian was made acting Xu prefect military commissioner.

entries.zh: 三月己卯，以華州感化軍留後尹皓為華州節度使，加檢校太保、同平章事。
entries.en: On jimao in the third month, Yin Hao of Hua was made Hua commissioner and promoted to honorary Grand Guardian and Grand Counselor.
entries.literal: On jimao in the third month, Hua Ganhua Army retention commissioner Yin Hao was made Hua military commissioner and advanced to honorary Grand Guardian and Grand Counselor.

entries.zh: 癸未，製削奪兗州節度使張守進在身官爵，以其叛故也。
entries.en: On guiwei the court stripped rebel Yan commissioner Zhang Shoujin of every title he held.
entries.literal: On guiwei an order stripped Yan military commissioner Zhang Shoujin of all offices and ranks he held, because of his rebellion.

entries.zh: 仍命劉鄩為兗州管內安撫製置使，領兵以攻之。
entries.en: Liu Xun was appointed pacification commissioner for Yan and sent with troops against him.
entries.literal: Liu Xun was then appointed pacification and disposition commissioner within Yan Prefecture and ordered to lead troops against him.

entries.zh: 秋七月，晉王自魏州還太原。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn the Prince of Jin left Weizhou for Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Prince of Jin returned from Weizhou to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 八月乙未朔，滑州節度使賀瑰卒，輟視朝三日，詔贈侍中。
entries.en: On yiwei, first of the eighth month, He Gui of Hua died; the court mourned three days and posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: On yiwei, first day of the eighth month, Hua military commissioner He Gui died; court audience was suspended three days and he was posthumously given Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 是月，命開封尹王瓚為北面行營招討使。
entries.en: That month Wang Zan, Kaifeng prefect, was named Northern Line pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: That month Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan was made Northern Line camp pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 瓚乃與許州留後王彥章等率大軍自黎陽濟，營於楊村，造浮梁以通津路。
entries.en: Zan crossed from Liyang with Wang Yanzhang of Xu, camped at Yang village, and bridged the ford.
entries.literal: Zan then with Xu retention commissioner Wang Yanzhang and others led a great army across from Liyang, encamped at Yang village, and built a floating bridge to open the crossing.

entries.zh: 九月丙寅，製削奪廣州節度使、南平王劉岩在身官爵，以其將謀僭號故也。
entries.en: On bingyin in the ninth month the court stripped Liu Yan of Guang and his Prince of Nanping title for impending usurpation.
entries.literal: On bingyin in the ninth month an order stripped Guang military commissioner and Prince of Nanping Liu Yan of all offices and ranks he held, because he was about to usurp a title.

entries.zh: 仍詔天下兵馬元帥錢鏐指揮攻討。
entries.en: Qian Liu, marshal of all armies, was ordered to lead the punitive campaign.
entries.literal: An edict still ordered marshal of all armies Qian Liu to direct the attack.

entries.zh: 冬十月，晉王復至魏州。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter the Prince of Jin returned to Weizhou.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Prince of Jin came again to Weizhou.

entries.zh: 是月，劉鄩攻下兗州，擒張守進，夷其族。
entries.en: That month Liu Xun took Yan, captured Zhang Shoujin, and exterminated his clan.
entries.literal: That month Liu Xun captured Yan Prefecture, seized Zhang Shoujin, and exterminated his clan.

entries.zh: 十一月丁丑，以兗州安撫製置使、特進、檢校太傅、大彭郡開國公劉鄩為兗州節度使、開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、同平章事，賞平兗之功也。
entries.en: On dingchou in the eleventh month, Liu Xun was made military commissioner of Yan, granted Open Office with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, and promoted to honorary Grand Commandant and Grand Counselor in reward for pacifying Yan.
entries.literal: On dingchou in the eleventh month, Liu Xun, pacification and disposition commissioner of Yan Prefecture, Specially Advanced, honorary Grand Mentor, and Founding Duke of Dapeng Commandery, was made military commissioner of Yan, granted Open Office with Rank Equal to the Three Excellencies, and promoted to honorary Grand Commandant and Grand Counselor in reward for pacifying Yan.

entries.zh: 辛卯，王瓚帥師至戚城，遇晉軍。
entries.en: On xinmao, Wang Zan marched to Qi city and encountered the Jin.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Wang Zan led troops to Qi city and met Jin troops.

entries.zh: 交綏而退。
entries.en: After a brief clash both sides drew off.
entries.literal: They crossed arms and withdrew.

entries.zh: 六月，遣兗州節度使劉鄩、華州節度使尹皓、崇州節度使溫昭圖、莊宅使段凝領軍攻同州。
entries.en: In the sixth month Liu Yan of Yan, Yin Hao of Hua, Wen Zhaotu of Chong, and Duan Ning of the Manor Estates marched on Tongzhou.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, Yanzhou military commissioner Liu Yan, Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao, Chongzhou military commissioner Wen Zhaotu, and Manor Estates commissioner Duan Ning led armies to attack Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 先是，河中朱友謙襲陷同州，節度使程全暉單騎奔京師。
entries.en: Zhu Youqian of Hedong had seized Tongzhou and Cheng Quanhui, its commissioner, rode alone to the capital.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhu Youqian of Hedong had raided and taken Tongzhou; military commissioner Cheng Quanhui fled alone on horseback to the capital.

entries.zh: 友謙以其子令德為同州留後，表求節旄，不允；
entries.en: Youqian installed his son Lingde as acting commissioner and asked for the seal; the court refused;
entries.literal: Youqian made his son Lingde Tongzhou retention commissioner and memorialized for the military commission; it was not granted;

entries.zh: 既而帝慮友謙怨望，遂命兼鎮同州，製命將下而友謙已叛，遣使求援於晉，故命將討之。
entries.en: Fearing resentment, the Emperor then named Youqian concurrent commissioner of Tong—but before the edict arrived Youqian rebelled and sought Jin’s aid, and punitive armies were dispatched.
entries.literal: then the Emperor, fearing Youqian’s resentment, ordered him to hold Tongzhou concurrently; the edict was about to issue when Youqian had already rebelled, sending envoys to seek aid from Jin—hence generals were ordered to punish him.

entries.zh: 以宣和庫使、守右領衛將軍李嚴權知兗州軍州事。
entries.en: Li Yan of the Xuanhe Treasury was given acting command of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Xuanhe Treasury commissioner and acting Right Forest-Unicorn general Li Yan was made acting Yanzhou military and prefectural commissioner.

entries.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「郊禋大禮，舊有渥恩，御殿改元，比無賞給。
entries.en: On dinghai an edict said: "Suburban sacrifices brought largesse, but this era change had no rewards.
entries.literal: On dinghai, an edict said: "Suburban and border sacrifices, the old have generous grace; changing the era at the imperial hall, by comparison there was no reward grant.

entries.zh: 今則不循舊例，別示特恩。
entries.en: The throne therefore granted a special bounty.
entries.literal: Now we do not follow the old example but separately show special grace.

entries.zh: 其行營將士賞賚已給付本家，宜令招討使霍彥威、副招討使王彥章、陳州行營都指揮使張漢傑曉示諸軍知委。」
entries.en: Campaign bonuses sent to soldiers’ families should be announced by Huo Yanwei, Wang Yanzhang, and Zhang Hanjie."
entries.literal: Campaign soldiers’ rewards already paid to their families—the Pacification commissioner Huo Yanwei, deputy Pacification commissioner Wang Yanzhang, and Chenzhou campaign commander-in-chief Zhang Hanjie should announce to all armies for their knowledge."

entries.zh: 是月，兗州節度使、充河東道行營都招討使劉鄩卒。
entries.en: That month Liu Yan, Yanzhou commissioner and Hedong campaign commander, died.
entries.literal: That month, Yanzhou military commissioner and Hedong circuit campaign commander-in-chief Liu Yan died.

entries.zh: 二月己未，以權知靜勝軍節度觀察留後、前汝州防禦使華溫琪為靜勝軍節度觀察留後，依前檢校太傅。
entries.en: On jiwei in the second month Hua Wenqi became Jingsheng observation commissioner with his former honorary Grand Mentor title.
entries.literal: On jiwei in the second month, acting Jingsheng Army observation and retention commissioner and former Ruzhou defense commissioner Hua Wenqi was made Jingsheng observation and retention commissioner, continuing as before honorary Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以荊南節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、渤海郡王高季昌為守中書令，依前荊南節度使。
entries.en: On bingyin Gao Jichang of Jingnan was named acting Secretariat Director while remaining Jingnan commissioner.
entries.literal: On bingyin, Jingnan military commissioner, honorary Grand Preceptor, concurrent Secretariat Director, Prince of Bohai Gao Jichang was made acting Secretariat Director, continuing as Jingnan military commissioner.

entries.zh: 庚午，以晉州建寧軍節度觀察留後劉玘為晉州節度使、檢校太保。
entries.en: On gengwu Liu Qi became Jinzhou military commissioner and honorary Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On gengwu, Jinzhou Jianning Army observation and retention commissioner Liu Qi was made Jinzhou military commissioner and honorary Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 壬申，史館上言：「伏見北齊文士魏收著《後魏書》，於時自魏太武之初，至於北齊，書不獲就，乃大征百官家傳，刊總斟酌，隨條甄舉，搜訪遺亡，數年之間，勒為一代典籍，編在北史，固非虛言。
entries.en: On renshen the Historiography Office memorialized: "Citing Wei Shou’s 《History of Later Wei》, unable to finish from Taiwu to Northern Qi, he gathered officials’ genealogies, sifted and recovered lost material, and within years produced a classic now preserved in the Northern History.
entries.literal: On renshen the Historiography Office memorialized: "We humbly see the Northern Qi man of letters Wei Shou compile the 《History of Later Wei》; at the time from the beginning of Northern Wei Emperor Taiwu down to Northern Qi the book could not be completed, so they greatly summoned the family genealogies of the hundred officials, collated and weighed them, selected item by item, searched out what was lost—within several years it was carved into the canon of one age, compiled in the Northern History; this is truly no empty saying.

entries.zh: 臣今請明下製，敕內外百官及前資士子、帝戚勳家，並各納家傳，具述父祖事行源流及才術德業灼然可考者，並纂述送史館。
entries.en: We ask an edict requiring officials, scholars, kin, and meritorious houses to submit genealogies of verifiable ancestors and send compiled accounts to the Historiography Office.
entries.literal: Your servant now asks that an edict be clearly issued commanding inner and outer officials, former qualified scholars, imperial kin, and meritorious families each to submit family genealogies fully narrating fathers’ and grandfathers’ conduct, origins, and clearly verifiable talent, arts, virtue, and achievement, all compiled and sent to the Historiography Office.

entries.zh: 如記得前朝會昌已後公私，亦任抄錄送官，皆須直書，不用文藻。
entries.en: Memories of public affairs since Huichang may be copied in plain prose without ornament.
entries.literal: If they recall public and private matters after Huichang of the prior dynasty, they may also copy and send them to the authorities—all must be straight writing, without literary ornament.

entries.zh: 兼以兵火之後，簡牘罕存，應內外臣僚，曾有奏行公事，關涉製置，或討論沿革，或章疏文詞，有可采者，並許編錄送納。
entries.en: Moreover, after the fires of war, documents rarely survive. Officials inside and outside the court who once memorialized on public business touching institutions, discussed precedents and changes, or wrote memorial language worth preserving may all compile and submit it.
entries.literal: Moreover after the fires of war documents rarely survive; inner and outer officials who once memorialized on business touching institutions, discussing evolution, or memorial language worth adopting—all may compile and send in.

entries.zh: 候史館修撰之日，考其所上公事，與中書門下文案事相符會，或格言正辭詢訪不謬者，並與編載。
entries.en: At compilation time their submissions will be checked against Secretariat files; verified material and sound phrases will enter the history.
entries.literal: When the Historiography Office day of compilation arrives, examine the public business they submit against Secretariat records, or upright words and correct phrases found on inquiry not in error—all shall be compiled together.

entries.zh: 所冀忠臣名士，共流家國之耿光；
entries.en: Thus loyal ministers and eminent men may shine in the annals of the realm;
entries.literal: What is hoped is that loyal ministers and famous scholars together may stream the bright glory of state and family;

entries.zh: 孝子順孫，獲記祖先之丕烈。
entries.en: and filial descendants may preserve their forebears’ fame.
entries.literal: filial sons and obedient grandsons may obtain record of ancestors’ great achievements.

entries.zh: 而且周德見乎殷紀，舜典存乎禹功，非唯十世可知，庶成一朝大典。
entries.en: As Zhou virtue appears in Yin records and Shun’s canon in Yu’s deeds, ten generations may be known and our dynasty’s great history completed.
entries.literal: Moreover Zhou virtue appears in Yin annals; Shun’s canon rests in Yu’s achievement—not only may ten generations be known, but perhaps one dynasty’s great canon may be completed.

entries.zh: 臣叨庸委任，獲領監修，將贖素食，輒幹元覽。」
entries.en: Humbly overseeing compilation, I venture this plea before your majesty."
entries.literal: Your servant, unworthily entrusted, has obtained charge of compilation oversight; wishing to repay the debt of drawing an unearned salary, I rashly trouble the imperial gaze."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The throne approved.
entries.literal: The edict followed it.

entries.zh: 鹽鐵轉運使敬翔奏：「請於雍州、河陽、徐州三處重置場院稅茶。」
entries.en: Jing Xiang, Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, memorialized: "Please restore tea taxes at market yards in Yong, Heyang, and Xu."
entries.literal: Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Jing Xiang memorialized: "I ask that at Yongzhou, Heyang, and Xuzhou three places the market-yard tea tax be re-established."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: It was followed.

entries.zh: 己卯，禮部尚書、充西都副留守兼判尚書省事崔沂奏：「西京都省，凡有公事奏聞，常須借印施行，伏請鑄尚事省分司印一面。」
entries.en: On jimao Cui Yi of Rites memorialized: "The Western Capital directorate must borrow seals for public business; please cast a branch seal for the directorate office."
entries.literal: On jimao, Rites Minister, acting Western Capital deputy defender and acting overseer of the Secretariat office Cui Yi memorialized: "In the Western Capital directorate, whenever public business is memorialized, seals must usually be borrowed to execute; I humbly ask that one branch seal of the Directorate office be cast."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The throne agreed.
entries.literal: It was followed.

entries.zh: 是月，鎮州大將王德明殺其帥王熔，自稱留後，遣使來求援。
entries.en: That month Wang Deming of Zhenzhou murdered Wang Rong, declared himself acting commissioner, and asked for help.
entries.literal: That month, Zhenzhou great general Wang Deming killed his commander Wang Rong, styled himself retention commissioner, and sent envoys to seek aid.

entries.zh: 宰臣敬翔請許之，租庸使趙岩等以為不可，乃止。
entries.en: Jing Xiang favored acceptance; Zhao Yan and others refused, and the court declined.
entries.literal: Chief minister Jing Xiang asked to grant it; Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan and others held it impossible, and it stopped.

entries.zh: 貞明六年春正月戊子，以曹州刺史朱漢賓為安州宣威軍節度使；
entries.en: On wuzi in the first month of Zhenming 6, Zhu Hanbin, prefect of Cao, was appointed military commissioner of the Xuanwei Army at An.
entries.literal: On wuzi, first month of spring of Zhenming 6, Cao prefect Zhu Hanbin was made Anzhou Xuanwei Army military commissioner;

entries.zh: 以許州匡國軍節度觀察留後、充散指揮都軍使、檢校太傅王彥章為匡國軍節度使，進封開國侯，軍職如故。
entries.en: Wang Yanzhang—Kuangguo observation commissioner at Xu, acting commander of the Scattered Command, and honorary Grand Mentor—was made Kuangguo military commissioner and enfeoffed Marquis Who Opens the State, retaining his army posts.
entries.literal: Xu Prefecture Kuangguo Army observation and retention commissioner, acting Scattered Command all-armies commander, honorary Grand Mentor Wang Yanzhang was made Kuangguo Army military commissioner, advanced to Marquis Who Opens the State, military posts unchanged.

entries.zh: 文惠皇太后王氏，開平初追諡。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Wenhui (Wang) received her posthumous title early in the Kaiping era.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Wenhui, née Wang, was given a posthumous title at the beginning of Kaiping.

entries.zh: 太祖性孝願，奉太后未嘗小失色，朝夕視膳，為士君子之規範。
entries.en: The Founder was deeply filial: he never let his manner slip before the Empress Dowager and attended her at every meal, morning and night—a standard for the cultivated man.
entries.literal: The Founder by nature was filial and reverent; in serving the Empress Dowager he never once showed the slightest lapse of countenance, morning and evening attending her meals—a model for gentlemen and scholars.

entries.zh: 帝嚴察用法，無纖毫假貸，太后言之，帝頗為省刑。
entries.en: The Emperor enforced the law without mercy; when the Empress Dowager intervened, he often eased sentences.
entries.literal: The Emperor was strict in investigation and application of law, granting not the slightest indulgence; when the Empress Dowager spoke of it, the Emperor considerably lightened punishments.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖父誠蚤卒，有三子俱幼。
entries.en: (The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 records that the Liang founder’s father Cheng died early, with three sons still small.
entries.literal: (《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s father Cheng died young, leaving three sons all still young.

entries.zh: 母王氏，攜養寄於同縣人劉崇家。
entries.en: Their mother Wang entrusted the boys to Liu Chong, a man of the same county.
entries.literal: The mother, née Wang, took them to be raised and lodged with Liu Chong of the same county.

entries.zh: 昆弟之中，惟溫狡猾無行，崇母撫養之，崇兄弟嘗加譴杖。
entries.en: Of the brothers only Wen was sly and unruly; Liu Chong’s mother cared for him, while Chong’s brothers often thrashed him.
entries.literal: Among the brothers, only Wen was cunning and without proper conduct; Chong’s mother raised him, and Chong’s brothers sometimes beat him with rods.

entries.zh: 一日，偷崇家釜而竄，為崇追回，崇母遮護，以免撲責。
entries.en: Once he stole a pot from the Chong household and ran; caught and dragged back, he was spared the rod only because Chong’s mother stood between him and punishment.
entries.literal: One day he stole a cauldron from Chong’s house and fled; Chong caught him and brought him back, but Chong’s mother shielded him so he escaped a beating.

entries.zh: 善逐走鹿，往往及而獲之。
entries.en: He could run down deer on foot and usually brought them down.
entries.literal: He was skilled at chasing running deer and often overtook and caught them.

entries.zh: 又，崇母常見其有龍蛇之異。
entries.en: Liu Chong’s mother also claimed to see dragon-and-serpent portents about him.
entries.literal: Moreover, Chong’s mother often saw in him omens of dragons and serpents.

entries.zh: 他日與仲兄存入黃巢軍作賊，伯兄昱與母王氏尚依劉家。
entries.en: Later Wen and his second brother Cun went off with Huang Chao’s rebels; the eldest, Yu, and Mother Wang remained with the Lius.
entries.literal: Another day he and his second brother Cun joined Huang Chao’s army as bandits; the eldest brother Yu and their mother Wang still relied on the Liu household.

entries.zh: 溫既辭去，不知存亡。
entries.en: After Wen departed, his fate was unknown.
entries.literal: Once Wen had left, none knew whether he lived or died.

entries.zh: 及溫領鎮於汴，盛飾輿馬，使人迎母於崇家。
entries.en: When Wen became military governor at Bian, he sent a splendid escort to bring his mother from the Chong home.
entries.literal: When Wen held command at Bian, he lavishly adorned carriage and horses and sent men to welcome his mother from Chong’s house.

entries.zh: 王氏惶恐，辭避深藏，不之信，謂人曰：「朱三落拓無行，何處作賊送死，焉能自致富貴？
entries.en: Wang was afraid, refused, and hid; she told others: "That good-for-nothing Zhu Third is off robbing somewhere—how could he possibly have become rich and powerful?
entries.literal: Wang was terrified, declined, and hid deep away, not believing it, and said to people: "Zhu Third is shiftless and without conduct—where is he playing bandit and courting death, that he could enrich himself and rise to nobility?

entries.zh: 汴帥非吾子也。」
entries.en: The lord of Bian cannot be my boy."
entries.literal: The Bian commander is not my son."

entries.zh: 使者具陳離鄉去裏之由，歸國立功之事，王氏方泣而信。
entries.en: The envoy explained how Wen had left home, served the dynasty, and won distinction; at last Wang wept and believed.
entries.literal: The messenger fully set forth the reasons for leaving home and native place and the deeds of returning to the state and achieving merit; only then did Wang weep and believe.

entries.zh: 是日，與崇母並迎歸汴。
entries.en: The same day both mothers were brought to Bian.
entries.literal: That day she and Chong’s mother were both welcomed back to Bian.

entries.zh: 溫盛禮郊迎，人士改觀。
entries.en: Wen met them with full suburban ceremony, and onlookers saw him in a new light.
entries.literal: Wen received them with grand rites at the suburban greeting; gentlemen changed their view of him.

entries.zh: 崇以舊恩，位至列卿，為商州刺史。
entries.en: For past kindness to the family, Chong rose to a chief-ministerial post and served as prefect of Shang.
entries.literal: Chong, because of old kindness, rose to rank among chief ministers and became prefect of Shangzhou.

entries.zh: 王氏以溫貴，封晉國太夫人。
entries.en: With Wen’s rise, Wang was created Grand Lady of Jin.
entries.literal: Because Wen had become noble, Wang was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.

entries.zh: 仲兄存，於賊中為矢石所中而卒。
entries.en: The second brother Cun died in the rebel ranks, killed by missile weapons.
entries.literal: The second brother Cun, in the bandit army, was struck by arrow and stone and died.

entries.zh: 溫置酒於母，歡甚，語及家事，謂母曰：「朱五經辛苦業儒，不登一命，今有子為節度使，無忝前人矣！」
entries.en: At a feast for his mother Wen grew merry and said: "Father Zhu Five Classics studied the classics in poverty and never won office—yet his son is now a military commissioner. We have not shamed our ancestors!"
entries.literal: Wen set out wine for his mother, very merry, and speaking of family affairs said to her: "Zhu Five Classics toiled at Confucian learning yet never received a single appointment; now there is a son who is military commissioner—no disgrace to our forebears!"

entries.zh: 母不懌，良久謂溫曰：「汝致身及此，信為英特，行義未必如先人。
entries.en: His mother was unmoved and after a pause told Wen: "You have risen high—no doubt you are gifted—but your conduct is hardly like your father’s.
entries.literal: His mother was displeased and after a long while said to Wen: "You have reached this station—truly you are extraordinary—but in conduct you surely do not match your forebears.

entries.zh: 朱二與汝同入賊軍，身死蠻徼，孤男稚女，艱食無告。
entries.en: Your brother Zhu Second went into the rebels with you and died on the frontier; his widow and children are destitute, with no one to help them.
entries.literal: Zhu Second entered the bandit army with you and died on the barbarian frontier; orphaned boys and young girls eat bitterly with none to plead for them.

entries.zh: 汝未有恤孤之心，英特即有，諸無取也。」
entries.en: You show no care for his orphans. Talent alone is nothing to boast of."
entries.literal: You have not the heart to succor orphans—if you are extraordinary, still do not take pride in it."

entries.zh: 溫垂涕謝罪，即令召諸兄子皆至汴。
entries.en: Wen wept and apologized, then had every nephew brought to Bian.
entries.literal: Wen shed tears and apologized, and at once ordered all his brothers’ sons summoned to Bian.

entries.zh: 友寧、友倫皆立軍功，位至方鎮。）〉
entries.en: Youning and Youlun both won military honors and rose to govern provinces.)〉
entries.literal: Youning and Youlun both established military merit and reached posts as regional commissioners.)〉

entries.zh: 元貞皇后張氏，乾化中追諡。
entries.en: Empress Yuanzhen (Zhang) was posthumously honored during Qianhua.
entries.literal: Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang, was given a posthumous title in the Qianhua era.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：太祖皇后張氏早崩，開平二年，追封賢妃，至乾化二年十一月二十三日，追冊曰元貞皇后。
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that Empress Zhang died young; in Kaiping 2 she was posthumously made Worthy Consort, and on 23 xi of month 11, Qianhua 2, was elevated to Empress Yuanzhen.
entries.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s empress Zhang died early; in Kaiping year 2 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Worthy Consort; on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month of Qianhua year 2 she was posthumously invested as Empress Yuanzhen.

entries.zh: 又，《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖魏國夫人張氏，碭山富室女，父蕤，曾為宋州刺史。
entries.en: The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 adds that Lady Zhang of Wei came from a rich Dangshan family; her father Rui had served as Songzhou prefect.
entries.literal: Moreover, 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s Lady of Wei, née Zhang, was daughter of a wealthy house in Dangshan; her father Rui had once been prefect of Song.

entries.zh: 溫時聞張有姿色，私心傾慕，有麗華之歎。
entries.en: Hearing of Zhang’s beauty, Wen secretly yearned for her and sighed like a man longing for Lady Lihua.
entries.literal: When Wen heard that Zhang had beauty, he secretly admired her and sighed with the lament of Lady Lihua.

entries.zh: 及溫在同州，得張於兵間，因以婦禮納之。
entries.en: At Tongzhou Wen took Zhang from among the captives and married her properly.
entries.literal: When Wen was at Tongzhou he obtained Zhang amid the troops and took her in with the rites of a wife.

entries.zh: 溫以其宿款，深加禮異。
entries.en: Wen had loved her long before; he honored her with exceptional ceremony.
entries.literal: Because of his long-standing affection, Wen treated her with deep courtesy and distinction.

entries.zh: 張賢明有禮，溫雖虎狼其心，亦所景伏。
entries.en: Zhang was intelligent and decorous; even Wen’s brutal nature bowed before her.
entries.literal: Zhang was wise, clear, and observant of ritual; though Wen had the heart of a wolf or tiger, toward her he also bowed in awe.

entries.zh: 每軍謀國計，必先延訪。
entries.en: On every matter of war or statecraft he consulted her first.
entries.literal: Whenever there was military planning or state policy, he first extended invitation to consult her.

entries.zh: 或已出師，中途有所不可，張氏一介請旋，如期而至，其信重如此。
entries.en: If a campaign had to be recalled mid-march, a single word from Zhang brought the army back on time—such was her authority.
entries.literal: Even after the army had marched out, if midway something could not proceed, Zhang with a single message would request return—and arrived on the appointed day; such was the trust placed in her.

entries.zh: 初收兗、鄆，得朱瑾妻，溫告之曰：「彼既無依，寓於輜車。」
entries.en: After the capture of Yan and Yun they took Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her travel in the supply train."
entries.literal: When Yan and Yun were first taken, they obtained Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her lodge in the baggage train."

entries.zh: 張氏遣人召之，瑾妻再拜，張氏答拜泣下，謂之曰：「兗、鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故尋戈，致吾姒如此。
entries.en: Zhang sent for her; Jin’s wife bowed low, Zhang bowed back in tears and said: "Yan and Yun share our house’s surname—brothers quarreled over a trifle, and you, my sister-in-law, suffer for it.
entries.literal: Zhang sent someone to summon her; Jin’s wife bowed twice, Zhang returned the bow weeping, and said to her: "Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Minister of Works; between brothers a small quarrel drew swords, and my sister-in-law has come to this.

entries.zh: 設不幸汴州失守，妾亦似吾姒之今日也。」
entries.en: Should Bian fall, I would share your fate."
entries.literal: If by misfortune Bianzhou should fall, I too would be as my sister-in-law is today."

entries.zh: 又泣下，乃度為尼，張恒給其費。
entries.en: Weeping again, she had Jin’s wife take the veil and paid her upkeep.
entries.literal: Again she wept, then had her tonsured as a nun; Zhang constantly supplied her expenses.

entries.zh: 張既卒，繼寵者非人，及僭號後，大縱朋淫，骨肉聚麀，帷薄荒穢，以致友珪之禍，起於婦人。
entries.en: After Zhang’s death Wen’s favorites were unworthy; once emperor he plunged into orgies and incest until Yougui’s revolt—born of a woman’s grievance.
entries.literal: After Zhang died, those who succeeded her in favor were not worthy; after he assumed the imperial title he greatly indulged debauchery with companions, kin coupled like beasts, curtains and screens foul—so that Yougui’s disaster arose from a woman.

entries.zh: 始能以柔婉之德，製豺虎之心，如張氏者，不亦賢乎！
entries.en: At first, with soft grace she tamed a tiger’s heart—was Zhang not truly virtuous?
entries.literal: To begin with, by gentle and yielding virtue to restrain the heart of wolf and tiger—as with Zhang—is she not worthy?

entries.zh: 又，案《五代會要》所載，內職有梁太祖昭儀陳氏、昭容李氏，《歐陽史》並見《家人傳》。）〉
entries.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 also lists the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li, both noted in Ouyang Xiu’s 《New History》 Family section.)〉
entries.literal: Moreover, examining what the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records, among inner offices were the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li; both appear in 《Ouyang’s History》 in the Family Biographies.)〉

entries.zh: 末帝德妃張氏。
entries.en: Virtue Consort Zhang, consort of the Last Emperor.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor’s Virtue Consort, née Zhang.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：少帝妃張氏，乾化五年九月二十四日，冊為德妃，其夕薨。
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that the Young Emperor’s consort Zhang was created Virtue Consort on 24 ix, Qianhua 5, and died the same night.
entries.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Young Emperor’s consort Zhang, on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of Qianhua year 5, was invested as Virtue Consort; that very evening she died.

entries.zh: 案《歐陽史次妃郭氏傳》云：晉天福三年，詔太社先藏罪人首級，許親屬收葬，乃出末帝首，遣右衛將軍安崇阮與妃同葬。
entries.en: Ouyang’s 《History》 biography of Consort Guo notes that in Tianfu 3 Jin permitted families to claim criminals’ heads from the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released and General An Chongruan buried it with his consort.
entries.literal: Examining 《Ouyang’s History》, in the biography of the second consort Guo it says: In Jin Tianfu year 3 an edict allowed kin to bury heads of criminals long stored at the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was produced, and Right Palace Guard general An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.

entries.zh: 妃卒洛陽。
entries.en: She died at Luoyang.
entries.literal: The consort died at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 又案：《五代史》無外戚傳。
entries.en: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 contains no treatise on imperial in-laws.
entries.literal: Moreover, examining: 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has no biography of maternal kin.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》云：梁太祖長女安陽公主，降羅廷規，開平二年八月追封。
entries.en: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 lists the Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess Anyang, married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping 2, month 8.
entries.literal: 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess of Anyang, was married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping year 2, eighth month.

entries.zh: 長樂公主，降趙岩，開平元年五月十一日封。
entries.en: Princess Changle wed Zhao Yan and was enfeoffed on 11 v, Kaiping 1.
entries.literal: Princess of Changle was married to Zhao Yan and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.

entries.zh: 普寧公主，降昭祚王氏，開平元年五月十一日封。
entries.en: Princess Puning wed Wang Zhaozuo on the same date, 11 v, Kaiping 1.
entries.literal: Princess of Puning was married to Wang Zhaozuo and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.

entries.zh: 金華公主，開平二年十月封。
entries.en: Princess Jinhua was enfeoffed in month 10, Kaiping 2.
entries.literal: Princess of Jinhua was enfeoffed in the tenth month of Kaiping year 2.

entries.zh: 真寧公主，乾化三年十月五日封。
entries.en: Princess Zhenning was enfeoffed on 5 x, Qianhua 3.
entries.literal: Princess of Zhenning was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the tenth month of Qianhua year 3.

entries.zh: 少帝長女壽春公主，乾化三年四月五日封。
entries.en: The Young Emperor’s eldest, Princess Shouchun, was enfeoffed on 5 iv, Qianhua 3.
entries.literal: The Young Emperor’s eldest daughter, Princess of Shouchun, was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the fourth month of Qianhua year 3.

entries.zh: 第二女壽昌公主，貞明元年九月二十三日封。
entries.en: His second daughter, Princess Shouchang, was enfeoffed on 23 ix, Zhenming 1.
entries.literal: His second daughter, Princess of Shouchang, was enfeoffed on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of Zhenming year 1.

entries.zh: 今考《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣列傳》云：羅廷規尚安陽公主，又尚金華公主。
entries.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 collation cites the 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married both Princess Anyang and Princess Jinhua.
entries.literal: Now examining 《Comprehensive Mirror: Collation of Variants》, which cites 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married Princess of Anyang and also married Princess of Jinhua.

entries.zh: 《薛史羅紹威傳》亦載開平四年，詔金華公主出家為尼。
entries.en: The 《Old History》 biography of Luo Shaowei likewise records an edict in Kaiping 4 ordering Princess Jinhua to take the veil.
entries.literal: 《Xue History》, biography of Luo Shaowei, also records that in Kaiping year 4 an edict had Princess of Jinhua leave the world and become a nun.

entries.zh: 是金華公主實歸羅氏，而《五代會要》不載亦闕文也。）〉
entries.en: So Jinhua truly married into the Luo house, though the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 omits it—another gap in the record.)〉
entries.literal: Thus Princess of Jinhua in fact went to the Luo clan, while the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 does not record it—again a lacuna in the text.)〉

entries.zh: 廣王全昱，太祖長兄，受禪後封。
entries.en: Quan Yu, Prince of Guang, was the Founder's eldest brother and received his princely title when the dynasty was founded.
entries.literal: Prince of Guang Quan Yu was the Founder's eldest brother; enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.

entries.zh: 乾化元年，還睢陽，命內臣拜餞都外。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianhua he went back to Suiyang; court eunuchs were sent outside the city to bid him farewell.
entries.literal: In Qianhua year 1, he returned to Suiyang; the Emperor ordered inner-court attendants to perform farewell rites outside the capital.

entries.zh: 王出宿至於偃師，仍詔其子衡王友諒侍從以歸。
entries.en: On the road he spent a night at Yanshi; an edict also directed his son You Liang, Prince of Heng, to escort him home.
entries.literal: The Prince departed, lodged overnight reaching Yanshi; moreover an edict ordered his son Prince of Heng You Liang to attend and accompany him home.

entries.zh: 庶人篡位，授宋州節度使。
entries.en: After the commoner (Zhu Yougui) usurped the throne, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Songzhou.
entries.literal: When the commoner usurped the throne, [he] was appointed military commissioner of Songzhou.

entries.zh: 貞明二年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the second year of Zhenming.
entries.literal: In Zhenming year 2, he died.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：全昱，贈尚書令，諡德靖。
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the posthumous title Dejing.
entries.literal: (《Five Dynasties Essentials》: Quan Yu was posthumously given Minister of Works; posthumous title Dejing.

entries.zh: 《五代史闕文》：全昱，梁祖之兄也。
entries.en: The 《Lacunae of the History of the Five Dynasties》 identifies Quan Yu as the Liang founder's elder brother.
entries.literal: 《Lacunae of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Quan Yu was elder brother of the Liang Founder.

entries.zh: 既受禪，宮中開宴，惟親王得與。
entries.en: Once the dynasty was founded, palace feasts were held to which only imperial princes were admitted.
entries.literal: After receiving the abdication, the palace held banquets; only imperial princes were permitted to attend.

entries.zh: 因為博戲，全昱酒酣，忽起取骰子擊盆迸散，大呼梁祖曰：「朱三，汝碭山一民，因天下饑荒，入黃巢作賊，天子用汝為四鎮節度使，富貴足矣，何故滅他李家三百年社稷，稱王稱朕，吾不忍見血吾族矣，安用博為！」
entries.en: At dice play Quan Yu, drunk, leaped up, smashed the bowl with his dice, and shouted at the Liang founder: "Zhu Third! You were a peasant from Dangshan who joined Huang Chao's rebels in famine; the throne made you lord of four circuits—that should have been enough. Why wipe out the Li dynasty's three-century altars and call yourself king and Son of Heaven? I will not watch our family slaughtered—why gamble at all!"
entries.literal: During gambling, Quan Yu, wine deep, suddenly rose, took dice and struck the bowl scattering them, loudly calling to the Liang Founder: "Zhu Third! You, a commoner of Dangshan—because the realm suffered famine you entered Huang Chao's bandits as a thief; the Son of Heaven used you as military commissioner of four circuits—wealth and honor are enough—why destroy the Li family's three hundred years of state altars, call yourself king and emperor? I cannot bear to see our clan's blood shed—what need for gambling!"

entries.zh: 梁祖不悅而罷。
entries.en: The founder took offense and ended the feast.
entries.literal: The Liang Founder was displeased and broke up [the party].

entries.zh: 臣護按《梁史》《廣王全昱傳》曰：昱樸野，常呼帝為「三」。
entries.en: Your subject Hu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."
entries.literal: Your subject Hu annotates: 《History of Liang》《Biography of Prince of Guang Quan Yu》 says: Yu was rustic and uncouth, often calling the Emperor "Third."

entries.zh: 宮中博戲之事諱之。
entries.en: Gambling in the palace became a forbidden topic.
entries.literal: Palace gambling affairs were tabooed.

entries.zh: 夫梁祖弑二君，弑一皇后，名臣被害者不可勝紀。
entries.en: The Liang founder had killed two emperors and an empress, and slaughtered famous ministers beyond count.
entries.literal: Now the Liang Founder murdered two sovereigns, murdered one empress; famous ministers murdered—countless beyond recording.

entries.zh: 及莊宗即位，盡誅朱氏，惟全昱先令終。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to power he killed the whole Zhu house; only Quan Yu had already died in his bed.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he executed the entire Zhu clan; only Quan Yu had earlier died a natural death.

entries.zh: 至道初，知單州有稱廣王之後與尼訟田者，豈以一言之善，獨存其嗣耶！）〉
entries.en: Early in the Zhidao reign a man at Shan prefecture claiming descent from Prince Guang sued a nun over land—did a single honest speech alone spare his line?!)〉
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, it was known at Shan prefecture there was one claiming to be descendant of Prince of Guang disputing fields with a nun—could it be that for one good saying alone his posterity was preserved?!)〉

entries.zh: 安王友寧，字安仁，少習詩禮，長喜兵法，有倜儻之風。
entries.en: You Ning, Prince of An (courtesy name Anren), studied the classics as a boy and warfare as a man, with a dashing temper.
entries.literal: Prince of An You Ning, style Anren, in youth studied Poetry and Rites, in maturity delighted in military methods, had a bold and unbounded air.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮汴，累署軍職，每因出師，多命統驍果以從。
entries.en: Under the Founder's rule at Bian he rose through army commands and usually led elite troops on campaign.
entries.literal: When the Founder governed Bian, repeatedly appointed to army posts; whenever campaigns arose he was often ordered to lead fierce warriors in attendance.

entries.zh: 及擒秦宗權，太祖令友寧監送宗權西獻於長安，詔加檢校右散騎常侍、行右監門衛將軍。
entries.en: After the capture of Qin Zongquan the Founder sent You Ning to escort him to Chang'an; the court promoted him to acting palace attendant and acting gate guard commander.
entries.literal: When Qin Zongquan was captured, the Founder ordered You Ning to supervise escorting Zongquan west to present at Chang'an; edict added acting Right Palace Attendant and Acting Right Supervisor of the Palace Gate Guards.

entries.zh: 自是繼立軍功，累官至檢校司空兼龔、柳二州刺史。
entries.en: Thereafter he won repeated victories and rose to acting Minister of Works while governing Gong and Liu.
entries.literal: From then on he repeatedly achieved military merit, rising through offices to acting Minister of Works concurrently prefect of Gong and Liu prefectures.

entries.zh: 太祖駐軍岐下，遣友寧領所部兵先歸梁苑，以備守禦。
entries.en: While the Founder camped near Qi he sent You Ning ahead with his division to secure the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: The Founder encamped below Qi, dispatched You Ning to lead his troops first back to Liang Garden to prepare defense.

entries.zh: 屬青帥王師範構亂，以關東諸鎮兵悉在岐、隴，欲乘虛竊發，自齊、魯至於華下，羅布奸黨，皆詐以委輸貢奉為名，陰與淮夷、並門結好。
entries.en: Wang Shifan of Qingzhou rebelled, hoping to exploit the absence of eastern armies at Qi and Long: from Shandong to the Guanzhong frontier he planted agents posing as tribute missions while secretly courting Huainan and Bingzhou.
entries.literal: At this time the Qing military commissioner Wang Shifan plotted rebellion; because all eastern-pass troops were at Qi and Long, he wished to strike while the realm was empty—from Qi and Lu down to below Hua he spread secret agents, all falsely under the name of delivering tribute, while secretly allying with Huaiyi and Bingmen.
