entries.zh: 會有青人詣裴迪言其狀，迪以事告，友寧不俟命乃率兵萬餘人東討。
entries.en: A Qing informer told Pei Di, who reported to You Ning; without waiting for orders You Ning marched east with ten thousand men.
entries.literal: It happened a man of Qing came to Pei Di and reported the situation; Di told the affair, and You Ning without awaiting orders led more than ten thousand troops east to punish.

entries.zh: 師範遣其弟將兵圍齊州。
entries.en: Shifan sent his brother to lay siege to Qi prefecture.
entries.literal: Shifan sent his younger brother to lead troops and besiege Qi prefecture.

entries.zh: 友寧引兵救之，青寇大敗，奪馬四千蹄，斬首數千級。
entries.en: You Ning relieved the city and routed the Qing forces, taking four thousand horses and thousands of heads.
entries.literal: You Ning led troops to rescue; Qing bandits were greatly defeated, seizing four thousand horse hooves, beheading several thousand.

entries.zh: 及昭宗歸長安，朝廷議迎駕功，友寧授嶺南西道節度使，加特進、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。
entries.en: After Emperor Zhaozong's return to Chang'an the court rewarded those who had escorted him: You Ning became military commissioner of Lingnan West, Special Grandee, and acting Minister of Works, with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, the court discussed merit in welcoming the imperial carriage; You Ning was given military commissioner of Lingnan West Circuit, advanced to Special Grandee and acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.

entries.zh: 時青寇數千，越險潛伏，欲入兗州。
entries.en: Several thousand Qing raiders were moving through the hills toward Yanzhou.
entries.literal: At the time several thousand Qing bandits, crossing rugged terrain, lay hidden, wishing to enter Yan prefecture.

entries.zh: 友寧知之，伏兵於兗南邀之，大破賊眾，竟無免者。
entries.en: You Ning set an ambush south of Yan, destroyed the force, and left no survivor.
entries.literal: You Ning knew it, ambushed troops south of Yan to intercept them, greatly defeating the bandit host; in the end none escaped.

entries.zh: 自是兗壁危窘，友寧督諸軍進逼營兵。
entries.en: With Yanzhou hard pressed, You Ning drove his columns against the rebel encampment.
entries.literal: From then on the Yan ramparts were perilous and strained; You Ning supervised the armies pressing the rebel camp.

entries.zh: 首攻博昌縣，月餘未能拔。
entries.en: He first assaulted Bochang but failed to capture it for over a month.
entries.literal: First attacking Bochang county, more than a month unable to take it.

entries.zh: 太祖怒，遣劉捍督戰。
entries.en: The Founder, enraged, sent Liu Han to take command of the siege.
entries.literal: The Founder was angry and dispatched Liu Han to supervise the battle.

entries.zh: 友寧乃下俘民眾十餘萬，各領負木石、牽牛驢，於城南為土山。
entries.en: You Ning drove more than a hundred thousand captives—each hauling timber and stone behind oxen and donkeys—to heap an assault ramp south of the walls.
entries.literal: You Ning then released more than a hundred thousand captive common people, each leading and bearing timber and stone, driving oxen and donkeys, building an earthen mound south of the city.

entries.zh: 既至，合人畜木石排而築之，冤枉之聲，聞數十里。
entries.en: As the ramp rose, human and animal labor was driven in ranks; wails of the dying carried for miles.
entries.literal: When complete, men and beasts, timber and stone were ranged and piled; cries of injustice were heard for several tens of li.

entries.zh: 俄而城陷，盡屠其邑人，清河為之不流。
entries.en: The city soon fell and every inhabitant was massacred until the Qing River ran thick with blood.
entries.literal: Shortly the city fell; the entire populace of the district was slaughtered, and the Qing River ceased to flow.

entries.zh: 及進迫寇壘，與青人戰於石樓，王師小卻，友寧旁自峻阜馳騎以赴敵，所乘馬蹶而仆，遂沒於陣。
entries.en: Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when the royal army slightly wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.
entries.literal: When advancing to press the rebel fortress, fighting Qing troops at Shilou, Wang's army slightly retreated; You Ning from a steep height galloped to meet the enemy, his mount stumbled and fell, and he perished in the formation.

entries.zh: 友寧將戰之前日，有大白蛇蟠於帳中，友寧心惡之，既而果遇禍焉。
entries.en: On the eve of battle a great white snake coiled in his tent—an omen he loathed—and the next day he was killed.
entries.literal: The day before You Ning was to fight, a great white serpent coiled in his tent; You Ning's heart hated it, and afterward he indeed met calamity.

entries.zh: 密王友倫，幼聰悟，喜筆劄，曉聲律。
entries.en: You Lun, Prince of Mi, was bright as a child, loved literature, and had an ear for music.
entries.literal: Prince of Mi You Lun, in youth clever and perceptive, delighted in letters, understood musical tones.

entries.zh: 及長，好騎射，有經度之智，太祖每奇之，曰：「吾家千里駒也。」
entries.en: As a man he excelled at horsemanship and archery and showed sound judgment; the Founder often praised him: "He is the fleet steed of our clan."
entries.literal: When grown, he loved riding and shooting, had the wisdom of governance; the Founder often marveled at him, saying: "A thousand-li colt of our house."

entries.zh: 年十九，為宣武軍校。
entries.en: He entered the Xuanwu Army as an officer at nineteen.
entries.literal: At nineteen he became an officer of the Xuanwu Army.

entries.zh: 景福初，充元從騎軍都將，尋表為右武衛將軍，漸委戎事。
entries.en: Early in Jingfu he commanded the emperor's mounted guard, was soon made Right Martial Guard general, and gradually took on field command.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, he served as commander of the personal cavalry guard; soon memorialized as Right Martial Guard general, gradually entrusted with military affairs.

entries.zh: 太祖征兗、鄆，友倫勒所部兵收聚糧穀，以濟軍須。
entries.en: During campaigns in Yan and Yun he gathered grain for the army.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Yan and Yun, You Lun led his troops to gather grain to supply the army.

entries.zh: 幽、滄軍至內黃，友倫前鋒夜渡河擊賊，奪馬千匹，擒斬甚眾。
entries.en: When Youzhou and Cangzhou forces reached Neihuang, his vanguard crossed the river at night, took a thousand horses, and killed or captured many.
entries.literal: You and Cang troops reached Neihuang; You Lun's vanguard crossed the river by night to strike bandits, seizing a thousand horses, capturing and beheading many.

entries.zh: 因引兵往八議關，卒逢晉軍萬餘騎，友倫乃分布兵士，多設疑軍。
entries.en: Marching toward Bayi Pass he met more than ten thousand Jin horsemen and spread his men in feigned formations.
entries.literal: Thereupon he led troops toward Bayi Pass, suddenly encountering more than ten thousand Jin cavalry; You Lun then distributed soldiers, setting many decoy units.

entries.zh: 因聲鼓誓眾，士伍奮躍，追斬數十里。
entries.en: He drummed the troops to an oath, they charged, and the pursuit ran for miles.
entries.literal: Thereupon beating drums and swearing the host, the ranks leaped forward, pursuing and beheading for several tens of li.

entries.zh: 其後，李罕之請以上黨來歸，為晉軍所圍。
entries.en: Later Li Hanzhi offered to surrender Shangdang but was besieged by Jin forces.
entries.literal: Afterward Li Hanzhi requested to submit Shangdang and return to allegiance, but was besieged by Jin troops.

entries.zh: 太祖遣友倫總步騎數萬，越險救應，遂大破晉軍。
entries.en: The Founder sent You Lun with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry over difficult ground to relieve him and routed the Jin army.
entries.literal: The Founder dispatched You Lun to command several tens of thousands of foot and horse, crossing rugged terrain to rescue and respond, and greatly defeated Jin troops.

entries.zh: 唐朝加檢校司空、守藤州刺史。
entries.en: Tang promoted him to acting Minister of Works and acting prefect of Teng.
entries.literal: The Tang court added acting Minister of Works, acting prefect of Teng prefecture.

entries.zh: 天復元年，岐、隴用兵，晉人乘虛侵於北鄙。
entries.en: In Tianfu 1, while war raged at Qi and Long, Jin raiders struck the northern border.
entries.literal: In Tianfu year 1, troops were used at Qi and Long; Jin men took advantage of emptiness to invade the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 友倫率徒兵三萬徑往礬山，晉人望塵奔逸。
entries.en: You Lun marched thirty thousand foot soldiers to Fanshan and the Jin army fled at his approach.
entries.literal: You Lun led thirty thousand foot soldiers straight to Fanshan; Jin men fled at sight of dust.

entries.zh: 友倫與氏叔琮等躡其轍，追至太原，摩壘挑戰，獲牛馬萬餘。
entries.en: With Shi Shuzong he pursued to Taiyuan, challenged the walls, and seized more than ten thousand cattle and horses.
entries.literal: You Lun with Shi Shuzong and others followed their tracks, pursuing to Taiyuan, pressing the ramparts and challenging battle, obtaining more than ten thousand cattle and horses.

entries.zh: 二年，領所部兵西赴鳳翔，前後累接戰。
entries.en: In the second year he marched west to Fengxiang and fought a series of engagements.
entries.literal: Year 2, he led his troops west to rush to Fengxiang, before and after repeatedly joining battle.

entries.zh: 三年，昭宗歸長安，製授友倫寧遠軍節度使、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。
entries.en: In the third year, after Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, You Lun became Ningyuan military commissioner and acting Minister of Works with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.
entries.literal: Year 3, Zhaozong returned to Chang'an; by decree You Lun was made military commissioner of the Ningyuan Army, acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.

entries.zh: 及太祖東歸，留友倫宿衛京師。
entries.en: When the Founder went east he left You Lun to guard the capital.
entries.literal: When the Founder returned east, he left You Lun to garrison and guard the capital.

entries.zh: 歲餘，因會賓擊鞠，墜馬而卒。
entries.en: More than a year later he fell from his horse during a polo match with guests and died.
entries.literal: After more than a year, while meeting guests playing cuju, he fell from a horse and died.

entries.zh: 昭宗輟視朝一日，詔贈太傅，歸葬於碭山縣。
entries.en: Zhaozong mourned him with a day without court and posthumously made him Grand Tutor; he was buried in Dangshan.
entries.literal: Zhaozong suspended court audience for one day, edict posthumously gave Grand Tutor, burial returned to Dangshan county.

entries.zh: 郴王友裕，字端夫，太祖長子也。
entries.en: You Yu, Prince of Chen (courtesy name Duanfu), was the Founder's eldest son.
entries.literal: Prince of Chen You Yu, style Duanfu, was the Founder's eldest son.

entries.zh: 幼善射禦，從太祖征伐，性寬厚，頗得士心。
entries.en: Trained in archery and horsemanship, he campaigned with the Founder, won troops by his easy manner.
entries.literal: In youth skilled at shooting and driving; followed the Founder in campaigns; nature generous and thick, considerably won soldiers' hearts.

entries.zh: 唐中和中，太祖會並帥李克用攻圍華州，賊將黃鄴固守甚堅。
entries.en: In Tang Zhonghe the Founder and Li Keyong besieged Hua prefecture, where the rebel Huang Ye held the walls stubbornly.
entries.literal: In the Zhonghe era of Tang, the Founder joined Bing military commissioner Li Keyong to besiege Hua prefecture; bandit general Huang Ye held firm defense extremely solid.

entries.zh: 俄有一人登陴大詈，克用令北騎連射，終不能中，命友裕射之，應弦而斃。
entries.en: A man on the wall shouted abuse; Keyong's northern archers could not bring him down, but You Yu's arrow killed him on the first shot.
entries.literal: Shortly a man ascended the wall and cursed loudly; Keyong ordered northern cavalry to shoot in succession, ultimately unable to hit; he ordered You Yu to shoot, and at the bowstring's release [the man] died.

entries.zh: 大軍喜噪，聲震山谷，克用因以良弓百矢遺焉。
entries.en: The army roared until the hills echoed; Keyong rewarded him with a hundred fine bows.
entries.literal: The great army rejoiced and clamored, sound shaking mountains and valleys; Keyong therefore with a hundred good bows and arrows gifted him.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮汴，表為宣武軍牙校。
entries.en: When the Founder held Bian he was made a junior officer of the Xuanwu Army.
entries.literal: When the Founder governed Bian, memorialized as Xuanwu Army junior officer.

entries.zh: 及蔡賊殄滅，朝廷議功，加檢校左僕射，尋為牙內馬步都指揮使。
entries.en: After the destruction of the Cai rebels the court rewarded him with acting Left Vice Minister of Works and soon commander of the inner horse-and-foot guard.
entries.literal: When Cai bandits were exterminated, the court discussed merit, added acting Left Vice Minister of Works, soon made commander of all inner palace horse and foot.

entries.zh: 景福元年，總大軍伐徐。
entries.en: In Jingfu 1 he led the main force against Xu.
entries.literal: Jingfu year 1, commanded the great army to attack Xu.

entries.zh: 時朱瑾領兗、鄆之眾，為徐戎外援，陣於彭門南石佛山下。
entries.en: Zhu Jin of Yan and Yun brought allied troops to aid Xu and drew up south of Pengmen at Stone Buddha Mountain.
entries.literal: At the time Zhu Jin led Yan and Yun hosts as outer support for Xu bandits, arrayed below Stone Buddha Mountain south of Peng Gate.

entries.zh: 友裕縱兵擊之，斬獲甚眾，瑾領殘黨宵遁。
entries.en: You Yu attacked, inflicted heavy losses, and Jin fled by night with the survivors.
entries.literal: You Yu loosed troops to strike them, beheading and capturing very many; Jin led the remnant party to flee by night.

entries.zh: 時都虞候朱友恭羽書聞於太祖，誣友裕按兵不追賊，太祖大怒，因驛騎傳符，令裨將龐師古代友裕為帥，仍令按劾其事。
entries.en: Chief Commandant Zhu You Gong reported that You Yu had held his men back; the Founder, furious, sent Pang Shigu by relay to replace him and investigate.
entries.literal: At the time Chief Commandant Zhu You Gong's urgent dispatch reached the Founder, falsely accusing You Yu of holding troops and not pursuing bandits; the Founder was greatly angry, and through post-horse transmitted tally, ordered deputy general Pang Shigu to replace You Yu as commander, still ordering investigation of the affair.

entries.zh: 會使人誤致書於友裕，友裕懼，遂以數騎遁於山中。
entries.en: A courier misdelivered the order to You Yu, who fled into the hills with a few riders.
entries.literal: It happened the messenger mistakenly delivered the letter to You Yu; You Yu was afraid, and with several horsemen fled into the mountains.

entries.zh: 尋詣廣王於輝州，以訴其冤。
entries.en: He soon sought out Prince Guang at Hui prefecture to plead his case.
entries.literal: Shortly he went to Prince of Guang at Hui prefecture to plead his injustice.

entries.zh: 賴元貞皇后聞而召之，令束身歸汴，力為營救，太祖乃舍之，令權知許州。
entries.en: Empress Yuanzhen intervened, had him return to Bian in custody, and secured his pardon; the Founder then put him in temporary charge of Xu.
entries.literal: Relying on Empress Yuanzhen hearing and summoning him, ordered him to bind himself and return to Bian, vigorously pleading rescue; the Founder then released him, ordered temporary charge of Xu prefecture.

entries.zh: 乾寧二年，加檢校司空，尋為武寧軍節度留後。
entries.en: In Qianning 2 he was made acting Minister of Works and soon acting Wuning military commissioner.
entries.literal: Qianning year 2, added acting Minister of Works, soon made acting military commissioner of the Wuning Army.

entries.zh: 四年，太祖下東平，改天平軍留後，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: In the fourth year, after the Founder took Dongping, he became acting Tianping commissioner with acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Year 4, the Founder descended on Dongping, changed to acting Tianping Army commissioner, added acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 光啟元年，再領許州。
entries.en: In Guangqi 1 he again governed Xu.
entries.literal: Guangqi year 1, again held Xu prefecture.

entries.zh: 天復初，為奉國軍節度留後。
entries.en: Early in Tianfu he became acting Fengguo military commissioner.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, made acting military commissioner of the Fengguo Army.

entries.zh: 太祖兼鎮河中，以友裕為護國軍節度留後，尋遷華州節度使，加檢校太保、興德尹。
entries.en: When the Founder also held Hezhong he made You Yu acting Huguo commissioner, then Hua commissioner, Grand Guardian, and Xingde intendant.
entries.literal: When the Founder concurrently governed Hezhong, made You Yu acting Huguo Army military commissioner, soon moved to Hua military commissioner, added acting Grand Guardian and Xingde Intendant.

entries.zh: 天祐元年七月，兼行營都統，領步騎數萬，經略邠、岐。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Tianyou 1 he became campaign commander-in-chief with tens of thousands of troops operating in Bin and Qi.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 1, seventh month, concurrently acting commander of all campaign armies, leading several tens of thousands of foot and horse, administering Bin and Qi.

entries.zh: 十月，友裕有疾，將校乃謀旋師，尋卒於梨園，歸葬東京。
entries.en: In the tenth month he fell ill; his officers prepared to withdraw, and he died at Liyuan and was buried in the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Tenth month, You Yu had illness; officers then plotted to withdraw the army; shortly he died at Liyuan, burial returned to the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 開平初，追贈郴王。
entries.en: Early in Kaiping he was posthumously created Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping, posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 乾化三年，又贈太師。
entries.en: In Qianhua 3 he was further posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Qianhua year 3, again posthumously given Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 博王友文，本姓康，名勤，太祖養以為子，受禪後封為王。
entries.en: You Wen, Prince of Bo, born Kang Qin, was adopted by the Founder and enfeoffed after the founding of the dynasty.
entries.literal: Prince of Bo You Wen, original surname Kang, name Qin; the Founder adopted him as son, after receiving the abdication enfeoffed as prince.

entries.zh: 為東京留守，嗜酒，頗怠於為政。
entries.en: As Eastern Capital regent he drank heavily and neglected government.
entries.literal: Served as regent of the Eastern Capital, addicted to wine, considerably slack in governing.

entries.zh: 友珪弑逆，並殺友文。
entries.en: When Zhu Yougui murdered the Founder he killed You Wen as well.
entries.literal: Zhu Yougui murdered and usurped; together killed You Wen.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，盡復官爵。
entries.en: The Last Emperor restored his titles in full.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, fully restored office and rank.

entries.zh: 友珪，小字遙喜，母失其姓，本亳州營妓也。
entries.en: Zhu Yougui, childhood name Yaoxi, was born to a Bozhou camp courtesan whose family name is unknown.
entries.literal: Zhu Yougui, childhood name Yaoxi; mother lost her surname—originally a camp courtesan of Bozhou.

entries.zh: 唐光啟中，帝徇地亳州，召而侍寢。
entries.en: During Tang Guangqi, while campaigning in Bozhou, the Founder took her to his bed.
entries.literal: In the Guangqi era of Tang, the Emperor toured Bozhou territory, summoned her to attend his bed.

entries.zh: 月餘，將舍之而去，以娠告。
entries.en: After a month he was about to leave when she told him she was with child.
entries.literal: After more than a month, about to leave her and depart, she reported pregnancy.

entries.zh: 是時，元貞皇后賢而有寵，帝素憚之，由是不果攜歸大梁，因留亳州，以別宅貯之。
entries.en: The Founder feared his capable consort Yuanzhen and never brought the woman to the capital, keeping her in a separate house at Bozhou.
entries.literal: At the time Empress Yuanzhen was worthy and held favor; the Emperor always feared her, and therefore did not succeed in bringing [the mother] back to Great Liang, but left her at Bozhou, storing her in a separate residence.

entries.zh: 及期，妓以生男來告，帝喜，故字之曰遙喜。
entries.en: When she bore a son he was delighted and gave the boy the childhood name Yaoxi.
entries.literal: When the term came, the courtesan reported bearing a male child; the Emperor rejoiced, therefore styled him Yaoxi.

entries.zh: 後迎歸汴。
entries.en: Mother and son were later brought to Bian.
entries.literal: Later welcomed back to Bian.

entries.zh: 受禪後封郢王。
entries.en: After the founding of the dynasty he was created Prince of Ying.
entries.literal: After receiving the abdication, enfeoffed Prince of Ying.

entries.zh: 開平四年十月，檢校司徒，充左右控鶴都指揮使，兼管四蕃將軍。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Kaiping 4 he became acting Minister of Works, commander of the Left and Right Crane-Control Guards, and overseer of the Four Barbarian Generals.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 4, tenth month, acting Minister of Works, served as commander of the Left and Right Crane-Control Guards, concurrently supervising the Four Barbarian Generals.

entries.zh: 乾化元年，充諸軍都虞候。
entries.en: In Qianhua 1 he was made chief commandant of all armies.
entries.literal: Qianhua year 1, served as chief commandant of all armies.

entries.zh: 二年，弑太祖篡位，均王以兵討之，自殺，追廢為庶人。
entries.en: In the second year he murdered the Founder and seized the throne; Prince of Jun marched against him; he committed suicide and was posthumously degraded to commoner.
entries.literal: Year 2, murdered the Founder and usurped the throne; Prince of Jun led troops to punish him; he killed himself, posthumously deposed as commoner.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：郢王友珪，開平元年五月九日封，至乾化二年六月三日篡位，偽改鳳曆元年。
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Zhu Yougui, Prince of Ying, was enfeoffed on the ninth day of the fifth month of Kaiping 1, usurped on the third day of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, and proclaimed the false era Fengli.
entries.literal: (《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says: Prince of Ying Zhu Yougui, on the ninth day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1 enfeoffed, until the third day of the sixth month of Qianhua year 2 usurped the throne, falsely changed to Fengli year 1.

entries.zh: 三月十七日，京城軍亂，侍衛袁象先率兵入宮，友珪自殺。
entries.en: On the seventeenth day of the third month the capital garrison mutinied; Palace Guard Yuan Xiangxian stormed the palace and Zhu Yougui took his own life.
entries.literal: Third month, seventeenth day, capital army mutiny; Palace Guard Yuan Xiangxian led troops into the palace; Zhu Yougui killed himself.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，追削為庶人。
entries.en: The Lesser Emperor posthumously reduced him to commoner status.
entries.literal: When the Lesser Emperor took the throne, posthumously stripped to commoner.

entries.zh: 又載：周廣順中，張昭修實錄，奏云：梁末帝之上，有郢王友珪，篡弑居位，未有紀錄，請依《宋書》劉劭例，書為「元凶友珪」。
entries.en: The same source adds: In Later Zhou Guangshun, Zhang Zhao revised the Veritable Records and proposed that Zhu Yougui, who had murdered his way to the throne above the Last Emperor, be entered—as with Liu Shao in the 《History of Song》—under the title "Arch-rebel Zhu Yougui."
entries.literal: Also recorded: In the Guangshun era of Zhou, Zhang Zhao revised the Veritable Records, memorializing: Above the Last Emperor of Liang was Prince of Ying Zhu Yougui, who usurped and murdered and held the throne, with no record yet—request according to 《Song History》 Liu Shao's precedent to write as "Arch-rebel Zhu Yougui."

entries.zh: 案《梁實錄》今無考。）〉
entries.en: The 《Liang Veritable Records》 cited here are no longer extant.)〉
entries.literal: Case: 《Liang Veritable Records》 now has no examination.)〉

entries.zh: 福王友璋，太祖第五子，受禪後封。
entries.en: You Zhang, Prince of Fu, was the Founder's fifth son and received his title at the founding.
entries.literal: Prince of Fu You Zhang, the Founder's fifth son, enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.

entries.zh: 賀王友雍，太祖第六子，受禪後封。
entries.en: You Yong, Prince of He, was the Founder's sixth son and was enfeoffed when the dynasty was founded.
entries.literal: Prince of He You Yong, the Founder's sixth son, enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.

entries.zh: 建王友徽，太祖第七子，受禪後封。
entries.en: You Hui, Prince of Jian, was the Founder's seventh son and received his title at the founding.
entries.literal: Prince of Jian You Hui, the Founder's seventh son, enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.

entries.zh: 康王友孜，太祖第八子，末帝即位後封，以反誅。
entries.en: You Zi, Prince of Kang, the Founder's eighth son, was enfeoffed under the Last Emperor and executed for treason.
entries.literal: Prince of Kang You Zi, the Founder's eighth son, enfeoffed after the Last Emperor took the throne, executed for rebellion.

entries.zh: 開平初，有司上言曰：「東漢受命，伯升預其始謀；
entries.en: Early in Kaiping the authorities reported: "When the Eastern Han received Heaven's mandate, Bo Sheng shared in the founding design;
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping, the relevant office memorialized saying: "When Eastern Han received the Mandate, Bo Sheng took part in the initial planning;

entries.zh: 西周尚親，叔虞荷其封邑。
entries.en: the Western Zhou cherished kin, and Shu Yu received his fief.
entries.literal: Western Zhou honored kin; Shu Yu bore its enfeoffed domain.

entries.zh: 故皇兄存，凋零霜露，綿曆歲時，恩莫逮於陟岡，禮方宏於事日。
entries.en: Our elder imperial brother Cun lies long in the grave; years have passed without fitting rites at his tomb.
entries.literal: Therefore the imperial elder brother Cun, withered by frost and dew, spanning years in time—kindness could not reach the mound on the hill, rites should be enlarged for the day of service.

entries.zh: 皇侄故邕州節度使友寧、故容州節度使友倫，頃因締構，俱習韜鈐，並以戰功，歿於王事，永言帶礪，合議封崇。」
entries.en: Imperial nephews You Ning, late commissioner of Yong, and You Lun, late commissioner of Rong, were trained in war from the founding days and died in service; they deserve posthumous honors befitting founders of the house."
entries.literal: Imperial nephew, late Yongzhou military commissioner You Ning, late Rongzhou military commissioner You Lun—recently because of founding the structure, both studied military manuals, and both through battle merit died in royal service; forever speaking of belt and flint, together we should discuss enfeoffment and elevation."

entries.zh: 於是存追封朗王，友寧追封安王，友倫追封密王。
entries.en: Cun was posthumously created Prince of Lang, You Ning Prince of An, and You Lun Prince of Mi.
entries.literal: Thereupon Cun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lang, You Ning posthumously Prince of An, You Lun posthumously Prince of Mi.

entries.zh: 既而為茂貞左右石簡顒等間之，免其軍政，寓於岐下，掩關曆年。
entries.en: Courtiers slandered him; he lived under Qi in seclusion for years.
entries.literal: Soon he was set aside from military government by Maozhen's close associates Shi Jian'e and others; he dwelt under Qi, shutting his gate for years.

entries.zh: 茂貞猶子繼崇鎮秦州，因來寧覲，言知俊途窮至此，不宜以讒嫉見疑，茂貞乃誅簡顒等以安其心。
entries.en: Nephew Jichong pleaded for Zhijun; Maozhen executed the slanderers to reassure him.
entries.literal: Maozhen's nephew Jichong governed Qin prefecture; coming to pay respects he said Zhijun, driven to extremity, should not be suspected through slander; Maozhen then executed Jian'e and others to calm his heart.

entries.zh: 繼崇又請令知俊挈家居秦州，以就豐給，茂貞從之。
entries.en: Jichong invited Zhijun's family to Qin; Maozhen agreed.
entries.literal: Jichong again asked that Zhijun be allowed to bring his household to live at Qin to enjoy abundance; Maozhen consented.

entries.zh: 未幾，邠州亂，茂貞命知俊討之。
entries.en: Bin rebelled; Maozhen sent Zhijun to suppress it.
entries.literal: Before long, Bin prefecture rebelled; Maozhen ordered Zhijun to suppress it.

entries.zh: 時邠州都校李保衡納款於朝廷，末帝遣霍彥威率眾先入於邠，知俊遂圍其城，半載不能下。
entries.en: Li Baoheng had surrendered to Liang; Huo Yanwei entered Bin first; Zhijun besieged it six months in vain.
entries.literal: At that time Bin's commander Li Baoheng had submitted to the court; the Last Emperor sent Huo Yanwei with troops to enter Bin first; Zhijun then besieged the city; half a year could not take it.

entries.zh: 會李繼崇以秦州降於蜀，知俊妻孥皆遷於成都，遂解邠州之圍而歸岐陽。
entries.en: Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu; Zhijun's family was taken to Chengdu; he abandoned Bin and returned to Qiyang.
entries.literal: When Li Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu, Zhijun's wife and children were all moved to Chengdu; he then lifted the siege of Bin and returned to Qiyang.

entries.zh: 以舉家入蜀，終慮猜忌，因與親信百餘人夜斬關奔蜀。
entries.en: Fearing suspicion after his family went to Shu, he fled by night with a hundred men.
entries.literal: Because his whole household had entered Shu, he finally feared suspicion; with more than a hundred trusted men he cut the pass by night and fled to Shu.

entries.zh: 王建待之甚至，即授偽武信軍節度使，尋命將兵伐岐，不克，班師，因圍隴州，獲其帥桑宏誌以歸。
entries.en: Wang Jian honored him as Wuxin commissioner; he failed against Qi, took Long and Sang Hongzhi, and returned.
entries.literal: Wang Jian treated him to the utmost; he was at once made false Wuxin military commissioner; soon he was ordered to lead troops against Qi without success and withdrew; then he besieged Long prefecture, took its commander Sang Hongzhi, and returned.

entries.zh: 久之，復命為都統，再領軍伐岐。
entries.en: Later he was made overall commander and marched on Qi again.
entries.literal: After a long time he was again ordered as overall commander and again led troops against Qi.

entries.zh: 時部將皆王建舊人，多違節度，不成功而還，蜀人因而毀之。
entries.en: At the time his subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they returned without success, and the Shu people slandered him for it.
entries.literal: At that time the subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they did not succeed and returned; Shu men therefore slandered him.

entries.zh: 先是，王建雖加寵待，然亦忌之，嘗謂近侍曰：「吾漸衰耗，恒思身後。
entries.en: Jian favored yet feared him and told aides, "I age and think of what follows my death.
entries.literal: Earlier, though Wang Jian added favor and treatment, he also was jealous; he once told close attendants: "I gradually decline and constantly think of after my death.

entries.zh: 劉知俊非爾輩能駕馭，不如早為之所。」
entries.en: Zhijun is not for you to control—deal with him early."
entries.literal: Liu Zhijun is not what you can drive and rein—better early do something about him."

entries.zh: 又嫉其名者於裏巷間作謠言云：「黑牛出圈棕繩斷。」
entries.en: Enemies spread a rhyme: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope snaps."
entries.literal: Those who envied his name also made a street song in the lanes: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope breaks."

entries.zh: 知俊色黔而醜生，棕繩者，王氏子孫皆以「宗」、「承」為名，故以此構之。
entries.en: Zhijun was dark and ugly; "palm rope" punned on Wang names using Zong and Cheng.
entries.literal: Zhijun's complexion was dark and he was born ugly; "palm rope" means Wang's sons and grandsons all used "Zong" and "Cheng" in their names—thus they framed him with this.

entries.zh: 偽蜀天漢元年冬十二月，建遣人捕知俊，斬於成都府之炭市。
entries.en: False-Shu Tianhan 1, month 12, Jian had him beheaded at Chengdu's charcoal market.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of winter of false-Shu Tianhan year 1, Jian sent men to seize Zhijun and behead him at the charcoal market of Chengdu prefecture.

entries.zh: 及王衍嗣偽位，以其子嗣禋尚偽峨眉長公主，拜駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Under Wang Yan his son Sichen married the Emei princess and became chief son-in-law.
entries.literal: When Wang Yan succeeded the false throne, his son Sichen married the false Emei senior princess and was appointed Chief Son-in-law.

entries.zh: 後唐同光末，隨例遷於洛，卒。
entries.en: At Later Tang Tongguang he moved to Luoyang and died.
entries.literal: At the end of Later Tang Tongguang, following precedent he moved to Luo and died.

entries.zh: 朱瑄，宋州下邑人也。
entries.en: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.
entries.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.

entries.zh: 父慶，里之豪右，以攻剽販鹽為事，吏捕之伏法。
entries.en: His father Qing, a village strongman, lived by banditry and salt-running until the authorities caught and executed him.
entries.literal: His father Qing was a local magnate who made his living by raiding and smuggling salt; officials seized him and he was executed by law.

entries.zh: 瑄坐父罪以笞免。
entries.en: Xuan was caned and dismissed because of his father's offense.
entries.literal: Xuan, implicated in his father's crime, was flogged and released.

entries.zh: 因入王敬武軍為小校。
entries.en: He then joined Wang Jingwu's forces as a low-ranking officer.
entries.literal: Thereupon he entered Wang Jingwu's army as a junior officer.

entries.zh: 唐中和二年，諫議大夫張浚征兵於青州，敬武遣將曹全晸率軍赴之，以瑄隸焉。
entries.en: In Tang Zhonghe year 2, Censor Zhang Jun mustered troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu dispatched Cao Quanzhen's army to answer the call, and Xuan went with it.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe of Tang, Remonstrance Censor Zhang Jun raised troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu sent the general Cao Quanzhen with an army to join him, with Xuan attached to that force.

entries.zh: 以戰功累遷列校。
entries.en: Repeated victories raised him through the ranks of field officers.
entries.literal: Through battle merit he was repeatedly promoted among the column commanders.

entries.zh: 賊敗出關，全晸以本軍還鎮。
entries.en: After the rebels broke and fled beyond the passes, Quanzhen marched his own troops back to their post.
entries.literal: When the rebels were defeated and driven out of the passes, Quanzhen returned to garrison with his original army.

entries.zh: 會鄆帥薛崇卒，部將崔君預據城叛，全晸攻之，殺君預自為留後。
entries.en: Yan commander Xue Chong died; his subordinate Cui Junyu rebelled and held the city. Quanzhen stormed it, killed Junyu, and declared himself acting commissioner.
entries.literal: When Yan military commissioner Xue Chong died, his officer Cui Junyu seized the city in revolt; Quanzhen attacked, killed Junyu, and made himself acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 瑄以功授濮州刺史、鄆州馬步軍都將。
entries.en: For his service Xuan received Pu prefecture and command of Yanzhou's combined cavalry and infantry.
entries.literal: Xuan, for merit, was appointed prefect of Pu and commander of Yan's horse-and-foot forces.

entries.zh: 光啟初，魏博韓允中攻鄆，全晸為其所害。
entries.en: Early in the Guangqi reign Han Yunzhong of Weibo attacked Yan, and Quanzhen fell in the fighting.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Weibo's Han Yunzhong attacked Yan; Quanzhen was killed by him.

entries.zh: 瑄據城自固。
entries.en: Xuan barricaded himself inside the city.
entries.literal: Xuan held the city and fortified himself.

entries.zh: 三軍推為留後。
entries.en: The army proclaimed him acting commissioner.
entries.literal: The three armies pushed him to be acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 允中敗，朝廷以瑄為天平軍節度使，累加官至檢校太尉、同平章事。
entries.en: After Yunzhong's defeat the throne appointed Xuan commissioner of Tianping; he eventually reached honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
entries.literal: When Yunzhong was defeated, the court made Xuan military commissioner of Tianping, and he rose in rank to honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

entries.zh: 太祖初鎮大梁，兵威未振，連歲為秦宗權所圍，士不解甲，危殆日數四。
entries.en: When the Founder first governed Daliang his power was still weak; Qin Zongquan besieged him year after year, troops never out of mail, danger threatening several times daily.
entries.literal: When the Founder first held Daliang, his military prestige was not yet established; year after year he was besieged by Qin Zongquan, his men never doffing armor, peril coming several times a day.

entries.zh: 太祖以瑄同宗，早兄事之，乃遣使求援於瑄。
entries.en: Calling Xuan kin, the Founder had long treated him as an elder brother and now begged him for help.
entries.literal: The Founder, treating Xuan as a clansman, had long addressed him as elder brother, and sent envoys to seek aid from Xuan.

entries.zh: 光啟末，宗權急攻大梁，瑄與弟瑾率兗、鄆之師來援，大敗蔡賊，解圍而遁。
entries.en: Late in Guangqi, Zongquan hammered Daliang; Xuan and Jin marched troops from Yan and Yanzhou, crushed the Cai army, broke the siege, and retired.
entries.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Zongquan pressed the attack on Daliang; Xuan and his younger brother Jin led Yan and Yanzhou forces to the rescue, routed the Cai rebels, lifted the siege, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 太祖感其力，厚禮以歸之。
entries.en: Grateful for the rescue, the Founder honored them lavishly on their departure.
entries.literal: The Founder, grateful for their effort, sent them home with rich courtesy.

entries.zh: 先是，瑄、瑾駐於大梁，睹太祖軍士驍勇，私心愛之。
entries.en: While stationed at Daliang, Xuan and Jin had seen how fierce the Founder's troops were and coveted them.
entries.literal: Earlier, while Xuan and Jin were encamped at Daliang, they saw the Founder's soldiers were fierce, and secretly admired them.

entries.zh: 及歸，厚懸金帛於界上以誘焉。
entries.en: Back home they posted rich bounties of gold and silk along the frontier to lure deserters.
entries.literal: On returning home they hung out heavy rewards of gold and silk on the border to entice them.

entries.zh: 諸軍貪其厚利，私遁者甚眾。
entries.en: Many of the Founder's men slipped away for the generous pay.
entries.literal: The various armies, greedy for the rich profit, deserted in great numbers.

entries.zh: 太祖移牒以讓之，瑄來詞不遜，由是始構隙焉。
entries.en: The Founder rebuked him in writing; Xuan answered rudely, and enmity began.
entries.literal: The Founder sent a written protest; Xuan came with insolent words, and from this the rift began.

entries.zh: 及秦宗權敗，太祖移軍攻時溥於徐州。
entries.en: After Zongquan's fall the Founder turned his armies on Shi Pu at Xuzhou.
entries.literal: When Qin Zongquan was defeated, the Founder shifted his army to attack Shi Pu at Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 時瑄方右溥，乃遣使來告太祖曰：「巢、權繼為蛇虺，毒螫中原，與君把臂同盟，輔車相依。
entries.en: Xuan was then siding with Pu and wrote the Founder: "Chao and Zongquan were serpents in turn, stinging the heartland; we clasped arms as allies, dependent as chariot wheels.
entries.literal: At that time Xuan was backing Pu, and sent an envoy to tell the Founder: "Huang Chao and Zongquan in succession were vipers, poisoning the Central Plain; you and I clasped arms in alliance, cheek by jowl as in a chariot.

entries.zh: 今賊已平殄，人粗聊生，吾弟宜念遠圖，不可自相魚肉。
entries.en: The rebels are gone and men barely survive; brother, keep the larger design—do not devour each other.
entries.literal: Now the bandits are wiped out and people barely live again; my younger brother should think of the long view and not tear one another apart like fish and flesh.

entries.zh: 或行人之失辭，疆吏之逾法，可以理遣，未得便睽和好。
entries.en: A courier's slip or a frontier officer's breach can be reasoned away; do not break our bond lightly.
entries.literal: Perhaps a traveler's loose word or a border officer's excess may be settled by reason; you must not lightly break the good understanding.

entries.zh: 投鼠忌器，弟幸思之。」
entries.en: Strike the rat but spare the vessel—brother, weigh that."
entries.literal: When casting at a rat, one fears the vessel—brother, think on this."

entries.zh: 太祖方怒時溥通於孫儒，不從其言。
entries.en: The Founder, furious that Pu was colluding with Sun Ru, ignored the plea.
entries.literal: The Founder was then angry that Pu was in league with Sun Ru and did not heed his words.

entries.zh: 及龐師古攻徐州，瑄出師來援，太祖深銜之。
entries.en: When Pang Shigu besieged Xuzhou, Xuan came to Pu's aid, and the Founder never forgave it.
entries.literal: When Pang Shigu attacked Xuzhou, Xuan marched out to aid Pu; the Founder deeply resented it.

entries.zh: 徐既平，太祖並兵以攻鄆，自景福元年冬遣朱友裕領軍渡濟，至乾寧三年宿軍齊、鄆間，大小凡數十戰，語在《太祖紀》中。
entries.en: Once Xuzhou fell he massed troops against Yan: from winter of Jingfu 1 Zhu Youyu crossed the Ji, and by Qianning 3 armies lay between Qi and Yan in dozens of clashes recorded in the 《Founder's Annals》.
entries.literal: After Xu was pacified, the Founder united his forces to attack Yan; from winter of Jingfu year 1 he sent Zhu Youyu with an army across the Ji, until in Qianning year 3 he camped between Qi and Yan, fighting great and small battles several tens of times, as told in the 《Founder's Annals》.

entries.zh: 自是野無人耕，屬城悉為我有。
entries.en: Fields lay empty; every subordinate city fell to him.
entries.literal: From then the countryside was untilled; all dependent prefectures became his.

entries.zh: 瑄乃遣人求救於太原，李克用遣其將李承嗣、史儼等援之。
entries.en: Xuan appealed to Taiyuan; Li Keyong sent Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and other generals to help.
entries.literal: Xuan then sent men to beg rescue from Taiyuan; Li Keyong dispatched his generals Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and others to aid him.

entries.zh: 尋為羅宏信所扼，援路既絕，瑄、瑾竟敗。
entries.en: Luo Hongxin soon blocked the road; aid failed, and Xuan and Jin were ruined.
entries.literal: Soon they were choked off by Luo Hongxin; the relief route cut, Xuan and Jin were defeated at last.

entries.zh: 乾寧四年正月，龐師古攻陷鄆州，遁至中都北，匿於民家，為其所箠，並妻榮氏擒之來獻，俱斬於汴橋下。
entries.en: In Qianning 4, month 1, Pang Shigu captured Yan. Xuan fled north of Zhongdu and hid in a peasant home; the family thrashed and seized him and Lady Rong, and both were executed at Bian Bridge.
entries.literal: In the first month of Qianning year 4, Pang Shigu took Yanzhou; fleeing north of Zhongdu, hiding in a commoner's house, he was beaten by the household, and together with his wife Lady Rong was seized and presented; both were beheaded below Bian Bridge.

entries.zh: 韓建，字佐時，許州長社人。
entries.en: Han Jian, styled Zuoshi, came from Changshe in Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Han Jian, style name Zuoshi, was a native of Changshe in Xu prefecture.

entries.zh: 父叔豐，世為牙校。
entries.en: His father Shufeng served for generations as a guard officer.
entries.literal: His father Shufeng for generations were guard officers.

entries.zh: 初，秦宗權之據蔡州，招合亡命，建隸為軍士，累轉至小校。
entries.en: When Qin Zongquan held Caizhou he recruited fugitives; Jian joined as a soldier and rose to junior officer.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Qin Zongquan held Caizhou, he gathered fugitives; Jian was attached as a soldier and rose through ranks to junior officer.

entries.zh: 唐中和初，忠武監軍楊復光起兵於蔡，宗權遣其將鹿宴宏赴之，建與里人王建俱隸宴宏軍，入援京師。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Tang dynasty's Zhonghe era, Yang Fuguang, military supervisor of the Zhongwu Army, raised troops at Cai. Qin Zongquan sent his general Lu Yanhong to join him; Han Jian and his fellow townsman Wang Jian then joined Yanhong's army and entered the capital to reinforce it.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe of Tang, Zhongwu overseer Yang Fuguang raised troops at Cai; Zongquan sent his general Lu Yanhong to go; Jian and fellow townsman Wang Jian both were attached to Yanhong's army and entered the capital to aid.

entries.zh: 賊平，復光暴卒。
entries.en: After the rebels fell, Fuguang died suddenly.
entries.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Fuguang died suddenly.

entries.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，宴宏率所部赴行在。
entries.en: With Xizong in Shu, Yanhong marched to the court.
entries.literal: At that time Xizong was in Shu; Yanhong led his command to the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 路出南山，因攻剽郡邑，據有興元。
entries.en: Marching through the Qinling he raided towns and seized Xingyuan.
entries.literal: The road passed through the southern mountains; he therefore raided prefectures and districts and held Xingyuan.

entries.zh: 宴宏自為留後，以建為蜀郡刺史。
entries.en: Yanhong made himself commissioner and appointed Jian Shu prefect.
entries.literal: Yanhong made himself acting commissioner and made Jian prefect of Shu Commandery.

entries.zh: 唐軍容使田令孜密遣人誘建，啖以厚利，建時懼為宴宏所並，乃率所部歸行在，令孜補為神策都校、金吾將軍，出為潼關防禦使兼華州刺史。
entries.en: Tian Lingzi lured Jian away from Yan Hong with rich promises. Fearing that Yan Hong would absorb him, Jian led his troops back to the traveling court, where Lingzi appointed him Shence column commander and Golden Guard general, then sent him out as Tong Pass defense commissioner and concurrently prefect of Huazhou.
entries.literal: Tang Army Rong Commissioner Tian Lingzi secretly sent men to entice Jian, feeding him rich profit; Jian then feared being absorbed by Yanhong, led his command to return to the traveling palace; Lingzi supplemented him as Shence column commander and Golden Guard general, sent out as Tong Pass defense commissioner and concurrent Hua prefect.

entries.zh: 河、潼經大寇之後，戶口流散，建披荊棘，辟汙萊，勸課農事，樹植蔬果，出入閭裏，親問疾苦，不數年，流亡畢復，軍民充實。
entries.en: After the ravaging of He and Tong he cleared land, urged farming, and within years restored refugees and prosperity.
entries.literal: After great banditry in He and Tong, households scattered in flight; Jian cleared brambles, opened foul wasteland, urged farming, planted fruits and vegetables, went in and out of lanes, personally asked of suffering and illness—in several years exiles all returned and army and people were full.

entries.zh: 建比不知書，治郡之暇，日課學習。
entries.en: Illiterate at first, he studied daily while governing.
entries.literal: Jian by nature did not know books; in leisure from governing the prefecture he daily set lessons in study.

entries.zh: 遣人於器皿、床榻之上各題其名，建視之既熟，乃漸通文字。
entries.en: He had the names of vessels, beds, and couches written on them and, once familiar with the labels, gradually learned to read.
entries.literal: He sent men to label his name on vessels, beds, and couches; when Jian had viewed them until familiar, he gradually penetrated written characters.

entries.zh: 俄遷華商節度、潼關守捉等使，累加檢校太尉、平章事。
entries.en: Soon he became Hua-Shang commissioner, Tong Pass commander, honorary Grand Marshal, and chief minister.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred Hua-Shang military commissioner and Tong Pass guard commissioner and the like, repeatedly raised to honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

entries.zh: 天復元年十一月，宦官韓全誨迫天子幸鳳翔，建亦預其謀。
entries.en: Tianfu 1, month 11, Han Quanhui seized the emperor for Fengxiang; Jian helped.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of Tianfu year 1 eunuch Han Quanhui forced the Son of Heaven to go to Fengxiang; Jian also shared the plot.

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，自河中引軍而西。
entries.en: The Founder marched west from Hezhong.
entries.literal: The Founder heard it and led troops from Hezhong west.

entries.zh: 前鋒至同州，建判官司馬鄴以城降，遂移軍迫華州，建懼乞降。
entries.en: The vanguard reached Tongzhou, where Jian's staff officer Sima Ye surrendered the city. The Founder then shifted his army against Huazhou, and Jian, afraid, begged to surrender.
entries.literal: The vanguard reached Tongzhou; Jian's aide Sima Ye surrendered the city; he then shifted troops to press Huazhou; Jian in fear begged surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖責以脅君之罪，建拜伏稱從事李巨川之謀也，太祖即誅巨川。
entries.en: The Founder blamed him for intimidating the throne; Jian blamed Li Juchuan and the Founder killed Juchuan.
entries.literal: The Founder blamed him for coercing the sovereign; Jian bowed prostrate and said it was follower Li Juchuan's plot; the Founder at once executed Juchuan.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：韓建曰：「某不識字，凡朝廷章奏、鄰封書檄，皆巨川為之。」
entries.en: (The 《Northern Dream》 says Jian admitted, "I cannot read; Juchuan wrote all my court papers and neighboring letters."
entries.literal: (The 《Fragmentary Tales of the Northern Dream》: Han Jian said: "I do not know characters; all court memorials and neighboring letters were done by Juchuan."

entries.zh: 因斬之。
entries.en: So he was beheaded.
entries.literal: Therefore he was beheaded.

entries.zh: 《新唐書· 李巨川傳》云：巨川詣軍門納款，因言當世利害。
entries.en: The 《New Book of Tang》 says Juchuan came to submit and argued policy.
entries.literal: The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of Li Juchuan》 says: Juchuan came to the army gate to submit and spoke on current benefit and harm.

entries.zh: 全忠屬官敬翔以文翰事左右，疑巨川用則全忠待己或衰，乃詭說曰：「巨川誠奇才，顧不利主人，若何！」
entries.en: Jing Xiang feared rivalry and told Quanzhong, "Juchuan is truly a rare talent, but he is not good to his lord—what then!"
entries.literal: Quanzhong's officer Jing Xiang handled documents at his side and suspected if Juchuan were used Quanzhong's treatment of himself might decline, and therefore spoke deceitfully: "Juchuan is truly a rare talent, but he is not good to his lord—what then!"

entries.zh: 是日，全忠殺之。）〉
entries.en: That day Quanzhong killed him.)〉
entries.literal: That day Quanzhong killed him.)〉

entries.zh: 太祖與建素有軍中昆弟之契，及見，其怒驟息，尋表建為許州節度使。
entries.en: They had long been bound as brothers-in-arms. On seeing Jian, his anger quickly subsided, and before long he petitioned for Jian to be appointed military governor of Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: The Founder and Jian from old had army brotherhood pact; when he saw him his anger suddenly ceased; soon he memorialized Jian as Xu military commissioner.

entries.zh: 昭宗東遷，以建為佑國軍節度使、京兆尹。
entries.en: When the emperor moved east Jian became Youguo commissioner and Jingzhao prefect.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved east, he made Jian Youguo military commissioner and Jingzhao prefect.

entries.zh: 車駕至陝，召太祖與建侍宴，宮妓奏樂，何皇后舉觴以賜太祖，建躡足，太祖遽起曰：「臣醉不任。」
entries.en: At a feast in Shan the empress toasted the Founder; Jian trod his foot and the Founder hastily rose saying, "Your subject is drunk and cannot bear it."
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Shan, the Founder and Jian were summoned to attend a feast; palace performers played music; Empress He raised a cup to bestow on the Founder; Jian trod on his foot; the Founder hastily rose saying: "Your subject is drunk and cannot bear it."

entries.zh: 偽若顛仆即去。
entries.en: He staggered away as if drunk.
entries.literal: He pretended as if to fall headlong and went away.

entries.zh: 建私謂太祖曰：「上與宮人附耳而語，幕下有兵仗聲，恐圖王爾。」
entries.en: Jian whispered to the Founder, "The emperor and empress are whispering; I heard weapons beneath the curtain—they may be plotting against you."
entries.literal: Jian privately told the Founder: "The sovereign and palace people speak ear to ear; below the curtain there is the sound of weapons—perhaps they plot against you, Prince."

entries.zh: 天祐三年，改青州節度使。
entries.en: Tianyou 3 he was made Qing commissioner.
entries.literal: In Tianyou year 3 he was changed to Qing military commissioner.

entries.zh: 及受禪，征為司徒、平章事，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
entries.en: At the abdication he became Minister of Works, chief minister, and salt-and-iron transport commissioner.
entries.literal: When he received the abdication he was summoned as Minister of Works and co-equal chief minister, full commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.

entries.zh: 開平二年，加侍中，充建昌宮使。
entries.en: Kaiping 2 he became Palace Secretary and Jianchang Palace commissioner.
entries.literal: In Kaiping year 2 he was made Palace Secretary and full Jianchang Palace commissioner.

entries.zh: 三年，郊祀於洛，以建為大禮使。
entries.en: Year 3 he directed the Luo suburban rites.
entries.literal: In year 3 suburban sacrifice at Luo, he made Jian great rites commissioner.

entries.zh: 建為上宰，每謁見，時有直言。
entries.en: As chief minister he sometimes spoke bluntly to the throne.
entries.literal: Jian as chief minister at each audience sometimes spoke straight words.

entries.zh: 太祖為性剛嚴，群下將迎不暇，待建稍異，故優容之。
entries.en: The stern Founder indulged Jian more than other ministers.
entries.literal: The Founder by nature was stern and strict; subordinates could not answer in time; toward Jian he was slightly different, therefore indulged him.

entries.zh: 九月，冊拜太保，罷知政事。
entries.en: In the ninth month he was appointed Grand Guardian and left the government.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he was formally appointed Grand Guardian and removed from participation in government.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：開平三年十月，詔曰：太保韓建，每月旦、十五日入閣稱賀，即令赴朝參，餘時弗入見。
entries.en: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the tenth month of Kaiping 3, an edict ordered Grand Guardian Han Jian to enter the hall to offer congratulations on the first and fifteenth of each month and then attend court; at other times he was not to appear.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》: In the tenth month of Kaiping 3, an edict ordered Grand Guardian Han Jian to enter the hall to offer congratulations on the first and fifteenth of each month and then attend court; at other times he was not to appear.

entries.zh: 示優禮也。）〉
entries.en: A mark of favor.)〉
entries.literal: Showing preferential courtesy.)〉

entries.zh: 四年三月，除匡國軍節度使、陳許蔡觀察使，仍令中書不議除替。
entries.en: In the third month of the fourth year, he took Kuangguo and Chen-Xu-Cai with a pledge of no replacement.
entries.literal: In the third month of year 4 he was made Kuangguo military commissioner and Chen-Xu-Cai surveillance commissioner, still ordering the Secretariat not to discuss replacement.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：乾化元年正月，敕：許昌雄鎮，太保韓建，朕用以布政，民耕盜止，久居其位，庶可勝殘矣。
entries.en: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the first month of Qianhua 1, an edict praised the powerful stronghold of Xuchang and Grand Guardian Han Jian's government there: the people tilled their fields, banditry ceased, and by remaining long in office he might overcome lawlessness.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》: In the first month of Qianhua 1, an edict praised the powerful stronghold of Xuchang and Grand Guardian Han Jian's government there: the people tilled their fields, banditry ceased, and by remaining long in office he might overcome lawlessness.

entries.zh: 宜令中書門下不計年月，勿議替。）〉
entries.en: The court would not discuss replacing him.)〉
entries.literal: It is fitting to order the Secretariat and Chancellery not to count months and not discuss replacement.)〉

entries.zh: 乾化二年六月，朝廷新有內難，人心動搖，部將張厚因作亂，害建於衙署，時年五十八。
entries.en: Qianhua 2, month 6, subordinate Zhang Hou murdered Jian in the yamen at fifty-eight.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of Qianhua year 2 the court newly had inner turmoil, hearts were shaken, and subordinate Zhang Hou because of it made disorder and killed Jian in the yamen at age fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 李罕之，陳州項城人。
entries.en: Li Hanzhi came from Xiangcheng in Chenzhou.
entries.literal: Li Hanzhi was a Xiangcheng man of Chen prefecture.

entries.zh: 父文，世田家。
entries.en: His father Wen was a farming family for generations.
entries.literal: His father Wen for generations were farming families.

entries.zh: 罕之拳勇趫捷，力兼數人。
entries.en: Hanzhi was a fierce fighter of several men's strength.
entries.literal: Hanzhi was fist-brave, nimble, and swift; his strength matched several men.

entries.zh: 少學為儒，不成，又落發為僧，以其無賴，所至不容。
entries.en: He failed as a scholar, became a monk, and was driven out everywhere for unruliness.
entries.literal: In youth he studied to be a Ruist; it did not succeed; he again shaved his head and became a monk; because he was unruly, wherever he went he was not tolerated.

entries.zh: 曾乞食於酸棗縣，自旦至晡，無與之者，乃擲缽於地，毀棄僧衣，亡命為盜。
entries.en: Begging all day at Suozao without alms, he smashed his bowl, cast off his robes, and became a bandit.
entries.literal: Once he begged food at Suozao county from dawn to dusk with none giving; he then threw his bowl to the ground, destroyed and cast off monk's robes, and fled as an outlaw to become a bandit.

entries.zh: 會黃巢起曹、濮，罕之因合徒作剽，漸至魁首。
entries.en: When Huang Chao rose he raided and became a bandit chief.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao rose in Cao and Pu, Hanzhi therefore joined followers in raiding and gradually reached chieftain.

entries.zh: 及賊巢渡江，罕之因以兵將背賊歸於唐，高駢錄其功，表為光州刺史。
entries.en: When Chao crossed the Yangzi he defected to Tang; Gao Pian made him Guang commissioner.
entries.literal: When bandit Chao crossed the river, Hanzhi therefore with troops turned his back on the bandits and returned to Tang; Gao Pian recorded his merit and memorialized him Guang prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 歲餘，為蔡賊秦宗權寇迫，不能守，乃棄郡歸項城，收合餘眾，依河陽諸葛爽，爽署為懷州刺史。
entries.en: Zongquan drove him from Guang; he regrouped at Xiangcheng and Zhuge Shuang made him Huai commissioner.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was harried by Cai bandit Qin Zongquan and could not hold it; he then abandoned the prefecture and returned to Xiangcheng, gathered remnant masses, relied on Heyang's Zhuge Shuang, and Shuang appointed him Huai prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 光啟初，僖宗以爽為東南面招討，以擊宗權，爽乃表罕之為副，令將兵屯宋州。
entries.en: At the beginning of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong appointed Zhuge Shuang commander of the campaign forces on the southeastern front against Qin Zongquan. Shuang then petitioned for Hanzhi to serve as his deputy and sent him with troops to garrison Song Prefecture.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Xizong made Shuang southeast campaign commander to strike Zongquan; Shuang then memorialized Hanzhi as deputy and ordered him to lead troops encamped at Song prefecture.

entries.zh: 蔡寇凶焰日熾，兵鋒不敵。
entries.en: Cai armies grew too strong to face.
entries.literal: Cai bandits' ferocious flame daily grew keener; military edge could not match.

entries.zh: 中和四年，爽表罕之為河南尹、東都留守。
entries.en: Zhonghe 4 Shuang made him Henan prefect and eastern capital regent.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe, Shuang memorialized Hanzhi as Henan prefect and eastern capital acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 是歲，李克用脫上源之難，斂軍西歸，路由洛陽，罕之迎謁，供帳館待甚優，因與克用厚相結托。
entries.en: That year he lavishly hosted Keyong passing through Luoyang and bonded with him.
entries.literal: That year Li Keyong escaped the Shangyuan crisis, gathered troops and returned west; the road passed Luoyang; Hanzhi welcomed and attended, provisions and lodge reception very generous, and therefore thickly joined trust with Keyong.

entries.zh: 時罕之有眾三千，以聖善寺為府。
entries.en: He held three thousand men at Shengyi Monastery.
entries.literal: At that time Hanzhi had masses three thousand, taking Shengyi Monastery as headquarters.

entries.zh: 光啟元年，蔡賊秦宗權遣將孫儒來攻，罕之對壘數月，以兵少備竭，委城而遁，西保於澠池。
entries.en: Guangqi 1 Sun Ru besieged Luoyang; outnumbered, Hanzhi fled to Mianchi.
entries.literal: In Guangqi year 1, Cai bandit Qin Zongquan sent general Sun Ru to attack; Hanzhi faced the camp several months; because soldiers were few and stores exhausted, he abandoned the city and fled, west guarding at Mianchi.

entries.zh: 蔡賊據京城月餘，焚燒宮闕，剽剝居民。
entries.en: Cai rebels held the capital a month, burning palaces and looting the people.
entries.literal: Cai bandits held the capital more than a month, burned palace halls, and plundered residents.

entries.zh: 賊既退去，鞠為煨燼，寂無雞犬之音。
entries.en: They left only ashes and silence.
entries.literal: When the bandits had withdrawn, it was kneaded to embers; silent without chicken or dog sound.

entries.zh: 罕之復引其眾，築壘於市西。
entries.en: Hanzhi rebuilt camps west of the market.
entries.literal: Hanzhi again led his masses and built ramparts west of the market.

entries.zh: 明年冬，諸葛爽死，其將劉經推爽子仲方為帥，經懼罕之難製，自引兵鎮洛陽。
entries.en: The next winter Zhuge Shuang died. His general Liu Jing acclaimed Shuang's son Zhongfang as commander, but, fearing Hanzhi could not be controlled, Liu Jing personally led troops to garrison Luoyang.
entries.literal: The next winter Zhuge Shuang died; his general Liu Jing pushed Shuang's son Zhongfang as commander; Jing feared Hanzhi hard to control and himself led troops to garrison Luoyang.

entries.zh: 罕之部曲有李瑭、郭璆者，情不相葉，欲相圖害，罕之怒，誅璆，軍情由是不睦。
entries.en: Two of Hanzhi's officers, Li Tang and Guo Qiu, were at odds and plotted against each other. Hanzhi angrily executed Qiu, after which dissension spread through the army.
entries.literal: Hanzhi's officers Li Tang and Guo Qiu were not on good terms and wished to harm each other; Hanzhi in anger executed Qiu; army hearts from this were not harmonious.

entries.zh: 劉經因其有間，掩擊罕之於澠池。
entries.en: Liu Jing ambushed him at Mianchi.
entries.literal: Liu Jing took advantage of the rift and struck Hanzhi at Mianchi in ambush.

entries.zh: 軍亂，保乾壕。
entries.en: Defeated, he held Qianhao.
entries.literal: The army was in disorder and guarded at Qianhao.

entries.zh: 經急攻之，為罕之所敗，罕之乘勝追至洛陽。
entries.en: He beat Jing back and pursued to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Jing urgently attacked; he was defeated by Hanzhi; Hanzhi took victory in pursuit to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 時經保敬愛寺，罕之保苑中飛龍廄。
entries.en: Jing held Jing'ai Monastery; Hanzhi held the imperial stable.
entries.literal: At that time Jing guarded Jing'ai Monastery; Hanzhi guarded Flying Dragon Stable in the imperial park.

entries.zh: 罕之激勵其眾攻敬愛寺，數日，因風縱火，盡燔之，經眾奔竄，追斬殆盡。
entries.en: He burned Jing'ai Monastery and slaughtered Jing's army.
entries.literal: Hanzhi roused his masses to attack Jing'ai Monastery; after several days, taking advantage of wind he set fire and burned it all; Jing's troops fled scattered; pursuit beheaded nearly all.

entries.zh: 罕之進逼河陽，營於鞏縣，陳舟於汜水，將渡，諸葛仲方遣將張言率師拒於河上。
entries.en: He pressed Heyang from Gong and crossed toward Sishui until Zhang Yan blocked the river.
entries.literal: Hanzhi advanced to press Heyang, camped at Gong county, arrayed boats at Sishui intending to cross; Zhuge Zhongfang sent general Zhang Yan with troops to resist on the river.

entries.zh: 時仲方年幼，政在劉經，諸將心多不附。
entries.en: Young Zhongfang was ruled by Liu Jing; the officers were divided.
entries.literal: At that time Zhongfang was young; government was in Liu Jing's hands; the generals' hearts mostly did not attach.

entries.zh: 張言密與罕之修好；
entries.en: Zhang Yan secretly allied with Hanzhi;
entries.literal: Zhang Yan secretly made good relations with Hanzhi;

entries.zh: 經知其謀，言懼，引眾渡河歸罕之，因合勢攻河陽，為經所敗，罕之與言退保懷州。
entries.en: Yan crossed to Hanzhi; together they attacked Heyang, lost, and fled to Huai.
entries.literal: Jing knew his plot; Yan in fear led masses across the river to return to Hanzhi, and together attacked Heyang; they were defeated by Jing; Hanzhi and Yan retreated to guard Huai prefecture.

entries.zh: 冬，蔡將孫儒陷河陽。
entries.en: Winter brought Sun Ru's capture of Heyang.
entries.literal: In winter, Cai general Sun Ru took Heyang.

entries.zh: 仲方泛輕舟來奔，孫儒遂自稱節度使。
entries.en: Zhongfang fled by boat; Sun Ru seized Heyang.
entries.literal: Zhongfang came fleeing in a light boat; Sun Ru then declared himself military commissioner.

entries.zh: 俄而蔡賊為我軍所敗，孫儒棄河陽歸蔡。
entries.en: Soon our armies beat Cai and Sun Ru abandoned Heyang.
entries.literal: Soon Cai bandits were defeated by our army; Sun Ru abandoned Heyang and returned to Cai.

entries.zh: 罕之與言收合其眾，求援於太原，李克用遣澤州刺史安金俊率騎助之，遂收河陽。
entries.en: Hanzhi and Yan begged Taiyuan; Keyong sent An Jinjun and they retook Heyang.
entries.literal: Hanzhi and Yan gathered their masses, sought aid from Taiyuan; Li Keyong sent Ze prefecture military commissioner An Jinjun with cavalry to aid them and then recovered Heyang.

entries.zh: 克用表罕之為節度、同平章事；
entries.en: Keyong made Hanzhi commissioner and chief minister;
entries.literal: Keyong memorialized Hanzhi as military commissioner and co-equal chief minister;

entries.zh: 又表言為河南尹、東都留守。
entries.en: He also petitioned for Zhang Yan to be appointed Administrator of Henan and Regent of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: He also petitioned for Zhang Yan to be appointed Administrator of Henan and Regent of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 罕之既與言患難交契，刻臂為盟，永同休戚，如張耳、陳餘之義也。
entries.en: He and Yan swore blood brotherhood like Zhang Er and Chen Yu.
entries.literal: Hanzhi, having with Yan shared hardship and sworn brotherhood, cut arms to covenant, forever sharing fortune and misfortune, like Zhang Er and Chen Yu's righteousness.

entries.zh: 罕之雖有膽決，雄猜翻覆，而撫民禦眾無方略，率多苛暴，性復貪冒，不得士心。
entries.en: Brave yet treacherous and greedy, he ruled without strategy and won no loyalty.
entries.literal: Though Hanzhi had daring resolve and was fierce, suspicious, and changeable, in comforting the people and controlling the masses he had no strategy—mostly harsh and violent, nature again greedy, and could not win officers' hearts.

entries.zh: 既得河陽，出兵攻晉、絳。
entries.en: He then raided Jin and Jiang from Heyang.
entries.literal: Once he had Heyang he sent troops to attack Jin and Jiang.

entries.zh: 時大亂之後，野無耕稼，罕之部下以俘剽為資，啖人作食。
entries.en: His men lived by capture and cannibalism amid famine.
entries.literal: At that time after great disorder the wild had no plowing; Hanzhi's subordinates took captives and plunder as resources and ate people as food.

entries.zh: 絳州刺史王友遇以城降，罕之乃進攻晉州，河中王重盈遣使求援於太祖。
entries.en: Wang Youyu, prefect of Jiang Prefecture, surrendered the city; Hanzhi then advanced to attack Jin Prefecture, and Wang Chongying of Hezhong sent envoys requesting aid from the Founder.
entries.literal: Jiang prefecture military commissioner Wang Youyu surrendered the city; Hanzhi then advanced to attack Jin prefecture; Hezhong's Wang Chongying sent envoys begging aid from the Founder.

entries.zh: 時張言治軍有法，善積聚，勤於播植，軍儲不乏。
entries.en: Zhang Yan supplied grain efficiently while Hanzhi demanded endlessly.
entries.literal: At that time Zhang Yan governed troops with method, was good at accumulation, diligent in planting, and army stores did not lack.

entries.zh: 言輸粟於罕之，以給其軍，罕之求索無限，言頗苦之，力不能應，罕之則錄河南府吏笞責之。
entries.en: When Yan could not meet his demands Hanzhi flogged Henan clerks.
entries.literal: Yan transported grain to Hanzhi to supply his army; Hanzhi's demands were without limit; Yan was quite distressed, strength could not answer; Hanzhi then recorded Henan prefecture clerks and flogged and blamed them.

entries.zh: 東諸侯修貢行在，多為罕之邀留，王重盈苦其侵削，密結張言請圖之。
entries.en: He seized eastern tribute and Chongying plotted with Yan against him.
entries.literal: Eastern feudatories sent tribute to the traveling palace; many were detained by Hanzhi; Wang Chongying suffered his encroachments and secretly joined Zhang Yan to plot against him.

entries.zh: 文德元年春，會罕之盡出其眾攻平陽，言夜出師掩擊河陽，罕之無備，單步僅免，舉族為言所俘。
entries.en: Wende 1 spring Yan seized Heyang while Hanzhi attacked Pingyang; Hanzhi fled alone and his clan was captured.
entries.literal: In spring of Wende year 1, when Hanzhi led out all his masses to attack Pingyang, Yan by night marched troops in ambush strike on Heyang; Hanzhi was unprepared, alone on foot barely escaped, and his whole clan was captured by Yan.

entries.zh: 罕之奔於太原，李克用表為澤州刺史，仍領河陽節度使。
entries.en: Fleeing to Taiyuan, Keyong made him Ze prefect while he still claimed Heyang.
entries.literal: Hanzhi fled to Taiyuan; Li Keyong memorialized him Ze prefecture military commissioner, still holding Heyang military commission.

entries.zh: 三月，克用遣其將李存孝率師三萬助之，來攻懷、孟。
entries.en: Month 3 Keyong sent Li Cunxiao with thirty thousand against Huai and Meng.
entries.literal: In the third month Li Keyong sent his general Li Cunxiao with thirty thousand troops to aid him, coming to attack Huai and Meng.

entries.zh: 城中食盡，備豫皆竭，張言遣其孥入質，且求救於太祖；
entries.en: Starving, Yan sent hostages and begged the Founder;
entries.literal: In the cities food was exhausted and stores all depleted; Zhang Yan sent his wife and children in as hostages and also begged rescue from the Founder;

entries.zh: 太祖遣葛從周、牛存節赴之，逆戰於流河店。
entries.en: the Founder sent Ge Congzhou and Niu Cunjie to Liuhe Store.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Ge Congzhou and Niu Cunjie to go; they met in battle at Liuhe Store.

entries.zh: 會晉將安休休以一軍奔於蔡，存孝引軍而退，罕之保於澤州。
entries.en: When An Xiuxiu defected to Cai, Cunxiao withdrew and Hanzhi held Ze.
entries.literal: When Jin general An Xiuxiu with one army fled to Cai, Cunxiao led troops and withdrew; Hanzhi guarded at Ze prefecture.

entries.zh: 自是罕之日以兵寇鈔懷、孟、晉、絳，數百里內，郡邑無長吏，閭裏無居民。
entries.en: Thereafter he ravaged Huai, Meng, Jin, and Jiang until the land lay empty of officials and people.
entries.literal: From then Hanzhi daily with troops raided and plundered Huai, Meng, Jin, and Jiang; within several hundred li, prefectures and districts had no long officials, lanes and hamlets no residents.

entries.zh: 河內百姓，相結屯寨，或出樵汲，即為俘馘。
entries.en: Hezhong peasants who ventured out for fuel or water were taken.
entries.literal: Hezhong commoners together formed stockaded hamlets; if they went out for fuel or water they became captives.

entries.zh: 雖奇峰絕磴，梯危架險，亦為罕之部眾攻取。
entries.en: Even mountain strongholds fell to his raiders.
entries.literal: Even strange peaks and sheer cliffs, ladders dangerous and bridges perilous, were also taken by Hanzhi's command masses.

entries.zh: 先是，蒲、絳之間有山曰摩雲，邑人立柵於上，以避寇亂；
entries.en: On Mount Cloud-Touching between Pu and Jiang peasants had built a refuge;
entries.literal: Earlier between Pu and Jiang there was a mountain called Cloud-Touching; townspeople set a stockade on it to avoid bandit disorder;

entries.zh: 罕之以百餘人攻下之，軍中因號罕之為李摩雲。
entries.en: he took it with a hundred men and was nicknamed Li Cloud-Touching.
entries.literal: Hanzhi with a hundred-odd men attacked and took it; in the army they therefore called Hanzhi Li Cloud-Touching.

entries.zh: 自是數州之民，屠啖殆盡，荊棘蔽野，煙火斷絕，凡十餘年。
entries.en: For more than ten years his cannibal raids left the region a dead wilderness.
entries.literal: From then the people of several prefectures were slaughtered and eaten nearly clean; brambles covered the wild; smoke and fire cut off—for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 乾寧二年，李克用出師以拒邠、鳳，營於渭北，天子以克用為邠州行營四面都統，克用乃表罕之為副。
entries.en: In Qianning 2 Li Keyong marched out against Binzhou and Fengxiang and camped north of the Wei River. The emperor appointed him commander-in-chief of the Binzhou campaign, and Keyong then petitioned for Hanzhi to serve as his deputy.
entries.literal: In Qianning year 2 Li Keyong led troops to resist Bin and Feng, camped north of Wei; the Son of Heaven made Keyong overall commander on four sides for Bin; Keyong then memorialized Hanzhi as deputy.

entries.zh: 及誅王行瑜，罕之以功授檢校太尉，食邑千戶。
entries.en: After Xingyu's death Hanzhi became honorary Grand Marshal with a thousand-household fief.
entries.literal: When Wang Xingyu was executed, Hanzhi for merit was granted honorary Grand Marshal, fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 罕之自以功多，私謂晉將蓋寓曰：「餘自河陽失守，來依巨蔭，歲月滋久，功效未施。
entries.en: He told Gai Yu, "Since losing Heyang I have relied on great patronage, yet for years I have shown no achievement.
entries.literal: Hanzhi himself thought his merit great and privately told Jin general Gai Yu: "I since losing Heyang have come to rely on great shade; months and years increase yet achievement is not shown.

entries.zh: 比年以來，倦於師旅，所謂老夫耄矣，無能為也。
entries.en: In recent years I have wearied of campaigns—this old man is aged and can do no more.
entries.literal: In recent years I am weary of campaigns—what is called this old man is aged and cannot act.

entries.zh: 望吾王仁湣，太傅哀憐，與一小鎮，休兵養疾，一二年間即歸老菟裘，幸也。」
entries.en: I beg our prince and the Grand Tutor to pity me with a small post to rest my troops and heal my illness—in one or two years I would retire to my rabbit burrow. That would be fortune."
entries.literal: I hope our prince is benevolent and the Grand Tutor takes pity, gives me a small post, rests troops and heals illness—in one or two years I return old to my rabbit burrow—that would be fortunate."

entries.zh: 寓為言之，克用不對。
entries.en: Gai Yu pleaded; Keyong was silent.
entries.literal: Yu spoke for him; Keyong did not answer.

entries.zh: 每藩鎮缺帥，議所不及，罕之私心鬱鬱，蓋寓懼其他圖，亟為論之。
entries.en: Passed over for every command, he brooded until Gai Yu feared treachery and pleaded again.
entries.literal: Whenever a frontier post lacked a commander, discussion did not reach him; Hanzhi in private was depressed; Gai Yu feared he would plot otherwise and urgently argued for him.

entries.zh: 克用曰：「吾於罕之，豈惜一鎮；
entries.en: Keyong said, "It is not that I begrudge him a post;
entries.literal: Keyong said: "My toward Hanzhi—how would I begrudge one post;

entries.zh: 吾有罕之，亦如董卓之有呂布，雄則雄矣，鷹鳥之性，飽則颺去，實懼翻覆毒餘也。」
entries.en: I keep him as Dong Zhuo kept Lü Bu—fierce but untrustworthy when fed."
entries.literal: my having Hanzhi is also like Dong Zhuo's having Lü Bu—fierce he is fierce, but hawk-and-bird nature, sated then flies away; truly I fear he will turn and poison the remainder."

entries.zh: 光化元年十二月，晉之潞帥薛誌勤卒，罕之乘其喪，自澤州率眾徑入潞州，自稱留後，以狀聞於克用曰：「聞誌勤之喪，新帥未至，慮為他盜所窺，不俟命，已屯於潞矣。」
entries.en: Guanghua 1, month 12, after Xue Zhiqin died as Lu commander, Hanzhi marched from Ze into Lu, declared himself commissioner, and told Keyong, "With Zhiqin dead and no successor yet, I feared raiders and garrisoned Lu without orders."
entries.literal: Guanghua year 1, twelfth month, Jin's Lu commander Xue Zhiqin died; Hanzhi seized the mourning interval, led his forces from Ze prefecture straight into Lu prefecture, declared himself acting commissioner, and reported to Keyong: "Hearing of Zhiqin's death, the new commander has not arrived; fearing other bandits may spy, without awaiting orders I have already encamped at Lu."

entries.zh: 克用怒，遣李昭嗣討之，罕之執其守將馬溉、伊鐸、何萬友，沁州刺史傅瑤等，遣其子顥拘送於太祖以求援焉。
entries.en: Keyong sent Li Zhaosi against him; Hanzhi seized Ma Gai, Yi Duo, He Wanyou, Fu Yao, and others and sent his son Hao to the Founder for help.
entries.literal: Keyong was angry and sent Li Zhaosi to attack him; Hanzhi seized the garrison commanders Ma Gai, Yi Duo, He Wanyou, Qin prefecture commissioner Fu Yao, and the rest, and sent his son Hao bound to the Founder to beg for aid.

entries.zh: （《新唐書》：全忠表罕之昭義軍節度使。）
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Quanzhong memorialized Hanzhi as Zhaoyi military commissioner.)
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Quanzhong memorialized Hanzhi as Zhaoyi military commissioner.)

entries.zh: 會罕之暴病，不能視事。
entries.en: Hanzhi then fell suddenly ill and could not govern.
entries.literal: When Hanzhi suddenly fell ill he could not handle affairs.

entries.zh: 明年六月，病篤，太祖令丁會代之，移罕之為河陽節度使；
entries.en: The following year, in the sixth month, when Hanzhi became gravely ill, the Founder ordered Ding Hui to replace him and transferred Hanzhi to serve as military governor of Heyang;
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the next year, gravely ill, the Founder had Ding Hui replace him and moved Hanzhi to Heyang military commissioner;

entries.zh: 行至懷州，卒於傳舍，時年五十八。
entries.en: he died at a relay station in Huai at fifty-eight.
entries.literal: reaching Huai prefecture he died at the relay station at age fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 其子顥以舟載柩，歸葬河陰縣。
entries.en: Son Hao brought the coffin by boat to bury him in Heyin.
entries.literal: His son Hao carried the coffin by boat and buried him in Heyin county.

entries.zh: 開平二年春，詔贈中書令。
entries.en: Kaiping 2 spring he was posthumously named Chief Minister.
entries.literal: In the spring of Kaiping year 2 an edict posthumously made him Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 及太祖義旗西征，行襲遣副使魯崇矩稟受制令。
entries.en: When the Founder marched west, Xingxi sent deputy Lu Chongju for orders.
entries.literal: When the Founder raised his righteous banner west, Xingxi sent deputy Lu Chongju to receive controlled orders.

entries.zh: 會唐昭宗幸鳳翔，太祖帥師奉迎，久之未出。
entries.en: When Zhaozong went to Fengxiang the Founder marched to meet him but lingered outside.
entries.literal: When Tang Zhaozong went to Fengxiang, the Founder led troops to welcome him but after long time did not come out.

entries.zh: 中尉韓全誨遣中官郤文晏等二十餘人分命矯詔，欲征江、淮兵屯於金州，以脅太祖之軍，行襲定策盡殺之，收其詔敕送於太祖。
entries.en: Han Quanhui sent Xi Wenyan and twenty eunuchs with forged orders to raise Jiang-Huai troops at Jin and threaten the Founder; Xingxi killed them and sent the edicts to the Founder.
entries.literal: Army Rong Commissioner Han Quanhui sent inner officials Xi Wenyan and more than twenty others with divided forged edicts, wishing to levy Jiang and Huai troops to camp at Jin prefecture and coerce the Founder's army; Xingxi decided on a plan and killed them all, collected their edicts and sent them to the Founder.

entries.zh: 天祐元年，兼領洋州節度使。
entries.en: In Tianyou 1 he concurrently became military governor of Yang Prefecture.
entries.literal: In Tianyou 1 he concurrently became military governor of Yang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 太祖之伐荊、襄，行襲令其子勖以舟師會於均、房，預收復功，遷匡國軍節度使。
entries.en: In the Jing-Xiang campaign Xingxi sent son Xu by river to Jun and Fang; rewarded, he became Kuangguo commissioner.
entries.literal: When the Founder attacked Jing and Xiang, Xingxi ordered his son Xu with river forces to join at Jun and Fang, sharing in the recovery merit; he was moved to Kuangguo military commissioner.

entries.zh: 到任，誅大吏張澄，暴其罪，州人莫不惴懾。
entries.en: Taking office he executed clerk Zhang Cheng and terrified the prefecture.
entries.literal: On reaching his post he executed senior clerk Zhang Cheng, exposed his crimes, and the prefecture people were all fearful.

entries.zh: 在許三年，上供外，別進助軍羨糧二十萬石。
entries.en: For three years at Xu he sent two hundred thousand piculs of extra grain beyond tribute.
entries.literal: At Xu for three years, beyond tribute he separately presented two hundred thousand piculs of surplus grain to aid the army.

entries.zh: 及太祖郊禋，行襲請入覲，貢獻巨萬，恩禮殊厚。
entries.en: At the suburban rites Xingxi came to court with lavish gifts and exceptional honor.
entries.literal: When the Founder performed suburban sacrifice, Xingxi asked to enter court audience, presented gifts worth tens of thousands, and favor and courtesy were exceptionally thick.

entries.zh: 尋詔翰林學士杜曉撰德政碑以賜之，累官至兼中書令，冊拜司空。
entries.en: Du Xiao wrote his merit stele; he rose to concurrent chief minister and Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Soon an edict ordered Hanlin academician Du Xiao to compose a merit stele to bestow on him; he rose through offices to concurrent Chief Minister of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 開平中卒，輟朝一日，贈太傅，諡曰忠敬。
entries.en: He died in Kaiping; mourning paused one day; posthumously Grand Tutor, loyal and respectful.
entries.literal: He died in Kaiping; court mourning ceased one day; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with posthumous title Loyal and Respectful.

entries.zh: 孫德昭，鹽州五原縣人，世為州校。
entries.en: Sun Dezhao of Wuyuan in Yanzhou came from a line of prefectural officers.
entries.literal: Sun Dezhao was a Wuyuan county man of Yan prefecture; for generations they were prefecture officers.

entries.zh: 父惟晸，有功於唐朝，遙領荊南節度，分判右神策軍事。
entries.en: His father Weijing served Tang with distant Jingnan commission and Shence command.
entries.literal: His father Weijing had merit toward the Tang house, held Jingnan military commission at a distance, and divided judgment of the Right Shence army affairs.

entries.zh: 德昭藉父蔭，累職為右神策軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Dezhao inherited rank as Right Shence commander.
entries.literal: Dezhao relied on father's shade, successively served as Right Shence army overall commander.

entries.zh: 光化三年，唐昭宗為閹宦所廢，矯立德王，時中外以權在禁闥，莫能致討，近藩朋附，章表繼有至者。
entries.en: Guanghua 3 eunuchs deposed Zhaozong and set up Prince De while none could resist.
entries.literal: In Guanghua year 3 Tang Zhaozong was deposed by eunuchs, who falsely established Prince De; at that time authority was in the inner court and none could strike in correction; near feudatories attached in factions; memorials continuously arrived.

entries.zh: 丞相崔胤，外與太祖申結輔佐之好，內遣心腹密講忠義。
entries.en: Cui Yin allied with the Founder and secretly plotted restoration.
entries.literal: Chief minister Cui Yin outwardly with the Founder declared assisting friendship, inwardly sent trusted men secretly to discuss loyal righteousness.

entries.zh: 有以事喻德昭者，
entries.en: Someone persuaded Dezhao,
entries.literal: There was one who used affairs to persuade Dezhao,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：德昭常惋不平，崔胤聞之，遣判官石戩與之遊。
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Cui Yin sent Shi Kan to win Dezhao.
entries.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Dezhao often grieved in injustice; Cui Yin heard it and sent aide Shi Kan to roam with him.

entries.zh: 德昭每酒酣必泣，戩知其誠，乃密以允意說之。）〉
entries.en: Dezhao wept when drunk; Shi Kan secured his pledge.)〉
entries.literal: Whenever Dezhao was deep in wine he must weep; Kan knew his sincerity and secretly with consent's intent persuaded him.)〉

entries.zh: 德昭感慨，乃與本軍孫承誨、董從實三人，奮發應命，誓圖返正，崔又割衣手筆以通其志。
entries.en: Moved, Dezhao joined Sun Chenghui and Dong Congshi to restore the throne; Cui Yin sealed the pact in writing.
entries.literal: Dezhao was moved and therefore with this army's Sun Chenghui and Dong Congshi three men roused to answer the mandate, swore to plot restoration; Cui again cut robe and wrote by hand to communicate his will.

entries.zh: 其年十一月，閹宦韓全誨縱火脅昭宗西幸鳳翔，承誨、從實並變節，為中官所誘，始欲驅擁百僚，將圖出令。
entries.en: Month 11 Han Quanhui took the emperor to Fengxiang; Chenghui and Congshi turned traitor with the eunuchs.
entries.literal: That year, eleventh month, eunuch Han Quanhui set fire and coerced Zhaozong west to Fengxiang; Chenghui and Congshi both changed sides, enticed by inner officials, at first wishing to drive and crowd the hundred officials and plot to issue orders.

entries.zh: 而德昭獨按兵，與太祖親吏婁敬思葉力衛丞相及文武百官，與長安吏民保於街東，免為所劫。
entries.en: Only Dezhao held his troops and with Lou Jingsi shielded Cui Yin and the court east of the street.
entries.literal: Only Dezhao held troops still, with the Founder's personal aide Lou Jingsi strove to guard the chief minister and civil and military officials, with Chang'an clerks and people protecting east of the street, spared from being seized.

entries.zh: 太祖遣從事相繼勞問，遺以龍鳳劍、鬥雞紗，委令製輯。
entries.en: The Founder sent gifts and entrusted him to keep order.
entries.literal: The Founder sent staff in succession to comfort and ask, gifted dragon-phoenix sword and fighting-cock gauze, entrusted with restraint and arrangement.

entries.zh: 於是百官次華州，連狀請太祖迎奉。
entries.en: Officials at Hua begged the Founder to restore the court.
entries.literal: Then the hundred officials at Huazhou jointly memorialized begging the Founder to welcome and attend.

entries.zh: 及大旆入關，德昭以軍禮上謁，立道左，太祖命左右扶騎控至長安，賜與甚厚，署權知同州節度留後。
entries.en: When the Founder's banner entered the passes, Dezhao paid his respects with military rites and stood at the left of the road. The Founder ordered attendants to help him mount and escort him by the reins to Chang'an, gave him lavish gifts, and appointed him acting military commissioner of Tongzhou.
