entries.literal: When the great banner entered the passes, Dezhao with army rites paid court, stood by the road's left; the Founder ordered attendants to support, mount, and rein-control to Chang'an, gifts very thick, appointed provisional Tongzhou military acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 將赴任，復徇民請，留充兩街製置使，賜錢百萬。
entries.en: The people kept him as capital disposition commissioner with a million cash.
entries.literal: About to go to his post, again yielding to the people's request, he was kept as two-streets disposition commissioner, granted a million cash.

entries.zh: 德昭以本部兵八千人獻於太祖，由是愈見賞重，又賜甲第一區，俾先還洛陽。
entries.en: He gave eight thousand men to the Founder, received a mansion, and went first to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Dezhao presented his original command's eight thousand men to the Founder; from this he was even more seen and valued; again given one mansion of armor, ordered first to return to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 及昭宗東遷，奏授左威衛上將軍，以疾免，歸於別墅。
entries.en: When the emperor moved east he became Left Valiant Guard general, then retired ill to his villa.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved east he was memorialized Left Valiant Guard upper general; because of illness released, he returned to his villa.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，以左領衛上將軍征赴闕。
entries.en: At the abdication he was summoned as Left Collar Guard general.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was summoned as Left Collar Guard upper general to audience.

entries.zh: 開平四年，拜左金吾大將軍，充街使。
entries.en: Kaiping 4 he became Left Golden Guard general and street commissioner.
entries.literal: In Kaiping year 4 he was made Left Golden Guard great general, full street commissioner.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，俾將命於兩浙，對見失儀，不果行。
entries.en: The Last Emperor sent him to Zhe but he failed audience and did not go.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he was sent on mission to the two Zhe circuits; audience demeanor failed and the journey did not proceed.

entries.zh: 尋改授右武衛上將軍，俄復左金吾大將軍。
entries.en: He was shifted to Right Martial Guard, then back to Left Golden Guard.
entries.literal: Soon he was changed to Right Martial Guard upper general; soon again Left Golden Guard great general.

entries.zh: 卒於官，詔贈太傅，輟視朝一日。
entries.en: He died in office and was posthumously named Grand Tutor; court mourned one day.
entries.literal: He died in office; an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor and halted court audience one day.

entries.zh: 天復元年正月一日未旦，逆豎左軍容劉季述早入，德昭伏甲要路以俟，追其前驅，邀而斬之，孫承誨等分捕左軍容王仲先黨伍。
entries.en: Tianfu 1, New Year's dawn, Dezhao ambushed and killed Liu Jishu; Chenghui seized Wang Zhongxian's faction.
entries.literal: Tianfu year 1, first month, first day before dawn, rebel eunuch Left Army Rong Commissioner Liu Jishu early entered; Dezhao hid armor on the crucial road to wait, pursued his vanguard, intercepted and beheaded him; Sun Chenghui and the rest separately captured Left Army Rong Commissioner Wang Zhongxian's faction.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗方幽辱東內，聞外喧，大恐。
entries.en: Zhaozong, imprisoned in the eastern palace, heard the uproar and feared.
entries.literal: Tang Zhaozong was just humiliated in the eastern inner palace; hearing outer clamor, he was greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 德昭馳至，扣閣曰：「逆賊劉季述伏誅矣，請上皇開鑰復皇帝位。」
entries.en: Dezhao galloped up, knocked on the gate, and cried, "The rebel Liu Jishu has been executed—open the gate and restore the emperor!"
entries.literal: Dezhao galloped to him, knocked on the gate and said: "Rebel bandit Liu Jishu has submitted to execution—beg the High Sovereign open the lock and restore the Son of Heaven's throne."

entries.zh: 皇后何氏呼曰：「汝可進逆人首，門乃可開。」
entries.en: The empress called out, "Bring the rebel's head—then the gate may open."
entries.literal: Empress He called: "You may advance the rebel's head—then the gate can be opened."

entries.zh: 俄而承誨、從實俱以馘獻，昭宗悲而嘉之。
entries.en: They brought heads; Zhaozong wept and praised them.
entries.literal: Soon Chenghui and Congshi both presented heads; Zhaozong grieved and praised them.

entries.zh: 於是丞相崔胤奉迎禦丹鳳樓，率百辟待罪，泣且奏曰：「臣居大位，不能討奸，賴東平王全忠首奮忠貞，誅殺邸吏，遂致德昭等擒戮妖逆，再清禁闈。」
entries.en: Cui Yin welcomed the emperor at Danfeng Tower, led the assembled officials in awaiting punishment, and wept as he memorialized, "I hold high office yet was unable to suppress the traitors. Thanks to Zhu Quanzhong, Prince of Dongping, who first displayed loyal resolve and killed the palace agents, Dezhao and the others were able to capture and execute the wicked rebels and cleanse the palace once more."
entries.literal: Then chief minister Cui Yin welcomed the imperial carriage at Danfeng Tower, led the assembled officials in awaiting punishment, and wept as he memorialized: "Your subject holds high office yet was unable to suppress the traitors. Thanks to Zhu Quanzhong, Prince of Dongping, who first displayed loyal resolve and killed the palace agents, Dezhao and the others were able to capture and execute the wicked rebels and cleanse the palace once more."

entries.zh: 即日議功，以德昭為檢校太保、靜海軍節度使，承誨邕州節度使，從實容州節度使，並同平章事，錫姓李，賜號扶傾濟難忠烈功臣，圖形淩煙閣，俱留京師。
entries.en: Dezhao became honorary Grand Guardian and Jinghai commissioner; his allies received circuits, Li surname, merit titles, and Lingyan portraits.
entries.literal: That day merit was discussed; Dezhao was made honorary Grand Guardian, Jinghai military commissioner; Chenghui Yong prefecture commissioner; Congshi Rong prefecture commissioner—all co-equal chief ministers, granted surname Li, bestowed title Upright-Overturning, Calamity-Aiding Loyal Martyr Merit Minister, portraits in Lingyan Pavilion, all kept at the capital.

entries.zh: 錫賚宴賞之厚，恩寵權幸之勢，近代罕比。
entries.en: Rewards and favor were unmatched in their day.
entries.literal: Bestowal, feasts, and rewards were thick; favor and fortune's power—rare in recent generations.

entries.zh: 趙克裕，河陽人也。
entries.en: Zhao Keyu came from Heyang.
entries.literal: Zhao Keyu was a Heyang man.

entries.zh: 祖、父皆為軍吏。
entries.en: His grandfather and father were army clerks.
entries.literal: Grandfather and father were all army clerks.

entries.zh: 克裕少為牙將，好讀書，謹儀範，牧伯皆奇待之。
entries.en: A guard officer who loved books and decorum, he won every commander's favor.
entries.literal: Keyu in youth was a guard officer, loved reading books, was careful in ritual measure, and military commissioners all treated him as extraordinary.

entries.zh: 累居右職，擢為虎牢關使。
entries.en: He rose to command Hulao Pass.
entries.literal: He successively held right posts and was promoted to Hulao Pass commissioner.

entries.zh: 光啟中，蔡寇陷河陽，克裕率所部歸於太祖，隸於宣義軍。
entries.en: During the Guangqi era, when Cai bandits captured Heyang, Keyu led his command over to the Founder and was attached to the Xuanyi Army.
entries.literal: In Guangqi, Cai bandits took Heyang; Keyu led his command to return to the Founder and was attached to the Xuanyi army.

entries.zh: 太祖東征徐、鄆，克裕屢受指顧，無不如意。
entries.en: In eastern campaigns against Xu and Yan he never failed the Founder.
entries.literal: The Founder east campaigned Xu and Yan; Keyu repeatedly received direction and care—nothing not as wished.

entries.zh: 數年之內，繼領亳、鄭二州刺史。
entries.en: Within years he held Bo and Zheng.
entries.literal: Within several years he successively held Bo and Zheng prefecture military commissions.

entries.zh: 時關東藩鎮方為蔡寇所毒，黎元流散，不能相保，克裕妙有農戰之備，復善於綏懷，民賴而獲安者眾。
entries.en: While Cai ravaged the east he fed and protected the people better than other lords.
entries.literal: At that time east-of-the-pass feudatories were just poisoned by Cai bandits; common people scattered in flight and could not protect one another; Keyu was subtle in farming-and-war preparation and again good at soothing and holding—many relied on him and obtained peace.

entries.zh: 太祖表為河陽節度使、檢校右僕射，尋移理許田，入為金吾衛大將軍、檢校司空。
entries.en: He became Heyang commissioner, then governed Xu, and entered court as Golden Guard general and honorary Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: The Founder memorialized him Heyang military commissioner and honorary Right Vice Director; soon he moved to govern Xu fields, entered as Golden Guard great general and honorary Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 及太祖為元帥，以克裕為元帥府左都押衙，復統六軍，兗州平，命權知泰寧軍留後。
entries.en: As marshal's left adjutant and six-army commander he acted as Taining commissioner after Yan fell.
entries.literal: When the Founder was marshal, he made Keyu marshal's headquarters left overall holding ya; again commanded the six armies; when Yan prefecture was pacified he was ordered provisional Taining military acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 數月，暴疾而卒。
entries.en: Within months he died suddenly.
entries.literal: Within months he died suddenly of illness.

entries.zh: 開平初，追贈太保。
entries.en: At the beginning of Kaiping he was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping he was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 張慎思，清河人。
entries.en: Zhang Shensi came from Qinghe.
entries.literal: Zhang Shensi was a Qinghe man.

entries.zh: 自黃巢軍來歸，累授軍職，曆諸軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Defecting from Huang Chao, he rose through commands to overall army commander.
entries.literal: Returning from Huang Chao's army, he successively received military posts and served as overall commander of various armies.

entries.zh: 從平巢、蔡、兗、鄆，皆著功，表授檢校工部尚書，兼宋州長史。
entries.en: He distinguished himself pacifying Chao, Cai, Yan, and Yun and became honorary Minister of Works and Song chief secretary.
entries.literal: Following the pacification of Chao, Cai, Yan, and Yun, he distinguished himself in merit and was memorialized as honorary Minister of Works and concurrent Song prefecture chief secretary.

entries.zh: 光化中，加檢校右僕射，權知亳州。
entries.en: In Guanghua he became honorary Right Vice Director and acting Bo commissioner.
entries.literal: In Guanghua he was made honorary Right Vice Director and provisional Bo prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 天復三年，昭宗還長安，以從太祖迎駕功，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣，尋除汝州防禦使。
entries.en: Tianfu 3, for welcoming the emperor with the Founder, he received the title Welcome-the-Carriage Merit Minister and became Ruzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: Tianfu year 3, when Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, for merit in following the Founder to welcome the imperial carriage he was granted the title Welcome-the-Carriage, Resolute-and-Brave Merit Minister; soon he was made Ruzhou defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 天祐元年，授左龍武統軍。
entries.en: Tianyou 1 he became Left Dragon Martial commander.
entries.literal: In Tianyou year 1 he was appointed Left Dragon Martial army commander.

entries.zh: 其冬，除許州匡國軍節度使。
entries.en: That winter he became Xu Kuangguo commissioner.
entries.literal: That winter he was made Xu prefecture Kuangguo military commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年十一月，權知徐州武寧軍兩使留後。
entries.en: Next year, month 11, he acted as Xuzhou Wuning commissioner.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the next year he was provisional acting commissioner of Xuzhou Wuning military commission.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，入為左金吾大將軍。
entries.en: At the abdication he entered as Left Golden Guard great general.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he entered as Left Golden Guard great general.

entries.zh: 開平二年，除宋州刺史，未幾，復拜左金吾大將軍。
entries.en: Kaiping 2 he governed Song, then again became Left Golden Guard great general.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 2 he was made Song prefecture military commissioner; soon he was again appointed Left Golden Guard great general.

entries.zh: 三年冬，除蔡州刺史，以貪貨大失民情，詔追赴闕。
entries.en: Winter, year 3, as Cai commissioner greed cost him popular support and he was recalled.
entries.literal: Winter of year 3 he was made Cai prefecture military commissioner; for greedy seizure of goods he greatly lost the people's hearts and an edict recalled him to court.

entries.zh: 未幾，扈從北征還，以疾臥洛陽之私第。
entries.en: Soon after returning from the northern campaign he fell ill at his Luoyang home.
entries.literal: Soon, returning from escorting the northern campaign, he lay ill in a private residence at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 馭家不肅，為其子所弒。
entries.en: His household discipline failed and his son murdered him.
entries.literal: He did not keep his household in order and was murdered by his son.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：韓建遇唐朝之衰運，據潼關之要地，不能藩屏王室，翻務斫喪宗枝，雖有阜俗之能，何補不臣之咎。
entries.en: The historian says: Han Jian met the Tang house in its declining fortune and held the crucial ground of Tong Pass, yet he could not shield the royal house. Instead he devoted himself to cutting down the imperial branches. Though he had the ability to enrich local customs, how could that offset the fault of disloyalty?
entries.literal: The historian says: Han Jian met the Tang house's declining fortune, held Tong Pass's crucial ground, could not screen and protect the royal house, instead devoted himself to cutting off and destroying the imperial branches—though he had ability to enrich customs, how does it repair the fault of disloyalty?

entries.zh: 罕之負驍雄之氣，蓄向背之謀，武皇比之呂布，斯知人矣。
entries.en: Hanzhi possessed a fierce, heroic spirit but harbored schemes of changing allegiance. The Martial Emperor compared him to Lü Bu; in this he truly knew the man.
entries.literal: Hanzhi bore fierce valor's spirit and stored facing-and-turning plots; the Martial Emperor compared him to Lü Bu—he knew the man.

entries.zh: 行襲勵納忠之節，德昭立反正之功，俱善其終，固其宜矣。
entries.en: Xingxi and Dezhao served loyally and ended well, as they should.
entries.literal: Xingxi encouraged loyal submission's integrity; Dezhao established restoration's merit; both completed their ends well—it is fitting.

entries.zh: 克裕而下，無譏可也。
entries.en: Keyu and the rest merit no reproach.
entries.literal: Keyu and below—no reproach is possible.

entries.zh: 葛從周，字通美，濮州鄄城人也。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou, styled Tongmei, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
entries.literal: Ge Congzhou, style name Tongmei, was a native of Juancheng in Pu prefecture.

entries.zh: 曾祖阮，祖遇賢，父簡，累贈兵部尚書。
entries.en: His line reached posthumous Minister of War through his father Jian.
entries.literal: Great-grandfather Ruan, grandfather Yu Xian, father Jian—repeatedly posthumously made Minister of War.

entries.zh: 從周少豁達，有智略，初入黃巢軍，漸至軍校。
entries.en: Open and shrewd in youth, he joined Huang Chao and rose to guard officer.
entries.literal: Congzhou in youth was open and generous, had wisdom and stratagem; he first entered Huang Chao's army and gradually reached guard officer.

entries.zh: 唐中和四年三月，太祖大破巢軍於王滿渡，從周與霍存、張歸霸昆弟相率來降。
entries.en: Tang Zhonghe 4, month 3, after the Founder crushed Chao at Wangman Ford, Congzhou surrendered with Huo Cun and the Zhang brothers.
entries.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhonghe of Tang the Founder greatly defeated Chao's army at Wangman Ford; Congzhou with Huo Cun and Zhang Guiba and his brothers in succession came to surrender.

entries.zh: 七月，從太祖屯兵於西華，破蔡賊王夏寨。
entries.en: Month 7 he camped at Xihua and broke Cai rebel Wang Xia's camp.
entries.literal: In the seventh month the Founder encamped troops at Xihua and broke Cai bandit Wang Xia's stockade.

entries.zh: 太祖臨陣馬踣，賊眾來追甚急，從周扶太祖上馬，與賊軍格鬥，傷面，矢中於肱，身被數槍，奮命以衛太祖。
entries.en: When the Founder's horse fell under pursuit, Congzhou mounted him, fought on wounded by face, arm, and spears, and saved his life.
entries.literal: The Founder in battle his horse fell; bandit masses came pressing in pursuit very urgently; Congzhou helped the Founder mount, grappled with the bandit army, wounded his face, an arrow struck his upper arm, his body received several spears, and he exhausted his life to guard the Founder.

entries.zh: 賴張延壽回馬轉鬥，從周與太祖俱免，退軍溵水。
entries.en: Zhang Yanshou's countercharge let Congzhou and the Founder escape to Yin River.
entries.literal: Relying on Zhang Yanshou wheeling his horse and turning to fight, Congzhou and the Founder both escaped; the army withdrew to Yin River.

entries.zh: 諸將並削職，惟擢從周、延壽為大校。
entries.en: Other generals were demoted; only Congzhou and Yanshou were promoted.
entries.literal: The generals all had offices reduced; only Congzhou and Yanshou were promoted to great colonels.

entries.zh: 其從入長葛、靈井，大敗蔡賊，至斤溝、淝河，殺鐵林三千人，獲九寨都虞候王涓。
entries.en: He helped take Changge and Lingjing, killed three thousand Iron Forest troops at Fei River, and captured commander Wang Juan.
entries.literal: Following in to enter Changge and Lingjing, he greatly defeated Cai bandits; reaching Jingou and Fei River he killed three thousand Iron Forest troops and captured nine-stockade commander Wang Juan.

entries.zh: 胡真，江陵人也。
entries.en: Hu Zhen came from Jiangling.
entries.literal: Hu Zhen was a Jiangling man.

entries.zh: 體貌洪壯，長七尺，善騎射，少為縣吏。
entries.en: Seven feet tall and a master archer, he began as a county clerk.
entries.literal: His physique was huge and strong, seven feet tall, skilled at mounted archery; in youth he was a county clerk.

entries.zh: 及在巢寇中，寇推為名將，隨巢涉淮、浙，陷許、洛，入長安。
entries.en: In Huang Chao's ranks he became a famed general and entered Chang'an with the rebels.
entries.literal: When in Chao's banditry the bandits pushed him as a famous general; he followed Chao across Huai and Zhe, took Xu and Luo, and entered Chang'an.

entries.zh: 及太祖以眾歸唐，真時為元從都將，
entries.en: When the Founder submitted to Tang, Zhen was an original-follower commander,
entries.literal: When the Founder with masses returned to Tang, Zhen was then original-follower overall commander,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：溫見巢兵勢日蹙，知其將亡，親將胡真、謝瞳勸溫歸國。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Wen, seeing Chao's power daily wane and knowing he would fall, was urged by his trusted generals Hu Zhen and Xie Tong to return to the Tang state.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Wen saw Chao's military power daily pinched, knew he would perish, and his trusted generals Hu Zhen and Xie Tong urged Wen to return to the state.)〉

entries.zh: 從至梁苑，表授檢校刑部尚書，頻從破巢、蔡於陳、鄭間。
entries.en: At Liang Garden he became honorary Minister of Punishments and fought Chao and Cai.
entries.literal: Following to Liang Garden he was memorialized honorary Minister of Punishments and repeatedly followed in breaking Chao and Cai between Chen and Zheng.

entries.zh: 尋以奇兵襲取滑州，乃署為滑州節度留後，復表為鄭滑節度使、檢校右僕射。
entries.en: He seized Huazhou and became Zheng-Hua commissioner.
entries.literal: Soon with strange troops he raided and took Huazhou and was appointed Huazhou military acting commissioner; again memorialized Zheng-Hua military commissioner and honorary Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 數年，征為右金吾衛大將軍，俄拜寧遠軍節度使、容州刺史、檢校太保。
entries.en: Later he was Golden Guard general, then Ningyuan and Rong commissioner and honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: After several years he was summoned as Right Golden Guard great general; soon he was made Ningyuan army military commissioner, Rong prefecture military commissioner, and honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 卒贈太傅。
entries.en: He was posthumously named Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: On death he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 光化二年，權知邢州事。
entries.en: Guanghua 2 he governed Xingzhou provisionally.
entries.literal: In Guanghua year 2 he was provisional Xingzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 明年春，李嗣昭以蕃漢五萬來寇，歸霸堅壁設備，晉軍不敢顧其城，遂移軍攻洺州，陷焉。
entries.en: The following spring, Li Sizhao invaded with fifty thousand tribal and Chinese troops. Guiba fortified Xingzhou and made ready to defend it. The Jin army did not dare assault the city, so it moved on to Mingzhou and captured it instead.
entries.literal: The following spring, Li Sizhao invaded with fifty thousand tribal and Chinese troops. Guiba kept behind strong walls and prepared his defenses. The Jin army did not dare attack his city, so it shifted to Ming Prefecture and captured it.

entries.zh: 時太祖在滑，頗慮邢之失守。
entries.en: The Founder at Hua feared Xing would fall.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder was at Hua and quite feared Xing's loss.

entries.zh: 及葛從周復洺，嗣昭北遁，歸霸出兵襲之，殺二萬餘眾。
entries.en: When Congzhou retook Ming, Guiba ambushed Sizhao and killed twenty thousand.
entries.literal: When Ge Congzhou recovered Ming, Sizhao fled north; Guiba led troops in ambush strike and killed more than twenty thousand.

entries.zh: 捷至，賞錫殊等，旋以功奏加檢校司空。
entries.en: He was richly rewarded and made honorary Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Victory arrived; rewards and gifts were special; soon for merit memorialized added honorary Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 天祐初，遷萊州刺史，秩滿授左衛上將軍，又除曹州刺史。
entries.en: Early Tianyou he governed Lai, then became Left Guard general and Cao commissioner.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was transferred Laizhou prefect; when term expired he was appointed Left Guard upper general; again made Cao prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 其秋，加檢校司徒，副劉知俊禦邠、鳳之寇，敗之。
entries.en: That autumn he helped Liu Zhijun beat Bin and Feng raiders.
entries.literal: That autumn he was added honorary Minister of Works, deputy to Liu Zhijun in resisting Bin and Feng raiders, and defeated them.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，拜右龍虎統軍，改左驍衛上將軍，充河陽諸軍都指揮使。
entries.en: At the abdication he commanded dragon-tiger and valiant guard troops and Heyang armies.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was made Right Dragon-Tiger overall commander, changed to Left Valiant Guard upper general, full Heyang all-armies overall commander.

entries.zh: 明年夏六月，就除河陽節度使、檢校太保，尋加同平章事。
entries.en: Next summer he became Heyang commissioner, Grand Guardian, and chief minister.
entries.literal: The next summer, sixth month, he was appointed Heyang military commissioner and honorary Grand Guardian; soon added co-equal chief minister.

entries.zh: 二年秋七月，卒於位。
entries.en: Year 2, autumn, month 7, he died in office.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of year 2 he died in office.

entries.zh: 詔贈太傅。
entries.en: He was posthumously named Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 景福初，從太祖伐鄆，帝軍不利，太祖為寇所逼，歸厚殿馬翼衛，左右馳射，矢發如雨，賊騎千百，披靡而退。
entries.en: Jingfu he covered the Founder's retreat with arrow storms at Yan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu following the Founder in attacking Yan the imperial army was unfavorable; the Founder was pressed by bandits; Guihou brought up the rear wing-guarding, left and right galloping and shooting; arrows fell like rain; bandit cavalry by thousands and hundreds collapsed and retreated.

entries.zh: 明年，與葛從周禦晉軍於洹水，殊績尤著。
entries.en: Next year at Huan River his merit was outstanding.
entries.literal: The next year with Ge Congzhou he met Jin troops at Huan River; special merit was especially marked.

entries.zh: 詔加檢校右僕射。
entries.en: He became honorary Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: An edict added honorary Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 其後，討滄州，復洺州，咸以功聞，太祖錄其勳，命權知洺州事。
entries.en: After Cang and Ming campaigns he governed Ming provisionally.
entries.literal: Afterward attacking Cangzhou and recovering Ming prefecture—all with merit reported—the Founder recorded his merit and ordered him provisional Ming prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 是郡嘗兩為晉人所陷，井邑蕭條，歸厚撫之，數月之內，民庶翕然。
entries.en: He restored desolate Ming within months.
entries.literal: This prefecture had twice been taken by Jin men; towns and hamlets were desolate; Guihou comforted it; within months the people were harmonious.

entries.zh: 太祖自鎮、定還，睹其緝理之政，大喜，賞之。
entries.en: The Founder praised his governance on return from Zhen and Ding.
entries.literal: The Founder returning from Zhen and Ding saw his governing policy and was greatly pleased and rewarded him.

entries.zh: 天復元年冬，真拜洺州刺史，加檢校左僕射，尋授絳州刺史。
entries.en: Tianfu 1 winter he became Ming then Jiang commissioner.
entries.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1 he was formally made Ming prefecture military commissioner, added honorary Left Vice Director; soon appointed Jiang prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 三年秋，改晉州刺史，仍檢校司空。
entries.en: Year 3 autumn he became Jin commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: In autumn of year 3 he was changed Jin prefecture military commissioner, still honorary Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 唐帝遷都洛陽，除右神武統軍。
entries.en: When the court moved to Luoyang he commanded Right Divine Martial.
entries.literal: When Tang emperor moved the capital to Luoyang he was made Right Divine Martial overall commander.

entries.zh: 天祐二年，改左羽林統軍，與徐懷玉同守澤州。
entries.en: Tianyou 2 he guarded Ze with Xu Huaiyu.
entries.literal: In Tianyou year 2 he was changed Left Feathered Forest overall commander and with Xu Huaiyu jointly guarded Ze prefecture.

entries.zh: 時晉軍五萬來攻，郡中戎士甚寡，歸厚極力拒守，並軍乃還。
entries.en: He held Ze against fifty thousand Jin until they withdrew.
entries.literal: At that time fifty thousand Jin troops came to attack; warriors in the prefecture were very few; Guihou exhausted strength holding fast and Jin army then returned.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，加檢校司空。
entries.en: At the abdication he became honorary Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was added honorary Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 開平二年夏，劉知俊以同州叛，歸厚副楊師厚、劉鄩等討平之。
entries.en: Kaiping 2 summer he helped suppress Liu Zhijun at Tong.
entries.literal: In summer of Kaiping year 2 Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; Guihou as deputy to Yang Shihou and Liu Ye and others suppressed and pacified it.

entries.zh: 秋，軍還，授亳州團練使。
entries.en: Autumn he became Bozhou training commissioner.
entries.literal: In autumn the army returned; he was appointed Bozhou training commissioner.

entries.zh: 乾化二年，拜鎮國軍節度使、陝虢等州觀察處置等使。
entries.en: Qianhua 2 he became Zhenguo and Shan-Guo commissioner.
entries.literal: In Qianhua year 2 he was made Zhenguo military commissioner and Shan-Guo surveillance and disposition commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年夏，以疾卒於位。
entries.en: Next summer he died in office.
entries.literal: The next summer he died of illness in office.

entries.zh: 詔贈太師。
entries.en: He was posthumously named Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 子漢卿。
entries.en: His son was Hanqing.
entries.literal: Son Hanqing.

entries.zh: 張歸霸，字正臣，清河人。
entries.en: Zhang Guiba, styled Zhengchen, came from Qinghe.
entries.literal: Zhang Guiba, style name Zhengchen, was a Qinghe man.

entries.zh: 祖進言，陽穀令。
entries.en: His grandfather Jinyan was magistrate of Yanggu.
entries.literal: Grandfather Jinyan was Yanggu county magistrate.

entries.zh: 父實，亦有宦緒。
entries.en: His father Shi also held office.
entries.literal: Father Shi also had an official pedigree.

entries.zh: 少倜儻，好兵術。
entries.en: Young, he was bold and loved warfare.
entries.literal: In youth he was unconventional, loved military arts.

entries.zh: 唐乾符中，寇盜蜂起，歸霸率昆弟三人棄家投黃巢，頗以勇略聞。
entries.en: In Qianfu he and three brothers joined Huang Chao for their fighting fame.
entries.literal: In Qianfu of Tang bandits and robbers swarmed; Guiba led three brothers to abandon home and join Huang Chao, quite known for courage and stratagem.

entries.zh: 巢陷長安，遂署為左番功臣。
entries.en: When Chao took Chang'an he became Left Merit Baron.
entries.literal: When Chao took Chang'an he was appointed Left Merit Baron.

entries.zh: 中和中，巢領徒走宛丘。
entries.en: In Zhonghe Chao fled to Wankiu.
entries.literal: In Zhonghe, Chao led followers to flee to Wankiu.

entries.zh: 時太祖在汴，奉詔南討，巢黨日窘，歸霸昆仲與葛從周、李讜等相率來降，尋補宣武軍劇職。
entries.en: At Bian Guiba and his brothers surrendered with Congzhou and Li Rang and joined the Xuanyi army.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder was at Bian, received edict for southern campaign; Chao's party daily pressed; Guiba and his brothers with Ge Congzhou, Li Rang, and others in succession came to surrender; soon he was supplemented to Xuanyi army key posts.

entries.zh: 光啟二年，與蔡將張存戰於盧氏。
entries.en: Guangqi 2 he fought Zhang Cun at Lushi.
entries.literal: In Guangqi year 2 he fought Cai general Zhang Cun at Lushi.

entries.zh: 三年夏，又與蔡將盧瑭戰於雙丘，復與秦宗賢戰於萬勝，皆敗而殲之。
entries.en: Year 3 summer he destroyed Lu Tang at Shuangqiu and Qin Zongxian at Wansheng.
entries.literal: In summer of year 3 he again fought Cai general Lu Tang at Shuangqiu and again fought Qin Zongxian at Wansheng—all defeated and annihilated.

entries.zh: 翌日，宗權遣將張郅來寇，列寨於赤堈。
entries.en: Next day Zhang Zhi of Cai camped at Chijin.
entries.literal: The next day Zongquan sent general Zhang Zhi to raid, arraying stockades at Chijin.

entries.zh: 一日，出騎將較勝，歸霸為飛戈所中。
entries.en: In a cavalry duel he was struck by a flying halberd.
entries.literal: One day he sent out cavalry to contest victory; Guiba was struck by a flying halberd.

entries.zh: 即拔馬卻逸，控弦一發，賊洞頸而墜，遂兼騎而還。
entries.en: He wheeled, shot the rider through the neck, and seized his horse.
entries.literal: He at once pulled his horse back and fled, drew his bow one shot—the bandit pierced through the neck and fell; he then took the horse and returned.

entries.zh: 太祖時於高丘下瞰，備見其狀，麵加賞激，厚以金帛及所獲馬錫之。
entries.en: The Founder watched from Gaomound and richly rewarded him.
entries.literal: The Founder at that time overlooked from Gaomound and fully saw the scene; he added praise and stimulation to his face and richly bestowed gold silks and captured horses.

entries.zh: 又嘗被命以控弦之士五百人伏於壕內，太祖統數百騎稍逼其寨，蔡人果以銳士摩壘來追，歸霸發伏兵，掩殺千餘人，奪馬數十匹，尋奏授檢校左散騎常侍。
entries.en: His trench ambush killed a thousand Cai pursuers and won him honorary Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
entries.literal: He was also ordered with five hundred archers to lie in ambush in a trench; the Founder with several hundred horse slightly pressed their stockade; Cai men indeed with crack troops rubbed the ramparts in pursuit; Guiba released ambush troops, ambushed and killed more than a thousand, seized several tens of horses, and soon memorialized honorary Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

entries.zh: 其後從太祖伐鄆，副李唐賓渡淮，鹹著奇績。
entries.en: He crossed the Huai with Li Tangbin against Yan with striking merit.
entries.literal: Afterward he followed the Founder in attacking Yan and as deputy to Li Tangbin crossed the Huai, all showing strange merit.

entries.zh: 文德初，大軍臨蔡州，賊將蕭顥來斫寨，歸霸於徐懷玉各以所領兵自東南二扉分出，合勢殺賊，蔡人大敗。
entries.en: Wende at Caizhou he and Xu Huaiyu sallied and crushed Xiao Hao.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wende the great army approached Caizhou; bandit general Xiao Hao came to cut the stockade; Guiba with Xu Huaiyu each led their commands out from southeast and second gates, joined force and killed bandits; Cai men were greatly defeated.

entries.zh: 及太祖振眾離營，寇塵已息。
entries.en: When the Founder left camp the field was already clear.
entries.literal: When the Founder rallied the masses and left camp the bandit dust had already settled.

entries.zh: 太祖召至，賞之曰：「昔耿弇不俟光武擊張步，言不以賊遺君父，弇之功，爾其二焉。」
entries.en: The Founder summoned and rewarded him, saying, "Formerly Geng Yan did not wait for Guangwu to strike Zhang Bu, saying he would not leave bandits to lord and father—Yan's merit; yours is twice it."
entries.literal: The Founder summoned him and rewarded him saying: "Formerly Geng Yan did not wait for Guangwu to strike Zhang Bu, saying he would not leave bandits to lord and father—Yan's merit, yours is twice it."

entries.zh: 大順中，郭紹賓拔曹州，歸霸率兵數千守之。
entries.en: Dashun he garrisoned Cao after Guo Shaobin took it.
entries.literal: In Dashun, Guo Shaobin took Cao prefecture; Guiba led several thousand troops to guard it.

entries.zh: 俄而朱瑾統大軍自至，歸霸與丁會逆擊之於金鄉，瑾大敗，擒賊將宗江等七十餘人，曹州以寧。
entries.en: He and Ding Hui routed Zhu Jin at Jinxiang and captured seventy officers.
entries.literal: Soon Zhu Jin led a great army in person; Guiba with Ding Hui met and struck them at Jinxiang; Jin was greatly defeated; bandit generals Zong Jiang and more than seventy men were captured; Cao prefecture was pacified.

entries.zh: 明年，破濮州，生擒刺史邵儒。
entries.en: Next year he took Pu and captured Shao Ru alive.
entries.literal: The next year he took Pu prefecture and captured military commissioner Shao Ru alive.

entries.zh: 又佐葛從周與晉軍戰於洹水，生獲克用愛子落落。
entries.en: At Huan River he helped capture Keyong's son Luoluo.
entries.literal: He again aided Ge Congzhou in fighting Jin troops at Huan River and captured Keyong's beloved son Luoluo alive.

entries.zh: 復與燕人戰於內黃，殺仁恭兵三萬餘眾。
entries.en: At Neihuang he killed thirty thousand Yan troops.
entries.literal: He again fought Yan men at Neihuang and killed more than thirty thousand of Rengong's troops.

entries.zh: 戎績超特，居諸將之右，累官至檢校左僕射。
entries.en: His merit topped the generals; he reached honorary Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Military achievement exceptionally surpassing, he stood to the right of the generals, successively reaching honorary Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 大順元年，奏加檢校兵部尚書，又命統親軍。
entries.en: Dashun 1 he became honorary Minister of War and commanded the guard.
entries.literal: In Dashun year 1 he was memorialized added honorary Minister of War and ordered to command the personal guard.

entries.zh: 是歲，郴王遷寨，未知所往，忽逢兗、鄆賊寇甚眾，太祖亟登道左高阜以觀之，命歸厚領所部廳子馬直突之。
entries.en: When Yan raiders swarmed he charged with the hall-son horse at the Founder's order.
entries.literal: That year Prince of Chen moved stockade, destination unknown; suddenly meeting Yan and Yanzhou bandits very many, the Founder urgently climbed a high mound by the road to observe and ordered Guihou to lead his hall-son horse to charge straight in.

entries.zh: 出沒二十餘合，賊大敗將北，而救軍雲至，歸厚即綴賊苦戰，請太祖以數十騎先還。
entries.en: After twenty clashes he held the enemy while the Founder escaped with a few horsemen.
entries.literal: Emerging and withdrawing more than twenty rounds, bandits were greatly defeated and about to flee north, but rescue troops clouded in; Guihou then fought the bandits bitterly and begged the Founder with several tens of horse to return first.

entries.zh: 時歸厚所乘馬中流矢而踣，乃持槊步鬥漸退，賊不敢逼。
entries.en: His horse fell; he fought on foot with his spear until the enemy dared not close.
entries.literal: At that time Guihou's mounted horse was struck by a flowing arrow and fell; he then held his spear and fought on foot gradually retreating; bandits did not dare press.

entries.zh: 太祖至寨，亟命張筠、劉儒飛騎來迎，然謂已歿矣。
entries.en: The Founder sent Zhang Yun and Liu Ru to find him, fearing him dead.
entries.literal: The Founder reached camp and urgently ordered Zhang Yun and Liu Ru with flying horse to welcome; yet he thought him already dead.

entries.zh: 歸厚體被二十餘箭，尚復拒戰，筠等既至，賊解乃歸。
entries.en: Wounded by twenty arrows he fought until Yun arrived and the enemy broke.
entries.literal: Guihou's body received more than twenty arrows yet still resisted battle; when Yun and the rest arrived bandits dispersed and he returned.

entries.zh: 太祖見之，撫背泣下曰：「得歸厚身全，縱廣喪戎馬，何足計乎！」
entries.en: The Founder, seeing him, stroked his back and wept, saying, "To get Guihou back whole—even if we lose horses wholesale, what does it matter!"
entries.literal: The Founder seeing him stroked his back and wept, saying: "To get Guihou back whole—even if broadly losing army horses, what is worth counting!"

entries.zh: 便令肩舁歸汴，日降問賚，恩旨甚厚，尋遷中軍指揮使。
entries.en: Carried to Bian he was richly honored and made central army commander.
entries.literal: He then ordered him carried on shoulders back to Bian; daily descending inquiries and gifts; imperial favor very thick; soon he was transferred central army commander.

entries.zh: 太祖遣郭言募兵於陝州，有黃花子賊據於溫穀，從周擊破之。
entries.en: He broke the Yellow Flower bandits at Wengu while Guo Yan recruited at Shan.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Guo Yan to recruit troops at Shan prefecture; Yellow Flower bandits held Wengu; Congzhou broke and defeated them.

entries.zh: 又破秦賢之眾於滎陽，尋佐朱珍收兵於淄、青間。
entries.en: He beat Qin Xian at Xingyang and aided Zhu Zhen in Zi and Qing.
entries.literal: He again defeated Qin Xian's masses at Xingyang and soon aided Zhu Zhen in gathering troops between Zi and Qing.

entries.zh: 時兗州齊克護軍於任城，從周敗之，擒其將呂全真。
entries.en: He defeated Qi Kehu at Rencheng and captured Lü Quanzhen.
entries.literal: At that time Yanzhou's Qi Kehu had troops at Rencheng; Congzhou defeated him and captured his general Lü Quanzhen.

entries.zh: 淄人不受制，復與之戰，獲其驍將鞏約。
entries.en: When Zi resisted he fought again and took the fierce Gong Yue.
entries.literal: Zi people would not submit; he fought them again and took their fierce general Gong Yue.

entries.zh: 會青州以步騎萬餘人列三寨於金嶺，以厄要害，從周與朱珍大殲其眾，擄其將楊昭範五人而還。
entries.en: He and Zhu Zhen annihilated Qing troops at Jin Ridge and captured Yang Zhaofan and five generals.
entries.literal: When Qing prefecture with more than ten thousand foot and horse arrayed three stockades at Jin Ridge to choke the crucial point, Congzhou with Zhu Zhen greatly annihilated their masses, captured their general Yang Zhaofan and five men, and returned.

entries.zh: 至大梁，不解甲，徑至板橋擊蔡賊，破盧瑭寨；
entries.en: Without resting at Daliang he struck Cai at Banqiao and broke Lu Tang's camp;
entries.literal: Reaching Daliang, not doffing armor, he went straight to Banqiao to strike Cai bandits and broke Lu Tang's stockade;

entries.zh: 瑭自溺而死，又於赤岡殺蔡軍二萬餘人。
entries.en: Tang drowned; at Red Mound he killed twenty thousand Cai troops.
entries.literal: Tang drowned himself; again at Red Mound he killed more than twenty thousand Cai troops.

entries.zh: 從討謝殷於亳州，擒之。
entries.en: He captured Xie Yin at Bozhou.
entries.literal: Following in the attack on Xie Yin at Bozhou, he captured him.

entries.zh: 回襲曹州，擄刺史丘宏禮以歸。
entries.en: Raiding Cao he took commissioner Qiu Hongli.
entries.literal: Returning to raid Cao prefecture he captured military commissioner Qiu Hongli and returned.

entries.zh: 與兗、鄆軍遇於臨濮之劉橋，殺數萬人，朱瑄、朱瑾僅以身免，擒都將鄒務卿已下五十人。
entries.en: At Liu Bridge he killed tens of thousands; Zhu Xuan and Jin barely escaped; he took fifty officers including Zou Wuqing.
entries.literal: Meeting Yan and Yanzhou troops at Liu Bridge in Linpu he killed tens of thousands; Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin barely escaped with their bodies; he captured commander Zou Wuqing and below fifty men.

entries.zh: 從太祖至範縣，復與朱瑄戰，擄尹萬榮等三人，遂平濮州。
entries.en: At Fan he beat Zhu Xuan, took Yin Wanrong and others, and pacified Pu.
entries.literal: Following the Founder to Fan county he again fought Zhu Xuan, captured Yin Wanrong and three others, and then pacified Pu prefecture.

entries.zh: 未幾，與朱珍擊蔡賊於陳、亳間，獲都將石璠。
entries.en: With Zhu Zhen he beat Cai between Chen and Bo and took Shi Fan.
entries.literal: Before long with Zhu Zhen he struck Cai bandits between Chen and Bo and captured commander Shi Fan.

entries.zh: 文德元年，魏博軍亂，樂從訓來告急，從太祖渡河，拔黎陽、李固、臨河等鎮，至內黃，破魏軍萬餘眾，獲其將周儒等十人。
entries.en: Wende 1 he crossed the river with the Founder, took Li Yang and other posts, and at Neihuang captured Zhou Ru and ten Wei officers.
entries.literal: In Wende year 1 Wei-Bo army mutinied; Le Congxun came reporting urgent distress; following the Founder across the river he took Li Yang, Liguo, Linhe, and other posts; reaching Neihuang he broke more than ten thousand Wei troops and captured their generals Zhou Ru and ten men.

entries.zh: 李罕之引並人圍張全義於河陽，從周與丁會、張存敬、牛存節率兵赴援，大破並軍，殺蕃漢二萬人，解河陽之圍，以功表授檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: He relieved Heyang from Li Hanzhi's Jin siege, killed twenty thousand, and became honorary Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Li Hanzhi led Jin men to besiege Zhang Quanyi at Heyang; Congzhou with Ding Hui, Zhang Cunjing, and Niu Cunjie led troops to the rescue, greatly defeated Jin troops, killed twenty thousand Han and barbarian, lifted Heyang's siege, and for merit was memorialized honorary Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 從朱珍討徐州，撥豐縣，敗時溥於吳康，得其輜重，加檢校刑部尚書。
entries.en: At Xuzhou he took Feng, beat Shi Pu at Wukang, and became honorary Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: Following Zhu Zhen to attack Xuzhou he took Feng county, defeated Shi Pu at Wukang, obtained his baggage train, and was added honorary Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 佐龐師古討孫儒於淮南，略地至廬、壽、滁等州，下天長、高郵，破邵伯堰。
entries.en: In Huainan with Pang Shigu he took Lu, Shou, Chu, Tianchang, and Gaoyou and broke Shaobo Dam.
entries.literal: Aiding Pang Shigu against Sun Ru in Huainan he swept territory to Lu, Shou, and Chu prefectures, took Tianchang and Gaoyou, and broke Shaobo Dam.

entries.zh: 回軍攻濠州，殺刺史魏勳，得餉船十艘。
entries.en: He took Haozhou, killed Wei Xun, and seized ten supply boats.
entries.literal: Returning he attacked Haozhou, killed military commissioner Wei Xun, and obtained ten supply boats.

entries.zh: 大順元年八月，並帥圍潞州，太祖遣從周率敢死之士，夜銜枚犯圍而入，會王師不利於馬牢川，即棄上黨而歸。
entries.en: Dashun 1, month 8, he slipped into besieged Lu; after defeat at Malaichuan the army abandoned Shangdang.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Dashun year 1 Jin commander besieged Lu prefecture; the Founder sent Congzhou with dare-death troops who by night held branches in their mouths and broke through the encirclement to enter; when the royal army was unfavorable at Malaichuan he then abandoned Shangdang and returned.

entries.zh: 其年十二月，與丁會諸將討魏州，連收十邑。
entries.en: Month 12 he and Ding Hui took ten Wei districts.
entries.literal: That year, twelfth month, with Ding Hui and generals he attacked Wei prefecture and in succession took ten districts.

entries.zh: 明年正月，大破魏軍於永定橋，魏軍五敗，斬首萬餘級。
entries.en: Month 1 next year he routed Wei five times at Yongding Bridge with ten thousand heads.
entries.literal: The next year, first month, he greatly defeated Wei troops at Yongding Bridge; Wei army five defeats, beheading more than ten thousand.

entries.zh: 十月，佐丁會攻宿州，從周壅水灌其城，刺史張筠以郡降。
entries.en: Month 10 he flooded Suzhou and Zhang Yun surrendered.
entries.literal: In the tenth month aiding Ding Hui in attacking Suzhou, Congzhou dammed water to flood the city; military commissioner Zhang Yun surrendered the prefecture.

entries.zh: 從討兗州，破朱瑾之軍於馬溝。
entries.en: He broke Zhu Jin at Magou in the Yanzhou campaign.
entries.literal: Following in the attack on Yanzhou he broke Zhu Jin's army at Magou.

entries.zh: 景福二年二月，與諸將大破徐、兗之兵於石佛山。
entries.en: Jingfu 2, month 2, he crushed Xu and Yan troops at Stone Buddha Mountain.
entries.literal: In the second month of Jingfu year 2 with generals he greatly defeated Xu and Yanzhou troops at Stone Buddha Mountain.

entries.zh: 八月，與龐師古同攻兗州。
entries.en: Month 8 he besieged Yanzhou with Pang Shigu.
entries.literal: In the eighth month with Pang Shigu he jointly attacked Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 乾寧元年三月，軍至新泰縣，朱瑾令都將張約、李胡椒率三千人來拒戰，師古遣從周、張存敬掩襲，生擒張約、李胡椒等都將數十人。
entries.en: Qianning 1, month 3, he ambushed and captured Zhang Yue, Li Hujiao, and dozens of Yan officers at Xintai.
entries.literal: In the third month of Qianning year 1 the army reached Xintai county; Zhu Jin ordered commander Zhang Yue and Li Hujiao to lead three thousand men to resist; Shigu sent Congzhou and Zhang Cunjing in ambush strike and captured Zhang Yue, Li Hujiao, and several tens of commanders alive.

entries.zh: 二年十月，圍兗州，兗人不出，從周詐揚言並人、鄆人來救，即引軍趨高吳，夜半卻潛歸寨。
entries.en: Besieging Yan he feigned a Jin-Yan relief march, then doubled back at night.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of year 2 besieging Yanzhou, Yan people did not come out; Congzhou falsely proclaimed Jin and Yanzhou men coming to rescue, then led troops toward Gaowu; at midnight he secretly returned to camp.

entries.zh: 朱瑾果出兵攻外壕，我軍士突出，掩殺千餘人，生擒都將張漢筠。
entries.en: Jin sallied; Congzhou ambushed and killed a thousand and captured Zhang Hanyun.
entries.literal: Zhu Jin indeed sent troops to attack the outer moat; our soldiers burst out, ambushed and killed more than a thousand, and captured commander Zhang Hanyun alive.

entries.zh: 從周累立戰功，自懷州刺史曆曹、宿二州刺史，累遷檢校左僕射。
entries.en: He rose from Huai to Cao and Su commissioner to honorary Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Congzhou repeatedly established battle merit; from Huai prefecture military commissioner he passed through Cao and Su prefecture military commissioners, repeatedly rising to honorary Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 三年五月，並帥以大軍侵魏，遣其子落落率二千騎屯洹水，從周以馬步二千人擊之，殺戮殆盡，擒落落於陣，並帥號泣而去。
entries.en: Month 5, year 3, he destroyed Luoluo's two thousand cavalry at Huan River and captured Keyong's son.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of year 3 the Jin commander with a great army invaded Wei and sent his son Luoluo with two thousand cavalry to camp at Huan River; Congzhou with two thousand horse and foot struck them, slaughter nearly all, and captured Luoluo in the formation; the Jin commander wailed and left.

entries.zh: 遂自洹水與龐師古渡河擊鄆。
entries.en: He crossed from Huan with Pang Shigu to attack Yan.
entries.literal: He then from Huan River with Pang Shigu crossed the river to attack Yan.

entries.zh: 四年正月，下之。
entries.en: Month 1, year 4, Yan fell.
entries.literal: In the first month of year 4 he took it.

entries.zh: 從周乘勝伐兗，會朱瑾出師在徐境，其將康懷英以城降。
entries.en: Pressing Yan he took it when Kang Huaiying surrendered while Jin was away.
entries.literal: Congzhou took victory in stride to attack Yan; when Zhu Jin marched out on campaign in Xu territory his general Kang Huaiying surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 以功授兗州留後、檢校司空。
entries.en: He became Yan acting commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed Yanzhou acting commissioner and honorary Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 復領兵萬餘人渡淮討楊行密，至濠州，聞龐師古清口之敗，遽班師。
entries.en: Crossing the Huai against Yang Xingmi he withdrew on news of Qingkou.
entries.literal: Again he led more than ten thousand troops across the Huai to attack Yang Xingmi; reaching Haozhou he heard of Pang Shigu's defeat at Qingkou and hastily withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 光化元年四月，率師經略山東，時並帥以大軍屯邢、洺，從周至钜鹿與並軍遇，大破之，並帥遁走。
entries.en: Guanghua 1, month 4, he routed the Jin army at Julu in Shandong.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Guanghua year 1 he led troops to pacify Shandong; at that time the Jin commander with a great army camped at Xing and Ming; Congzhou at Julu met Jin troops and greatly defeated them; the Jin commander fled.

entries.zh: 我軍追襲至青山口，數日之內，邢、洺、磁三州連下，斬首二萬級，獲將吏一百五十人，即以從周兼領邢州留後。
entries.en: He pursued to Qingshan and took Xing, Ming, and Ci with twenty thousand heads.
entries.literal: Our army pursued to Qingshan Pass; within several days Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures fell in succession; beheading twenty thousand, capturing a hundred fifty officers and clerks; Congzhou was made concurrent Xingzhou acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 十月，復破並軍五千騎於張公橋。
entries.en: Month 10 he beat five thousand Jin horse at Zhanggong Bridge.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he again defeated five thousand Jin cavalry at Zhanggong Bridge.

entries.zh: 晉將李嗣昭急攻邢州，陣於城門外，從周大破之，擒蕃將賁金鐵、慕容騰百餘人。
entries.en: The Jin general Li Sizhao pressed the attack on Xingzhou and formed his ranks outside the city gate. Congzhou routed him, capturing the tribal commanders Ben Jintie and Murong Teng along with more than a hundred men.
entries.literal: Jin general Li Sizhao pressed his attack on Xingzhou and drew up outside the city gate. Congzhou routed him and captured the tribal commanders Ben Jintie and Murong Teng, together with more than a hundred men.

entries.zh: 二年春，幽州劉仁恭率軍十萬寇魏州，屠貝郡。
entries.en: Spring year 2 Liu Rengong ravaged Wei and slaughtered Bei.
entries.literal: In spring of year 2 Youzhou's Liu Rengong led a hundred thousand army to raid Wei prefecture and slaughter Bei prefecture.

entries.zh: 從周自邢台馳入魏州，燕軍突上水關，攻館陶門。
entries.en: He galloped from Xingtai as Yan stormed Guantao Gate.
entries.literal: Congzhou from Xingtai galloped into Wei prefecture; Yan army suddenly rushed the upper water gate and attacked Guantao Gate.

entries.zh: 從周與賀德倫率五百騎出戰，謂門者曰：「前有敵，不可返顧！」
entries.en: With He Delun he charged out, telling the gatekeepers, "Enemies ahead—do not turn back!"
entries.literal: Congzhou with He Delun led five hundred cavalry out to battle and told the gatekeepers: "Enemies ahead—you must not look back!"

entries.zh: 命闔其門。
entries.en: He had the gates shut.
entries.literal: He ordered the gates shut.

entries.zh: 從周等極力死戰，大敗燕人，擒都將薛突厥、王郃郎等。
entries.en: They fought to the death and captured Xue Tujue and Wang Helang.
entries.literal: Congzhou and the rest exhausted strength in death battle, greatly defeated Yan men, and captured commanders Xue Tujue and Wang Helang and others.

entries.zh: 翌日，破其八寨，追擊至臨清，劉仁恭走滄州，從周授宣義軍行軍司馬。
entries.en: Next day he broke eight camps, pursued to Linqing, and Rengong fled to Cang.
entries.literal: The next day he broke their eight stockades, pursued to Linqing; Liu Rengong fled to Cangzhou; Congzhou was appointed Xuanyi army campaign deputy.

entries.zh: 五月，並人討李罕之於潞州，太祖以丁會代罕之，令從周馳入上黨。
entries.en: Month 5 he galloped into Shangdang as Jin attacked Lu.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Jin men attacked Li Hanzhi at Lu prefecture; the Founder made Ding Hui replace Hanzhi and ordered Congzhou to gallop into Shangdang.

entries.zh: 七月，並人陷澤州，太祖召從周，令賀德倫守潞州，德倫等尋棄城而歸。
entries.en: Month 7 Ze fell; He Delun abandoned Lu despite orders.
entries.literal: In the seventh month Jin men took Ze prefecture; the Founder summoned Congzhou and ordered He Delun to guard Lu prefecture; Delun and the rest soon abandoned the city and returned.

entries.zh: 三年四月，領軍討滄州，先攻德州，下之。
entries.en: Month 4, year 3, he took De then marched on Cang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of year 3 he led troops to attack Cangzhou, first attacking De prefecture and taking it.

entries.zh: 及進攻浮陽，幽州劉仁恭大舉來援。
entries.en: Besieging Fuyang he faced Liu Rengong's great relief army.
entries.literal: When advancing to attack Fuyang, Youzhou's Liu Rengong came in great force to aid.

entries.zh: 時都監蔣元暉謂諸將曰：「吾王命我護軍，志在攻取，今燕帥來赴，不可外戰，當縱其入壁，聚食囷廩，力屈糧盡，必可取也。」
entries.en: Overseer Jiang Yuanhui told the generals, "Our prince ordered me to protect the army with intent to attack and take. Now the Yan commander comes to the rescue—we cannot fight outside. We should let them enter the walls, gather and eat from the granaries, and when strength is spent and grain exhausted they can surely be taken."
entries.literal: At that time overseer Jiang Yuanhui told the generals: "Our prince ordered me to protect the army with intent to attack and take; now the Yan commander comes to the rescue—we cannot fight outside; we should let them enter the walls, gather and eat from granaries, and when strength is spent and grain exhausted they can surely be taken."

entries.zh: 從周對曰：「兵在機，機在上將，非督護所言也。」
entries.en: Congzhou replied, "War lies in opportunity; opportunity lies in the chief general—not what the overseer says."
entries.literal: Congzhou replied: "War lies in opportunity; opportunity lies in the chief general—not what the overseer says."

entries.zh: 乃令張存敬、氏叔琮守其寨。
entries.en: He left Zhang Cunjing and Shi Shuzong to hold camp.
entries.literal: He then ordered Zhang Cunjing and Shi Shuzong to guard the stockades.

entries.zh: 從周逆戰於乾寧軍老鴉堤，大破燕軍，斬首三萬，獲將佐馬慎交已下百餘人，奪馬三千匹。
entries.en: At Old Crow Embankment he killed thirty thousand Yan troops and took three thousand horses.
entries.literal: Congzhou met battle at Qianning army Old Crow Embankment, greatly defeated Yan army, beheaded thirty thousand, captured generals and aides Ma Shenjiao and below a hundred men, and seized three thousand horses.

entries.zh: 八月，並人攻邢、洺，從太祖破之。
entries.en: Month 8 he beat Jin at Xing and Ming with the Founder.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Jin men attacked Xing and Ming; following the Founder he defeated them.

entries.zh: 從周追襲至青山口，斬首五千級，獲其將王郃郎、楊師悅等，得馬千匹，表授檢校太保，兼徐州兩使留後，尋為兗州節度使。
entries.en: Pursuing to Qingshan he took five thousand heads and became Yan commissioner and honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Congzhou pursued to Qingshan Pass, beheaded five thousand, captured their generals Wang Helang, Yang Shiyue, and others, obtained a thousand horses, was memorialized honorary Grand Guardian, concurrent Xu two-circuits acting commissioner, soon Yanzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 天復元年三月，與氏叔琮討太原，從周以兗、鄆之眾，自土門路入，與諸軍會於晉陽城下，以糧運不給，班師。
entries.en: Tianfu 1, month 3, with Shi Shuzong he marched on Taiyuan; Congzhou led the Yan and Yun forces in by the Tumen route, joined the armies below Jinyang, and withdrew when supplies failed.
entries.literal: In the third month of Tianfu year 1, with Shi Shuzong he campaigned against Taiyuan; Congzhou led the Yan and Yun forces in by the Tumen route, joined the armies beneath Jinyang, and withdrew when grain transport failed.

entries.zh: 頃之，從周染疾，會青州將劉鄩陷兗州，太祖命討之，遂力疾臨戎。
entries.en: Soon after he fell ill; when Liu Xun of Qingzhou took Yanzhou, the Founder ordered him to attack and he took the field despite illness.
entries.literal: Soon after Congzhou fell ill; when Qingzhou general Liu Xun took Yanzhou, the Founder ordered him to attack and he took the field despite illness.

entries.zh: 三年十一月，鄩舉城降，以功授檢校太傅。
entries.en: Month 11, Tianfu 3, Xun surrendered the city and Congzhou was made honorary Grand Tutor for the merit.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of year 3, Xun surrendered the city; for merit he was made honorary Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 太祖以從周抱疾既久，命康懷英代之，授左金吾上將軍，以風恙不任朝謁，改右衛上將軍致仕。
entries.en: The Founder, since Congzhou's illness had long lingered, had Kang Huaiying replace him and made Congzhou Left Golden Crow general; wind ailment kept him from court, so he was changed to Right Guard general and retired.
entries.literal: The Founder, since Congzhou's illness had long lingered, ordered Kang Huaiying to replace him and made Congzhou General of the Left Golden Crow Guards; because wind ailment prevented court attendance, he was changed to General of the Right Guard and retired.

entries.zh: 養疾偃師縣亳邑鄉之別墅。
entries.en: He nursed his illness at a villa in Boyi township, Yanshi county.
entries.literal: He nursed his illness at a villa in Boyi township, Yanshi county.

entries.zh: 頃之，授太子太師，依前致仕。
entries.en: Soon after he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, still retired as before.
entries.literal: Soon after he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, still retired as before.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，製授潞州節度使，令坐食其俸，加開府儀同三司、檢校太師、兼侍中，封陳留郡王，累食邑至七千戶，命近臣賚旌節就別墅以賜之。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, an edict made him Lu commissioner with seated salary, added the Golden Pocket and Honored Equal to the Three Dukes, honorary Grand Preceptor, and Palace Secretary, enfeoffed him as Prince of Chenliu with a fief reaching seven thousand households, and sent a close official with banners and credentials to his villa.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, an edict appointed him military commissioner of Lu with seated salary, added Bearer of the Golden Pocket with Honored Equal to the Three Dukes, honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Palace Secretary, enfeoffed him as Prince of Chenliu commandery with cumulative food domain to seven thousand households, and ordered a close official to bring banners and credentials to his villa as gifts.

entries.zh: 貞明初，卒於家。
entries.en: Early in Zhenming he died at home.
entries.literal: Early in Zhenming he died at home.

entries.zh: 冊贈太尉。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 謝彥章，許州人。
entries.en: Xie Yanzhang came from Xu prefecture.
entries.literal: Xie Yanzhang was a Xu prefecture man.

entries.zh: 幼事從周為養父，從周憐其敏慧，教以兵法，常以千錢於大盤中，布其行陣偏伍之狀，示以出沒進退之節，彥章盡得其訣。
entries.en: Adopted by Congzhou, he learned warfare on a tray of coins modeling formations.
entries.literal: In youth he served Congzhou as adopted father; Congzhou pitied his quick intelligence, taught him military arts, often used a thousand cash on a great tray to array battle formations and partial units, showing advance-and-retreat rhythm; Yanzhang fully obtained the secrets.

entries.zh: 及壯，事太祖為騎將。
entries.en: Grown, he served the Founder as cavalry officer.
entries.literal: When grown he served the Founder as a cavalry officer.

entries.zh: 末帝嗣位，用為兩京馬軍都軍使，累與晉軍接戰有功，尋領河陽節度使。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor he commanded both capitals' cavalry, won against Jin, and became Heyang commissioner.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, he was used as both-capitals horse army overall commander; repeatedly fighting Jin troops he had merit; soon he held Heyang military commission.

entries.zh: 及從周卒，臨喪行服，躬預葬事，時人義之。
entries.en: He mourned Congzhou in full filial rites and was praised.
entries.literal: When Congzhou died he attended the mourning wearing funeral garb and personally took part in burial; men of the time praised the righteousness.

entries.zh: 彥章後為許州節度使、檢校太傅。
entries.en: Later he was Xu commissioner and honorary Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Yanzhang later was Xu military commissioner and honorary Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 貞明四年冬，滑州節度使賀瑰為北面招討使，彥章為排陣使，同領大軍，駐於行台寨，與晉人對壘。
entries.en: Zhenming 4 winter he and He Gui camped at Xingtai against the Jin army.
entries.literal: In winter of Zhenming year 4 Huazhou military commissioner He Gui was northern campaign commander; Yanzhang was array commander; together they led the great army, camped at Xingtai Stockade, and faced Jin men in opposing camps.

entries.zh: 彥章時領騎軍與之挑戰，晉人或望我軍行陣整肅，則相謂曰：「必兩京太傅在此也。」
entries.en: Yanzhang led cavalry to challenge them; Jin troops seeing our formations would say to one another, "The two-capitals Grand Tutor must be here."
entries.literal: Yanzhang then led cavalry to challenge them; Jin men sometimes seeing our army's formations neat and stern would say to one another: "The two-capitals Grand Tutor must be here."

entries.zh: 不敢以名呼，其為敵人所憚如此。
entries.en: They would not speak his name aloud.
entries.literal: They did not dare call him by name; such was the enemy's fear of him.

entries.zh: 是時咸謂賀瑰能將步軍，彥章能領騎士，既名聲相軋，故瑰心忌之。
entries.en: He Gui resented Yanzhang because both were famed commanders.
entries.literal: At that time all said He Gui could command foot soldiers and Yanzhang could lead cavalry; since fame rubbed against each other, Gui therefore resented him in heart.

entries.zh: 一日，與瑰同設伏於郊外，瑰指一方地謂彥章曰：「此地岡阜隆起，中央坦夷，好列柵之所。」
entries.en: One day Gui pointed at a plot of ground and told Yanzhang, "This mound rises and the center is level—good for setting palisades."
entries.literal: One day with Gui he jointly set ambush in the suburbs; Gui pointed at one plot of ground and told Yanzhang: "This place's mound rises and the center is level—good for setting palisades."

entries.zh: 尋而晉人舍之，故瑰疑彥章與晉人通；
entries.en: Jin avoided it; Gui suspected Yanzhang of collusion;
entries.literal: Soon Jin men abandoned it; therefore Gui suspected Yanzhang communicated with Jin men;

entries.zh: 又瑰欲速戰，彥章欲持重以老敵人，瑰益疑之。
entries.en: Gui wanted battle; Yanzhang wanted delay; suspicion grew.
entries.literal: Again Gui wished swift battle; Yanzhang wished to hold weight and wear out the enemy; Gui's suspicion increased.

entries.zh: 會為行營馬步都虞候朱珪所誣，瑰遂與珪邦協謀，因享士伏甲以殺彥章及濮州刺史孟審澄、別將侯溫裕等於軍，以謀叛聞。
entries.en: Zhu Gui slandered him; at a feast Gui ambushed and killed Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu as traitors.
entries.literal: When camp horse-and-foot chief commandant Zhu Gui slandered him, Gui then with Gui conspired, and at a feast for officers set hidden armor and killed Yanzhang, Bozhou military commissioner Meng Shencheng, and separate commander Hou Wenyu and others in the army, reporting it as plotting rebellion.

entries.zh: 晉王聞之，喜曰：「彼將帥如是，亡無日矣。」
entries.en: The Prince of Jin rejoiced, "With generals like that they will soon fall."
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin heard it and said with pleasure: "Their generals like this—ruin will come in no long day."

entries.zh: 張歸厚，字德坤，
entries.en: Zhang Guihou, styled Dekun,
entries.literal: Zhang Guihou, style name Dekun,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣列傳》云：歸厚祖興，父處讓。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Mirror Examined》 supplement cites the 《Biographies of Liang Merit Ministers》: grandfather Xing, father Churang.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Mirror Examined》 cites the 《Biographies of Liang Merit Ministers》: Guihou's grandfather Xing, father Churang.)〉

entries.zh: 少驍勇，有機略，尤長於弓槊之用。
entries.en: Young he was fierce, clever, and master of bow and spear.
entries.literal: In youth fierce and brave, had resourcefulness, especially excelled in bow and spear use.

entries.zh: 中和末，與兄歸霸自巢軍相率來降，太祖署為軍校。
entries.en: Late Zhonghe he surrendered from Chao with Guiba as army officer.
entries.literal: At the end of Zhonghe with elder brother Guiba he came from Chao's army in succession to surrender; the Founder appointed him army officer.

entries.zh: 時淮西兵力方壯，太祖之師尚寡，歸厚以少擊眾，往無不捷。
entries.en: Though few against many, he never lost.
entries.literal: At that time Huaixi military power was just strong; the Founder's army was still few; Guihou with few struck many and went nowhere without victory.

entries.zh: 光啟三年春，與秦宗賢戰於萬勝，大破之。
entries.en: Guangqi 3 spring he crushed Qin Zongxian at Wansheng.
entries.literal: In spring of Guangqi year 3 he fought Qin Zongxian at Wansheng and greatly defeated him.

entries.zh: 其夏，蔡將張至以數萬眾屯於赤堈，歸厚嘗與至單騎鬥於陣，至不能支而奔，師徒乘此大捷。
entries.en: He single-handedly drove off Zhang Zhi at Chijin in a mounted duel.
entries.literal: That summer Cai general Zhang Zhi with tens of thousands encamped at Chijin; Guihou once single-horse dueled Zhi in the formation; Zhi could not sustain and fled; the army took this great victory.

entries.zh: 太祖大悅，立署為騎軍長，仍以鞍馬器幣錫之。
entries.en: The Founder made him cavalry chief and gave him horse and gear.
entries.literal: The Founder was greatly pleased, immediately appointed him cavalry army chief, and still bestowed saddle, horse, vessels, and silks.

entries.zh: 及佐朱珍討時溥，寨於豐、蕭之間，歸厚乘徐壘如行坦途，甚為諸將歎伏。
entries.en: Besieging Shi Pu he crossed Xu walls as if on flat ground.
entries.literal: When aiding Zhu Zhen against Shi Pu he stockaded between Feng and Xiao; Guihou crossed Xu ramparts as if on level road—generals deeply sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 龍紀初，奏遷檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: Longji he became honorary Minister of Works.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was memorialized transferred honorary Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 其年冬，復伐徐，歸厚以偏師徑進，至九里山下與徐兵遇。
entries.en: That winter he advanced to Jiuli Mountain against Xu.
entries.literal: That winter he again attacked Xu; Guihou with a separate column went straight forward to below Jiuli Mountain and met Xu troops.

entries.zh: 時我之叛將陳璠在賊陣中，歸厚忽見之，因瞋目大罵，單馬直往，期於必取，會飛矢中左目而退；
entries.en: Seeing rebel Chen Fan he charged alone until an arrow blinded his left eye;
entries.literal: At that time our rebel Chen Fan was in the bandit formation; Guihou suddenly saw him, glared and loudly cursed, single horse went straight there intending surely to take him; a flying arrow struck the left eye and he withdrew;

entries.zh: 徐戎甚眾，莫敢追之。
entries.en: Xu troops dared not pursue.
entries.literal: Xu troops were very many; none dared pursue.

entries.zh: 張歸弁，字從冕。
entries.en: Zhang Guibian, styled Congmian.
entries.literal: Zhang Guibian, style name Congmian.

entries.zh: 始與兄歸霸、歸厚同歸於太祖，得署為牙校。
entries.en: At first he and his elder brothers Guiba and Guihou together gave allegiance to the Founder, and he was appointed a guard officer.
entries.literal: At first with brothers Guiba and Guihou he together returned to the Founder and was appointed guard officer.

entries.zh: 時太祖初鎮宣武，屢命歸弁結好於近境，頗得行人之儀。
entries.en: When the Founder first held Xuanwu, he repeatedly ordered Guibian to knit good relations with the nearby borders, and he quite obtained the travelers' courtesy.
entries.literal: When the Founder first held Xuanwu, he repeatedly ordered Guibian to knit good relations with near borders, quite obtaining travelers' courtesy.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，以偏師佐葛從周禦並軍於洹水。
entries.en: Qianning he aided Congzhou at Huan River.
entries.literal: In Qianning he with a separate column aided Ge Congzhou in meeting Jin troops at Huan River.

entries.zh: 光啟中，又佐張存敬與燕人戰於內黃，積前後功，表授檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: In Guangqi he again aided Zhang Cunjing in fighting Yan men at Neihuang; accumulating former and later merit, he was memorialized as honorary Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In Guangqi he again aided Zhang Cunjing in fighting Yan men at Neihuang; accumulating former and later merit he was memorialized honorary Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 大順初，攻討兗、鄆，命歸弁佐衡王友諒屯單父，軍聲大振，尋為齊州指揮使。
entries.en: At the beginning of Dashun, when attacking Yan and Yun, he was ordered to aid Prince of Heng Youliang in camping at Shanfu; military prestige greatly shook, and he was soon made Qi prefecture commander.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dashun, attacking Yan and Yun, he was ordered to aid Prince of Heng Youliang to camp at Shanfu; military prestige greatly shook; soon he was Qi prefecture commander.

entries.zh: 屬青帥王師範叛，遣將詐為賈人，挽車數十乘，匿兵器於其中，將謀竊發，歸弁察而擒之，州城以寧。
entries.en: He foiled Wang Shifan's merchants smuggling arms into Qi.
entries.literal: When Qing commander Wang Shifan rebelled he sent generals feigning merchants, several tens of carts, hiding weapons within, intending to steal a sudden outbreak; Guibian detected and captured them; the prefectural city was thereby pacified.

entries.zh: 明年春，青寇大舉來伐，州兵既寡，民意頗搖，有本郡都將。
entries.en: Next spring Qing attacked; the city wavered when officers plotted treason.
entries.literal: The next spring Qing raiders came in great force to attack; prefectural troops were few and popular hearts somewhat shaken; there were native-command officers.

entries.zh: 康文爽等三人欲謀外應，即時擒獲誅之，人心遂定。
entries.en: Kang Wenshuang and two others—three in all—wished to plot an outer response; he at once captured and executed them; popular hearts were then settled.
entries.literal: Kang Wenshuang and three others wished to plot outer response; he at once captured and executed them; popular hearts were then settled.

entries.zh: 歸弁又罄發私帑，賞給士伍，青州平，超加檢校右僕射，遙領愛州刺史。
entries.en: He spent his own treasury on the troops; after Qing fell he became honorary Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: Guibian also exhausted his private stores to reward and give to soldiers; Qing was pacified; he was specially added honorary Right Vice Director, holding Ai prefecture military commission at a distance.

entries.zh: 從征荊、襄回，轉檢校左僕射。
entries.en: After Jing and Xiang he became honorary Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Returning from campaigning in Jing and Xiang he was transferred honorary Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 天祐三年春，太祖入魏誅牙軍，魏之郡邑多叛，歸弁與諸將等分布攻討，封境悉平。
entries.en: Tianyou 3 spring he helped pacify Wei after the guard massacre.
entries.literal: In spring of Tianyou year 3 the Founder entered Wei and executed the guard army; Wei's prefectures and districts mostly rebelled; Guibian with generals and others separately distributed attack and suppression; the sealed borders were all pacified.

entries.zh: 而歸弁於高唐攻賊太猛，飛矢中於臆，太祖嘉之，命賜鞍勒馬一匹、金帶一條。
entries.en: Wounded storming Gaotang he won a horse and gold belt from the Founder.
entries.literal: Yet Guibian at Gaotang attacked bandits too fiercely; a flying arrow struck his chest; the Founder praised it and ordered bestowed one saddle, bridle, and horse, one gold belt.

entries.zh: 夏五月，命權知晉州。
entries.en: Summer month 5 he acted as Jin commissioner.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer he was ordered provisional Jin prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 冬十一月，真授晉州刺史，加檢校司空。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of winter he was formally appointed Jin prefecture military commissioner and added honorary Director of Works.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter he was formally appointed Jin prefecture military commissioner, added honorary Director of Works.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，改滑州長劍指揮使。
entries.en: At the abdication he commanded Huazhou long-sword troops.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was changed Huazhou long-sword commander.

entries.zh: 開平二年秋九月，並軍圍平陽，詔歸弁統兵救之。
entries.en: Kaiping 2 autumn he relieved besieged Pingyang.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of autumn of Kaiping year 2 Jin troops besieged Pingyang; an edict ordered Guibian to lead troops to rescue.

entries.zh: 軍至，解其圍，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: When the army arrived it lifted the encirclement; he was added honorary Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: When the army arrived it lifted the encirclement; he was added honorary Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 三年春三月，寢疾，卒於滑州之私第。
entries.en: Year 3 spring he died at his Huazhou home.
entries.literal: In the third month of spring of year 3 he fell ill in bed and died at his private residence in Huazhou.

entries.zh: 子漢融。
entries.en: His son was Hanrong.
entries.literal: Son Hanrong.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：從周以驍武之才，事雄猜之主，而能取功名於馬上，啟手足於牖下，靜而言之，斯為賢矣！
entries.en: The historian praises Congzhou for serving a suspicious lord yet dying in honor.
entries.literal: The historian says: Congzhou with fierce martial talent served a heroically suspicious lord, yet could take fame and achievement on horseback and open hands and feet below the window—in calm speech, this is worthy.

entries.zh: 彥章蔚有將才，死於讒口，身既歿矣，國亦隨之，惜哉！
entries.en: Yanzhang's murder doomed the state—pity!
entries.literal: Yanzhang had abundant general talent yet died at slander's mouth; body already perished, state also followed—pity!

entries.zh: 歸霸昆仲，皆脫身於巨盜之流，宣力於興王之運。
entries.en: The Zhang brothers left banditry to build the Liang dynasty.
entries.literal: The Guiba brothers all escaped from great bandit streams and displayed strength in the rising-king's fortune.

entries.zh: 由介胄而析圭爵，可不謂壯夫歟！
entries.en: From soldiers to nobles—they were true stalwarts!
entries.literal: From armor and helmet to split tallies and ranks—can they not be called stalwart men!

entries.zh: 初，澧、朗二州，本屬荊南，乾寧中，為土豪雷滿所據。
entries.en: Li and Lang, once part of Jingnan, fell to the local strongman Lei Man in Qianning.
entries.literal: At first Li and Lang two prefectures originally belonged to Jingnan; in Qianning they were held by local strongman Lei Man.

entries.zh: 汭奏請割隸，唐宰相徐彥若執而不行，汭由是銜之。
entries.en: Rui asked the court to annex them; Chancellor Xu Yanruo refused, and Rui nursed a grudge.
entries.literal: Rui memorialized requesting to detach and subordinate them; Tang chancellor Xu Yanruo held firm and did not carry it out; Rui thereby harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 及彥若出鎮南海，路過江陵，汭雖加延接，而猶怏怏。
entries.en: When Yanruo passed Jiangling en route to his Nanhai post, Rui received him coldly despite the courtesies.
entries.literal: When Yanruo went out to command Nanhai, passing Jiangling, Rui though adding courtesies was still displeased.

entries.zh: 嘗因對酒，語及其事，彥若曰：「令公位尊方面，自比桓、文。
entries.en: At wine Yanruo said, "You rank yourself with Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi and Jin.
entries.literal: Once over wine he spoke of the matter; Yanruo said: "My lord's position is honored in your quarter, comparing yourself to Huan and Wen.

entries.zh: 雷滿者，偏州一草賊爾，令公盍不加兵，而反怨朝廷乎！」
entries.en: Yet you resent the court over Lei Man, a mere frontier bandit—why not march against him instead?"
entries.literal: Lei Man is but a petty prefecture grass bandit—why does my lord not send troops instead of resenting the court!"

entries.zh: 汭赧然而屈。
entries.en: Rui flushed and fell silent.
entries.literal: Rui blushed and was subdued.

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
entries.en: (The text below is lost.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉

entries.zh: 累官至檢校太尉，封上穀郡王。
entries.en: He rose to honorary Grand Commandant and was made Prince of Shanggu.
entries.literal: In succession he reached honorary Grand General and was enfeoffed Prince of Shanggu commandery.

entries.zh: 楊行密以兵圍鄂州，汭出師以援鄂，淮寇乘之，以火焚其艦，汭投江而死。
entries.en: When Yang Xingmi besieged Ezhou, Rui sailed to relieve it; the Huainan fleet burned his ships and he drowned himself in the river.
entries.literal: Yang Xingmi with troops besieged Ezhou; Rui marched out to relieve E; Huainan raiders seized the moment, used fire to burn his warships; Rui threw himself in the river and died.

entries.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖以汭歿於王事，上表於唐帝，請為汭立廟於荊門，優詔可之。
entries.en: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder had the Tang court approve a temple for Rui at Jingmen, honoring his death in service.
entries.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder because Rui died in royal service memorialized the Tang emperor requesting a temple for Rui at Jingmen; gracious edict approved.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：鄭準，不知何許人，性諒直，能為文章，長於箋奏。
entries.en: (The 《Supplement》 says Zheng Zhun, of unknown origin, was upright, literate, and expert at memorials.
entries.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Zheng Zhun, origin unknown, nature frank and upright, able at writing, skilled at memorials and reports.

entries.zh: 成汭鎮荊南，辟為推官。
entries.en: When Cheng Rui held Jingnan he made Zhun his investigating officer.
entries.literal: Cheng Rui garrisoned Jingnan and recruited him as investigating officer.

entries.zh: 汭嘗仇殺人，懼為吏所捕，改姓郭氏。
entries.en: After a feud killing he had taken the surname Guo to evade the law.
entries.literal: Rui once killed in feud; fearing capture by officers, changed surname to Guo.

entries.zh: 及為荊南節度使，命準為表，乞歸本姓。
entries.en: As Jingnan commissioner he had Zhun draft a memorial to restore the name Cheng.
entries.literal: When he became Jingnan military commissioner, ordered Zhun to draft a memorial begging restoration of original surname.

entries.zh: 準援筆而成，其略云：「臣門非冠蓋，家本軍戎。
entries.en: Zhun wrote at once; it began, "My house wears no court caps; my family comes from the army.
entries.literal: Zhun took brush and completed it; gist said: "Your subject's house is not of noble caps and canopies; family origin is military camp.

entries.zh: 親朋之內，盱睢為人報怨；
entries.en: Among kin and friends, eyes glaring to settle others' scores;
entries.literal: Among kin and friends, glaring and gnashing to avenge others;

entries.zh: 昆弟之間，點染無處求生。
entries.en: Among brothers, marked with blood and nowhere to live.
entries.literal: Among brothers, stained with nowhere to seek life.

entries.zh: 背故國以狐疑，望鄰封而鼠竄。
entries.en: I turned from my homeland in doubt and scurried to a neighbor like a cornered rat.
entries.literal: Turning back on the old state in hesitant doubt, looking to neighboring borders and fleeing like a rat.

entries.zh: 名非霸越，乘舟難效於陶朱；
entries.en: I was no lord of Wu or Yue—by boat I could not follow Fan Li;
entries.literal: Name not Ba and Yue, boarding a boat hard to emulate Tao Zhu;

entries.zh: 誌切投秦，出境遂稱於張祿。」
entries.en: My heart set on Qin, I crossed the border and called myself Zhang Lu."
entries.literal: Aspiration keen to throw in with Qin, crossing the border then styled as Zhang Lu."

entries.zh: 又云：「成為本姓，郭乃冒稱。
entries.en: It added, "Cheng is my true name; Guo was a borrowed lie.
entries.literal: Also said: "Cheng is the original surname; Guo is usurped claim.

entries.zh: 本避犯禁之辜，敢歸司寇；
entries.en: I fled a capital crime; I dare submit again to justice;
entries.literal: Originally avoiding the guilt of forbidden offense, dare return to the Minister of Crime;

entries.zh: 別族受封之典，誠愧諸侯。
entries.en: yet to hold a fief under a false name shames me before the lords.
entries.literal: Separate-surname receiving enfeoffment rites—truly ashamed before the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 伏乞聖慈，許歸本姓」云云。
entries.en: I kneel and beg Your Majesty to let me bear my true name again," and so on.
entries.literal: Kneeling beg sacred kindness, permit restoration of original surname," etc.

entries.zh: 其表甚為朝廷所重。
entries.en: The court held that memorial in high regard.
entries.literal: That memorial was greatly valued by the court.

entries.zh: 後因汭生辰，淮南楊行密遣使致禮幣之外，仍貺《初學記》一部。
entries.en: On Rui's birthday Yang Xingmi sent gifts from Huainan—and added a copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.
entries.literal: Later because of Rui's birthday Huainan Yang Xingmi sent envoys with ceremonial gifts besides, still bestowing one copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.

entries.zh: 準忿然以為不可，謂汭曰：「夫《初學記》，蓋訓童之書爾，今敵國交聘，以此書為貺，得非相輕之甚耶！
entries.en: Zhun was furious and told Rui, "The 《Elementary Studies》 is a schoolbook for children. An enemy state sends it as a state gift—is that not open contempt?
entries.literal: Zhun angrily deemed it unacceptable, told Rui: "The 《Elementary Studies》 is merely a book for instructing children; now enemy states exchange missions—using this book as a gift, is it not extreme mutual slight!

entries.zh: 宜書責讓。」
entries.en: You should answer with a written rebuke."
entries.literal: Should write to reprove and blame."

entries.zh: 汭不納，準自歎曰：「若然，見輕敵國，足彰幕府之無人也。
entries.en: Rui refused. Zhun sighed, "Accept this and we show the enemy our staff has no one with spine.
entries.literal: Rui did not accept; Zhun sighed to himself: "If so, being slighted by the enemy state sufficiently shows the headquarters has no men.

entries.zh: 參佐無狀，安可久！」
entries.en: I cannot serve such a court any longer!"
entries.literal: Staff officers unworthy—how can one long remain!"

entries.zh: 遽請解職。
entries.en: He resigned at once.
entries.literal: Hastily requested dismissal from office.

entries.zh: 汭怒其去，潛使人於途中殺之。）〉
entries.en: Rui, enraged, had him murdered on the road home.)〉
entries.literal: Rui angry at his departure, secretly sent men on the road to kill him.)〉

entries.zh: 杜洪者，江夏伶人。
entries.en: Du Hong had been an entertainer in Jiangxia.
entries.literal: Du Hong was a Jiangxia entertainer.

entries.zh: 鍾傳者，豫章小校。
entries.en: Zhong Chuan was a low officer in Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Zhong Chuan was a Yuzhang junior officer.

entries.zh: 唐光啟中，秦宗權凶焰飆起，屢擾江、淮，郡將不能城守。
entries.en: In Guangqi, Qin Zongquan ravaged the Jiang-Huai region until prefectural garrisons could no longer hold their walls.
entries.literal: In Tang Guangqi, Qin Zongquan's vicious flame rose like a whirlwind, repeatedly harassed Jiang and Huai; prefectural defenders could not hold the walls.

entries.zh: 洪、傳各為部校，因戰立威，逐其廉使，自稱留後，朝廷因而命之。
entries.en: Hong and Chuan rose as unit commanders, fought their way to power, expelled their superiors, declared themselves acting governors, and won court recognition.
entries.literal: Hong and Chuan each were division officers; through battle established prestige, drove out their provincial inspectors, styled themselves acting governors; court thereby appointed them.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：光啟二年，洪乘虛入鄂，自為節度使留後，僖宗即拜本軍節度使。
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says that in Guangqi 2 Hong seized Ezhou, made himself acting commissioner, and Xizong confirmed him.)
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Guangqi year 2, Hong seized an opening to enter E, styled himself acting military commissioner, Emperor Xizong at once appointed him full army military commissioner.

entries.zh: 中和三年，傳逐江西觀察使高茂卿，遂有洪州，僖宗擢傳江西團練使，俄拜鎮南節度使。）〉
entries.en: (In Zhonghe 3 Chuan expelled Gao Maoqing from Jiangxi, took Hongzhou, and was made training commissioner, then Zhennan military commissioner.)〉
entries.literal: Zhonghe year 3, Chuan drove out Jiangxi observation commissioner Gao Maoqing, then held Hongzhou; Xizong promoted Chuan Jiangxi training commissioner, soon appointed Zhennan military commissioner.)〉

entries.zh: 及為楊行密所攻，洪、傳首尾相應，皆遣求援於太祖；
entries.en: When Yang Xingmi attacked them, Hong and Chuan backed each other and both appealed to the Founder;
entries.literal: When attacked by Yang Xingmi, Hong and Chuan head and tail responded, all sent seeking aid from the Founder;

entries.zh: 太祖遣朱友恭赴之，大破淮寇於武昌，二鎮稍寧。
entries.en: The Founder sent Zhu Yougong, who routed the Huainan army at Wuchang and gave the two regions brief relief.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Zhu Yougong to go; greatly defeated Huainan bandits at Wuchang; the two prefectures gradually calmed.

entries.zh: 及行密乘勝急攻洪、鄂，洪復乞師於太祖；
entries.en: When Xingmi pressed the attack on Hong and E, Hong again begged the Founder for troops;
entries.literal: When Xingmi seized victory to press attack on Hong and E, Hong again begged troops from the Founder;

entries.zh: 太祖命荊南成汭率荊、襄舟師以赴之。
entries.en: The Founder ordered Cheng Rui of Jingnan to sail the Jing-Xiang fleet to his aid.
entries.literal: The Founder ordered Jingnan Cheng Rui to lead Jing and Xiang river fleets to go relieve.

entries.zh: 未至夏口，汭敗溺死，淮人遂陷鄂州，洪為其所擒，被害於廣陵市，時唐天復二年也。
entries.en: Rui drowned in defeat before Xiakou; the Huainan army took Ezhou, seized Hong, and executed him at Guangling market in Tianfu 2.
entries.literal: Before reaching Xiakou, Rui was defeated and drowned; Huainan men then took Ezhou; Hong was captured by them, killed at Guangling market—then Tang Tianfu year 2.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·劉存傳》：存急焚鄂州城樓，梁援兵將突圍而出，諸將欲急擊之，存曰：「擊之賊必復入，復入則城愈固矣，不若聽其遁去。」
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says Liu Cun burned Ezhou's tower as Liang relief tried to break out. His officers wanted a hard strike; Cun said, "Hit them and they will rush back in and the wall will only tighten—let them go."
