entries.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Liu Cun》: Cun urgently burned Ezhou's tower; Liang relief troops were about to break out; the generals wished to strike them hard; Cun said: "Strike them and the bandits will re-enter; re-enter and the city will be firmer still—better to let them escape."

entries.zh: 諸將皆曰：「善。」
entries.en: The generals said, "Good."
entries.literal: The generals all said: "Good."

entries.zh: 是日城陷，擒杜洪父子，斬於廣陵市。）〉
entries.en: That day the city fell; Du Hong and his son were taken and beheaded at Guangling market.)〉
entries.literal: That day the city fell; Du Hong father and son were captured and beheaded at Guangling market.)〉

entries.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖表請為洪立廟於其鎮，優詔可之。
entries.en: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder won approval for a temple to Du Hong in his old command.
entries.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder memorialized requesting a temple for Hong at his command; gracious edict approved.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈太傅。
entries.en: After the Founder took the throne, Hong was posthumously named Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 先是，鍾傳卒於江西，其子繼之，
entries.en: Earlier Zhong Chuan had died in Jiangxi and his son succeeded him,
entries.literal: Before this, Zhong Chuan died in Jiangxi; his son succeeded him,

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·秦裴傳》：天祐三年，洪州鍾傳卒，州人立其子匡時。
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that in Tianyou 3 Zhong Chuan died at Hongzhou and the people set up his son Kuangshi.)
entries.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Qin Pei》: Tianyou year 3, Hongzhou Zhong Chuan died; the prefecture's people installed his son Kuangshi.

entries.zh: 江州刺史延規，傳之養子，忿不得立，以其郡納款，因授裴西南面行營招討使，攻匡時。
entries.en: Yan Gui, Chuan's adopted son and Jiangzhou prefect, resenting his exclusion, surrendered his prefecture; Qin Pei was sent to attack Kuangshi.
entries.literal: Jiangzhou prefect Yan Gui, Chuan's adoptive son, angry at not being installed, submitted his prefecture in surrender; therefore Pei was appointed southwest campaign pacification commissioner and attacked Kuangshi.

entries.zh: 城陷，擒匡時以獻。）〉
entries.en: The city fell and Kuangshi was captured and sent in.)〉
entries.literal: The city fell; Kuangshi was captured and presented.)〉

entries.zh: 尋為楊行密所敗，其地亦入於淮夷。
entries.en: Soon Yang Xingmi defeated them and Jiangxi too passed to Huainan.
entries.literal: Soon defeated by Yang Xingmi; that territory too entered Huainan barbarians.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：鍾傳雖起於商販，尤好學重士，時江西上流有名第者，多因傳薦，四遠騰然，謂之曰英明。
entries.en: (The 《Supplement》 says Chuan began as a trader but prized learning and patronized scholars; eminent Jiangxi families often owed their posts to him, and men far and wide called him "the enlightened."
entries.literal: (The 《Supplement》: Though Zhong Chuan rose from merchant peddlers, he especially loved learning and honored scholars; at that time famous clans of upper Jiangxi mostly entered through Chuan's recommendation; from the four quarters it soared—people called him "the enlightened one."

entries.zh: 諸葛浩素有詞學，嘗為泗州管驛巡官，仰傳之風，因擇其所行事赫赫可稱者十條，列於啟事以投之。
entries.en: Zhuge Hao, a man of letters once posted at a Sizhou relay station, admired Chuan and sent a memorial listing ten of his finest deeds.
entries.literal: Zhuge Hao always had literary learning; once was Sizhou postal-station patrol officer; admiring Chuan's reputation, he therefore selected ten items from Chuan's deeds that shone and could be praised, arrayed them in a memorial to submit.

entries.zh: 十啟凡五千字，皆文理典贍，傳覽之驚歎，謂賓佐曰：「此啟事每一字可以千錢酬之。」
entries.en: Ten sections, five thousand characters, all polished; Chuan read them in wonder and told his staff, "Every character in this is worth a thousand cash."
entries.literal: Ten memorials in all five thousand characters, all literary reasoning elegant and ample; Chuan on reading was startled and sighed, told his staff: "This memorial—each character can be rewarded with a thousand cash."

entries.zh: 遂以五千貫贈，仍辟在幕下，其激勸如此。
entries.en: He gave five thousand strings, took Hao onto his staff, and rewarded talent that lavishly.
entries.literal: Thereupon with five thousand strings he was gifted, still recruited to the headquarters—such was his encouragement.

entries.zh: 上藍和尚，失其名，居於洪州上藍院，精究術數，大為鍾傳所禮。
entries.en: A monk of Shanglan Monastery in Hongzhou, name forgotten, was a master of divination whom Chuan treated with great respect.
entries.literal: The Shanglan monk, his name lost, dwelt at Hongzhou Shanglan monastery, deeply studied numerology, greatly honored by Zhong Chuan.

entries.zh: 一旦疾篤，往省之，且曰：「老夫於和尚可謂無間矣，和尚或不諱，得無一言相付耶！」
entries.en: When the monk fell gravely ill Chuan visited him and said, "I have held nothing back from you—won't you leave me one word before you go?"
entries.literal: One day gravely ill, Chuan went to visit and said: "This old man toward the monk can be said without gap—monk, if you do not mind, can you not leave one word to entrust?"

entries.zh: 上藍強起，索筆作偈以援，其末云：「但看來年二三月，柳條堪作打鍾槌。」
entries.en: The monk roused himself, wrote a verse, and ended it, "Watch the second or third month next year—willow twigs will do for beating the bell."
entries.literal: Shanglan forced himself up, sought brush and wrote a gatha to hand over; its end said: "Only look at the second or third month of the coming year—willow branches can serve as bell-striking mallets."

entries.zh: 偈終而卒。
entries.en: He died as soon as the verse was finished.
entries.literal: When the gatha ended he died.

entries.zh: 傳得之，不能測。
entries.en: Chuan could not make sense of it.
entries.literal: Chuan obtained it and could not fathom it.

entries.zh: 洎明年春，淮帥引兵奄至，洪州陷，江南遂為楊氏有。
entries.en: Next spring the Huainan army swept in, Hongzhou fell, and the lower Yangzi passed to the Yang house.
entries.literal: By the next spring the Huainan commander led troops in sudden arrival; Hongzhou fell; south of the river then belonged to the Yang clan.

entries.zh: 「打鍾」之偈，人始悟焉。）〉
entries.en: Only then did men grasp the "beat the bell" prophecy.)〉
entries.literal: "Bell-striking" gatha—people then understood it.)〉

entries.zh: 趙匡凝，
entries.en: Next was Zhao Kuangning,
entries.literal: Zhao Kuangning,

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：匡凝字光儀。）〉
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 gives his style as Guangyi.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Kuangning's style name was Guangyi.)〉

entries.zh: 蔡州人也。
entries.en: was a native of Cai prefecture.
entries.literal: was a man of Cai prefecture.

entries.zh: 父德諲，初事秦宗權為列校，當宗權強暴時，表為襄州留後。
entries.en: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan as a column commander and was made acting commissioner of Xiang when Zongquan grew violent.
entries.literal: Father Dexin at first served Qin Zongquan as a column commander; when Zongquan was violent and fierce, he memorialized him as Xiangzhou acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 唐光啟四年夏六月，德諲審宗權必敗，乃舉漢南之地以歸唐朝，仍遣使投分於太祖，兼誓戮力，同討宗權。
entries.en: In summer, month 6 of Guangqi 4, Dexin saw Zongquan would fall, surrendered Hannan to Tang, sent envoys to the Founder, and swore to destroy Zongquan together.
entries.literal: Tang Guangqi year 4 summer sixth month, Dexin judged Zongquan would surely be defeated and thereupon raised the Hannan lands to return to Tang, still sending envoys to declare separation to the Founder and jointly swearing united strength to attack Zongquan together.

entries.zh: 時太祖為蔡州四面行營都統使，乃表德諲為副，仍領襄州節度使。
entries.en: The Founder, then overall commander against Cai, made Dexin his deputy and confirmed him as Xiang commissioner.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder was Caizhou four-sides campaign overall commander; he memorialized Dexin as deputy and still had him lead Xiangzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 蔡州平，以功累加官爵，封淮安王。
entries.en: After Cai fell he rose in rank and was enfeoffed Prince of Huai'an.
entries.literal: When Cai prefecture was pacified, by merit offices and titles were repeatedly added; he was enfeoffed Prince of Huai'an.

entries.zh: 匡凝以父功為唐州刺史兼七州馬步軍都校。
entries.en: Kuangning became Tang prefect inspector and overall commander of seven prefectures' horse and foot through his father's merit.
entries.literal: Kuangning by his father's merit was Tang prefecture inspector and concurrent seven-prefecture horse-and-foot army overall commander.

entries.zh: 及德諲卒，匡凝自為襄州留後，朝廷即以旄鉞授之。
entries.en: When Dexin died Kuangning made himself acting commissioner and received the court commission.
entries.literal: When Dexin died, Kuangning made himself Xiangzhou acting commissioner; the court thereupon bestowed the command baton and axe.

entries.zh: 作鎮數年，甚有威惠，累官至檢校太尉、兼中書令。
entries.en: He ruled Xiang for years with authority and kindness and rose to Honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: As commissioner for several years he had great authority and kindness; offices repeatedly reached Honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Central Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 匡凝氣貌甚偉，好自修飾，每整衣冠，必使人持巨鑒前後照之。
entries.en: Tall and vain, he had great mirrors held before and behind him whenever he dressed.
entries.literal: Kuangning's bearing was very grand; he loved self-adornment—each time he arranged cap and robes he must have men hold great mirrors before and behind to shine on him.

entries.zh: 對客之際，烏巾上微覺有塵，即令侍妓持紅拂以去之。
entries.en: If he sensed dust on his black cap before guests, maids brushed it away with red dusters.
entries.literal: When facing guests, on the black cap he slightly sensed dust and at once ordered serving girls to hold red dusters to remove it.

entries.zh: 人有誤犯其家諱者，往往遭其木檟楚，其方嚴也如是。
entries.en: Anyone who breached his name taboo risked a beating with a wooden club.
entries.literal: Those who by mistake violated his family taboo often suffered his wooden cudgel beating—his severity was thus.

entries.zh: 光化初，匡凝以太祖有清口之敗，密附於淮夷，太祖遣氏叔琮率師伐之。
entries.en: Early in Guanghua, after the Founder's defeat at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly sided with the Huai rebels and the Founder sent Shi Shucong against him.
entries.literal: At the start of Guanghua, because the Founder had been defeated at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly attached himself to the Huai forces; the Founder sent Shi Shucong with troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 未幾，其泌州刺史趙璠越墉來降，隨州刺史趙匡璘臨陣就擒。
entries.en: Soon his Bi inspector Zhao Fan climbed the wall to surrender and Suizhou inspector Zhao Kuanglin was taken in battle.
entries.literal: Before long, his Bi prefecture inspector Zhao Fan scaled the wall to come surrender; Suizhou inspector Zhao Kuanglin at the battle line was captured on the spot.

entries.zh: 俄而康懷英攻下鄧州，匡凝懼，遣使乞盟，太祖許之，自是附庸於太祖。
entries.en: Kang Huaiying took Deng; Kuangning sued for peace, the Founder agreed, and he became a vassal.
entries.literal: Soon Kang Huaiying attacked and took Deng prefecture; Kuangning feared and sent envoys to beg alliance—the Founder permitted it; from then he was a vassal of the Founder.

entries.zh: 及成汭敗於鄂州，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。
entries.en: After Cheng Rui fell at Ezhou, Kuangning had his brother Kuangming made acting Jingnan commissioner.
entries.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated at E prefecture, Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as Jingnan acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 是時唐室微弱，諸道常賦多不上供，惟匡凝昆仲雖強據江山，然盡忠帝室，貢賦不絕。
entries.en: While Tang weakened and most circuits withheld tribute, the Zhao brothers still sent loyal levies from their strongholds.
entries.literal: At that time the Tang house was weak; many circuits' regular levies often did not go up in tribute—only Kuangning and his brothers, though strongly holding rivers and mountains, yet were wholly loyal to the imperial house and tribute and levies did not cease.

entries.zh: 田頵，本揚府之大校也。
entries.en: Tian Yun had begun as a senior officer in the Yangzhou garrison.
entries.literal: Tian Yun originally was a Yang prefecture great colonel.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》：頵字德臣，廬州合肥人。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 gives his style Dechen and his home as Hefei in Luzhou.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Yun, style name Dechen, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.)〉

entries.zh: 朱延壽，不知何許人。
entries.en: Zhu Yanshou's origins are unknown.
entries.literal: Zhu Yanzhou, origin unknown.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》：延壽，廬州舒城人。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says Yanshou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Yanzhou was a native of Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉

entries.zh: 唐天祐初，楊行密雄據淮海，時頵為宣州節度使，延壽為壽州刺史。
entries.en: Early in Tianyou, Yang Xingmi dominated the Huai-Hai region; Yun held Xuancheng and Yanshou held Shou prefecture.
entries.literal: Early Tang Tianyou, Yang Xingmi heroically held Huai and Hai; then Yun was Xuancheng military commissioner, Yanzhou was Shou prefect magistrate.

entries.zh: 頵以行密專恣跋扈，嘗移書諷之曰：「侯王守方，以奉天子，古之制也。
entries.en: Finding Yang Xingmi arrogant, Yun wrote to admonish him: "Princes are meant to guard their lands for the Son of Heaven—that is the ancient order.
entries.literal: Yun because Xingmi was willful and overbearing, once sent a letter admonishing him, saying: "Marquises and kings guard their regions to serve the Son of Heaven—this is the ancient system.

entries.zh: 其或逾越者，譬如百川不朝於海，雖狂奔猛注，澶漫遐廣，終為涸土，不若恬然順流，淼茫無窮也。
entries.en: Whoever overreaches is like a stream that never reaches the sea: however fierce the flood, it ends in dust. Better to flow with the tide and never run dry.
entries.literal: Whoever oversteps is like a hundred streams not paying court to the sea—though wildly rushing and pouring, vast and wide, in the end they become dry earth; better to calmly follow the current, boundless and without end.

entries.zh: 況東南之鎮，楊為大，塵賤刀布，阜積金玉，願公上恒賦，頵將悉儲峙，具單車從。」
entries.en: You are greatest in the southeast, piled with gold and goods. Send the regular tribute through me—I will store it and deliver it myself in one cart."
entries.literal: Moreover among southeast commands Yang is greatest; dust and base coin and cloth, heaped gold and jade—may my lord remit the standing tax; Yun will store it all and follow with a single cart."

entries.zh: 行密怒曰：「今財賦之行，必由於汴，適足以資於敵也。」
entries.en: Xingmi snapped, "Revenue now must pass through Bian—that only feeds our enemy."
entries.literal: Xingmi angrily said: "Now the flow of wealth and levies must pass through Bian—just enough to enrich the enemy."

entries.zh: 不從。
entries.en: He refused.
entries.literal: He did not comply.

entries.zh: 時延壽方守壽春，
entries.en: Yanshou was then holding Shouchun,
entries.literal: At that time Yanzhou was just defending Shouchun,

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》：天復初，北司擁駕西幸，昭宗聞延壽有武幹，遣李儼間道齎詔授延壽蔡州節度使。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that early in Tianfu, with the court driven west, Zhaozong heard of Yanshou's ability and sent Li Yan secretly to name him Cai commissioner.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Early Tianfu, the northern offices held the emperor on a western progress; Emperor Zhaozong hearing Yanzhou had martial talent sent Li Yan by hidden route bearing an edict appointing Yanzhou Cai prefecture military commissioner.)〉

entries.zh: 直頵之事，密遣人告於頵曰：「公有所欲為者，願為公執鞭。」
entries.en: With Yun's plot in mind, he secretly sent word: "Whatever you intend, I will serve as your man."
entries.literal: Straight at Yun's affair, secretly sent men to tell Yun: "Whatever my lord wishes to do, I wish to hold the whip for my lord."

entries.zh: 頵聞之，頗會其志，乃召進士杜荀鶴具述其意，復語曰：「昌本朝，奉盟主，在斯一舉矣。」
entries.en: Yun took his meaning, summoned the scholar Du Xunhe, laid out the plan, and said, "To restore the dynasty and serve our ally—everything hangs on this."
entries.literal: Yun on hearing greatly grasped his intent, then summoned presented scholar Du Xunhe to fully relate his intent, again saying: "To prosper the dynasty, serve the alliance lord—it's in this one move."

entries.zh: 即遣荀鶴具述密議，自間道至大梁。
entries.en: He sent Xunhe by secret road to Daliang with the full plot.
entries.literal: At once sent Xunhe to fully relate the secret design, by hidden route to Daliang.

entries.zh: 太祖大悅，遽屯兵於宿州，以會其變。
entries.en: The Founder was delighted and rushed troops to Suzhou to meet the plot.
entries.literal: The Founder greatly rejoiced and swiftly stationed troops at Suzhou to await their mutiny.

entries.zh: 不數月，事微泄，行密乃先以公牒征延壽，
entries.en: Within months the plot leaked; Xingmi summoned Yanshou by official order,
entries.literal: Within not many months the matter slightly leaked; Xingmi then first with an official dispatch summoned Yanshou,

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：行密妻，延壽姊也，遣辯士召延壽。
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Xingmi's wife was Yanshou's sister and sent a persuader to call him.
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Xingmi's wife was Yanshou's elder sister; he sent an eloquent man to summon Yanshou.

entries.zh: 疑不肯赴，姊遣婢報，故延壽疾走揚州。）〉
entries.en: Warned by his sister's maid, Yanshou galloped to Yangzhou.)〉
entries.literal: Suspecting he would not come, the sister sent a maid to report; therefore Yanshou galloped posthaste to Yangzhou.)〉

entries.zh: 次悉兵攻宣城，頵戎力寡薄，棄壁走，不能越境，為行密軍所得。
entries.en: Xingmi then attacked Xuancheng; Yun, outmatched, fled the walls but was caught before he could escape the prefecture.
entries.literal: Next he marshaled all troops to attack Xuancheng; Yun's defending strength was thin and few—he abandoned the walls and fled, could not cross the border, and was taken by Xingmi's army.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》：行密別遣台濛、王茂章率步騎以往，頵委舟師於汪建、王壇，自出廣德迎戰，大為濛所敗，遂率殘眾遁保宛陵。
entries.en: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Xingmi sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang by land; Yun entrusted the fleet to Wang Jian and Wang Tan, then fought at Guangde, was routed, and fled to Wanyang with survivors.
entries.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》: Xingmi separately sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang leading foot and horse to go; Yun entrusted the fleet to Wang Jian and Wang Tan, himself going out from Guangde to meet battle, and was greatly defeated by Meng; he then led remnant masses to flee and hold Wanyang.

entries.zh: 壇、建聞其敗，因盡以舟師歸款於行密。
entries.en: Wang Tan and Wang Jian heard of the defeat and surrendered the whole fleet to Xingmi.
entries.literal: Tan and Jian heard of his defeat and therefore entirely with the fleet submitted to Xingmi.

entries.zh: 十二月，頵出外州柵疾戰，橋陷馬墜，為外軍所殺。）〉
entries.en: In the twelfth month Yun fought at the outer stockade; the bridge gave way, his horse fell, and the besiegers killed him.)〉
entries.literal: Twelfth month, Yun went out of Wai prefecture stockade to fight fiercely; the bridge collapsed and his horse fell—he was killed by the outer army.)〉

entries.zh: 延壽飛騎赴命，邇揚州一舍，行密使人殺之。
entries.en: Yanshou galloped toward Yangzhou; a stage short of the city, Xingmi's men killed him.
entries.literal: Yanshou with flying horse rushed to answer the summons; nearing Yangzhou by one stage, Xingmi sent men to kill him.

entries.zh: 太祖將期受禪，以匡凝兄弟並據藩鎮，乃遣使先諭旨焉。
entries.en: As the Founder prepared to take the throne, he sent envoys ahead to the Zhao brothers holding the frontier commands.
entries.literal: The Founder was about to fix the date to receive the abdication mandate; because Kuangning and his brothers both held frontier commissions, he sent envoys first to announce the intent.

entries.zh: 匡凝對使者流涕，答以受國恩深，豈敢隨時妄有他誌。
entries.en: Kuangning wept before the envoy and said the state's grace was too deep for him to change sides with the times.
entries.literal: Kuangning to the envoy wept and replied that the state's grace was deep—how dare he follow the times and rashly have another intent.

entries.zh: 使者復命，太祖大怒。
entries.en: The envoy returned; the Founder flew into a rage.
entries.literal: The envoy returned to report; the Founder was greatly enraged.

entries.zh: 天祐二年秋七月，遣楊師厚率師討之。
entries.en: In autumn, month 7 of Tianyou 2, he sent Yang Shihou to attack him.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn seventh month, he sent Yang Shihou to lead troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 八月，太祖親領大軍南征，仍請削匡凝在身官爵。
entries.en: Month 8 the Founder marched south in person and had Kuangning stripped of rank.
entries.literal: Eighth month, the Founder personally led a great army south on campaign and still requested stripping Kuangning of his personal offices and titles.

entries.zh: 及師厚濟江，匡凝以兵數萬逆戰，大為師厚所敗，匡凝乃燔其舟，單舸急棹，沿漢而遁於金陵。
entries.en: Shihou crossed the river; Kuangning met him with tens of thousands, was routed, burned his fleet, and fled alone up the Han to Jinling.
entries.literal: When Shihou crossed the river, Kuangning with tens of thousands of troops met him in battle and was greatly defeated by Shihou; Kuangning then burned his boats, in a single skiff urgently rowed, and along the Han fled to Jinling.

entries.zh: 後卒於淮南。
entries.en: He later died in Huainan.
entries.literal: Later he died in Huainan.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：師厚由陰穀伐木為梁，匡凝以兵二萬瀕江戰，大敗，乃燔州，單舸夜奔揚州。
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou bridged Yin Valley, Kuangning lost twenty thousand along the river, burned the prefecture, and fled by night to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou by Yin Valley felled timber for beams; Kuangning with twenty thousand troops fought along the river, was greatly defeated, then burned the prefecture and in a single skiff fled by night to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 行密見之，曰：「君在鎮，輕車重馬輸於賊，今敗，乃歸我邪！」
entries.en: Xingmi greeted him: "You fed the enemy from your post—now you come to me defeated?"
entries.literal: Xingmi saw him and said: "Lord, in your commission you sent light carts and heavy horses as tribute to the enemy—now defeated, you return to me!

entries.zh: 匡明亦謀奔淮南，子承規諫曰：「昔諸葛兄弟分仕二國，若適揚州，是自取疑也。」
entries.en: Kuangming meant to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui warned, "Like the Zhuge brothers serving rival states, going to Yangzhou would invite suspicion."
entries.literal: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui remonstrated: "In old times the Zhuge brothers each served a different state—if you go to Yangzhou, it is yourself inviting suspicion."

entries.zh: 匡明謂然，乃趨成都。
entries.en: Kuangming agreed and fled to Chengdu instead.
entries.literal: Kuangming thought it so and thereupon hastened to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》云：行密厚遇匡凝，其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。
entries.en: Ouyang's 《History》 says Xingmi treated Kuangning well, but after Xingmi's death Yang Wo grew rude to him.
entries.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》 says: Xingmi treated Kuangning generously; afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo gradually was without courtesy to him.

entries.zh: 渥方宴食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。」
entries.en: At a feast Wo ate green plums; Kuangning warned, "Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children."
entries.literal: Wo was just feasting and eating green plums; Kuangning looked at Wo and said: "Do not eat much—it brings children's fever."

entries.zh: 諸將以為慢，渥遣匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。）〉
entries.en: Officers took it as insult; Wo exiled him to Hailing, where Xu Wen later killed him.)〉
entries.literal: The generals thought it disrespect; Wo sent Kuangning to Hailing and later Xu Wen killed him.)〉

entries.zh: 初，匡凝好聚書，及敗，楊師厚獲數千卷於第，悉以來獻。
entries.en: Kuangning had loved books; after his defeat Shihou seized thousands of scrolls from his house and presented them to the Founder.
entries.literal: At first Kuangning loved gathering books; when defeated, Yang Shihou obtained several thousand scrolls at his residence and entirely brought them as tribute.

entries.zh: 匡凝弟匡明，字讚堯，幼以父貴，一子出身，為江陵府文學。
entries.en: His brother Kuangming, styled Zanyao, entered office young as a literary officer at Jiangling through their father's rank.
entries.literal: Kuangning's younger brother Kuangming, style name Zanyao, in youth by his father's eminence entered office as a single son—he was Jiangling prefecture literary officer.

entries.zh: 及壯，以軍功曆繡、峽二州刺史。
entries.en: Grown, he won military merit as inspector of Xiuxi and Xia.
entries.literal: When grown, by military merit he passed through Xiuxi and Xia prefecture inspector posts.

entries.zh: 成汭之敗，其兄匡凝表為荊南留後。
entries.en: After Cheng Rui's defeat his brother made him acting Jingnan commissioner.
entries.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated, his elder brother Kuangning memorialized him as Jingnan acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 未至鎮，而朗、陵之兵先據其城矣。
entries.en: Before he took office, Lang and Ling forces had already seized the city.
entries.literal: Before he reached the commission, Lang and Ling troops had already seized the city.

entries.zh: 匡明領兵逐之，遂鎮於渚宮。
entries.en: Kuangming drove them off and held court at Zhugong.
entries.literal: Kuangming led troops to drive them off and then held commission at Zhugong.

entries.zh: 天祐二年秋，太祖既平襄州，遣楊師厚乘勝以趨荊門。
entries.en: Autumn, Tianyou 2, after Xiang fell the Founder sent Shihou on toward Jingmen.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn, the Founder having pacified Xiangzhou sent Yang Shihou to ride the victory toward Jingmen.

entries.zh: 匡明懼，乃舉族上峽奔蜀，王建待以賓禮。
entries.en: Kuangming fled upriver to Shu with his clan; Wang Jian received him as an honored guest.
entries.literal: Kuangming feared and thereupon led his clan up the gorge to flee to Shu; Wang Jian received him with guest ceremony.

entries.zh: 及建稱帝，用為大理卿、工部尚書。
entries.en: When Wang Jian became emperor he made him Grand Court director and Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Jian declared himself emperor, he used him as Grand Court of Review director and Works Ministry minister.

entries.zh: 久之，卒於蜀。
entries.en: He died in Shu many years later.
entries.literal: After long time he died in Shu.

entries.zh: 及死，子彥恭繼之。
entries.en: At his death his son Yiangong took over.
entries.literal: When he died, his son Yiangong succeeded him.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：滿以天復元年卒，子彥威自立，弟彥恭結忠義節度使趙匡凝以逐彥威。）〉
entries.en: (The New Tang History says: Man died in Tianfu 1; his son Yanwei established himself; Yanwei's younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man died in Tianfu year 1; son Yanwei established himself; younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)〉

entries.zh: 蠻蜒狡獪，深有父風，燼墟落，榜舟楫，上下於南郡、武昌之間，殆無人矣。
entries.en: Savage and sly like his father, he burned villages and raided by boat between Nanjun and Wuchang until hardly anyone remained.
entries.literal: A crafty southern barbarian, deeply having his father's manner: burning ruins and villages, plying boats and oars, up and down between Nanjun and Wuchang—nearly no people remained.

entries.zh: 又與淮、蜀結連，阻絕王命。
entries.en: He allied with Huai and Shu and blocked the court's orders.
entries.literal: Again he linked with Huai and Shu, obstructing and cutting off the royal commands.

entries.zh: 太祖詔湖南節度使馬殷、荊南節度使高季昌練精兵五千，遣將倪可福統之，下澧州，與潭兵合。
entries.en: The Founder ordered Ma Yin and Gao Jichang to send five thousand elite troops under Ni Kefu to take Li and join the Tan army.
entries.literal: The Founder issued an edict ordering Hunan military commissioner Ma Yin and Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jichang to drill five thousand elite troops, send general Ni Kefu to command them, descend on Li prefecture, and unite with the Tan troops.

entries.zh: 先是，滿塹沅江，以周其壘，門臨長橋，勢不可入。
entries.en: Man had moated the Yuan around his walls; the gate on the long bridge was impregnable.
entries.literal: Earlier Man had moated the Yuan River to surround his ramparts; the gate faced a long bridge—momentum could not enter.

entries.zh: 殷極其兵力，攻圍周歲，彥恭食盡兵敗，間使求救於淮夷。
entries.en: Yin besieged a full year; starving and beaten, Yiangong sent to the Huai for aid.
entries.literal: Yin exhausted his military strength; attack and siege a full year; Yiangong food exhausted, troops defeated, through envoys begged rescue from the Huai barbarians.

entries.zh: 及淮軍來援，高季昌逆戰於治津馬頭岸，大破之，俄而攻陷朗州，彥恭單棹遁去。
entries.en: When Huai reinforcements came, Gao Jichang routed them at Matou Bank, then took Langzhou as Yiangong fled alone in a skiff.
entries.literal: When Huai troops came to rescue, Gao Jichang met them in battle at Zhijin Matou Bank and greatly defeated them; soon he attacked and took Lang prefecture; Yiangong in a single punt fled away.

entries.zh: 馬殷擒其弟彥雄及逆黨七人，械送至闕，皆斬於汴橋下，時開平二年十一月也。
entries.en: Ma Yin seized Yanxiong and seven rebels, sent them to Bian—all were executed at Bian Bridge in Kaiping 2, month 11.
entries.literal: Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yanxiong and seven rebel partisans, sent them in shackles to the capital—all were beheaded below Bian Bridge; it was Kaiping year 2, eleventh month.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：成汭、鍾、杜、田、朱之流，皆因否運，雄據大藩，雖無濟代之勞，且有勤王之節，功雖不就，誌亦可嘉，若較其誠明，則田頵、延壽斯為優矣。
entries.en: The historian writes: Cheng Rui, Zhong, Du, Tian, Zhu and the like seized great domains in dark times; they lacked power to save the realm yet showed loyalty to the throne; merit failed but intent deserves praise—of them Tian Yun and Yanshou showed the truest hearts.
entries.literal: The historian says: Cheng Rui, Zhong, Du, Tian, Zhu, and their kind all because of adverse fortune boldly held great circuits; although they had no merit of saving the age, yet they had the integrity of assisting the king; achievement although not accomplished, intention also may be praised—if comparing their sincerity and clarity, then Tian Yun and Yanshou are superior.

entries.zh: 匡凝一門昆仲，千里江山，失守藩垣，不克負荷，斯乃劉景升之子之徒歟！
entries.en: The Kuangning brothers held a thousand li yet lost their domain and could not sustain it—were they not Liu Biao's sons reborn?
entries.literal: Kuangning one family's brothers, a thousand li of rivers and mountains, lost guard of the frontier walls, could not bear the burden—is this not the sort of Liu Jingsheng's sons!

entries.zh: 張佶有讓帥之賢，雷滿辱俾侯之寄，優劣可知矣。
entries.en: Zhang Ji showed the grace to yield command; Lei Man shamed the trust of a commissioner—the contrast tells all.
entries.literal: Zhang Ji had the virtue of yielding command; Lei Man disgraced the entrustment of vice-lord—superior and inferior can be known.

entries.zh: 成汭，淮西人。
entries.en: Cheng Rui came from west of the Huai.
entries.literal: Cheng Rui was a native of Huai West.

entries.zh: 少年任俠，乘醉殺人，為仇家所捕，因落發為僧，冒姓郭氏。
entries.en: As a young man he killed someone in a drunken brawl, was hunted by the victim's kin, shaved his head as a monk, and took the surname Guo.
entries.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold, killed a man while drunk, was seized by the enemy family, and therefore shaved his head to become a monk and usurped the surname Guo.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：入蔡賊中，為賊帥假子，更姓名為郭禹。）〉
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says he joined the Cai rebels as an adopted son and renamed himself Guo Yu.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: entering Cai rebel bands, he became a rebel chief's adoptive son and changed his name to Guo Yu.)〉

entries.zh: 亡匿久之，及貴，方復本姓。
entries.en: He lived in hiding for years and only restored his true name once he had risen.
entries.literal: He hid in flight a long time; when he reached eminence he then restored his original surname.

entries.zh: 唐僖宗朝，為蔡州軍校，領本郡兵戍荊南，帥以其凶暴，欲害之，遂棄本軍奔於秭歸。
entries.en: Under Xizong he was a Caizhou officer garrisoning Jingnan until his commander, fearing his violence, tried to kill him; he fled to Zigui with his troops.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xizong's Tang he was a Cai prefecture army officer, led the prefecture's troops to garrison Jingnan; the commander because of his ferocity wished to harm him, so he abandoned his army and fled to Zigui.

entries.zh: 一夕，巨蛇繞其身，幾至於殞，乃祝曰：「苟有所負，死生惟命。」
entries.en: One night a giant snake coiled around him until he nearly died; he prayed, "If I am guilty, let fate decide."
entries.literal: One night a huge serpent coiled around his body, almost to his death; he then prayed, saying: "If I bear some guilt, life and death are fate's alone."

entries.zh: 逡巡，蛇亦解去。
entries.en: In time the snake loosened and slid away.
entries.literal: After a moment the serpent too unwound and left.

entries.zh: 後據歸州，招集流亡，練士伍，得兵千餘人，沿流以襲荊南，遂據其地。
entries.en: He took Guizhou, rallied refugees into a thousand-man force, sailed downriver against Jingnan, and seized it.
entries.literal: Later he seized Guizhou, gathered fugitives, drilled soldiers, obtained more than a thousand troops, along the river struck Jingnan, and thus held that territory.

entries.zh: 朝廷即以旄鉞授之。
entries.en: The court soon invested him with full military command.
entries.literal: The court at once granted him command pennant and axe.

entries.zh: 是時荊州經巨盜之後，居民才一十七家，汭撫輯凋殘，勵精為理，通商訓農，勤於惠養，比及末年，僅及萬戶。
entries.en: Jingzhou after the great devastations held only seventeen households; Rui rebuilt trade and agriculture until, by his last years, the city neared ten thousand families.
entries.literal: At that time Jingzhou after great bandits had only seventeen resident households; Rui pacified the devastated ruin, strove in governance, opened commerce and trained farming, diligently in nurturing kindness—by his last years barely reaching ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 汭性豪暴，事皆意斷，又好自矜伐，騁辯淩人，深為識者所鄙。
entries.en: Rui was domineering, arrogant in debate, and widely scorned by men of judgment.
entries.literal: Rui's nature was arrogant and violent; affairs were all decided by his own intent; he also loved self-praise, vaunted eloquence to overbear others, and was deeply despised by the knowing.

entries.zh: 張策，字少逸，敦煌人。
entries.en: Zhang Ce, styled Shaoyi, came from Dunhuang.
entries.literal: Zhang Ce, style Shaoyi, was a native of Dunhuang.

entries.zh: 父同，仕唐，官至容管經略使。
entries.en: His father Tong served Tang and rose to Military Commissioner of Rongguan.
entries.literal: His father Tong served Tang and reached Military Commissioner of Rongguan.

entries.zh: 策少聰警好學，尤樂章句。
entries.en: As a boy Ce was quick-witted and studious, with a special love of chapter-and-verse learning.
entries.literal: Ce in youth was clever and fond of learning, especially delighting in chapter-and-phrase study.

entries.zh: 居洛陽敦化裏，嘗浚甘泉井，得古鼎，耳有篆字曰：「魏黃初元年春二月，匠吉千」，且又製作奇巧，同甚寶之。
entries.en: In Dunhua Lane, Luoyang, he dredged the Sweet Spring well and found an ancient tripod inscribed in seal script: "Huangchu year 1, spring, second month, artisan Ji Qian." The work was exquisitely wrought, and Tong prized it.
entries.literal: Living in Dunhua Lane in Luoyang, he once dredged the Sweet Spring well and obtained an ancient tripod whose ears bore seal script: "First year of Huangchu, spring, second month, craftsman Ji Qian"—and its workmanship was marvelously ingenious; Tong treasured it greatly.

entries.zh: 策時在父旁，徐言曰：「建安二十五年，曹公薨，改年為延康，其年十月，文帝受漢禪，始號黃初，則是黃初元年無二月明矣。
entries.en: Standing beside his father, Ce said quietly, "In Jian'an 25 Cao Cao died and the era became Yan'kang; in the tenth month of that year Emperor Wen accepted Han's abdication and first used Huangchu—so Huangchu year 1 plainly had no second month.
entries.literal: Ce was then at his father's side and said slowly: "In the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an Cao Gong died and the era was changed to Yan'kang; in the tenth month of that year Emperor Wen received Han's abdication and first took the name Huangchu—so clearly Huangchu year 1 had no second month.

entries.zh: 鼎文何謬歟！」
entries.en: The inscription on this vessel is wrong!"
entries.literal: How erroneous is the tripod's inscription!"

entries.zh: 同大驚，亟遣啟書室，取《魏志》展讀，一不失所啟，宗族奇之，時年十三。
entries.en: Tong was astonished, had the study opened, and sent for the 《Records of Wei》—every detail matched. The clan was amazed; Ce was thirteen.
entries.literal: Tong was greatly startled, hurriedly sent someone to open the study, fetch the 《Records of Wei》, and read—nothing missed from what Ce had said; the clan marveled at him; he was then thirteen.

entries.zh: 然而妙通因果，酷奉空教，未弱冠，落發為僧，居雍之慈恩精廬，頗有高致。
entries.en: Yet he was drawn to karma and devoted to Buddhism; before coming of age he tonsured and lived at Cien Monastery in Yong, cultivating a refined detachment.
entries.literal: Yet he was finely versed in cause and effect and ardently followed the Empty Teaching; before his weak cap he shaved his head as a monk and lived at Cien Monastery in Yong, with quite a lofty air.

entries.zh: 唐廣明末，大盜犯闕，策遂返初服，奉父母逃難，君子多之。
entries.en: When bandits took the capital at the end of Guangming, he put off his robes, fled with his parents, and won praise from men of principle.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang Guangming great bandits breached the capital; Ce then returned to lay dress, escorted his parents in flight, and gentlemen praised him.

entries.zh: 及丁家艱，以孝聞。
entries.en: When his father died, his mourning was widely praised.
entries.literal: Upon his father's death he was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 服滿，自屏郊藪，一無幹進意，若是者十餘載，方出為廣文博士，改秘書郎。
entries.en: After mourning he hid in the countryside without seeking office for more than ten years, then took up posts as National University erudite and Secretary.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he secluded himself in the wilds with no thought of advancement for more than ten years, then emerged as Erudite of the National University and was changed to Secretary.

entries.zh: 王行瑜帥邠州，辟為觀察支使，帶水曹員外郎，賜緋。
entries.en: Wang Xingyu of Binzhou made him observation aide and Water Bureau Registrar and gave him crimson robes.
entries.literal: Wang Xingyu commanded Bin prefecture and recruited him as observation aide, with concurrent Water Bureau Registrar, and granted crimson.

entries.zh: 及行瑜反，太原節度使李克用奉詔討伐，行瑜敗死，邠州平。
entries.en: When Xingyu rebelled, Li Keyong of Taiyuan marched under imperial orders; Xingyu was defeated and killed, and Binzhou was pacified.
entries.literal: When Xingyu rebelled, Taiyuan Military Commissioner Li Keyong received the edict to campaign; Xingyu was defeated and died, and Binzhou was pacified.

entries.zh: 策與婢肩輿其親，南出邠境，屬邊寨積雪，為行者所哀。
entries.en: Ce bore his family south from Bin in a litter borne with a servant girl; snow blocked the frontier posts, and passersby wept for them.
entries.literal: Ce carried his kin in a shoulder litter with a maid south of Bin, and because border forts were deep in snow travelers pitied them.

entries.zh: 太祖聞而嘉之，奏為鄭滑支使，尋以內憂去職。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor heard and praised him, had him named aide to Zheng-Hua, and soon he left for mourning at home.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor heard and commended this, memorialized him as Zheng-Hua aide, and soon he left office for domestic mourning.

entries.zh: 製闋，除國子博士，遷膳部員外郎。
entries.en: After mourning he became National University erudite, then Registrar of the Provisions Bureau.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made National University erudite and promoted to Bureau Registrar of Provisions.

entries.zh: 不一歲，華帥韓建辟為判官，及建領許州，又為掌記。
entries.en: Within a year Han Jian of Hua recruited him as judge; when Jian took Xuzhou, Ce became his recorder.
entries.literal: Within a year Hua Military Commissioner Han Jian recruited him as judge; when Jian took Xuzhou, Ce again served as recorder.

entries.zh: 天復中，策奉其主書幣來聘，太祖見而喜曰：「張夫子且至矣。」
entries.en: In Tianfu, Ce came on embassy with his lord's letter and gifts; the Founding Emperor rejoiced and said, "Master Zhang is on his way."
entries.literal: In Tianfu, Ce brought his lord's letter and gifts on a mission; the Founding Emperor on seeing him rejoiced and said: "Master Zhang is coming."

entries.zh: 即奏為掌記，兼賜金紫。
entries.en: He was at once named recorder and given gold and purple insignia.
entries.literal: At once he was memorialized as recorder and also granted gold and purple.

entries.zh: 天祐初，表其才，拜職方郎中，兼史館修撰，俄召入為翰林學士，轉兵部郎中，知制誥，依前修史。
entries.en: Early in Tianyou his talent was recommended; he became Appointments Director and Historiographer, entered the Hanlin, became War Director and edict drafter, and kept compiling history.
entries.literal: Early in Tianyou he was recommended for talent, made Bureau Director of Appointments and concurrent Historiographer, soon summoned to the Hanlin, transferred to Bureau Director of War and edict drafter, still compiling history.

entries.zh: 未幾，遷中書舍人，職如故。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter with the same duties.
entries.literal: Before long he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, duties unchanged.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，改工部侍郎，加承旨。
entries.en: At the founding Ce became Vice Minister of Works and Hanlin Expositor.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Ce was made Vice Minister of Works and Expositor.

entries.zh: 其年冬，轉禮部侍郎。
entries.en: That winter he moved to Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: That winter he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 明年，從征至澤州，拜刑部侍郎、平章事，仍判戶部，尋遷中書侍郎。
entries.en: The next year, on campaign at Zezhou, he became Punishments Vice Minister and Chief Councillor, still overseeing Revenue, then Secretariat Vice Minister.
entries.literal: The next year, on campaign to Ze prefecture, he was made Vice Minister of Punishments, Chief Councillor, still administering Revenue, and soon promoted to Secretariat Vice Minister.

entries.zh: 以風恙拜章乞骸，改刑部尚書致仕。
entries.en: Ill with wind disorder, he asked to retire and was made Minister of Punishments in retirement.
entries.literal: Because of wind ailment he memorialized begging to retire bones and was changed to Minister of Punishments, retired.

entries.zh: 即日肩輿歸洛，居於福善裏，修篁嘉木，圖書琴酒，以自適焉。
entries.en: The same day he went home to Luoyang in a litter, settling in Fushan Lane among bamboo, fine trees, books, wine, and zither.
entries.literal: That same day he returned to Luoyang in a shoulder litter, living in Fushan Lane amid fine bamboo, good trees, books, zither, and wine, to suit himself.

entries.zh: 乾化二年秋，卒。
entries.en: He died in autumn of Qianhua 2.
entries.literal: In autumn of the second year of Qianhua he died.

entries.zh: 所著《典議》三卷、詞製歌詩二十卷、箋表三十卷，存於其家。
entries.en: His writings—three fascicles of 《Canonical Discussions》, twenty of verse and songs, thirty of memorials—remain with his family.
entries.literal: His works—the three fascicles of 《Canonical Discussions》, twenty fascicles of regulated compositions, songs, and poems, and thirty fascicles of memorials and reports—remain in his household.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，趙、張之族皆處權要，翔愈不得志。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor the Zhao and Zhang families held power, and Xiang grew still more frustrated.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, the Zhao and Zhang clans all held crucial power; Xiang grew still more without satisfaction.

entries.zh: 及劉鄩失河朔，安彥之喪楊劉，翔奏曰：「國家連年遣將出征，封疆日削，不獨兵驕將怯，亦製置未得其術。
entries.en: After Liu Xun lost Hebei and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized: "Year after year we send armies abroad while our borders shrink—not only are the troops arrogant and the generals timid; our strategy is wrong as well.
entries.literal: When Liu Xun lost Hebei, and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized saying: "The state year after year sends generals on campaign; the borders daily shrink—not only are troops arrogant and generals timid; disposition too has not obtained its method.

entries.zh: 陛下處深宮之中，與之計事者皆左右近習，豈能量敵之勝負哉！
entries.en: Your Majesty sits deep in the palace while only favorites advise you—how can you judge the enemy's strength?
entries.literal: Your Majesty dwells deep in the palace; those who plan affairs with you are all close attendants on left and right—how can one measure the enemy's victory or defeat!

entries.zh: 先皇時，河朔半在，親禦虎臣驍將，猶不得志於敵人。
entries.en: Under the late emperor half of Hebei was still ours; he led his best commanders in person and still could not beat the foe.
entries.literal: In the late emperor's time, half of Hebei remained; he personally led tiger ministers and fierce generals—yet still could not satisfy his will upon the enemy.

entries.zh: 今寇馬已至鄆州，陛下不留聖念，臣所未喻一也。
entries.en: Now the enemy has reached Yunzhou while Your Majesty shows no alarm—that is what I cannot understand first.
entries.literal: Now the enemy's horses have already reached Yun prefecture; Your Majesty does not keep sage concern—what I cannot understand is the first point.

entries.zh: 臣聞李亞子自墨縗統眾，於今十年，每攻城臨陣，無不親當矢石，昨聞攻楊劉，率先負薪渡水，一鼓登城。
entries.en: Li Yazi has led his men in mourning garb for ten years; in every siege he faces arrows and stones himself; at Yangliu he carried fuel to ford the river and took the city at the first drum.
entries.literal: I hear Li Yazi from hemp mourning has commanded the masses—already ten years now; whenever he attacks cities and faces battle lines, there is none at which he does not personally meet arrows and stones; yesterday I heard attacking Yangliu, he first shouldered fuel to cross the water, and at one drum took the walls.

entries.zh: 陛下儒雅守文，未嘗如此，俾賀瑰輩與之較力，而望攘逐寇戎，臣所未喻二也。
entries.en: Your Majesty is a scholar-king who has never done such things, yet you send He Gui and others to match him and still hope to drive the invaders away—that is what I cannot understand second.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is refined and cultured, guarding the written law, and has never been thus; you make He Gui and his ilk compare strength with him, yet hope to drive away and expel the enemy raiders—what I cannot understand is the second point.

entries.zh: 陛下所宜詢於黎老，別運沉謀，不然，則憂未艾也。
entries.en: You should consult seasoned elders and lay deeper plans—or our troubles will not end.
entries.literal: What Your Majesty ought to do is consult the grey-haired elders and separately deploy deep strategy—otherwise worry will not end.

entries.zh: 臣雖駑怯，受國恩深，陛下必若乏材，乞於邊陲效試。」
entries.en: I am untalented but deeply in your debt; if you lack men, let me prove myself on the frontier."
entries.literal: Though I am dull and timid, I have received the state's grace deeply; if Your Majesty must lack talent, I beg to be tried in effect at the frontier."

entries.zh: 末帝雖知其懇惻，竟以趙、張輩言翔怨望，不之聽。
entries.en: The Last Emperor knew he spoke sincerely, but Zhao and Zhang called it resentment, and he would not listen.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor though he knew his earnest sincerity, in the end because the Zhao and Zhang crowd said Xiang harbored resentment, did not heed him.

entries.zh: 及王彥章敗於中都，晉人長驅而南，末帝急召翔，謂之曰：「朕居常忽卿所奏，果至今日。
entries.en: When Wang Yanzhang fell at Zhongdu and the Jin army swept south, the Last Emperor summoned Xiang in haste and said: "I ignored your warnings, and it has come to this.
entries.literal: When Wang Yanzhang was defeated at Zhongdu, Jin men drove at length south; the Last Emperor urgently summoned Xiang and said to him: "I in ordinary times neglected what you memorialized—it has indeed come to this day.

entries.zh: 事急矣，勿以為懟，且使朕安歸？」
entries.en: Matters are desperate; do not be angry—where can I go in safety?"
entries.literal: Matters are urgent; do not take it as offense—and where shall I return in peace?"

entries.zh: 翔泣奏曰：「臣受國恩，僅將三紀，從微至著，皆先朝所遇，雖名宰相，實朱氏老奴耳。
entries.en: Xiang wept and replied: "I have served nearly thirty years, raised from nothing by the former court; though called chancellor, I am only an old retainer of the Zhu house.
entries.literal: Xiang wept and memorialized saying: "Your servant has received the state's grace for nearly three decades; from slight to manifest—all from the former court's encounter; though named chancellor, in truth I am the Zhu clan's old bondservant.

entries.zh: 事陛下如郎君，以臣愚誠，敢有所隱！
entries.en: I serve you as a young master would be served—with my poor loyalty I dare hide nothing!
entries.literal: Serving Your Majesty like a young master—for your servant's dull sincerity, how dare I hide anything!

entries.zh: 陛下初任段凝為將，臣已極言，小人朋附，致有今日。
entries.en: When you first made Duan Ning commander I warned you to the utmost; petty factions brought us to this day.
entries.literal: Your Majesty at first appointed Duan Ning as general—I already spoke to the limit; petty men banded together and brought about this day.

entries.zh: 晉軍即至，段凝限水。
entries.en: The Jin army is upon us, and Duan Ning is blocked by the river.
entries.literal: The Jin army will soon arrive; Duan Ning is cut off by water.

entries.zh: 欲請陛下出居避敵，陛下必不聽從；
entries.en: If I urge you to leave the capital to escape the enemy, you will not listen;
entries.literal: I wish to ask Your Majesty to go out and dwell to avoid the enemy—Your Majesty certainly will not obey;

entries.zh: 欲請陛下出奇應敵，陛下必不果決。
entries.en: if I urge a bold stroke against the enemy, you will not decide.
entries.literal: I wish to ask Your Majesty to deploy surprise to answer the enemy—Your Majesty certainly will not in the end decide.

entries.zh: 縱良、平復生，難以轉禍為福，請先死，不忍見宗廟隕墜。」
entries.en: Even Zhang Liang and Chen Ping reborn could not turn this ruin to blessing; let me die first—I cannot watch the ancestral temples fall."
entries.literal: Even if Liang and Ping were reborn, it would be hard to turn disaster into fortune; I beg to die first—I cannot bear to see the ancestral temples fall."

entries.zh: 言訖，君臣相向慟哭。
entries.en: They ended in tears together.
entries.literal: When words ended, ruler and minister faced each other and wailed.

entries.zh: 初，貞明中，史臣李琪、張袞、郤殷象、馮錫嘉奉詔修撰《太祖實錄》三十卷，敘述非工，事多漏略。
entries.en: Early in Zhenming, Li Qi, Zhang Gun, Xi Yinxiang, and Feng Xijia were ordered to compile thirty scrolls of the 《Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor》; the narrative was poor and much was left out.
entries.literal: At the start, in Zhenming, historians Li Qi, Zhang Gun, Xi Yinxiang, and Feng Xijia received edict to compile the 《Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor》 thirty scrolls; the narration was unskilled and affairs were much omitted.

entries.zh: 復詔翔補緝其闕，翔乃別纂成三十卷，目之曰《大梁編遺錄》，與《實錄》偕行。
entries.en: Xiang was then ordered to fill the gaps; he compiled another thirty scrolls titled 《Compiled Remnant Records of Great Liang》, issued together with the 《Veritable Records》.
entries.literal: Again an edict ordered Xiang to supplement and edit its gaps; Xiang then separately compiled into completion thirty scrolls, titled them 《Compiled Remnant Records of Great Liang》, and they circulated together with the 《Veritable Records》.

entries.zh: 翔妻劉氏，父為藍田令。
entries.en: Xiang's wife, Lady Liu, was daughter of the magistrate of Lantian.
entries.literal: Xiang's wife, the Liu clan—her father was magistrate of Lantian.

entries.zh: 廣明之亂，劉為巢將尚讓所得，巢敗，讓攜劉降於時溥，及讓誅，時溥納劉於妓室。
entries.en: In the Guangming disorders she was seized by Huang Chao's general Shang Rang; after Chao's fall Rang surrendered her to Shi Pu, and when Rang was killed Pu kept her among his entertainers.
entries.literal: In the Guangming turmoil Liu was taken by Huang Chao's general Shang Rang; when Chao was defeated, Rang brought Liu and surrendered to Shi Pu; when Rang was executed, Shi Pu took Liu into his courtesans' quarters.

entries.zh: 太祖平徐，得劉氏嬖之，屬翔喪妻，因以劉氏賜之。
entries.en: When the Founder took Xuzhou he favored Lady Liu; Xiang was widowed, and the Founder gave her to him.
entries.literal: When the Founder pacified Xu, he obtained Lady Liu and favored her; as Xiang had lost his wife, he therefore gave Lady Liu to him.

entries.zh: 及翔漸貴，劉猶出入太祖臥內，翔情禮稍薄，劉於曲室讓翔曰：「卿鄙餘曾失身於賊耶，以成敗言之，尚讓巢之宰輔，時溥國之忠臣，論卿門第，辱我何甚，請從此辭！」
entries.en: As Xiang rose, Liu still visited the Founder's bedchamber; Xiang's affection cooled. In private she reproached him: "Do you scorn me for having served rebels? Shang Rang was Huang Chao's chancellor and Shi Pu a loyal minister of the state—and by your own birth, how deeply you insult me! I will leave you!"
entries.literal: When Xiang gradually grew eminent, Liu still entered and left the Founder's sleeping quarters; Xiang's sentiment and courtesy grew somewhat thin; Liu in a side room reproached Xiang saying: "Sir, do you despise me because I once lost my integrity to bandits? Judging by success and failure—Shang Rang was Chao's chancellor, Shi Pu the state's loyal minister; considering your clan standing—how greatly you insult me! I beg to part from here!"

entries.zh: 翔謝而止之。
entries.en: Xiang apologized and kept her.
entries.literal: Xiang apologized and stopped her.

entries.zh: 劉恃太祖之勢，
entries.en: Lady Liu relied on the Founder's favor,
entries.literal: Liu relied on the Founder's power,

entries.zh: 〈（案：下有缺文。）〉
entries.en: (The text below is lost.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉

entries.zh: 太祖四鎮時，劉已得「國夫人」之號。
entries.en: While the Founder held four commands she already bore the title "State Lady."
entries.literal: When the Founder held four commands, Liu already had the title "Lady of the State."

entries.zh: 車服驕侈，婢媵皆珥珠翠，其下別置爪牙典謁，書幣聘使，交結藩鎮，近代婦人之盛，無出其右，權貴皆相附麗，寵信言事，不下於翔。
entries.en: Her equipage was lavish, her maids jeweled; she kept her own agents and messengers and cultivated the frontier lords; no woman of the age matched her power; the great all courted her, and her influence rivaled Xiang's.
entries.literal: Carriages and robes were arrogant and extravagant; maids and concubines all wore pearl and kingfisher in their ears; below her she separately set claw-and-tooth managers of audience; letters and gifts and envoys for betrothal—she linked with frontier commands; among women of recent ages none exceeded her on the right; power and nobility all attached to her; favor and trust in speaking affairs were not below Xiang.

entries.zh: 當時貴達之家，從而效之，敗俗之甚也。
entries.en: Great families imitated her—a grave debasement of manners.
entries.literal: At that time eminent and reaching households followed and imitated her—a great corruption of custom.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：敬翔應《三傳》，數舉不第，發憤投太祖，願備行陣。
entries.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says Xiang had studied the Three Commentaries, failed the exams repeatedly, and in anger joined the Founder, asking to serve in the ranks.
entries.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Jing Xiang answered on the Three Commentaries, repeatedly sat for the examination without passing, in angry resolution threw himself on the Founder, willing to serve in the ranks.

entries.zh: 太祖問曰：「足下通《春秋》久矣，今吾主盟，其為戰欲效春秋時可乎？」
entries.en: The Founder asked: "You have long known the 《Spring and Autumn》; I now lead the alliance—should our wars follow the Spring and Autumn model?"
entries.literal: The Founder asked: "You, sir, have long mastered the 《Spring and Autumn》; now I preside over the covenant—do you wish warfare to imitate Spring and Autumn times?"

entries.zh: 翔曰：「不可。
entries.en: Xiang said: "No.
entries.literal: Xiang said: "It cannot be done.

entries.zh: 夫禮樂猶不相沿襲，況兵者詭道，宜其變化無窮。
entries.en: Even rites and music are not copied unchanged—how much more war, the art of deception, which must shift without limit.
entries.literal: Rites and music still do not follow in succession—how much more warfare, the way of deception—fitly it changes without end.

entries.zh: 若復如春秋時，則所謂務虛名而喪其實效，大王之事去矣。」
entries.en: To fight like the Spring and Autumn age would chase empty form and lose real gain—your enterprise would fail."
entries.literal: If again like Spring and Autumn times, then what is called pursuing empty names while losing real effect—my lord's enterprise is gone."

entries.zh: 太祖大悅，以為知兵，遽延之幕府，委以軍事，竟至作相。）〉
entries.en: The Founder was delighted, judged him a strategist, brought him into headquarters, entrusted him with military affairs, and in the end made him chancellor.)〉
entries.literal: The Founder greatly rejoiced, considered him to know warfare, hastily extended him to the headquarters, entrusted him with military affairs, and in the end he reached chancellor.)〉

entries.zh: 李振，字興緒，唐潞州節度使抱真之曾孫也。
entries.en: Li Zhen, styled Xingxu, was great-grandson of Li Baozhen, Tang military commissioner of Lu.
entries.literal: Li Zhen, styled Xingxu, was great-grandson of Tang's Li Baozhen, military commissioner of Lu prefecture.

entries.zh: 祖、父，皆至郡守。
entries.en: His grandfather and father both rose to commandery prefect.
entries.literal: Grandfather and father both reached prefect of a commandery.

entries.zh: 振仕唐，自金吾將軍改台州刺史。
entries.en: He served Tang as a Golden Guard general, then became prefect of Taizhou.
entries.literal: Zhen served Tang; from Golden Guard general he was changed to prefect of Tai prefecture.

entries.zh: 會盜據浙東，不克之任，因西歸過汴，以策略幹太祖，太祖奇之，辟為從事。
entries.en: Rebels held Zhedong and he could not take office; passing Bian on his return west he presented a plan to the Founder, who was impressed and took him on staff.
entries.literal: As bandits held Zhedong, he could not reach his post; he therefore returned west passing Bian, with strategy approached the Founder; the Founder marveled at him and recruited him as staff officer.

entries.zh: 太祖兼領鄆州，署天平軍節度副使。
entries.en: When the Founder also held Yunzhou he made him deputy commissioner of the Tianping army.
entries.literal: When the Founder also held Yun prefecture, he appointed him deputy military commissioner of Tianping army.

entries.zh: 湖南馬殷為朗州雷滿所逼，振奉命馳往和解，殷、滿皆稟命。
entries.en: When Ma Yin of Hunan was harried by Lei Man of Langzhou, Zhen was sent to mediate; both submitted.
entries.literal: Hunan's Ma Yin was pressed by Langzhou's Lei Man; Zhen received command and galloped to mediate; Yin and Man both obeyed orders.

entries.zh: 光啟三年十一月，太祖遣振入奏於長安，舍於州邸，邸吏程岩白振曰：「劉中尉命其侄希貞來計大事，欲上謁，願許之。」
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Guangqi 3 the Founder sent Zhen to report at Chang'an; lodging at the circuit hostel, clerk Cheng Yan said: "Vice Director Liu has sent his nephew Xizhen to discuss a great matter and wishes an audience—will you allow it?"
entries.literal: Guangqi year 3, eleventh month: the Founder sent Zhen to memorialize at Chang'an; he lodged at the prefecture residence; residence clerk Cheng Yan told Zhen: "Vice Director Liu ordered his nephew Xizhen to come to plan the great affair and wishes to pay court audience—may you permit it."

entries.zh: 既至，岩乃先啟曰：「主上嚴急，內官憂恐，左中尉欲行廢黜之事，岩等協力以定中外，敢以事告。」
entries.en: When Xizhen came, Yan announced: "The emperor is harsh; the eunuchs are afraid; the Left Vice Director means to depose him—we have joined forces to settle the realm and report this to you."
entries.literal: When he arrived, Yan then first announced: "The sovereign is severe and urgent; inner officials are anxious and afraid; the Left Vice Director wishes to carry out deposition—Yan and others exert strength together to settle inner and outer; we dare report the affair."

entries.zh: 振顧希貞曰：「百歲奴事三歲主，亂國不義，廢君不祥，非敢聞也。
entries.en: Zhen told Xizhen: "An old servant plotting against a young lord is unrighteous; deposing the ruler is ill-omened—I will not hear of it.
entries.literal: Zhen turned to Xizhen and said: "A hundred-year bondservant serving a three-year master—disordering the state is unrighteous, deposing the ruler is inauspicious; I dare not hear of it.

entries.zh: 況梁王以百萬之師，匡輔天子，禮樂尊戴，猶恐不及，幸熟計之。」
entries.en: The Prince of Liang leads a million men to aid the Son of Heaven in restoring rites and honor—he can scarcely do enough; think carefully."
entries.literal: Moreover the Prince of Liang with a million troops aids and supports the Son of Heaven—rites and music, honored support—he still fears he does not reach it; I hope you will maturely plan."

entries.zh: 希貞大沮而去。
entries.en: Xizhen withdrew in dismay.
entries.literal: Xizhen greatly dejected left.

entries.zh: 及振復命，劉季述等果作亂，程岩率諸道邸吏牽帝下殿，以立幼主，奉昭宗為太上皇。
entries.en: When Zhen returned, Liu Jishu and his party had rebelled; Cheng Yan and the hostel clerks of every circuit dragged the emperor from the hall, enthroned a child, and made Zhaozong Retired Emperor.
entries.literal: When Zhen returned with his reply, Liu Jishu and others indeed made disorder; Cheng Yan led residence clerks of all circuits to drag the emperor down from the hall, set up the young ruler, and made Zhaozong Retired Emperor.

entries.zh: 振至陝，陝已賀矣。
entries.en: When Zhen reached Shaan, Shaan had already offered congratulations.
entries.literal: Zhen reached Shaan; Shaan had already congratulated [the new ruler].

entries.zh: 護軍韓彝範言其事，振曰：「懿皇初升遐，韓中尉殺長立幼，以利其權，遂亂天下，今將軍復欲爾耶！」
entries.en: Protector-general Han Yifan raised the matter; Zhen said: "When Emperor Yizong died, Vice Director Han killed the elder prince and set up the younger for his own power and threw the realm into chaos—do you mean to do the same?"
entries.literal: Protector-general Han Yifan spoke of the affair; Zhen said: "When Emperor Yizong first ascended to the far journey, Vice Director Han killed the elder and set up the young to profit his power—and so disordered all under Heaven; now General, do you again wish to do so!"

entries.zh: 彝範即文約孫也，由是不敢言。
entries.en: Yifan was Wenyao's grandson and dared not speak again.
entries.literal: Yifan was Wenyao's grandson, and therefore dared not speak further.

entries.zh: 振東歸，太祖方在邢、洺，遽還於汴，大計未決，季述遣養子希度以唐之社稷欲輸於太祖，又遣供奉官李奉本、副介支彥勳詐齎上皇誥諭至，皆季述黨也。
entries.en: Zhen returned east while the Founder was at Xing and Ming and hurried back to Bian before policy was fixed; Liu Jishu sent his adopted son Xidu to hand Tang's realm to him, and Palace Attendant Li Fengben and Vice Messenger Zhi Yanxun with forged retired-emperor edicts—all Jishu's men.
entries.literal: Zhen returned east; the Founder was then at Xing and Ming, hurried back to Bian, and the great plan was not yet settled; Jishu sent his adopted son Xidu to offer Tang's altars to the Founder, and also sent Palace Attendant Li Fengben and Vice Messenger Zhi Yanxun falsely bearing the Retired Emperor's edicts—all were Jishu's partisans.

entries.zh: 太祖未及迎命，振又言曰：「夫豎貂、伊戾之亂，所以資霸者之事也。
entries.en: Before the Founder could receive them, Zhen said again: "Rebellions like Shu Diao's and Yi Li's are what make a hegemon's career.
entries.literal: Before the Founder could welcome the envoys, Zhen again said: "The disorders of Shu Diao and Yi Li are what supply a hegemon's affairs.

entries.zh: 今閹豎幽辱天子，王不能討，無以令諸侯。」
entries.en: Eunuchs now hold and humiliate the emperor; if you will not punish them, you cannot command the lords."
entries.literal: Now eunuchs imprison and insult the Son of Heaven; if the King cannot punish them, you cannot command the feudal lords."

entries.zh: 時監軍使劉重楚，季述兄也，舊相張浚，寓於河南緱氏，亦來謂太祖曰：「同中官則事易濟，且得所欲。」
entries.en: Military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chancellor Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan also urged the Founder: "Side with the eunuchs and all goes easily—you get what you want."
entries.literal: At that time military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chief minister Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan, also came to tell the Founder: "Join the inner attendants and affairs go easily, and you get what you want."

entries.zh: 惟振堅執不改，獨曰：「行正道則大勳可立。」
entries.en: Only Zhen held firm and said alone: "Follow the righteous way and great merit can be won."
entries.literal: Only Zhen firmly held and would not change, alone saying: "Walk the upright path and great merit can be established."

entries.zh: 太祖英悟，忽厲色曰：「張公勸我同敕使，欲傾附自求宰相耶！」
entries.en: The Founder was sharp-witted; suddenly he said sternly: "Lord Zhang wants me to join the edict commissioners—are you angling to topple me and buy the chancellorship!"
entries.literal: The Founder was keen-witted; suddenly with stern countenance he said: "Lord Zhang urges me to join the edict commissioners—do you wish to topple and attach yourself to seek the chancellorship!"

entries.zh: 乃定策縶偽使李奉本、支彥勳與希度等，即日請振將命於京師，與宰相謀返正。
entries.en: He bound the false envoys Li Fengben, Zhi Yanxun, and Xidu, and that day sent Zhen to the capital to work with the chancellors on restoring the throne.
entries.literal: He then fixed policy to bind the false envoys Li Fengben, Zhi Yanxun, and Xidu, and that same day asked Zhen to lead the mission to the capital to plot with the chancellors to restore legitimacy.

entries.zh: 未幾，劉季述伏誅，昭宗復帝位，太祖聞之喜，召振，執其手謂之曰：「卿所謀是吾本誌，穹蒼其知之矣！」
entries.en: Soon Liu Jishu was executed and Zhaozong restored; the Founder rejoiced, summoned Zhen, took his hand and said: "Your plan was always mine—Heaven knows!"
entries.literal: Before long Liu Jishu was executed, Zhaozong restored to the throne; the Founder heard and rejoiced, summoned Zhen, took his hand and said: "Your plan is my original intent—Heaven knows!"

entries.zh: 自是益重之。
entries.en: From then he valued Zhen all the more.
entries.literal: From then he valued him all the more.

entries.zh: 天祐二年春正月，太祖召振，謂曰：「王師範來降，易歲尚處故藩，今將奏請徙授方面，其為我馳騎，以茲意達之。」
entries.en: Tianyou 2, spring month 1, the Founder told Zhen: "Wang Shifan has surrendered but still holds his old domain after nearly a year; I will ask to move him to a new post—ride for me and make that clear."
entries.literal: Tianyou 2 spring month 1, the Founder summoned Zhen and said: "Wang Shifan has submitted; nearly a year he still dwells in his old fief; now I will memorialize to transfer him to a circuit commission—ride for me and convey this intent."

entries.zh: 振至青州，師範即日出公府，以節度、觀察二印及文簿管鑰授於振。
entries.en: At Qingzhou, Shifan left headquarters the same day and gave Zhen the military and surveillance seals, records, and keys.
entries.literal: Zhen reached Qingzhou; Shifan that same day left the government hall and handed Zhen the military commissioner and surveillance commissioner seals and documents and keys.

entries.zh: 師範雖已受代，而疑撓特甚，屢揮泣求貸其族，振因以切理諭之曰：「公不念張繡事耶！
entries.en: Though replaced, Shifan was deeply afraid and wept repeatedly, begging mercy for his clan; Zhen reasoned with him: "Have you forgotten Zhang Xiu!
entries.literal: Shifan though already replaced was extremely doubtful and fearful, repeatedly weeping and begging mercy for his clan; Zhen therefore admonished with keen reasoning: "Sir, do you not recall Zhang Xiu's affair!

entries.zh: 漢末，繡屢與曹公立敵，豈德之耶，及袁紹遣使招繡，賈詡曰：『袁家父子自不相容，何能主天下英士，曹公挾天子令諸侯，其志大，不以私仇為意，不宜疑之。』
entries.en: At the end of Han, Xiu had often fought Lord Cao—would Cao have treated that as a kindness? When Yuan Shao sent envoys to recruit Xiu, Jia Xu said: 'The Yuan father and son cannot abide each other—how could they lead the realm's heroes? Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords; his aim is great and he does not settle private scores—you should not doubt him.'
entries.literal: End of Han, Xiu repeatedly was enemy to Lord Cao—was that virtue? When Yuan Shao sent envoys to recruit Xiu, Jia Xu said: 'The Yuan father and son cannot abide each other—how can they lead the empire's heroes? Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords; his ambition is great and he does not bear private grudges in mind—you should not doubt him.'

entries.zh: 今梁王亦豈以私怨害忠賢耶！」
entries.en: Would the King of Liang now destroy loyal men over old grudges!"
entries.literal: Today too would the King of Liang harm the loyal and worthy over private grudge!"

entries.zh: 師範灑然大悟，翌日，以其族遷。
entries.en: Shifan saw the point; the next day he moved his family.
entries.literal: Shifan suddenly awakened; next day he moved his clan.

entries.zh: 太祖乃表振為青州留後，未幾，征還。
entries.en: The Founder made Zhen acting commissioner of Qingzhou, then soon recalled him.
entries.literal: The Founder then memorialized Zhen as Qingzhou acting commissioner; before long he was recalled.

entries.zh: 唐自昭宗遷都之後，王室微弱，朝廷班行，備員而已。
entries.en: After Zhaozong moved the capital the Tang house was feeble and court posts were empty titles.
entries.literal: Tang since Zhaozong moved the capital, the royal house was weak; court ranks were mere placeholders.

entries.zh: 振皆頤指氣使，旁若無人，朋附者非次獎升，私晉者沈棄。
entries.en: Zhen ordered everyone about as if alone in the room; allies rose out of turn and private petitioners were ruined.
entries.literal: Zhen everywhere pointed and commanded breath, as if no one else were present; partisans were promoted out of turn, private petitioners were sunk and abandoned.

entries.zh: 振每自汴入洛，朝中必有貶竄，故唐朝人士目為「鴟鴞」。
entries.en: Whenever Zhen came from Bian to Luoyang someone at court was demoted or exiled—Tang officials called him "the owl."
entries.literal: Every time Zhen came from Bian to Luoyang, someone in court was demoted or banished—so Tang court people called him "owl."

entries.zh: 天祐中，唐宰相柳璨希太祖旨，譖殺大臣裴樞、陸扆等七人於滑州白馬驛。
entries.en: In Tianyou the Tang chancellor Liu Can, courting the Founder, slandered to death seven ministers including Pei Shu and Lu Yi at Baima post in Huazhou.
entries.literal: In Tianyou, Tang chief minister Liu Can hoping to please the Founder's intent slandered to death seven great ministers including Pei Shu and Lu Yi at Baima post in Huazhou.

entries.zh: 時振自以咸通、乾符中嘗應進士舉，累上不第，尤憤憤，乃謂太祖曰：「此輩自謂清流，宜投於黃河，永為濁流。」
entries.en: Zhen had failed the jinshi repeatedly in Xiantong and Qianfu and burned with resentment; he told the Founder: "These men call themselves the Clear Stream—they should be thrown into the Yellow River and be muddy water forever."
entries.literal: At that time Zhen himself had in Xiantong and Qianfu repeatedly taken the jinshi examination and repeatedly failed to pass—especially resentful; he told the Founder: "This lot call themselves the Clear Stream—they ought to be thrown into the Yellow River and be the muddy stream forever."

entries.zh: 太祖笑而從之。
entries.en: The Founder laughed and agreed.
entries.literal: The Founder laughed and followed it.

entries.zh: 洎太祖受禪，自宣義軍節度副使、檢校司徒授殿中監，累遷戶部尚書。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Zhen rose from Xuanyi vice commissioner and honorary Minister of Works to Palace Supervisor and then Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, from Xuanyi army vice commissioner and honorary Minister of Works he was made Palace Supervisor, rising in time to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 庶人友珪篡立，代敬翔為崇政院使。
entries.en: When Yougui seized the throne, Zhen replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
entries.literal: When commoner Yougui usurped the throne, Zhen replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，趙、張二族用事，遂為所間，謀猷獻替，多不見從，振每稱疾避事。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor the Zhao and Zhang clans ruled; Zhen was sidelined and his counsel was mostly ignored—he often pleaded illness to stay out of affairs.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, the Zhao and Zhang clans held power; he was thus set at odds; stratagems and proposals mostly were not followed—Zhen often claimed illness to avoid affairs.

entries.zh: 龍德末，閑居私第將期矣，晉主入汴，振謁見首罪，郭崇韜指振謂人曰：「人言李振乃一代奇才，吾今見之，乃常人耳！」
entries.en: At the end of Longde he had lived in retirement nearly a year; when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen came to beg mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at him and said: "They call Li Zhen a wonder of the age—I see an ordinary man!"
entries.literal: End of Longde, living in retirement at his private residence nearly a year, when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen paid court asking mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at Zhen and said to people: "People say Li Zhen is a generation's strange talent—I see him now and he is just an ordinary man!"

entries.zh: 會段凝等疏梁氏權要之臣，振與敬翔等同日族誅。
entries.en: When Duan Ning and others denounced Liang power-holders, Zhen and Jing Xiang were executed to the third degree on the same day.
entries.literal: It happened that Duan Ning and others impeached Liang power-holders; Zhen and Jing Xiang were on the same day clan-exterminated.

entries.zh: 張文蔚，字右華，河間人也。
entries.en: Zhang Wenyu, styled Youhua, came from Hejian.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenyu, style Youhua, was a native of Hejian.

entries.zh: 父裼，唐僖宗朝，累為顯官。
entries.en: His father Ti rose through several high posts under Emperor Xizong of Tang.
entries.literal: His father Ti, in Emperor Xizong's Tang, repeatedly held prominent offices.

entries.zh: 文蔚幼礪文行，求知取友，藹然有佳士之稱。
entries.en: From youth he cultivated letters and character, sought learning and worthy companions, and was known as a man of fine quality.
entries.literal: As a youth Wenyu honed literary conduct, sought knowledge and chose friends, and was amiably styled an outstanding gentleman.

entries.zh: 唐乾符初，登進士第，時丞相裴坦兼判鹽鐵，解褐署巡官。
entries.en: In the early Qianfu era he took the jinshi degree; Chief Minister Pei Tan, who also oversaw the salt monopoly, gave him his first appointment as a patrol official.
entries.literal: Early in Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi; when Chief Minister Pei Tan concurrently administered the salt monopoly, he received his first appointment as a patrol official under him.

entries.zh: 未幾，以畿尉直館。
entries.en: Soon he served as a capital aide and was posted to the Hanlin archive.
entries.literal: Before long he was made a capital-district aide and entered the Hanlin archive.

entries.zh: 丁家艱，以孝聞。
entries.en: When his father died, his mourning won wide praise.
entries.literal: Upon his father's death he was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 中和歲，僖宗在蜀，大寇未滅，急於軍費，移鹽鐵於揚州，命李都就判之，奏為轉運巡官。
entries.en: During the Zhonghe reign, with the emperor in Shu and rebels still unchecked, the court moved salt administration to Yangzhou under Li Du; Wenyu was named transport patrol official.
entries.literal: In the Zhonghe years, with Xizong in Shu, great bandits not yet destroyed, and military funds urgent, the salt monopoly was moved to Yangzhou; Li Du was ordered to administer it, and Wenyu was recommended as transport patrol official.

entries.zh: 駕還長安，除監察御史，遷左補闕侍御史、起居舍人、司勳吏部員外郎，拜司勳郎中、知制誥，歲滿授中書舍人。
entries.en: After the court returned to Chang'an he rose from supervising censor through remonstrator, attendant censor, and diarist to bureau director, then Merit Director and edict drafter; a year later he became Secretariat Drafter.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Chang'an, he was made supervising censor, then promoted through Left Remonstrator, attendant censor, diarist, and bureau registrars, appointed Director of Merit and drafter of edicts, and after a full year made Secretariat Drafter.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，退居東畿，哀毀過禮。
entries.en: He mourned his mother in the eastern suburbs, his grief so deep it outstripped the rites.
entries.literal: Upon his mother's death he retired to the eastern capital suburbs, his grief exceeding ritual.

entries.zh: 服闋，復拜中書舍人，俄召入翰林，為承旨學士。
entries.en: After mourning he resumed as Secretariat Drafter and was soon called into the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was again made Secretariat Drafter, soon summoned to the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.

entries.zh: 屬昭宗初還京闕，皇綱浸微，文蔚所發詔令，靡失厥中，論者多之。
entries.en: When Zhaozong first came back to the capital, the throne was failing; Wenyu's edicts struck the right note every time, and men of judgment approved.
entries.literal: As Zhaozong first returned to the capital, imperial governance grew weak; the edicts Wenyu drafted never missed the mark, and critics praised him.

entries.zh: 轉戶部侍郎，仍依前充職，尋出為禮部侍郎。
entries.en: He became Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining his old duties, then moved to Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue while keeping his former duties, then sent out as Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 天祐元年夏，拜中書侍郎、平章事，兼判戶部。
entries.en: In summer of Tianyou 1 he was made Secretariat Vice Minister, Chief Councillor, and put in charge of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the summer of the first year of Tianyou he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Chief Councillor, and concurrently administered Revenue.

entries.zh: 時柳璨在相位，擅權縱暴，傾陷賢俊，宰相裴樞等五家及三省而下三十餘人，鹹抱冤就死；
entries.en: Liu Can then dominated the court, abused power, and destroyed the worthy: Chancellor Pei Shu and four other families, with more than thirty men from the Three Departments, all died unjustly.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Can held the chancellery, usurped power and ran wild, crushed worthy men—the chancellor Pei Shu and four other households plus more than thirty from the Three Departments all died innocent.

entries.zh: 縉紳以目，不敢竊語其是非，餘怒所注，亦不啻十許輩。
entries.en: Officials watched in silence, afraid even to murmur judgment; a dozen more still lay in the path of his rage.
entries.literal: The gentry watched with their eyes and dared not whisper right from wrong; those still in his wrath numbered no fewer than ten-odd.

entries.zh: 文蔚殫其力解之，乃止，士人賴焉。
entries.en: Wenyu spent himself to halt the slaughter, and the scholarly class owed him their lives.
entries.literal: Wenyu exhausted his strength to save them and stopped it; scholars relied on him.

entries.zh: 璨敗死，文蔚兼度支鹽鐵使。
entries.en: After Can's fall and death, Wenyu was also made Commissioner of Finance and Salt.
entries.literal: When Can fell and died, Wenyu was made concurrent Commissioner of Finance and Salt.

entries.zh: 天祐四年，天子以土運將革，天命有歸，四月，命文蔚與楊涉等總率百僚，奉禪位詔至大梁。
entries.en: In Tianyou 4, believing the age of earth was ending and Heaven's mandate had turned, the emperor in the fourth month sent Wenyu and Yang She at the head of the bureaucracy to Daliang with the abdication edict.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou the Son of Heaven, seeing the earthly cycle about to change and Heaven's mandate shifting, in the fourth month ordered Wenyu and Yang She to lead all officials bearing the abdication edict to Daliang.

entries.zh: 太祖受命，文蔚等不易其位。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Wenyu and his colleagues kept their offices.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Wenyu and the rest kept their posts.

entries.zh: 開平二年春，暴卒於位，詔贈右僕射。
entries.en: In spring of Kaiping 2 he died suddenly at his post; the court posthumously made him Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaiping he died suddenly in office; an edict posthumously made him Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 氏叔琮，尉氏人也。
entries.en: Shi Shucong came from Weishi.
entries.literal: Shi Shucong was a native of Weishi.

entries.zh: 唐中和末，應募為騎軍，初隸於龐師古，為伍長。
entries.en: In the last years of Zhonghe he joined the cavalry under Pang Shigu as a squad leader.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang Zhonghe he answered the levy as cavalry, first attached to Pang Shigu as squad chief.

entries.zh: 叔琮壯勇沈毅，膽力過人。
entries.en: Shucong was burly, brave, and steady; none matched his nerve.
entries.literal: Shucong was stalwart, brave, and deep-steady; in daring and strength he surpassed others.

entries.zh: 太祖討巢、蔡於陳、許間，叔琮奮擊，首出諸校，太祖壯之，自行伍間擢為後院馬軍都將。
entries.en: Fighting Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan between Chen and Xu, Shucong led the charge; the Founder pulled him from the ranks to command the rear-guard cavalry.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Chao and Cai between Chen and Xu, Shucong struck hard and led all the officers; the Founder admired him and from the ranks promoted him rear-courtyard horse-army commander.

entries.zh: 時東伐徐、鄆，多曆年所，叔琮身當矢石，奮不顧命，觀者許焉。
entries.en: Years of war in Xu and Yan saw Shucong take every blow without flinching; men who watched approved.
entries.literal: When the eastern campaign against Xu and Yan spanned many years, Shucong met arrows and stones in person, striving without regard for life—onlookers approved.

entries.zh: 累遷為指揮使，尋奏授宿州刺史、檢校右僕射。
entries.en: He rose to commander, then to Suzhou prefect and acting Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to commander; soon memorialized and appointed Suzhou prefect and acting Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 太祖伐襄陽，叔琮失利，降為陽翟鎮遏使；
entries.en: After a defeat at Xiangyang the Founder reduced him to frontier commissioner at Yangzhai;
entries.literal: When the Founder attacked Xiangyang Shucong was defeated and demoted to Yangzhai frontier suppression commissioner;

entries.zh: 尋又捍禦晉軍於洹水有功，遷曹州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he held the Jin army at the Huan and was made prefect of Cao.
entries.literal: soon after defending against Jin troops at the Huan River with merit, he was moved to Cao prefect.

entries.zh: 天復元年春，領大軍攻拔澤、潞，叔琮遂引兵北掠太原。
entries.en: Spring of Tianfu 1, the great army took Ze and Lu; Shucong marched north to raid Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In spring of Tianfu year 1 he led a great army to capture Ze and Lu; Shucong then led troops north to raid Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 師還，除晉州節度使。
entries.en: On the return he received Jinzhou as his command.
entries.literal: When the army returned he was made Jinzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年，太祖屯軍於岐下，晉軍潛襲絳州，前軍不利。
entries.en: Next year, with the Founder at Qi, Jin struck Jiang by stealth and the van was beaten.
