entries.literal: The next year the Founder encamped below Qi; Jin troops secretly raided Jiangzhou and the vanguard fared ill.

entries.zh: 晉軍恃勝攻臨汾，叔琮嚴設備禦。
entries.en: Emboldened by victory, the Jin army moved on Linfen; Shucong fortified every approach.
entries.literal: Jin troops relying on victory attacked Linfen; Shucong strictly set defenses.

entries.zh: 乃於軍中選壯士二人，深目虯須，貌如沙陀者，令就襄陵縣牧馬於道間。
entries.en: He picked two broad-shouldered men with deep eyes, curling beards, and Shatuo looks, and set them to graze horses on the road near Xiangling.
entries.literal: He then chose from the army two stalwart men, deep-eyed with curly beards, in appearance like Shatuo, and ordered them to pasture horses by the road near Xiangling county.

entries.zh: 蕃寇見之不疑，二人因雜其行間，俄而伺隙各擒一人而來。
entries.en: The raiders took no alarm; the two slipped among them and, seizing their chance, each dragged back a prisoner.
entries.literal: Barbarian raiders seeing them did not doubt; the two mingled in their ranks and presently each seized one man and came back.

entries.zh: 晉軍大驚，且疑有伏兵，遂退據蒲縣。
entries.en: The Jin host panicked at the thought of ambush and fell back to Pu county.
entries.literal: Jin troops were greatly alarmed and suspected an ambush, so they withdrew to hold Pu county.

entries.zh: 時太祖遣朱友寧將兵數萬赴應，悉委叔琮節制。
entries.en: The Founder sent Zhu Youning with an army of tens of thousands and gave Shucong full command.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder sent Zhu Youning with tens of thousands of troops to assist and wholly entrusted command to Shucong.

entries.zh: 既至，諸將皆欲休軍，叔琮曰：「若然，則賊必遁矣，遁則何功焉！」
entries.en: Once there, every general wanted rest; Shucong said, "Do that and they will run—and what glory is there in that?"
entries.literal: When they arrived all the generals wished to rest the army; Shucong said: "If so, the bandits will surely flee—what merit if they flee!"

entries.zh: 因夜出，潛師截其歸路，遇晉軍遊騎數百，盡殺之；
entries.en: That night he stole out, cut their retreat, and slaughtered several hundred Jin scouts;
entries.literal: Thereupon by night he went out, secretly sent troops to cut their line of retreat, met several hundred Jin patrol horse, and killed them all;

entries.zh: 遂攻其壘，拔之，斬獲萬餘眾，奪馬三百匹。
entries.en: then stormed their camp, took it, killed or captured more than ten thousand, and seized three hundred horses.
entries.literal: then attacked their fort, took it, beheaded and captured over ten thousand, and seized three hundred horses.

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，喜謂左右曰：「殺蕃賊，破太原，非氏老不可！」
entries.en: When word reached the Founder he told his staff, "To kill these barbarians and break Taiyuan we need none but Old Shi!"
entries.literal: The Founder heard and joyfully told his attendants: "To kill the barbarian bandits and break Taiyuan—none but Old Shi will do!"

entries.zh: 叔琮乃長驅收汾州，與晉人轉戰，直抵並壘。
entries.en: Shucong drove on to recover Fenzhou, traded blows with the Jin all the way to the walls of Bing.
entries.literal: Shucong then drove far to recover Fenzhou, fought in turn with the Jin, and straight to the walls of Bing.

entries.zh: 軍回，以其功奏加檢校司空。
entries.en: On the army's return his deeds won him acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When the army returned, his merit was memorialized and he was given acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 自後累年，晉軍不敢侵軼。
entries.en: For years after, the Jin army did not dare cross the border.
entries.literal: From then for accumulated years Jin troops did not dare invade or raid.

entries.zh: 叔琮養士愛民，甚有能政。
entries.en: Shucong kept good men close and cared for the people; his rule was capable.
entries.literal: Shucong nourished scholar-officers and loved the people; he had quite able governance.

entries.zh: 天復三年，為鄜州留後，尋真領保大軍節度使、檢校司徒。
entries.en: In Tianfu 3 he became regent of Fuzhou, then full military governor of the Baoda Army with acting Minister over the Masses rank.
entries.literal: In Tianfu year 3 he was made Fuzhou regent and soon truly held Baoda Army military governor and acting Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 及昭宗東遷，征為右龍虎統軍，以衛洛陽。
entries.en: When Zhaozong moved east, Shucong was called to guard Luoyang as commander of the Right Dragon-Tiger Guard.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved east he was summoned as Right Dragon-Tiger commander to guard Luoyang.

entries.zh: 天祐元年八月，與朱友恭同受太祖密旨，弑昭宗於大內。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Tianyou 1 he and Zhu Yougong, on the Founder's secret order, killed Zhaozong inside the palace.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Tianyou year 1 he with Zhu Yougong together received the Founder's secret order and assassinated Zhaozong in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 既而責以軍政不理，貶白州司戶。
entries.en: Soon he was blamed for slack command and demoted to registrar at Baizhou.
entries.literal: Soon after he was charged with disorder in military government and demoted to Baizhou registrar.

entries.zh: 尋賜自盡。
entries.en: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to take his own life.
entries.literal: Before long he was granted suicide.

entries.zh: 叔琮將死，呼曰：「賣我性命，欲塞天下之謗，其如神理何！」
entries.en: Facing death Shucong cried, "You sell my life to silence the world—what of heaven's judgment!"
entries.literal: As Shucong was about to die he cried: "You sell my life to plug the world's blame—what of divine principle!"

entries.zh: 乾化二年，詔許歸葬。
entries.en: In Qianhua 2 an edict allowed his body to be brought home for burial.
entries.literal: In Qianhua year 2 an edict permitted return for burial.

entries.zh: 朱友恭，壽春人，本姓李，名彥威。
entries.en: Zhu Yougong came from Shouchun; his birth name was Li Yanwei.
entries.literal: Zhu Yougong, a man of Shouchun, originally surnamed Li and named Yanwei.

entries.zh: 瑽角事太祖，性穎利，善體太祖意，太祖憐之，因畜為己子，賜姓，初名克讓，後改之。
entries.en: A boy in the Founder's service, clever and quick to read his mood, he was adopted, given the Zhu surname, first Kerang, then Yougong.
entries.literal: From boyhood he served the Founder; nature keen and clever, good at grasping the Founder's intent—the Founder pitied him and therefore raised him as his own son, granting the surname; first named Kerang, later changed.

entries.zh: 時初建左長劍都，以友恭董之。
entries.en: When the Left Long-Sword Corps was formed, Yougong was placed at its head.
entries.literal: When the Left Long-Sword Corps was first established, Yougong was put in charge.

entries.zh: 從太祖四征，稍立軍功，累遷諸軍都指揮使、檢校左僕射。
entries.en: Four campaigns with the Founder won him steady promotions to army commander and acting Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Following the Founder on four campaigns he gradually achieved military merit, repeatedly promoted to all-armies commander and acting Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，授汝州刺史，加檢校司空。
entries.en: Under Qianning he became prefect of Ru with acting Minister of Works rank.
entries.literal: In the Qianning years he was appointed Ruzhou prefect and added acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 光化初，淮夷侵鄂渚，武昌帥杜洪來乞師，太祖遣友恭將兵萬餘，濟江應援，引兵至龍沙、九江而還，軍聲大振。
entries.en: Early Guanghua, when Huainan raiders struck Ezhou, Du Hong of Wuchang begged help; Yougong crossed the Yangzi with ten thousand men, swept to Longsha and Jiujiang, and returned to thunderous reputation.
entries.literal: Early Guanghua, Huaiyi invaded E's shallows; Wuchang commander Du Hong came begging troops; the Founder sent Yougong with over ten thousand troops across the river to aid, led troops to Longsha and Jiujiang and returned—the army's fame greatly shook.

entries.zh: 時淮寇據黃州，友恭攻陷其壁，獲賊將瞿章，俘斬萬計。
entries.en: He stormed Huangzhou, took the rebel Qu Zhang, and killed or captured ten thousand.
entries.literal: At that time Huai bandits held Huangzhou; Yougong stormed their fortress, captured bandit commander Qu Zhang, prisoners beheaded numbered in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 途經安陸，因襲殺刺史武瑜，盡收其眾，以功為潁州刺史，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: Passing Anlu he killed Prefect Wu Yu, absorbed his troops, and for that deed was made prefect of Ying with acting Minister over the Masses rank.
entries.literal: Passing through Anlu he thereupon raided and killed prefect Wu Yu, wholly gathered his troops, and for merit was made Yingzhou prefect with acting Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 天復中，為武寧軍留後。
entries.en: During Tianfu he served as regent of Wuning.
entries.literal: In Tianfu he was made Wuning army regent.

entries.zh: 天祐初，昭宗東遷洛邑，征拜左龍虎統軍，以衛宮闕。
entries.en: Early Tianyou, when Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Yougong was called to guard the palace as Left Dragon-Tiger commander.
entries.literal: Early Tianyou, Zhaozong moved east to Luoyi; summoned as Left Dragon-Tiger commander to guard the palace gates.

entries.zh: 尋與氏叔琮同受太祖密旨，弑昭宗於洛陽宮。
entries.en: Soon he and Shi Shucong, on the same secret order, killed Zhaozong in the Luoyang palace.
entries.literal: Soon with Shi Shucong he together received the Founder's secret order and assassinated Zhaozong at Luoyang Palace.

entries.zh: 既而太祖自河中至，責以慢於軍政，貶崖州司戶，復其本姓名，與氏叔琮同日賜死。
entries.en: When the Founder came from Hezhong he accused Yougong of negligence, stripped him to registrar at Yazhou, restored the name Li Yanwei, and had him executed the same day as Shucong.
entries.literal: Soon the Founder came from Hezhong, charged him with laxity in military government, demoted to Yazhou registrar, restored his original surname and name, and on the same day as Shi Shucong granted death.

entries.zh: 王重師，潁州長社人也。
entries.en: Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Chongshi was a native of Changshe in Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 材力兼人，沈嘿大度，臨事有權變，劍槊之妙，冠絕於一時。
entries.en: Strong as three men, quiet and broad-minded, quick with expedients in crisis, his spear-work was unmatched in his day.
entries.literal: In talent and strength he matched many men; deep, silent, and great-minded; facing affairs he had timely expedients; in spear and halberd skill he crowned the age.

entries.zh: 唐中和末，蔡寇陷許昌，重師脫身而來，太祖異其狀貌，乃隸於拔山都。
entries.en: When Cai rebels seized Xuchang at the end of Zhonghe, Chongshi broke free and fled to the Founder, who marveled at him and enrolled him in the Mount Uprooted Corps.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang Zhonghe Cai bandits took Xuchang; Chongshi escaped and came; the Founder marveled at his appearance and attached him to the Uproot-Mountains Corps.

entries.zh: 每於軍前效用，頗出儕類。
entries.en: In action he always outshone his fellows.
entries.literal: Whenever he served before the army he quite surpassed his peers.

entries.zh: 文德中，令董左右長劍軍。
entries.en: Under Wende he took charge of the Left and Right Long-Sword armies.
entries.literal: In the Wende years he was ordered to direct the Left and Right Long-Sword armies.

entries.zh: 太祖伐上蔡，重師力戰有功。
entries.en: At Shangcai he fought with distinguished valor.
entries.literal: When the Founder attacked Shangcai, Chongshi fought hard with merit.

entries.zh: 及討兗、鄆，擢為指揮使，奏授檢校右僕射。
entries.en: In the Yan and Yun campaigns he rose to commander and acting Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: When campaigning against Yan and Yun he was promoted to commander and memorialized as acting Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 重師枕戈擐甲五六年，於齊、魯間凡經百餘戰，由是威震敵人。
entries.en: For five or six years he slept in armor; between Qi and Lu he fought more than a hundred battles until the enemy feared his name.
entries.literal: Chongshi slept on his spear and buckled armor five or six years; between Qi and Lu he passed through altogether more than a hundred battles—thereby his awe shook the enemy.

entries.zh: 尋授檢校司空，為潁州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made acting Minister of Works and prefect of Ying.
entries.literal: Soon appointed acting Minister of Works and made Yingzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，太祖攻濮州，縱兵壞其墉，濮人因屯火塞其壞壘，煙焰亙空，人莫敢越。
entries.en: At Puzhou in Qianning the breach was made, but defenders piled fire in the gap until smoke blotted the sky and no man would cross.
entries.literal: In Qianning the Founder attacked Puzhou, sent troops to break its wall; Pu people heaped fire to block the breach, smoke and flame spanning the sky, and none dared cross.

entries.zh: 重師方苦金瘡，臥於軍次，諸將或勉之，乃躍起，命壯士悉取軍中氈罽投水中，擲於火上，重師然後率精銳，持短兵突入，諸軍踵之，濮州乃陷。
entries.en: Wounded, he lay in camp until his officers roused him; he leaped up, had men soak felt and fling it on the flames, then led elite troops with short blades through the gap—the army poured after and Puzhou fell.
entries.literal: Chongshi was then suffering a metal wound, lying in the army camp; generals sometimes urged him—he then leaped up, ordered stalwarts to take all the army's felt blankets and throw them in water and onto the fire; Chongshi then led crack troops with short weapons bursting in; the armies followed—and Puzhou fell.

entries.zh: 重師為劍槊所傷，身被八九創，丁壯荷之還營，且將斃矣。
entries.en: Spears left eight or nine wounds; bearers carried him back half dead.
entries.literal: Chongshi was wounded by spear and halberd, his body bearing eight or nine cuts; strong youths carried him back to camp—he was near death.

entries.zh: 太祖驚惜尤甚，曰：「雖得濮壘，而失重師，奈何！」
entries.en: The Founder was stricken: "We have Puzhou but may lose Chongshi—what then!"
entries.literal: The Founder was startled and grieved beyond measure, saying: "Though we have taken the Pu fortress, we have lost Chongshi—what is to be done!"

entries.zh: 亟命以奇藥療之，彌月始愈。
entries.en: He sent rare drugs; a full month passed before Chongshi could rise.
entries.literal: He at once ordered extraordinary medicines to treat him; a full month passed before recovery.

entries.zh: 尋知平盧軍留後，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: He was soon made regent of Pinglu with acting Minister over the Masses rank.
entries.literal: Soon made acting Pinglu army regent and added acting Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 其後北伐幽、滄、鎮、定，屢與晉軍接戰，頗得士心，故多勝捷。
entries.en: Northern campaigns against You, Cang, Zhen, and Ding brought repeated clashes with Jin; he won his men's hearts and many victories.
entries.literal: Afterward on northern expeditions to You, Cang, Zhen, and Ding he repeatedly met Jin troops in battle, quite won soldiers' hearts, and therefore had many victories.

entries.zh: 天祐中，授雍州節度使，加同平章事。
entries.en: In Tianyou he became military governor of Yongzhou and Honorary Councilor.
entries.literal: In Tianyou appointed Yongzhou military governor and added Honorary Councilor.

entries.zh: 數年治戎恤民，頗有威惠。
entries.en: For years he drilled the army and cared for the people; awe and kindness attended his rule.
entries.literal: For several years governing the army and cherishing the people, he had quite awe and kindness.

entries.zh: 開平中，為劉捍所構，太祖深疑之，然未有以發其事。
entries.en: In Kaiping Liu Han slandered him; the Founder grew suspicious but lacked cause to act.
entries.literal: In Kaiping he was framed by Liu Han; the Founder deeply suspected him, yet had no means to raise the matter.

entries.zh: 無何，擅遣裨將張君練縱兵深入邠、鳳，君練敗北。
entries.en: Then, without leave, he sent Zhang Junlian raiding into Bin and Feng; Junlian was routed.
entries.literal: Before long he on his own authority sent lieutenant Zhang Junlian to lead troops deep into Bin and Feng; Junlian was defeated and fled north.

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，怒其專擅，因追而斬之。
entries.en: Hearing of it, the Founder raged at his insubordination, overtook him, and beheaded him.
entries.literal: The Founder heard, was angry at his willful authority, and pursued and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云劉捍至長安，王重師不為禮，捍譖之帝，曰：「重師潛與邠、岐通。」
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Liu Han reached Chang'an and Chongshi refused him courtesy; Han told the Emperor, "Chongshi is in secret contact with Bin and Qi."
entries.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: When Liu Han reached Chang'an, Wang Chongshi did not show courtesy; Han slandered him to the Emperor, saying: "Chongshi secretly communicates with Bin and Qi."

entries.zh: 甲申，貶溪州刺史，尋賜自盡，夷其族。）〉
entries.en: On jiashen he was demoted to Xi, then ordered to die; his clan was destroyed.）〉
entries.literal: On jiashen he was demoted to Xizhou prefect; soon granted suicide and his clan exterminated.）〉

entries.zh: 朱珍，徐州豐縣雍鳳里人也。
entries.en: Zhu Zhen came from Yongfeng lane in Feng county, Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Zhu Zhen was a man of Yongfeng lane, Feng county, Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 太祖初起兵，珍與龐師古、許唐、李暉、丁會、氏叔琮、鄧季筠、王武等八十餘人，以中涓從，摧堅陷陣，所向蕩決。
entries.en: When the Founder first took up arms, Zhen and more than eighty comrades—including Pang Shigu, Xu Tang, Li Hui, Ding Hui, Shi Shucong, Deng Jiyun, and Wang Wu—rode at his side and broke every line they met.
entries.literal: When the Founder first raised troops, Zhen with Pang Shigu, Xu Tang, Li Hui, Ding Hui, Shi Shucong, Deng Jiyun, Wang Wu, and more than eighty others followed as personal attendants—overthrowing strongholds and smashing battle arrays, wherever they aimed swept away.

entries.zh: 及太祖鎮汴，兼領招討使，署珍為宣武右職，以總腹心。
entries.en: When the Founder held Bian as punitive commissioner, he made Zhen his right hand at Xuanwu to command his trusted men.
entries.literal: When the Founder held Bian and concurrently led the punitive commissioner, he appointed Zhen to Xuanwu right duties to oversee the inner circle.

entries.zh: 於是簡練軍伍，裁制綱紀，平巢破蔡，多珍之力也。
entries.en: He drilled the ranks and enforced discipline; much of the victory over Chao and Cai was Zhen's doing.
entries.literal: Thereupon he selected and drilled the army host, trimmed and set regulations—pacifying Chao and breaking Cai owed much to Zhen's strength.

entries.zh: 始尚讓以驍騎五千人至繁臺，珍與龐師古、齊奉國等擊退之。
entries.en: When Shang Rang brought five thousand horsemen to Fantai, Zhen, Pang Shigu, and Qi Fengguo beat them back.
entries.literal: At first Shang Rang came with five thousand fierce cavalry to Fantai; Zhen with Pang Shigu, Qi Fengguo, and others drove him back.

entries.zh: 及黃巢敗，珍與並帥李克用追至冤句而還。
entries.en: After Huang Chao's defeat Zhen pursued with Li Keyong of Bing as far as Yuanqu, then turned back.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao was defeated, Zhen with Bing commander Li Keyong pursued to Yuanqu and returned.

entries.zh: 尋從太祖以汴、宋、亳之師入西華，破王夏寨，勇冠軍鋒，以功加秩。
entries.en: He followed the Founder into Xihua with armies from Bian, Song, and Bo, stormed Wang Xia's camp, led the van in valor, and won higher rank.
entries.literal: Soon following the Founder with Bian, Song, and Bo troops into Xihua, he broke Wang Xia's stockade, courage crowning the army's point—for merit rank was added.

entries.zh: 光啟元年，署諸軍都指揮使，始為上將。
entries.en: In Guangqi 1 he became army commander—a full general at last.
entries.literal: Guangqi year 1, appointed all-armies commander—first becoming a senior general.

entries.zh: 於是軍焦夷，敗蔡師鐵林三千人，盡俘其將。
entries.en: At Jiaoyi he smashed three thousand Iron Forest Guards of the Cai army and took every officer prisoner.
entries.literal: Thereupon the army was at Jiaoyi, defeated three thousand Iron Forest troops of Cai army, wholly captured their generals.

entries.zh: 復西至汝、鄭，南過陳、潁，繚宋、亳、滑、濮間，與蔡賊交戰，鏖伏襲殺，不知其數。
entries.en: West to Ru and Zheng, south through Chen and Ying, he ranged Song, Bo, Hua, and Pu fighting Cai rebels in ambush after battle beyond count.
entries.literal: Again west to Ru and Zheng, south past Chen and Ying, winding among Song, Bo, Hua, and Pu—battling Cai bandits in grinding fights, ambushes, and killings beyond counting.

entries.zh: 會滑州節度使安師儒戎政不治，太祖命珍與李唐賓率步騎以經略之。
entries.en: When An Shiru of Huazhou misgoverned his command, the Founder sent Zhen and Li Tangbin to seize the province.
entries.literal: When Huazhou military governor An Shiru had disorderly military government, the Founder ordered Zhen with Li Tangbin to lead foot and horse to take it in hand.

entries.zh: 始入境，遇大雪，令軍士無得休息，一夕馳至壁下，百梯並升，遂乘其墉，滑州平。
entries.en: Snow met them at the border; he allowed no halt. In one night they were at the walls, a hundred ladders went up together, and Huazhou fell.
entries.literal: Just entering the border they met great snow; he ordered soldiers not to rest—one night galloped to below the wall, a hundred ladders rose together, then mounted the rampart, and Huazhou was pacified.

entries.zh: 時太祖方謀齊師，乃遣珍往淄州募兵，行次任縣，東面都統齊克讓伏兵於孫師陂以邀珍，珍大破之。
entries.en: While the Founder planned against Qi, Zhen went to Zizhou to raise troops; Qi Kerang ambushed him at Sunshi Slope near Ren county—Zhen broke him utterly.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder was planning Qi armies and sent Zhen to Zizhou to raise troops; passing Ren county, Eastern Front commander Qi Kerang lay in ambush at Sunshi Slope to intercept Zhen—Zhen greatly defeated him.

entries.zh: 進軍至牙山，都虞候張仁遇白珍曰：「軍有不齊者，當先斬本都將，後以狀聞，願許之。」
entries.en: At Yashan, Inspector Zhang Renyu asked Zhen: "When a unit falters, let me kill its commander first and report after—grant me that right."
entries.literal: Advancing to Yashan, ward-inspector Zhang Renyu reported to Zhen: "When the army is out of step, first behead that unit's commander, then report by memorial—I beg permission."

entries.zh: 珍怒其專，乃斬仁遇以徇軍，由是諸將咸懼。
entries.en: Zhen, furious at the presumption, executed Renyu before the ranks, and every officer thereafter lived in fear.
entries.literal: Zhen was angry at his presumption, beheaded Renyu to warn the army, and thereby all generals feared.

entries.zh: 兵至乾封，與淄人戰於白草口，敗之。
entries.en: At Qianfeng he met the Qi army at Baicao Mouth and routed them.
entries.literal: Troops reached Qianfeng and fought Qi men at Baicao Mouth—defeated them.

entries.zh: 青人以步騎二萬，列三寨於金嶺驛，珍與戰，連破之，殲其師，盡獲軍器戎馬。
entries.en: Twenty thousand Qi troops held three camps at Jinling Post; Zhen broke them in succession, destroyed the army, and took all arms and horses.
entries.literal: Qing men with twenty thousand foot and horse set three camps at Jinling Post; Zhen fought them, repeatedly broke them, annihilated their army, and wholly seized weapons and war horses.

entries.zh: 是夕，攻博昌，大獲兵眾。
entries.en: That night he stormed Bochang and swelled his ranks with captives.
entries.literal: That night he attacked Bochang and greatly gained troops.

entries.zh: 其後破盧瑭、張至及朱瑄、朱瑾之眾，平定曹、濮，未嘗不在戰中。
entries.en: He fought Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, Zhu Xuan, and Zhu Jin, pacified Cao and Pu, and was never far from the fighting.
entries.literal: Afterward he broke the hosts of Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, Zhu Xuan, and Zhu Jin, pacified Cao and Pu—never absent from battle.

entries.zh: 梁山之役，始與李唐賓不協。
entries.en: At Liangshan he first clashed with Li Tangbin.
entries.literal: In the battle at Liangshan he first fell out with Li Tangbin.

entries.zh: 珍在軍嘗私迎其室於汴，而不先請，太祖疑之，密令唐賓察之，二將不相下，因而交諍。
entries.en: Zhen had his wife brought to Bian without permission; the Founder suspected collusion and set Tangbin to watch—the two generals quarreled and would not yield.
entries.literal: Zhen in the army once privately welcomed his household to Bian without asking first; the Founder suspected this and secretly ordered Tangbin to observe— the two generals would not yield, and thus quarreled.

entries.zh: 唐賓夜斬關還汴以訴，珍亦棄軍單騎而至，太祖兩惜之，故不罪，俾還於師。
entries.en: Tangbin broke through at night to complain at Bian; Zhen rode alone from the camp; the Founder valued both and sent them back without punishment.
entries.literal: Tangbin by night cut the pass and returned to Bian to complain; Zhen too abandoned the army and came alone on horseback; the Founder cherished both and therefore did not punish, ordering them back to the army.

entries.zh: 復以踏白騎士入陳、亳間，以邀蔡人，遂南至斤溝，破淮西石璠之師二萬，擄璠以獻。
entries.en: With scout horse he raided between Chen and Bo, drove south to Jingou, shattered Shi Fan's twenty thousand Huai troops, and brought Fan in chains.
entries.literal: Again with scout cavalry he entered between Chen and Bo to intercept Cai men, then south to Jingou, broke Huaixi Shi Fan's army of twenty thousand, and captured Fan to present.

entries.zh: 珍旋師自亳北趣靜戎，濟舟於滑，破黎陽、臨河、李固三鎮。
entries.en: Turning north from Bo toward Jingrong, he crossed the river at Hua and took Liyang, Linhe, and Ligu.
entries.literal: Zhen wheeled the army from north of Bo toward Jingrong, crossed boats at Hua, and broke the three garrisons of Liyang, Linhe, and Ligu.

entries.zh: 軍於內黃，敗樂從訓萬餘人，分命聶金、範居實略澶州，與魏師遇於臨黃；
entries.en: At Neihuang he beat Yue Congxun's ten thousand, sent Nie Jin and Fan Jushi against Caozhou, and met the Wei army at Linhuang;
entries.literal: Army at Neihuang defeated Yue Congxun's more than ten thousand, separately ordered Nie Jin and Fan Jushi to take Caozhou, met Wei army at Linhuang;

entries.zh: 魏軍有豹子軍二千人，戮之無噍類，威振河朔。
entries.en: He slaughtered the two thousand Leopard Guards to the last man, and his name shook the north.
entries.literal: Wei army had two thousand Leopard Corps—slaughtered to the last mouthful; awe shook Hebei.

entries.zh: 復攻淮西，至蔡，夾河而寨，敗賊將蕭皓之眾，皆擁於河溺死之。
entries.en: Again in Huaixi he reached Cai, camped along both banks of the river, routed Xiao Hao's rebels, and drove them into the water to drown.
entries.literal: Again attacked Huaixi, reached Cai, camped on both sides of the river, defeated bandit commander Xiao Hao's host—all were crowded into the river and drowned.

entries.zh: 進軍蔡州，營其西南，既破羊馬垣，遇雨班師。
entries.en: He besieged Caizhou from the southwest, broke the outer rampart, then withdrew in the rain.
entries.literal: Advanced on Caizhou, camped southwest, having broken sheep-and-horse rampart met rain and withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 珍以兵援劉讚，赴楚州，至襄山南，遇徐戎扼其路，珍乃攻豐，下之。
entries.en: Marching to aid Liu Zan at Chuzhou, he found Xu troops blocking the road south of Xiangshan and took Feng by storm.
entries.literal: Zhen with troops aided Liu Zan, went to Chuzhou, reached south of Xiangshan, met Xu troops blocking the road—Zhen then attacked Feng and took it.

entries.zh: 時溥乃以全師會戰於豐南吳康裏，珍乃收豐，破其三萬餘眾。
entries.en: Shi Pu met him with his full army at Wukang li south of Feng; Zhen held the city and shattered thirty thousand.
entries.literal: Shi Pu then with full army joined battle at Wukang li south of Feng—Zhen secured Feng and broke his more than thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 及蔡賊平，珍比諸將功居多。
entries.en: When Cai fell, his share of the credit exceeded every other general.
entries.literal: When Cai bandits were pacified, Zhen compared with other generals had the greater share of merit.

entries.zh: 龍紀初，與諸將屯於蕭縣，以禦時溥，珍慮太祖自至，令諸軍葺馬廄以候巡撫，李唐賓之裨將嚴郊獨慢焉，軍候範權恃珍以督之。
entries.en: Early Longji he held Xiaoxian against Shi Pu; expecting the Founder's inspection, Zhen ordered every unit to rebuild its stables; Yan Jiao, Tangbin's lieutenant, alone was slack, and Fan Quan, backed by Zhen, pressed him.
entries.literal: Early Longji, with generals he garrisoned at Xiaoxian to oppose Shi Pu; Zhen feared the Founder would come in person, ordered all armies to repair horse stables to await inspection; Li Tangbin's lieutenant Yan Jiao alone was slack; army scout Fan Quan relied on Zhen to supervise.

entries.zh: 唐賓素與珍不協，果怒，乃見以訴其事。
entries.en: Tangbin had long hated Zhen; predictably furious, he went to the Founder to complain.
entries.literal: Tangbin had long been at odds with Zhen; as expected he was angry, then went in audience to complain of the affair.

entries.zh: 珍亦怒曰：「唐賓無禮！」
entries.en: Zhen snapped: "Tangbin has no manners!"
entries.literal: Zhen also angrily said: "Tangbin is rude!"

entries.zh: 遂拔劍斬之，珍命騎列狀陳其事。
entries.en: He drew his sword and killed him, then had the cavalry file a report on what had happened.
entries.literal: Then he drew his sword and slew him; Zhen ordered the cavalry to file a report stating the matter.

entries.zh: 太祖初聞唐賓之死，驚駭，與敬翔謀，詐令有司收捕唐賓妻子下獄，以安珍心。
entries.en: When the Founder first heard Tangbin was dead he was shocked; with Jing Xiang he pretended to arrest Tangbin's family to calm Zhen.
entries.literal: When the Founder first heard of Tangbin's death he was alarmed; with Jing Xiang he plotted to have officials falsely arrest Tangbin's wife and children and imprison them to reassure Zhen.

entries.zh: 太祖遂徑往蕭縣，距蕭一舍，珍率將校迎謁，梁祖令武士執之，責其專殺，命丁會行戮。
entries.en: The Founder rode straight to Xiao county; a stage short of the city Zhen came out with his officers to greet him; the Liang Founder had guards seize him, blamed him for killing on his own authority, and ordered Ding Hui to carry out the sentence.
entries.literal: The Founder went straight to Xiao county; one stage from Xiao, Zhen led the generals to welcome him; the Liang Founder had warriors seize him, blamed him for unauthorized killing, and ordered Ding Hui to execute him.

entries.zh: 都將霍存等數十人叩頭以救，太祖怒，以坐床擲之，乃退。
entries.en: Several dozen commanders led by Huo Cun kowtowed to beg for his life; the Founder in rage hurled his couch at them, and they fell back.
entries.literal: Several dozen commanders including Huo Cun knocked their heads to plead for him; the Founder in anger threw his couch at them, and they withdrew.

entries.zh: 李思安，陳留張亭里人也。
entries.en: Li Si'an came from Zhangting in Chenliu.
entries.literal: Li Si'an was a native of Zhangting hamlet in Chenliu.

entries.zh: 初事汴將楊彥洪為騎士。
entries.en: He first served Yang Yanhong of Bian as a horse soldier.
entries.literal: At first he served Bian general Yang Yanhong as a cavalryman.

entries.zh: 好拳勇，未弱冠，長七尺，超然有乘時自奮之意。
entries.en: Fond of boxing and daring, he was seven feet tall before manhood and burned to make his mark in the world.
entries.literal: He loved fists and valor; before his cap was grown he stood seven feet, with surpassing ambition to seize the moment and exert himself.

entries.zh: 唐中和三年，太祖鎮汴，嘗大閱戎旅，睹其材，甚偉之，因錫名思安，字貞臣。
entries.en: In Zhonghe 3 of Tang, when the Founder held Bian he reviewed the troops, admired his build, and gave him the name Si'an, styled Zhenchen.
entries.literal: Tang Zhonghe 3, the Founder held Bian; at a great review of the army he saw his talent, greatly admired him, and bestowed the name Si'an, style Zhenchen.

entries.zh: 思安善飛槊，所向披靡，每從太祖征伐，常馳馬出敵陣之後，測其厚薄而還。
entries.en: Si'an wielded the flying lance to devastating effect and often rode alone behind enemy lines to test their strength before returning.
entries.literal: Si'an was skilled with the flying lance; wherever he went none could stand; each time he followed the Founder in campaigns he would often gallop out behind the enemy lines, gauge their strength, and return.

entries.zh: 或敵人有恃猛自炫者，多命取之，必鷹揚飆卷，擒馘於萬眾之中，出入自若，如蹈無人之地。
entries.en: When the foe put forward swaggering champions, he was sent to take them—swooping through ten thousand men to seize heads and ride out as if the field were empty.
entries.literal: When enemies had fierce men who relied on their might to show off, he was often ordered to take them; he must soar like an eagle in the gale and capture heads in the midst of ten thousand—entering and leaving as if treading where no man was.

entries.zh: 太祖甚惜之，命副王虔裕為踏白將。
entries.en: The Founder valued him and made him Wang Qianyu's deputy as Tread-White commander.
entries.literal: The Founder prized him greatly and ordered him to assist Wang Qianyu as Tread-White commander.

entries.zh: 時巢、蔡合從，太祖每遣偵邏，必率先獨往。
entries.en: While Huang Chao and the Cai rebels were allied, Si'an always went ahead alone whenever the Founder sent scouts.
entries.literal: When Chao and Cai allied, whenever the Founder sent scouts Si'an always went first alone.

entries.zh: 巢敗走，思安領所部百餘人追賊，殺戮掩奪，眾莫敢當。
entries.en: When Chao fled in defeat, Si'an led a hundred-odd men in pursuit, killing and looting until none dared face him.
entries.literal: When Chao was defeated and fled, Si'an led his command of over a hundred men in pursuit, slaying and seizing plunder—the masses did not dare stand against him.

entries.zh: 尋領軍襲蔡寇於鄭，都將李唐賓馬躓而墜，思安援槊刺追者，唐賓復其騎而還。
entries.en: He later struck Cai rebels at Zheng; when Li Tangbin was thrown, Si'an speared the pursuers so Tangbin could remount and escape.
entries.literal: Soon he led troops in a raid on Cai bandits at Zheng; commander Li Tangbin's horse stumbled and he fell; Si'an with his lance stabbed the pursuers and Tangbin remounted and returned.

entries.zh: 又嘗與蔡人鬥，當陣生擒賊將柳行實。
entries.en: In another fight with the Cai army he took their general Liu Xingshi alive in the front ranks.
entries.literal: He also once fought Cai men in battle and in the front line personally captured the bandit general Liu Xingshi.

entries.zh: 其後渡長淮，下天長、高郵二邑，又拒孫儒，迫濠州，皆有奇績。
entries.en: He then crossed the Huai, took Tianchang and Gaoyou, held off Sun Ru, and pressed Chuzhou—each exploit was remarkable.
entries.literal: After that he crossed the Long Huai, took Tianchang and Gaoyou, and also resisted Sun Ru and pressed Chuzhou—all had strange merit.

entries.zh: 累遷為諸軍都指揮使，奏官至檢校左僕射，尋拜亳州刺史。
entries.en: He rose to overall army commander and Acting Left Vice Director, then became prefect of Bozhou.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to overall commander of the armies; memorialized to Acting Left Vice Director; soon made Bozhou prefect.

entries.zh: 練兵禦寇，邊境肅然。
entries.en: He trained troops and held the border; the frontier grew quiet.
entries.literal: He drilled troops and guarded against bandits; the border was solemnly ordered.

entries.zh: 思安為性勇悍，每統戎臨敵，不大勝，必大敗。
entries.en: Fierce by nature, Si'an in command either won a crushing victory or suffered a crushing defeat.
entries.literal: Si'an by nature was fierce and bold; whenever he commanded the army facing the enemy, if he did not win greatly he must lose greatly.

entries.zh: 開平元年春，率兵伐幽州，營於桑乾河，擄獲甚眾，燕人大懼。
entries.en: In spring of Kaiping 1 he attacked Youzhou and camped on the Sanggan, taking many captives and terrifying the Yan.
entries.literal: Kaiping 1 spring, he led troops to attack Youzhou; camped on the Sanggan River; captures were very many; Yan men greatly feared.

entries.zh: 及軍回，率諸軍伐潞，累月不克，師人多逸。
entries.en: On the return march he besieged Lu for months without success, and many soldiers deserted.
entries.literal: When the army returned he led the armies to attack Lu; for many months could not take it; many in the army deserted.

entries.zh: 太祖怒甚，詔疏其罪，盡奪其官爵，委本郡以民戶係焉。
entries.en: The Founder was furious, published his crimes, stripped every rank, and bound him to his home prefecture as a common household.
entries.literal: The Founder was greatly enraged; an edict listed his crimes; stripped all ranks and titles; relegated to the prefecture as civilian household attachment.

entries.zh: 逾歲起之，復令領兵，亦無巨績可紀。
entries.en: A year later he was recalled to lead troops again, but still won no great fame.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was raised again, again ordered to lead troops—also no great achievement to record.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗因命將授鉞，謂左右曰：「李思安當敵果敢，無出其右者，然每遇藩方擇材，吾將用之，則敗聞必至，如是者二三矣，則知飛將數奇，前史豈虛言哉！」
entries.en: Once, as he gave axes to his generals, the Founder told his attendants: "Li Si'an is matchless in a fight, yet whenever I post him to a frontier command defeat follows—two or three times now. The old books were right about unlucky flying generals!"
entries.literal: The Founder once when appointing generals and granting axes said to those at his side: "Li Si'an facing the enemy is bold and decisive, none surpasses him; yet each time when a border region chooses talent I intend to use him, defeat news must arrive—so two or three times—then one knows the flying general's repeated odd fate; former histories were not empty words!"

entries.zh: 乾化元年秋，又以為相州刺史。
entries.en: In autumn of Qianhua 1 he was again made prefect of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: Qianhua 1 autumn, again made Xiangzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 思安自謂當擁旄仗鉞，及是殊不快意，但日循晏安，無意為政。
entries.en: Si'an had expected a military commission; bitterly disappointed, he idled in comfort and ignored government.
entries.literal: Si'an thought he ought to hold the banner and battle-axe; at this he was especially displeased; he only daily followed peaceful ease, with no mind for governing.

entries.zh: 及太祖北征，以候騎之誤，落然無所具，而復壁壘荒圮，帑廩空竭，太祖怒，貶柳州司戶，尋賜死於相州。
entries.en: On a northern campaign the Founder arrived unexpectedly; Si'an had nothing ready, his walls were broken, and his stores were bare. The Founder demoted him to Liuzhou registrar and soon had him executed at Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: When the Founder went north on campaign, because of scout error he was suddenly without all preparations; walls and fortifications in ruins, treasury empty; the Founder was angry, demoted to Liuzhou registrar, soon ordered to die at Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：開化元年丙午，至相州，刺史李思安不意帝猝至，落然無具，坐削官爵。
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: In Qianhua 1, on the bingwu day, the Emperor reached Xiangzhou; Prefect Li Si'an, caught unprepared, was stripped of rank on the spot.
entries.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: In Qianhua 1, on the bingwu day, [the emperor] arrived at Xiangzhou; Prefect Li Si’an did not expect the emperor’s sudden arrival and was utterly unprepared, for which he was demoted and stripped of rank.

entries.zh: 二年正月丁卯，帝至獲嘉，追思李思安去歲供饋有闕，貶柳州司戶，尋長流思安於崖州，賜死。）〉
entries.en: In the first month of the second year, dingmao day, at Huojia he recalled Si'an's short rations the year before, demoted him to Liuzhou registrar, then exiled him to Yazhou and ordered his death.)
entries.literal: Year 2 first month dingmao, the Emperor arrived at Huojia; recalling Li Si'an's last year provisions were lacking, demoted to Liuzhou registrar; soon exiled Si'an to Yazhou for life, ordered to die.)

entries.zh: 鄧季筠，宋州下邑人也。
entries.en: Deng Jiyun came from Xiayi in Songzhou.
entries.literal: Deng Jiyun was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou.

entries.zh: 少入黃巢軍，隸於太祖麾下。
entries.en: As a youth he joined Huang Chao and later entered the Founder's service.
entries.literal: In youth he entered Huang Chao's army; attached to the Founder's command.

entries.zh: 及太祖鎮汴，首署為牙將，主騎軍。
entries.en: When the Founder held Bian he made Jiyun a personal guard officer commanding the cavalry.
entries.literal: When the Founder held Bian he first appointed him as dental officer in charge of cavalry.

entries.zh: 伐鄆之役，生擒排陣將劉矯以獻。
entries.en: In the Yan campaign he took the enemy battle-line general Liu Jiao alive and presented him.
entries.literal: In the Yan campaign he personally captured battle-array general Liu Jiao and presented him.

entries.zh: 唐大順初，唐帝命丞相張浚伐太原，太祖奉詔出師，西至高平，與晉人接戰，軍既不利，季筠為晉人所擒。
entries.en: Early in Dashun of Tang, the emperor sent Chancellor Zhang Jun against Taiyuan; the Founder marched west to Gaoping, was beaten, and Jiyun was captured by the Jin.
entries.literal: Tang Dashun early, Tang Emperor ordered Chancellor Zhang Jun to attack Taiyuan; the Founder received edict and marched; west to Gaoping, engaged Jin troops; the army was unfavorable; Jiyun was captured by Jin men.

entries.zh: 克用見之甚喜，釋縛，待以賓禮，俄典戎事。
entries.en: Keyong was delighted, freed him, entertained him as a guest, and soon put him in charge of troops.
entries.literal: Keyong saw him and was greatly pleased, released his bonds, treated him as guest; soon put in charge of military affairs.

entries.zh: 季筠在並門凡四稔。
entries.en: Jiyun stayed at Taiyuan four years.
entries.literal: Jiyun at Bing Gate altogether four years.

entries.zh: 景福二年，晉軍攻邢台，季筠領偏師預其役，將及邢，邢人陣於郊，兩軍酣戰之際，季筠出陣，飛馬來歸；
entries.en: In Jingfu 2 the Jin besieged Xingtai; Jiyun led a flank corps; as the armies fought outside Xing he broke from the line and galloped back to the Founder;
entries.literal: Jingfu 2, Jin army attacked Xingtai; Jiyun led flank army sharing the campaign; about to reach Xing; Xing men arrayed at the suburbs; as the two armies fought hotly Jiyun left the line, on flying horse came back;

entries.zh: 太祖大加獎歎，賞賚甚厚。
entries.en: The Founder praised him lavishly and gave rich rewards.
entries.literal: The Founder greatly praised and rewarded him richly.

entries.zh: 時初置廳子都，最為親軍，命季筠主之，旋改統親騎，又遷將中軍。
entries.en: He then formed the Hall Sons—the Founder's closest guard—and put Jiyun in command, soon made him head of the intimate cavalry and then of the central army.
entries.literal: At the time first established the Hall Sons army, most intimate troops; ordered Jiyun to command it; soon changed to command intimate cavalry; again promoted to command center army.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，奏授登州刺史，下車稱理。
entries.en: In Tianyou 3 he became prefect of Dengzhou and governed well from the day he arrived.
entries.literal: Tianyou 3, memorialized as Dengzhou prefect; on taking office he was praised for good governance.

entries.zh: 登州舊無羅城，及季筠至郡，率丁壯以築之，民甚安之，因相與立碑以頌其績。
entries.en: Dengzhou had no outer wall; Jiyun raised labor to build one, the people were secure, and they set up a stele to praise him.
entries.literal: Dengzhou formerly had no outer wall; when Jiyun reached the prefecture he led strong young men to build it; the people were very at ease; therefore together they erected a stele to praise his merit.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，改鄭州刺史，尋主兵於河中，為都指揮使。
entries.en: At the founding of Liang he became prefect of Zhengzhou, then commanded the army at Hezhong as overall commander.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, changed to Zhengzhou prefect; soon commanded troops at Hezhong as overall commander.

entries.zh: 時並人寇平陽，季筠接戰於洪洞，大克，拜華州防禦使。
entries.en: When the Jin raided Pingyang he routed them at Hongdong and was made defense commissioner of Huazhou.
entries.literal: At the time Jin men raided Pingyang; Jiyun engaged at Hongdong and greatly overcame; made Huazhou defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 又繼領龍驤等諸軍騎士，累官至檢校司空。
entries.en: He later led the Longxiang and other cavalry corps and rose to Acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Again successively commanded Longxiang and other army cavalry; repeatedly rose to Acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 柏鄉之役，季筠臨陣前卻，太祖亦未之罪。
entries.en: At Bai Bridge Jiyun pulled back in the fighting, yet the Founder did not punish him.
entries.literal: At the Battle of Bai Bridge, Jiyun before the battle drew back; the Founder also did not blame him.

entries.zh: 乾化二年春，太祖親伐鎮、定，駐於相州，因閱馬，怒其馬瘦，與魏博軍校何令稠、陳令勳同斬於纛下。
entries.en: In spring of Qianhua 2 the Founder attacked Zhen and Ding and halted at Xiangzhou; reviewing the horses, he found them lean and beheaded Jiyun with the Weibo officers He Lingchou and Chen Lingxun beneath his banner.
entries.literal: Qianhua 2 spring, the Founder in person attacked Zhen and Ding, halted at Xiangzhou; because of reviewing horses he was angry their horses were thin and with Weibo army officers He Lingchou and Chen Lingxun alike cut them beneath the banner.

entries.zh: 黃文靖，金鄉人。
entries.en: Huang Wenjing came from Jinxiang.
entries.literal: Huang Wenjing was a native of Jinxiang.

entries.zh: 少附於黃巢黨中，巢敗，歸於太祖，累署牙職，繼遷諸軍指揮使。
entries.en: He had followed Huang Chao; after Chao's fall he joined the Founder, served in the guard corps, and rose to army commander.
entries.literal: In youth he attached to Huang Chao's party; when Chao was defeated returned to the Founder; repeatedly appointed dental posts; successively promoted to army commanders.

entries.zh: 從太祖南平巢、蔡，北定兗、鄆，皆有功。
entries.en: He fought south against Chao and Cai and north in Yan and Yun, winning merit in each.
entries.literal: Following the Founder south pacified Chao and Cai, north settled Yan and Yun—all had merit.

entries.zh: 唐大順中，佐葛從周送朱崇節入潞。
entries.en: In Dashun of Tang he helped Ge Congzhou escort Zhu Chongjie into Lu.
entries.literal: Tang Dashun, assisted Ge Congzhou in escorting Zhu Chongjie into Lu.

entries.zh: 會晉軍十餘萬近逼垣寨，文靖慮孤軍難守，乃與葛從周啟出師，文靖為殿，命矢刃皆外向，持重而還，晉人不敢逼。
entries.en: When more than a hundred thousand Jin troops pressed the camp, Wenjing and Ge Congzhou slipped out by night; Wenjing covered the rear with weapons turned outward and withdrew in good order while the Jin held back.
entries.literal: Jin army over a hundred thousand pressed near the stockade; Wenjing feared lone army hard to hold; with Ge Congzhou secretly led troops out; Wenjing as rearguard ordered arrow blades all face outward, moved deliberately and returned; Jin men dared not press.

entries.zh: 其年冬，與康懷英渡淮，入壽春之境，下安豐、霍丘，至光州而還。
entries.en: That winter he crossed the Huai with Kang Huaiying, took Anfeng and Huoqiu in Shouzhou, reached Guangzhou, and returned.
entries.literal: That winter with Kang Huaiying crossed Huai, entered Shouchun border, took Anfeng and Huoqiu, reached Guangzhou and returned.

entries.zh: 光化初，晉將李嗣昭、周德威寇於山東，文靖佐葛從周統大軍禦之。
entries.en: Early in Guanghua, when Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei raided Shandong, Wenjing joined Ge Congzhou in commanding the main army against them.
entries.literal: Guanghua early, Jin generals Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei raided Shandong; Wenjing assisted Ge Congzhou in commanding great army to resist.

entries.zh: 至沙河，敗晉軍五千餘騎，遂逐之，越張公橋乃止。
entries.en: At Shahe he routed more than five thousand Jin horsemen and pursued them past Zhanggong Bridge before halting.
entries.literal: Reached Shahe, defeated Jin army over five thousand cavalry; pursued them past Zhanggong Bridge then stopped.

entries.zh: 後旬日，復與晉人戰於邢州之北，擒蕃將賁金鐵、慕容藤、李存建等百餘人，奪馬數千匹。
entries.en: Ten days later he fought again north of Xingzhou, capturing the Tatar generals Ben Jintie, Murong Teng, Li Cunjian, and more than a hundred others, with thousands of horses.
entries.literal: Ten days later again fought Jin at north of Xingzhou; captured Tatar generals Ben Jintie, Murong Teng, Li Cunjian and over a hundred men; seized horses several thousand.

entries.zh: 尋以功表授檢校左僕射、耀州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was memorialized Acting Left Vice Director and prefect of Yaozhou.
entries.literal: Soon for merit memorialized Acting Left Vice Director and Yaozhou prefect.

entries.zh: 天祐二年春，命佐楊師厚深入淮甸，越壽春，侵廬江，軍至大獨山，遇淮夷，殺五千餘眾，振旅而還。
entries.en: In spring of Tianyou 2 he aided Yang Shihou deep into the Huai, passed Shouchun, raided Lujiang, reached Great Solitary Mountain, killed more than five thousand Huai fighters, and returned in triumph.
entries.literal: Tianyou 2 spring, ordered to assist Yang Shihou in deep penetration Huai region; past Shouchun, invaded Lujiang; army reached Great Solitary Mountain; met Huai barbarians, killed over five thousand; army returned in triumph.

entries.zh: 改蔡州刺史，加檢校司空，又遷潁州刺史。
entries.en: He became prefect of Cai with Acting Minister of Works, then moved to Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Changed to Cai prefect; added Acting Minister of Works; again moved to Ying prefect.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，復為蔡州刺史，入為左神武統軍，又改左龍驤使。
entries.en: At the Liang founding he was again prefect of Cai, then Left Divine Martial commander and Left Dragon Flying commissioner.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, again Cai prefect; entered as Left Divine Martial overall commander; again changed to Left Dragon Flying commissioner.

entries.zh: 乾化元年，從太祖北征，因閱馬得罪，命斬之。
entries.en: In Qianhua 1 he joined the northern campaign; the horse review angered the Founder and he was executed.
entries.literal: Qianhua 1, followed Founder north campaign; because of horse review offended; ordered executed.

entries.zh: 文靖驍果善戰，諸將皆惜之。
entries.en: Wenjing was a fierce fighter whom every general regretted losing.
entries.literal: Wenjing was fierce and good in battle; all generals prized him.

entries.zh: 胡規，兗州人。
entries.en: Hu Gui came from Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Hu Gui was a native of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 初事朱瑾為中軍都校。
entries.en: He first served Zhu Jin as a central-army commandant.
entries.literal: At first he served Zhu Jin as central-army commandant.

entries.zh: 兗州平，署為宣武軍都虞候。
entries.en: After Yanzhou fell he was made chief adjutant of the Xuanwu Army.
entries.literal: When Yanzhou was pacified, he was appointed Xuanwu Army chief adjutant.

entries.zh: 佐葛從周伐鎮、定，從張存敬收晉、絳，皆有功，署為河中都虞候，榷鹽務。
entries.en: He helped Ge Congzhou against Zhen and Ding and Zhang Cunjing against Jin and Jiang, winning merit each time; he was then made chief adjutant of Hezhong and put in charge of the salt monopoly.
entries.literal: He aided Ge Congzhou in attacking Zhen and Ding, followed Zhang Cunjing in taking Jin and Jiang—all with merit—and was appointed chief adjutant of Hezhong and put in charge of the salt monopoly.

entries.zh: 天復中，太祖迎駕至岐下，以規權知洽州。
entries.en: During Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed the emperor to Qixia, he made Gui acting prefect of Qiazhou.
entries.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed the imperial carriage to Qixia, he made Gui acting prefect of Qiazhou.

entries.zh: 昭宗還長安，詔授皇城使。
entries.en: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, an edict made him imperial-city commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, an edict appointed him imperial-city commissioner.

entries.zh: 及東遷，以為御營使。
entries.en: When the court moved east, he was made imperial-camp commissioner.
entries.literal: When the court moved east, he was made imperial-camp commissioner.

entries.zh: 駕至洛，授內園莊宅使。
entries.en: When the emperor reached Luoyang, he was made commissioner of the inner gardens and estates.
entries.literal: When the carriage reached Luoyang, he was appointed commissioner of the inner gardens and estates.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，佐李周彝討相州，獨當州之一面，頗以功聞，軍還，權知耀州事。
entries.en: In Tianyou 3 he aided Li Zhouyi at Xiangzhou, holding one sector of the siege alone and winning fame; after the campaign he acted as prefect of Yaozhou.
entries.literal: In Tianyou 3 he aided Li Zhouyi against Xiangzhou, alone holding one face of the prefecture, and won considerable fame; when the army returned he was acting prefect of Yaozhou.

entries.zh: 明年，討滄州，為諸軍壕寨使。
entries.en: The next year, in the campaign against Cangzhou, he served as trench-and-camp commissioner for the combined armies.
entries.literal: The next year, campaigning against Cangzhou, he was trench-and-camp commissioner for the armies.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，除右羽林統軍，尋佐劉鄩統兵收潼關，擒劉知浣獻之，乃以為右龍虎統軍兼侍衛指揮使。
entries.en: At the Liang founding he was made Right Feathered Forest commander; he soon helped Liu Yan recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and commander of the palace guard.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, Gui was made Right Feathered Forest commander; soon he aided Liu Yan in leading troops to recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and also commander of the palace guard.

entries.zh: 乾化元年，詔修洛河堤堰，軍士因之斬伐百姓園林太甚，河南尹張宗奭奏之，規得罪，賜死。
entries.en: In Qianhua 1 an edict ordered repairs on the Luo River dikes; soldiers used the work to strip commoners' gardens and groves, and Henan governor Zhang Zongshi reported it; Gui was condemned and put to death.
entries.literal: In Qianhua 1 an edict ordered repair of the Luo River dikes; soldiers used this to cut down commoners' gardens and groves far too much; Henan governor Zhang Zongshi memorialized it; Gui was found guilty and ordered to die.

entries.zh: 李讜，河中臨晉人。
entries.en: Li Dang came from Linjin in Hezhong.
entries.literal: Li Dang was a native of Linjin in Hezhong.

entries.zh: 少時遊秦、雍間，為人勇悍多力，甚有氣誼。
entries.en: In youth he wandered Qin and Yong; bold, fierce, and strong, he was famed for loyalty among friends.
entries.literal: In youth he roamed Qin and Yong regions; as a man brave, fierce, and very strong, greatly had chivalrous friendship.

entries.zh: 唐廣明初，黃巢陷長安，讜遂得仕於其間。
entries.en: Early in Guangming of Tang, when Huang Chao took Chang'an, Dang entered his service.
entries.literal: Tang Guangming early, Huang Chao took Chang'an; Dang then obtained office among them.

entries.zh: 巢以讜為內樞密使，蓋讜曾委質於宦者，出入於宮禁間，巢以此用焉。
entries.en: Chao made him inner privy commissioner, for Dang had once served eunuchs and knew the palace—Chao used him for that.
entries.literal: Chao made Dang inner privy commissioner; because Dang had once placed himself under eunuchs and went in and out of palace confines—Chao used him thus.

entries.zh: 其後巢軍既敗，讜乃束身歸於太祖，署為左德勝騎軍都將。
entries.en: After Chao's defeat Dang surrendered to the Founder and was made commander of the Left Victorious Virtue cavalry.
entries.literal: After Chao's army was defeated Dang bound himself and returned to the Founder; appointed Left Victorious Virtue cavalry commander.

entries.zh: 從太祖討蔡賊，頗立軍功。
entries.en: He followed the Founder against the Cai rebels and won solid merit.
entries.literal: Following the Founder against Cai bandits, considerably established military merit.

entries.zh: 及東伐兗、鄆，以所部士伍俘獲甚眾，改元從騎將，表授檢校右僕射。
entries.en: In the eastern campaigns against Yan and Yun his men took many prisoners; he became a yuancong cavalry general and Acting Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: And east attacking Yan and Yun, with his command's soldiers captured very many; changed to yuancong cavalry general; memorialized Acting Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 郴王友裕領兵攻澤州，時太祖駐大軍於盟津，乃令讜將兵越太行，授以籌謀。
entries.en: When Prince of Chen Youyu besieged Zezhou the Founder camped at Meng Ford and sent Dang across the Taihang with full discretion over the plan.
entries.literal: Prince of Chen Youyu led troops to attack Zezhou; the Founder then stationed great army at Meng Ford; then ordered Dang to lead troops across Taihang; entrusted with planning.

entries.zh: 讜頗違節度，久而無功。
entries.en: Dang disobeyed orders and after a long while had nothing to show.
entries.literal: Dang quite violated command; for long had no merit.

entries.zh: 太祖遣追還，廷責其罪，戮之於河橋。
entries.en: The Founder recalled him, rebuked him at court, and executed him at He Bridge.
entries.literal: The Founder sent to recall him; at court blamed his crime; executed him at He Bridge.

entries.zh: 李重胤，宋州下邑人。
entries.en: Li Chongyin came from Xiayi in Songzhou.
entries.literal: Li Chongyin was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou.

entries.zh: 狀貌雄武，初在黃巢黨中，推為剛鷙。
entries.en: Bold and martial in bearing, he was first acclaimed among Huang Chao's followers as fierce and harsh.
entries.literal: In bearing he was bold and martial; at first among Huang Chao's party he was acclaimed as fierce and harsh.

entries.zh: 唐中和四年五月，同尚讓、李讜等率眾至繁台，與太祖之軍相拒。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Zhonghe 4 he joined Shang Rang, Li Dang, and others at Fantai to face the Founder's army.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Zhonghe 4 of Tang, together with Shang Rang, Li Dang, and others he led masses to Fantai and faced the Founder's army.

entries.zh: 及巢寇漸衰，乃率眾來降。
entries.en: As Chao's cause waned, he led his men to surrender.
entries.literal: When Chao's bandits gradually declined, he then led the masses to surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖素識之，拔用不次，署為先鋒步軍都頭。
entries.en: The Founder already knew him and promoted him out of turn, making him vanguard infantry commander.
entries.literal: The Founder had long known him and raised him out of turn, appointing him vanguard infantry commander.

entries.zh: 與胡真援河陽，逼懷州。
entries.en: With Hu Zhen he relieved Heyang and pressed Huai prefecture.
entries.literal: With Hu Zhen he relieved Heyang and pressed Huai prefecture.

entries.zh: 重胤以部下兵突之，射中蕃將安休休。
entries.en: Chongyin charged with his own troops and shot the foreign general An Xiuxiu.
entries.literal: Chongyin with his command's troops charged them and shot the foreign general An Xiuxiu.

entries.zh: 又令與李讜率騎軍至陝，應接郭言，回次澠池，破賊帥黃花子之眾，改滑州夾馬指揮使。
entries.en: He was again ordered with Li Dang to lead cavalry to Shan to link with Guo Yan; on the return march he stopped at Mianchi and broke the band of the rebel chief Huang Huazi, then became Jiamma commander at Huazhou.
entries.literal: He was again ordered with Li Dang to lead cavalry to Shan to link with Guo Yan; returning he halted at Mianchi and broke the band of the rebel chief Huang Huazi; he was changed to Huazhou Jiamma commander.

entries.zh: 蔡賊圍汴，重胤以步兵攻下三寨，擄獲甚多。
entries.en: When Cai rebels besieged Bian, Chongyin's infantry took three camps and captured many prisoners.
entries.literal: When Cai bandits besieged Bian, Chongyin with infantry stormed three camps and captured very many.

entries.zh: 太祖大舉伐宗權，俾重胤以滑兵為先鋒。
entries.en: When the Founder launched a major campaign against Zongquan, he put Chongyin and the Huazhou troops in the vanguard.
entries.literal: When the Founder launched a great campaign against Zongquan, he had Chongyin lead the Huazhou troops as vanguard.

entries.zh: 及東討徐州，下豐、蕭二邑，轉右廂馬步軍指揮使。
entries.en: In the eastern campaign against Xuzhou he took Feng and Xiao and was made commander of the Right Wing horse-and-foot corps.
entries.literal: When he campaigned east against Xuzhou and took the districts of Feng and Xiao, he was transferred to Right Wing horse-and-foot commander.

entries.zh: 大順元年秋，從郴王友裕收澤州，與晉軍戰於馬牢川，王師敗績，回守河陽。
entries.en: In autumn of Dashun 1 he followed Prince of Chen Youyu to recover Zezhou; at Malao River the imperial army was beaten by the Jin and fell back to Heyang.
entries.literal: In autumn of Dashun 1 he followed Prince of Chen Youyu in recovering Zezhou; the imperial army fought Jin forces at Malao River, was defeated, and withdrew to hold Heyang.

entries.zh: 太祖謂諸將曰：「李讜、重胤違我節度，不能立功，頗辜任使。」
entries.en: The Founder told his generals: "Li Dang and Chongyin disobeyed my orders and won no merit—they have badly failed the trust I placed in them."
entries.literal: The Founder told the generals: "Li Dang and Chongyin violated my command and could not establish merit—they have quite betrayed the trust placed in them."

entries.zh: 於是與李讜並戮於河橋。
entries.en: He and Li Dang were then executed together at He Bridge.
entries.literal: Thereupon he and Li Dang were together executed at He Bridge.

entries.zh: 範居實，絳州翼城人。
entries.en: Fan Jushi came from Yicheng in Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Fan Jushi was a native of Yicheng in Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 事太祖，初為隊將，從討巢、蔡有功。
entries.en: Serving the Founder, he began as a squad commander and won merit in the campaigns against Chao and Cai.
entries.literal: Serving the Founder, at first he was a squad commander; following campaigns against Chao and Cai he had merit.

entries.zh: 又從朱珍收滑州，改左廂都虞候。
entries.en: He followed Zhu Zhen in recovering Huazhou and was made Left Wing chief adjutant.
entries.literal: He again followed Zhu Zhen in recovering Huazhou and was changed to Left Wing chief adjutant.

entries.zh: 預破兗、鄆功。
entries.en: He shared in the victories over Yan and Yun.
entries.literal: He shared in the merit of breaking Yan and Yun.

entries.zh: 遷感義都頭、鄭州馬軍指揮使。
entries.en: He became Ganyi squad chief and cavalry commander at Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Ganyi squad chief and Zhengzhou cavalry commander.

entries.zh: 幽州劉仁恭舉眾南下，寇魏郡北，居實與葛從周、張存敬率兵救魏，大破幽、滄之眾於內黃。
entries.en: When Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched south and raided north of Wei, Jushi joined Ge Congzhou and Zhang Cunjing to relieve Wei and routed the You and Cang armies at Neihuang.
entries.literal: When Youzhou's Liu Rengong raised masses and marched south, raiding north of Wei commandery, Jushi with Ge Congzhou and Zhang Cunjing led troops to rescue Wei and greatly defeated the You and Cang forces at Neihuang.

entries.zh: 太祖迎昭宗於岐下，以居實為河中馬軍都指揮使。
entries.en: When the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qixia, he made Jushi cavalry commander of Hezhong.
entries.literal: When the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qixia, he made Jushi Hezhong cavalry commander.

entries.zh: 及昭宗還京，賜迎鑾毅勇功臣，遙領錦州刺史，又遷左龍驤馬軍都指揮使。
entries.en: When Zhaozong returned to the capital, he received the title Resolute and Brave Merit Lord of the Imperial Welcome, held Jing prefecture in absentia, and was made Left Dragon Flying cavalry commander.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned to the capital, he was granted the title Resolute and Brave Merit Lord of the Imperial Welcome, held Jing prefecture in absentia, and was again transferred to Left Dragon Flying cavalry commander.

entries.zh: 從征淮南回，改登州刺史，轉左神勇軍使。
entries.en: After the Huainan campaign he became prefect of Dengzhou and then commissioner of the Left Divine Valor Guard.
entries.literal: Returning from the Huainan campaign, he was changed to Dengzhou prefect and transferred to Left Divine Valor commissioner.

entries.zh: 開平元年，用軍於潞州，命居實統軍以解澤州之圍。
entries.en: In Kaiping 1, when troops were deployed at Luzhou, he was ordered to command an army to lift the siege of Zezhou.
entries.literal: In Kaiping 1, when troops were deployed at Luzhou, Jushi was ordered to command an army to lift the siege of Zezhou.

entries.zh: 授耀州刺史，令以郡兵屯固鎮，尋除澤州刺史。
entries.en: He was made prefect of Yaozhou and ordered to station his troops at Guzhen; soon he was transferred to prefect of Zezhou.
entries.literal: He was appointed Yaozhou prefect and ordered to station the prefecture's troops at Guzhen; soon he was removed to Zezhou prefect.

entries.zh: 居實拳勇善戰，頗立軍功，在郡以戎備不理，詔追赴闕，暴其玩寇之罪而斬之。
entries.en: Jushi was a fierce fighter who won solid merit, but as prefect he neglected defense; recalled to court, he was condemned for treating the enemy lightly and executed.
entries.literal: Jushi was fierce in fist and brave in battle and considerably established military merit; in the prefecture he neglected military readiness; an edict recalled him to court, exposed his crime of treating the enemy lightly, and executed him.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：叔琮而下，咸以鷹犬之才，適遇雲龍之會，勤勞王室，踐履將壇，然俱不得其死，豈不惜哉！
entries.en: The historian writes: From Shuzong on, these men had the talent of hawks and hounds and met a dragon in the clouds; they toiled for the throne and stood on the general's dais—yet none died in his bed. How pitiable!
entries.literal: The historiographer says: From Shuzong down, all with hawk-and-hound talent met the cloud-dragon's conjunction; diligently served the royal house, trod the general's altar—yet all did not obtain their death; how is it not pitiable!

entries.zh: 得非鳥盡弓藏，理當如是耶？
entries.en: When the birds are gone, does not every lord put away his bow? Is that not fate?
entries.literal: Is it not that when birds are gone bows are stored—reason ought to be thus?

entries.zh: 將梁祖之雄猜，無漢高之大度歟？
entries.en: Was the Liang Founder's jealous courage so far below Han Gaozu's breadth of mind?
entries.literal: Was the Liang Founder's heroic suspiciousness without Han Gaozu's great magnanimity?

entries.zh: 乃知自古帝王，能保全功臣者，唯光武一人而已矣。
entries.en: So of all emperors since antiquity, only Guangwu truly kept his merit ministers safe.
entries.literal: Thus one knows from ancient emperors and kings, those who could wholly preserve meritorious ministers were only Guangwu alone!

entries.zh: 語曰：「弑父與君，亦不從也」，而叔琮、友恭從之，何也？
entries.en: The Analects says, "One must not obey even a father or lord in murder"—yet Shuzong and Yougong obeyed. Why?
entries.literal: The saying goes: "To kill father and lord—yet also do not obey"; yet Shuzong and Yougong followed—why?

entries.zh: 既為盜蹠所嗾，豈免成濟之誅，臨終之言，益彰其醜也。
entries.en: Urged on by a Zhi, they could only share Cheng Ji's fate; their dying words exposed their shame all the more.
entries.literal: Already driven by robber Zhi—how escape Cheng Ji punishment; words at life's end all the more reveal their ugliness.

entries.zh: 謝瞳，字子明，福州人。
entries.en: Xie Tong, who styled himself Ziming, came from Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Xie Tong, styled Ziming, was a man of Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 唐咸通末舉進士，因留長安，三歲不中第。
entries.en: Late in Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; for three years he failed to place.

entries.zh: 廣明初，黃巢陷長安，遂投跡於太祖，洎居門下，未嘗一日不在左右。
entries.en: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an in the first year of Guangming, Tong entered the Founder's service and from that day was never far from his side.
entries.literal: Early Guangming, Huang Chao took Chang'an; he then cast his lot with the Founder, and once under his gate never a day was absent from his side.

entries.zh: 及太祖據同州，遂署右職。
entries.en: Once the Founder held Tongzhou, he gave Tong a chief post on his staff.
entries.literal: When the Founder held Tong Prefecture, he then appointed him to a right-hand post.

entries.zh: 其年秋，太祖與河中交戰，再不利，連上章請兵於巢，偽右軍都尉孟楷抑而不進。
entries.en: That autumn, twice beaten fighting Hezhong, the Founder pleaded again and again to Chao for reinforcements, but the rebel Right Army commissioner Meng Kai blocked every dispatch.
entries.literal: That autumn the Founder fought Hezhong and twice met ill fortune; repeatedly he sent memorials asking troops of Chao, but the false Right Army commissioner Meng Kai suppressed them and they did not advance.

entries.zh: 瞳揣太祖有擇福意，乃進說曰：「黃家以數十萬之師，值唐朝久安，人不習戰，因利乘便，遂下兩京。
entries.en: Reading the Founder's wish to change sides, Tong urged him: "Huang's army of hundreds of thousands took both capitals only because the Tang had grown soft in long peace and men had forgotten war.
entries.literal: Tong gauged that the Founder intended to choose fortune, and thereupon advanced counsel, saying: "The Huang house with an army of hundreds of thousands, encountering the Tang's long peace and men unpractised in war, rode advantage and seized both capitals.

entries.zh: 然始竊偽號，任用已失其所。
entries.en: Yet the moment they claimed an emperor's title, every appointment went wrong.
entries.literal: Yet having first stolen a false title, their appointments already miss their place.

entries.zh: 今將軍勇冠三軍，力戰於外，而孟楷專務壅蔽，奏章不達，下為庸才所製，無獨斷之明，破亡之兆必矣。
entries.en: You fight abroad with unmatched courage while Meng Kai chokes every letter to court; mediocrities below him run the show, and without firm command ruin is certain.
entries.literal: Now the general's courage crowns the three armies, fighting hard abroad, yet Meng Kai devotes himself to blocking; memorials do not arrive, below he is constrained by mediocrities and lacks the clarity of sole decision—the omen of ruin is sure.

entries.zh: 況土德未厭，外兵四集，漕運波注，日以收復為名，惟將軍察之。」
entries.en: Heaven's mandate still favors the Tang: armies close from every quarter, grain fleets pour in, and every day another force marches to restore the throne—think on that, General."
entries.literal: Moreover earth's virtue is not yet spent; armies gather from four sides, grain-ships pour in waves, day by day they march under the name of restoration—only let the general consider it."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「我意素決，爾又如是，復何疑哉！」
entries.en: The Founder replied, "My mind was made long ago; hearing you say the same, what doubt could remain?"
entries.literal: The Founder said: "My mind was long settled; you speak thus too—what doubt remains!"

entries.zh: 翌日，遂定策，戮偽監軍使，悉眾歸順於河中。
entries.en: Next day the plan was fixed: the false inspector was killed, and the whole army went over to Hezhong.
entries.literal: The next day he settled strategy, killed the false army supervisor, and with all his host submitted to Hezhong.

entries.zh: 王重榮表瞳為檢校屯田員外郎，賜緋，令奉表於蜀。
entries.en: Wang Chongrong made Tong acting Director of the Palace Farms, dressed him in crimson, and sent him to present the submission to Shu.
entries.literal: Wang Chongrong memorialized Tong as acting Director of Palace Farms, granted him crimson robes, and ordered him to present a memorial in Shu.

entries.zh: 唐僖宗大悅，召入顧問，錫賚甚厚，以功授朝散大夫、太子率更令，賜紫，為陵州刺史。
entries.en: Xizong rejoiced, called him in for counsel, heaped gifts upon him, and for his service made him Grand Master of the Palace and Director of the Crown Prince's water clocks, clothed him in purple, and gave him Lingzhou.
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Xizong was greatly pleased, summoned him for consultation, bestowed gifts very generously, and for merit appointed him Grand Master of the Palace, Crown Prince's Director of Water Clocks, granted purple, and made him prefect of Ling.

entries.zh: 治郡一歲，改檢校右散騎常侍、通州刺史。
entries.en: After one year as prefect he was promoted to acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and made governor of Tongzhou.
entries.literal: He governed the prefecture one year, then was changed to acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and prefect of Tong.

entries.zh: 在任四考，頗有政績。
entries.en: Four terms in office won him a solid record of good rule.
entries.literal: In office through four evaluations, he had quite administrative achievement.

entries.zh: 秋罷，詣蜀行在，太祖遣人迎之。
entries.en: When autumn brought his term to an end, he went to the imperial camp in Shu, and the Founder sent escorts to meet him.
entries.literal: Autumn dismissed, he went to the Shu traveling court; the Founder sent men to welcome him.

entries.zh: 龍紀二年，至東京，勞徠彌厚，賜第墅各一區，錢千緡，表為亳州團練使兼太清宮副使，加檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: In Longji 2 he reached the Eastern Capital; the Founder received him with exceptional honors—a mansion, a country villa, a thousand strings of cash—and memorialized him Bozhou regimental commissioner and deputy head of the Grand Pure Palace, with acting rank as Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Longji year 2, he reached the Eastern Capital; rewards and comfort were thicker still, granted one ward each of mansion and villa, a thousand strings of cash, memorialized as Bozhou regimental commissioner and vice-director of the Grand Pure Palace, added acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 是年冬，太祖征淮南，過郡，因求侍府幕，表為宣義軍節度副使，充兩使留後。
entries.en: That winter, as the Founder marched on Huainan and passed through his circuit, Tong asked to join his staff and was made vice-commissioner of the Xuanyi army and regent for both civil and military commissioners.
entries.literal: That winter the Founder campaigned against Huainan, passed through his prefecture; he therefore asked to serve in the commandery staff, was memorialized as vice-commissioner of the Xuanyi army and acting regent for both commissioners.

entries.zh: 瞳在滑十三年，部內增戶約五萬，益兵數千人，累遷至大中大夫、檢校右僕射，卒於滑。
entries.en: Thirteen years at Hua added fifty thousand households and several thousand troops to his circuit; he rose to Grand Master and acting Right Vice Director, and died there.
entries.literal: Tong was at Hua thirteen years; within his circuit households increased by about fifty thousand, troops increased by several thousand; he rose in succession to Grand Master and acting Right Vice Director, and died at Hua.

entries.zh: 開平初，追贈司徒。
entries.en: At the opening of Kaiping he was posthumously named Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Early Kaiping he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 劉捍，開封人。
entries.en: Liu Han came from Kaifeng.
entries.literal: Liu Han, a man of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 父行仙，宣武軍大將。
entries.en: His father Xingxian was a senior general of the Xuanyi army.
entries.literal: His father Xingxian was a great general of the Xuanyi army.

entries.zh: 捍少為牙職，太祖初鎮夷門，以捍聰敏，擢副典客。
entries.en: As a youth Han served in the yamen staff; when the Founder first took Bian he made the quick-witted Han his deputy master of ceremonies.
entries.literal: Han in youth was a yamen staffer; when the Founder first held Yimen he because Han was clever promoted him deputy master of ceremonies.

entries.zh: 唐中和四年夏，太祖以朱珍為淄州刺史，令收兵於淄、青間，命捍監其兵，路逢大敵，皆破之。
entries.en: Summer of Zhonghe 4, the Founder sent Zhu Zhen to gather troops between Zi and Qing with Han overseeing his force; every major foe they met was defeated.
entries.literal: Summer, Tang Zhonghe year 4, the Founder made Zhu Zhen prefect of Zi and ordered him to gather troops between Zi and Qing; he ordered Han to supervise his troops; on the road they met great enemies and all were broken.

entries.zh: 入博昌，獲精兵三萬以歸。
entries.en: At Bochang they took thirty thousand picked troops back with them.
entries.literal: Entering Bochang, he obtained elite troops thirty thousand and returned.

entries.zh: 四月，合大軍敗蔡賊秦宗賢數萬眾於汴西。
entries.en: In the fourth month the combined army routed tens of thousands of Qin Zongxian's Cai rebels west of Bian.
entries.literal: Fourth month, joining the great army he defeated the Cai bandit Qin Zongxian's host of tens of thousands west of Bian.

entries.zh: 文德元年十一月，蔡將申叢折宗權足，納款於太祖，使捍奏其事，加兼御史大夫。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Wende 1 the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot and surrendered; Han carried word of it to the Founder and received concurrent rank as Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Wende year 1, eleventh month, the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot, submitted to the Founder; he had Han report the affair and added him concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 光化三年六月，太祖北伐鎮、定，至常山，而王钅容危懾，送款於太祖，命捍入壁門傳諭。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Guanghua 3 the Founder marched north against Zhen and Ding; at Changshan a terrified Wang Rong submitted, and the Founder sent Han through the barbican to announce terms.
entries.literal: Guanghua year 3, sixth month, the Founder north campaigned against Zhen and Ding, reaching Changshan; Wang Rong in peril and fear sent submission to the Founder, and ordered Han to enter the barbican gate to proclaim the message.

entries.zh: 時兩軍未整，守門者戈戟千匝，捍馳騎而入，竟達其命。
entries.en: While both armies were still unprepared, spears ringed the gate a thousand deep; Han rode straight through and carried out his orders.
entries.literal: At that time the two armies were not yet arrayed; gate guards with spears and halberds ringed a thousandfold; Han galloped in on horseback and at last delivered his charge.

entries.zh: 又移師以攻中山，至懷德驛，大破定人五萬眾，王處直乞降，捍復單馬入州，安撫而回。
entries.en: He marched on Zhongshan next; at Huaidi post fifty thousand men of Ding were shattered; Wang Chuzhi sued for peace; Han rode in alone again to calm the city and came back.
entries.literal: Again he moved troops to attack Zhongshan; reaching Huaidi post, he greatly defeated Ding's fifty thousand; Wang Chuzhi begged surrender; Han again entered the prefecture alone on horseback, pacified, and returned.

entries.zh: 太祖迎昭宗於岐下，以捍為親軍指揮。
entries.en: When the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qi's walls, he made Han commander of his personal guard.
entries.literal: The Founder welcomed Zhaozong below Qi and made Han commander of the personal army.

entries.zh: 天復三年正月，宋文通令客將郭啟奇使於太祖，命捍復命。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianfu 3, Song Wentong sent his guest-officer Guo Qiqi to the Founder with Han as the envoy to reply.
entries.literal: Tianfu year 3, first month, Song Wentong ordered the guest-officer Guo Qiqi as envoy to the Founder and ordered Han to answer the mission.

entries.zh: 昭宗聞其至，即召見，詢東兵之事，仍以錦服、銀鞍勒馬賜之。
entries.en: Zhaozong summoned him at once, questioned him on the eastern armies, and gave him brocade robes and a horse with silver saddle and bridle.
entries.literal: Zhaozong hearing he had arrived at once summoned him, asked about eastern army affairs, and also bestowed brocade robes and a silver-saddled bridled horse.

entries.zh: 翌日，授光祿大夫、檢校司空、登州刺史。
entries.en: Next day he received Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Sikong, and the prefecture of Deng.
entries.literal: The next day he was granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Sikong, and made prefect of Deng.

entries.zh: 昭宗還京，改常州刺史，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。
entries.en: When Zhaozong returned to the capital Han became prefect of Chang and received the title "Meritous Minister for Courageously Welcoming the Imperial Chariot."
entries.literal: Zhaozong returned to the capital, changed him to Chang prefect and gave the title Meritous Minister Courageously Welcoming the Imperial Chariot.

entries.zh: 四月，太祖伐王師範於青州，改左右長直都指揮使。
entries.en: In the fourth month, as the Founder attacked Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Han was made commander of the left and right Long-Straight guards.
entries.literal: Fourth month, the Founder campaigned against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou and changed him to commander of the left and right Long-Straight commands.

entries.zh: 天祐三年正月，授宋州刺史。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianyou 3 he was made prefect of Song.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 3, first month, he was granted Song Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四月，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: In the fourth month he received acting rank as Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Fourth month, added acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，授左龍虎統軍兼元從新軍馬步都虞候。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne he made Han commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Guard and chief adjutant of his personal new army, horse and foot.
entries.literal: The Founder received the abdication and appointed him commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Guard and concurrently chief military adjutant of the original-following new army, horse and foot.

entries.zh: 及上黨纏兵，太祖親往巡撫，以捍為御營使。
entries.en: When war tangled at Shangdang the Founder went in person and made Han commissioner of the imperial camp.
entries.literal: When Shangdang tangled troops, the Founder in person went to oversee; he made Han imperial-camp commissioner.

entries.zh: 大軍次昂車，斥候來告蕃戎逼澤州，命捍以兵千人赴之，並軍遂遁，車駕還京，授捍侍衛親軍都指揮使。
entries.en: The army halted at Angche; scouts reported barbarians pressing Ze; the Founder sent Han with a thousand men and the enemy fled; when the emperor returned to the capital Han was made commander of the palace guard.
entries.literal: The great army halted at Angche; scouts came reporting barbarians pressing Ze Prefecture; he ordered Han with a thousand troops to go; the combined armies thereupon fled; the imperial carriage returned to the capital and Han was granted commander of the personal guard of the palace guards.

entries.zh: 晉人侵晉州，從幸陝回，加檢校太保。
entries.en: When the Jin struck Jinzhou and Han followed the court to Shan and back, he received acting rank as Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Jin men invaded Jin Prefecture; following the imperial progress to Shan and back, he was added acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 及從駕幸河中，詔追王重師赴行在，以捍為雍州節度觀察留後。
entries.en: When the court moved to Hezhong, Wang Chongshi was recalled and Han was made acting military and surveillance commissioner of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: When he followed the carriage to Hezhong, an edict recalled Wang Chongshi to the traveling court and made Han regent military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Yong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 才逾月，劉知俊據同州反，潛使人以厚利啖將校，遂為部下所執，送於知俊。
entries.en: Barely a month later Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou and secretly bribed Han's officers; they seized him and handed him to Zhijun.
entries.literal: Barely past a month, Liu Zhijun held Tong Prefecture and rebelled, secretly sent men with thick profit to entice commanders; Han was thereupon seized by subordinates and sent to Zhijun.

entries.zh: 知俊縶捍歸於鳳翔，為李茂貞所害。
entries.en: Zhijun sent Han bound to Fengxiang, where Li Maozhen put him to death.
entries.literal: Zhijun bound Han and returned to Fengxiang; he was harmed by Li Maozhen.

entries.zh: 開平四年，贈太傅。
entries.en: In Kaiping 4 he was posthumously named Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 4, gifted Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，又贈太尉。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor ascended he was posthumously named Grand Commandant as well.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, again gifted Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 馬嗣勳，濠州鍾離縣人，世為軍吏。
entries.en: Ma Sixun of Zhongli in Haozhou came from a family of army officers.
entries.literal: Ma Sixun, a man of Zhongli county in Hao Prefecture, for generations military clerks.

entries.zh: 嗣勳有口辯，習武藝，初為州客將。
entries.en: Sixun was eloquent and trained in arms; he began as the prefecture's guest-officer.
entries.literal: Sixun had mouth and debate, practised martial arts; at first he was the prefecture's guest-officer.

entries.zh: 唐景福元年三月，太祖以壽州刺史江儒反下蔡鎮使，李立率兵攻濠梁，刺史張遂俾嗣勳持州印籍戶口以歸於太祖。
entries.en: In the third month of Jingfu 1, when Shou prefect Jiang Ru rebelled at Xia'ai, Li Li attacked Hao and Liang; prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and household registers to submit to the Founder.
entries.literal: Tang Jingfu year 1, third month, the Founder because Shou prefect Jiang Ru rebelled [at] Xia'ai garrison commander Li Li led troops attacking Hao and Liang; prefect Zhang Sui had Sixun hold the prefectural seal and register households to return submission to the Founder.

entries.zh: 乾寧二年三月，楊行密復攻濠州，張遂遣嗣勳求援於太祖。
entries.en: In the third month of Qianning 2, when Yang Xingmi attacked Haozhou again, Zhang Sui sent Sixun to plead for help.
entries.literal: Qianning year 2, third month, Yang Xingmi again attacked Hao Prefecture; Zhang Sui sent Sixun to beg aid from the Founder.

entries.zh: 俄而郡陷，嗣勳無所歸，即署為元從押牙、副典客，頗稱任使。
entries.en: When the city soon fell Sixun had nowhere to go; the Founder made him yamen adjutant of his personal following and deputy master of ceremonies, and found him thoroughly reliable.
entries.literal: Soon the prefecture fell; Sixun had nowhere to return; he was at once appointed original-following yamen adjutant and deputy master of ceremonies, quite fit for employment and missions.

entries.zh: 光化元年三月，太祖令往光州說刺史劉存背淮賊以向國，又從李彥威復黃州及武昌縣，獲刺史瞿章。
entries.en: In the third month of Guanghua 1 the Founder sent him to Guangzhou to urge Liu Cun to abandon the Huai rebels for the throne; he then joined Li Yanwei in retaking Huangzhou and Wuchang county and took Prefect Qu Zhang captive.
