entries.literal: Guanghua 1 third month, the Founder sent him to Guang prefecture to persuade Prefect Liu Cun to turn from Huai bandits toward the state; he also followed Li Yanwei to recover Huang prefecture and Wuchang county and captured Prefect Qu Zhang.

entries.zh: 俄復使光州，持幣馬以賜劉存。
entries.en: He was soon dispatched to Guangzhou again with gifts of silk and horses for Liu Cun.
entries.literal: Soon he was again sent to Guang prefecture, bearing silks and horses to bestow on Liu Cun.

entries.zh: 會淮賊急攻光州，存與嗣勳率兵大戰，敗而走之。
entries.en: When Huai rebels stormed Guangzhou, Liu Cun and Sixun gave battle and routed them.
entries.literal: When Huai bandits pressed Guang prefecture in force, Cun and Sixun led troops in great battle and defeated and drove them off.

entries.zh: 又遣使於蜀，及歸，得其助軍貲實甚多。
entries.en: He later went as envoy to Shu and on his return brought back abundant military stores.
entries.literal: He also was sent as envoy to Shu; on return he obtained very much military aid in goods and wealth.

entries.zh: 天復中，太祖迎昭宗於岐下，軍至華之西，使嗣勳入見，韓建即時同出迎謁。
entries.en: During Tianfu, as the Founder brought Zhaozong from Qixia and halted west of Hua, he sent Sixun in to audience; Han Jian came out at once to greet them together.
entries.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qixia and the army reached west of Hua, he sent Sixun in to see him; Han Jian at once came out together to welcome and pay court.

entries.zh: 及羅紹威將殺牙軍，遣使告於太祖，求為外援。
entries.en: When Luo Shaowei planned to destroy the guard corps, he asked the Founder for reinforcements.
entries.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to kill the guard army, he sent envoys to inform the Founder and beg for outside aid.

entries.zh: 時安陽公主初卒於魏，太祖乃遺嗣勳率長直官千人，實兵仗於橐中，肩舁以入於魏，聲言來致祭會葬，牙軍不之覺。
entries.en: Princess Anyang had just died at Wei; the Founder sent Sixun with a thousand hand-picked men, weapons hidden in coffers carried on poles into the city under cover of funeral rites, and the guard army never suspected.
entries.literal: At the time Princess Anyang had just died in Wei; the Founder then sent Sixun leading a thousand long-guard officers, with weapons packed in chests and borne on shoulders into Wei, declaring they came to offer sacrifice at the funeral—the guard army did not notice.

entries.zh: 天祐三年正月十六日夜，嗣勳與紹威親軍同攻牙軍，至曙，盡殪之。
entries.en: On the night of the sixteenth of the first month of Tianyou 3, Sixun and Shaowei's own troops struck the guard corps and wiped them out by dawn.
entries.literal: Tianyou 3 first month, night of the sixteenth, Sixun with Shaowei's personal troops together attacked the guard army; by dawn they were all annihilated.

entries.zh: 嗣勳重傷，旬日而卒。
entries.en: Sixun was badly wounded and died ten days later.
entries.literal: Sixun was gravely wounded and died within ten days.

entries.zh: 開平中，累贈太保。
entries.en: Under Kaiping he was posthumously raised to Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: In Kaiping he was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 司馬鄴，字表仁，其先河內溫人也。
entries.en: Sima Ye, who styled himself Biaoren, came of a family from Wen in Henei.
entries.literal: Si Maye, styled Biaoren, his ancestors were men of Wen in Henei.

entries.zh: 祖德璋，仕唐為杞王傅。
entries.en: His grandfather Dezang had served the Tang as tutor to the Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: His grandfather Dezang served Tang as tutor to the Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 父諲，左武衛大將軍。
entries.en: His father Yin held the post of Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
entries.literal: His father Yin was Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 鄴資蔭出身，頗知書，累官至大列。
entries.en: Maye entered service by yin privilege, was well read, and rose to Grand Array.
entries.literal: Maye entered office by hereditary privilege, knew books quite well, and rose in office to Grand Array.

entries.zh: 唐天復初，韓建用為同州節度留後。
entries.en: Early in Tianfu, Han Jian made him acting military commissioner of Tongzhou.
entries.literal: Early Tang Tianfu, Han Jian employed him as Tongzhou military regent.

entries.zh: 韓建傳判官司鄴昭宗之幸鳳翔也，太祖引兵入關，前鋒至左馮翊，鄴持印鑰迎謁道左。
entries.en: Maye had served as Han Jian's administrative officer; when Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder entered the Pass, Maye met the vanguard at Fengyi with seal and keys in hand.
entries.literal: Si Maye had been Han Jian's administrative officer; when Zhaozong went to Fengxiang the Founder led troops into the Pass, the vanguard reaching Left Fengyi; Maye holding seal and keys welcomed him by the roadside.

entries.zh: 太祖以兵圍華州，命入城招諭韓建，建果出降。
entries.en: The Founder besieged Hua and sent Maye into the city to parley with Han Jian, who promptly surrendered.
entries.literal: The Founder with troops besieged Hua Prefecture, ordered him into the city to summon and persuade Han Jian; Jian indeed came out and surrendered.

entries.zh: 及大軍在岐下，遣奏事於昭宗，再入復出。
entries.en: While the army camped at Qi's walls he carried dispatches to Zhaozong, going in twice and returning each time.
entries.literal: When the great army was below Qi, he was sent to report to Zhaozong, entering twice and coming out again.

entries.zh: 又使於金州，說其帥馮行襲，俾堅攀附。
entries.en: He was also sent to Jinzhou to bind Feng Xingxi firmly to the Founder's cause.
entries.literal: Again he was sent to Jin Prefecture to persuade its commander Feng Xingxi to hold fast to attachment.

entries.zh: 後曆宣武、天平等軍從事。
entries.en: Later he served on the staffs of the Xuanwu and Tianping commands.
entries.literal: Later he successively served as staff officer of the Xuanyi and Tianping armies.

entries.zh: 開平元年，拜右武衛上將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaiping he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 1, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 三年，使於兩浙。
entries.en: In his third year of office he was sent as envoy to the Two Zhes.
entries.literal: Year 3, he was envoy to the Two Zhes.

entries.zh: 時淮路不通，乘駔者迂回萬里，陸行則出荊、襄、潭、桂入嶺，自番禺泛海至閩中，達於杭、越。
entries.en: With the Huai route cut, couriers wound ten thousand li overland—through Jing, Xiang, Tan, and Gui into the ranges, then by sea from Panyu into Fujian until they reached Hang and Yue.
entries.literal: At that time the Huai route was not open; those who rode relay horses went round about ten thousand li; by land they went out through Jing, Xiang, Tan, Gui into the passes, from Panyu sailed the sea to Min, and reached Hang and Yue.

entries.zh: 復命則備舟楫，出東海，至於登、萊。
entries.en: The return passage meant fitting out ships, crossing the Eastern Sea, and making land at Deng and Lai.
entries.literal: On return they prepared boats, went out the Eastern Sea, and reached Deng and Lai.

entries.zh: 而揚州諸步多賊船，過者不敢循岸，必高帆遠引海中，謂之「入陽」，以故多損敗。
entries.en: Pirate fleets held the Yangzhou coast, so travelers dared not hug the shore but put out to open sea—"entering the sun"—and many ships were lost that way.
entries.literal: But Yangzhou's posts had many bandit ships; passers did not dare hug the shore, but must raise sails and draw far off into the sea, called "Entering the Sun," and for this reason many were lost or wrecked.

entries.zh: 鄴在海逾年，漂至躭羅國，一行俱溺。
entries.en: More than a year at sea carried Maye to Silla, where his whole escort perished.
entries.literal: Maye on the sea more than a year drifted to the Silla country; his whole party drowned together.

entries.zh: 後詔贈司徒。
entries.en: Later he was posthumously named Grand Preceptor by edict.
entries.literal: Later an edict posthumously gave him Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 寇彥卿，字俊臣，大梁人也。
entries.en: Kou Yanqing, styled Junchen, came from Daliang.
entries.literal: Kou Yanqing, style Junchen, was a man of Daliang.

entries.zh: 祖琯，父裔，皆宣武軍牙校。
entries.en: His grandfather Guan and father Yi had both been guard officers of the Xuanwu army.
entries.literal: Grandfather Guan and father Yi were both Xuanwu army guard officers.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮汴，以彥卿將家子，擢在左右。
entries.en: When the Founder governed Bian he kept Yanqing, a general's son, at his side.
entries.literal: When the Founder held Bian he, because Yanqing was a general's son, promoted him to his side.

entries.zh: 弱冠，選為通讚官。
entries.en: In his youth he was made a protocol officer.
entries.literal: At weak cap he was chosen as communications officer.

entries.zh: 太祖為元帥，補元帥府押牙，充四鎮通讚官行首兼右長直都指揮使，累奏授檢校司徒，領洺州刺史。
entries.en: As grand marshal the Founder made him headquarters guard officer, chief protocol officer of the four commands and Right Long Direct commander, and had him memorialized Acting Minister of Works and prefect of Mingzhou.
entries.literal: When the Founder was grand marshal he supplemented him as the marshal's headquarters guard officer, served as head of the four commands communications officers and concurrently Right Long Direct overall commander, and repeatedly memorialized to appoint Acting Minister of Works and grant Ming prefecture.

entries.zh: 羅紹威將殺牙軍，遣使告於太祖，太祖命彥卿使於魏，密與紹威謀之。
entries.en: When Luo Shaowei moved against the guard corps he asked the Founder for help; the Founder sent Yanqing to Wei to conspire with him.
entries.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to kill the guard army he sent envoys to inform the Founder; the Founder ordered Yanqing as envoy to Wei to plot secretly with Shaowei.

entries.zh: 竟成其事，彥卿之力也。
entries.en: The plot succeeded largely through Yanqing's efforts.
entries.literal: In the end the affair succeeded—Yanqing's strength.

entries.zh: 彥卿身長八尺，隆準方面，語音如鍾。
entries.en: Yanqing stood eight feet tall, with a high nose and square face, and a voice like a bell.
entries.literal: Yanqing was eight feet in height, with high nose and square face; his voice was like a bell.

entries.zh: 善騎射，好書史，復善伺太祖之旨，凡所作為，動皆云合。
entries.en: He excelled at riding and archery, loved history, and read the Founder's mind so well that his every act seemed foreordained.
entries.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, fond of books and histories, and again skilled at reading the Founder's intent—whatever he did always matched like clouds joining.

entries.zh: 太祖每言曰：「敬翔、劉捏、寇彥卿，蓋為我而生。」
entries.en: The Founder would say: "Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing might as well have been made for me."
entries.literal: The Founder often said: "Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing were surely born for me."

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Thus he was valued to this degree.

entries.zh: 太祖有所乘烏馬，號「一丈烏」，嘗以賜彥卿。
entries.en: The Founder once gave him his black charger, the "Ten-foot Crow."
entries.literal: The Founder had a black horse he rode called "One Zhang Crow"; he once bestowed it on Yanqing.

entries.zh: 捍便習賓讚，善於將迎，自司賓局及征討四出，必預其間。
entries.en: Han mastered guest rites and welcome ceremony; from the Bureau of Guest Rites to every campaign abroad he was always in the thick of it.
entries.literal: Han was skilled at guest rites and acclamation, good at receiving and escorting; from the Bureau of Guest Rites and on campaigns in four directions he was always in their midst.

entries.zh: 雖無決戰爭鋒之績，而承命奔走，數揚命令，勤幹涖職，以至崇顯焉。
entries.en: He won no great battle, yet by racing on every order, bearing the Founder's word again and again, and tireless service he rose to the highest honors.
entries.literal: Though he had no achievement of decisive battle and contending edge, yet receiving orders he ran and hastened, repeatedly proclaimed commands, diligently carried office—and so reached eminent display.

entries.zh: 王敬蕘，潁州汝陰人，世為郡武吏。
entries.en: Wang Jinrao of Ruyin in Yingzhou came from a line of county military officers.
entries.literal: Wang Jinrao, a man of Ruyin in Ying Prefecture, for generations were the prefecture's military clerks.

entries.zh: 唐乾符初，敬蕘為本州都知兵馬使。
entries.en: Early in Qianfu he became the prefecture's commander of horse and foot.
entries.literal: Early Tang Qianfu, Jinrao was the prefecture's commander knowing horse and troops.

entries.zh: 中和初，寇難益熾，郡守庸怯，不能自固，敬蕘遂代之監郡，俄真拜刺史，加檢校右散騎常侍。
entries.en: Early in Zhonghe, as raids grew fiercer and the timid prefect could not hold the city, Jinrao took charge of the circuit, was soon confirmed as prefect, and given acting rank as Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: Early Zhonghe, bandit calamity burned hotter; the prefect was mediocre and timid and could not secure himself; Jinrao thereupon replaced him supervising the prefecture, soon truly appointed prefect, added acting Right Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 時州境荒饉，大寇繼至，黃巢數十萬眾寨於州南，敬蕘極力抗禦，逾旬而退。
entries.en: Famine stalked the circuit while great armies came one after another; hundreds of thousands of Huang Chao's men camped south of the city, and Jinrao fought them off until they withdrew after more than ten days.
entries.literal: At that time the prefecture's borders were waste and famine; great bandits came in succession; Huang Chao's hundreds of thousands camped south of the prefecture; Jinrao strove with all strength to resist; after ten days and more they withdrew.

entries.zh: 俄又宗權之眾，淩暴益甚，合圍攻壁，皆力屈而去。
entries.en: Soon Zongquan's forces came with still worse violence, besieged the walls, and withdrew only when their strength gave out.
entries.literal: Soon again Zongquan's hosts, outrage growing worse, joined siege and stormed walls; all strained their strength and left.

entries.zh: 蔡賊復遣將刁君務以萬眾來逼，敬蕘列陣當之，身先馳突，殺敵甚多，由是竟全郡壘，遠近歸附。
entries.en: The Cai rebels sent Diao Junwu with ten thousand men; Jinrao formed his line, led the charge himself, and killed a great many; the walls held, and men near and far came to his banner.
entries.literal: The Cai bandits again sent the general Diao Junwu with ten thousand hosts to press; Jinrao arrayed ranks to meet them, himself first galloping in charge, killed enemies very many; thereby he at last preserved the whole prefecture's fortresses; near and far submitted.

entries.zh: 及淮人不恭，太祖屢以軍南渡，路由州境，敬蕘悉心供億，太祖甚嘉之。
entries.en: Each time the Founder crossed the Huai with an army and passed through Ying, Jinrao supplied his needs without stint, and the Founder took great notice.
entries.literal: When Huainan men were not respectful, the Founder repeatedly with armies crossed south, the route passing through his prefectural borders; Jinrao with whole heart supplied provisions; the Founder greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 乾寧二年，署為沿淮上下都指揮使。
entries.en: In Qianning 2 he was named commander of all forces along the upper and lower Huai.
entries.literal: Qianning year 2, he was appointed commander of all posts along the Huai above and below.

entries.zh: 四年冬，龐師古敗於清口，敗軍逃歸者甚眾，路出於潁。
entries.en: Winter of year 4, after Pang Shigu's defeat at Qingkou, shattered troops poured homeward through Ying.
entries.literal: Winter, year 4, Pang Shigu was defeated at Qingkou; defeated armies fleeing back were very many; the road went out through Ying.

entries.zh: 時雨雪連旬，軍士凍餒，敬蕘自淮燎薪，相屬於道，郡中設糜糗餅餌以待之，全活者甚眾，由是表知武寧軍節度、徐宿觀察留後。
entries.en: Snow fell ten days running; the troops were freezing and starving; Jinrao sent fuel from the Huai along the road and set out gruel and cakes in the city; many lived because of it, and he was memorialized acting commissioner of Wuning and regent of Xuzhou and Suzhou.
entries.literal: At that time rain and snow continued ten days; soldiers froze and starved; Jinrao from the Huai sent fire and fuel, one after another on the road; in the prefecture he set out gruel, dry provisions, and cakes to wait for them; very many were wholly kept alive; thereby memorialized as acting Wuning army military commissioner and Xuzhou-Suzhou surveillance regent.

entries.zh: 數月，真拜武寧軍節度使。
entries.en: A few months later he was confirmed full military commissioner of Wuning.
entries.literal: Several months, truly appointed Wuning army military commissioner.

entries.zh: 天復二年，入為右龍武統軍。
entries.en: In Tianfu 2 he was called to the capital as commander of the Right Dragon-Martial Guard.
entries.literal: Tianfu year 2, entered [the capital] as commander of the Right Dragon-Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，轉左衛上將軍。
entries.en: In Tianyou 3 he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 3, transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 開平元年八月，以疾致仕，尋卒於其第。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Kaiping 1 he retired for illness and soon died at home.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 1, eighth month, on illness he retired from office; soon after he died at his mansion.

entries.zh: 敬蕘魁傑沈勇，多力善戰，所用槍矢，皆以純鐵鍛就，槍重三十餘斤，摧鋒突陣，率以此勝。
entries.en: Jinrao was a towering man, deep and brave; his spears and arrows were forged from solid iron, his spear alone weighed more than thirty pounds, and he broke enemy lines by sheer weight of steel.
entries.literal: Jinrao was a towering hero, deep and brave, much strength and good at battle; the spears and arrows he used were all forged of pure iron; the spear weighed more than thirty jin; crushing the vanguard and piercing arrays, he generally won by this.

entries.zh: 雖非太祖舊臣，而遠輸懇款，保境合兵，以輔興王之運，有足稱者。
entries.en: He was no veteran of the Founder's camp, yet from afar he offered loyal service, held his territory, and marshaled troops to help the new dynasty—grounds enough for praise.
entries.literal: Though not an old minister of the Founder, yet from afar he conveyed earnest pledge, preserved borders and united troops, to assist the fortune of the rising king—there is enough to praise.

entries.zh: 高劭，字子將，淮南節度使駢之從子也。
entries.en: Gao Shao, who styled himself Zijiang, was a cousin of the Huainan commissioner Gao Pian.
entries.literal: Gao Shao, styled Zijiang, was the younger cousin of Huainan military commissioner Gao Pian.

entries.zh: 父泰，黔中觀察使。
entries.en: His father Tai had been surveillance commissioner of Qianzhong.
entries.literal: His father Tai was Qianzhong surveillance commissioner.

entries.zh: 唐僖宗避敵在蜀，駢鎮淮南為都統，兼諸道鹽鐵使，兵賦在己，朝廷優假之，以故劭幸而早官，年十四遙領華州刺史。
entries.en: While Xizong sheltered in Shu, Pian ruled Huainan as supreme commander and salt-and-iron commissioner with troops and taxes in his fist; the court indulged him, and Shao at fourteen was given distant command as prefect of Hua.
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Xizong avoided the enemy in Shu; Pian held Huainan as supreme commander and concurrently salt and iron commissioner for all circuits, troops and levies in his own hands—the court treated him generously; thus Shao by fortune received early office, at age fourteen distantly holding Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 光啟中，以駢命遏晉公王鐸於鄭。
entries.en: Midway through Guangqi he blocked Wang Duo, Duke of Jin, at Zheng on Pian's order.
entries.literal: Mid Guangqi, on Pian's order he blocked the Duke of Jin Wang Duo at Zheng.

entries.zh: 俄而州陷於蔡，劭為賊所得，使人守之，戒四門曰：「無出高大夫。」
entries.en: Soon Cai rebels took the city; they seized Shao and posted guards with orders at every gate: "Let no one let Lord Gao out."
entries.literal: Soon the prefecture fell to Cai; Shao was taken by bandits; they sent men to guard him and warned the four gates: "Do not let High Excellency out."

entries.zh: 劭伺守者稍惰，佯為乞食者，過危垣，取殍者衣，坌身易服，得他兒抱之行，出東郊門。
entries.en: When the guards slackened he played a beggar, crept past a broken wall, dressed in a dead man's rags, took up another child as if his own, and walked out the eastern gate.
entries.literal: Shao watched until guards slackened slightly, pretended to be a beggar-for-food, passed a perilous wall, took a corpse's clothes, covered his body and changed dress, got another child to carry and walked, exiting the eastern suburb gate.

entries.zh: 人以為丐者，不之止。
entries.en: Passers took him for a beggar and let him go.
entries.literal: People took him for a beggar and did not stop him.

entries.zh: 及稍遠，棄所抱兒，疾趨至中牟，遂達於汴。
entries.en: Once he was clear of the city he abandoned the child, ran to Zhongmu, and reached Bian.
entries.literal: When somewhat far, he abandoned the child he carried, hastened swiftly to Zhongmu, and at last reached Bian.

entries.zh: 太祖以客禮遇之，尋表為亳州團練副使，知州事。
entries.en: The Founder received him as an honored guest and soon made him vice-regimental commissioner at Bozhou with charge of the prefecture.
entries.literal: The Founder treated him with guest rites; soon memorialized him as Bozhou regimental vice-commissioner and acting prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 又數年，辟為宣武軍節度判官，在幕下頗以氣直自許。
entries.en: Some years later he joined the Xuanyi staff as chief adjutant and prided himself on blunt honesty.
entries.literal: Again several years, summoned as Xuanyi army military commissioner adjutant; in the staff he quite took straight spirit as his boast.

entries.zh: 後監鄭州事，復權知徐州留後。
entries.en: He later oversaw Zhengzhou and served acting regent at Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Later he supervised Zheng Prefecture affairs and again held acting authority as Xuzhou regent.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗之鳳翔，太祖迎奉未出，劭有疑謀，遂令赴華州，詣丞相府以議其事；
entries.en: When Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder had not yet marched to receive him, Shao's plotting aroused suspicion; he was sent to Hua to consult the chief minister's office—
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang; the Founder had not yet gone out to welcome him; Shao had doubtful schemes; he was then ordered to go to Hua Prefecture, to approach the chief minister's office to deliberate the affair;

entries.zh: 行至高陵，為盜所害。
entries.en: on the road at Gaoling bandits killed him.
entries.literal: traveling, reaching Gaoling, he was harmed by bandits.

entries.zh: 張存敬，譙郡人也。
entries.en: Zhang Cunjin came from Qiao commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Cunjing was a man of Qiao commandery.

entries.zh: 性剛直，有膽勇，臨危無所畏憚。
entries.en: Upright, bold, and utterly fearless in danger, he never flinched.
entries.literal: By nature upright and firm, with courage and daring, in facing peril he had no fear or dread.

entries.zh: 唐中和中，從太祖赴汴，以其折節，頗見親昵，首為右騎都將。
entries.en: In Zhonghe of Tang he followed the Founder to Bian; his discipline won favor, and he became the first Right Cavalry commander.
entries.literal: In Tang Zhonghe he followed the Founder to Bian; because of his self-restraint he was quite treated with intimacy, and first became Right Cavalry commander.

entries.zh: 從討巢、蔡，凡曆百戰，多於危蹙之間，顯有奇略，由是頻立殊效。
entries.en: In the wars on Chao and Cai he fought a hundred engagements and, again and again in tight corners, showed brilliant tactics that won him repeated distinction.
entries.literal: Following campaigns against Chao and Cai, in all he passed through a hundred battles; many times in moments of dire straits he showed strange strategy, and thereby repeatedly established extraordinary merit.

entries.zh: 光啟中，李罕之會晉軍圍張宗奭於盟津，太祖遣丁會、葛從周、存敬同往馳救。
entries.en: In Guangqi, Li Hanzhi and the Jin besieged Zhang Zongshi at Mengjin; the Founder sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Cunjin to relieve him.
entries.literal: In Guangqi, Li Hanzhi joined Jin troops in besieging Zhang Zongshi at Meng Ford; the Founder sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Cunjing together to gallop to the rescue.

entries.zh: 存敬引騎軍先犯敵將，諸軍翼之，敵騎大敗，乃解河橋之圍。
entries.en: Cunjin led the cavalry against the enemy commander while the rest flanked; the Jin horse were routed and the siege of He Bridge was broken.
entries.literal: Cunjing led cavalry first to strike the enemy commander; the armies flanked him; enemy horsemen were greatly defeated, and thus the siege at He Bridge was lifted.

entries.zh: 大順二年，為諸軍都虞候，佐霍存董大軍收宿州，以功奏加檢校兵部尚書。
entries.en: In Dashun 2 he was made army inspector, helped Huo Cun retake Suzhou, and was memorialized Acting Minister of War.
entries.literal: Datong 2 he became overall army inspector, assisted Huo Cun in directing the great army to recover Suzhou, and for merit was memorialized Acting Minister of War.

entries.zh: 太祖東征徐、兗，存敬屢有俘斬之功。
entries.en: In the eastern campaigns against Xu and Yan, Cunjin took many prisoners and heads.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned east against Xu and Yan, Cunjing repeatedly had merit in captures and beheadings.

entries.zh: 凡受指顧，皆與機會，矢石所及，必以身先，太祖屢加優異，以為行營都指揮使、檢校右僕射。
entries.en: He seized every chance in battle and always led where stones and arrows fell; the Founder favored him and made him field commander and Acting Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: Whenever he received orders he always seized the moment; wherever arrows and stones reached he must take the lead; the Founder repeatedly showed him special favor and made him field army overall commander and Acting Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 乾寧三年，充武寧軍留後，行潁州刺史。
entries.en: In Qianning 3 he was acting Wuning commissioner and prefect of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Qianning 3 he served as Wuning army acting commissioner, acting Yingzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 光化二年夏四月，幽、滄侵淩魏郡，復以存敬為都指揮使。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, Guanghua 2, when You and Cang raided Wei, Cunjin was again made overall commander.
entries.literal: Guanghua 2 summer fourth month, You and Cang harassed and encroached on Wei commandery; Cunjing was again made overall commander.

entries.zh: 三年，大舉，與葛從周連統諸軍攻浮陽，樹數十柵，圍劉守文累月。
entries.en: In year 3 he joined Ge Congzhou in a major siege of Fuyang, building dozens of camps around Liu Shouwen for months.
entries.literal: Year 3, on a great campaign, with Ge Congzhou jointly commanded the armies attacking Fuyang, erected several tens of stockades, and besieged Liu Shouwen for many months.

entries.zh: 時幽州劉仁恭舉兵來援，存敬潛軍擊之於乾寧軍南老鴉堤。
entries.en: When Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched to relieve the city, Cunjin ambushed him at Old Crow Embankment south of Qianning.
entries.literal: At the time Youzhou's Liu Rengong raised troops to aid; Cunjing secretly moved troops and struck him at Old Crow Embankment south of Qianning army.

entries.zh: 是日，燕人大敗，斬首五萬級，生擒馬慎交已下一百餘人，獲馬萬餘蹄。
entries.en: That day the Yan army was shattered: fifty thousand heads, more than a hundred captives led by Ma Shenjiao, and over ten thousand horses.
entries.literal: That day the Yan men were greatly defeated; heads cut numbered fifty thousand; alive captured Ma Shenjiao and over a hundred below him; horses obtained over ten thousand hooves.

entries.zh: 其年秋九月，引軍收鎮州，存敬勒眾涉滹沲河，師人鼓行而進，逢鎮之遊兵數千，因逐之，直入鎮之壅門，收鞍馬牛駝萬計。
entries.en: In the ninth month he marched on Zhenzhou; Cunjin crossed the Hutuo at the drum, routed several thousand scouts, chased them through the barrier gate, and seized tens of thousands of animals.
entries.literal: That year autumn ninth month, he led the army to take Zhen prefecture; Cunjing drove the masses across the Hutuo River; the army beat drums and advanced; met several thousand of Zhen's roaming troops; thereupon pursued them, straight into Zhen's barrier gate, and collected saddles, horses, cattle, and camels by the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 翌日，鎮人納質而旋。
entries.en: The next day Zhenzhou submitted hostages and he withdrew.
entries.literal: The next day the Zhen men offered hostages and withdrew.

entries.zh: 尋為宋州刺史，逾年，甚有能政。
entries.en: He soon became prefect of Songzhou and governed ably for more than a year.
entries.literal: Soon he became Song prefect; after more than a year he was very able in government.

entries.zh: 復擁眾伐薊門，數旬間連下瀛、莫、祁、景四州，擒俘不可勝紀。
entries.en: He again marched on Ji Gate and within weeks took Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing, with captives beyond count.
entries.literal: Again he led masses to campaign against Ji Gate; within several tens of days in succession he took Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing four prefectures; prisoners captured could not be fully counted.

entries.zh: 自懷德驛與中山兵接戰，枕屍數十里，中山開壁請降。
entries.en: At Huaide post he fought the Zhongshan army until the dead lay for miles; Zhongshan opened the walls and surrendered.
entries.literal: From Huaide post he joined battle with Zhongshan troops; corpses pillowed for several tens of li; Zhongshan opened the walls and begged surrender.

entries.zh: 天復元年春，太祖以河中節度使王珂與太原結親，憑恃驕恣，命存敬統大軍討之。
entries.en: In spring of Tianfu 1 the Founder, angered that Wang Ke of Hezhong had married into Taiyuan and grown insolent, sent Cunjin with a great army against him.
entries.literal: Tianfu 1 spring, the Founder because Hezhong military commissioner Wang Ke had allied with Taiyuan and relied on arrogance and license ordered Cunjing to command the great army to punish him.

entries.zh: 即日收絳州，擒刺史陶建釗，降晉州刺史張漢瑜，二郡平。
entries.en: The same day he took Jiangzhou, seized Tao Jianzhao, and won Zhang Hanyu of Jinzhou—both districts were pacified.
entries.literal: That very day he took Jiang prefecture, captured Prefect Tao Jianzhao, and Jiang prefecture's Zhang Hanyu submitted; the two commanderies were pacified.

entries.zh: 進圍河中，王珂請降。
entries.en: He then besieged Hezhong until Wang Ke surrendered.
entries.literal: Advancing to besiege Hezhong, Wang Ke begged surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉之，乃以存敬為護國軍留後。
entries.en: The Founder was pleased and made Cunjin acting commissioner of Huguo.
entries.literal: The Founder praised this and thereupon made Cunjing Huguo army acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 未幾，檢校司空，尋移宋州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was Acting Minister of Works, then transferred to Songzhou.
entries.literal: Before long, Acting Minister of Works; soon moved to Song prefect.

entries.zh: 將之任所，寢疾，逾旬卒於河中。
entries.en: On his way to take up Songzhou he fell ill and died at Hezhong within a fortnight.
entries.literal: About to go to his post of office, he took to bed with illness; after more than ten days he died at Hezhong.

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，痛惜移晷。
entries.en: The Founder mourned him for hours on hearing the news.
entries.literal: When the Founder heard it he grieved and regretted for a watch.

entries.zh: 開平初，追贈太保。
entries.en: At the founding of Kaiping he was posthumously made Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: At Kaiping's opening, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 乾化三年，又追贈太傅。
entries.en: In Qianhua 3 he was posthumously raised to Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Qianhua 3, again posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 天復中，太祖迎昭宗於鳳翔，累與岐軍對陣。
entries.en: During Tianfu, as the Founder brought Zhaozong from Fengxiang, he fought the Qi army again and again.
entries.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Fengxiang, he repeatedly faced Qi troops in array.

entries.zh: 時彥卿為諸道馬步軍都排陣使。
entries.en: Yanqing then served as overall battle-line marshal for the allied forces.
entries.literal: At the time Yanqing was overall array marshal of all circuits horse and foot armies.

entries.zh: 嘗躬擐甲胄，乘其所賜烏馬，馳騁於陣前，太祖目之曰：「真神王也！」
entries.en: Once, armored and mounted on his gifted black horse, he charged before the ranks; the Founder watched and cried, "A true war god!"
entries.literal: He once personally donned armor and helmet, rode the black horse bestowed on him, and galloped before the lines; the Founder eyed him and said: "Truly a spirit king!"

entries.zh: 昭宗還京，賜迎鑾毅勇功臣，改邢州刺史，尋遷亳州團練使。
entries.en: After Zhaozong returned to the capital he received the merit title Welcome-the-Chariot Bold and Brave, became prefect of Xingzhou, and soon regimental commissioner of Bozhou.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was granted the title Welcome-the-Chariot Bold and Brave Merit Subject, changed to Xing prefect, and soon moved to Bozhou regimental commissioner.

entries.zh: 〈（案《通鑒》：開平二年，帝從吳越王錢鏐之請，以亳州團練使寇彥卿為東南面行營都指揮使，使擊淮南。
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: In Kaiping 2, at Wuyue king Qian Liu's request the Emperor named Kou Yanqing of Bozhou overall commander of the southeast campaign against Huainan.
entries.literal: （Case note from the 《Comprehensive Mirror》: In Kaiping 2, the Emperor at King Qian Liu of Wuyue's request made Bozhou regimental commissioner Kou Yanqing southeast campaign overall commander to attack Huainan.

entries.zh: 十一月，彥卿率眾一千襲霍丘，為土豪朱景所敗；
entries.en: In the eleventh month Yanqing led a thousand men against Huoqiu and was beaten by the local chief Zhu Jing;
entries.literal: Eleventh month, Yanqing led a thousand men to raid Huoqiu and was defeated by local strongman Zhu Jing;

entries.zh: 又攻廬、壽二州，皆不勝。
entries.en: he then attacked Lu and Shou and failed in both.
entries.literal: again attacked Lu and Shou two prefectures, both without victory.

entries.zh: 淮南遣滁州刺史李儼拒之。
entries.en: Huainan sent Li Yi, prefect of Chuzhou, to oppose him.
entries.literal: Huainan sent Chuzhou prefect Li Yi to resist him.

entries.zh: 《九國誌·朱景傳》：梁祖聞景名，命寇彥卿率勁騎三千襲霍丘，圖取景，且諭梁祖之意令降，景率其徒戰於丘墟林澤中，射死者無數，彥卿兵折力殫而去。）〉
entries.en: The 《Nine States Chronicle · Biography of Zhu Jing》 says the Liang Founder sent Yanqing with three thousand elite cavalry to take Huoqiu and capture Jing, offering surrender terms; Jing fought him in scrub and marsh, killing many; Yanqing withdrew with his force spent.）〉
entries.literal: The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Zhu Jing》: The Liang Founder heard Jing's fame and ordered Kou Yanqing to lead three thousand crack horsemen to raid Huoqiu, intending to capture Jing, and also conveyed the Liang Founder's intent that he submit; Jing led his followers to fight in ruined mounds and forest marsh; those shot dead were countless; Yanqing's troops were broken and strength exhausted and departed.）〉

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，為華州節度使，加檢校太保。
entries.en: When the Founder received the mandate, he became military commissioner of Huazhou with Acting Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the mandate he became Hua prefecture military commissioner, added Acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 歲餘，入為左金吾衛大將軍，充街使。
entries.en: A year later he entered court as grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and city street commissioner.
entries.literal: After more than a year he entered as Left Golden Crow Guard grand general and served as street commissioner.

entries.zh: 一日，過天津橋，有老人誤衝其趨道者，排之，落橋而斃，為御史府所彈，太祖不得已，責授左衛中郎將。
entries.en: Once on Tianjin Bridge an old man blundered into his path; Yanqing shoved him off the bridge to his death; the censors impeached him, and the Founder reluctantly demoted him to middle-rank general of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: One day, crossing Tianjin Bridge, an old man by mistake rushed into his path of travel; he pushed him; he fell from the bridge and died; the censorate impeached him; the Founder had no choice and demoted him to Left Guard middle-rank general.

entries.zh: 不數月，除相州防禦使，依前行營諸軍排陣使。
entries.en: Within months he was made defense commissioner of Xiangzhou while keeping his post as army array marshal.
entries.literal: Within several months he was appointed Xiangzhou defense commissioner, retaining his former post as field army array marshal.

entries.zh: 未幾，授河陽節度使，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: Soon he received Heyang as military commissioner with Acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Before long he was granted Heyang military commissioner, added Acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 及太祖遇弑，彥卿追感舊恩，圖御容以奠之。
entries.en: After the Founder was murdered, Yanqing painted his portrait and made offerings in memory of old kindness.
entries.literal: When the Founder met assassination, Yanqing recalled old favor and painted the imperial likeness to offer sacrifice.

entries.zh: 每因對客言及先朝舊事，即涕泗交流。
entries.en: Whenever he spoke of the former court before guests he wept openly.
entries.literal: Whenever in facing guests he spoke of former-court old affairs, tears and mucus would stream together.

entries.zh: 末帝嗣位，遙領興元節度使、東南面行營都招討使。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor he held Xingyuan and the southeast suppression command in absentia.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, he held at a distance Xingyuan military commissioner and southeast campaign overall commander to suppress and recruit.

entries.zh: 以拒淮寇，尋改右金吾衛上將軍。
entries.en: Fighting the Huai rebels, he was soon made senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
entries.literal: To resist Huai bandits, soon changed to Right Golden Crow Guard senior general.

entries.zh: 貞明初，授鄧州節度使。
entries.en: Early in Zhenming he became military commissioner of Dengzhou.
entries.literal: At Zhenming's opening he was granted Deng prefecture military commissioner.

entries.zh: 會淮人圍安陸，彥卿奉詔領兵解圍，大破淮賊而回。
entries.en: When Huainan besieged Anlu he marched to the rescue, routed the Huai army, and returned.
entries.literal: When Huai men besieged Anlu, Yanqing received edict and led troops to relieve the siege, greatly defeated Huai bandits and returned.

entries.zh: 四年，卒於鎮，時年五十七。
entries.en: In year 4 he died in office at fifty-seven.
entries.literal: Year 4 he died in his post; at the time age fifty-seven.

entries.zh: 詔贈侍中。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously conferred Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 彥卿貞幹明敏，善事人主，然怙寵作威，多忌好殺，雖顯立功名，而猶為識者之所鄙焉。
entries.en: Yanqing was capable and shrewd in serving his prince, yet abused favor, was jealous and bloodthirsty, and despite his fame men of judgment held him in contempt.
entries.literal: Yanqing was upright, capable, bright, and keen, good at serving his lord; yet relying on favor he wielded power, was much jealous and fond of killing; though he clearly established merit and fame, still he was despised by those with insight.

entries.zh: 楊師厚，潁州斤溝人也。
entries.en: Yang Shihou came from Jingou in Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Yang Shihou, a man of Jingou in Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 為李罕之部將，以猛決聞，尤善騎射。
entries.en: A general under Li Hanzhi, he was known for boldness in battle and was an expert horse archer.
entries.literal: He was a subordinate general of Li Hanzhi, famed for fierce resolve, and especially skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 及罕之敗，退保澤州，師厚與李鐸、何絪等來降，太祖署為忠武軍牙將，繼曆軍職，累遷檢校右僕射，表授曹州刺史。
entries.en: After Hanzhi's defeat and retreat to Zezhou, Shihou surrendered with Li Duo, He Yin, and others; the Founder made him a Zhongwu staff officer, and he rose through the ranks to acting Right Vice Director and governor of Cao.
entries.literal: When Hanzhi was defeated and withdrew to hold Zezhou, Shihou with Li Duo, He Yin, and others came surrendering; the Founder appointed him a junior general of the Zhongwu army; he continued through military posts, rising in repeated promotions to acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was memorialized as prefect of Cao.

entries.zh: 唐天復三年，從太祖迎昭宗於岐下，李茂貞以勁兵出戰，為師厚所敗。
entries.en: In Tianfu 3 he joined the Founder in bringing Emperor Zhaozong back from Qi; Li Maozhen marched out with elite troops and Shihou routed him.
entries.literal: Tang Tianfu year 3, he followed the Founder to welcome Emperor Zhaozong below Qi; Li Maozhen led crack troops out to fight and was defeated by Shihou.

entries.zh: 及王師範以青州叛，太祖遣師厚率兵東討，時淮賊王景仁以眾二萬來援師範，師厚逆擊，破之，追至輔唐縣，斬數百級，授齊州刺史。
entries.en: When Wang Shifan rose at Qingzhou, the Founder sent Shihou east; Wang Jingren of the Huai came with twenty thousand to relieve Shifan; Shihou met him, shattered his force, pursued to Futang, took hundreds of heads, and received Qi prefecture.
entries.literal: When Wang Shifan rebelled at Qingzhou, the Founder sent Shihou east with troops; at that time the Huai bandit Wang Jingren came with twenty thousand men to aid Shifan; Shihou met and struck them, broke them, pursued to Futang county, beheaded several hundred, and was appointed prefect of Qi.

entries.zh: 將之任，太祖急召見於鄆西境，遣師厚率步騎屯於臨朐，而聲言欲東援密州，留輜重於臨朐。
entries.en: Before he could take office the Founder called him urgently to Yan's western border, posted him at Linqu with foot and horse, announced a march to relieve Mizhou, and left the baggage train there.
entries.literal: As he was about to take up the post, the Founder urgently summoned him to the western border of Yan, sent Shihou to lead infantry and cavalry to camp at Linqu, and publicly announced that he meant to march east to relieve Mizhou, leaving baggage at Linqu.

entries.zh: 師範果出兵來擊，師厚設伏於野，追擊至聖王山，殺萬餘眾，擒都將八十人。
entries.en: Shifan did march out; Shihou laid an ambush, chased the enemy to Shengwang Mountain, killed over ten thousand, and took eighty officers.
entries.literal: Shifan indeed sent troops to attack; Shihou set an ambush in the field, pursued to Shengwang Mountain, killed more than ten thousand, and captured eighty commanders.

entries.zh: 未幾，萊州刺史王師誨以兵救師範，又大敗之。
entries.en: Soon Laizhou prefect Wang Shihui came to Shifan's aid and was beaten again.
entries.literal: Before long Laizhou prefect Wang Shihui led troops to rescue Shifan, and Shihou again inflicted a great defeat.

entries.zh: 自是，師範不復敢戰。
entries.en: After that Shifan would not fight again.
entries.literal: From then on Shifan no longer dared give battle.

entries.zh: 師厚移軍寨於城下，師範力屈，竟降。
entries.en: Shihou shifted his camp under the walls; Shifan, exhausted, submitted at last.
entries.literal: Shihou moved his camp below the city; Shifan's strength gave way and he finally surrendered.

entries.zh: 天復四年三月，加檢校司徒、徐州節度使。
entries.en: In the third month of Tianfu 4 he was made acting Minister of Works and commissioner of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Tianfu year 4, third month, he was advanced to acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 師厚純謹敏幹，深為太祖知遇，委以重兵劇鎮，他莫能及。
entries.en: Pure, careful, and capable, Shihou won the Founder's deepest trust and held the heaviest commands as no one else did.
entries.literal: Shihou was pure, careful, and quick in affairs; the Founder knew and favored him deeply, entrusting him with heavy armies and hard circuits as no other could match.

entries.zh: 然而末年矜功恃眾，驟萌不軌之意，於是專割財賦，置銀槍效節軍凡數千人，皆選摘驍銳，縱恣豢養，復故時牙軍之態，時人病之。
entries.en: In old age he swaggered over his troops, skimmed the treasury, raised several thousand Silver Spear guards picked for brutality, pampered them, and brought back the old yamen-army arrogance that the people hated.
entries.literal: Yet in his last years he prided himself on merit and relied on his masses; suddenly he harbored disloyal intent; he then monopolized revenues and levies, established a Silver Spear and Effected Discipline army of several thousand men, all picked for fierceness, indulged and fed at will, and revived the old yamen-army ways—men resented it.

entries.zh: 向時河朔之俗，上元比屋夜遊，及師厚作鎮，乃課魏人戶立燈竿，千釭萬炬，洞照一城，縱士女嬉遊。
entries.en: Hebei families once roamed all night at Lantern Festival; Shihou forced every Wei household to raise lamp poles until thousands of lights blazed over the city and soldiers and women caroused in the streets.
entries.literal: Formerly in Hebei on the Lantern Festival every household roamed by night; when Shihou governed he levied on Wei households to set lamp poles—thousands of lamps, tens of thousands of torches—lighting the whole city, and let soldiers and women roam in sport.

entries.zh: 復彩畫舟舫，令女妓棹歌於御河，縱酒彌日。
entries.en: He painted pleasure boats, set courtesans to pole and sing on the imperial canal, and feasted for days on end.
entries.literal: He also painted pleasure boats and had singing girls pole and sing on the imperial canal, drinking wine for whole days.

entries.zh: 又於黎陽采巨石，將紀德政，以鐵車負載，驅牛數百以拽之，所至之處，丘墓廬舍悉皆毀壞，百姓望之，皆曰「碑來」。
entries.en: At Liyang he took a great stone for a virtue monument, loaded it on an iron cart, and drove hundreds of oxen to drag it; graves and homes in its path were smashed, and people cried, "The stele is coming."
entries.literal: Again at Liyang he quarried a huge stone to record his virtuous rule; an iron cart bore it, and several hundred oxen were driven to haul it; wherever it passed, mounds, tombs, and houses were all destroyed; the people on seeing it all said "The stele is coming."

entries.zh: 及碑石才至，而師厚卒，魏人以為「悲來」之應。
entries.en: The stone had barely arrived when Shihou died; Wei folk heard in "The stele is coming" the omen "Grief is coming."
entries.literal: When the stone had only just arrived Shihou died; the people of Wei took it as the omen of "grief is coming."

entries.zh: 末帝聞其卒也，於私庭受賀，乃議裂魏州為兩鎮。
entries.en: The Last Emperor rejoiced privately at the news and planned to split Wei in two.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor, hearing of his death, rejoiced in private and then debated splitting Wei into two circuits.

entries.zh: 既而所樹親軍，果為叛亂，以招外寇，致使河朔淪陷，宗社覆滅，由師厚兆之也。
entries.en: Soon his private guard rebelled, called in foreign enemies, and Hebei fell with the dynasty—the trail began with Shihou.
entries.literal: Before long the personal army he had raised indeed rebelled, inviting outside raiders, until Hebei was lost and the altars overturned—the beginning lay with Shihou.

entries.zh: 開平元年，加檢校太保、同平章事。
entries.en: In Kaiping 1 he was made acting Grand Guardian and given co-equal ministerial rank.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 1, he was advanced to acting Grand Guardian and co-equal to the chief ministers.

entries.zh: 明年，又加檢校太傅。
entries.en: The following year he rose to acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: The next year he was again advanced to acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 三年三月，入朝，詔兼潞州行營都招討使。
entries.en: In the third month of year 3 he came to court and was named overall commander for the Lu expedition.
entries.literal: Year 3, third month, he entered court; an edict also made him overall commander for the Lu campaign.

entries.zh: 無何，劉知俊據同州叛，師厚與劉鄩率軍西討，至潼關，擒知俊弟知浣以獻。
entries.en: Soon Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; Shihou and Liu Yan marched west, took his brother Zhihuan at Tong Pass, and sent him up.
entries.literal: Before long Liu Zhijun held Tongzhou in rebellion; Shihou with Liu Yan led troops west; reaching Tong Pass they captured Zhijun's younger brother Zhihuan and presented him.

entries.zh: 知俊聞師厚至，即西走鳳翔，師厚進攻，至長安。
entries.en: Zhijun fled west to Fengxiang when he heard Shihou was coming; Shihou drove on to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Hearing Shihou had come, Zhijun at once fled west to Fengxiang; Shihou pressed the attack to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 時知俊已引岐寇據其城，師厚以奇兵傍南山急行，自西門而入，賊將王建驚愕，不知所為，遽出降。
entries.en: Zhijun had already brought Qi forces into the city; Shihou raced picked men along the southern hills, burst in the west gate, and rebel commander Wang Jian, stunned, surrendered at once.
entries.literal: By then Zhijun had already led Qi raiders to hold the city; Shihou with picked troops hurried along the southern hills, entered by the west gate, and the rebel commander Wang Jian, startled and at a loss, promptly came out and surrendered.

entries.zh: 製加師厚檢校太尉。
entries.en: He was promoted to acting Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: An edict advanced Shihou to acting Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 頃之，晉王與周德威、丁會、符存審等以大眾攻晉州甚急，太祖遣師厚帥兵援之。
entries.en: Soon the Prince of Jin, Zhou Dewei, Ding Hui, Fu Cunshen, and others besieged Jinzhou fiercely; the Founder sent Shihou to the rescue.
entries.literal: Before long the Prince of Jin with Zhou Dewei, Ding Hui, Fu Cunshen, and others with a great host pressed Jinzhou very hard; the Founder sent Shihou to relieve it with troops.

entries.zh: 軍至絳州，晉軍扼蒙坑之險，師厚整眾而前，晉人乃徹圍而遁。
entries.en: At Jiangzhou the Jin held Mengkeng Pass; Shihou formed line and marched forward, and the Jin broke off and withdrew.
entries.literal: When the army reached Jiangzhou, Jin troops held the defile of Mengkeng; Shihou arrayed his host and advanced, and the Jin men then lifted the siege and fled.

entries.zh: 四年二月，移授陝州節度使。
entries.en: In the second month of year 4 he was transferred to Shan circuit.
entries.literal: Year 4, second month, he was transferred as military commissioner of Shan.

entries.zh: 五年正月，王景仁敗於柏鄉，晉人乘勝圍邢州，掠魏博，南至黎陽。
entries.en: In the first month of year 5 Wang Jingren fell at Baixiang; the Jin swept on, besieged Xing, plundered Weibo, and reached Liyang.
entries.literal: Year 5, first month, Wang Jingren was defeated at Baixiang; Jin men pressed the victory, besieged Xingzhou, raided Weibo, and came south to Liyang.

entries.zh: 師厚受詔以兵屯衛州，晉軍攻魏州，不克而退；
entries.en: Shihou was ordered to Weizhou; the Jin assaulted Wei, failed, and pulled back;
entries.literal: Shihou received orders to camp at Weizhou with troops; the Jin army attacked Weizhou, could not take it, and withdrew;

entries.zh: 師厚追襲，過漳河，解邢州之圍，改授滑州節度使。
entries.en: Shihou chased them over the Zhang, broke the siege of Xing, and was made commissioner of Hua.
entries.literal: Shihou pursued, crossed the Zhang River, lifted the siege of Xing, and was changed to military commissioner of Hua.

entries.zh: 明年，太祖北征，令師厚以大軍攻棗強，逾旬不能克，太祖屢加督責，師厚晝夜奮擊，乃破之，盡屠其城。
entries.en: Next year on the northern campaign the Founder ordered Shihou against Zaoqiang; for ten days the city held; the Founder drove him hard; Shihou stormed day and night, took it, and put every soul to the sword.
entries.literal: The next year the Founder campaigned north and ordered Shihou with the main army to attack Zaoqiang; for more than ten days he could not take it; the Founder repeatedly pressed him; Shihou fought day and night and then broke it, slaughtering the whole city.

entries.zh: 車駕還，師厚屯魏州。
entries.en: When the emperor returned, Shihou remained at Wei.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Shihou camped at Weizhou.

entries.zh: 牛存節，字讚貞，青州博昌人也。
entries.en: Niu Cunjie, who styled himself Zanzhen, came from Bochang in Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Niu Cunjie, styled Zanzhen, was a man of Bochang in Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 本名禮，太祖改而字之。
entries.en: His original name was Li; the Founder changed it and gave him his courtesy name.
entries.literal: His original name was Li; the Founder changed it and gave him this style.

entries.zh: 少以雄勇自負。
entries.en: As a youth he counted on his strength and daring.
entries.literal: In youth he prided himself on fierce courage.

entries.zh: 唐乾符末，鄉人諸葛爽為河陽節度使，存節往從之。
entries.en: Late in Qianfu his fellow townsman Zhuge Shuang took Heyang; Cunjie entered his service.
entries.literal: Late Tang Qianfu, his townsman Zhuge Shuang became military commissioner of Heyang; Cunjie went to follow him.

entries.zh: 爽卒，存節謂同輩曰：「天下洶洶，當擇英主事之，以圖富貴。」
entries.en: After Shuang's death Cunjie told his fellows, "The empire boils; choose a great master, serve him, and win rank and riches."
entries.literal: When Shuang died, Cunjie told his comrades: "The realm is in turmoil; one should choose an outstanding lord to serve and seek wealth and honor."

entries.zh: 遂歸於太祖。
entries.en: Then he joined the Founder.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went over to the Founder.

entries.zh: 初授宣義軍小將。
entries.en: He began as a junior officer in the Xuanyi army.
entries.literal: At first he was appointed a minor officer of the Xuanyi army.

entries.zh: 屬蔡寇至金堤驛，犯酸棗、靈昌，存節日與之鬥，凡二十餘往，每往必執俘而還，前後斬首二十餘級，獲孳畜甚眾。
entries.en: When Cai rebels hit Jindi and raided Suanzao and Lingchang, he fought them twenty-odd times in as many days, always bringing back prisoners, twenty heads, and great herds of booty.
entries.literal: When Cai bandits reached Jindi post, violating Suanzao and Lingchang, Cunjie fought them daily for more than twenty rounds; each time he returned with captives; in all he beheaded more than twenty and seized very many livestock.

entries.zh: 太祖擊蔡賊於板橋、赤岡、酸棗門、封禪寺、枯河北，存節皆預其行，與諸將於濮州南劉橋、範縣大破鄆眾，自此深為太祖獎遇。
entries.en: He fought with the Founder at Banqiao, Chigang, Suanzao Gate, Fengchan Temple, and north of the dry river, and with the other generals routed Yan troops at Liuqiao south of Pu and in Fan—after which the Founder prized him highly.
entries.literal: The Founder struck Cai bandits at Banqiao, Chigang, Suanzao Gate, Fengchan Temple, and north of the withered river; Cunjie took part in every march; with the generals he broke Yan forces south of Pu at Liuqiao and in Fan county, and from then on won the Founder's deep favor.

entries.zh: 文德元年夏，李罕之以並軍圍張宗奭於河陽，太祖遣存節率軍赴之。
entries.en: In the summer of Wende 1 Li Hanzhi besieged Zhang Zongshuang at Heyang with Bing troops; the Founder sent Cunjie to relieve him.
entries.literal: Wende year 1, summer, Li Hanzhi with Bing troops besieged Zhang Zongshuang at Heyang; the Founder sent Cunjie with troops to relieve him.

entries.zh: 屬歲歉，餉饋不至，村民有儲幹椹者，存節以器用、錢帛易之，以給軍食。
entries.en: Famine blocked supplies; Cunjie bought dried mulberry the villagers had stored, paying with goods and cash to feed his men.
entries.literal: It was a lean year and rations did not arrive; villagers had stored dry mulberry; Cunjie traded vessels and silks for it to feed the army.

entries.zh: 大破賊於浿河，罕之引眾北走。
entries.en: He crushed the enemy on the Pei; Hanzhi fled north.
entries.literal: He greatly defeated the bandits on the Pei River; Hanzhi led his host north in flight.

entries.zh: 又預討徐、宿有功。
entries.en: He later fought at Xu and Su with distinction.
entries.literal: He also took part in the campaigns against Xu and Su with merit.

entries.zh: 及討河北，存節前鋒下黎陽，收臨河，至內黃西，以兵千餘人當魏人萬二千眾，大破其陣，僵仆蔽野。
entries.en: On the Hebei campaign he took Liyang and Linhe in the van; west of Neihuang a thousand men routed twelve thousand Wei troops until the field was heaped with corpses.
entries.literal: In the Hebei campaign Cunjie as vanguard took Liyang and Linhe; west of Neihuang with a little more than a thousand men he met twelve thousand Wei troops and broke their line; the dead covered the field.

entries.zh: 太祖深所歎激，謂有神兵之助。
entries.en: The Founder marveled and said heaven had sent him soldiers.
entries.literal: The Founder sighed in deep admiration and said divine soldiers had aided him.

entries.zh: 大順元年，改滑州左右廂牢城使。
entries.en: In Dashun 1 he became commander of both wings of Hua's garrison force.
entries.literal: Dashun year 1, he was changed to commander of the left and right wings of Hua's garrison.

entries.zh: 與諸將討時溥，累破賊軍。
entries.en: He joined the generals against Shi Pu and broke his armies again and again.
entries.literal: With the generals he campaigned against Shi Pu and repeatedly broke his armies.

entries.zh: 景福元年秋，改遏後都指揮使。
entries.en: In the autumn of Jingfu 1 he was made commander of the Rearward Check.
entries.literal: Jingfu year 1, autumn, he was changed to commander of the Rearward Check.

entries.zh: 攻濮之役，領軍先登，遂拔其壘。
entries.en: At Pu he led the first escalade and took the camp.
entries.literal: In the attack on Pu he led the army in the first ascent and then stormed the stockade.

entries.zh: 二年四月，下徐州，梟時溥，存節力戰，其功居多。
entries.en: In the fourth month of year 2 Xuzhou fell and Shi Pu's head was sent up; Cunjie's fighting won the largest share of credit.
entries.literal: Year 2, fourth month, Xuzhou fell; Shi Pu was displayed; Cunjie fought hard and his merit was greatest.

entries.zh: 乾寧二年，授檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: In Qianning 2 he was made acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Qianning year 2, he was appointed acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 三年夏，太祖東討鄆州，存節領軍次故樂亭，扼其要路，都指揮使龐師古屯馬頰，存節密與都將王言謀入鄆壘。
entries.en: In the summer of year 3 the Founder marched on Yan; Cunjie blocked the road at old Leting while Pang Shigu camped at Majia; Cunjie and commander Wang Yan plotted a night entry into Yan.
entries.literal: Year 3, summer, the Founder campaigned east against Yan; Cunjie led troops to halt at old Leting, blocking the vital road; overall commander Pang Shigu camped at Majia; Cunjie secretly plotted with commander Wang Yan to enter the Yan ramparts.

entries.zh: 十二月，存節遣王言夜伏勇士於州西北，以船逾濠，舉梯登陴。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he sent Wang Yan to hide men northwest of the city; boats crossed the ditch and ladders reached the parapet.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, Cunjie sent Wang Yan by night to hide brave men northwest of the prefecture; boats crossed the moat and ladders went up the wall.

entries.zh: 既而王言不克入，存節獨率伏軍負梯童破其西甕城，奪其濠橋，諸軍俱進。
entries.en: Wang Yan could not enter; Cunjie alone led the hidden troops bearing ladders in a mass assault on the west barbican, seized the moat bridge, and all armies advanced together.
entries.literal: Wang Yan could not enter; Cunjie alone led the hidden troops bearing ladders in a mass assault on the west barbican, seized the moat bridge, and all armies advanced together.

entries.zh: 四年四月，陷其城，尋與葛從周降下兗州，加檢校右僕射。
entries.en: In the fourth month of year 4 the city fell; with Ge Congzhou he then took Yan and rose to acting Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: Year 4, fourth month, the city fell; soon with Ge Congzhou he took Yanzhou and was advanced to acting Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 天祐元年，加諸軍行營馬步都指揮使。
entries.en: In Tianyou 1 he was named supreme field commander of horse and foot for all armies.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 1, he was advanced to overall commander of all armies' horse and foot in the field.

entries.zh: 二年八月，太祖討趙匡凝於襄陽，命師厚統前軍以進，趙匡凝嚴兵以備。
entries.en: In the eighth month of year 2 the Founder attacked Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and put Shihou at the head of the advance; Kuangning drew up in full strength.
entries.literal: Year 2, eighth month, the Founder campaigned against Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and ordered Shihou to lead the vanguard forward; Zhao Kuangning arrayed his troops in readiness.

entries.zh: 師厚至穀城西童山，刊材造浮橋，引軍過漢水。
entries.en: Shihou reached Tongshan west of Gucheng, cut timber for a pontoon bridge, and crossed the Han with his men.
entries.literal: Shihou reached Tongshan west of Gucheng, felled timber to build a pontoon bridge, and led the army across the Han.

entries.zh: 一戰，趙匡凝敗散，攜妻子沿漢遁去。
entries.en: One engagement broke Kuangning's army; he fled down the Han with his family.
entries.literal: In one battle Zhao Kuangning was routed and scattered; he took wife and children and fled along the Han.

entries.zh: 翌日，表師厚為山南東道節度留後。
entries.en: Next day he was memorialized acting commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
entries.literal: The next day Shihou was memorialized as acting military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：天祐三年六月甲申，敕：「襄州近因趙匡凝作帥，請別立忠義軍額，既非往製，固是縱權，忠義軍額宜停廢，依舊為山南東道節度使。」）〉
entries.en: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 records that on jiashen in the sixth month of Tianyou 3 an edict declared: "Because Zhao Kuangning lately became commander at Xiangzhou and sought a separate Loyal and Righteous Army commission—neither the former institution nor anything but usurped authority—the Loyal and Righteous Army title should be abolished and Xiang restored to the Shannan East Circuit military commissioner.")
entries.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 says: Tianyou year 3, sixth month, day jiashen, an edict: "Xiangzhou lately, because Zhao Kuangning became commander, asked to establish separately the title of the Loyal and Righteous Army; this is neither the former system nor anything but usurped authority—the Loyal and Righteous Army title should be abolished and the former Shannan East Circuit military commissioner restored.")

entries.zh: 即令南討荊州，留後趙匡明亦棄軍上峽，不浹旬，並下兩鎮，乃正授襄州節度使。
entries.en: He was sent south on Jingzhou; acting commander Zhao Kuangming fled up the Yangzi gorges; within ten days both commands fell, and Shihou received full appointment at Xiang.
entries.literal: He was at once ordered south against Jingzhou; the acting commander Zhao Kuangming also abandoned his army and went up the gorges; within ten days both posts were taken, and Shihou was then formally appointed military commissioner of Xiang.

entries.zh: 先是，漢南無羅城，師厚始興板築，周十餘里，郛郭完壯。
entries.en: The Han south had lacked a city wall until Shihou built plank defenses for more than ten li and made the suburbs strong.
entries.literal: Earlier in the Han south there had been no outer wall; Shihou first raised plank ramparts more than ten li around, and the suburbs stood complete and strong.

entries.zh: 光化二年，罷歸，復為左衙都將兼馬步教練使。
entries.en: In Guanghua 2 he was dismissed to return home, then reappointed commander of the Left Garrison and joint horse-and-foot drill instructor.
entries.literal: Guanghua year 2, dismissed and returned, again made commander of the Left Garrison and also horse-and-foot drill instructor.

entries.zh: 天復元年，授潞州馬步都指揮使，法令嚴整，士庶安之。
entries.en: In Tianfu 1 he was made Lu's horse-and-foot commander; his regulations were strict and the people lived secure.
entries.literal: Tianfu year 1, appointed overall horse-and-foot commander of Lu; laws and orders were strict and orderly, officials and people were at peace.

entries.zh: 及追赴行在，士卒泣送者不絕於道，加金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空，改滑州左衙步軍指揮使，知邢州軍州事。
entries.en: Summoned to court, troops wept along the road as he left; he rose to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Cassia seal and acting Minister of Works, became commander of Hua Left Garrison infantry, and acted as Xing prefect and military commissioner.
entries.literal: When summoned to the imperial camp, soldiers weeping to see him off lined the road without end; he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Golden Cassia seal and acting Minister of Works, changed to commander of Hua's Left Garrison foot army, and made acting military commissioner of Xing.

entries.zh: 天祐元年，授邢州團練使。
entries.en: In Tianyou 1 he received Xing as defense commissioner.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 1, appointed defense commissioner of Xing.

entries.zh: 時州兵才及二百人，晉人知之，以大軍來寇。
entries.en: The prefecture had only two hundred troops; the Jin learned this and marched in force.
entries.literal: At the time the prefectural troops numbered barely two hundred; the Jin learned of it and came raiding with a great army.

entries.zh: 太祖在鄴，發長直兵二千人赴援，存節率壯健出鬥，以家財賞激戰士，並軍急攻，七日不能克而去。
entries.en: At Ye the Founder sent two thousand long-service men; Cunjie led his best troops out, paid warriors from his own purse, and with the relief force assaulted hard for seven days before the enemy withdrew.
entries.literal: The Founder was at Ye and sent two thousand long-service troops to the relief; Cunjie led the strong men out to fight, rewarded the warriors with his household wealth to spur them on; the allied armies pressed the attack fiercely but after seven days could not take the place and withdrew.

entries.zh: 太祖召至，勞慰久之，厚賚金帛鞍馬，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: The Founder summoned him, consoled him at length, gave rich gifts of gold, silk, saddles and horses, and made him acting Minister of Education.
entries.literal: The Founder summoned him, comforted him at length, richly rewarded him with gold, silks, saddles, and horses, and advanced him to acting Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 冬，罷軍，署為元帥府左都押衙。
entries.en: That winter the army was stood down and he was made Left Chief Escort of the Marshal's headquarters.
entries.literal: Winter, the army was disbanded; he was appointed Left Chief Escort Officer of the Marshal's headquarters.

entries.zh: 四年，太祖受禪，除右千牛衛上將軍。
entries.en: In year 4, when the Founder took the throne, he was made senior general of the Right Palace Guard.
entries.literal: Year 4, when the Founder received the abdication, he was appointed senior general of the Right Palace Guard.

entries.zh: 其秋，攻潞州，以存節為行營馬步軍都排陣使。
entries.en: That autumn, during the Lu campaign, he was named the field army's master of battle arrays for horse and foot.
entries.literal: That autumn, attacking Lu Prefecture, Cunjie was made overall array-master of the camp horse and foot.

entries.zh: 開平二年二月，自右監門衛上將軍轉右龍虎統軍，駐留洛下。
entries.en: In the second month of Kaiping 2 he rose from Right Gate Guard senior general to commander of the Right Dragon-Tiger army and stayed at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 2, second month, from Right Gate Guard senior general he was changed to Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief, remaining at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 是歲，王師敗於上黨，晉人乘勝進迫澤州，州城將陷。
entries.en: That year Wang's force lost at Shangdang; the Jin swept on toward Ze, and the city was near collapse.
entries.literal: That year Wang's army was defeated at Shangdang; Jin men pressed the victory and advanced on Zezhou; the city was about to fall.

entries.zh: 河南留守張全義召存節謀，遂以本軍及右龍虎、羽林等軍往應接上黨。
entries.en: Zhang Quanyi, regent of Henan, called Cunjie; he marched his own troops plus the Right Dragon-Tiger and Feathered Forest to relieve Shangdang.
entries.literal: Henan regent Zhang Quanyi summoned Cunjie to counsel; he then led his own army and the Right Dragon-Tiger, Feathered Forest, and other armies to answer Shangdang.

entries.zh: 師至天並關，存節謂諸將曰：「是行也，雖不奉詔旨，然要害之地，不可致失。」
entries.en: At Tianbing Pass Cunjie told his officers, "We have no fresh orders, but this choke point cannot be abandoned."
entries.literal: When the army reached Tianbing Pass, Cunjie told the generals: "On this march, though we do not carry imperial orders, yet this vital place must not be lost."

entries.zh: 時晉人新勝，其鋒甚盛，存節引從而前，銜枚夜至澤州，適遇守埤者已縱火鼓噪，以應外軍，刺史保衙城，不知所為。
entries.en: The Jin were fresh from victory and fierce; Cunjie pushed on, marched by night with gags, and reached Ze as the wall guards were already firing beacons and shouting to the relief force; the prefect held the yamen city and did not know what to do.
entries.literal: At that time the Jin had just won and their edge was very sharp; Cunjie led his followers forward, marched at night with gags in the men's mouths, and reached Ze; he happened on the wall guards already lighting fires and shouting to answer the outside army; the prefect held the yamen city and did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 存節才入，晉軍已至矣，乃分布守禦。
entries.en: He had barely entered when the Jin arrived; he spread his men for defense.
entries.literal: Cunjie had only just entered when Jin troops were already there; he then deployed for defense.

entries.zh: 晉軍四面攻鬥，開地道以入城，存節亦以隧道應之，逆戰於地中，晉軍不能進；
entries.en: The Jin assaulted from four sides and mined under the wall; Cunjie mined back and met them underground until they could not advance;
entries.literal: Jin troops attacked on four sides, opened tunnels into the city; Cunjie also met them with tunnels and fought them underground; the Jin could not advance;

entries.zh: 又以勁弩射之，中者人馬皆洞，經十三日，晉軍死傷者甚眾，焚營而退，郡以獲全，太祖屢歎賞之。
entries.en: he raked them with heavy crossbows that pierced men and horses; after thirteen days the Jin losses were heavy; they burned their camp and left; the prefecture was saved, and the Founder praised him again and again.
entries.literal: he also shot them with powerful crossbows; those hit, man and horse alike, were pierced through; after thirteen days Jin dead and wounded were very many; they burned camp and withdrew; the commandery was preserved whole; the Founder repeatedly sighed in praise.

entries.zh: 五月，遷左龍虎統軍，充六軍馬步都指揮使。
entries.en: In the fifth month he became commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger army and supreme horse-and-foot commander of the Six Armies.
entries.literal: Fifth month, he was moved to Left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and filled the post of overall horse-and-foot commander of the Six Armies.

entries.zh: 十月，授絳州刺史。
entries.en: In the tenth month he was made prefect of Jiang.
entries.literal: Tenth month, he was appointed Jiang prefect.

entries.zh: 其冬，蔣殷據徐州逆命，存節方以大眾戍潁州，得殷逆謀，密以上聞，遽奉詔與劉鄩同討之，頓於埇上。
entries.en: That winter Jiang Yin rebelled at Xuzhou while Cunjie was at Yingzhou with a large force; he reported in secret, received orders to join Liu Zhen, and encamped at Yong.
entries.literal: That winter, Jiang Yin held Xuzhou in defiance of orders; Cunjie was then garrisoning Yingzhou with a large host; learning of Yin's rebellion, he secretly reported above; hastily received an edict with Liu Zhen jointly to suppress him; encamped at Yong.

entries.zh: 淮賊朱瑾以兵救殷，距宿之兩舍，聞存節兵大至，即委糧棄甲而遁，竟平徐州。
entries.en: Zhu Jin of Huai marched to relieve Yin, but two stages from Su he heard Cunjie was coming in force, abandoned stores and arms, and fled; Xuzhou was pacified.
entries.literal: Huai rebel Zhu Jin led troops to rescue Yin; at two stages from Su he heard Cunjie's army was great and coming; he abandoned grain and armor and fled; Xuzhou was pacified in the end.

entries.zh: 詔加太尉。
entries.en: An edict made him Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: An edict added Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 夏中病渴且痟，屬河北用軍，末帝令率軍屯陽留以張劉鄩之勢。
entries.en: Midsummer he fell ill with fever and malaria; with Hebei in crisis the Last Emperor sent him to Yangliu to stiffen Liu Zhen's line.
entries.literal: Midsummer he suffered wasting thirst and malaria; as Hebei was in campaign, the Last Emperor ordered him to lead the army to encamp at Yangliu to strengthen Liu Zhen's position.

entries.zh: 存節忠憤彌篤，未嘗言病，料敵治戎，旦夕愈厲。
entries.en: His loyal zeal only sharpened; he never mentioned his illness and grew sterner each day in reading the enemy and commanding the host.
entries.literal: Cunjie's loyal indignation grew ever fiercer; he never spoke of illness; estimating the enemy and governing the host, morning and night grew the sterner.

entries.zh: 病革，詔歸汶陽，翌日而卒。
entries.en: When he worsened, an edict recalled him to Wenyang; he died the next day.
entries.literal: When illness turned critical, an edict sent him back to Wenyang; the next day he died.

entries.zh: 將終，戒其子知業、知讓等以忠孝，言不及他。
entries.en: Dying, he urged his sons Zhiye and Zhirang to loyalty and filial piety and said nothing else.
entries.literal: On the verge of death he admonished his sons Zhiye, Zhirang and others with loyalty and filial piety, speaking of nothing else.

entries.zh: 冊贈太師。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 存節武鷙慷慨，有大節，野戰壁守，皆其所長，威名聞於境外，深為末帝所重，而木強忠厚，有賈復之風焉。
entries.en: Fierce, generous, and resolute, he excelled in the field and behind walls; his fame reached beyond the border and the Last Emperor prized him, yet he was bluntly honest in the manner of Jia Fu.
entries.literal: Cunjie was martially fierce and generously spirited, with great integrity; field battle and wall defense were alike his strengths; his martial fame was heard beyond the borders; the Last Emperor valued him deeply, yet he was stubbornly honest and loyal, having the manner of Jia Fu.

entries.zh: 三年四月，除鄜州留後。
entries.en: In the fourth month of year 3 he was appointed regent of Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Year 3, fourth month, appointed Fuzhou regent.

entries.zh: 六月，劉知俊以同州叛，尋授同州留後，未幾，加檢校太保、同州節度使。
entries.en: In the sixth month Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; Cunjie was soon made regent there, then honorary Grand Guardian and military commissioner of Tong.
entries.literal: June, Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; soon he was appointed Tongzhou regent; before long, added honorary Grand Guardian and Tongzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 乾化二年，加檢校太傅，進封開國公。
entries.en: In Qianhua 2 he was made honorary Grand Mentor and advanced to Founding Duke.
entries.literal: Qianhua year 2, added honorary Grand Mentor, advanced to Founding Duke.

entries.zh: 存節戒嚴軍旅，常若敵至。
entries.en: Cunjie kept his troops on war footing as though the enemy were always near.
entries.literal: Cunjie kept the army on strict alert as if the enemy were always at hand.

entries.zh: 先是，州中井水鹹苦，人不可飲。
entries.en: The city wells had long been brackish and undrinkable.
entries.literal: Earlier, the prefectural wells were brackish and bitter, unfit to drink.

entries.zh: 及並人、岐人來迫州城，或以為兵士渴乏，陷在旦夕。
entries.en: When Jin and Qi armies besieged the city, some feared the troops would die of thirst and the walls would fall within days.
entries.literal: When Bing and Qi men came to press the city, some thought the soldiers would die of thirst and the city would fall within days.

entries.zh: 存節及肅拜虔祝，擇地鑿八十餘井，其味皆甘淡，由是人馬汲濯有餘，眾以為至誠之感。
entries.en: Cunjie bowed and prayed, then sank more than eighty wells whose water was sweet and clear; men and horses had plenty to drink, and the people called it a reward for his sincerity.
entries.literal: Cunjie solemnly bowed and prayed devoutly, chose ground and sank more than eighty wells; all tasted sweet and mild; thus men and horses had water to draw and wash in abundance; the mass took it as a response to utmost sincerity.

entries.zh: 自八月至三年春末，人馬未嘗釋甲，以至寇退。
entries.en: From the eighth month through the spring of year 3 his men never doffed armor until the enemy withdrew.
entries.literal: From the eighth month to the end of spring in year 3, men and horses never removed armor, until the raiders withdrew.

entries.zh: 尋加同平章事，詔赴闕。
entries.en: He was soon made Tongping Grand Councilor and summoned to court.
entries.literal: Soon added Tongping Grand Councilor; an edict ordered him to the capital.

entries.zh: 末帝召慰勉，賞賜甚厚。
entries.en: The Last Emperor received him with warm praise and rich gifts.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor summoned him to comfort and encourage him; rewards were very generous.

entries.zh: 十一月，加開府儀同三司，食邑一千戶，授鄆州節度使。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he was given permission to open an office with honors equal to the Three Dukes, a thousand-household fief, and the Yanzhou command.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, added Permitted to Open an Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, food domain one thousand households, appointed Yanzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 四年，加淮南西北面行營招討使，控扼淮濆，邊境安之。
entries.en: In year 4 he was made pacification commissioner for the northwest Huainan campaign, held the Huai shore, and kept the frontier quiet.
entries.literal: Year 4, added northwest Huainan campaign line-army pacification commissioner, controlled the Huai embankment region; the border was secure.

entries.zh: 大順元年，從龐師古渡淮深入，討孫儒之亂，奪邵伯堰，破高郵軍。
entries.en: In Dashun 1 he followed Pang Shigu deep across the Huai against Sun Ru, took Shaobo weir, and routed the Gaoyou force.
entries.literal: Dashun year 1, he followed Pang Shigu in crossing the Huai in depth to suppress Sun Ru's disorder, seized Shaobo weir, and broke the Gaoyou army.

entries.zh: 檀奮命擊賊，刃傷左臂。
entries.en: Tan fought desperately and took a blade wound in his left arm.
entries.literal: Tan fought desperately against the bandits and was wounded in the left arm by a blade.

entries.zh: 未幾，遷順義都將。
entries.en: Soon he was made commander of Shunyi.
entries.literal: Before long he was moved to commander of the Shunyi command.

entries.zh: 天復中，從太祖率四鎮之師圍鳳翔，以迎昭宗。
entries.en: In Tianfu he followed the Founder with the armies of four commands to besiege Fengxiang and restore Zhaozong.
entries.literal: In Tianfu he followed the Founder leading the armies of four commands to besiege Fengxiang and welcome Zhaozong.

entries.zh: 屢立戎效，遷左踏白指揮使。
entries.en: He won repeated distinction and became commander of the Left Taibai corps.
entries.literal: He repeatedly won military merit and was moved to commander of the Left Taibai corps.

entries.zh: 從攻王師範於青州，檀以偏師收復密郡，
entries.en: In the attack on Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Tan with a detached column recovered Mizhou,
entries.literal: Joining the attack on Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Tan with a detached force recovered Mizhou,

entries.zh: 〈（《永陽志》云：張訓守密州刺史，朱全忠至青州，訓謂諸將曰：「汴人將至，何以禦之？」
entries.en: (The 《Record of Yongyang》 says Zhang Xun was prefect of Mizhou; when Zhu Quanzhong reached Qingzhou, Xun asked his officers, "The Bian army is coming—how shall we meet them?"
entries.literal: (The 《Record of Yongyang》 says: Zhang Xun held the post of Mizhou prefect; Zhu Quanzhong reached Qingzhou; Xun said to the generals: "The men of Bian are coming—how shall we resist them?"

entries.zh: 諸將請焚城大掠而歸。
entries.en: His officers urged burning the city, looting it bare, and retreating.
entries.literal: The generals asked to burn the city, plunder greatly, and return.

entries.zh: 訓曰：「不可。」
entries.en: Xun said, "That we cannot do."
entries.literal: Xun said: "It cannot be done."

entries.zh: 乃封府庫，植旗幟於城上，遣羸弱居前，自以精兵殿其後而去。
entries.en: He sealed the treasury, raised banners on the walls, sent the weak forward, and withdrew with his best troops in the rear.
entries.literal: Then he sealed the treasury, planted banners on the city walls, sent the weak ahead, and himself with crack troops brought up the rear and left.

entries.zh: 全忠遣王檀攻密州，數日乃敢入城。）〉
entries.en: Quanzhong sent Wang Tan against Mizhou, and only after several days did Tan dare enter the city.)〉
entries.literal: Quanzhong sent Wang Tan to attack Mizhou; only after several days did he dare enter the city.)〉

entries.zh: 遂權知軍州事，充本州馬步軍都指揮使，尋表授檢校右僕射，守密州刺史。
entries.en: He then acted as military and civil commissioner of the prefecture and commander of its forces, and was soon made honorary Right Vice Director and defender of Mizhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was made acting military and prefectural commissioner of the prefecture, commander of local horse and foot forces; soon memorialized as honorary Right Vice Director and defender of Mizhou prefect.

entries.zh: 郡接淮戎，舊無壁壘，乃率夫修築羅城，六旬而畢，居民賴之，加檢校司空。
entries.en: The prefecture bordered Huai rebels and had no walls; he built an outer rampart in sixty days, to the people's relief, and was made honorary Grand Master.
entries.literal: The commandery bordered Huai bandits and formerly had no walls; he led laborers to build an outer wall, completing it in sixty days; the people relied on it; honorary Grand Master was added.

entries.zh: 開平二年六月，授邢州保義軍節度使、檢校司徒。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Kaiping 2 he was made Baoyi commissioner of Xing and honorary Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 2, sixth month, appointed Baoyi army military commissioner of Xingzhou, honorary Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 三年，加檢校太保，充潞州東北面行營招討使。
entries.en: In year 3 he was made honorary Grand Guardian and pacification commissioner for the northeast Luzhou campaign.
entries.literal: Year 3, added honorary Grand Guardian and made northeast Luzhou campaign line-army pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 乾化元年正月，王景仁與晉人戰於柏鄉，王師敗績，河朔大震。
entries.en: In the first month of Qianhua 1, Wang Jingren fought the Jin at Baixiang; the imperial army was routed and Hebei was shaken.
entries.literal: Qianhua year 1, first month, Wang Jingren fought Jin men at Baixiang; the royal army was badly defeated and Hebei was greatly shaken.

entries.zh: 景仁與眾為敵騎所追，檀嚴設備，應接敗軍，助以資裝，獲濟者甚眾。
entries.en: Jingren and his men were chased by enemy horse; Tan stood ready, received the fugitives, and supplied them so that many escaped.
entries.literal: Jingren and the host were pursued by enemy cavalry; Tan made strict preparations and received the defeated army, aiding them with supplies; very many were able to cross over.

entries.zh: 俄而晉軍大至，重圍四合，土山地穴，晝夜攻擊，太祖憂之。
entries.en: Soon the Jin came in force, besieged the city on every side with ramparts and mines, and attacked day and night; the Founder was deeply worried.
entries.literal: Before long the Jin army came in great force; on four sides they pressed close; earthworks and mining tunnels; day and night they attacked; the Founder was anxious.

entries.zh: 檀密上表，請駕不親征，而悉力枝梧，竟全城壘。
entries.en: Tan secretly urged the Founder not to take the field in person and braced the defense until the city held.
entries.literal: Tan secretly memorialized, asking that the imperial carriage not go on campaign in person while he exerted all strength in support; in the end the whole city and ramparts were preserved.

entries.zh: 三月，以功就加檢校太傅、同平章事。
entries.en: In the third month his merit won him honorary Grand Mentor and Tongping Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: Third month, for merit he was at once added honorary Grand Mentor and Tongping Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 七月，又加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，進封琅琊郡王，命宣徽使趙殷衡賚詔慰諭，賜絹千匹、銀千兩，賞守禦邢州之功也。
entries.en: In the seventh month he was further granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Honored Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, and advancement to Prince of Langya; Zhao Yinheng brought the edict, with a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand taels of silver for holding Xing.
entries.literal: Seventh month, again added Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Permitted to Open an Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, advanced to Prince of Langya commandery, ordered Palace Commissioner Zhao Yinheng to convey the edict in comfort, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand taels of silver—reward for defending Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 庶人友珪僭位，授鄧州宣化軍節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中。
entries.en: When Yougui seized the throne he made Tan Xuanhua commissioner of Deng, honorary Grand Marshal, and concurrent Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: The commoner Yougui usurped the throne and appointed him Xuanhua army military commissioner of Dengzhou, honorary Grand Marshal, and concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 王檀，字眾美，京兆人也。
entries.en: Wang Tan, styled Zhongmei, came from Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Wang Tan, style Zhongmei, was a native of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 曾祖泚，唐左金吾衛將軍、隴州防禦使。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Chi had been Left Golden Guard general and defense commissioner of Long.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Chi was Left Golden Guard general of Tang and Longzhou defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 祖曜，定難功臣、渭橋鎮遏使。
entries.en: His grandfather Yao was a Pacifier of Difficulties merit lord and commissioner at Wei Bridge.
