entries.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：劉鄩以機略自負，賀瑰以忠毅見稱，懷英以驍勇佐時，景仁以貞純許國，較其器業，皆名將也。
entries.en: The historian writes: Liu Xun trusted his stratagem, He Gui was praised for loyalty, Kang Huaiying for fierce service, Wang Jingren for steadfast devotion—each in his way a famous commander.
entries.literal: The historian writes: Liu Xun prided himself on stratagem, He Gui was famed for loyal resolve, Huaiying aided the age with fierce courage, Jingren pledged pure loyalty to the state; comparing their capacities, all were famous generals.

entries.zh: 然雖有善戰之勞，亦有敗軍之咎，則知兵無常勝，豈虛言哉！
entries.en: Yet each who fought well also knew defeat; arms win no permanent victory—that is no empty saying.
entries.literal: Yet though each had merit in good fighting, each also had the fault of defeated armies—thus one knows arms have no constant victory; how could that be empty talk!

entries.zh: 然鄩之據兗州，盡誠於師範，比跡於英公，方之數侯，加一等矣。
entries.en: Yet in holding Yanzhou and serving Shifan with full loyalty, Liu Xun matched the Duke of Ying and stood a rank above these other lords.
entries.literal: Yet in Liu Xun's holding of Yanzhou, his full loyalty to Shifan, his likeness to the Duke of Ying, compared with these several marquises, he ranks one degree higher.

entries.zh: 天復中，淮寇大舉圍夏口，逼巴陵，太祖患之，飛命成汭率水軍十萬援於鄂。
entries.en: During Tianfu Huai forces besieged Xiakou and threatened Baling; the Founder was alarmed and ordered Cheng Yan post-haste to Ezhou with a hundred thousand sailors.
entries.literal: In Tianfu, Huai raiders in force besieged Xiakou and pressed Baling; the Founder was anxious and sent urgent orders for Cheng Yan to lead a hundred thousand naval troops to aid Ezhou.

entries.zh: 珽入言曰：「今舳艫容介士千人，載稻倍之，緩急不可動。
entries.en: Ting advised him: "Each ship now carries a thousand fighting men and twice as much grain—it cannot maneuver when speed matters.
entries.literal: Ting entered and said: "Now each warship holds a thousand armored men and carries twice as much rice; it cannot move flexibly in urgent or slack moments.

entries.zh: 吳人剽輕，若為所絆，則武陵、武安皆我之仇也，將有後慮；
entries.en: The Wu are quick and light; if they pin you down, Wuling and Wu'an become our enemies and the rear is exposed;
entries.literal: The Wu men are swift and light; if entangled by them, Wuling and Wu'an will all be our enemies, and there will be future worry;

entries.zh: 不如遣驍將屯巴陵，大軍對岸，一日不與戰，則吳寇糧絕，而鄂州圍解矣。」
entries.en: better to post bold officers at Baling and keep the main fleet on the far bank—one day without battle and the Wu run out of grain and Ezhou is saved."
entries.literal: better to send bold generals to hold Baling, the main army on the opposite bank; if for one day they do not fight, the Wu raiders' grain will run out and the siege of Ezhou will be lifted."

entries.zh: 汭性剛決，不聽。
entries.en: Cheng was stubborn and would not heed him.
entries.literal: Cheng's nature was stubborn and decisive; he would not listen.

entries.zh: 淮人果乘風縱火，舟盡焚，兵盡溺，汭亦自沈於江，朗人、潭人遂入荊渚，一如所料。
entries.en: The Huai did ride the wind to burn the fleet; every ship was lost and every man drowned; Cheng drowned himself in the river; Lang and Tan troops then overran Jing—exactly as Ting had foretold.
entries.literal: The Huai men indeed rode the wind to set fire; all boats burned, all soldiers drowned; Cheng also drowned himself in the river; men of Lang and Tan then entered the Jing region—just as forecast.

entries.zh: 未幾，襄帥趙匡凝復奏為掌記，入為左補闕。
entries.en: Soon Xiang commander Zhao Kuangning again named him chief recorder; he entered court as Left Supplementation Censor.
entries.literal: Before long Xiang commander Zhao Kuangning again recommended him as chief recorder; he entered court as Left Supplementation Censor.

entries.zh: 又明年，太祖為元帥，以襄陽貳於己，率兵擊破之，趙匡凝奔揚州，太祖復署珽為天平軍掌書記。
entries.en: The next year, as commander-in-chief, the Founder attacked disloyal Xiangyang, broke it, and drove Zhao Kuangning to Yangzhou; he again made Ting secretary of the Tianping army.
entries.literal: The next year the Founder as commander-in-chief, because Xiangyang was disloyal, led troops to defeat it; Zhao Kuangning fled to Yangzhou; the Founder again appointed Ting chief clerk of the Tianping army.

entries.zh: 一日，大會將佐，指珽曰：「此真書記也。」
entries.en: One day at a council of officers he pointed to Ting and said, "There is a real secretary."
entries.literal: One day at a great meeting of officers he pointed to Ting and said: "This is the true secretary."

entries.zh: 杜荀鶴，池州人。
entries.en: Du Xunhe came from Chizhou.
entries.literal: Du Xunhe, a man of Chizhou.

entries.zh: 〈（辛文房《唐才子傳》：荀鶴，字彥之，牧之微子也。）〉
entries.en: (Xin Wenfang's 《Records of Tang Talents》 says Xunhe, styled Yanzhi, was an illegitimate son of Du Mu.)〉
entries.literal: (Xin Wenfang's 《Records of Tang Talents》: Xunhe, style Yanzhi, was a minor son of Muzhi.)〉

entries.zh: 善為詩，辭句切理，為時所許。
entries.en: He wrote poetry with phrases that cut to the point and won contemporary praise.
entries.literal: Skilled at poetry, his phrases cut to reason, approved by the age.

entries.zh: 既擢第，復還舊山。
entries.en: After passing the jinshi he went back to his old home in the hills.
entries.literal: Having passed the examination he returned again to his old mountain.

entries.zh: 〈（《唐才子傳》：荀鶴嘗謁梁王朱全忠，與之坐，忽無雲而雨，王以為天泣不祥，命作詩，稱意，王喜之。
entries.en: (The 《Records of Tang Talents》 records that Xunhe once visited Prince of Liang Zhu Quanzhong; as they sat together rain fell though the sky was clear; the prince took it as heaven weeping and ordered a poem; pleased with it, he was delighted.
entries.literal: (The 《Records of Tang Talents》 says: Xunhe once called on Prince of Liang Zhu Quanzhong and sat with him; suddenly rain fell from a cloudless sky; the prince thought heaven wept—an ill omen—and ordered him to compose a poem; it pleased him and the prince was delighted.

entries.zh: 荀鶴寒進，連敗文場，甚苦，至是送春官。
entries.en: Xunhe had come up in poverty, failed again and again in the examinations, and suffered greatly before he was finally sent to the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: Xunhe came up poor, failed repeatedly in the literary arena, suffered greatly, and only then was sent to the spring office.

entries.zh: 大順二年，裴贄侍郎放第八人登科，正月十日放榜，正荀鶴生朝也。
entries.en: In Dashun 2 Vice Minister Pei Zan placed him eighth on the list; the roster was posted on the tenth day of the first month—Xunhe's own birthday.
entries.literal: In Dazhun year 2 Vice Minister Pei Zan released the eighth man on the rolls; on the tenth day of the first month the list was posted—exactly Xunhe's birthday.

entries.zh: 王希羽獻詩曰：「金榜曉懸生世日，玉書潛記上升時。
entries.en: Wang Xiyu offered a poem: "At dawn the golden list marks the day of his birth; the jade register secretly records the hour of his rise.
entries.literal: Wang Xiyu presented a poem saying: "At dawn the golden list hangs on the day of his birth; the jade record secretly notes the hour of his ascent.

entries.zh: 九華山色高千尺，未必高於第八枝。」
entries.en: Mount Jiuhua stands a thousand feet high—yet hardly towers above the eighth place on the list."
entries.literal: Mount Jiuhua's color rises a thousand feet—yet may not be higher than the eighth branch."

entries.zh: 又，《唐新纂》云：荀鶴舉進士及第，東歸，過夷門，獻梁太祖詩句云：「四海九州空第一，不同諸鎮府封王。」
entries.en: The 《Tang New Compilation》 adds: Xunhe took his jinshi degree, went east, passed Yimen, and gave the Liang Founder this verse: "First in all the realm—unlike the warlords made kings of their circuits."
entries.literal: Further, the 《Tang New Compilation》 says: Xunhe passed the jinshi examination, returned east, passed Yimen, and presented lines to the Liang Founder: "Alone first through the four seas and nine provinces—unlike the various governors enfeoffed as kings."

entries.zh: 是則荀鶴之受知於梁祖舊矣，不待田頵之箋問而始被遇也。）〉
entries.en: So the Liang Founder had known Xunhe long before Tian Yun's letter brought him to court.)〉
entries.literal: Thus Xunhe had long won the Liang Founder's notice and did not await Tian Yun's letter of inquiry before first being received.)〉

entries.zh: 時田頵在宣州，甚重之。
entries.en: Tian Yun was then at Xuanzhou and held him in high esteem.
entries.literal: At that time Tian Yun was at Xuanzhou and valued him greatly.

entries.zh: 頵將起兵，乃陰令以箋問至，太祖遇之頗厚。
entries.en: When Yun prepared to rebel he secretly sent a letter of inquiry ahead; the Founder treated Xunhe very well.
entries.literal: When Yun was about to raise troops he secretly sent a letter of inquiry; the Founder received him quite generously.

entries.zh: 及頵遇禍，太祖以其才表之，尋授翰林學士、主客員外郎。
entries.en: After Yun's fall the Founder praised his talent at court and soon made him Hanlin academician and supernumerary vice director of the Ministry of Reception.
entries.literal: When Yun met disaster the Founder memorialized on his talent and soon made him Hanlin academician and Supernumerary Vice Director in the Ministry of Reception for Dependencies.

entries.zh: 既而恃太祖之勢，凡搢紳間己所不悅者，日屈指怒數，將謀盡殺之。
entries.en: Soon, trusting in the Founder's favor, he daily counted on his fingers the courtiers he hated and plotted to kill them all.
entries.literal: Before long, relying on the Founder's power, among the gentry anyone he disliked he would daily count on his fingers in anger, plotting to kill them all.

entries.zh: 苞蓄未及泄丁重疾，旬日而卒。
entries.en: His grudges had not yet been acted on when he fell gravely ill and died within ten days.
entries.literal: His hoarded spite had not yet been vented when he fell gravely ill and died within ten days.

entries.zh: 滄州節度使劉守文拒命，太祖引兵十餘萬圍之，久而未下，乃召珽草檄。
entries.en: When Cangzhou commissioner Liu Shouwen rebelled the Founder besieged him with more than a hundred thousand men; the city held for long months, and he called on Ting to draft the assault proclamation.
entries.literal: Cangzhou commissioner Liu Shouwen defied orders; the Founder led more than a hundred thousand troops to besiege him; long unable to take it, he summoned Ting to draft a proclamation.

entries.zh: 珽即就外次，筆不停綴，登時而成，大為太祖嗟賞。
entries.en: Ting stepped to a side room and wrote without pause; the draft was done at once and the Founder marveled.
entries.literal: Ting at once went to an outer station, his brush never pausing, finished in the moment, and greatly won the Founder's admiration.

entries.zh: 受禪之歲，宰臣除為考功員外郎、知制誥，珽揣太祖未欲首以舊僚超拜清顯，三上章固辭，優詔褒允，尋以本官監曹州事。
entries.en: In the year of the Founder's enthronement the chief ministers made him Acting Director of Examination and edict drafter; Ting sensed the Founder was loath to promote an old follower straight to a lofty post, declined three times in memorials, received a gracious edict of praise, and soon supervised Cao with his existing rank.
entries.literal: The year of receiving the mandate, the chief ministers appointed him Acting Director of Examination, outer rank, and drafter of edicts; Ting guessed the Founder was unwilling to be the first to advance an old subordinate to a lofty clear post, thrice submitted memorials firmly declining, a gracious edict praised and granted it, and soon with his original office he supervised Cao prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 曹去京數舍，吏民豪猾，前後十餘政，未有善罷者。
entries.en: Cao lay several stages from the capital; its officials and gentry were fierce; more than ten predecessors had left the post in disgrace.
entries.literal: Cao was several post-stages from the capital; officials and people were powerful and crafty; more than ten predecessors in office, none had ended well.

entries.zh: 珽在任期歲，眾庶以寧。
entries.en: In one year under Ting the people were calm.
entries.literal: Ting served one year in term; the multitude was thereby at peace.

entries.zh: 入為兵部郎中、崇政院學士。
entries.en: He was recalled as Bureau Director in the Ministry of War and academician of the Court for Upholding Governance.
entries.literal: He entered court as Bureau Director in the Ministry of War and Academic in the Court for Upholding Governance.

entries.zh: 未幾，以許帥馮行襲疾甚，出為許州留後。
entries.en: Soon, because Xu commander Feng Xingxi was gravely ill, he was sent out as acting governor of Xu.
entries.literal: Before long, because Xu commander Feng Xingxi was gravely ill, he went out as Xu prefecture acting governor.

entries.zh: 先是，行襲有牙兵二千，皆蔡人也，太祖深以為憂，乃遣珽馳往，以伺察之。
entries.en: Xingxi still had two thousand guard troops, all Cai men; the Founder was deeply uneasy and sent Ting post-haste to watch the situation.
entries.literal: Earlier Xingxi had two thousand guard troops, all men of Cai; the Founder deeply worried and sent Ting post-haste to observe them.

entries.zh: 珽至傳舍，召將吏親加撫慰。
entries.en: At the relay station Ting summoned the officers and comforted them in person.
entries.literal: Ting reached the relay station, summoned officers and clerks, and personally added consolation.

entries.zh: 行襲欲使人代受詔，珽曰：「東首加朝服，禮也。」
entries.en: Xingxi wanted a proxy to receive the edict; Ting said, "To face east in court dress is the proper rite."
entries.literal: Xingxi wished to have someone receive the edict in his place; Ting said: "Facing east and putting on court dress is the ritual."

entries.zh: 乃於臥內宣詔，令善自補養，苟有不諱，子孫俱保後福。
entries.en: He read the edict at the bedside, urging him to recover; should the worst come, his sons and grandsons would still enjoy lasting favor.
entries.literal: He then proclaimed the edict within the sickbed chamber, ordering him to nourish himself well; if there should be misfortune, his sons and grandsons would all secure later blessing.

entries.zh: 行襲泣謝，遂解二印以授珽，代掌軍府事。
entries.en: Xingxi wept his thanks and handed Ting both seals to run the headquarters in his stead.
entries.literal: Xingxi wept in thanks, then relinquished two seals to give to Ting, who acted in charge of military headquarters affairs.

entries.zh: 太祖覽奏曰：「予固知珽必辦吾事，行襲門戶不朽矣。」
entries.en: Reading the report, the Founder said, "I knew Ting would handle this for me—Xingxi's line will endure."
entries.literal: The Founder reading the memorial said: "I knew indeed Ting would accomplish my affair; Xingxi's house will not perish."

entries.zh: 乃以珽為匡國軍留後，尋征為左諫議大夫兼宣徽副使。
entries.en: He made Ting acting governor of Kuangguo, then recalled him as Left Remonstrance Grand Master and Vice Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: He then made Ting acting governor of Kuangguo army; soon he was summoned as Left Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 從征至魏縣，過內黃，因侍立於行廄，太祖顧曰：「此何故名內黃？」
entries.en: On campaign at Wei county he passed Neihuang; while attending the Founder at the traveling stable the Founder asked, "Why is this place called Neihuang?"
entries.literal: On campaign he reached Wei county, passed Neihuang, and as he attended standing at the traveling stable the Founder turned and said: "Why is this called Neihuang?"

entries.zh: 珽曰：「河南有外黃、小黃，故此有內黃。」
entries.en: Ting said, "South of the River are Waihuang and Xiaohuang, so this is Neihuang."
entries.literal: Ting said: "South of the River there are Waihuang and Xiaohuang, hence here is Neihuang."

entries.zh: 又曰：「在何處？」
entries.en: The Founder asked, "Where were those?"
entries.literal: He also said: "Where are they?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「秦有外黃都尉，理外黃，有故墉，今在雍丘。
entries.en: He answered, "Qin had a Waihuang commandant; the old rampart is at Yongqiu today.
entries.literal: He replied: "Qin had a Waihuang commandant administering Waihuang; there is an old wall, now at Yongqiu.

entries.zh: 小黃為高齊所廢，其故墉今在陳留。」
entries.en: Xiaohuang was abolished under Northern Qi; its old site is at Chenliu."
entries.literal: Xiaohuang was abolished by Northern Qi; its old wall is now at Chenliu."

entries.zh: 太祖稱獎數四。
entries.en: The Founder praised him again and again.
entries.literal: The Founder praised him several times.

entries.zh: 孫騭，滑台人。
entries.en: Sun Zhi came from Huatai.
entries.literal: Sun Zhi, a man of Huatai.

entries.zh: 嗜學知書，微有辭筆。
entries.en: He loved learning, was well read, and had some skill with the pen.
entries.literal: Fond of learning, knew books, and had slight literary skill.

entries.zh: 唐光啟中，魏博從事公乘億以女妻之，因教以箋奏程式。
entries.en: In Guangqi, Weibo staff officer Gongcheng Yi gave him his daughter in marriage and taught him the forms of memorials and reports.
entries.literal: In Tang Guangqi, Weibo staff officer Gongcheng Yi gave him his daughter in marriage and thereby taught him the forms of memorials and reports.

entries.zh: 時中原多難，文章之士，縮影竄跡不自顯。
entries.en: The central plains were in turmoil; men of letters hid themselves and did not seek notice.
entries.literal: At the time the central plains had many troubles; men of letters shrank their shadows, hid their tracks, and did not display themselves.

entries.zh: 億既死，魏帥以章表箋疏淹積，兼月不能發一字，或以騭為言，即署本職，主奏記事。
entries.en: After Yi died the Wei commander's desk was buried in memorials for more than a month with no reply sent; when Zhi was recommended he was put in charge of drafting at once.
entries.literal: After Yi died the Wei commander had memorials, reports, letters and memos piled up; for a month and more not a word could be sent; someone spoke of Zhi, and he was at once given his proper post, in charge of memorial writing.

entries.zh: 累遷職自支使、掌記至節度判官；
entries.en: He rose from branch commissioner and chief recorder to circuit judicial commissioner;
entries.literal: He rose through posts from branch commissioner, chief recorder, to circuit judicial commissioner;

entries.zh: 奏官自校書、御史郎官、中丞、檢校常侍至兵部尚書。
entries.en: and through presented ranks from collating clerk and censor to bureau director, acting regular attendant, and Minister of War.
entries.literal: and through presented offices from collating clerk, censor, bureau director, acting regular attendant, to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 太祖禦天下，念潛龍時，騭奉其主，好問往來數十返，甚錄之。
entries.en: When the Founder ruled the realm he remembered how Zhi had served him in his rise, their letters going back and forth dozens of times, and valued it highly.
entries.literal: The Founder ruled the realm, recalled his hidden-dragon days when Zhi served his lord, good questions going back and forth several tens of times, and greatly recorded it.

entries.zh: 開平三年，除右諫議大夫，滿歲，遷左散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Kaiping 3 he became Right Remonstrance Grand Master; after a year he was made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
entries.literal: Kaiping year 3 he was made Right Remonstrance Grand Master; at term's end he was transferred to Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

entries.zh: 騭雅好聚書，有《六經》、漢史洎百家之言，凡數千卷，皆簡翰精至，披勘詳定，得暇即朝夕耽玩，曾無少怠。
entries.en: Zhi loved books; he owned several thousand scrolls of the 《Six Classics》, Han histories, and the masters, all finely copied and collated, and whenever he had a moment he read morning and night without slack.
entries.literal: Zhi especially loved collecting books; he had the 《Six Classics》, Han histories, and the masters' words, in all several thousand scrolls, all script refined and examined in detail; when he had leisure he devoured them morning and evening without the slightest slack.

entries.zh: 乾化二年春，太祖將議北巡，選朝士三十餘人扈從。
entries.en: In the spring of Qianhua 2 the Founder planned a northern tour and chose more than thirty court officers to accompany him.
entries.literal: In the spring of Qianhua year 2 the Founder was to deliberate a northern tour and chose more than thirty court officers to attend in escort.

entries.zh: 二月甲子，車駕發自洛陽。
entries.en: On jiazi in the second month the imperial carriage left Luoyang.
entries.literal: Second month, day jiazi, the imperial carriage set out from Luoyang.

entries.zh: 禺中，次白馬頓，召文武官就食，以從臣未集，駐蹕以俟之；
entries.en: At midmorning they stopped at Baima post and called the civil and military officers to eat; the escort had not all arrived, so the procession waited;
entries.literal: At midmorning they halted at Baima post, summoned civil and military officers to eat; because the following ministers were not assembled, the procession halted to wait;

entries.zh: 又命飛騎促於道，而騭與諫議大夫張衍、兵部郎中張俊等累刻方至，太祖性本卞急，因茲大怒，並格殺於前墀。
entries.en: couriers were sent to hurry stragglers on the road, but Zhi, Remonstrance Grand Master Zhang Yan, Bureau Director Zhang Jun, and others arrived only after long delay; the Founder was by nature irascible, flew into a rage, and had them all beaten to death in the forecourt.
entries.literal: and again ordered flying riders to hurry them on the road, but Zhi, Remonstrance Grand Master Zhang Yan, Bureau Director in the Ministry of War Zhang Jun and others, after many quarter-hours only then arrived; the Founder's nature was originally brusque and quick-tempered; thereby he was greatly angry and all were beaten to death on the front courtyard.

entries.zh: 及庶人友珪篡位，除右散騎常侍，充侍講學士。
entries.en: When the commoner Yougui seized the throne, Ting was made Right Regular Cavalry Attendant and lecturer attendant.
entries.literal: When the commoner Yougui usurped the throne, he was appointed Right Regular Cavalry Attendant and served as lecturer attendant.

entries.zh: 內討之日，軍士大擾，珽其夕為亂兵所傷，卒於洛陽。
entries.en: On the day of the inner punitive campaign the army rioted; that night disorderly soldiers wounded Ting, and he died in Luoyang.
entries.literal: On the day of inner punitive action the soldiers were greatly disturbed; that evening Ting was wounded by disorderly troops and died in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 珽性孝友，與弟琪有敦睦之愛，為搢紳所稱。
entries.en: Ting was filial and brotherly; he and his brother Qi were deeply devoted, and the gentry praised them.
entries.literal: Ting's nature was filial and fraternal; with his brother Qi he had affection of close harmony, praised by the gentry.

entries.zh: 〈（案：《歐陽史》有《裴迪》、《韋震傳》，今原文已佚，無可采補。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Ouyang History》 contains biographies of Pei Di and Wei Zhen; the original passage is lost and cannot be restored.)〉
entries.literal: (Comment: the 《Ouyang History》 has biographies of Pei Di and Wei Zhen; the original text here is lost and nothing can be gathered to supplement it.)〉

entries.zh: 盧曾，字孝伯，其先范陽人也。
entries.en: Lu Ceng, styled Xiaobo, was of Fanyang descent.
entries.literal: Lu Ceng, style Xiaobo, his ancestors were men of Fanyang.

entries.zh: 頗好書，有所執守。
entries.en: He loved books and held firm convictions.
entries.literal: He rather loved books and had principles he upheld.

entries.zh: 始為齊州防禦使朱瓊從事，瓊降，預其謀，與之皆來。
entries.en: He first served Qizhou defense commissioner Zhu Qiong; when Qiong surrendered he helped plan it and came over with him.
entries.literal: At first he was staff officer to Qizhou defense commissioner Zhu Qiong; when Qiong surrendered he took part in the plot and came with him.

entries.zh: 瓊沒，太祖辟為宣義幕職。
entries.en: After Qiong died the Founder took him onto the Xuanyi staff.
entries.literal: When Qiong died the Founder recruited him to Xuanyi staff office.

entries.zh: 曾性忠狷，好貢直，又不能取容於眾，每勳府宴語稍洽，曾率然糾正，輒又忤旨。
entries.en: Ceng was loyal and blunt, given to straight talk, and ill at ease in company; whenever princes of merit were at ease in banquet talk, he would suddenly correct them and give offense again.
entries.literal: Ceng's nature was loyal and blunt, fond of candid remonstrance, yet unable to win acceptance from the multitude; whenever the merit princes' mansion banquets grew pleasant, Ceng would abruptly correct them and again offend the intent.

entries.zh: 左長直軍使劉捍委任方重，曾亦不能平。
entries.en: Left long-direct army commissioner Liu Kan was then in full favor; Ceng could not abide him either.
entries.literal: Left long-direct army commissioner Liu Kan's delegated power was then heavy; Ceng also could not get along with him.

entries.zh: 冀王友謙初定陝府，命曾往議事，有使院小將從行，嗜酒，荒逸過度。
entries.en: When Prince of Ji Youqian first secured Shanzhou he sent Ceng to negotiate; a minor officer of the envoy bureau went with him, a drunkard and utterly dissolute.
entries.literal: When Prince of Ji Youqian first secured Shan prefecture he ordered Ceng to go discuss affairs; a minor general of the envoy office accompanied him, fond of wine, dissolute beyond measure.

entries.zh: 曾復命，欲發其罪，致疏於袖中，累日未果言。
entries.en: On his return Ceng meant to report the man's misconduct and kept a memorial in his sleeve, but for days could not bring himself to speak.
entries.literal: Ceng returned to report, wished to expose his crime, put a memorial in his sleeve, and for many days failed to speak.

entries.zh: 小將恐事泄，先誣告曾使酒，幾敗軍事，劉捍因證之，由是罷職，歸於齊之別墅。
entries.en: The officer, fearing exposure, accused Ceng first of drunkenness on duty and nearly wrecked the mission; Liu Kan backed the charge; Ceng was dismissed and retired to a villa in Qi.
entries.literal: The minor general feared exposure, first falsely accused Ceng of being drunk on duty, nearly ruining military affairs; Liu Kan bore witness; thereby he was dismissed and returned to a suburban villa in Qi.

entries.zh: 俄而王師範起兵叛，太祖促召曾，謂之曰：「子能緩頰說青州使無背盟，吾不負子矣。」
entries.en: Soon Wang Shifan rebelled; the Founder urgently summoned Ceng and said, "If you can persuade Qingzhou not to break faith, I will not fail you."
entries.literal: Soon Wang Shifan raised troops in rebellion; the Founder urgently summoned Ceng and said: "If you can soothe Qingzhou and keep them from breaking the alliance, I will not fail you."

entries.zh: 曾持檄以往。
entries.en: Ceng took the edict and set out.
entries.literal: Ceng took the proclamation and went.

entries.zh: 既至青，師範囚之，送於淮南，遇害。
entries.en: At Qingzhou Shifan imprisoned him and sent him to Huainan, where he was killed.
entries.literal: Once he reached Qing, Shifan imprisoned him and sent him to Huainan, where he met disaster.

entries.zh: 後太祖暴師範之罪曰：「喪我骨肉，殺我賓僚。」
entries.en: Later the Founder denounced Shifan's crimes, saying, "He destroyed my kin and slew my retainers."
entries.literal: Later the Founder exposed Shifan's crimes, saying: "He bereaved my flesh and bone, killed my guest officials."

entries.zh: 遂族誅之。
entries.en: He then exterminated Shifan's clan.
entries.literal: He then executed his whole clan.

entries.zh: 因召曾二子，皆授以官。
entries.en: He then summoned Ceng's two sons and gave them both posts.
entries.literal: Thereupon he summoned Ceng's two sons and both gave them office.

entries.zh: 仇殷，不知何郡人也。
entries.en: Chou Yin came from a commandery that is not recorded.
entries.literal: Chou Yin—of what commandery he came is unknown.

entries.zh: 開平中，仕至欽天監，明於象緯曆數，藝術精密，近無其比。
entries.en: In Kaiping he reached Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, master of stars, calendars, and divination, unrivaled in his generation.
entries.literal: In Kaiping he rose to Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, skilled in the constellations, calendrical reckoning, and the arts; in precision none of his day could compare.

entries.zh: 光化中，太祖在滑，遣密王友倫以兵三萬禦幽州之師十餘萬，深慮其不敵，召殷問曰：「陣可行乎？」
entries.en: In Guanghua, at Hua, the Founder secretly sent Prince of Mi Wang Youlun with thirty thousand men against more than a hundred thousand from Youzhou; fearing defeat, he asked Yin: "Can we give battle?"
entries.literal: In Guanghua, when the Founder was at Hua, he secretly sent Prince of Mi Wang Youlun with thirty thousand men against a Youzhou host of more than a hundred thousand; deeply fearing they could not prevail, he summoned Yin and asked: "Can battle lines be formed?"

entries.zh: 曰：「其十四日過禺中乎！」
entries.en: Yin said: "On the fourteenth they will pass mid-morning!"
entries.literal: He said: "On the fourteenth they will pass the mid-morning hour!"

entries.zh: 又問之，曰：「賊敗塗地。」
entries.en: Asked again: "The enemy will be routed."
entries.literal: Asked again, he said: "The rebels will be crushed utterly."

entries.zh: 又曰：「既望，當見捷書。」
entries.en: He added: "On the sixteenth you will see the victory dispatch."
entries.literal: He also said: "On the day after the full moon you will see the victory report."

entries.zh: 果如其言，不失晷刻。
entries.en: Events matched his words to the very hour.
entries.literal: It happened exactly as he said, not missing a moment on the sundial.

entries.zh: 太祖之在長蘆也，諸將請攻壁，號令軍中，人負槁二圍，置千積，俄而雲集。
entries.en: At Changlu the generals urged an assault; the Founder ordered every soldier to carry two bundles of straw and pile a thousand stacks, which soon rose like clouds.
entries.literal: When the Founder was at Changlu the generals asked to assault the walls; he ordered the army that each man carry two armfuls of fodder and set a thousand stacks—soon they piled like clouds.

entries.zh: 殷曰：「何用？」
entries.en: Yin said: "What is the use?"
entries.literal: Yin said: "What use?"

entries.zh: 或以所謀告之，殷曰：「我占矣，不見攻壁象，無乃自退乎！」
entries.en: Told the plan, Yin said: "I have cast the signs—no image of storming walls; they will retreat on their own!"
entries.literal: When they told him the plan, Yin said: "I have divined—there is no sign of assaulting walls; will they not withdraw of themselves!"

entries.zh: 翌日，有騎馳報丁會以潞州叛，太祖令盡焚其槁而還，不克攻。
entries.en: Next day a courier reported Ding Hui's rebellion at Lu; the Founder had the straw burned and marched back without attacking.
entries.literal: The next day a rider galloped in reporting that Ding Hui had rebelled at Luzhou; the Founder ordered all the fodder burned and returned, and the assault was not made.

entries.zh: 開平中，殷一日朝罷，過崇政院，使敬翔直閣，翔問之曰：「月犯房次星，其逼若綴，是何祥也？」
entries.en: In Kaiping, leaving court one day Yin passed the Chongzheng Court where Jing Xiang was on duty; Xiang asked: "The moon encroaches on a star in Fang—the approach looks slow; what omen is this?"
entries.literal: In Kaiping, one day after court Yin passed the Chongzheng Court and had Attendant Jing Xiang on duty; Xiang asked him: "The moon trespasses on a star in the Fang mansion—the approach seems drawn out; what omen is this?"

entries.zh: 曰：「常度耳。」
entries.en: Yin said: "Nothing unusual."
entries.literal: He said: "A routine measure."

entries.zh: 殷欲不言，既過數步，自度不可默，乃反言曰：「三兩日當有不順語至，無或驟恐，宜先白上知。」
entries.en: He meant to say nothing; after a few steps he turned back: "In two or three days bad news will come—do not be alarmed; tell the Emperor first."
entries.literal: Yin wished not to speak; having gone several paces he reckoned he could not keep silent, turned back and said: "In two or three days ill news will arrive—do not panic suddenly; you should first inform His Majesty."

entries.zh: 既二日，陝府奏同州劉知俊閉關作叛。
entries.en: Two days later Shaanxi reported that Liu Zhijun of Tong had shut the passes and rebelled.
entries.literal: Two days later Shaanxi memorialized that Tongzhou's Liu Zhijun had closed the passes and rebelled.

entries.zh: 初，王景仁之出師也。
entries.en: Earlier, when Wang Jingren took the field.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Wang Jingren marched out.

entries.zh: 殷上言：「太陰虧，不利深入。」
entries.en: Yin warned: "The moon is waning—deep advance is unlucky."
entries.literal: Yin memorialized: "The yin moon is deficient—deep advance is ill-omened."

entries.zh: 太祖遽遣使止之，已敗於柏鄉矣。
entries.en: The Founder hurriedly sent orders to halt him, but Jingren had already been beaten at Baixiang.
entries.literal: The Founder hastily sent an envoy to stop him, but he had already been defeated at Baixiang.

entries.zh: 殷所見觸類如是，不可備錄。
entries.en: Cases like these fill his record and cannot all be given here.
entries.literal: Yin's divinations of this sort cannot all be recorded.

entries.zh: 然而畏慎特甚，居常寢默，未嘗敢顯言。
entries.en: Yet he was deeply cautious, usually kept silent, and never dared speak openly.
entries.literal: Yet he was exceedingly timid; he usually slept in silence and never dared speak plainly.

entries.zh: 縱言事跡，惟其語音，不可盡曉，以故屢貽責罰。
entries.en: When he did speak, his accent made him hard to understand, and he was often fined for it.
entries.literal: Even when he spoke of events, only his speech—none could fully understand—and for that he was repeatedly fined and punished.

entries.zh: 後卒於官。
entries.en: He later died in office.
entries.literal: Later he died in office.

entries.zh: 張俊，字彥臣。
entries.en: Zhang Jun, styled Yanchen.
entries.literal: Zhang Jun, style Yanchen.

entries.zh: 祖、父咸有聞於時。
entries.en: Both his grandfather and father were known in their day.
entries.literal: Grandfather and father both had repute in the age.

entries.zh: 俊少孤，自修飾，善為五言詩，其警句頗為人所稱。
entries.en: Orphaned young, he cultivated himself, wrote fine five-character verse, and his striking lines won praise.
entries.literal: Jun was orphaned young, self-cultivated in deportment, skilled at five-character verse; his striking lines were often praised by men.

entries.zh: 唐廣明中，黃巢犯京師，天子幸蜀，士皆竄伏窟穴，以保其生。
entries.en: In Guangming Huang Chao took the capital; the emperor fled to Shu; scholars hid wherever they could to survive.
entries.literal: In Tang Guangming, Huang Chao violated the capital; the Son of Heaven went to Shu; scholars all hid in holes and caves to preserve their lives.

entries.zh: 俊亦晦跡浮泛，不失其道。
entries.en: Jun too kept out of sight and drifted, yet never abandoned his principles.
entries.literal: Jun also concealed his tracks and drifted, not losing his way.

entries.zh: 及僖宗還京師，由校書郎、西畿尉登朝為御史、補闕、起居郎、司勳員外、萬年縣令，以事黜官峽中，將十年。
entries.en: When Xizong returned he rose from collating clerk and western capital district magistrate to censor, supplementation official, attendance director, acting director in the Bureau of Merit, and magistrate of Wan'ian; an offense sent him into exile in the gorges for nearly ten years.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital he rose from collating clerk and western capital district magistrate to court as censor, supplementation official, director of attendance, acting director in the Bureau of Merit, and Wan'ian county magistrate; for an affair he was dismissed to the gorges of the Three Gorges, nearly ten years.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，用宰臣薛貽矩為鹽鐵使，俊與貽矩同年登第，甚知其才，即奏為鹽鐵判官，遷職為禮部郎中，兼職如故。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne chief minister Xue Yiju became salt and iron commissioner; Jun had passed the jinshi with Yiju and knew his ability; he was soon made salt and iron judicial commissioner, then Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites while keeping the same concurrent duties.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne he used chief minister Xue Yiju as salt and iron commissioner; Jun and Yiju had passed the examination in the same year and well knew his talent; he at once memorialized Jun as salt and iron judicial commissioner, promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites, concurrent post as before.

entries.zh: 乾化二年二月，扈從後至，與孫騭、張衍同日遇禍於白馬頓。
entries.en: In the second month of Qianhua 2 he came late on the northern tour and, with Sun Zhi and Zhang Yan, was killed the same day at Baima post.
entries.literal: Qianhua year 2 second month, he came late in escort and with Sun Zhi and Zhang Yan on the same day met disaster at Baima post.

entries.zh: 張衍，字元用，河南尹魏王宗奭之猶子也。
entries.en: Zhang Yan, styled Yuanyong, was a nephew of Henan prefect and Prince of Wei Zong Shi.
entries.literal: Zhang Yan, style Yuanyong, was a nephew of Henan prefect and Prince of Wei Zong Shi.

entries.zh: 其父死於兵間。
entries.en: His father had died in the wars.
entries.literal: His father died amid war.

entries.zh: 衍樂讀書為儒，始以經學就舉，不中選。
entries.en: Yan loved the classics and first tried the civil service examination on classical learning but failed.
entries.literal: Yan delighted in reading books as a classicist; at first with classical learning he took the examination but was not selected.

entries.zh: 時諫議大夫鄭徽退居洛陽，以女妻之，遂令應辭科，不數上登第。
entries.en: Remonstrance Grand Master Zheng Hui, retired in Luoyang, gave him his daughter and had him try the literary examination; he passed after only a few attempts.
entries.literal: At the time Remonstrance Grand Master Zheng Hui retired to Luoyang, gave him his daughter in marriage, and then had him take the literary examination; in not many attempts he passed.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗東遷，以宗奭勳力隆峻，衍由校書郎拜左拾遺，旋召為翰林學士。
entries.en: When Zhaozong moved east, on Zong Shi's great merit Yan rose from collating clerk to Left Collector and Memorialist and was soon made Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhaozong moved east, because Zong Shi's merit was lofty and weighty, Yan from collating clerk was appointed Left Collector and Memorialist, and soon summoned as Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，罷之，特拜考功郎中，俄遷右諫議大夫。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne Yan was removed from the Hanlin post, made Acting Director of Examination, and soon Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne he was dismissed, specially appointed Acting Director of Examination in the inner rank, and soon transferred to Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

entries.zh: 衍巧生業，樂積聚。
entries.en: Yan was shrewd at profit and loved to hoard wealth.
entries.literal: Yan was clever at making a living and delighted in accumulation.

entries.zh: 太祖將北伐，頗以扈從間糜耗力用係意，屢幹托宰執求免是行；
entries.en: As the Founder prepared a northern campaign Yan dreaded the cost of escort duty and repeatedly asked the chief ministers to excuse him from the journey;
entries.literal: The Founder was about to campaign north; he greatly tied his mind to the waste of effort in escort service; repeatedly pleaded with the chief executives to be excused from this journey;

entries.zh: 太祖微聞之，又屬應召稽晚，與孫騭等同日遇禍。
entries.en: the Founder caught wind of it; when Yan was also slow to answer the summons he suffered the same fate as Sun Zhi that day.
entries.literal: the Founder slightly heard of it, and again as he was slow in answering the summons, with Sun Zhi and the rest he met disaster on the same day.

entries.zh: 羅隱，
entries.en: Luo Yin,
entries.literal: Luo Yin,

entries.zh: 〈（《唐才子傳》：隱字昭諫。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 gives his style as Zhaojian.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 says: Yin, style Zhaojian.)〉

entries.zh: 餘杭人。
entries.en: was from Yuhang.
entries.literal: a native of Yuhang.

entries.zh: 詩名於天下，尤長於詠史，然多所譏諷，以故不中第，大為唐宰相鄭畋、李蔚所知。
entries.en: His verse was known everywhere; he excelled at historical poems but often mocked his betters, failed the examinations for it, and was nevertheless prized by chancellors Zheng Tian and Li Wei.
entries.literal: His poetry was famed throughout the realm; he was especially adept at historical verse, yet often satirical, and for that reason never passed the examinations—though greatly esteemed by Tang chancellors Zheng Tian and Li Wei.

entries.zh: 隱雖負文稱，然貌古而陋。
entries.en: For all his literary fame, Yin looked old and plain.
entries.literal: Though Yin bore a literary reputation, his appearance was archaic and uncomely.

entries.zh: 畋女幼有文性，嘗覽隱詩卷，諷誦不已，畋疑其女有慕才之意。
entries.en: Tian's daughter was literary; reading Yin's poems she could not stop reciting them, and Tian thought she admired the poet.
entries.literal: Tian's daughter had literary gifts from youth; once reading Yin's poetry she recited it endlessly, and Tian suspected she admired the man's talent.

entries.zh: 一日，隱至第，鄭女垂簾而窺之，自是絕不詠其詩。
entries.en: When Yin visited the house the girl peeked through the curtain; from then on she never read his verse again.
entries.literal: One day Yin came to the mansion; the Zheng girl peered through a lowered curtain—after that she never chanted his poems again.

entries.zh: 唐廣明中，因亂歸鄉里，節度使錢鏐辟為從事。
entries.en: During Guangming he went home in the turmoil; Qian Liu of Zhexi took him on as staff.
entries.literal: In Tang's Guangming era, owing to disorder he returned home; military commissioner Qian Liu engaged him as staff.

entries.zh: 開平初，太祖以右諫議大夫征，不至。
entries.en: At the start of Kaiping the Founder called him to court as Right Remonstrance Counselor; he refused.
entries.literal: Early in Kaiping the Founder summoned him as Right Remonstrance Counselor; he did not come.

entries.zh: 魏博節度使羅紹威密表推薦，乃授給事中。
entries.en: Luo Shaowei of Wei-Bo secretly recommended him, and he was made Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: Wei-Bo military commissioner Luo Shaowei secretly memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 年八十餘，終於錢塘。
entries.en: He was over eighty when he died at Qiantang.
entries.literal: Over eighty years old, he died at Qiantang.

entries.zh: 〈（《澗泉日記》云：唐光啟三年，吳越王表奏為錢塘令，遷著作郎，辟掌書記。
entries.en: (The 《Jianquan Diary》 says: In Guangqi 3 the King of Wuyue had him made magistrate of Qiantang, then drafting gentleman and chief secretary.
entries.literal: (The 《Jianquan Diary》 says: In Tang Guangqi 3 the King of Wuyue memorialized him as magistrate of Qiantang, promoted him to Drafting Gentleman, and engaged him as chief secretary.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，充判官。
entries.en: In Tianyou 3 he was a judge-adviser.
entries.literal: In Tianyou 3 he served as judge-adviser.

entries.zh: 梁開平二年，授給事中。
entries.en: In Kaiping 2 of Liang he became Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: In Liang Kaiping 2 he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 三年，遷發運使。
entries.en: In year 3 he was made grain transport commissioner.
entries.literal: Year 3 he was transferred to grain transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 是年卒，葬於定山鄉。
entries.en: He died that year and was buried in Dingshan township.
entries.literal: That year he died and was buried in Dingshan township.

entries.zh: 金部郎中沈崧銘其墓。）〉
entries.en: Shen Song of the Revenue Department wrote his tomb inscription.)〉
entries.literal: Revenue-department cadre Shen Song inscribed his tomb.)〉

entries.zh: 有文集數卷行於世。
entries.en: Several fascicles of his collected works still circulate.
entries.literal: Several fascicles of collected works circulate in the world.

entries.zh: 〈（《唐才子傳》云：隱所著《讒書》、《讒本》、《淮海寓言》、《湘南應用集》、《甲乙集》、外集啟事等，並行於世。
entries.en: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 lists his 《Book of Satire》, 《Satire Originals》, 《Parables of Huaihai》, 《Applied Collection of Xiangnan》, 《Jia-yi Collection》, memorial collections, and other works in circulation.
entries.literal: (The 《Biographies of Tang Talents》 says: Yin's works—the 《Book of Satire》, 《Satire Originals》, 《Parables of Huaihai》, 《Applied Collection of Xiangnan》, 《Jia-yi Collection》, outer collections of memorials and the like—all circulate.

entries.zh: 《五代史補》：羅隱在科場，恃才傲物，尤為公卿所惡，故六舉不第。
entries.en: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: In the examinations Yin leaned on his talent, was proud and rude, and was so hated by the great families that he failed six times.
entries.literal: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Luo Yin in the examination field, relying on talent and arrogant toward others, was especially hated by court nobles, and thus failed six times.

entries.zh: 時長安有羅尊師者，深於相術，隱以貌陋，恐為相術所棄，每與尊師接談，常自大以沮之。
entries.en: In Chang'an there was a Master Luo skilled in physiognomy; Yin, fearing his looks would doom him, always bragged when they met to discourage a reading.
entries.literal: At that time in Chang'an there was Master Luo, deep in physiognomy; Yin, fearing his ugly looks would be rejected by the art, whenever he talked with the master would boast greatly to put him off.

entries.zh: 及其累遭黜落，不得已始往問焉。
entries.en: After repeated failures he finally went to ask his fortune.
entries.literal: After repeated failures he had no choice and at last went to ask.

entries.zh: 尊師笑曰：「貧道知之久矣，但以吾子決在一第，未可與語。
entries.en: The master laughed: "I have known you long—but you are fated for only one jinshi success, and until now I could not tell you.
entries.literal: The master laughed and said: "This poor Taoist has known long—but your fate is fixed at a single jinshi pass, and I could not yet speak with you.

entries.zh: 今日之事，貧道敢有所隱乎！
entries.en: Today I dare hide nothing from you!
entries.literal: Today's matter—can this poor Taoist still hide anything!

entries.zh: 且吾子之於一第也，貧道觀之，雖首冠群英，亦不過簿尉爾。
entries.en: Even if you topped the jinshi list, I see you rising no higher than a county clerk or sheriff.
entries.literal: As for your jinshi, this poor Taoist sees that even were you first among all the gifted, you would rise no higher than registrar or sheriff.

entries.zh: 若能罷舉，東歸霸國以求用，則必富且貴矣。
entries.en: Quit the examinations, go east to the hegemon's court, and you will grow rich and honored.
entries.literal: If you can abandon the examinations, return east to the hegemon's state and seek employment, then you will surely be rich and noble.

entries.zh: 兩途，吾子宜自擇之。」
entries.en: Two paths—choose between them."
entries.literal: Two roads—my son, choose for yourself."

entries.zh: 隱懵然不知所措者數日。
entries.en: Yin was stunned and for days could not decide.
entries.literal: Yin was dazed and for several days did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 鄰居有賣飯媼，見隱驚曰：「何辭色之沮喪如此，莫有不決之事否？」
entries.en: A neighbor who sold meals saw his gloom and said: "Why so wretched—something you cannot decide?"
entries.literal: A neighbor who sold meals, seeing Yin's dismay, said in surprise: "Why such a downcast look—surely something is unresolved?"

entries.zh: 隱謂知之，因盡以尊師之言告之。
entries.en: Thinking she might understand, he told her everything the master had said.
entries.literal: Yin thought she understood and told her the master's words in full.

entries.zh: 媼歎曰：「秀才何自迷甚焉，且天下皆知羅隱，何須一第然後為得哉！
entries.en: She sighed: "Scholar, you fool yourself! Everyone knows Luo Yin—why must a degree be your only success?
entries.literal: The old woman sighed: "Scholar, how deeply you mislead yourself! All the world knows Luo Yin—why must a jinshi degree be the only way to succeed!

entries.zh: 不如急取富貴，則老婆之願也。」
entries.en: Take wealth and office now—that is what I wish for you."
entries.literal: Better hurry to wealth and rank—that is this old woman's wish."

entries.zh: 隱聞之釋然，遂歸錢塘。
entries.en: Relieved, he went straight back to Qiantang.
entries.literal: Hearing this Yin felt relieved and at once returned to Qiantang.

entries.zh: 時錢鏐方得兩浙，置之幕府，使典軍中書檄，其後官給事中。
entries.en: Qian Liu had just taken the two Zhes; he put Yin in his secretariat to draft army papers and later made him Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: Qian Liu had just secured the two Zhes; he placed Yin in his staff to draft military documents, and afterward made him Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 初，隱罷上中書之日，費窘，因抵魏謁鄴王羅紹威，將入其境，先貽書敘其家世，鄴王為侄。
entries.en: Once, broke after failing the Secretariat exam, he went to Wei to see Luo Shaowei and beforehand sent a letter claiming kinship—the prince was his nephew.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yin left the capital after failing the Secretariat examination, he was in straits; he therefore went to Wei to visit Prince Luo Shaowei and, before entering his territory, sent a letter stating their family kinship—the prince was his nephew.

entries.zh: 幕府僚吏見其書，皆怒曰：「羅隱一布衣爾，而侄視大王，其可乎！」
entries.en: His staff read the letter and cried: "Luo Yin is a nobody—yet he calls the prince his nephew! Impossible!"
entries.literal: Staff officers who saw the letter all said in anger: "Luo Yin is only a commoner—yet he treats the king as nephew! How can that be!"

entries.zh: 紹威素重士，且曰：「羅隱名振天下，王公大夫多為所薄，今惠然肯顧，其何以勝！
entries.en: Shaowei, who loved scholars, said: "Luo Yin's name fills the realm; lords and ministers he has often scorned—now he honors me—how can I not be overwhelmed!
entries.literal: Shaowei had always valued scholars and said: "Luo Yin's name shakes the world; many lords and grandees he has belittled—now that he willingly comes, how can I not be overcome!

entries.zh: 得在侄行，為幸多矣，敢不致恭，諸公慎勿言。」
entries.en: To receive him as a nephew is already my luck; I dare not be cold—say nothing, gentlemen."
entries.literal: To stand in the nephew's place is already great fortune; how dare I not show respect—gentlemen, say no more."

entries.zh: 於是擁旆郊迎，一見即拜，隱亦不讓。
entries.en: He went out with banners to meet him at the suburbs, bowed at once, and Yin accepted without demur.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went with banners to welcome him at the suburbs; at first sight he bowed, and Yin did not decline.

entries.zh: 及將行，紹威贈以百萬，他物稱是，仍致書於鏐謂叔父，鏐首用之。）〉
entries.en: On his departure Shaowei gave him a million cash and rich gifts, and wrote Qian Liu as to an uncle—Liu took him up at once.)〉
entries.literal: When Yin was about to leave, Shaowei gave him a million in cash and gifts in proportion, and also wrote Qian Liu calling him uncle—Liu employed him from the first.)〉

entries.zh: 段深，不知何許人。
entries.en: Duan Shen came from a place that is not recorded.
entries.literal: Duan Shen—of what place he came is unknown.

entries.zh: 開平中，以善醫待詔於翰林。
entries.en: In Kaiping, as a skilled physician, he served in the Hanlin.
entries.literal: In Kaiping, for skill in medicine he attended at court in the Hanlin.

entries.zh: 時太祖抱疾久之，其溲甚濁，僧曉微侍藥有征，賜紫衣師號，錫賚甚厚。
entries.en: The Founder had been ill a long time with foul urine; the monk Xiaowei treated him with success and received purple robes, a master's title, and lavish rewards.
entries.literal: The Founder had long been ill; his urine was very turbid; the monk Xiaowei attended with medicine that took effect, and he was given purple robes, a master's title, and very rich gifts.

entries.zh: 頃之疾發，曉微剝服色，去師號。
entries.en: When the illness returned, Xiaowei lost his robes and title.
entries.literal: Soon the illness flared again; Xiaowei was stripped of his robes and title.

entries.zh: 因召深問曰：「疾愈復作，草藥不足恃也，我左右粒石而效者眾矣，服之如何？」
entries.en: The Founder called Shen and asked: "I improved and relapsed—herbs are not enough; many at court swear by powdered stone—should I take it?"
entries.literal: The Founder then summoned Shen and asked: "The illness eased and has returned—herbs are not to be relied on; many around me have taken powdered stone with effect—how would it be to take it?"

entries.zh: 深對曰：「臣嘗奉詔診切，陛下積憂勤，失調護，脈代芤而心益虛。
entries.en: Shen answered: "When I examined Your Majesty by order, I found long worry and overwork, poor care, a hollow pulse, and a weakening heart.
entries.literal: Shen replied: "Your servant has examined Your Majesty by imperial order; Your Majesty has accumulated worry and toil, lost proper care, the pulse is hollow in succession and the heart grows ever weaker.

entries.zh: 臣以為宜先治心，心和平而溲變清，當進飲劑，而不當粒石也。
entries.en: Treat the heart first; when the heart is calm the urine will clear—give decoctions, not powdered stone.
entries.literal: Your servant thinks the heart should be treated first; when the heart is calm the urine will clear—decoctions should be given, not powdered stone.

entries.zh: 臣謹案，《太倉公傳》曰：『中熱不溲者不可服石，石性精悍，有大毒。』
entries.en: I cite the 《Biography of the Granary Lord》: 'Internal heat with no urine forbids stone medicine; stone is sharp, fierce, and highly toxic.'
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully notes that the 《Biography of the Granary Lord》 says: 'One who has internal heat and cannot urinate must not take stone; stone is keen and fierce and greatly toxic.'

entries.zh: 凡餌毒藥如甲兵，不得已而用之，非有危殆，不可服也。」
entries.en: Poisonous drugs are like arms—use them only when there is no other way; without mortal danger, do not take them."
entries.literal: All taking poisonous drugs is like deploying armor—use them only when there is no choice; without grave danger they must not be taken."

entries.zh: 太祖善之，令進飲劑，疾稍愈，乃以幣帛賜之。
entries.en: The Founder agreed, took decoctions, improved somewhat, and rewarded him with silks.
entries.literal: The Founder approved, ordered decoctions given, the illness eased somewhat, and then bestowed silks on him.

entries.zh: 李珽，字公度，隴西敦煌人。
entries.en: Li Ting, styled Gongdu, came from Dunhuang in Longxi.
entries.literal: Li Ting, style Gongdu, a man of Dunhuang in Longxi.

entries.zh: 五世祖忠懿公憕，有大節，見《唐史》。
entries.en: His fifth-generation ancestor, Duke of Loyal Benevolence Cheng, was a man of great principle, as recorded in the 《History of Tang》.
entries.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Duke of Loyal Benevolence Cheng had great integrity; see the 《History of Tang》.

entries.zh: 父縠，仕懿、僖朝，官至右諫議大夫。
entries.en: His father Gu had served under Emperors Yizong and Xizong and reached the post of Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
entries.literal: His father Gu served in the Yi and Xi reigns and rose to Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

entries.zh: 珽聰悟，有才學，尤工詞賦。
entries.en: Ting was quick-minded, widely read, and especially gifted at rhapsodies and fu.
entries.literal: Ting was sharp-witted, learned, and especially skilled at lyric prose.

entries.zh: 僖宗朝，晉公王鐸提兵柄，鎮滑台，縠居賓席，鐸見珽，大賞歎之。
entries.en: During Xizong's reign Duke of Jin Wang Duo held the armies at Huatai; Gu was among his retainers; when Duo met Ting he admired him greatly.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xizong's reign Duke of Jin Wang Duo held military authority and governed Huatai; Gu sat among his guests; Duo met Ting and greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 年二十四登進士第，解褐授校書郎，拜監察御史，俄丁內艱。
entries.en: At twenty-four he passed the jinshi, entered service as collating clerk, became investigating censor, and soon entered mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: At twenty-four he passed the jinshi examination, left the robe for collating clerk, was appointed investigating censor, and soon mourned his mother.

entries.zh: 先是，父旅殯在遠，家貧無以襄事，與弟琪當臘雪以單縗扶杖，銜哀告人，由是兩克遷祔。
entries.en: His father's coffin had long lain far from home and the family was too poor to bury him properly; Ting and his brother Qi, in deep winter snow, wore plain hemp mourning and leaned on staffs as they went begging in grief until they could bring both parents home for joint burial.
entries.literal: Earlier his father's body lay in burial far away; the family was poor and could not afford the funeral; with his brother Qi, in midwinter snow, in plain hemp mourning garments and leaning on staffs, they grieved and begged people, and thereby managed to relocate both for joint enshrinement.

entries.zh: 而珽日不過食一溢，恒羸臥喪廬中不能興。
entries.en: Ting ate barely a dipper of food a day, grew gaunt, and for long stretches could not leave the mourning hut.
entries.literal: Yet Ting ate no more than one dipper a day, constantly emaciated lying in the mourning hut unable to rise.

entries.zh: 大為時賢所歎。
entries.en: Men of the age greatly admired him for it.
entries.literal: Greatly admired by the worthies of the age.

entries.zh: 憂闋，再征為御史，以瘠不起。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was summoned again as censor but was too frail to serve.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was again summoned as censor but was too emaciated to take office.

entries.zh: 成汭之鎮荊州，辟為掌書記，逾時乃就。
entries.en: When Cheng Rui took Jingzhou he made Ting his chief secretary; Ting delayed some time before accepting.
entries.literal: When Cheng Yan governed Jingzhou he recruited him as chief clerk; only after some time did he accept.

entries.zh: 三月，邢州節度使安知建叛，奔青州。
entries.en: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.
entries.literal: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 天子以知建為神武統軍，自棣州溯河歸朝。
entries.en: The emperor named him commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court up the river from Di Prefecture.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven made Zhijian commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court by river upstream from Di Prefecture.

entries.zh: 鄆州朱瑄邀斬於河上，傳首晉陽。
entries.en: Zhu Xuan of Yanzhou cut him down on the river and sent his head to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Yanzhou's Zhu Xuan intercepted and beheaded him on the river, and sent the head to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 以李存孝為邢州節度使。
entries.en: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.
entries.literal: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.

entries.zh: 四月，武皇大舉兵討赫連鐸於雲州，遣騎將薛阿檀率前軍以進攻，武皇設伏兵於御河之上，大破之，因塹守其城。
entries.en: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army against Helian Duo at Yunzhou, sent the cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to press the attack, and set ambushers along the Yu River; he broke Duo utterly and then walled the city in.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army to attack Helian Duo at Yun Prefecture, sent cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to advance the assault; Wuhuang set ambush troops above the Yu River, routed them utterly, and thereby besieged the city with trenches.

entries.zh: 七月，武皇進軍柳會，赫連鐸力屈食盡，奔於吐渾部，遂歸幽州，雲州平。
entries.en: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Duo, out of strength and food, fled to the Tuyuhun and then to Youzhou; Yunzhou was pacified.
entries.literal: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Duo, strength exhausted and provisions spent, fled to the Tuyuhun, then went to You Prefecture; Yun Prefecture was pacified.

entries.zh: 武皇表石善友為大同軍防禦使。
entries.en: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.
entries.literal: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

entries.zh: 邢州節度使李存孝以鎮州王熔托附汴人，謀亂河朔，北連燕寇，請乘雲、代之捷，平定燕、趙，武皇然之。
entries.en: Li Cunxiao of Xing, seeing that Wang Rong of Zhen had thrown in with Bian, plotted to stir trouble in Hebei and ally with Yan in the north; he asked to use the Yun and Dai victories to pacify Yan and Zhao, and Wuhuang agreed.
entries.literal: Xing military commissioner Li Cunxiao, because Zhen's Wang Rong had entrusted himself to Bian, plotted to throw Hebei into disorder and link with northern Yan raiders; he asked to use the victory at Yun and Dai to pacify Yan and Zhao; Wuhuang agreed.

entries.zh: 八月，大搜於晉陽，遂南巡澤、潞，略地懷、孟，河陽趙克裕望風送款，請修鄰好。
entries.en: In the eighth month he held a great hunt at Jinyang, then marched south through Ze and Lu and overran Huai and Meng; Zhao Keyu of Heyang submitted at his approach and asked for peace between neighbors.
entries.literal: In the eighth month a great hunt was held at Jinyang; then he toured south through Ze and Lu, overran the lands of Huai and Meng; Heyang's Zhao Keyu submitted at the first rumor of his approach and asked for neighborly peace.

entries.zh: 九月，蒐於邢州。
entries.en: In the ninth month he hunted at Xingzhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth month a hunt at Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 十月，李存孝董前軍攻臨城，鎮人五萬營於臨城西北龍尾崗。
entries.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao led the vanguard against Lincheng; fifty thousand men of Zhen camped on Longwei Ridge northwest of the city.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao directed the vanguard to attack Lincheng; fifty thousand Zhen troops encamped at Longwei Ridge northwest of Lincheng.

entries.zh: 武皇令李存審、李存賢以步軍攻之，鎮人大敗，殺獲萬計，拔臨城，進攻元氏。
entries.en: Wuhuang sent Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with infantry against them; the Zhen army was routed, with tens of thousands killed or taken; Lincheng fell and the attack moved on Yuanshi.
entries.literal: Wuhuang ordered Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with foot troops to attack them; the Zhen army was badly defeated, with tens of thousands killed or captured; Lincheng was taken and the attack pressed on Yuanshi.

entries.zh: 幽州李匡威以步騎五萬營於鄗邑，以援鎮州，武皇分兵大掠，旋軍邢州。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou camped at Hao with fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang split his forces for wide raiding and then wheeled back to Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Youzhou's Li Kuangwei with fifty thousand foot and horse encamped at Hao town to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang divided his forces for wide plunder and then turned the army back to Xing.

entries.zh: 太祖武皇帝，諱克用，本姓朱耶氏，其先隴右金城人也。
entries.en: The Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, personal name Keyong, was born of the Zhuye clan; his ancestors came from Jincheng in Longyou.
entries.literal: Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, taboo name Keyong, originally surnamed Zhuye; his forebears were men of Jincheng in Longyou.

entries.zh: 始祖拔野，唐貞觀中為墨離軍使，從太宗討高麗、薛延陁有功，為金方道副都護，因家於瓜州。
entries.en: The founding ancestor Baye served as Mori Army commissioner under Zhenguan; he followed Taizong against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo, was rewarded as deputy protector of the Jin-fang Circuit, and settled his family at Guazhou.
entries.literal: Founding ancestor Baye, in Tang Zhenguan served as Mori Army commissioner; following Taizong in campaigns against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo he had merit, was made Deputy Protector-General of the Jin-fang Circuit, and took residence at Guazhou.

entries.zh: 太宗平薛延陁諸部，於安西、北庭置都護屬之，分同羅、仆骨之人，置沙陁都督府。
entries.en: After Taizong subdued the Xueyantuo, he set protectors at Anxi and Beiting, assigned the Tongluo and Pugu to them, and founded the Shatuo Chief Commandery.
entries.literal: Taizong pacified the Xueyantuo tribes, placed protectors at Anxi and Beiting subject to them, divided the Tongluo and Pugu peoples, and established the Shatuo Chief Commandery.

entries.zh: 蓋北庭有磧曰沙陁，故因以為名焉。
entries.en: A desert tract at Beiting was called Shatuo, and the name followed from that.
entries.literal: For Beiting had a desert tract called Shatuo, hence the name.

entries.zh: 永徽中，以拔野為都督，其後子孫五世相承。
entries.en: Under Yonghui, Baye became chief; five generations of his line succeeded one another.
entries.literal: In Yonghui, Baye was made chief; thereafter descendants held the post for five generations in succession.

entries.zh: 曾祖盡忠，貞元中，繼為沙陀府都督。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Jingzhong became Shatuo prefectural chief in the Zhenyuan era.
entries.literal: Great-grandfather Jingzhong, in Zhenyuan, succeeded as Shatuo prefectural chief.

entries.zh: 既而為吐蕃所陷，乃舉其族七千帳徙於甘州。
entries.en: The Tibetans soon overran him; he led seven thousand tents of his clan to relocate at Ganzhou.
entries.literal: Soon after he was trapped by the Tibetans; he then moved his clan, seven thousand tents, to Ganzhou.

entries.zh: 盡忠尋率部眾三萬東奔，俄而吐蕃追兵大至，盡忠戰歿。
entries.en: Jingzhong soon fled east with thirty thousand followers; Tibetan pursuit caught up and he fell in battle.
entries.literal: Jingzhong soon led thirty thousand of his following east in flight; presently Tibetan pursuers came in force and Jingzhong died in battle.

entries.zh: 祖執宜，即盡忠之長子也，收合餘眾，至於靈州，德宗命為陰山府都督。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, rallied the survivors, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong made him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.
entries.literal: Grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, gathered the remnant following, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong appointed him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 元和初，入為金吾將軍，遷蔚州刺史、代北行營招撫使。
entries.en: Early in Yuanhe he became a Golden Crow general, then prefect of Wei and pacification commissioner for the northern Dai frontier.
entries.literal: At the start of Yuanhe he entered court as Golden Crow general, was transferred to prefect of Wei, and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書·沙陀傳》：元和三年，盡忠款靈州塞，詔處其部鹽州置陰山府，以執宜為府兵馬使。
entries.en: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》 says: In Yuanhe 3 Jingzhong came in at Lingzhou; the court settled his people at Yanzhou as Yinshan Prefecture and made Zhiyi its horse commissioner.
entries.literal: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》: In Yuanhe year 3 Jingzhong submitted at the Lingzhou pass; an edict settled his tribe at Yanzhou and established Yinshan Prefecture, making Zhiyi prefectural horse commissioner.

entries.zh: 朝長安，授特進、金吾衛將軍。
entries.en: At Chang'an he received Special Advancement and a post in the Golden Crow Guard.
entries.literal: He attended court at Chang'an and was given Special Advancement and general of the Golden Crow Guard.

entries.zh: 從攻鎮州，進蔚州刺史。
entries.en: He took part in the Zhenzhou campaign and was promoted to Wei prefect.
entries.literal: Following the attack on Zhen prefecture, he was advanced to prefect of Wei.

entries.zh: 破吳元濟，授檢校刑部尚書。
entries.en: After Wu Yuanji was broken he received the acting post of Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Defeating Wu Yuanji, he was made acting Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 長慶初，破賊深州，入朝留宿衛，拜金吾衛將軍。
entries.en: Early in Changqing he crushed rebels at Shenzhou, stayed at court on palace guard duty, and became a Golden Crow Guard general.
entries.literal: At the start of Changqing he defeated bandits at Shen prefecture, entered court and remained on palace guard, and was made general of the Golden Crow Guard.

entries.zh: 太和中，授陰山府都督、代北行營招撫使。）〉
entries.en: Under Taihe he was named governor of Yinshan Prefecture and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉
entries.literal: In Taihe he was given Yinshan Prefecture governorship and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為昭烈皇帝，廟號懿祖。
entries.en: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Zhaolie with temple name Ancestor Yi.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaolie, temple name Ancestor Yi.

entries.zh: 烈考國昌，本名赤心，唐朔州刺史。
entries.en: His father Guochang, born Chixin, had been Tang prefect of Shuo.
entries.literal: His stern father Guochang, original name Chixin, was Tang prefect of Shuo.

entries.zh: 咸通中，討龐勳有功，入為金吾上將軍，賜姓李氏，名國昌，
entries.en: Under Xiantong he helped crush Pang Xun, entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, and received the imperial surname Li and the name Guochang,
entries.literal: In Xiantong, campaigning against Pang Xun with merit, he entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, was granted the surname Li and the name Guochang,

entries.zh: 〈（代州有《唐故龍武軍統軍檢校司徒贈太保隴四李公神道碑》云：公諱國昌，字德興。）〉
entries.en: (A Dai stele, the 《Stele of Lord Li, Late Tang Longwu Commander, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi》, records: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉
entries.literal: (At Dai prefecture there is the 《Stele of the Late Tang Longwu Army Commander-in-Chief, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi, Lord Li》 saying: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉

entries.zh: 仍係鄭王房。
entries.en: and he was entered in the genealogical line of the Prince of Zheng.
entries.literal: and he was enrolled in the Prince of Zheng branch.

entries.zh: 出為振武節度使，尋為吐渾所襲，退保於神武川。
entries.en: He was posted as Zhenwu military commissioner; the Tuyuhun soon struck, and he fell back to Shenwu River.
entries.literal: He went out as Zhenwu military commissioner; soon the Tuyuhun attacked and he withdrew to hold Shenwu River.

entries.zh: 及武皇鎮太原，表為代北軍節度使。
entries.en: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized Guochang as military commissioner of the northern Dai army.
entries.literal: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized him as northern-campaign military commissioner.

entries.zh: 中和三年薨。
entries.en: He died in Zhonghe 3.
entries.literal: He died in the third year of Zhonghe.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為文皇，廟號獻祖。
entries.en: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Wen with temple name Ancestor Xian.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, temple name Ancestor Xian.

entries.zh: 景福元年正月，鎮州王鎔恃燕人之援，率兵十餘萬攻邢州之堯山。
entries.en: In the first month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, backed by the Yan, marched more than one hundred thousand men against Yaoshan in Xingzhou.
entries.literal: First month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, relying on Yan aid, led more than one hundred thousand men to attack Yaoshan in Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 武皇遣李存信將兵應援，李存孝素與存信不協，遞相猜貳，留兵不進。
entries.en: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin to relieve the siege, but Li Cunxiao, long at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, kept his troops from advancing.
entries.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin with troops to relieve the siege; Li Cunxiao had long been at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, and held his men back.

entries.zh: 武皇又遣李嗣勳、李存審將兵援之，大破燕、趙之眾，斬首三萬，收其軍實。
entries.en: Wuhuang then sent Li Sixun and Li Cunshen to reinforce them, routed the Yan and Zhao armies, took thirty thousand heads, and captured their stores.
entries.literal: Wuhuang also sent Li Sixin and Li Cunshen with troops to reinforce them, thoroughly defeated the Yan and Zhao forces, beheaded thirty thousand, and seized their military stores.

entries.zh: 三月，武皇進軍渡滹沱，攻欒城，下鼓城、槁城。
entries.en: In the third month he advanced across the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.
entries.literal: Third month, Wuhuang advanced, crossed the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.

entries.zh: 四月，燕軍寇雲、代，武皇班師。
entries.en: In the fourth month Yan forces raided Yun and Dai, and Wuhuang withdrew.
entries.literal: Fourth month, Yan troops raided Yun and Dai; Wuhuang withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 八月，赫連鐸誘幽州李匡威之眾八萬，寇天成軍，遂攻雲州，營於州北，連亙數里。
entries.en: In the eighth month Helian Duo won over eighty thousand of Li Kuangwei's Youzhou troops, struck Tiancheng Army, then besieged Yunzhou with camps stretching several li north of the city.
entries.literal: Eighth month, Helian Duo induced eighty thousand of Youzhou Li Kuangwei's troops, raided Tiancheng Army, then attacked Yunzhou, encamping north of the prefecture in a line several li long.

entries.zh: 武皇潛軍入於雲州，詰旦，出騎軍以擊之，斬獲數萬，李匡威燒營而遁。
entries.en: Wuhuang slipped into Yunzhou with his army; at dawn his horsemen fell on them, killing or capturing tens of thousands, and Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.
entries.literal: Wuhuang secretly entered Yunzhou with troops; at dawn he led cavalry out to attack, beheading and capturing tens of thousands; Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.

entries.zh: 十月，邢州李存孝叛，納款於梁，李存信構之也。
entries.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao of Xingzhou rebelled and went over to Liang after Li Cunxin set him up.
entries.literal: Tenth month, Xingzhou's Li Cunxiao rebelled, submitted allegiance to Liang; Li Cunxin had framed him.

entries.zh: 景福二年春，大舉以伐王鎔，以其通好於李存孝也。
entries.en: In the spring of Jingfu 2 Wuhuang marched in force against Wang Rong for keeping ties with Li Cunxiao.
entries.literal: Spring of Jingfu year 2, a great campaign was launched against Wang Rong because he was on good terms with Li Cunxiao.

entries.zh: 二月，攻天長鎮，旬日不下。
entries.en: In the second month he attacked Tianchang Fort, which held out for ten days.
entries.literal: Second month, they attacked Tianchang Fort; for ten days it would not fall.

entries.zh: 王鎔出師三萬來援，武皇逆戰於叱日嶺下，鎮人敗，斬首萬餘級。
entries.en: Wang Rong sent thirty thousand reinforcements; Wuhuang met them at Chiri Ridge, routed the Zhen army, and took more than ten thousand heads.
entries.literal: Wang Rong sent thirty thousand men to the relief; Wuhuang met them below Chiri Ridge; the Zhen men were defeated and more than ten thousand heads were taken.

entries.zh: 時歲饑，軍乏食，脯屍肉而食之。
entries.en: Famine left the army starving; they ate dried flesh from the dead.
entries.literal: Famine struck that year; the army lacked food and dried flesh from corpses to eat.

entries.zh: 進軍下井陘，李存孝將兵夜入鎮州，鎮人乞師於汴；
entries.en: He pushed down Jingxing Pass; Li Cunxiao stole into Zhenzhou by night while the city called on Bian for aid;
entries.literal: Advancing through Jingxing Pass, Li Cunxiao led troops by night into Zhenzhou; the Zhen men begged Bian for troops;

entries.zh: 汴帥方攻時溥，不暇應之。
entries.en: but the Bian commander was busy attacking Shi Pu and could not answer.
entries.literal: The Bian commander was then attacking Shi Pu and had no leisure to respond.

entries.zh: 乃求援於幽州，李匡威率兵赴之，武皇乃班師。
entries.en: Wang Rong turned to Youzhou; Li Kuangwei marched to help, and Wuhuang withdrew.
entries.literal: They then sought aid from Youzhou; Li Kuangwei led troops to the rescue, and Wuhuang withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 七月，武皇討李存孝於邢州，遂攻平山，渡滹水，攻鎮州。
entries.en: In the seventh month Wuhuang attacked Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou, took Pingshan, crossed the Hutuo, and moved on Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Seventh month, Wuhuang campaigned against Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou, then attacked Pingshan, crossed the Hutuo River, and attacked Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 王鎔懼，以帛五十萬犒軍，請修舊好，仍以鎮、冀之師助擊存孝，許之。
entries.en: Wang Rong, in terror, sent five hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, sued for peace, and pledged Zhen and Ji troops against Cunxiao; Wuhuang agreed.
entries.literal: Wang Rong was afraid; with five hundred thousand bolts of silk he rewarded the army, asked to renew the old friendship, and still offered Zhen and Ji troops to help strike Cunxiao; this was granted.

entries.zh: 武皇進圍邢州。
entries.en: Wuhuang pressed the siege of Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Wuhuang advanced to besiege Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 十二月，武皇狩於近郊，獲白兔，有角長三寸。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he hunted near the capital and took a white hare with three-inch horns.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, Wuhuang hunted near the suburbs and caught a white hare with horns three inches long.

entries.zh: 八月壬戌，天子自華還宮。
entries.en: On renxu in the eighth month the emperor returned from Hua to the capital.
entries.literal: On renxu of the eighth month the Son of Heaven returned from Hua to the palace.

entries.zh: 是時，車駕初復，而欲諸侯輯睦，賜武皇詔，令與汴帥通好。
entries.en: The court had only just returned to Chang'an and wanted peace among the warlords; Wuhuang was ordered to reconcile with the Bian commander.
entries.literal: At that time the carriage had just returned and the court wished the feudatories to live in harmony; an edict was granted to Wuhuang to make peace with the Bian commander.

entries.zh: 武皇不欲先下汴帥，乃致書於鎮州王鎔，令導其意。
entries.en: Unwilling to make the first move toward Bian, Wuhuang wrote Wang Rong of Zhenzhou to sound him out.
entries.literal: Wuhuang did not wish to yield first to the Bian commander; he wrote to Wang Rong of Zhen prefecture to convey his intent.

entries.zh: 明年，汴帥遣使奉書幣來修好，武皇亦報之。
entries.en: The following year the Bian commander sent envoys with letters and gifts to reopen relations, and Wuhuang answered in kind.
entries.literal: The next year the Bian commander sent envoys with letters and gifts to restore good relations; Wuhuang also replied.

entries.zh: 自是使車交馳，朝野相賀。
entries.en: Envoys then traveled constantly between the two sides, and the realm breathed easier.
entries.literal: From then envoys shuttled back and forth, and court and countryside rejoiced.

entries.zh: 九月，武皇遣周德威、李嗣昭率兵三萬出青山口，以迫邢、洺。
entries.en: In the ninth month Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with thirty thousand men through Qing Mountain Pass against Xing and Ming.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with thirty thousand men out Qing Mountain Pass to press Xing and Ming.

entries.zh: 十月，遇汴將葛從周於張公橋，既戰，我軍大敗。
entries.en: In the tenth month they met Ge Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge and were routed.
entries.literal: Tenth month, they met the Bian general Ge Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge; after battle our army was utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 是月，河中王珂來告急，言王珙引汴軍來寇，武皇遣李嗣昭將兵三千以援之，屯於胡壁堡。
entries.en: That month Wang Ke of Hezhong begged for help against Wang Gong and the Bian army; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men to Hubi Fort.
entries.literal: That month Wang Ke of Hezhong reported urgency, saying Wang Gong was leading the Bian army to raid; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men to aid him, encamped at Hubi Fort.

entries.zh: 汴軍萬餘人來拒戰，嗣昭擊退之。
entries.en: When more than ten thousand Bian troops came up, Sizhao beat them back.
entries.literal: More than ten thousand Bian troops came to resist; Sizhao repelled them.

entries.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
entries.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
entries.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

entries.zh: 詰旦，天復昏霧，進軍直抵夾城。
entries.en: At dawn fog returned; they marched straight on Jiacity.
entries.literal: At dawn fog returned; they advanced straight to Jiacity.

entries.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
entries.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
entries.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

entries.zh: 李存璋、王霸率丁夫燒寨，劚夾城為二道；
entries.en: Li Cunzhang and Wang Ba had laborers burn the camps and split Jiacity in two;
entries.literal: Li Cunzhang and Wang Ba led laborers burning stockades, cutting Jiacity in two;

entries.zh: 周德威、李存審各分道進攻，軍士鼓噪，三道齊進。
entries.en: Zhou Dewei and Li Cunshen struck on separate routes amid a roar as three columns closed in.
entries.literal: Zhou Dewei and Li Cunshen each attacked by a route; soldiers shouted; three paths advanced together.

entries.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
entries.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
entries.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

entries.zh: 梁招討使康懷英得百餘騎，出天井關而遁。
entries.en: Liang's pacifier Kang Huaiying fled with barely a hundred horse through Tianjing Pass.
entries.literal: Liang pacification commissioner Kang Huaiying escaped with a little over a hundred horsemen through Tianjing Pass.

entries.zh: 梁祖聞其敗也，既懼而歎曰：「生子當如是，李氏不亡矣！
entries.en: Hearing the defeat, Liang's founder sighed in fear, "A son like that—and the Li will not die!
entries.literal: The Liang founder heard of the defeat, was afraid, and sighed: "To have a son like this—the Li family will not perish!

entries.zh: 吾家諸子乃豚犬爾。」
entries.en: My own sons are piglets and curs."
entries.literal: My sons are pig-dogs."

entries.zh: 初，唐龍紀元年，帝才五歲，從武皇校獵於三垂崗，崗上有明皇原廟在焉。
entries.en: Long ago, in Tang Longji 1, five-year-old Cunxu hunted Sanchui Ridge with Wuhuang, where Minghuang's shrine stood.
entries.literal: Earlier, in Tang Longji year 1, the Emperor was five; he accompanied Wuhuang hunting at Sanchui Ridge, where the original shrine of Minghuang stood.

entries.zh: 武皇於祠前置酒，樂作，伶人奏《百年歌》者，陳其衰老之狀，聲調悽苦。
entries.en: Wuhuang poured wine before the shrine; players sang the 《Hundred Year Song》, voicing old age in mournful tones.
entries.literal: Wuhuang set wine before the shrine; when music played, actors performed the 《Hundred Year Song》, portraying the state of aging, the tune mournful.

entries.zh: 武皇引滿，捋須指帝曰：「老夫壯心未已，二十年後，此子必戰於此。」
entries.en: Wuhuang drank his fill, tugged his beard, pointed at Cunxu and said, "I am not done yet—in twenty years this boy will fight here."
entries.literal: Wuhuang filled his cup, stroked his beard, pointed at the Emperor and said: "My old ambition is not spent—in twenty years this child will surely fight here."

entries.zh: 及是役也，果符其言焉。
entries.en: This battle proved him right.
entries.literal: At this campaign it indeed matched his words.

entries.zh: 六月，鳳翔李茂貞、邠州楊崇本合四川王建之師五萬，以攻長安，遣使會兵於帝，帝遣張承業率師赴之。
entries.en: In the sixth month Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Yang Chongben of Bin with fifty thousand of Wang Jian's Shu attacked Chang'an and asked Cunxu to join; he sent Zhang Chengye.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Fengxiang's Li Maozhen and Binzhou's Yang Chongben with Sichuan's Wang Jian's army of fifty thousand attacked Chang'an and sent envoys to join armies with the Emperor; the Emperor sent Zhang Chengye with troops to answer.

entries.zh: 九月，邠、岐、蜀三鎮復大舉攻長安，遣李嗣昭、周德威將兵三萬攻晉州以應之。
entries.en: In the ninth month Bin, Qi, and Shu struck Chang'an again; Cunxu sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand against Jinzhou in reply.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the Bin, Qi, and Shu three commands again mounted a great attack on Chang'an and sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand troops to attack Jinzhou in response.

entries.zh: 德威與梁將尹皓戰於神山北，梁人大敗。
entries.en: Zhou Dewei met Yin Hao of Liang north of Shenshan and routed him.
entries.literal: Dewei with Liang general Yin Hao fought north of Shenshan; the Liang army was greatly defeated.

entries.zh: 是時，晉之騎將夏侯敬受以一軍奔於梁，德威乃退保隰州。
entries.en: Then Jin's Xiahou Jingshou defected with his command; Dewei pulled back to Yizhou.
entries.literal: At that time Jin cavalry general Xiahou Jingshou with one army fled to Liang; Dewei withdrew to guard Yizhou.

entries.zh: 九月，德威班師。
entries.en: In the ninth month Dewei brought the army back.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Dewei returned the army.

entries.zh: 冬十月，梁祖遣大將李思安、楊師厚率師營於澤州，以攻上黨。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter the Liang Founder sent Li Si'an and Yang Shihou with a host to camp at Ze and besiege Shangdang.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Liang Founder sent great generals Li Si'an and Yang Shihou to lead troops and encamp at Ze prefecture to attack Shangdang.
