entries.zh: 十一月，鎮州王鎔遣使來求援。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Wang Rong of Zhen sent envoys asking for aid.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, Wang Rong of Zhen prefecture sent envoys to beg for relief.

entries.zh: 是時，梁祖以羅紹威初卒，全有魏博之地，因欲兼並鎮、定，遣供奉官杜廷隱、丁延徽督魏軍三千人入於深、冀，鎮人懼，故來告難。
entries.en: The Liang Founder had just absorbed Weibo after Luo Shaowei's death and now aimed at Zhen and Ding as well; he sent Du Tingyin and Ding Yanhui with three thousand Wei troops into Shen and Ji, and the frightened Zhen lords sent word that they were in peril.
entries.literal: At that time, because the Liang Founder had just taken all of Weibo after Luo Shaowei's death, he wished also to annex Zhen and Ding; he sent palace attendant Du Tingyin and Ding Yanhui to supervise three thousand Wei troops into Shen and Ji; the Zhen men were afraid and therefore came to report their distress.

entries.zh: 帝集軍吏議之，鹹欲按甲治兵，徐觀勝負，惟帝獨斷，堅欲救之，乃遣周德威率軍屯於趙州。
entries.en: The Emperor called his commanders to council; all favored standing pat and waiting, but he alone insisted on rescue and sent Zhou Dewei to camp at Zhao.
entries.literal: The Emperor gathered the army officers to discuss it; all wished to hold their arms and watch the outcome, but the Emperor alone decided and firmly wished to save them; he then sent Zhou Dewei with troops to encamp at Zhao prefecture.

entries.zh: 是月，行營都招討使丁會卒。
entries.en: That month Ding Hui, overall campaign commander, died.
entries.literal: That month, overall campaign commander Ding Hui died.

entries.zh: 十二月丁巳朔，梁祖聞帝軍屯趙州，命寧國軍節度使王景仁為北面行營招討使，韓為副，相州刺史李思安為前鋒，會魏州之兵以討王鎔；
entries.en: On dingsi, the first day of the twelfth month, learning that the Jin host lay at Zhao, the Liang Founder made Wang Jingren of Ningguo overall northern commander, with Han as his deputy and Li Si'an of Xiang as vanguard, to unite Wei forces against Wang Rong;
entries.literal: Twelfth month, first day dingsi, the Liang Founder heard that the Emperor's army was encamped at Zhao and appointed Ningguo Army military commissioner Wang Jingren overall northern campaign commander, with Han as deputy and Xiangzhou prefect Li Si'an as vanguard, to join Wei troops and attack Wang Rong;

entries.zh: 又令閻寶、王彥章率二千騎，會景仁於邢、洺。
entries.en: He also ordered Yan Bao and Wang Yanzhang with two thousand horse to rendezvous with Jingren at Xing and Ming.
entries.literal: He also ordered Yan Bao and Wang Yanzhang to lead two thousand cavalry to join Jingren at Xing and Ming.

entries.zh: 丁丑，景仁營於柏鄉，帝遂親征，自讚皇縣東下。
entries.en: On dingchou Jingren camped at Baixiang; the Emperor marched in person east from Zanhuang.
entries.literal: On dingchou Jingren encamped at Baixiang; the Emperor then took the field in person, marching east from Zanhuang county.

entries.zh: 辛巳，至趙州，與周德威兵合。
entries.en: On xinsi he reached Zhao and united with Zhou Dewei.
entries.literal: On xinsi he reached Zhao prefecture and joined Zhou Dewei's army.

entries.zh: 帝令史建瑭以輕騎嘗寇，獲芻牧者二百人，問其兵數，精兵七萬。
entries.en: He sent Shi Jiantang with light horse to scout, took two hundred foragers, and learned that the enemy elite alone numbered seventy thousand.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Shi Jiantang with light cavalry to probe the enemy; he seized two hundred foragers and asked their strength—they said the elite numbered seventy thousand.

entries.zh: 是日，帝觀兵於石橋南。
entries.en: That day he reviewed the army south of Stone Bridge.
entries.literal: That day the Emperor reviewed the troops south of Shiqiao.

entries.zh: 詰旦，進軍，距柏鄉一舍，周德威、史建瑭率蕃落勁騎以挑戰，四面馳射，梁軍閉壁不出，乃退。
entries.en: At dawn he moved up to within one march of Baixiang; Dewei and Jiantang led tough frontier horse in circling challenges and volleys until the Liang men shut their walls and would not fight, then drew off.
entries.literal: At dawn he advanced, halting one stage from Baixiang; Zhou Dewei and Shi Jiantang led fierce frontier cavalry to challenge, riding about on four sides shooting; the Liang army shut their walls and would not come out, and they withdrew.

entries.zh: 翌日，進軍，距柏鄉五里，遣騎軍逼其營。
entries.en: Next day he came within five li of Baixiang and sent horse to harass the camp.
entries.literal: The next day he advanced to within five li of Baixiang and sent cavalry to press their camp.

entries.zh: 梁將韓、李思安率步騎三萬，鎧甲炫曜，其勢甚盛，分道以薄帝軍。
entries.en: Han and Li Si'an of Liang led thirty thousand foot and horse in gleaming armor and came on in columns against the Emperor's line.
entries.literal: The Liang generals Han and Li Si'an led thirty thousand foot and horse, armor dazzling bright; their momentum was very strong and they split into columns to close on the Emperor's army.

entries.zh: 德威且戰且退，距河而止。
entries.en: Dewei fought as he fell back and made his stand at the river.
entries.literal: Dewei fought while retreating and halted at the river.

entries.zh: 既而德威偵知梁人造浮橋，乃退保高邑。
entries.en: Soon scouts reported a Liang pontoon bridge; Dewei pulled back to Gaoyi.
entries.literal: Before long Dewei learned by reconnaissance that the Liang men were building a pontoon bridge; he then withdrew to defend Gaoyi.

entries.zh: 乙酉，致師於柏鄉，帝禱戰於光武廟。
entries.en: On yiyou he drew up before Baixiang; the Emperor prayed for victory at Guangwu's temple.
entries.literal: On yiyou he arrayed the army at Baixiang; the Emperor prayed for victory at the Temple of Emperor Guangwu.

entries.zh: 柏鄉無芻粟之備，梁軍以樵采為給，為帝之遊軍所獲，由是堅壁不出，剉屋茅坐席以秣其馬，眾心益恐。
entries.en: Baixiang had no fodder; the Liang host lived on foraging until Jin raiders cut them off; they stayed behind their walls, stripped thatch and mats to feed their horses, and fear spread through the camp.
entries.literal: Baixiang had no stores of fodder or grain; the Liang army lived on woodcutting and foraging, which the Emperor's roaming detachments seized; therefore they held their walls and would not come out, shaved roof thatch and mats to feed their horses, and hearts grew more fearful.

entries.zh: 天祐八年正月丁亥，周德威、史建瑭帥三千騎致師於柏鄉，設伏於村塢間，遣三百騎直壓其營。
entries.en: On dinghai in the first month of Tianyou 8, Dewei and Jiantang led three thousand horse to Baixiang, hid men in the hamlets, and sent three hundred to ride straight at the Liang camp.
entries.literal: Tianyou year 8, first month, day dinghai, Zhou Dewei and Shi Jiantang led three thousand cavalry to offer battle at Baixiang, set ambush among village hamlets, and sent three hundred horse straight against the camp.

entries.zh: 梁將怒，悉其軍結陣而來，德威與之轉戰至高邑南，梁軍列陣，橫亙六七里。
entries.en: The Liang commander came out in full array; Dewei sparred with him south of Gaoyi until the Liang line stretched six or seven li.
entries.literal: The Liang general was enraged and brought out his whole army in battle order; Dewei fought with them wheeling south of Gaoyi; the Liang army formed ranks stretching six or seven li.

entries.zh: 時帝軍未成列，李存璋引諸軍陣於野河之上，梁以五百人爭橋，鎮、定之師與血戰，梁軍敗而復整者數四。
entries.en: The main host was not yet formed when Li Cunzhang drew the armies up along the Wild River; five hundred Liang men fought for the bridge with the Zhen and Ding troops in bloody seesaw fighting that broke and re-formed four times.
entries.literal: At that time the Emperor's army had not yet finished forming; Li Cunzhang led the various armies into line above Yeh River; the Liang sent five hundred men to contest the bridge; the Zhen and Ding troops fought them hand to hand; the Liang army was beaten and re-formed four times.

entries.zh: 帝與張承業登高觀望，梁人戈矛如束，申令之後，囂聲若雷，王師進退有序，步騎嚴整，寂然無聲。
entries.en: The Emperor and Zhang Chengye watched from a height; Liang spears stood thick as sheaves and their shouts rolled like thunder, while the royal line moved in silence, foot and horse in tight order.
entries.literal: The Emperor with Zhang Chengye climbed high to watch; Liang spears and halberds stood like sheaves; after the order was given the shouting was like thunder; the royal army advanced and withdrew in order, foot and horse sternly arrayed, utterly silent.

entries.zh: 帝臨陣誓眾，人百其勇，短兵既接，無不奮力。
entries.en: He swore the host before the line; at close quarters every man fought with redoubled fury.
entries.literal: The Emperor faced the battle line and swore the host; each man doubled his courage; once close weapons met, none failed to strain every strength.

entries.zh: 梁有龍驤、神威、拱宸等軍，皆武勇之士也，每一人鎧仗，費數十萬，裝以組繡，飾以金銀，人望而畏之。
entries.en: Liang Dragon Soar, Divine Might, Arch-Guard, and other picked corps wore armor worth fortunes, brocaded and gilded, and struck fear at a glance.
entries.literal: The Liang had Dragon Soar, Divine Might, Arch-Guard, and other corps—all warriors of martial courage; each man's armor and weapons cost several hundred thousand, adorned with brocade and trimmed with gold and silver; men looked on them with dread.

entries.zh: 自巳及午，騎軍接戰，至晡，梁軍欲抽退，塵埃漲天，德威周麾而呼曰：「汴人走矣！」
entries.en: Cavalry fought from si to noon; by you the Liang line tried to break off; dust filled the sky; Dewei turned in his saddle and cried, "The Bian men are running!"
entries.literal: From si hour to noon the cavalry clashed; by you hour the Liang army wished to pull back; dust billowed to the sky; Dewei wheeled about shouting: "The Bian men are running!"

entries.zh: 帝軍齊噪以進，魏人收軍漸退。
entries.en: The Jin host roared forward as the Wei troops fell back step by step.
entries.literal: The Emperor's army shouted together and pressed forward; the Wei men gathered their troops and gradually withdrew.

entries.zh: 李嗣源率親軍與史建瑭、安金全兼北部吐渾諸軍衝陣夾攻，梁軍大敗，棄鎧投仗之聲，震動天地，龍驤、神威、神捷諸軍，殺戮殆盡。
entries.en: Li Siyuan, Jiantang, An Jinquan, and the northern Tuguhun horse hit the Liang line from both flanks; the Liang host collapsed; discarded arms thundered on the ground; Dragon Soar, Divine Might, Divine Swift, and the rest were cut down almost to a man.
entries.literal: Li Siyuan led the personal guard with Shi Jiantang and An Jinquan and the northern Tuguhun troops together to charge the line from both sides; the Liang army was utterly defeated; the sound of cast-off armor and weapons shook heaven and earth; Dragon Soar, Divine Might, Divine Swift, and other corps were slaughtered nearly to the last man.

entries.zh: 自陣至柏鄉數十里，僵屍枕籍，敗旗折戟，所在蔽地。
entries.en: For tens of li from the field to Baixiang corpses lay heaped and broken flags and halberds carpeted the ground.
entries.literal: From the battlefield to Baixiang for several tens of li, corpses lay piled head to foot; broken flags and snapped halberds covered the ground everywhere.

entries.zh: 夜漏一鼓，帝軍入柏鄉，梁軍輜重、帳幄、資財、奴仆，皆為帝軍所有。
entries.en: At the first watch the Jin army entered Baixiang and took Liang baggage, tents, wealth, and servants.
entries.literal: At the first watch of night the Emperor's army entered Baixiang; Liang baggage, tents, wealth, and servants all became the Emperor's army's property.

entries.zh: 梁將王景仁、韓、李思安等以數十騎夜遁。
entries.en: Wang Jingren, Han, Li Si'an, and other Liang commanders escaped by night with a few dozen horsemen.
entries.literal: The Liang generals Wang Jingren, Han, Li Si'an, and others fled by night with several tens of horse.

entries.zh: 是役也，斬首二萬級，獲馬三千匹，鎧甲兵仗七萬，輜車鍋幕不可勝計。
entries.en: The victory yielded twenty thousand heads, three thousand horses, seventy thousand sets of arms, and wagons and camp gear past counting.
entries.literal: In this battle they took twenty thousand heads, seized three thousand horses, seventy thousand suits of armor and weapons, and baggage wagons, cauldrons, and tents beyond counting.

entries.zh: 擒梁將陳思權以下二百八十五人。
entries.en: Two hundred eighty-five Liang officers including Chen Siquan were taken.
entries.literal: They captured two hundred eighty-five Liang officers including Chen Siquan.

entries.zh: 帝號令收軍於趙州。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered the army to regroup at Zhao.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered the army gathered at Zhao prefecture.

entries.zh: 既而梁人棄深、冀二州而遁。
entries.en: Soon the Liang abandoned Shen and Ji and fled.
entries.literal: Before long the Liang men abandoned Shen and Ji prefectures and fled.

entries.zh: 初，杜廷隱之襲深、冀也，聲言分兵就食。
entries.en: When Du Tingyin seized Shen and Ji he had claimed he was only sending detachments for supplies.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Du Tingyin raided Shen and Ji, he claimed he was dividing troops to draw rations.

entries.zh: 時王鎔將石公立戍深州，欲杜關不納，鎔遽令啟關，命公立移車於外，廷隱遂據其城。
entries.en: Shi Gongli held Shen for Wang Rong and wanted to keep the gates shut; Rong ordered them opened and told Gongli to move his wagons out, and Tingyin took the city.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Rong's general Shi Gongli was garrisoning Shen prefecture and wished to shut the gate and refuse entry; Rong hastily ordered the gate opened and commanded Gongli to move his carts outside; Tingyin then seized the city.

entries.zh: 公立既出，指城而言曰：「開門納盜，後悔何追，此城數萬生靈，生為俘馘矣！」
entries.en: Gongli pointed at the walls and cried, "You opened the gate to thieves—how can you undo it? Tens of thousands in this city are lost to captivity and the blade!"
entries.literal: Once Gongli was out, he pointed at the city and said: "To open the gate and admit robbers—what regret can follow? The tens of thousands of lives in this city are born to be captives and heads!"

entries.zh: 因投刃泣下。
entries.en: He flung down his sword and wept.
entries.literal: He then cast down his blade and wept.

entries.zh: 數日，廷隱閉城殺鎮兵數千人，遂登陴拒守，王鎔方命公立攻之，即有備矣。
entries.en: Days later Tingyin massacred thousands of Zhen soldiers, manned the walls, and when Wang Rong sent Gongli to retake the city the defenders were ready.
entries.literal: Several days later Tingyin shut the city and killed several thousand Zhen troops, then mounted the walls to hold defense; only then did Wang Rong order Gongli to attack—but they were already prepared.

entries.zh: 及柏鄉之敗，兩州之人悉為奴擄，老弱者皆坑之。
entries.en: After Baixiang the people of both prefectures were enslaved and the old and weak were buried in pits.
entries.literal: After the defeat at Baixiang the people of the two prefectures were all taken as slaves; the old and weak were all buried alive in pits.

entries.zh: 己亥，遣史建瑭、周德威徇地於邢、魏，先馳檄以諭之。
entries.en: On jihai he sent Jiantang and Dewei to overrun Xing and Wei with proclamations sent ahead.
entries.literal: On jihai he sent Shi Jiantang and Zhou Dewei to sweep Xing and Wei, first dispatching proclamations to instruct them.

entries.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》載晉王諭邢、洺、魏、博、衛、滑諸郡縣檄。
entries.en: (The 《Cefu Yuangui》 preserves the Jin Prince's proclamation to Xing, Ming, Wei, Bo, Wei, and Hua.
entries.literal: (The 《Cefu Yuangui》 records the Jin Prince's proclamation to the prefectures and counties of Xing, Ming, Wei, Bo, Wei, and Hua.

entries.zh: 天祐八年正月，周德威等破賊，徇地邢、洺，先馳檄諭邢、洺、魏、博、衛、滑諸郡縣曰：「王室遇屯，七廟被陵夷之酷；
entries.en: In the first month of Tianyou 8, after Dewei's victory, a proclamation to Xing, Ming, Wei, Bo, Wei, and Hua ran: "The throne is in peril and the ancestral temples have been violated;
entries.literal: Tianyou year 8, first month, Zhou Dewei and others defeated the bandits and swept Xing and Ming; they first sent a flying proclamation to the prefectures and counties of Xing, Ming, Wei, Bo, Wei, and Hua saying: "The royal house has met hardship; the seven temples have suffered the outrage of desecration;

entries.zh: 昊天不吊，萬民罹塗炭之災。
entries.en: Heaven shows no mercy and the people burn in misery.
entries.literal: High Heaven does not pity; the myriad people suffer the disaster of fire and charcoal.

entries.zh: 必有英主奮庸，忠臣仗順，斬長鯨而清四海，靖襖祲以泰三靈。
entries.en: A hero must rise and loyal men take the righteous path—to slay the monster, pacify the realm, and restore order under Heaven.
entries.literal: Surely a heroic lord will rise in merit, and loyal ministers will take up the righteous cause, cut the great whale and clear the four seas, and still the evil omens to bring peace to the three spirits.

entries.zh: 予位忝維城，任當分閫，念茲顛覆，詎可宴安。
entries.en: I hold the frontier charge of a bulwark prince; faced with ruin, how could I sit at ease?
entries.literal: My post disgraces the bulwark of the state and my charge is the frontier command; thinking on this overthrow, how could I feast in ease?

entries.zh: 故仗桓、文輔合之規，問羿、浞凶狂之罪。
entries.en: I follow the alliance of Huan and Wen and demand justice for the crimes of Yi and Zhuo.
entries.literal: Therefore I take Huan and Wen's plan of allied support and call to account the crimes of Yi and Zhuo's wicked violence.

entries.zh: 逆溫碭山庸隸，巢孽餘凶，當僖宗奔播之初，我太祖掃平之際，束身泥首，請命牙門，苞藏奸詐之心，惟示婦人之態。
entries.en: The traitor Wen was a Dangshan menial, a Huang Chao remnant; when Xizong fled the court my Grand Ancestor was pacifying the realm, and Wen groveled at the gate while nursing treachery behind a woman's meekness.
entries.literal: The rebel Wen was a menial of Mount Dang, a remnant villain of the Huang Chao band; when Emperor Xizong fled in disorder, at the time my Grand Ancestor was sweeping the realm flat, Wen bound himself in mud and begged life at the army gate, harboring treacherous deceit in his heart while showing only a woman's manner.

entries.zh: 我太祖俯憐窮鳥，曲為開懷，特發表章，請帥梁汴，才出萑蒲之澤，便居茅社之尊，殊不感恩，遽行猜忍。
entries.en: My Grand Ancestor spared him and raised him to command Bian; scarcely out of the marshes he took a prince's seat—ungrateful, he turned at once to suspicion and cruelty.
entries.literal: My Grand Ancestor pitied the cornered bird and opened his heart in kindness, specially sent a memorial asking him to command Liang and Bian; he had barely left the reed marsh when he sat in the rank of a feudal lord—utterly ungrateful, he at once turned suspicious and cruel.

entries.zh: 我國家祚隆周、漢，跡盛伊、唐，二十聖之鎡基，三百年之文物。
entries.en: Our house rivals Zhou and Han in fortune and Tang in glory—twenty sage rulers and three hundred years of ritual and law.
entries.literal: Our state's fortune rivals Zhou and Han; its traces match Yi and Tang; twenty sage emperors laid the foundation; three hundred years of culture and ritual.

entries.zh: 外則五侯九伯，內則百辟千官，或代襲簪纓，或門傳忠孝，皆遭陷害，永抱沉冤。
entries.en: Marquises and ministers without, officials within—many hereditary houses of loyalty—were destroyed and live on in wronged silence.
entries.literal: Without were the five marquises and nine chiefs; within were the hundred ministers and thousand officials; some inherited office generation after generation, some handed down loyalty and filial piety from gate to gate—all met with ruin and forever bear drowned injustice.

entries.zh: 且鎮、定兩藩，國家巨鎮，冀安民而保族，鹹屈節以稱藩。
entries.en: Zhen and Ding, great pillars of the state, bent to serve as loyal vassals to keep their people safe.
entries.literal: Moreover the two circuits of Zhen and Ding are great bulwarks of the state; wishing to settle the people and preserve their clans, all alike bent their stature to serve as vassal domains.

entries.zh: 逆溫唯伏陰謀，專行不義，欲全吞噬，先據屬州。
entries.en: Wen plotted in secret and seized their prefectures before moving to swallow them whole.
entries.literal: The rebel Wen only harbored secret plots and specialized in unrighteous acts; wishing to swallow them whole, he first seized their subordinate prefectures.

entries.zh: 趙州特發使車，來求援助。
entries.en: Zhao sent envoys to beg for rescue.
entries.literal: Zhao prefecture specially sent envoys by carriage to beg for aid.

entries.zh: 予情惟蕩寇，義切親仁，躬率賦輿，赴茲盟約。
entries.en: My heart is to crush the rebels and stand by an ally; I have led the levy here myself.
entries.literal: My feeling is only to sweep away bandits; my righteousness urgently embraces kin; I personally lead the levy carts and come to this covenant.

entries.zh: 賊將王景仁將兵十萬，屯據柏鄉，遂驅三鎮之師，授以七擒之略。
entries.en: The rebel Wang Jingren held Baixiang with a hundred thousand men and the hosts of three circuits with a conqueror's brief.
entries.literal: The bandit general Wang Jingren led a hundred thousand troops and encamped at Baixiang; he then drove the armies of the three circuits and entrusted them with the seven-capture stratagem.

entries.zh: 鸛鵝才列，梟獍大奔，易如走阪之丸，勢若燎原之火。
entries.en: Their array scarcely stood when they broke like routed beasts—easy as a ball on a slope, fierce as a prairie fire.
entries.literal: Their lines had barely formed when the owls and beasts fled in rout; it was as easy as rolling a pellet down a slope; the momentum was like prairie fire.

entries.zh: 僵屍仆地，流血成川。
entries.en: Corpses littered the field and blood ran in streams.
entries.literal: Corpses fell to the ground; blood formed streams.

entries.zh: 組甲雕戈，皆投草莽，謀夫猛將，盡作俘囚。
entries.en: Gilded armor and carved blades littered the grass; their best men were taken.
entries.literal: Linked armor and carved halberds were all cast into the grass; strategists and fierce generals all became captives.

entries.zh: 群凶既快於天誅，大憝須垂於鬼錄。
entries.en: The rebels have tasted Heaven's stroke; the arch-villain belongs in the registers of the dead.
entries.literal: The mass of villains have already tasted Heaven's punishment; the great enemy must soon be entered in the ghost registers.

entries.zh: 今則選搜兵甲，簡練車徒，乘勝長驅，翦除元惡。
entries.en: We are gathering arms, drilling troops, and pressing the victory to destroy the chief villain.
entries.literal: Now we select and search out armor and weapons, drill chariots and troops, drive the victory in long pursuit, and cut down the chief evil.

entries.zh: 凡爾魏、博、邢、洺之眾，感恩懷義之人，乃祖乃孫，為聖唐赤子，豈徇虎狼之黨，遂忘覆載之恩。
entries.en: You of Wei, Bo, Xing, and Ming—sons of the Tang for generations—how can you follow wolves and forget the grace that sustains you?
entries.literal: All you multitudes of Wei, Bo, Xing, and Ming—men who cherish gratitude and righteousness—generation after generation you are crimson sons of the holy Tang; how could you follow the tiger-and-wolf faction and forget the grace that covers and carries you?

entries.zh: 蓋以封豕長蛇，馮陵薦食，無方逃難，遂被脅從。
entries.en: The boar and serpent ravage every land; with no escape you were forced to follow them.
entries.literal: Because the great boar and long serpent rampage and feed wherever they pass, with no way to escape hardship, you were thus compelled to follow.

entries.zh: 空嘗膽以銜冤，竟無門而雪憤，既聞告捷，想所慰懷。
entries.en: You bore wrongs in silence with no redress; hearing of our victory, your hearts should be eased.
entries.literal: In vain you tasted gall to bear injustice; in the end there was no gate to clear your wrath; now that you have heard of the victory, I trust your hearts are comforted.

entries.zh: 今義旅徂征，止於招撫。
entries.en: Our righteous host advances to win men over, not to destroy.
entries.literal: Now the righteous army marches forth and stops only at winning men over.

entries.zh: 昔耿純焚廬而向順，蕭何舉族以從軍，皆審料興亡，能圖富貴，殊勳茂業，翼子貽孫，轉禍見機，決在今日。
entries.en: Geng Chun burned his home for loyalty; Xiao He brought his clan to the colors—both read the times and won lasting honor; the moment to turn fortune is today.
entries.literal: Formerly Geng Chun burned his house to turn loyal; Xiao He moved his whole clan to join the army—both weighed rise and fall and sought fortune; rare merit and lofty achievement they bequeathed to sons and grandsons; to turn calamity by seizing the moment—the decision is today.

entries.zh: 若能詣轅門而效順，開城堡以迎降，長官則改補官資，百姓則優加賞賜，所經詿誤，更不推窮。
entries.en: Come to the gate in submission, open your walls, and officers will be reappointed and people rewarded; past errors will not be traced.
entries.literal: If you can come to the camp gate and show obedience, open your fortress and welcome surrender, the chief official will be given a new office and rank, the common people will receive generous rewards, and errors along the way will not be pursued further.

entries.zh: 三鎮諸軍，已申嚴令，不得焚燒廬舍，剽掠馬牛，但仰所在生靈，各安耕織。
entries.en: The three armies are under strict orders not to burn homes or seize livestock; let every district return to field and loom.
entries.literal: The armies of the three circuits have already announced strict orders not to burn houses, plunder horses and cattle, but only look to the people everywhere to keep at plowing and weaving.

entries.zh: 予恭行天罰，罪止元凶，已外歸明，一切不問，凡爾士眾，鹹諒予懷。」）〉
entries.en: I execute Heaven's punishment on the arch-villain alone; all who come over are pardoned; soldiers and people alike, know my intent.")〉
entries.literal: I respectfully execute Heaven's punishment; guilt stops with the chief villain; beyond those who return to the light, all are exempt from question; all you soldiers and people, understand my heart.")〉

entries.zh: 帝御親軍南征。
entries.en: The Emperor marched south at the head of the host.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally led the army south on campaign.

entries.zh: 庚子，至洺州，梁祖令其將徐仁浦將兵五百，夜入邢州。
entries.en: On gengzi he reached Ming; the Liang Founder sent Xu Renpu with five hundred men into Xing by night.
entries.literal: On gengzi he reached Ming prefecture; the Liang Founder ordered his general Xu Renpu to lead five hundred men into Xing prefecture by night.

entries.zh: 張承業、李存璋以三鎮步兵攻邢州，遣周德威、史建瑭將三千騎，長驅至澶魏，帝與李嗣源率親軍繼進。
entries.en: Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang besieged Xing with foot from the three circuits while Dewei and Jiantang raced three thousand horse to Chan and Wei; the Emperor and Li Siyuan followed with the guard.
entries.literal: Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang with infantry of the three circuits attacked Xing prefecture; they sent Zhou Dewei and Shi Jiantang with three thousand cavalry on a long drive to Chan and Wei; the Emperor with Li Siyuan led the personal guard in follow-up.

entries.zh: 二月戊午，師次洹水，周德威進至臨河。
entries.en: On wuwu in the second month the host camped on the Huan; Dewei pushed to Linhe.
entries.literal: Second month, day wuwu, the army halted at Huan River; Zhou Dewei advanced to Linhe.

entries.zh: 己未，魏帥羅周翰出兵五千，塞石灰窯口，周德威以騎掩擊，迫入觀音門。
entries.en: On jiwei Luo Zhouhan of Wei led five thousand to hold Lime Kiln Pass; Dewei's horse surprised them and chased them to Guanyin Gate.
entries.literal: On jiwei Wei commander Luo Zhouhan led five thousand men out to block Lime Kiln Pass; Zhou Dewei with cavalry struck by surprise and drove them into Guanyin Gate.

entries.zh: 是日，王師迫魏州，帝舍於狄公祠西。
entries.en: That day the royal army closed on Wei; the Emperor lodged west of the Di Gong shrine.
entries.literal: That day the royal army pressed Wei prefecture; the Emperor lodged west of the Temple of Lord Di.

entries.zh: 周翰閉壁自固，帝軍攻之，其城幾陷。
entries.en: Zhouhan held the walls; the assault nearly took the city.
entries.literal: Zhouhan shut the walls and held firm; the Emperor's army attacked and the city nearly fell.

entries.zh: 帝歎曰：「予為兒童時，從先王渡河，今其忘矣。
entries.en: The Emperor sighed, "As a boy I crossed this river with the late king—that is forgotten now.
entries.literal: The Emperor sighed and said: "When I was a child I followed the late king across the river—now that is forgotten.

entries.zh: 方春桃花水滿，思一觀之，誰從予者？」
entries.en: Spring floods the peach-blossom river; I would see it again—who will come with me?"
entries.literal: In spring the peach-blossom waters are full; I wish to see them once—who will go with me?"

entries.zh: 癸亥，帝觀河於黎陽。
entries.en: On guihai he viewed the river at Liyang.
entries.literal: On guihai the Emperor viewed the river at Liyang.

entries.zh: 是時，梁祖發兵萬餘將渡河，聞王師至，棄舟而退。
entries.en: The Liang Founder had sent ten thousand men to cross; hearing the Jin host was near, they abandoned their boats and fled.
entries.literal: At that time the Liang Founder sent more than ten thousand troops to cross the river; hearing the royal army had come, they abandoned their boats and withdrew.

entries.zh: 黎陽都將張從楚、曹儒以部下兵三千人來降，立其軍為左右匡霸使。
entries.en: Zhang Congchu and Cao Ru of Liyang surrendered with three thousand men and were formed as the Left and Right Kuangba Commissioners.
entries.literal: Liyang garrison commander Zhang Congchu and Cao Ru came over with three thousand men of their commands; their corps was established as the Left and Right Kuangba Commissioners.

entries.zh: 乙丑，周德威自臨清徇地貝郡，攻博州，下東武、朝城。
entries.en: On yichou Dewei from Linqing overran Bei, took Bo, and seized Dongwu and Chaocheng.
entries.literal: On yichou Zhou Dewei from Linqing swept Bei circuit, attacked Bo prefecture, and took Dongwu and Chaocheng.

entries.zh: 時澶州刺史張可臻棄城而遁，遂攻黎陽，下臨河、淇門。
entries.en: Chan's Zhang Kezhen fled; Dewei then took Liyang, Linhe, and Qimen.
entries.literal: At that time Chan prefect Zhang Kezhen abandoned his city and fled; he then attacked Liyang and took Linhe and Qimen.

entries.zh: 庚午，梁祖在洛，聞王師將攻河陽，率親軍屯白馬坡。
entries.en: On gengwu the Liang Founder, at Luoyang, heard the Jin host aimed at Heyang and camped his guard at White Horse Slope.
entries.literal: On gengwu the Liang Founder was at Luoyang; hearing the royal army would attack Heyang, he led the personal guard to camp at White Horse Slope.

entries.zh: 壬申，帝下令班師。
entries.en: On renshen the Emperor ordered withdrawal.
entries.literal: On renshen the Emperor ordered the army to withdraw.

entries.zh: 帝至趙州，王鎔迎謁。
entries.en: At Zhao, Wang Rong came out to welcome him.
entries.literal: The Emperor reached Zhao prefecture; Wang Rong came out to welcome and pay respects.

entries.zh: 翌日，大饗諸軍。
entries.en: The next day he feasted the armies.
entries.literal: The next day he gave a great feast to the various armies.

entries.zh: 壬午，帝發趙州，歸晉陽，留周德威戍趙州。
entries.en: On rengwu he left Zhao for Jinyang and left Dewei to hold the city.
entries.literal: On rengwu the Emperor set out from Zhao prefecture, returned to Jinyang, and left Zhou Dewei to garrison Zhao.

entries.zh: 五月，六鎮使至幽州，梁使亦集。
entries.en: In the fifth month envoys of the six circuits and of Liang alike gathered at Youzhou.
entries.literal: Fifth month, envoys of the six circuits reached Youzhou; Liang envoys also gathered.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》引《莊宗實錄》云：三月己丑，鎮州遣押衙劉光業至，言劉守光凶淫縱毒，欲自尊大，請稔其惡以咎之，推為尚父。
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 “Examination of Variants” cites the 《Veritable Record of Zhuangzong》: On jichou in the third month Zhen sent Liu Guangye to say Shouguang was brutal and lustful, sought to exalt himself, and asked that he be made August Father to ripen his guilt.
entries.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 “Examination of Variants” cites the 《Veritable Record of Zhuangzong》: Third month, day jichou, Zhen prefecture sent escort officer Liu Guangye reporting that Liu Shouguang was vicious, lewd, and tyrannical, wished to exalt himself, and asked to ripen his wickedness to bring blame upon him by advancing him as August Father.

entries.zh: 乙未，上至晉陽宮，召張承業諸將等議討燕之謀，諸將亦云宜稔其惡。
entries.en: On yiwei he reached Jinyang, called Zhang Chengye and the generals to plan the Yan campaign, and they too said his crimes should be ripened.
entries.literal: On yiwei the Emperor reached the Jinyang Palace, summoned Zhang Chengye and the generals to discuss the plan to attack Yan; the generals also said his wickedness should be ripened.

entries.zh: 上令押衙戴漢超持墨製及六鎮書如幽州，其辭曰：「天祐八年三月二十七日，天德軍節度使宋瑤、振武節度使周德威、昭義節度使李嗣昭、易定節度使王處直、鎮州節度使王鎔、河東節度使尚書令晉王謹奉冊進盧龍橫海等軍節度、檢校大尉、中書令、燕王為尚書令、尚父。」
entries.en: He ordered Dai Hanchao to Youzhou with the ink edict and six-circuit letters reading: "On the twenty-seventh day of the third month of Tianyou 8, Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiding, Wang Rong of Zhen, and the Jin Prince, Minister Director and military commissioner of Hedong, reverently advance Liu Shouguang, commissioner of the Lulong and Henghai armies, honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Councilor, and Prince of Yan, to Minister Director and August Father."
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered escort officer Dai Hanchao to carry the ink edict and letters of the six circuits to Youzhou; the text says: "Tianyou year 8, third month, twenty-seventh day, Tiande Army military commissioner Song Yao, Zhenwu Army military commissioner Zhou Dewei, Zhaoyi Army military commissioner Li Sizhao, Yiding Army military commissioner Wang Chuzhi, Zhen prefecture military commissioner Wang Rong, and Hedong military commissioner, Minister Director, Jin Prince, reverently present the register advancing the Lulong and Henghai etc. armies military commissioner, honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Councilor, Prince of Yan, to Minister Director and August Father."

entries.zh: 五月，六鎮使至，汴使亦集。
entries.en: In the fifth month the six-circuit envoys arrived, and Bian envoys gathered as well.
entries.literal: In the fifth month envoys of the six circuits arrived, and Bian envoys also gathered.

entries.zh: 六月，守光令有司定尚父、采訪使議。）〉
entries.en: In the sixth month Shouguang ordered the relevant offices to fix the protocol for Sire Father and the investigative commissioner.）〉
entries.literal: In the sixth month Shouguang ordered the appropriate offices to settle the rites for Sire Father and the investigative commissioner.）〉

entries.zh: 是月，梁祖遣都招討使楊師厚將兵三萬屯邢州，帝令李嗣昭出師掠相、衛而還。
entries.en: That month the Liang Founder sent Yang Shihou, overall campaign commander, with thirty thousand men to camp at Xingzhou; the emperor ordered Li Sizhao to strike Xiang and Wei and withdraw.
entries.literal: That same month the Liang Founder sent the overall campaign commander Yang Shihou with thirty thousand troops to camp at Xingzhou; the emperor ordered Li Sizhao to march out, raid Xiang and Wei, and return.

entries.zh: 秋七月，帝會王鎔於承天軍。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn the emperor met Wang Rong at Chengtian Army.
entries.literal: Seventh month of autumn, the emperor met Wang Rong at Chengtian Army.

entries.zh: 鎔，武皇之友也，帝奉之盡敬，捧卮酒為壽，鎔亦捧酒酬帝。
entries.en: Rong was Wuhuang's friend; the emperor treated him with full courtesy, lifted a cup to toast his years, and Rong raised wine in reply.
entries.literal: Rong was Wuhuang's friend; the emperor showed him utmost respect, raised a cup of wine to wish him long life, and Rong also raised wine in return to the emperor.

entries.zh: 鎔幼子昭誨從行，因許為婚。
entries.en: Rong's youngest son Zhaohui came along, and a marriage alliance was agreed.
entries.literal: Rong's youngest son Zhaohui accompanied the journey; they therefore pledged marriage.

entries.zh: 八月甲子，幽州劉守光僭稱大燕皇帝，年號應天。
entries.en: On jiazi in the eighth month Liu Shouguang of Youzhou declared himself emperor of Great Yan and took the era name Yingtian.
entries.literal: On jiazi in the eighth month Liu Shouguang of Youzhou presumptuously titled himself emperor of Great Yan, with era name Yingtian.

entries.zh: 九月庚子，梁祖將親軍自洛渡河而北，至相州，聞帝軍未出，乃止。
entries.en: On gengzi in the ninth month the Liang Founder led his personal army from Luoyang north across the Yellow River to Xiangzhou; learning the emperor's forces had not moved, he stopped.
entries.literal: On gengzi in the ninth month the Liang Founder led his personal army from Luoyang north across the river to Xiangzhou; hearing the emperor's army had not marched out, he halted.

entries.zh: 十月，幽州劉守光殺帝之行人李承勳，忿其不行朝禮也。
entries.en: In the tenth month Liu Shouguang of Youzhou killed the emperor's envoy Li Chengxun, furious that he would not observe court ceremony.
entries.literal: Tenth month, Liu Shouguang of Youzhou killed the emperor's traveling envoy Li Chengxun, angry that he did not perform court rites.

entries.zh: 莊宗光聖神閔孝皇帝，諱存勖，武皇帝之長子也。
entries.en: Zhuangzong, the Guangsheng Shenmin Xiao emperor, bore the taboo name Cunxu and was Wuhuang's eldest son.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong Guangsheng Shenmin Xiao, taboo name Cunxu, was the eldest son of Emperor Wuhuang.

entries.zh: 母曰貞簡皇后曹氏，以唐光啟元年歲在乙巳，冬十月二十二日癸亥，生帝於晉陽宮。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Zhenjian, née Cao; in Tang Guangqi 1 (yisi), on the twenty-second of the tenth month (guihai), he was born at the Jinyang palace.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Zhenjian of the Cao clan; in Tang Guangqi year 1, year yisi, on the twenty-second day of the tenth winter month, day guihai, the Emperor was born in the Jinyang palace.

entries.zh: 妊時，曹後嘗夢神人，黑衣擁扇，夾侍左右。
entries.en: During her pregnancy Empress Cao dreamed of a god in black with a fan, flanked by attendants.
entries.literal: While pregnant, Empress Cao once dreamed of a divine man in black holding a fan, attendants flanking left and right.

entries.zh: 載誕之辰，紫氣出於窗戶。
entries.en: At his birth purple mist rose from the windows.
entries.literal: On the day of birth, purple vapor issued from the windows.

entries.zh: 及為嬰兒，體貌奇特，沈厚不群，武皇特所鍾愛。
entries.en: Even as a baby he looked unusual—solemn and apart—and Wuhuang doted on him.
entries.literal: As an infant his form was extraordinary, grave and unlike the crowd; Wuhuang especially cherished him.

entries.zh: 及武皇之討王行瑜，帝時年十一，從行。
entries.en: When Wuhuang marched against Wang Xingyu, Cunxu was eleven and went with him.
entries.literal: When Wuhuang campaigned against Wang Xingyu, the Emperor was eleven and accompanied the expedition.

entries.zh: 初令入覲獻捷，迎駕還宮，昭宗一見駭之，曰：「此兒有奇表。」
entries.en: Sent first to court with news of victory to escort the throne home, he so startled Zhaozong that the emperor said, "This boy has a remarkable face."
entries.literal: He was first sent to court to present victory and welcome the carriage back to the palace; Zhaozong on seeing him was startled and said: "This child has an extraordinary mien."

entries.zh: 因撫其背曰：「兒將來之國棟也，勿忘忠孝於予家。」
entries.en: Zhaozong stroked his back and said, "You will be a pillar of the realm—do not forget loyalty and filial duty to our house."
entries.literal: He stroked his back and said: "Child, you will be a pillar of the state; do not forget loyalty and filial piety toward our house."

entries.zh: 因賜鸂鶒酒卮、翡翠盤。
entries.en: He gave him a xichi wine cup and a jadeite dish.
entries.literal: He then bestowed a xichi wine cup and a jadeite plate.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：昭宗曰：「此子可亞其父。」
entries.en: (The 《Northern Dreams Miscellany》 records Zhaozong saying, "This boy can stand next to his father."
entries.literal: (The 《Northern Dreams Miscellany》 says: Zhaozong said: "This son can rank next to his father."

entries.zh: 時人號曰「亞子」。）〉
entries.en: So people called him "Lesser Son." )〉
entries.literal: People of the time nicknamed him "Lesser Son." )〉

entries.zh: 賊平，授檢校司空、隰州刺史，改汾、晉二郡，皆遙領之。
entries.en: After the rebels were crushed he received acting Sikong and Xi prefect, then Fen and Jin as well—all in absentia.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was made acting Sikong and prefect of Xi; he was transferred to the two prefectures Fen and Jin, both held in absentia.

entries.zh: 帝洞曉音律，常令歌舞於前。
entries.en: Cunxu knew music well and kept singers and dancers before him.
entries.literal: The Emperor thoroughly understood music and often had song and dance before him.

entries.zh: 十三習《春秋》，手自繕寫，略通大義。
entries.en: At thirteen he studied the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, copied it himself, and understood its gist.
entries.literal: At thirteen he studied the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, copied it by hand, and grasped the main meaning.

entries.zh: 及壯，便射騎，膽略絕人，其心豁如也。
entries.en: Grown, he excelled at mounted archery, with courage and daring few could match and a mind at ease.
entries.literal: When grown he was skilled at mounted archery; courage and strategy were beyond others, and his mind was open and clear.

entries.zh: 四月甲申，燕將李暉等二十餘人舉族來奔。
entries.en: On jiashen in the fourth month over twenty Yan officers led by Li Hui defected with their families.
entries.literal: Fourth month, jiashen, more than twenty Yan officers including Li Hui came over with their clans.

entries.zh: 德威攻幽州南門。
entries.en: Dewei assaulted the south gate of Youzhou.
entries.literal: Dewei attacked Youzhou's south gate.

entries.zh: 壬辰，劉守光遣使王遵化致書哀祈於德威，德威戲遵化曰：「大燕皇帝尚未郊天，何怯劣如是耶！」
entries.en: On renchen Liu Shouguang sent Wang Zunhua with a groveling letter; Dewei mocked him: "The Great Yan emperor has not even sacrificed at the suburbs—why so craven!"
entries.literal: On renchen Liu Shouguang sent envoy Wang Zunhua with a letter of tearful plea to Dewei; Dewei jested to Zunhua: "The Great Yan emperor has not yet performed the suburban sacrifice—why so timid!"

entries.zh: 守光再遣哀祈，德威乃以狀聞。
entries.en: Shouguang pleaded again, and Dewei forwarded the report.
entries.literal: Shouguang again sent tearful pleas, and Dewei then reported it in a memorial.

entries.zh: 己亥，劉光浚攻下平州，獲刺史張在吉。
entries.en: On jihai Liu Guangjun seized Ping prefecture and took Prefect Zhang Zaiji.
entries.literal: On jihai Liu Guangjun took Ping prefecture and captured prefect Zhang Zaiji.

entries.zh: 六月壬申朔，帝遣監軍張承業至幽州，與周德威會議軍事。
entries.en: On the renshen new moon of the sixth month Cunxu sent Zhang Chengye to Youzhou to plan with Zhou Dewei.
entries.literal: Sixth month, first day renshen, the Emperor sent supervising commissioner Zhang Chengye to Youzhou to confer on military affairs with Zhou Dewei.

entries.zh: 秋七月，承業與德威率千騎至幽州西，守光遣人持信箭一隻，乞修和好。
entries.en: In the seventh month Chengye and Dewei took a thousand horse to the west of Youzhou; Shouguang sent a man with a single signal arrow suing for peace.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Chengye and Dewei led a thousand horse west of Youzhou; Shouguang sent a man with one signal arrow begging to restore peace.

entries.zh: 承業曰：「燕帥當令子弟一人為質則可。」
entries.en: Chengye answered, "The Yan lord must leave a son or younger brother as hostage—only then."
entries.literal: Chengye said: "The Yan commander must send one son or younger brother as hostage—only then is it acceptable."

entries.zh: 是日，燕將司全爽等十一人，並舉族來奔。
entries.en: That same day eleven Yan officers led by Si Quanshuang defected with their families.
entries.literal: That day eleven Yan officers including Si Quanshuang, each with their clans, came over.

entries.zh: 辛亥，德威進攻諸城門。
entries.en: On xinhai Dewei assaulted the gates.
entries.literal: On xinhai Dewei pressed the attack on the city gates.

entries.zh: 壬子，賊將楊師貴等五十人來降。
entries.en: On renzi fifty enemy officers led by Yang Shigui surrendered.
entries.literal: On renzi fifty rebel officers including Yang Shigui came to surrender.

entries.zh: 甲子，五院軍使李信攻下莫州。
entries.en: On jiazi Li Xin of the Five-Courts Army seized Mo prefecture.
entries.literal: On jiazi Five-Courts Army commissioner Li Xin took Mo prefecture.

entries.zh: 時守光繼遣人乞降，將緩帝軍，陰令其將孟修、阮通謀於滄州節度使劉守奇，及求援於楊師厚，帝之遊騎擒其使以獻。
entries.en: Shouguang kept suing to surrender to stall Cunxu while Meng Xiu and Ruan Tong secretly dealt with Liu Shouqi at Cangzhou and asked Yang Shihou for help—until Jin scouts seized the envoys and brought them in.
entries.literal: At that time Shouguang repeatedly sent men begging to surrender, intending to slow the Emperor's army; secretly he ordered his generals Meng Xiu and Ruan Tong to plot with Cangzhou military commissioner Liu Shouqi and also to seek aid from Yang Shihou—the Emperor's roaming scouts seized their envoys and presented them.

entries.zh: 是月，帝會王鎔於天長。
entries.en: That month Cunxu met Wang Rong at Tianchang.
entries.literal: That month the Emperor met Wang Rong at Tianchang.

entries.zh: 五月壬寅朔，光浚進迫營州，刺史楊靖以城降。
entries.en: On the renyin new moon of the fifth month Guangjun pressed Ying; Prefect Yang Jing yielded the city.
entries.literal: Fifth month, first day renyin, Guangjun advanced on Ying prefecture; prefect Yang Jing surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 乙巳，梁將楊師厚會劉守奇率大軍侵鎮州。
entries.en: On yisi Yang Shihou united with Liu Shouqi and invaded Zhen with a large force.
entries.literal: On yisi Liang general Yang Shihou joined Liu Shouqi with a great army invading Zhen prefecture.

entries.zh: 時帝之先鋒將史建瑭自趙州率五百騎入真定，師厚大掠鎮、冀之屬邑。
entries.en: Cunxu's vanguard Shi Jiantang rode five hundred horse from Zhao into Zhending while Shihou ravaged the Zhen and Ji countryside.
entries.literal: At that time the Emperor's vanguard Shi Jiantang from Zhao prefecture led five hundred horse into Zhending; Shihou greatly plundered the subordinate counties of Zhen and Ji.

entries.zh: 王熔告急於周德威，德威分兵赴援，師厚移軍寇滄州，張萬進懼，遂降於梁。
entries.en: Wang Rong begged Zhou Dewei for help; Dewei detached a relief column; Shihou turned on Cangzhou, and a frightened Zhang Wanjin went over to Liang.
entries.literal: Wang Rong reported urgency to Zhou Dewei; Dewei divided troops to go to the rescue; Shihou shifted the army to raid Cangzhou, and Zhang Wanjin in fear then surrendered to Liang.

entries.zh: 十二月庚午，墨製授周德威幽州節度使。
entries.en: On gengwu in the twelfth month a black-edict made Zhou Dewei military commissioner of Youzhou.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, gengwu, by black-edict Zhou Dewei was made Youzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 癸酉，檀州燕樂縣人執劉守光並妻李氏祝氏、子繼祚以獻。
entries.en: On guiyou men of Yanle in Tan seized Liu Shouguang with his wives Lady Li and Lady Zhu and his son Jizuo and delivered them.
entries.literal: On guiyou the people of Yanle county in Tan prefecture seized Liu Shouguang together with his wife Lady Li, Lady Zhu, and son Jizuo and presented them.

entries.zh: 己卯，帝下令班師，自雲、代而旋。
entries.en: On jimao Cunxu ordered the host to withdraw by way of Yun and Dai.
entries.literal: On jimao the Emperor ordered withdrawal of the army, returning by Yun and Dai.

entries.zh: 時鎮州王鎔、定州王處直遣使請帝由井陘而西，許之。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Zhen and Wang Chuzhi of Ding asked him to return west through Jingxing, and he consented.
entries.literal: At that time Zhen prefecture's Wang Rong and Ding prefecture's Wang Chuzhi sent envoys asking the Emperor to go west by Jingxing Pass; he agreed.

entries.zh: 庚辰，帝發幽州，擄仁恭父子以行。
entries.en: On gengchen he left Youzhou with Rengong and his son in bonds.
entries.literal: On gengchen the Emperor set out from Youzhou, taking Rengong and his son as captives.

entries.zh: 甲申，次定州，舍於關城。
entries.en: On jiashen he stopped at Ding and lodged at Guancheng.
entries.literal: On jiashen he halted at Ding prefecture and lodged at Guancheng.

entries.zh: 翌日，次曲陽，與王處直謁北嶽祠。
entries.en: The next day he reached Quyang and with Wang Chuzhi worshipped at the North Peak shrine.
entries.literal: Next day he halted at Quyang and with Wang Chuzhi paid respects at the North Peak temple.

entries.zh: 是日，次衡唐，鎮州王鎔迎謁於路。
entries.en: That day he reached Hengtang, where Wang Rong met him on the road.
entries.literal: That day he halted at Hengtang; Zhen prefecture's Wang Rong met and welcomed him on the road.

entries.zh: 天祐十一年春正月戊戌朔，王鎔以履新之日，與其子昭祚、昭誨奉觴上壽置宴。
entries.en: On the wuxu new moon of the first month of Tianyou 11 Wang Rong, on the day of new shoes, feasted Cunxu with his sons Zhaozuo and Zhaohui, toasting his long life.
entries.literal: Spring of Tianyou 11, first month, first day wuxu, Wang Rong on the day of renewed shoes, with his sons Zhaozuo and Zhaohui, raised a cup, offered longevity wishes, and set a banquet.

entries.zh: 鎔啟曰：「燕主劉太師頃為鄰國，今欲挹其風儀，可乎？」
entries.en: Rong asked, "Grand Tutor Liu was our neighbor—may I meet the man?"
entries.literal: Rong opened and said: "Grand Tutor Liu of Yan was lately a neighboring state; now I wish to draw on his bearing—may I?"

entries.zh: 帝即命主者破械，引仁恭、守光至，與之同宴，鎔饋以衣被飲食。
entries.en: Cunxu had their bonds struck off and brought Rengong and Shouguang to the table; Rong supplied them with clothes, bedding, food, and drink.
entries.literal: The Emperor at once ordered the chief steward to break their fetters and led Rengong and Shouguang to the same banquet; Rong gave them clothing, bedding, food, and drink.

entries.zh: 己亥，帝發鎮州，因與王鎔畋於衡唐之西。
entries.en: On jihai he left Zhen and hunted west of Hengtang with Wang Rong.
entries.literal: On jihai the Emperor set out from Zhen prefecture and with Wang Rong hunted west of Hengtang.

entries.zh: 壬子，至晉陽，以組練繫仁恭、守光，號令而入。
entries.en: On renzi he reached Jinyang, led Rengong and Shouguang in with silken bonds, and entered in state.
entries.literal: On renzi he reached Jinyang, bound Rengong and Shouguang with silken cords, and entered at the command.

entries.zh: 是日，誅守光。
entries.en: That day Shouguang was put to death.
entries.literal: That day Shouguang was executed.

entries.zh: 遣大將李存霸拘送仁恭於代州，刺其心血奠告於武皇陵，然後斬之。
entries.en: Li Cunba escorted Rengong to Dai, pierced his heart and offered the blood at Wuhuang's tomb, then struck off his head.
entries.literal: A great general, Li Cunba, was sent to escort Rengong under guard to Dai prefecture, pierce his heart-blood and offer it in report at Wuhuang's tomb, and then behead him.

entries.zh: 是月，鎮州王鎔、定州王處直遣使推帝為尚書令。
entries.en: That month Wang Rong and Wang Chuzhi sent envoys urging Cunxu to accept the post of Director-in-Chief.
entries.literal: That month Zhen prefecture's Wang Rong and Ding prefecture's Wang Chuzhi sent envoys urging the Emperor as Director-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 初，王鎔稱藩於梁，梁以鎔為尚書令，至是鎮、定以帝南破梁軍，北定幽、薊，乃共推崇焉。
entries.en: Rong had once bowed to Liang and been made Director-in-Chief; now Zhen and Ding, after Cunxu's southern victories and northern pacification, jointly pressed the title on him.
entries.literal: Earlier Wang Rong had submitted as a vassal to Liang, and Liang made Rong Director-in-Chief; now Zhen and Ding, because the Emperor had broken Liang armies in the south and settled You and Ji in the north, together promoted him.

entries.zh: 使三至，帝讓乃從之，遂選日受冊，開霸府，建行台，如武德故事。
entries.en: Three embassies came before he yielded; he chose a day for the rite, opened a hegemon's office, and set up a field headquarters after the Wude precedent.
entries.literal: Envoys came thrice; the Emperor declined until he followed; he then chose a day to receive the investiture, opened a hegemon's bureau, and established a field headquarters on the Wude model.

entries.zh: 天祐九年春正月庚辰朔，周德威等自飛狐東下。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianyou 9 (gengchen new moon), Zhou Dewei led his force east from Feihu.
entries.literal: In spring of Tianyou 9, first month, first day gengchen, Zhou Dewei and others marched east from Feihu.

entries.zh: 丙戌，會鎮、定之師進營祁溝。
entries.en: On bingxu the Zhen and Ding columns joined and encamped at Qigou.
entries.literal: On bingxu the armies of Zhen and Ding united and advanced to camp at Qigou.

entries.zh: 庚子，次涿州，刺史劉知溫以城歸順。
entries.en: On gengzi they reached Zhuozhou, where Prefect Liu Zhiwen opened the gates.
entries.literal: On gengzi they halted at Zhuozhou; prefect Liu Zhiwen surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 德威進迫幽州，守光出兵拒戰，燕將王行方等以部下四百人來奔。
entries.en: Dewei closed on Youzhou; Shouguang marched out to fight, while Yan officers including Wang Xingfang defected with four hundred men.
entries.literal: Dewei pressed toward Youzhou; Shouguang led troops to resist; Yan generals Wang Xingfang and others with four hundred followers came over.

entries.zh: 天祐十八年春正月，魏州開元寺僧傳真獲傳國寶，獻於行台。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianyou 18 the Kaiyuan monk Chuanzhen at Weizhou found the heirloom seal and sent it to headquarters.
entries.literal: Spring of Tianyou 18, first month, a monk of Weizhou's Kaiyuan Temple named Chuanzhen obtained the dynastic heirloom seal and presented it to the field headquarters.

entries.zh: 驗其文，即「受命於天，子孫寶之」八字也，群僚稱賀。
entries.en: The characters proved to be the eight words "Mandated by Heaven—may sons and grandsons treasure it," and the staff hailed the omen.
entries.literal: Examining the inscription, it was exactly the eight characters "Mandated by Heaven—may sons and grandsons treasure it"; the officials all offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 傳真師於廣明中，遇京師喪亂得之，秘藏已四十年矣。
entries.en: Chuanzhen said he had taken it during the Guangming disorders and kept it secret for forty years.
entries.literal: Chuanzhen said that in the Guangming era, amid the capital's turmoil, he had obtained it and kept it hidden for forty years.

entries.zh: 篆文古體，人不之識，至是獻之。
entries.en: The archaic seal script had baffled everyone until he brought it forward.
entries.literal: The seal script was ancient and none could read it; only now was it presented.

entries.zh: 時淮南楊溥、四川王衍皆遣使致書，勸帝嗣唐帝位，帝不從。
entries.en: Yang Pu of Huainan and Wang Yan of Shu both wrote urging Cunxu to take the Tang throne; he refused.
entries.literal: At that time Yang Pu of Huainan and Wang Yan of Sichuan both sent envoys with letters urging the Emperor to succeed to the Tang throne; the Emperor would not agree.

entries.zh: 二月，代州刺史王建及卒。
entries.en: In the second month Wang Jianji of Dai died.
entries.literal: Second month, Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji died.

entries.zh: 是月，鎮州大將張文禮殺其帥王鎔。
entries.en: That month Zhang Wenli, a senior Zhen commander, murdered his lord Wang Rong.
entries.literal: That month a great Zhen officer, Zhang Wenli, killed his commander Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 時帝方與諸將宴，酒酣樂作，聞鎔遇弑，遽投觶而泣曰：「趙王與吾把臂同盟，分如金石，何負於人，覆宗絕祀，冤哉！」
entries.en: Cunxu was drinking with his officers when word came that Rong had been killed; he flung down his cup and wept: "The Prince of Zhao was my sworn brother, our bond iron-hard—what had he done to anyone, that his clan is wiped out? Monstrous wrong!"
entries.literal: The Emperor was then feasting with his generals; when the music was loud and the wine deep he heard that Rong had been assassinated, abruptly cast aside his cup and wept, saying: "Prince Zhao clasped arms with me in alliance, our bond like metal and stone—what wrong did he do anyone, that his house is destroyed and his line cut off? What injustice!"

entries.zh: 先是，滹沱暴漲，漂關城之半，溺死者千計。
entries.en: Earlier the Hutuo had burst and swept away half the frontier town, drowning thousands.
entries.literal: Earlier the Hutuo had flooded violently, washing away half the pass city; those drowned numbered in the thousands.

entries.zh: 是歲，天西北有赤昆如血，占者言趙分之災，至是果驗。
entries.en: That year a blood-red cloud hung in the northwest; seers called it Zhao's doom—and so it proved.
entries.literal: That year in the northwest sky a crimson vapor like blood appeared; diviners said it foretold disaster for Zhao territory—and now it was fulfilled.

entries.zh: 時張文禮遣使請旄節於帝，帝曰：「 文禮之罪，期於無赦，敢邀予旄節！」
entries.en: Wenli then asked Cunxu for a commission; Cunxu said, "Wenli deserves no mercy—how dare he ask for my seal!"
entries.literal: Zhang Wenli then sent envoys begging a commission from the Emperor; the Emperor said: "Wenli's crime admits no pardon—how dare he ask my banner!"

entries.zh: 左右曰：「方今事繁，不欲與人生事。」
entries.en: His attendants said, "Matters are urgent—we should not pick another fight."
entries.literal: Those beside him said: "Affairs are pressing now; we do not wish to pick another fight."

entries.zh: 帝不得已而從之，乃承製授文禮鎮州兵馬留後。
entries.en: Cunxu yielded and, by rescript, confirmed Wenli as acting military commissioner of Zhen.
entries.literal: The Emperor had no choice but to agree and, by imperial rescript, made Wenli Zhenzhou military commissioner in temporary charge.

entries.zh: 八月庚申，令天平節度使閻寶、成德兵馬留後符習率兵討張文禮於鎮州。
entries.en: On gengshen in the eighth month Yan Bao of Taiping and Fu Xi, acting commander of Chengde, marched on Wenli at Zhen.
entries.literal: Eighth month, gengshen, ordered Taiping commissioner Yan Bao and Chengde acting commander Fu Xi to lead troops against Zhang Wenli at Zhen.

entries.zh: 初，王鎔令偏將符習以本部兵從帝屯於德勝。
entries.en: Rong had earlier detached Fu Xi with his own command to serve at Desheng under Cunxu.
entries.literal: Earlier Wang Rong had ordered subordinate general Fu Xi to bring his own troops with the Emperor's camp at Desheng.

entries.zh: 文禮既行弑逆，忌鎔故將，多被誅戮，因遣使聞於帝，欲以他兵代習歸鎮，習等懼，請留。
entries.en: After the murder Wenli purged Rong's veterans and asked Cunxu to swap other troops for Fu Xi's return; Xi and his men, in fear, begged to remain.
entries.literal: After Wenli's regicide he feared Rong's old officers and many were executed; he therefore sent word to the Emperor wishing other troops to replace Xi and return to Zhen, and Xi and the rest were afraid and asked to stay.

entries.zh: 帝令傳旨於習及別將趙仁貞、烏震等，明正文禮弑逆之罪，且言：「爾等荷戟從征，蓋君父之故，銜冤報恩，誰人無心。
entries.en: Cunxu sent orders to Xi, Zhao Renzhen, and Wu Zhen, spelling out Wenli's crime and saying, "You marched for lord and father—who would not want vengeance?
entries.literal: The Emperor sent word to Xi and the other commanders Zhao Renzhen and Wu Zhen, stating Wenli's regicide plainly and saying: "You bore arms on campaign for father and lord; who lacks a heart to repay a wrong with gratitude?

entries.zh: 吾當給爾資糧，助爾兵甲，爾試思之！」
entries.en: I will feed you and arm you—think on it!"
entries.literal: I shall give you provisions and aid you with arms—think on it!"

entries.zh: 於是習等率諸將三十餘人，慟哭於牙門，請討文禮。
entries.en: Xi and thirty-odd officers wept at the gate and begged leave to punish Wenli.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xi and more than thirty other commanders wept at headquarters and begged to punish Wenli.

entries.zh: 帝因授習成德軍兵馬留後，以部下鎮、冀兵致討於文禮；
entries.en: Cunxu made Xi acting commander of Chengde and sent the Zhen and Ji columns against Wenli;
entries.literal: The Emperor then appointed Xi acting Chengde army commander and sent the Zhen and Ji troops under him against Wenli;

entries.zh: 又遣閻寶以助之，以史建瑭為前鋒。
entries.en: Yan Bao followed to assist, with Shi Jiantang in the van.
entries.literal: he also sent Yan Bao to help, with Shi Jiantang as vanguard.

entries.zh: 甲子，攻趙州，刺史王鋌送符印以迎，閻寶遂引軍至鎮州城下，營於西北隅。
entries.en: On jiazi they took Zhao; Prefect Wang Di handed over his seal; Yan Bao then pitched camp below Zhen's northwest wall.
entries.literal: On jiazi they attacked Zhao prefecture; prefect Wang Di surrendered his seal to welcome them; Yan Bao then led the army to below the walls of Zhen and camped at the northwest corner.

entries.zh: 是月，張文禮病疽而卒，其子處瑾代掌軍事。
entries.en: That month Wenli died of a boil; his son Chujin succeeded him.
entries.literal: That month Zhang Wenli died of carbuncle; his son Chujin took command.

entries.zh: 九月，前鋒將史建瑭與鎮人戰於城下，為流矢所中而卒。
entries.en: In the ninth month Shi Jiantang fought under the walls and fell to a stray shaft.
entries.literal: Ninth month, vanguard Shi Jiantang fought the Zhen men below the walls and was struck by a stray arrow and died.

entries.zh: 天祐十六年春正月，李存審城德勝，夾河為柵。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianyou 16 Li Cunshen fortified Desheng and ran stockades along both sides of the Yellow River.
entries.literal: In spring of Tianyou 16, first month, Li Cunshen walled Desheng and set palisades along both banks of the river.

entries.zh: 帝還魏州，命昭義軍節度使李嗣昭權知幽州軍府事。
entries.en: Cunxu went back to Weizhou and left Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi as acting head of the Youzhou command.
entries.literal: The Emperor returned to Weizhou and ordered Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao to act as provisional administrator of the Youzhou military headquarters.

entries.zh: 三月，帝兼領幽州，遣近臣李紹宏提舉府事。
entries.en: In the third month he added Youzhou to his own titles and sent Li Shaohong to run the prefectural office.
entries.literal: Third month, the Emperor also took Youzhou in personal charge and sent close attendant Li Shaohong to oversee headquarters affairs.

entries.zh: 辛卯，亳州太清宮道士上言，聖祖殿前古檜萎瘁已久再生一枝，圖畫以進。
entries.en: On xinmao a Taoist of Bozhou's Taiqing Palace reported that before the Sacred Ancestor's hall an ancient cypress, long withered, had sprouted a new branch and submitted a painting of it.
entries.literal: On xinmao, a Taoist of Taiqing Palace in Bozhou submitted word that before the hall of the Sacred Ancestor an ancient cypress, long withered, had put forth a new branch; he presented a painted image of it.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「當聖祖舊殿生枯檜新枝，應皇家再造之期，顯大國中興之運。
entries.en: An edict said, "When the Sacred Ancestor's old hall bore new shoots on a withered cypress, it marked the royal house's renewal and the great state's revival.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Where the Sacred Ancestor's old hall bore withered cypress and new branch, it answers the royal house's term of renewed creation and shows the great state's fortune of revival.

entries.zh: 同上林仆柳，祥既葉於漢宣；
entries.en: Like the fallen willow at Shanglin that answered under Han Xuandi,
entries.literal: It matches the fallen willow at Shanglin—its auspice already answered under Han Xuandi;

entries.zh: 比南頓嘉禾，瑞更超於光武。
entries.en: and like the fine grain at Nandun, a sign surpassing even Guangwu.
entries.literal: it compares to the fine grain at Nandun—a portent surpassing even Guangwu.

entries.zh: 宜標史冊，以示寰瀛」云。
entries.en: Let it be written in the histories and shown to the realm." Thus ended the edict.
entries.literal: It should be recorded in the histories and shown to the realm" — thus.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：唐高祖神堯皇帝武德二年，枯檜重華，至安祿山僭號萎瘁。
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says: In Wude 2 of Tang Gaozu the withered cypress put out new growth; when An Lushan usurped the throne it withered again.
entries.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says: In Wude 2 of Tang Gaozu the Divine Yao Emperor, the withered cypress flourished anew; when An Lushan usurped the title it withered and failed.

entries.zh: 明皇自蜀歸京，枝葉復盛。
entries.en: When Minghuang returned from Shu to the capital it flourished again.
entries.literal: When Minghuang returned from Shu to the capital, branches and leaves flourished again.

entries.zh: 至是再生一枝，長二尺餘。）〉
entries.en: Now a branch sprouted again, more than two chi long.)〉
entries.literal: By this time a branch grew anew, more than two chi long.)〉

entries.zh: 壬辰，幸伊闕。
entries.en: On renchen the Emperor went to Yique.
entries.literal: On renchen, the Emperor visited Yique.

entries.zh: 己巳，以中書舍人崔居儉為刑部侍郎，充史館修撰、判館事。
entries.en: On jisi Palace Attendant Cui Jujian was made Vice Minister of Punishments and charged as reviser of the History Office with direction of its affairs.
entries.literal: On jisi, Palace Attendant Cui Juyi was made Vice Minister of Punishments, and charged as reviser of the History Office and chief of the institute.

entries.zh: 甲午，以租庸副使、光祿大夫、檢校司徒、守衛尉卿孔謙為鹽鐵轉運副使。
entries.en: On jiawu Kong Qian, assistant commissioner for tributary and labor levies, honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Education, and Defender of the Guard, was made deputy commissioner for salt, iron, and transport.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Assistant Commissioner for Tributary and Labor Levies, Honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Education, and Defender of the Guard Kong Qian was made Deputy Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport.

entries.zh: 同光元年冬十月辛未朔，日有食之。
entries.en: On the xinwei new moon of the tenth month in winter of Tongguang 1 the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, Tongguang year 1, xinwei new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.

entries.zh: 是日，皇后劉氏、皇子繼岌歸鄴宮，帝送於離亭，歔欷而別。
entries.en: That day Empress Liu and Prince Jiji left for Ye; Cunxu saw them off at the roadside pavilion, weeping as they parted.
entries.literal: That day, Empress Liu and Prince Jiji returned to the Ye palace; the Emperor saw them off at the parting pavilion and parted with sobs.

entries.zh: 詔宣徽使李紹宏、宰相豆盧革、租庸使張憲、興唐尹王正言同守鄴城。
entries.en: He left Li Shaohong of the Secretariat, Chancellor Dou Luge, revenue chief Zhang Xian, and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan to hold Ye together.
entries.literal: He ordered Palace Secretariat commissioner Li Shaohong, chancellor Dou Luge, revenue commissioner Zhang Xian, and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan jointly to hold Ye city.

entries.zh: 壬申，帝御大軍自楊劉濟河。
entries.en: On renshen Cunxu led the main force across from Yangliu.
entries.literal: On renshen the Emperor led the great army across the river from Yangliu.

entries.zh: 癸酉，至鄆州。
entries.en: On guiyou he reached Yunzhou.
entries.literal: On guiyou he reached Yun prefecture.

entries.zh: 是夜三鼓，渡汶。
entries.en: That night at the third watch they forded the Wen.
entries.literal: That night at the third watch they crossed the Wen.

entries.zh: 時王彥章守中都。
entries.en: Wang Yanzhang was then defending Zhongdu.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Yanzhang was holding Zhongdu.

entries.zh: 甲戌，帝攻之，中都素無城守，師既雲合，梁眾自潰。
entries.en: On jiaxu Cunxu assaulted it; Zhongdu had no real walls, his hosts closed in like clouds, and the Liang force broke apart.
entries.literal: On jiaxu the Emperor attacked it; Zhongdu had never had proper city defenses, the armies massed like clouds, and the Liang masses collapsed on their own.

entries.zh: 是日，擒梁將王彥章及都監張漢傑、趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、康文通、王山興等將吏二百餘人，斬馘二萬，奪馬千匹。
entries.en: That day he took Wang Yanzhang and overseers Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Kang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and over two hundred officers—twenty thousand heads and a thousand horses.
entries.literal: That day he captured Liang general Wang Yanzhang and overseers Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Kang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and more than two hundred officers and clerks; twenty thousand heads were taken, and a thousand horses seized.

entries.zh: 時既獲中都之捷，帝召諸將謀其所向，或言且徇兗州，徐圖進取，唯李嗣源曰：「宜急趨汴州。
entries.en: After Zhongdu fell Cunxu asked his generals where to strike; some urged taking Yanzhou first and advancing slowly, but Li Siyuan alone said, "March straight on Bian.
entries.literal: Now that the victory at Zhongdu was won, the Emperor summoned the generals to debate their next move; some said to sweep Yanzhou first and plan advance slowly, but only Li Siyuan said: "We should hurry on Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 段凝方領大軍駐於河上，假如便來赴援，直路又阻決河，須自滑州濟渡，十萬之眾，舟楫焉能卒辦？
entries.en: Duan Ning still holds the main army on the river; even if he rushed to help, the cut in the Yellow River blocks the straight road and he must cross at Huazhou—boats for a hundred thousand cannot be got in a day.
entries.literal: Duan Ning is just now leading the great army camped on the river; even if he came at once to relieve them, the direct route is blocked by the breached river and he would have to cross from Huazhou—how could a hundred thousand men ready boats overnight?

entries.zh: 此去汴城咫尺，若晝夜兼程，信宿即至，段凝未起河堧，夷門已為我有矣。
entries.en: Bian is a step away; march without rest and we are there in two nights—before Duan Ning stirs from the river, Yimen is ours.
entries.literal: From here Bian city is within a stone's throw; if we march day and night we reach it in two nights, and before Duan Ning leaves the riverbank Yimen will already be ours.

entries.zh: 臣請以千騎前驅，陛下禦軍徐進，鮮不克矣。」
entries.en: Let me take a thousand horse ahead while Your Majesty follows with the host—we cannot miss."
entries.literal: Your servant asks to lead a thousand horse in the van while Your Majesty brings the army slowly after—how could we fail?"

entries.zh: 帝嘉之。
entries.en: Cunxu approved.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved.

entries.zh: 是夜，嗣源率前軍先進。
entries.en: That night Siyuan marched ahead with the van.
entries.literal: That night Siyuan led the vanguard forward first.

entries.zh: 翌日，車駕即路。
entries.en: The next day the court set out.
entries.literal: Next day the imperial carriage took the road.

entries.zh: 丁丑，次曹州，郡將出降。
entries.en: On dingchou he stopped at Caozhou and the prefect surrendered.
entries.literal: On dingchou he halted at Cao prefecture; the prefect came out to surrender.

entries.zh: 是日，詔曰：「皇綱已正，紫禁方嚴，凡事內官，不合更居外地。
entries.en: That day an edict read, "The throne is secure and the palace strict; palace eunuchs must not live outside the capital.
entries.literal: That day an edict said: "The imperial net is already set right and the Forbidden City is now strict; in general palace eunuchs should not again reside outside the capital.

entries.zh: 詔諸道應有內官，不計高低，並仰逐處並家口發遣赴闕，不得輒有停滯。」
entries.en: Every circuit must send its eunuchs and families to court at once, without delay."
entries.literal: All circuits with eunuchs, regardless of rank, are ordered to send them and their households to court at once from each place, with no delay."

entries.zh: 帝龍潛時，寺人數已及五百，至是合諸道赴闕者，約千餘人，皆給賜優贍，服玩華侈，委之事務，付以腹心。
entries.en: In his days as heir Cunxu already had five hundred eunuchs; now a thousand from the circuits came to court, richly paid, splendidly dressed, and trusted with power.
entries.literal: While the Emperor was still heir, eunuchs already numbered five hundred; now with those from the circuits who came to court there were about a thousand, all given generous stipends and splendid dress, entrusted with affairs and treated as confidants.

entries.zh: 唐時宦官為內諸司使務、諸鎮監軍，出納王命，造作威福，昭宗以此亡國。
entries.en: Under Tang eunuchs ran inner offices and supervised circuits, wielding royal power until Zhaozong lost the realm.
entries.literal: Under Tang, eunuchs served as inner-office commissioners and circuit supervisors, issuing the royal command and making their own might; Zhaozong for this lost the state.

entries.zh: 及帝奄有天下，當知戒彼前車，以為殷鑒，一朝復興茲弊，議者惜之。
entries.en: Having taken the realm he should have heeded that overturned cart, yet the abuse returned at once—commentators mourned it.
entries.literal: Now that the Emperor held all under heaven, he should have taken the overturned cart ahead as a warning, yet in one morning this abuse rose again—commentators lamented it.

entries.zh: 新羅王金樸英遣使朝貢。
entries.en: Silla's King Geumpyeong sent tribute envoys.
entries.literal: King Geumpyeong of Silla sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 辛亥，中書門下奏：「準本朝故事，諸王、內命婦、宰臣、學士、中書舍人、諸道節度、防禦、團練使、留後官告，即中書帖官告院索綾紙褾軸，下所司書寫印署畢，進入宣賜。
entries.en: On xinhai the Secretariat said, "By precedent, patents for princes, consorts, ministers, and commissioners need brocade from the Patent Office, then sealing and imperial grant.
entries.literal: On xinhai the Secretariat memorialized: "According to our court's precedent, patent scrolls for princes, inner consorts, chief ministers, academicians, Secretariat drafters, and military commissioners, observers, and regents require the Secretariat to obtain brocade paper and mounting shafts from the Patent Office, have the relevant office write and seal them, and present them for imperial bestowal.

entries.zh: 其文武兩班及諸道官員並奏薦將校，並合於所司送納朱膠綾紙價錢。
entries.en: Other civil and military officers and recommended commanders must pay for their brocade and paper.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials of both ranks and circuit officers, and commanders recommended in memorials, should all pay the price of vermilion glue and brocade paper to the relevant office.

entries.zh: 伏自偽梁，不分輕重，並從官給，今後如非前件事例，請官中不給告敕，其內司大官侍衛將校轉官，即不在此限。」
entries.en: Under Liang all ranks were supplied free; hereafter only the cases above get court paper—inner-office guards and promoted commanders excepted."
entries.literal: Since the false Liang court, rank was not distinguished and all were supplied from government stores; hereafter, except for the cases above, the court should not supply patents; inner-office great officers, bodyguards, and commanders promoted in rank are outside this limit."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 壬子，蜀主王衍致書於帝，稱有詐為天使，馳報收復汴州者，詔捕之，不獲。
entries.en: On renzi Wang Yan of Shu wrote that a fake envoy had reported Bian recovered; Cunxu ordered arrest but found no one.
entries.literal: On renzi Shu ruler Wang Yan wrote the Emperor that someone had falsely posed as an envoy and rushed word that Bian had been recovered; an edict ordered his arrest, but he was not caught.

entries.zh: 癸丑，有司奏：郊祀前二日，迎祔高祖、太宗、懿祖、獻祖、太祖神主於太廟。
entries.en: On guichou the rites office said that two days before the suburban rite the tablets of Gaozu through the Grand Ancestor should be brought to the temple.
entries.literal: On guichou the relevant office memorialized: two days before the suburban sacrifice, the spirit tablets of Gaozu, Taizong, the Honored Ancestor, the Offered Ancestor, and the Grand Ancestor should be welcomed and enshrined in the Imperial Temple.

entries.zh: 議者以中興唐祚，不宜以追封之祖雜有國之君以為昭穆，自懿祖已下，宜別立廟於代州，如後漢南陽故事可也。
entries.en: Some argued that restored Tang should not rank enfeoffed forebears with reigning emperors; from the Honored Ancestor down they wanted separate temples at Dai, as under Later Han.
entries.literal: Commentators held that in restoring Tang's fortune one should not mix posthumously enfeoffed ancestors with reigning sovereigns in the zhao-mu order; from the Honored Ancestor down they should have separate temples at Dai prefecture, as in Later Han's Nanyang precedent.

entries.zh: 幽州北面軍前奏，契丹還塞，詔李嗣源班師。
entries.en: Youzhou reported the Khitan had left; Li Siyuan was ordered home.
entries.literal: The northern Youzhou front reported that the Khitan had returned beyond the pass; an edict ordered Li Siyuan to withdraw.

entries.zh: 鳳翔節度使、秦王李茂貞上表，請行藩臣之禮，帝優報之。
entries.en: Li Maozhen of Fengxiang asked to act as a feudatory prince; Cunxu answered graciously.
entries.literal: Fengxiang military commissioner and Qin Prince Li Maozhen memorialized asking to perform the ritual of a feudatory prince; the Emperor answered him graciously.

entries.zh: 甲寅，帝於中興殿麵賜郭崇韜鐵券。
entries.en: On jiayin Cunxu personally gave Guo Chongtao an iron tally at Zhongxing Hall.
entries.literal: On jiayin the Emperor in person at Zhongxing Hall bestowed on Guo Chongtao an iron tally of mercy.

entries.zh: 有司上言：「皇太后到闕，皇帝合於銀台門內奉迎。」
entries.en: The rites office memorialized, "When the Empress Dowager reaches court, the Emperor should welcome her inside Yintai Gate."
entries.literal: The relevant office memorialized: "When the Empress Dowager reaches court, the Emperor should welcome her within the Yintai Gate."

entries.zh: 詔親至懷州奉迎。
entries.en: Cunxu was ordered to go himself to Huai to meet her.
entries.literal: An edict ordered him to go in person to Huai prefecture to welcome her.

entries.zh: 中書奏：「自二十三日後散齋內，車駕不合遠出。」
entries.en: The Secretariat memorialized, "From the twenty-third onward, during the scattering fast within the inner precinct, the imperial carriage should not go far."
entries.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "From the twenty-third onward, during the scattering fast within the inner precinct, the imperial carriage should not go far."

entries.zh: 詔改至河陽奉迎。
entries.en: Cunxu changed the meeting place to Heyang.
entries.literal: An edict changed the welcome to Heyang.

entries.zh: 以禮部尚書、興唐尹王正言依前禮部尚書，充租庸使。
entries.en: Wang Zhengyan stayed Minister of Rites and was made land-tax commissioner.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan remained Minister of Rites and was made commissioner of land tax and corvée.

entries.zh: 同光二年春正月庚子朔，帝御明堂殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the gengzi new moon in spring of Tongguang 2, Cunxu held new-year court in Mingtang Hall with full guard.
entries.literal: Spring, first month, Tongguang year 2, gengzi new moon: the Emperor took the Mingtang Hall to receive new-year congratulations; guards and escort followed the prescribed form.

entries.zh: 壬寅，南郊禮儀使、太常卿李燕進太廟登歌酌獻樂舞名，懿祖室曰《昭德之舞》，獻祖室曰《文明之舞》，太祖室曰《應天之舞》，昭宗室曰《永平之舞》。
entries.en: On renyin Li Yan, director of southern-suburb rites and Grand Master of Ceremonies, submitted the names of the ascent songs, libation offerings, and dances for the Imperial Ancestral Temple: for the chamber of the Honored Ancestor, 《Dance of Manifest Virtue》; for the Offered Ancestor, 《Dance of Civilizing Brilliance》; for the Grand Ancestor, 《Dance of Responding to Heaven》; and for Zhaozong, 《Dance of Eternal Peace》.
entries.literal: On renyin, Director of Southern Suburbs Rites and Grand Master of Ceremonies Li Yan presented the names of the ascent songs, libation offerings, and dances for the Imperial Ancestral Temple: for the chamber of the Honored Ancestor, the 《Dance of Manifest Virtue》; for the Offered Ancestor, the 《Dance of Civilizing Brilliance》; for the Grand Ancestor, the 《Dance of Responding to Heaven》; for Zhaozong, the 《Dance of Eternal Peace》.

entries.zh: 甲辰，幽州上言，契丹入寇至瓦橋。
entries.en: On jiachen Youzhou reported Khitan raiders at Wa Bridge.
entries.literal: On jiachen Youzhou reported that the Khitan had raided as far as Wa Bridge.

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》：時契丹日益強盛，遣使就唐求幽州，以處盧文進。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Records of the Khitan State》 says the Khitan were growing stronger and asked Tang for Youzhou for Lu Wenjin.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Records of the Khitan State》 says: At that time the Khitan grew daily stronger and sent envoys to Tang to ask for Youzhou to settle Lu Wenjin.)〉

entries.zh: 以天平軍節度使李嗣源為北面行營都招討使，陝州留後霍彥威為副，率軍援幽州。
entries.en: Li Siyuan of Tianping was made northern commander with Huo Yanwei of Shanzhou as deputy to relieve Youzhou.
entries.literal: Tianping military commissioner Li Siyuan was made overall northern campaign commander, with Shanzhou acting prefect Huo Yanwei as deputy, to lead troops to relieve Youzhou.

entries.zh: 己巳，故宣武軍節度副使、權知軍州事、檢校太傅王瓚贈太子太師。
entries.en: On jisi the late Wang Zan of Xuanwu was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On jisi the late Xuanwu deputy commissioner, acting prefect, and Grand Mentor Wang Zan was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 丁未，詔改朝元殿復為明堂殿，又改崇勳殿為中興殿。
entries.en: On dingwei Chaoyuan Hall was restored to Mingtang and Chongxun to Zhongxing.
entries.literal: On dingwei an edict changed Chaoyuan Hall back to Mingtang Hall and Chongxun Hall to Zhongxing Hall.

entries.zh: 戊申，以振武軍節度使、檢校太傅、同平章事李存霸權知潞州留後；
entries.en: On wushen Li Cunba of Zhenwu was made acting Lu prefect;
entries.literal: On wushen Zhenwu military commissioner, Grand Mentor, and co-equal chief minister Li Cunba was made acting Lu prefect;

entries.zh: 以知保大軍軍州事高允韜為檢校太保。
entries.en: and Gao Yuntao of Baoda was made Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Gao Yuntao, who held Baoda army and prefecture affairs, was made Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 庚戌，以涇原節度使、充秦王府諸道行軍司馬、開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼侍中李從嚴為檢校太尉、兼中書令，依前涇原軍節度使，充秦王府諸道行軍司馬。
entries.en: On gengxu Li Congyan, military governor of Jingyuan, campaign marshal for all circuits of the Prince of Qin's household, Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, honorary Grand Commandant, and concurrently Palace Attendant, was made honorary Grand Commandant and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, while remaining military governor of Jingyuan and campaign marshal for all circuits of the Prince of Qin's household.
entries.literal: On gengxu Jingyuan military commissioner, Qin Prince campaign marshal, Grand Preceptor, and vice director Li Congyan was made Grand Preceptor and chief minister, remaining Jingyuan commissioner and Qin Prince campaign marshal.

entries.zh: 詔改應順門為永曜門，太平門為萬春門，通政門為廣政門，鳳明門為韶和門，萬春門為中興門，解卸殿為端明殿。
entries.en: Gates and halls were renamed: Yingshun to Yongyao, Taiping to Wanchun, Tongzheng to Guangzheng, Fengming to Shaohe, Wanchun to Zhongxing, Jiezhuang to Duanming.
entries.literal: An edict changed Yingshun Gate to Yongyao Gate, Taiping Gate to Wanchun Gate, Tongzheng Gate to Guangzheng Gate, Fengming Gate to Shaohe Gate, Wanchun Gate to Zhongxing Gate, and Jiezhuang Hall to Duanming Hall.

entries.zh: 秋七月戊戌朔，故宣武軍節度使李存審男彥超進其父牙兵八千七百人。
entries.en: On the wuxu new moon of the seventh month Yanchao presented his late father Li Cunshen's guard of 8,700 men.
entries.literal: Seventh month, wuxu new moon: the late Xuanyang military commissioner Li Cunshen's son Yanchao presented his father's personal guard of eight thousand seven hundred men.

entries.zh: 己亥，中書門下奏：「每年南郊壇四祠祭，太微宮五薦獻，並宰臣攝太尉行事，惟太廟遣庶僚行事，此後太廟祠祭，亦望差宰臣行事。」
entries.en: "On jihai the Secretariat asked that temple rites, like altar and Taiwei offerings, be performed by chief ministers rather than junior staff."
entries.literal: On jihai the Secretariat memorialized: "Each year at the southern altar the four shrine offerings and at Taiwei Palace the five presentations are all performed by chief ministers acting as libationer; only the Imperial Temple sends junior officials—hereafter Imperial Temple offerings should also be assigned to chief ministers."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 乙巳，汴州雍丘縣大風，拔木傷稼。
entries.en: On yisi Yongqiu in Bianzhou had a wind that uprooted trees and ruined crops.
entries.literal: On yisi Yongqiu county in Bianzhou had a great wind that uprooted trees and damaged crops.

entries.zh: 曹州大雨，平地水三尺。
entries.en: Caozhou flooded three feet deep on level ground.
entries.literal: Caozhou had heavy rain and three feet of water on level ground.

entries.zh: 丙午，以襄州節度使孔為潞州節度使，李存霸為鄆州節度使。
entries.en: On bingwu Kong Qing, military governor of Xiang Prefecture, was made military governor of Lu Prefecture, and Li Cunba was made military governor of Yun Prefecture.
entries.literal: On bingwu Xiang military commissioner Kong was made Luzhou military commissioner, and Li Cunba was made Yun military commissioner.

entries.zh: 乙酉，幸龍門之雷山，祭天神，從北俗之舊事也。
entries.en: On yiyou Cunxu sacrificed at Thunder Mountain on Longmen, following a northern custom.
entries.literal: On yiyou the Emperor went to Thunder Mountain at Longmen to sacrifice to Heaven—following the northern custom of old.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以鄆州副使李紹珙為襄州留後，以前澤州刺史董璋為邠州留後。
entries.en: On xinhai Li Shaogong became Xiang regent, and Dong Zhang became Binzhou regent.
