entries.literal: On xinhai Yan deputy commissioner Li Shaogong was made Xiang regent; former Ze prefect Dong Zhang was made Bin regent.

entries.zh: 戊午，西川王衍遣偽署戶部侍郎歐陽彬來朝貢，稱「大蜀皇帝上書大唐皇帝」。
entries.en: On wuwu Wang Yan of Shu sent Ouyang Bin as tribute envoy, signing as "Great Shu Emperor to Great Tang Emperor."
entries.literal: On wuwu Shu ruler Wang Yan sent his false-appointed Vice Minister of Revenue Ouyang Bin to court with tribute, styling himself "Great Shu Emperor writing to the Great Tang Emperor."

entries.zh: 庚申，以應州為雲州屬郡，升新州為威塞軍節度使，以媯、儒、武等州為屬郡。
entries.en: On gengshen Ying was attached to Yun and Xin became Weisai commissioner over Ji, Ru, and Wu.
entries.literal: On gengshen Ying prefecture was made a subordinate of Yun prefecture; Xin was raised to Weisai military commissioner with Ji, Ru, and Wu as subordinates.

entries.zh: 壬戌，皇子繼岌妻王氏封魏國夫人。
entries.en: On renxu Jiji's wife Lady Wang was made Lady of Wei state.
entries.literal: On renxu the wife of Prince Jiji, Lady Wang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei state.

entries.zh: 幽州奏，契丹安巴堅東攻渤海。
entries.en: Youzhou said Khitan leader Ambagyan was attacking Bohai in the east.
entries.literal: Youzhou reported that the Khitan Ambagyan was attacking Bohai eastward.

entries.zh: 同光二年夏五月己亥，帝御文明殿，冊齊王張全義為太尉。
entries.en: On jihai in summer of Tongguang 2 Cunxu invested Zhang Quanyi as Prince of Qi and Grand Commandant at Wenming Hall.
entries.literal: Summer, fifth month, jihai, Tongguang year 2: the Emperor took Wenming Hall to invest Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 禮畢，全義赴尚書省領事，左諫議大夫竇專不降階，為御史所劾，專援引舊典，宰相不能詰，寢而不行。
entries.en: After the rite Quanyi took office at the Directorate; Dou Zhuan refused to step down and was impeached; citing precedent, he left the ministers unable to answer and the case died.
entries.literal: When the rite was done Quanyi went to the Directorate to take up office; Left Remonstrance Councillor Dou Zhuan did not descend the steps, was impeached by the censorate, cited old precedent, and the chief ministers could not rebut it—the matter was shelved.

entries.zh: 庚子，太常卿李燕卒。
entries.en: On gengzi Li Yan, Director of Ceremonies, died.
entries.literal: On gengzi Director of Ceremonies Li Yan died.

entries.zh: 壬寅，以教坊使陳俊為景州刺史，內園使儲德源為憲州刺史，皆梁之伶人也。
entries.en: On renyin Chen Jun of the Music Bureau became Jing prefect and Chu Deyuan of the Inner Gardens Xian prefect—both Liang actors.
entries.literal: On renyin Chen Jun, commissioner of the Music Bureau, was made Jing prefect, and Chu Deyuan, commissioner of the Inner Gardens, Xian prefect—both were Liang actor-retainers.

entries.zh: 初，帝平梁，俊與德源皆為寵伶周匝所薦，帝因許除郡，郭崇韜以為不可，伶官言之者眾，帝密召崇韜謂之曰：「予已許除郡，經年未行，我慚見二人，卿當屈意行之。」
entries.en: When Cunxu conquered Liang, Zhou Zha had recommended Jun and Deyuan for posts; Cunxu had promised them commands but Guo Chongtao objected; many actors pressed the case; Cunxu secretly told Guo, "I promised them prefectures a year ago and am ashamed to face them—humor me."
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor had pacified Liang, Jun and Deyuan had both been recommended by his favored actor Zhou Zha; he had promised them prefectures; Guo Chongtao held it impossible, yet many actor-officials spoke for it; the Emperor secretly summoned Chongtao and said, "I already promised them prefectures and for a year have not acted—I am ashamed to face the two of them; you must bend your will and carry it out."

entries.zh: 故有是命。
entries.en: Hence these appointments.
entries.literal: Hence this order.

entries.zh: 八月壬戌，詔諸司人吏，不許諸處奏薦，如有勞績，隻許本司奏聞。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on renxu, clerks were barred from outside recommendations; merit cases went only through their own office.
entries.literal: Eighth month, renxu: an edict forbade clerks of the various offices to seek recommendation everywhere; if they had merit, only their own office might memorialize it.

entries.zh: 詔有司，吳越王印宜以黃金鑄成，其文曰「吳越國王之印」。
entries.en: The court ordered a gold seal for the King of Wu-Yue inscribed "Seal of the King of Wu-Yue."
entries.literal: An edict ordered the relevant office: the seal of the King of Wu-Yue should be cast in gold, its inscription reading "Seal of the King of Wu-Yue."

entries.zh: 丁卯，帝釋服，百官奉慰於長壽宮。
entries.en: On dingmao Cunxu left mourning; officials consoled him at Changshou Palace.
entries.literal: On dingmao the Emperor ended mourning; the hundred officials offered condolences at Changshou Palace.

entries.zh: 戊辰，客省使李嚴使蜀回。
entries.en: On wuchen Li Yan returned from Shu.
entries.literal: On wuchen Guest Reception commissioner Li Yan returned from an embassy to Shu.

entries.zh: 初，帝令往市蜀中珍玩，蜀法嚴峻，不許奇貨東出，其許市者謂之「入草物」。
entries.en: Cunxu had sent him to buy Shu luxuries; Shu law barred rare goods from the east, allowing only what it called "entering-grass goods."
entries.literal: Earlier the Emperor had ordered him to buy Shu curios; Shu law was severe and did not allow rare goods to leave eastward—what was permitted was called "entering-grass goods."

entries.zh: 嚴不獲珍貨，歸而奏之，帝大怒曰：「物歸中夏者命之曰『入草』，王衍寧免為入草之人耶！」
entries.en: Yan brought back no treasures and reported it; Cunxu thundered, "Goods that reach China are called 'entering grass'—is Wang Yan not a man who enters the grass!"
entries.literal: Yan obtained no curios; on returning he memorialized this, and the Emperor raged: "Goods that reach the Central Realm are called 'entering grass'—can Wang Yan escape being a man who enters the grass!"

entries.zh: 由是伐蜀之意銳矣。
entries.en: From that his will to conquer Shu sharpened.
entries.literal: Hence his intent to attack Shu grew keen.

entries.zh: 庚辰，幸壽安山陵作所。
entries.en: On gengchen he inspected the Shou'an tomb site.
entries.literal: On gengchen he visited the Shou'an mountain tomb works.

entries.zh: 鄴都大水，御河泛溢。
entries.en: Ye flooded and the Imperial Canal burst its banks.
entries.literal: Ye capital had great floods; the Imperial Canal overflowed.

entries.zh: 癸未，河南縣令羅貫長流崖州，尋委河南府決痛杖一頓，處死，坐部內橋道不修故也。
entries.en: On guiwei Luo Guan of Henan was sent to Yazhou, then Henan was told to flog him once and kill him for neglected bridges and roads.
entries.literal: On guiwei Henan county magistrate Luo Guan was exiled to Yazhou; soon Henan prefecture was ordered to beat him severely once and execute him—for failing to repair bridges and roads within his jurisdiction.

entries.zh: 及死，人皆冤之。
entries.en: At his death the people called it unjust.
entries.literal: When he died everyone deemed it unjust.

entries.zh: 甲申，山陵禮儀使奏：「山陵封城之內，先有丘墳，合令子孫改卜。
entries.en: On jiashen the tomb commissioner reported, "Within the tomb enclosure there are old mounds; their descendants should be ordered to rebury elsewhere.
entries.literal: On jiashen the mountain tomb rites commissioner memorialized: "Within the tomb enclosure there are old mounds; their descendants should be ordered to rebury elsewhere.

entries.zh: 舊例給其所費，無子孫者官為瘞藏。
entries.en: Precedent paid the cost; the state buried the heirless.
entries.literal: By old precedent they are given the expense; where there are no descendants the government buries and stores the remains.

entries.zh: 如是五品以上官，所司仍以禮致祭。」
entries.en: Fifth-rank officials and above still received state sacrifice."
entries.literal: If they were officials of the fifth rank or above, the relevant office still performed rites of sacrifice."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 鳳翔奏，大水。
entries.en: Fengxiang reported major floods.
entries.literal: Fengxiang reported great floods.

entries.zh: 己酉，中書門下上言：「據禮儀使狀，準故事，太常少卿定大行太后諡議，太常卿署定訖，告天地宗廟。
entries.en: On jiyou the Secretariat cited precedent: "According to the rites commissioner's report and established precedent, the Ceremonies vice director drafts the dowager's posthumous evaluation, the director signs it, then Heaven, Earth, and the temples are told.
entries.literal: On jiyou the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "According to the rites commissioner's report and established precedent, the Director of Ceremonies vice director drafts the late Empress Dowager's posthumous evaluation, the Director of Ceremonies signs and fixes it, and Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples are notified.

entries.zh: 伏準禮文：賤不得誄貴，子不得爵母，後必諡於廟者，受成於祖宗。
entries.en: Rites forbid the low to eulogize the high and a son to ennoble his mother; temple posthumous titles need ancestral completion.
entries.literal: We submit that ritual texts say: the low may not eulogize the high, a son may not ennoble his mother, and posthumous titles given in the temple receive completion from the ancestors.

entries.zh: 今大行太后諡，請太常卿署定後，集百官連署諡狀訖，讀於太廟太祖皇帝室，然後差丞郎一人撰冊文，別定日，命太尉上諡冊於西宮靈座，同日差官告天地、太微宮、宗廟，如常告之儀。」
entries.en: They asked that after Ceremonies signed the dowager's title, all officials countersign, read it in Taizu's temple chamber, draft the patent, have the Grand Marshal present it at the western spirit seat, and that day notify Heaven, Earth, Taiwei, and the temples as usual."
entries.literal: Now for the late Empress Dowager's posthumous title, after the Director of Ceremonies signs and fixes it, let all officials jointly sign the evaluation document, then read it in the Taizu Emperor's chamber of the Imperial Temple; afterward let one aide draft the patent text, fix another day, and order the Grand Marshal to present the posthumous patent at the western palace spirit seat; the same day let officers notify Heaven, Earth, the Taiwei Palace, and the ancestral temples by the usual notification rites."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 青州大水、蝗。
entries.en: Qing reported flood and locusts.
entries.literal: Qingzhou reported great floods and locusts.

entries.zh: 己丑，以襄州留後李紹珙為襄州節度使，以邠州留後董璋為邠州節度使。
entries.en: On jichou Li Shaogong of Xiang and Dong Zhang of Bin became their circuits' commissioners.
entries.literal: On jichou Xiangzhou acting regent Li Shaogong was made Xiangzhou military commissioner, and Binzhou acting regent Dong Zhang was made Binzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 冬十月庚申朔，宰臣及文武三品以上官赴長壽宮，上大行皇太后諡曰貞簡皇太后。
entries.en: On the gengshen new moon of the tenth month, ministers and officials of the third rank and above went to Changshou Palace and presented the late Empress Dowager's posthumous title as Empress Dowager Zhenjian.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, gengshen new moon: chief ministers and civil and military officials of the third rank and above went to Changshou Palace and presented the late Empress Dowager's posthumous title as Empress Dowager Zhenjian.

entries.zh: 辛酉，幸甘泉，遂幸壽安陵。
entries.en: On xinyou he visited Ganquan, then Shou'an tomb.
entries.literal: On xinyou he visited Ganquan, then visited Shou'an tomb.

entries.zh: 壬戌，魏王繼岌率師至鳳翔，先遣使馳檄以諭蜀部。
entries.en: On renxu Jiji reached Fengxiang and sent a swift proclamation to Shu.
entries.literal: On renxu Prince of Wei Jiji led the army to Fengxiang and first sent envoys with a flying proclamation to instruct the Shu command.

entries.zh: 丁卯，奉皇太后尊諡寶冊赴西京錄座，宰臣豆盧革攝太尉讀冊文，吏部尚書李琪讀寶文，百官素服，班於長壽宮門外奉慰。
entries.en: On dingmao the dowager's patent and treasure went to the western capital spirit seat; Dou Luge as acting Grand Marshal read the patent, Li Qi the treasure text, and officials in white lined outside Changshou Palace.
entries.literal: On dingmao the honored posthumous patent and treasure were sent to the western capital spirit seat; chief minister Dou Luge acted as Grand Marshal and read the patent; Minister of Personnel Li Qi read the treasure text; the hundred officials in plain robes formed ranks outside Changshou Palace gate to offer condolences.

entries.zh: 淮南楊溥遣使進慰禮。
entries.en: Yang Pu of Huainan sent condolence envoys.
entries.literal: Huainan's Yang Pu sent envoys with condolence gifts.

entries.zh: 己巳，中書上言：「貞簡太后陵請以坤陵為名。」
entries.en: On jisi the Secretariat asked to name the dowager's tomb Kunling.
entries.literal: On jisi the Secretariat memorialized: "We ask that Empress Dowager Zhenjian's tomb be named Kunling."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 初卜山陵，帝欲祔於代州武皇陵，奏議：「天子以四海為家，不當分其南北。」
entries.en: At first the Emperor wished to bury her beside the Martial Emperor's tomb at Daizhou; memorial debate said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home and should not divide north and south."
entries.literal: When the tomb site was first divined, the Emperor wished to bury her beside the Martial Emperor's tomb at Daizhou; memorial debate said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home and should not divide north and south."

entries.zh: 乃於壽安縣界別卜是陵。
entries.en: So a separate site was chosen on the Shou'an border.
entries.literal: Then at the Shou'an county border a separate site was divined for this tomb.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載中書門下奏議云：「人君以四海為家，不當分其南北。
entries.en: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 cites a Secretariat memorial: "The ruler's home is the four seas, not north against south.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 records a Secretariat and Chancellery memorial: "The ruler takes the four seas as home and should not divide north and south.

entries.zh: 洛陽是帝王之宅，四時朝拜，禮須便近，不能遠幸代州。
entries.en: Luoyang is the imperial seat; seasonal rites need nearness, not distant Daizhou.
entries.literal: Luoyang is the imperial dwelling; seasonal audiences require convenient proximity and cannot rely on distant travel to Daizhou.

entries.zh: 今漢朝諸陵，皆近秦雍，國朝陵寢，布列京畿。
entries.en: Han tombs cluster near Qin and Yong; Tang imperial tombs lie around the capital.
entries.literal: Now the Han dynasty's tombs all lie near Qin and Yong; our dynasty's imperial tombs are spread through the capital region.

entries.zh: 後魏文帝自代遷洛之後，園陵皆在河南，兼敕功臣之家，不許北葬，今魏氏諸陵尚在京畿。
entries.en: After Wei Wendi left Dai for Luo, tombs stayed in Henan and meritorious houses could not bury north; Wei tombs still stand near the capital.
entries.literal: After Northern Wei Wendi moved from Dai to Luo, park-tombs were all in Henan, and meritorious households were forbidden northern burial; Wei clan tombs still lie in the capital region.

entries.zh: 祔葬代州，理未為允。」
entries.en: Burial at Daizhou is not reasonable."
entries.literal: Burial beside Daizhou is not reasonable in principle."

entries.zh: 從之。）〉
entries.en: Approved.)〉
entries.literal: It was approved.)〉

entries.zh: 丙子，以前翰林學士、戶部侍郎馮道依前本官充職。
entries.en: On bingzi Feng Dao kept his former Hanlin and Revenue posts.
entries.literal: On bingzi former Hanlin academician and Minister of Revenue Feng Dao was confirmed in his former office and post.

entries.zh: 戊寅，西征之師入大散關，
entries.en: On wuyin the western campaign force entered Great Scatter Pass,
entries.literal: On wuyin, the western campaign army entered Great Scatter Pass,

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·趙廷隱傳》云：自入敵境，即禁兵士焚廬舍，剽財物，蜀人德之。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Zhao Tingyin》 says that on entering Shu they forbade burning homes or looting, and the people were grateful.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Zhao Tingyin Biography》 says: from entering enemy territory they forbade soldiers to burn houses or plunder goods, and the Shu people were grateful.)〉

entries.zh: 偽命鳳州節度使王承捷、故鎮屯駐指揮使唐景思次第迎降，得兵一萬二千、軍儲四十萬。
entries.en: Shu-appointed Fengzhou commissioner Wang Chengjie and former garrison commander Tang Jingsi surrendered in turn, yielding twelve thousand men and four hundred thousand in stores.
entries.literal: The Shu-appointed Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie and the former garrison commander Tang Jingsi in succession came to surrender; they gained twelve thousand troops and four hundred thousand in military stores.

entries.zh: 又下三泉，得軍儲三十餘萬。
entries.en: They also took Sanquan and gained over three hundred thousand in stores.
entries.literal: They also took Sanquan and gained more than three hundred thousand in military stores.

entries.zh: 自是師無匱乏，軍聲大振。
entries.en: From then the army wanted for nothing and its fame soared.
entries.literal: From then on the army lacked nothing and its renown greatly swelled.

entries.zh: 辛巳，偽興州刺史王承鑒、成州刺史王承樸棄城遁去，康延孝大破蜀軍於三泉。
entries.en: On xinsi the Shu Xingzhou prefect Wang Chengjian and Chengzhou prefect Wang Chengpu fled their cities, and Kang Yanxiao crushed the Shu army at Sanquan.
entries.literal: On xinsi, Shu Xingzhou prefect Wang Chengjian and Chengzhou prefect Wang Chengpu abandoned their cities and fled; Kang Yanxiao routed the Shu army at Sanquan.

entries.zh: 時王衍將幸秦州，以其軍五萬屯於利州。
entries.en: Wang Yan was then bound for Qinzhou with fifty thousand men at Lizhou.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Yan was about to visit Qinzhou and stationed his fifty-thousand-man army at Lizhou.

entries.zh: 聞我師至，遣步騎三萬逆戰於三泉，延孝與李嚴以勁騎三千擊之，蜀軍大敗，斬首五千級，餘眾奔潰。
entries.en: Hearing of our approach he sent thirty thousand foot and horse to Sanquan; Yanxiao and Li Yan with three thousand picked cavalry routed them, took five thousand heads, and drove the rest to flight.
entries.literal: Hearing our army had come, he sent thirty thousand foot and horse to meet battle at Sanquan; Yanxiao and Li Yan with three thousand crack cavalry struck them, the Shu army was greatly defeated, five thousand heads were taken, and the rest scattered in flight.

entries.zh: 王衍聞敗，自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津，浮梁而去。
entries.en: Wang Yan fled Lizhou for Chengdu, severed the Jibo crossing, and escaped on a pontoon bridge.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, hearing of defeat, fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, cut the Jibo Ford, and crossed on a pontoon bridge.

entries.zh: 丁亥，文武百官上表，以貞簡皇太后靈駕發引，請車駕不至山陵所。
entries.en: On dinghai the civil and military ranks asked that with Empress Dowager Zhenjian's spirit carriage setting out Cunxu not go to the tomb precinct.
entries.literal: On dinghai, civil and military officials jointly memorialized that with the spirit carriage of Empress Dowager Zhenjian setting out, they asked that the imperial carriage not go to the mausoleum precinct.

entries.zh: 戊子，葬貞簡太后於坤陵。
entries.en: On wuzi Empress Dowager Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.
entries.literal: On wuzi, Empress Dowager Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 己丑，魏王繼岌至興州，偽東川節度使宋光葆以梓、綿、劍、龍、普五州來降；
entries.en: On jichou Prince of Wei Jiji reached Xing; Shu Dongchuan commissioner Song Guangbao surrendered Zi, Mian, Jian, Long, and Pu;
entries.literal: On jichou, the Prince of Wei Jiji reached Xingzhou; Shu Dongchuan military commissioner Song Guangbao surrendered Zi, Mian, Jian, Long, and Pu prefectures;

entries.zh: 武定軍使王承肇以達、蓬、璧三州來降；
entries.en: Wuding commissioner Wang Chengzhao surrendered Da, Peng, and Bi;
entries.literal: Wuding army commissioner Wang Chengzhao surrendered Da, Peng, and Bi prefectures;

entries.zh: 興元節度使王宗威以梁、開、通、渠、麟五州來降；
entries.en: Xingyuan commissioner Wang Zongwei surrendered Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin;
entries.literal: Xingyuan military commissioner Wang Zongwei surrendered Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin prefectures;

entries.zh: 階州刺史王承嶽納符印請命；
entries.en: Jie prefect Wang Chengyue handed over his seal and asked for orders;
entries.literal: Jiezhou prefect Wang Chengyue submitted his tally and seal to request orders;

entries.zh: 秦州節度使王承休棄城自扶路奔於西川。
entries.en: Qin commissioner Wang Chengxu abandoned his city and fled by the Fulu road into Shu.
entries.literal: Qinzhou military commissioner Wang Chengxu abandoned the city and fled by the Fulu road into western Shu.

entries.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》引《王氏見聞記》云：王承休握銳兵於天水，兵刃不舉。
entries.en: (The 《Extensive Records》 cites the 《Wang Clan Seen and Heard》: Wang Chengxu held elite troops at Tianshui yet never fought.
entries.literal: (The 《Extensive Records》 cites the 《Wang Clan Seen and Heard》: Wang Chengxu held crack troops at Tianshui yet would not raise weapons.

entries.zh: 既知東軍入蜀，遂擁麾下之師及婦女孩幼萬餘口、金銀繒帛，於西蕃買路歸蜀。
entries.en: Learning the eastern army had entered Shu, he marched his command and more than ten thousand women and children with gold and silk to buy passage through the western tribes.
entries.literal: Once he knew the eastern army had entered Shu, he led his troops and more than ten thousand wives, children, girls, and young, with gold, silk, and brocade, and bought a road through the western tribes back to Shu.

entries.zh: 沿路為西蕃擄奪，凍餓相踐而死，迨至蜀，存者百餘人，唯與田宗汭等脫身而至。
entries.en: Tribes along the road plundered them; cold and hunger killed multitudes; barely a hundred reached Shu, and only he, Tian Zongrui, and a few others got through.
entries.literal: Along the way western tribes plundered them; freezing and hunger trampled one another to death; by the time they reached Shu barely more than a hundred survived, and only he with Tian Zongrui and a few others escaped through alive.

entries.zh: 魏王使人問之曰：「親握重兵，何得不戰？」
entries.en: The Prince of Wei's envoy asked, "You held a great army—why not fight?"
entries.literal: The Prince of Wei sent someone to ask him: "Holding heavy forces in your own hand, why did you not fight?"

entries.zh: 曰：「畏大王神武，不敢當其鋒。」
entries.en: He said, "I feared Your Highness's might and dared not meet your edge."
entries.literal: He said: "I feared the great prince's divine martial prowess and dared not meet his edge."

entries.zh: 曰：「何不早降？」
entries.en: The envoy asked, "Why not surrender sooner?"
entries.literal: They said: "Why not surrender early?"

entries.zh: 曰：「蓋緣王師不入封部，無門納款。」
entries.en: He said, "The royal army had not entered my circuit; I had no way to submit."
entries.literal: He said: "It was because the royal army had not entered my circuit; there was no gate to offer allegiance."

entries.zh: 曰：「初入蕃部幾許人？」
entries.en: The envoy asked, "How many entered the tribes at first?"
entries.literal: They said: "How many entered the foreign lands at first?"

entries.zh: 曰：「 萬餘口。」
entries.en: He said, "More than ten thousand mouths."
entries.literal: He said: "More than ten thousand mouths."

entries.zh: 「今存者幾何？」
entries.en: The envoy asked, "How many survive now?"
entries.literal: They said: "How many survive now?"

entries.zh: 曰：「才及百數。」
entries.en: He said, "Only about a hundred."
entries.literal: He said: "Only about a hundred."

entries.zh: 魏王曰：「汝可償萬人之命。」
entries.en: The Prince of Wei said, "You owe ten thousand lives."
entries.literal: The Prince of Wei said: "You can pay for ten thousand lives."

entries.zh: 遂斬之。）〉
entries.en: He was beheaded.)〉
entries.literal: Then he was beheaded.)〉

entries.zh: 十一月庚寅朔，帝幸壽安，號慟於坤陵。
entries.en: On the gengyin new moon of the eleventh month Cunxu visited Shou'an and wailed at Kun Mausoleum.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, gengyin new moon: the Emperor visited Shou'an and wailed at Kun Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以振武節度使朱守殷為兗州節度使。
entries.en: On wuxu Zhu Shouyin of Zhenwu became Yan commissioner.
entries.literal: On wuxu, Zhenwu military commissioner Zhu Shouyin was made Yanzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 徐州、鄴都上言，十月二十五日夜，地大震。
entries.en: Xu and Yedu reported a great earthquake on the night of the twenty-fifth of the tenth month.
entries.literal: Xuzhou and Yedu memorialized that on the night of the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month the earth greatly quaked.

entries.zh: 康延孝至利州，修吉柏津浮梁。
entries.en: Kang Yanxiao reached Lizhou and rebuilt the Jibo pontoon bridge.
entries.literal: Kang Yanxiao reached Lizhou and repaired the Jibo Ford pontoon bridge.

entries.zh: 偽昭武軍節度使林思諤來降。
entries.en: The Shu Zhaowu commissioner Lin Si'e surrendered.
entries.literal: The Shu Zhaowu army military commissioner Lin Si'e came to surrender.

entries.zh: 辛丑，魏王過利州，帝賜王衍詔，諭以禍福。
entries.en: On xinchou the Prince of Wei passed Lizhou; Cunxu sent Wang Yan an edict on fortune and ruin.
entries.literal: On xinchou, the Prince of Wei passed Lizhou; the Emperor bestowed an edict on Wang Yan, instructing him on fortune and calamity.

entries.zh: 甲辰，魏王至劍州，偽武信軍節度使王宗壽以遂、合、渝、瀘、忠五州來降。
entries.en: On jiachen the Prince of Wei reached Jian; the Shu Wuxin commissioner Wang Zongshou surrendered Sui, He, Yu, Lu, and Zhong.
entries.literal: On jiachen, the Prince of Wei reached Jianzhou; Shu Wuxin army military commissioner Wang Zongshou surrendered Sui, He, Yu, Lu, and Zhong prefectures.

entries.zh: 丁未，高麗國遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On dingwei Goryeo sent tribute envoys.
entries.literal: On dingwei, the Goryeo state sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 康延孝、李嚴至漢州，王衍遣人送牛酒請降，李嚴遂先入成都。
entries.en: Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan reached Han; Wang Yan sent oxen and wine to sue for surrender, and Li Yan entered Chengdu first.
entries.literal: Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan reached Hanzhou; Wang Yan sent men with oxen and wine to request surrender, and Li Yan thereupon first entered Chengdu.

entries.zh: 戊申，祔貞簡皇太后神主於太廟。
entries.en: On wushen Empress Dowager Zhenjian's tablet was placed in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: On wushen, Empress Dowager Zhenjian's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 己酉，魏王至綿州，王衍遣使上箋歸命。
entries.en: On jiyou the Prince of Wei reached Mian; Wang Yan sent envoys with a written submission of allegiance.
entries.literal: On jiyou, the Prince of Wei reached Mianzhou; Wang Yan sent envoys with a written submission to offer allegiance.

entries.zh: 庚戌，皇弟鄆州節度使存霸、滑州節度使存渥、左金吾大將軍晉州節度使存乂、邢州節度使存紀，並授起復雲麾將軍、右金吾大將軍同正。
entries.en: On gengxu the emperor's younger brothers Cunba, military governor of Yun Prefecture; Cunwo, military governor of Hua Prefecture; Cunyi, Left Golden Guard senior general and military governor of Jin Prefecture; and Cunji, military governor of Xing Prefecture, were all appointed, while recalled from mourning, as Cloud Banner generals and Right Golden Guard senior generals of the same rank.
entries.literal: On gengxu, the Emperor's younger brother Yunzhou military commissioner Cunba, Hua prefecture military commissioner Cunwo, Left Golden Wu Guard senior general and Jinzhou military commissioner Cunyi, and Xingzhou military commissioner Cunji were all appointed recalled-from-mourning Cloud Banner generals and Right Golden Wu Guard senior generals of the same rank.

entries.zh: 荊南節度使高季興奏，收復歸、夔、忠等州。
entries.en: Jingnan commissioner Gao Jixing reported recovering Gui, Kui, and Zhong.
entries.literal: Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jixing memorialized that he had recovered Gui, Kui, and Zhong prefectures.

entries.zh: 辛亥，魏王至德陽。
entries.en: On xinhai the Prince of Wei reached Deyang.
entries.literal: On xinhai, the Prince of Wei reached Deyang.

entries.zh: 偽六軍使王宗弼報，王衍舉家遷於西宅，宗弼權稱西川兵馬留後；
entries.en: The Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi reported that Wang Yan had moved his household to the western residence and Zongbi styled himself acting western Shu army retention commissioner;
entries.literal: The Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi reported that Wang Yan had moved his whole household to the western residence and Zongbi provisionally styled himself western Shu army-and-horse retention commissioner;

entries.zh: 又報偽樞密使宋光嗣景潤澄、宣徽使李周輅歐陽晃同有異謀，惑亂蜀主，已梟斬訖。
entries.en: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu and Ouyang Huang, alike had plotted, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.
entries.literal: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu and Ouyang Huang, alike harbored divergent plots, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王宗弼傳》：唐師陷鳳州，衍遣三招討屯三泉以拒唐師，未戰，三招討俱遁走，因令宗弼守綿穀而誅三招討，宗弼遂與三招討同送款於魏王。
entries.en: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Wang Zongbi》 says when Tang took Feng, Yan sent three campaign commanders to Sanquan; before battle all three fled; Yan ordered Zongbi to hold Mian Valley and killed the three commanders; Zongbi then with them submitted to the Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Wang Zongbi Biography》: when Tang troops took Fengzhou, Yan dispatched the three campaign commanders to camp at Sanquan to resist Tang; before battle all three campaign commanders fled; he then ordered Zongbi to hold Mian Valley and executed the three campaign commanders; Zongbi thereupon with the three campaign commanders together sent allegiance to the Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 乃還成都，斬宋光嗣等，函首送於魏王，遷衍及母妻於西宮。）〉
entries.en: He returned to Chengdu, killed Song Guangsi and the rest, sent their heads to the Prince of Wei, and moved Yan, his mother, and his wife to the western palace.)〉
entries.literal: He then returned to Chengdu, beheaded Song Guangsi and the rest, sent their heads in boxes to the Prince of Wei, and moved Yan and his mother and wife to the western palace.)〉

entries.zh: 壬子，王衍遣使上表請降。
entries.en: On renzi Wang Yan sent envoys with a surrender memorial.
entries.literal: On renzi, Wang Yan sent envoys with a memorial requesting surrender.

entries.zh: 癸丑，以吳越國馬步統軍使、檢校太傅錢元球為檢校太尉、守侍中，充靜海軍節度使。
entries.en: On guichou Qian Yuanqiu of Wuyue—horse-and-foot overall commander and acting Grand Tutor—became acting Grand Preceptor, palace attendant, and Jinghai commissioner.
entries.literal: On guichou, Wuyue state horse-and-foot overall commander and acting Grand Tutor Qian Yuanqiu was made acting Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant, and Jinghai army military commissioner.

entries.zh: 乙卯，魏王至西川城北。
entries.en: On yimao the Prince of Wei reached the north wall of the Shu capital.
entries.literal: On yimao, the Prince of Wei reached the north of western Shu's capital city.

entries.zh: 丙辰，蜀主王衍出降，語在衍傳。
entries.en: On bingchen Shu ruler Wang Yan surrendered—the account is in his biography.
entries.literal: On bingchen, Shu ruler Wang Yan came out to surrender—the account is in the Yan biography.

entries.zh: 同光三年秋七月丁酉，以久雨，詔河南府依法祈晴。
entries.en: On dingyou in autumn of Tongguang 3, prolonged rain led Cunxu to order Henan to pray for fair weather by statute.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingyou, Tongguang year 3: because of prolonged rain, an edict ordered Henan prefecture to pray for clear skies according to law.

entries.zh: 滑州上言，黃河決。
entries.en: Huazhou reported a Yellow River breach.
entries.literal: Huazhou reported that the Yellow River had burst its banks.

entries.zh: 壬寅，皇太后崩於長壽宮，帝執喪於內，出遺令以示於外。
entries.en: On renyin the Empress Dowager died at Changshou Palace; Cunxu mourned within and published her last testament without.
entries.literal: On renyin the Empress Dowager died at Changshou Palace; the Emperor observed mourning within and published her testament without.

entries.zh: 癸卯，帝於長壽宮成服，百官於長壽宮幕次成服後，於殿前立班奉慰。
entries.en: On guimao Cunxu donned mourning at Changshou Palace; officials robed in the tent, then lined up before the hall to console him.
entries.literal: On guimao the Emperor put on mourning robes at Changshou Palace; after the hundred officials had put on robes in the tent at Changshou Palace, they formed ranks before the hall to offer condolences.

entries.zh: 乙巳，宰臣上表請聽政，不允；
entries.en: On yisi the chief ministers asked Cunxu to resume court; he refused;
entries.literal: On yisi the chief ministers memorialized asking that he resume governance; it was not granted;

entries.zh: 表再上，敕旨宜廢朝七日。
entries.en: they petitioned again, and he ordered seven days without court.
entries.literal: the memorial came again, and an edict said court should be suspended seven days.

entries.zh: 丁未，宏文館上言：「請依《六典》，改宏文館為崇文館。」
entries.en: On dingwei the Hongwen Academy asked, per the 《Six Statutes》, to rename itself the Chongwen Academy."
entries.literal: On dingwei the Hongwen Academy memorialized: "We ask, following the 《Six Statutes》, to change the Hongwen Academy to the Chongwen Academy."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 時樞密使郭崇韜亡父名宏，豆盧革希崇韜指，奏而改之。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao's father's taboo name was Hong; Dou Luge flattered him and had the name changed.
entries.literal: At the time Privy Council commissioner Guo Chongtao's deceased father's name was Hong; Dou Luge curried Chongtao's favor and memorialized to change it.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載同光三年敕云：崇文館比與宏文館並置，今請改稱，頗協舊典。
entries.en: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 cites a Tongguang 3 edict: Chongwen and Hongwen had stood side by side, and the rename fit old precedent.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 records a Tongguang 3 edict: the Chongwen and Hongwen academies had been established together; the request to rename accorded quite well with old canon.

entries.zh: 蓋豆盧革曲為之說也。）〉
entries.en: Dou Luge had twisted the case.)〉
entries.literal: It was Dou Luge who twisted the explanation.)〉

entries.zh: 洛水泛漲，壞天津橋，以舟濟渡，日有覆溺者。
entries.en: The Luo flooded and wrecked Tianjin Bridge; ferries ran daily and people drowned.
entries.literal: The Luo River swelled and destroyed the Tianjin Bridge; people crossed by boat, and each day some capsized and drowned.

entries.zh: 己酉，宰臣百官上表，請聽政；
entries.en: On jiyou ministers and officials again asked him to hold court;
entries.literal: On jiyou the chief ministers and hundred officials memorialized asking that he resume governance;

entries.zh: 又請復常膳，表凡三上。
entries.en: and three times asked him to resume regular meals.
entries.literal: they also asked that regular meals be resumed—the memorial was submitted three times.

entries.zh: 以刑部尚書李琪充大行皇太后山陵禮儀使，河南尹張全義充山陵橋道排頓使，孔謙充監護使。
entries.en: Li Qi of Punishments led the dowager's tomb rites; Zhang Quanyi of Henan handled roads and supply; Kong Qian oversaw the work.
entries.literal: Minister of Punishments Li Qi was made chief commissioner for the late Empress Dowager's mountain tomb rites; Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi was made commissioner for tomb roads and supply; Kong Qian was made overseer commissioner.

entries.zh: 壬子，河陽、陝州上言，河溢岸。
entries.en: On renzi Heyang and Shan reported river overflows.
entries.literal: On renzi Heyang and Shanzhou reported that the river had overflowed its banks.

entries.zh: 以禮部尚書王正言為戶部尚書，以御史中丞崔協為禮部尚書，以刑部侍郎、史館修撰、判館事崔居儉為御史中丞，以尚書左丞歸靄為刑部侍郎。
entries.en: Wang Zhengyan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Revenue; Cui Xie, censor-in-chief, was made Minister of Rites; Cui Jujian, Vice Minister of Punishments, History Office compiler, and acting institute director, was made censor-in-chief; and Gui Ai, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Zhengyan was made Minister of Revenue; censor-in-chief Cui Xie was made Minister of Rites; Punishments vice minister, History Office compiler, and acting institute director Cui Jujian was made censor-in-chief; Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Gui Ai was made Punishments vice minister.

entries.zh: 陝州上言，河漲二丈二尺，壞浮橋，入城門，居人有溺死者。
entries.en: Shan said the river rose 2.2 zhang, broke the pontoon bridge, entered the gate, and drowned townspeople.
entries.literal: Shanzhou reported that the river had risen two zhang two chi, destroyed the pontoon bridge, entered the city gate, and commoners had drowned.

entries.zh: 乙卯，汴州上言，汴水泛漲，恐漂沒城池，於州城東西權開壕口，引水入古河。
entries.en: On yimao Bian reported the Bian in flood and briefly cut moat mouths east and west of the city to send water into the old channel.
entries.literal: On yimao Bianzhou reported that the Bian River had swollen and might wash away the city walls; east and west of the prefectural city they temporarily opened moat mouths to draw water into the old river.

entries.zh: 澤潞上言，自今月一日雨，至十九日未止。
entries.en: Ze-Lu said rain from the first had not ceased by the nineteenth.
entries.literal: Ze-Lu reported that from the first day of this month rain had fallen and had not stopped by the nineteenth.

entries.zh: 戊午，以刑部尚書、判太常卿兼判吏部尚書銓事李琪為吏部尚書，依前判太常卿；
entries.en: On wuwu Li Qi of Punishments became Personnel minister while keeping Ceremonies;
entries.literal: On wuwu Minister of Punishments and acting Director of Ceremonies with concurrent oversight of Personnel selection Li Qi was made Minister of Personnel, still acting Director of Ceremonies;

entries.zh: 以兵部侍郎、集賢殿學士、判院事盧文紀為吏部侍郎；
entries.en: Lu Wenji of War became Personnel vice minister;
entries.literal: Vice Minister of War, Hall of Assembled Worthies academician, and acting institute director Lu Wenji was made Personnel vice minister;

entries.zh: 以給事中李光序為尚書右丞。
entries.en: Li Guangxu became Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: Presentation Attendant Li Guangxu was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 許州、滑州奏，大水。
entries.en: Xu and Hua reported major floods.
entries.literal: Xuzhou and Huazhou memorialized great floods.

entries.zh: 同光四年春正月戊午朔，帝不受朝賀，契丹寇渤海。
entries.en: On the wuwu new moon in spring of Tongguang 4, Cunxu skipped New Year court; Khitan forces raided Bohai.
entries.literal: Spring, first month, wuwu new moon, Tongguang year 4: the Emperor did not accept court congratulations; the Khitan raided Bohai.

entries.zh: 壬戌，詔以去歲災沴，物價騰踴，自今月三日後避正殿，減膳撤樂，以答天譴。
entries.en: On renxu an edict blamed last year's disasters for soaring prices and ordered him to leave the main hall, cut meals, and stop music from the third of the month to appease heaven.
entries.literal: On renxu an edict said that because of last year's disasters and calamities prices had soared; from the third day of this month onward he would avoid the main hall, reduce meals, and withdraw music, to answer heaven's reproach.

entries.zh: 應去年遭水災州縣，秋夏稅賦並與放免。
entries.en: Autumn and summer taxes were waived for every county flooded last year.
entries.literal: For prefectures and counties that had suffered flood disaster last year, autumn and summer tax levies were all remitted.

entries.zh: 自壬午年已前所欠殘稅，及諸色課利，已有敕命放免者，尚聞所在卻有征收，宜令租庸司切準前敕處分。
entries.en: Tax arrears before renwu and levies already remitted by edict were still being collected locally; the Zuyong Office was told to enforce the earlier order.
entries.literal: Arrears of residual tax owed before the renwu year, and various kinds of levies and profits, though already remitted by edict, were still heard to be collected in places; the Zuyong Office was ordered strictly to handle matters according to the prior edict.

entries.zh: 應京畿內人戶，有停貯斛斗者，並令減價出糶；
entries.en: Capital households hoarding grain were ordered to sell at reduced prices;
entries.literal: For households within the capital region who were hoarding grain in store, all were ordered to sell at reduced price;

entries.zh: 如不遵行，當令檢括。
entries.en: refusal would bring investigation and seizure.
entries.literal: if they did not comply, investigation and seizure were to be ordered.

entries.zh: 西川王衍父子及偽署將相官吏，除已行刑憲外，一切釋放。
entries.en: Wang Yan of Shu, his son, and Shu's puppet ministers and officials were freed except those already executed.
entries.literal: Wang Yan of Shu, father and son, and the falsely appointed generals, ministers, and officials, except those already punished under criminal law, were all released.

entries.zh: 天下禁囚，除十惡五逆、官典犯贓、屠牛毀錢、放火劫舍、持刀殺人，準律常赦不原外，應合抵極刑者，遞降一等。
entries.en: Prisoners nationwide except capital crimes, corruption, cattle-slaughter, coin-breaking, arson, robbery, and blade murder had death sentences cut one grade where statute allowed.
entries.literal: Among prisoners under ban throughout the realm, aside from the ten abominations, five capital crimes, official corruption, slaughtering cattle and destroying coin, arson and robbery, and murder with a blade—cases not normally pardoned by statute—those who should have received the extreme penalty had it reduced one grade.

entries.zh: 其餘罪犯悉與減降；
entries.en: all other offenders received further reductions;
entries.literal: all other criminals were likewise reduced and lowered;

entries.zh: 逃背軍健，並放逐便。
entries.en: deserters were banished outright.
entries.literal: deserter soldiers were all banished as convenient.

entries.zh: 癸亥，河中節度使李繼麟來朝。
entries.en: On guihai Li Jilin, military governor of Hezhong, presented himself at court.
entries.literal: On guihai Hezhong military commissioner Li Jilin came to court.

entries.zh: 諸州上言，準宣為去年十月地震，集僧道起消災道場。
entries.en: Prefectures reported ritual grounds for last October's earthquake, per edict.
entries.literal: The various prefectures reported that, according to an edict for the earthquake of last year's tenth month, monks and Daoists were gathered to establish disaster-averting ritual grounds.

entries.zh: 甲子，魏王繼岌殺樞密使郭崇韜於西川，夷其族。
entries.en: On jiazi Jiji killed Guo Chongtao in Shu and wiped out his family.
entries.literal: On jiazi Prince of Wei Jiji killed Privy Council commissioner Guo Chongtao in Shu and exterminated his clan.

entries.zh: 丙寅，百官上表，請復常膳，凡三上表，乃允之。
entries.en: On bingyin officials petitioned three times before Cunxu resumed regular meals.
entries.literal: On bingyin the hundred officials memorialized asking that regular meals be resumed; they memorialized three times before it was granted.

entries.zh: 西川行營都監李廷安進西川樂官二百九十八人。
entries.en: Li Ting'an of the Shu campaign staff sent 298 Shu musicians to court.
entries.literal: Li Ting'an, overall monitor of the Shu campaign force, presented two hundred ninety-eight Shu music officers.

entries.zh: 契丹寇女真、渤海。
entries.en: Khitan forces raided Jurchen and Bohai.
entries.literal: The Khitan raided Jurchen and Bohai.

entries.zh: 戊寅，契丹阿保機遣使貢良馬。
entries.en: On wuyin Abaoji sent fine horses as tribute.
entries.literal: On wuyin the Khitan Abaoji sent envoys presenting fine horses.

entries.zh: 庚辰，帝異母弟鄜州節度使存乂伏誅。
entries.en: On gengchen Cunxu's half-brother Cunyi, commissioner of Fuzhou, was beheaded.
entries.literal: On gengchen the Emperor's younger half-brother, Fuzhou military commissioner Cunyi, was executed by beheading.

entries.zh: 存乂，郭崇韜之子婿也，故亦及於禍。
entries.en: Cunyi had married Guo Chongtao's daughter, so he fell with the Guo clan.
entries.literal: Cunyi was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law; hence he too met disaster.

entries.zh: 是日，以河中節度使、守太師、兼尚書令、西平王李繼麟為滑州節度使，尋令朱守殷以兵圍其第，誅之，夷其族。
entries.en: That day Li Jilin, military governor of Hezhong, acting Grand Mentor, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Xiping, was made military governor of Hua Prefecture. Soon Zhu Shouyin was ordered to surround his residence with troops, execute him, and exterminate his clan.
entries.literal: That day Hezhong military commissioner, Guardian Grand Mentor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Xiping Li Jilin was made Huazhou military commissioner; soon Zhu Shouyin was ordered to surround his residence with troops, execute him, and exterminate his clan.

entries.zh: 辛巳，吐渾、奚各遣使貢馬。
entries.en: On xinsi Tuyuhun and Xi envoys brought horses.
entries.literal: On xinsi the Tuyuhun and Xi each sent envoys presenting horses.

entries.zh: 鎮州上言，部民凍死者七千二百六十人。
entries.en: Zhen reported 7,260 freeze deaths among its people.
entries.literal: Zhenzhou reported that among its people seven thousand two hundred sixty had frozen to death.

entries.zh: 又奏，準宣進花果樹栽及抽樂人梅審譯赴京。
entries.en: It also sent fruit trees and the musician Mei Shenyi to the capital, per edict.
entries.literal: It also memorialized that, according to edict, fruit-flower trees were to be presented and the musician Mei Shenyi escorted to the capital.

entries.zh: 甲申，以鄆州節度使、永王存霸為河中節度使，以滑州節度使、申王存渥為鄆州節度使。
entries.en: On jiashen Cunba of Yan became Hezhong commissioner and Cunwo of Hua became Yan commissioner.
entries.literal: On jiashen Yanzhou military commissioner and Prince of Yong Cunba was made Hezhong military commissioner; Huazhou military commissioner and Prince of Shen Cunwo was made Yanzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 乙酉，內人景姹上言：「昭宗遇難之時，皇屬千餘人同時遇害，為三穴瘞於宮城西古龍興寺北，請改葬。」
entries.en: On yiyou, the palace woman Jing Cha submitted a report: "When Emperor Zhaozong met his end, more than a thousand members of the imperial clan were killed at the same time and buried in three pits north of the old Longxing Temple, west of the palace city. I request that they be reburied."
entries.literal: On yiyou palace woman Jing Cha reported: "When Zhaozong met disaster, more than a thousand imperial kin were killed at once and buried in three pits north of the old Longxing Temple west of the palace city; we ask that they be reburied."

entries.zh: 從之，仍詔河南府監護其事。
entries.en: Approved, with Henan ordered to oversee the reburial.
entries.literal: It was approved, and Henan prefecture was still ordered to oversee the matter.

entries.zh: 丙戌，回鶻可汗阿咄欲遣使貢良馬。
entries.en: On bingxu the Uyghur qaghan Aduoyu sent envoys to present fine horses.
entries.literal: On bingxu the Uyghur qaghan Aduoyu sent envoys presenting fine horses.

entries.zh: 鎮州上言，平棘等四縣部民，餓死者二千五十人。
entries.en: Zhen said 2,050 had starved in Pingji and four neighboring counties.
entries.literal: Zhenzhou reported that among the people of Pingji and four other counties two thousand fifty had starved to death.

entries.zh: 丁亥，詔朱友謙同惡人史武等七人，已當國法，並籍沒家產。
entries.en: On dinghai an edict confiscated the estates of Zhu Youqian's seven accomplices, including Shi Wu, already executed.
entries.literal: On dinghai an edict said Zhu Youqian's fellow evildoers Shi Wu and six others had already met state law and all family property was to be confiscated.

entries.zh: 武等友謙舊將，時皆為刺史，並以無罪族誅。
entries.en: Wu and the others had been Youqian's generals and serving prefects, yet were killed with their clans though innocent.
entries.literal: Wu and the rest were Youqian's old generals; at the time all were prefects, yet all were clan-executed though guiltless.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》，丁亥，殺李繼麟之將史武、薛敬容、周唐殷、楊師太、王景、來仁、白奉國。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Ouyang History》 dates dinghai: Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo, Li Jilin's generals, were executed.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Ouyang History》 records dinghai: Li Jilin's generals—Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo—were executed.)〉

entries.zh: 庚戌，諸軍大集於鄴都，進攻其城，不克。
entries.en: On gengxu the armies massed at Ye and assaulted the city without success.
entries.literal: On gengxu all armies greatly massed at Ye and advanced to attack the city but could not take it.

entries.zh: 行欽又大治攻具。
entries.en: Yuan Xingqin again prepared siege engines in earnest.
entries.literal: Xingqin again greatly prepared siege engines.

entries.zh: 城中知其無赦，晝夜為備。
entries.en: Knowing there would be no pardon, the city prepared day and night.
entries.literal: Within the city, knowing there would be no pardon, day and night they made ready.

entries.zh: 朝廷聞之益恐，連發中使促繼岌西征之師。
entries.en: The court grew more afraid and sent envoys in succession to hurry Jiji's western army.
entries.literal: The court, hearing of it, grew ever more afraid and in succession sent palace envoys to urge Jiji's western campaign army.

entries.zh: 繼岌以康延孝據漢州，中軍之士從任圜進討，繼岌端居利州，不獲東歸。
entries.en: With Kang Yanxiao holding Hanzhou, Jiji sent the central army under Ren Huan while he stayed at Lizhou and could not return east.
entries.literal: Jiji, because Kang Yanxiao held Hanzhou, had the central army follow Ren Yuan to attack; Jiji sat at Lizhou and could not return east.

entries.zh: 是日，飛龍使顏思威部署西川宮人至。
entries.en: That day Yan Siwei of the Flying Dragon Office brought the Shu palace women in.
entries.literal: That day Flying Dragon commissioner Yan Siwei deployed the western Shu palace women to arrive.

entries.zh: 辛亥，淮南楊溥遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On xinhai Yang Pu of Huainan sent tribute envoys.
entries.literal: On xinhai Huainan's Yang Pu sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 西京上言，客省使李嚴押蜀主王衍至本府。
entries.en: The western capital reported that Li Yan of Guest Reception had brought Shu ruler Wang Yan there.
entries.literal: The western capital reported that Guest Reception commissioner Li Yan had escorted Shu ruler Wang Yan to that prefecture.

entries.zh: 壬子，以守太尉、中書令、河南尹兼河陽節度使、齊王張全義為檢校太師、兼尚書令，充許州節度使。
entries.en: On renzi Zhang Quanyi—acting Grand Preceptor, Secretariat director, Henan prefect, and Heyang commissioner—became Grand Preceptor and Secretariat director and took Xu as military commissioner.
entries.literal: On renzi Acting Grand Preceptor, Secretariat director, Henan prefect, and concurrent Heyang military commissioner Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi was made Grand Preceptor, concurrent Secretariat director, and charged as Xu military commissioner.

entries.zh: 東川董璋奏，準詔誅遂州節度使李令德於本州，夷其族。
entries.en: Dong Zhang of Dongchuan reported executing Suizhou commissioner Li Lingde there by edict and wiping out his clan.
entries.literal: Dongchuan's Dong Zhang memorialized that per edict he had executed Suizhou military commissioner Li Lingde in that prefecture and exterminated his clan.

entries.zh: 癸丑，湖南馬殷奏，福建節度使王審知疾甚，副使王延翰已權知軍府事，請降旄節。
entries.en: On guichou Ma Yin of Hunan reported Wang Shenzhi of Fujian gravely ill, Yanhan already running the prefecture, and asked for the commission.
entries.literal: On guichou Hunan's Ma Yin memorialized that Fujian military commissioner Wang Shenzhi was gravely ill, deputy Wang Yanhan already held military affairs in the prefecture, and asked that banners and tally be granted.

entries.zh: 司天監上言：自二月上旬後，晝夜陰雲，不見天象，自二十六日方晴，至月終，星辰無變。
entries.en: Astronomy reported overcast skies from early second month until clearing on the twenty-sixth, with no change in the stars through month's end.
entries.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy reported: from early in the second month day and night were overcast and the sky could not be seen; only on the twenty-sixth did it clear; to month's end the stars showed no change.

entries.zh: 以右衛上將軍朱漢賓知河南府事。
entries.en: Zhu Hanbin of the Right Weijun was made acting Henan prefect.
entries.literal: Right Weijun upper general Zhu Hanbin was made acting Henan prefect.

entries.zh: 丙辰，荊南高季興上言，請割峽內夔、忠、萬等三州卻歸當道，依舊管係，又請雲安監。
entries.en: On bingchen Gao Jixing of Jingnan asked to return Kui, Zhong, and Wan in the Gorges to his circuit and also sought the Yun'an salt office.
entries.literal: On bingchen Jingnan's Gao Jixing memorialized, asking to cut off and return the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan within the Gorges to his circuit under former jurisdiction, and also asked for the Yun'an salt office.

entries.zh: 初，將議伐蜀，詔高季興令率本軍上峽，自收元管屬郡。
entries.en: When the Shu campaign was first planned, Gao Jixing was ordered to lead his army up the Gorges and recover his old prefectures.
entries.literal: At first, when they were about to discuss attacking Shu, an edict had ordered Gao Jixing to lead his native army up the Gorges and himself recover the prefectures of his former jurisdiction.

entries.zh: 軍未進，夔、忠、萬三州已降，季興數請之，因賂劉皇后及宰臣樞密使，內外葉附，乃俞其請。
entries.en: Before his army moved, Kui, Zhong, and Wan had surrendered; Jixing kept asking, bribed Empress Liu and the chancellors and Privy Council, and won approval inside and out.
entries.literal: The army had not advanced when Kui, Zhong, and Wan had already surrendered; Jixing repeatedly asked for them and therefore bribed Empress Liu and the chief ministers and Privy Council commissioners; inner and outer were of one mind, and his request was granted.

entries.zh: 戊午，詔河南府預借今年秋夏租稅。
entries.en: On wuwu Henan was ordered to advance this year's autumn and summer taxes.
entries.literal: On wuwu an edict ordered Henan prefecture to advance this year's autumn and summer taxes.

entries.zh: 時年饑民困，百姓不勝其酷，京畿之民，多號泣於路，議者以為劉盆子復生矣。
entries.en: Famine pressed the people beyond bearing; capital folk wailed on the roads; some said Liu Penzi had come again.
entries.literal: At the time famine pressed the people; the common folk could not bear the harshness; people of the capital region many wept and wailed on the roads; commentators held that Liu Penzi had been reborn.

entries.zh: 庚申，詔潞州節度使孔赴闕，以右龍虎統軍安崇阮權知潞州。
entries.en: On gengshen Kong Qing of Luzhou was summoned to court; An Chongruan of the Right Dragon-Tiger was made acting Luzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: On gengshen an edict ordered Luzhou military commissioner Kong Qing to come to court; Right Dragon-Tiger overall commander An Chongruan was made acting Luzhou commissioner.

entries.zh: 是日，忠武軍節度使、齊王張全義薨。
entries.en: That day Zhang Quanyi, Zhongwu commissioner and Prince of Qi, died.
entries.literal: That day Zhongwu military commissioner Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi died.

entries.zh: 壬戌，宰臣豆盧革率百官上表，以魏博軍變，請出內府金帛優給將士。
entries.en: On renxu Dou Luge led the officials in asking, because of the Weibo mutiny, to take inner-treasury gold and silk for the troops.
entries.literal: On renxu chief minister Dou Luge led the hundred officials in a memorial because of the Weibo army's mutiny, asking to take gold and silk from the inner treasury to generously supply the soldiers.

entries.zh: 不報。
entries.en: There was no reply.
entries.literal: There was no reply.

entries.zh: 時知星者上言：「客星犯天庫，宜散府藏。」
entries.en: Astrologers said, "The guest star violates the Heavenly Storehouse—the treasury should be opened."
entries.literal: At the time those who knew the stars reported, "The guest star violates the Heavenly Storehouse—one should disperse the treasury."

entries.zh: 又云：「流星犯天棓，主御前有急兵。」
entries.en: They also said, "A meteor violates the Heavenly Club—urgent troops before the throne."
entries.literal: They also said, "A meteor violates the Heavenly Club—there will be urgent troops before the throne."

entries.zh: 帝召宰臣於便殿，皇后出宮中妝奩銀盆各二，並皇子滿哥三人，謂宰臣曰：「外人謂內府金寶無數，向者諸侯貢獻旋供賜與，今宮中有者，妝奩、嬰孺而已，可鬻之給軍。」
entries.en: Cunxu called the chancellors to the informal hall; the empress brought out from the palace two dressing cases and two silver basins, together with three imperial sons, including Mange, and said to the ministers, "Outsiders say the inner treasury is endless; tribute went out as fast as it came—now we have only dressing cases and infants—sell them for the army."
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned the chief ministers to the informal hall; the empress brought out from the palace two dressing cases and two silver basins, together with three imperial sons, including Mange, and said to the chief ministers, "Outsiders say the inner treasury has countless gold and treasure; when the feudal lords presented tribute it was at once given away in grants—what the palace now has is only dressing cases and infants—sell them to supply the army."

entries.zh: 革等惶恐而退。
entries.en: Dou Luge and the rest withdrew in fear.
entries.literal: Dou Luge and the rest withdrew in fear.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以偽置昭武軍節度使林思諤為閬州刺史。
entries.en: On guihai false Zhaowu commissioner Lin Si'e was made Lang prefect.
entries.literal: On guihai the false-appointed Zhaowu military commissioner Lin Si'e was made Langzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 是日，出錢帛給賜諸軍，兩樞密使及宋唐玉、景進等各貢助軍錢幣。
entries.en: That day money and silk were issued to the armies; the Privy Council commissioners, Song Tangyu, Jing Jin, and the rest each gave aid money.
entries.literal: That day money and silk were issued to bestow on the armies; the two Privy Council commissioners and Song Tangyu, Jing Jin, and the rest each presented money to aid the army.

entries.zh: 是時，軍士之家乏食，婦女掇蔬於野，及優給軍人，皆負物而詬曰：「吾妻子已殍矣，用此奚為！」
entries.en: Soldiers' families starved while women gleaned in the wild; when bounty reached the troops they shouldered goods and cursed, "Our wives and children are dead—what is this for!"
entries.literal: At the time soldiers' households lacked food; women gathered vegetables in the wild; when the soldiers were generously supplied they all shouldered goods and cursed, saying, "Our wives and children have already starved—what use is this!"

entries.zh: 甲子，元行欽自衛州率部下兵士歸，帝幸耀店以勞之。
entries.en: On jiazi Yuan Xingqin returned from Weizhou with his men; Cunxu went to Yaodian to comfort them.
entries.literal: On jiazi Yuan Xingqin came from Weizhou leading his subordinate soldiers in return; the Emperor went to Yaodian to comfort them.

entries.zh: 西川輦運金銀四十萬至闕，分給將士有差。
entries.en: Four hundred thousand in western Shu gold and silver reached court and was parceled to the troops by rank.
entries.literal: The western Shu transport of four hundred thousand in gold and silver reached the court and was distributed to the soldiers in graded shares.

entries.zh: 元行欽請車駕幸汴州，帝將發京師，遣中官向延嗣馳詔所在誅蜀主王衍，仍夷其族。
entries.en: Yuan Xingqin asked Cunxu to go to Bian; as he was about to leave the capital he sent Xiang Yansi with a flying edict to execute Wang Yan and exterminate his clan.
entries.literal: Yuan Xingqin asked that the imperial carriage go to Bianzhou; the Emperor was about to set out from the capital and sent a palace official, Xiang Yansi, with a flying edict to the place to execute Shu ruler Wang Yan and still exterminate his clan.

entries.zh: 乙亥，翰林學士、戶部侍郎、知制誥馮道，翰林學士、中書舍人趙鳳，俱以本官充端明殿學士。
entries.en: On yihai Feng Dao and Zhao Feng, Hanlin academicians, became Duanming Hall academicians at rank.
entries.literal: On yihai, Hanlin academician, Revenue vice minister, and edict drafter Feng Dao and Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafting officer Zhao Feng were both made Duanming Hall academicians at their present ranks.

entries.zh: 端明之職，自此始也。
entries.en: The Duanming post began here.
entries.literal: The post of Duanming began from this.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：明宗初登位，四方書奏，多令樞密使安重誨讀之，不曉文義。
entries.en: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 says when Mingzong first reigned, An Chonghui read most frontier memorials but lacked literary training.
entries.literal: (The 《Institutions of the Five Dynasties》 records: when Mingzong first took the throne, memorials from the four directions were mostly read by Privy Council commissioner An Chonghui, who did not understand literary meaning.

entries.zh: 於是孔循獻議，因唐室侍讀之號，即創端明學士之名，命馮道等為之。）〉
entries.en: Kong Xun then proposed reviving Tang's lecture-reader title as Duanming academician and named Feng Dao and others.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon Kong Xun offered a plan: following Tang's lecture-reader title, they created the name Duanming academician and appointed Feng Dao and others.)〉

entries.zh: 丙子，詔：「故西道行營都招討製置等使、守侍中、監修國史、兼樞密使郭崇韜宜許歸葬，其世業田宅並還與骨肉。
entries.en: On bingzi an edict said: "Guo Chongtao, late western-campaign commander and palace attendant, might be buried and his estates returned to his family.
entries.literal: On bingzi an edict said: "The late Western Circuit campaign overall pacification and disposition commissioner, Palace Attendant, historiographer, and concurrent Privy Council commissioner Guo Chongtao should be permitted burial; his hereditary estates and dwellings should all be returned to his kin.

entries.zh: 故萬州司戶朱友謙可復護國軍節度使、守太師、兼尚書令、河中尹、西平王，所有田宅財產，並還與骨肉。」
entries.en: Zhu Youqian, late Wan registrar, was restored as Huguo commissioner, grand preceptor, Heyang prefect, and Prince of Xiping, with estates returned to his kin."
entries.literal: The late Wanzhou registrar Zhu Youqian may be restored as Huguo military commissioner, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Heyang prefect, and Prince of Xiping; all estates and property should be returned to his kin."

entries.zh: 丁丑，西都衙內指揮使張篯進納偽蜀主王衍犀玉帶各二條、馬一百五十匹。
entries.en: On dingchou Zhang Qian, Western Capital inner commandant, presented two rhinoceros-and-jade belts and one hundred fifty horses from the false Shu ruler Wang Yan.
entries.literal: On dingchou, Western Capital inner commandant Zhang Qian presented two rhinoceros and jade belts each and one hundred fifty horses of the false Shu ruler Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 初，莊宗遣中官向延嗣就長安之殺王衍也，旋屬蕭牆之禍，延嗣藏竄，不知所之，而衍之資裝妓樂並為篯所有，復懼事泄，故聊有此獻。
entries.en: Zhuangzong had sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to Chang'an to kill Wang Yan; after the palace coup Yansi vanished and Yan's goods and entertainers passed to Zhang Qian, who now offered a slice of the hoard for fear of exposure.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhuangzong had sent the inner eunuch Xiang Yansi to Chang'an to kill Wang Yan; soon the palace turmoil followed, Yansi hid and his whereabouts were unknown, while Yan's goods, equipage, and entertainers all fell to Qian's possession; fearing exposure, he therefore made this brief presentation.

entries.zh: 六月戊子，前襄州節度使李紹珙起復，依前襄州節度使，仍復本姓名曰劉訓。
entries.en: On wuzi in the sixth month Li Shaogong was recalled to Xiangzhou and restored as Liu Xun.
entries.literal: Sixth month, wuzi: former Xiangzhou military commissioner Li Shaogong was recalled to service and continued as Xiangzhou military commissioner, his name also restored as Liu Xun.

entries.zh: 以皇子河中留後從珂為河中節度使，百僚表賀。
entries.en: Li Congke, Hezhong acting commissioner, became Hezhong commissioner; the court congratulated him.
entries.literal: The Prince's Hedong acting military commissioner Congke was made Hedong military commissioner; the hundred officials memorialized congratulations.

entries.zh: 以翰林承旨、兵部尚書、知制誥盧質為檢校司空，充同州節度使。
entries.en: Lu Zhi, Hanlin edict-drafter and War minister, became acting Minister of Works and Tong commissioner.
entries.literal: Hanlin edict-drafter, Minister of War, and edict drafter Lu Zhi was made acting Grand Preceptor and Tongzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 己丑，以使部尚書、判太常卿事李琪為御史大夫；
entries.en: On jichou Li Qi, envoy minister and acting Ceremonies director, became censor-in-chief;
entries.literal: On jichou, Envoy Minister and acting Director of Ceremonies Li Qi was made Censor-in-Chief;

entries.zh: 以禮部尚書崔協為太常卿、判吏部尚書銓事；
entries.en: Cui Xie of Rites became Ceremonies director and acting Personnel director;
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Cui Xie was made Director of Ceremonies and acting Director of Personnel selection;

entries.zh: 以御史中丞崔居儉為兵部侍郎；
entries.en: Cui Jujian became War vice minister;
entries.literal: censor-in-chief Cui Jujian was made Vice Minister of War;

entries.zh: 以太子賓客蕭頃為禮部尚書。
entries.en: Xiao Qing, crown prince mentor, became Rites minister.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Mentor Xiao Qing was made Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 中書奏：「請以九月九日皇帝降誕日為應聖節，休假三日。」
entries.en: The Secretariat asked that the ninth of the ninth, Mingzong's birthday, become the Yingsheng Festival with three days off."
entries.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "We ask that the ninth day of the ninth month, the Emperor's birthday, be made the Yingsheng Festival with three days' leave."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 故忠武軍節度使、檢校太師、兼尚書令、齊王張全義贈太師，以前尚書右丞崔沂為尚書左丞。
entries.en: Zhang Quanyi, late Zhongwu commissioner and Prince of Qi, was posthumously made grand preceptor; Cui Yi became left assistant minister.
entries.literal: The late Zhongwu military commissioner, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; former Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Cui Yi was made Left Assistant Minister.

entries.zh: 丙申，新州留後張庭裕、雲州留後高行珪並正授本軍節度使。
entries.en: On bingshen Zhang Tingyu of Xin and Gao Xinggui of Yun received full commissionerships.
entries.literal: On bingshen, Xinzhou acting military commissioner Zhang Tingyu and Yunzhou acting military commissioner Gao Xinggui were both fully appointed military commissioners of their armies.

entries.zh: 丁酉，詔曰：「四夷來王，歷代故事，前後各因強弱，撫製互有典儀。
entries.en: On dingyou an edict said: "Foreign rulers had always come to court, and each age had its rites scaled to their power.
entries.literal: On dingyou an edict said: "The four barbarians come to court—an institution of every age; before and after, each according to strength and weakness, the handling and control had their canonical rites.

entries.zh: 大蕃須示於威容，即於正衙引對；
entries.en: Great powers deserved full ceremony in the main hall;
entries.literal: Great barbarians required display of majesty and were led to audience in the main hall;

entries.zh: 小蕃但推於恩澤，仍於便殿撫懷。
entries.en: lesser ones received grace in the side hall.
entries.literal: small barbarians were only to be treated with grace and still received in the convenient hall with reassurance.

entries.zh: 憲府奏論，禮院詳酌，皆征故實，咸有明文。
entries.en: The Censorate and Rites Office had reviewed precedent and found clear rules for both.
entries.literal: The Censorate memorialized and the Rites Office examined in detail; all drew on precedent and all had clear text.

entries.zh: 正衙威容，未可全廢；
entries.en: Main-hall ceremony could not be dropped entirely;
entries.literal: Main-hall majesty could not be wholly abolished;

entries.zh: 內殿恩澤，且可常行。
entries.en: side-hall reception should remain routine.
entries.literal: inner-hall grace might still be carried out regularly.

entries.zh: 若遇大蕃入朝，即準舊儀，於正殿排比鋪陳立仗，百官排班，於正門引入對見。」
entries.en: Great embassies would follow the old rites: guards and officials in formation at the main gate and audience in the main hall."
entries.literal: When great barbarians came to court, follow the old rites: in the main hall arrange ranks and standing guards, the hundred officials in formation, and at the main gate introduce them for audience."

entries.zh: 時百僚入閣班退後，卻引對朝貢蕃客，御史大夫李琪奏論之，下禮院檢討，而降是命焉。
entries.en: Li Qi had protested that after hall audience the court still received tributary envoys in the side hall; Rites reviewed the case and Mingzong issued this order.
entries.literal: At the time, after the hundred officials' hall ranks had withdrawn, tributary foreign guests were still introduced for audience; Censor-in-Chief Li Qi memorialized on it; it was sent to the Rites Office for review, and this decree was then issued.

entries.zh: 天成元年夏四月丙午，帝自興聖宮赴西宮，文武百僚縞素於位，帝服斬衰，親奉攢，塗設奠，哭盡哀，乃於柩前即皇帝位。
entries.en: On bingwu in the fourth month of Tiancheng 1, Mingzong left Xingsheng Palace for the Western Palace; officials in white stood at their posts while he wore deepest mourning, bore the bier, set offerings, wept his fill, and took the throne before the coffin.
entries.literal: In summer, fourth month, bingwu of Tiancheng 1, the Emperor went from Xingsheng Palace to the Western Palace; civil and military officials in white stood at their posts; the Emperor wore the deepest mourning, personally bore the coffin bier, applied plaster and set offerings, wept to the utmost, and then before the bier assumed the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 百官易吉服班於位，帝御袞冕受冊訖，百僚稱賀。
entries.en: Officials changed to court dress and lined up; Mingzong in imperial robes received the investiture scroll, and the court congratulated him.
entries.literal: The hundred officials changed to auspicious dress and took ranks at their posts; the Emperor in imperial robes and cap received the investiture scroll; the hundred officials offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 丁未，群官縞素赴西宮臨。
entries.en: On dingwei officials in white went to the Western Palace to view the bier.
entries.literal: On dingwei, the mass of officials in white went to the Western Palace for viewing.

entries.zh: 以樞密使安重誨為檢校司空，守左領軍大將軍，依前充樞密使。
entries.en: An Chonghui, Privy Council commissioner, was made acting Minister of Works and Left Leading Infantry General while keeping the Privy Council post.
entries.literal: Privy Council commissioner An Chonghui was made acting Minister of Works, held as Left Leading Infantry General, and continued as before as Privy Council commissioner.

entries.zh: 宰臣豆盧革等三上表請聽政，從之。
entries.en: Dou Luge and the chief ministers three times asked Mingzong to hold court; he agreed.
entries.literal: Chief ministers Dou Luge and others three times memorialized asking that he hold court; it was approved.

entries.zh: 遣使往諸道及淮南告哀。
entries.en: Envoys announced Zhuangzong's death to the circuits and Huainan.
entries.literal: Envoys were sent to the circuits and Huainan to announce mourning.

entries.zh: 辛亥，帝始聽政於中興殿。
entries.en: On xinhai Mingzong first held court at Zhongxing Hall.
entries.literal: On xinhai, the Emperor first held court at Zhongxing Hall.

entries.zh: 壬子，西南面副招討使、工部尚書任圜率步騎二萬六千人入見。
entries.en: On renzi Ren Yuan, Southwest deputy pacification commissioner and Minister of Works, led twenty-six thousand foot and horse to audience.
entries.literal: On renzi, Southwest Deputy Pacification Commissioner and Minister of Works Ren Yuan led twenty-six thousand foot and horse to audience.

entries.zh: 甲寅，帝御文明殿受朝。
entries.en: On jiayin Mingzong received court at Wenhua Hall.
entries.literal: On jiayin, the Emperor at Wenhua Hall received court.

entries.zh: 製改同光四年為天成元年，大赦天下。
entries.en: A decree renamed Tongguang 4 as Tiancheng 1 and amnestied the realm.
entries.literal: A decree changed Tongguang 4 to Tiancheng 1 and granted a great amnesty to all under heaven.

entries.zh: 後宮內職量留一百人，內官三十人，教坊一百人，鷹坊二十人，禦廚五十人，其餘任從所適。
entries.en: The inner palace was cut to one hundred posts, thirty eunuchs, one hundred musicians, twenty falconers, and fifty kitchen staff; the rest could leave as they chose.
entries.literal: Inner-palace posts were limited to one hundred persons, inner eunuchs thirty, Music Office one hundred, Falcon Office twenty, Imperial Kitchen fifty; the rest were free to go where they wished.

entries.zh: 諸司使務有名無實者並停。
entries.en: Nominal commissioner posts in the ministries were abolished.
entries.literal: Commissioner posts in the various offices that had names but no reality were all abolished.

entries.zh: 分遣諸軍就食近畿，以減饋送之勞。
entries.en: Armies were sent to forage near the capital to ease supply lines.
entries.literal: Armies were dispatched in groups to forage near the capital to reduce the labor of supply transport.

entries.zh: 秋夏稅子，每鬥先有省耗一升，今後隻納正數，其省耗宜停。
entries.en: Autumn-summer grain tax had taken one sheng per dou as shrinkage; hereafter only the full measure was due and shrinkage ended.
entries.literal: For autumn-summer tax grain, each dou had formerly included one sheng of official shrinkage; hereafter only the full measure was to be paid, and shrinkage was to stop.

entries.zh: 天下節度、防禦使，除正、至、端午、降誕四節量事進奉，達情而已，自於州府圓融，不得科斂百姓。
entries.en: Circuit and defense commissioners could send only modest festival gifts at New Year, solstice, Dragon Boat, and birthday from their own funds, not levy the people.
entries.literal: Circuit and defense commissioners throughout the realm, aside from the four festivals of New Year, solstice, Dragon Boat, and birthday, might present limited ceremonial tribute to show sentiment only, from their own prefectural funds, and might not levy the common people.

entries.zh: 其刺史雖遇四節，不在貢奉。
entries.en: Prefects were exempt from festival tribute even on those four days.
entries.literal: Their prefectural governors, even on the four festivals, were not subject to tribute.

entries.zh: 諸州雜稅，宜定合稅物色名目，不得邀難商旅。
entries.en: Prefectures had to list taxable goods clearly and stop harassing merchants.
entries.literal: Miscellaneous taxes in the prefectures should fix the categories of taxable goods and might not harass travelers and merchants.

entries.zh: 租庸司先將係省錢物，與人回圖，宜令盡底收納，以塞幸門雲。
entries.en: The Rent and Corvée Office was ordered to recover all provincial funds it had lent for private trade and close the loophole.
entries.literal: The Rent and Corvée Office had advanced tied provincial funds for trade with others; they were ordered to collect them fully to block loopholes.

entries.zh: 乙卯，渤海國王大諲譔遣使朝貢。
entries.en: On yimao Bohai's King Da Yinzhuan sent tribute envoys.
entries.literal: On yimao, Bohai King Da Yinse sent envoys with tribute.

entries.zh: 是月，北京副留守、知留守事張憲賜死，以其失守故也。
entries.en: That month Zhang Xian, Northern Capital deputy commissioner, was executed for losing his post.
entries.literal: That month, Beiping deputy military commissioner and acting military commissioner Zhang Xian was granted death for having lost his post.

entries.zh: 新授青州節度使霍彥威奏，處斬新登州刺史王公儼，及同謀拒命指揮使李謹、王居厚等八人訖。
entries.en: New Qing commissioner Huo Yanwei reported executing Deng prefect Wang Gongyan and eight plotters, including Li Jin and Wang Juhou.
entries.literal: The newly appointed Qingzhou military commissioner Huo Yanwei reported that he had executed the new Dengzhou prefect Wang Gongyan and eight others who had plotted rebellion, including commanders Li Jin and Wang Juhou.

entries.zh: 初，同光中，符習為青州節度使，宦官楊希望為監軍，專製軍政。
entries.en: In Tongguang Fu Xi had held Qing while eunuch Yang Xiwang as monitor controlled the army.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the Tongguang era Fu Xi was Qingzhou military commissioner and eunuch Yang Xiwang was army monitor, monopolizing military government.

entries.zh: 趙在禮之據魏州，習奉詔以本軍進討，俄而帝為亂軍所劫，習即罷歸。
entries.en: When Zhao Zaili took Wei, Fu Xi marched to attack, but Zhuangzong was seized by mutineers and Fu Xi withdrew.
entries.literal: When Zhao Zaili seized Weizhou, Xi obeyed an edict and advanced with his army to attack; soon the Emperor was seized by mutinous troops and Xi withdrew.

entries.zh: 希望遣兵邀之，習懼而還。
entries.en: Yang Xiwang sent troops to cut him off; Fu Xi retreated in fear.
entries.literal: Xiwang sent troops to intercept him; Xi, afraid, turned back.

entries.zh: 至滑州，帝遣人招之，習至，乃從帝入汴。
entries.en: At Hua Zhuangzong summoned him; Fu Xi came and followed him into Bian.
entries.literal: At Hua Prefecture the Emperor sent men to summon him; when Xi arrived he followed the Emperor into Bian.

entries.zh: 希望聞魏軍亂，遣兵圍守習家，欲盡殺之。
entries.en: Hearing of the Wei mutiny, Yang Xiwang besieged Fu Xi's family to kill them all.
entries.literal: Hearing the Wei army had mutinied, Xiwang sent troops to surround Xi's household intending to kill everyone.

entries.zh: 公儼素受希望獎愛，謂希望曰：「內侍宜分腹心之兵，監四面守陴者，則誰敢異圖。」
entries.en: Gongyan, favored by Yang Xiwang, said to him, "Your Grace should divide your trusted troops to watch all four sides of the ramparts—then who would dare plot differently."
entries.literal: Gongyan had long been favored by Xiwang and said to him, "Your Grace should divide your trusted troops to watch all four sides of the ramparts—then who would dare plot differently."

entries.zh: 希望從之。
entries.en: Yang Xiwang agreed.
entries.literal: Xiwang followed this.

entries.zh: 公儼乘其無備，圍希望之第，擒而殺之。
entries.en: Gongyan surprised him, surrounded his house, seized Yang Xiwang, and killed him.
entries.literal: Gongyan took him unawares, surrounded Xiwang's residence, seized him, and killed him.

entries.zh: 公儼遂與州將李謹等謀據州城，以邀符節，即令軍府飛章留己，兼揚言符習在鎮，人不便其政，帝乃除公儼為登州刺史。
entries.en: Gongyan and Li Jin seized the city, memorialized to keep the post, and claimed Fu Xi's rule was unpopular; Zhuangzong named him Deng prefect.
entries.literal: Gongyan then with prefectural officers Li Jin and others plotted to hold the prefectural city to demand the commission, had the military government send a flying memorial to keep himself in post, and also spread word that while Fu Xi was in the prefecture the people found his rule hard; the Emperor then appointed Gongyan Dengzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 公儼不時赴任，即以霍彥威代符習，聚兵淄州，以圖進取。
entries.en: Gongyan delayed reporting; Huo Yanwei replaced Fu Xi, gathered troops at Zi, and prepared to advance.
entries.literal: Gongyan did not promptly take office; Huo Yanwei replaced Fu Xi, massed troops at Zi Prefecture, and planned an advance.

entries.zh: 彥威至淄州，會詔使至青州告諭，公儼即赴所任。
entries.en: At Zi an envoy reached Qing with the court order, and Gongyan set out for his post.
entries.literal: When Yanwei reached Zi, an edict envoy arrived at Qing to announce the matter, and Gongyan then went to his post.

entries.zh: 彥威懲其初心，遣人擒公儼於北海縣，與同黨斬於州東。
entries.en: Yanwei seized Gongyan at Beihai and beheaded him and his party east of the city.
entries.literal: Yanwei, punishing his original intent, sent men to seize Gongyan at Beihai County and with his accomplices beheaded him east of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：彥威聚兵淄州，以圖進取，公儼懼。
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Yanwei concentrated at Zi to advance and Gongyan panicked.
entries.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Yanwei massed troops at Zi Prefecture intending to advance; Gongyan was afraid.

entries.zh: 乙未，始之官。
entries.en: On yiwei he finally reported to his post.
entries.literal: On yiwei he finally took office.

entries.zh: 丁酉，彥威至青州，追擒之。）〉
entries.en: On dingyou Yanwei reached Qingzhou and arrested him.)〉
entries.literal: On dingyou Yanwei reached Qing and pursued and captured him.)〉

entries.zh: 有司上言：「莊宗祔廟，懿祖祧遷，準例舍故而諱新，懿祖例不諱，忌日不行香。」
entries.en: The ritual offices said: "With Zhuangzong enshrined and Yizu retired, the old taboo should yield to the new, but Yizu is not tabooed and needs no death-day incense."
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "With Zhuangzong enshrined and Yizu removed, precedent calls for abandoning the old taboo and honoring the new; Yizu is by precedent not tabooed, and on his death day no incense is burned."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 壬子，襄州節度使劉訓加檢校太傅，以偽蜀右僕射、中書侍郎、平章事、趙國公張格為太子賓客，充三司副使，從任圜請也。
entries.en: On renzi Liu Xun of Xiang became acting grand tutor; false Shu minister Zhang Ge became crown prince mentor and deputy Three Offices commissioner at Ren Yuan's request.
entries.literal: On renzi Xiangzhou military commissioner Liu Xun was advanced to acting Grand Tutor; the false Shu Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Vice Grand Councillor, and Duke of Zhao Zhang Ge was made Crown Prince Mentor and charged as deputy Three Offices commissioner—at Ren Yuan's request.

entries.zh: 九月乙卯朔，詔汴州扶溝縣復隸許州。
entries.en: On the yimao new moon of the ninth month Mingzong returned Bian's Fugou County to Xu.
entries.literal: Ninth month, yimao new moon: an edict returned Fugou County of Bian to Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以前絳州刺史婁繼英為冀州刺史，充北面水陸轉運製置使。
entries.en: Lou Jiying, former Jiang prefect, became Ji prefect and northern transport commissioner.
entries.literal: Former Jiang prefect Lou Jiying was made Ji prefect and charged as northern land-and-water transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 己未，幸至德宮，遂幸前隰州刺史袁建豐之第。
entries.en: On jiwei Mingzong visited Zhide Palace and then the home of former Xi prefect Yuan Jianfeng.
entries.literal: On jiwei the Emperor visited Zhide Palace, then visited the residence of former Xi prefect Yuan Jianfeng.

entries.zh: 帝嘗為太原內牙親將，建豐為副，至是建豐風疾沈廢，故親幸其第以撫之。
entries.en: Mingzong had been a personal guard commander in Taiyuan's inner barracks with Jianfeng as his deputy; now Jianfeng lay crippled by stroke, so Mingzong visited to comfort him.
entries.literal: The Emperor had once been a personal guard in the inner barracks at Taiyuan and Jianfeng his deputy; now Jianfeng was bedridden with wind illness, so the Emperor personally visited his house to comfort him.

entries.zh: 庚申，以都官郎中庾傳美充三州搜訪圖籍使。
entries.en: On gengshen Yu Chuanmei of Capital Punishments was sent to search three prefectures for maps and archives.
entries.literal: On gengshen Capital Punishments Bureau director Yu Chuanmei was charged as commissioner to search the three prefectures for maps and records.

entries.zh: 傳美為蜀王衍之舊僚，家在成都，便於歸計，且言成都具有本朝實錄，及傳美使回，所得才九朝實錄及殘缺雜舊而已。
entries.en: Chuanmei, once Wang Yan's retainer, had family in Chengdu and claimed the city still held Tang Veritable Records; his mission brought back only nine reigns' records and damaged old texts.
entries.literal: Chuanmei had been an old retainer of Shu ruler Wang Yan; his family was in Chengdu, which suited his plan to return, and he said Chengdu still held this dynasty's Veritable Records; when Chuanmei returned from his mission he obtained only the Veritable Records of nine reigns and miscellaneous damaged old texts.

entries.zh: 癸亥，應聖節，百僚於敬愛寺設齋，召緇黃之眾於中興殿講論，眾近例也。
entries.en: On guihai, Yingsheng day, officials held a feast at Jing'ai Temple and summoned clergy to Zhongxing Hall by recent precedent.
entries.literal: On guihai, the Yingsheng festival, the hundred officials set a vegetarian feast at Jing'ai Temple and summoned monks and laity to discourse at Zhongxing Hall—following recent precedent.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以偽蜀檢校太師、兼中書令、右金吾街使張貽範為兵部尚書致仕。
entries.en: On wuchen false Shu minister Zhang Yifan became War minister emeritus.
entries.literal: On wuchen the false Shu acting Grand Master, concurrent Secretariat Director, Right Golden Crow Street commissioner Zhang Yifan was made War Minister and retired.

entries.zh: 都官員外郎於鄴奏請指揮不得書契券輒賣良人，從之。
entries.en: Yu Ye of Capital Punishments asked to forbid contracts selling free persons, and Mingzong agreed.
entries.literal: Capital Punishments Bureau vice director Yu Ye memorialized asking that orders forbid writing contracts that sold free persons, and it was approved.

entries.zh: 癸酉，天策上將軍、湖南節度使、開府儀同三司、守太師、兼尚書令、楚王馬殷加檢校太師、守尚書令。
entries.en: On guiyou Ma Yin of Chu was advanced to acting grand preceptor and grand secretariat director.
