entries.en: Jingtang said, "Wang Hongzhi of Weizhou is an old acquaintance who knows how affairs are managed. Let us first go to Hongzhi and devise a plan."
entries.literal: Jingtang said: "Wang Hongzan of Weizhou is an old acquaintance versed in affairs; let us first go to Hongzan to devise a plan."

entries.zh: 敬瑭即馳騎而前，見宏贄曰：「主上播遷，至此危迫，吾戚屬也，何以圖全？」
entries.en: Jingtang immediately galloped ahead, saw Hongzan, and said, "The sovereign is in flight and has come to this desperate pass. We are kinsmen—how can we find a way to preserve him?"
entries.literal: Jingtang immediately galloped ahead, saw Hongzan and said: "The sovereign is in flight and has come to this desperate pass; we are kinsmen—how can we devise a way to preserve him whole?"

entries.zh: 宏贄曰：「天子避狄，古亦有之，然於奔迫之中，亦有將相、國寶、法物，所以軍長瞻奉，不覺其亡也。
entries.en: Hongzan said, "That an emperor flees barbarian invasion has happened before in antiquity, yet even in flight there are usually generals and ministers, national treasures, and ritual regalia, so that military commanders may look up in reverence and not realize that the dynasty is lost.
entries.literal: Hongzan said: "That an emperor flees barbarian invasion has occurred in antiquity; yet even in flight there are usually generals and ministers, national treasures, and ritual regalia, so that military commanders may look up in reverence and not notice that the dynasty is lost.

entries.zh: 今宰職近臣從乎？
entries.en: Are chief ministers and close attendants following now?
entries.literal: Are chief ministers and close attendants following now?

entries.zh: 寶玉、法物從乎？」
entries.en: Are jade treasures and ritual regalia following?"
entries.literal: Are jade treasures and ritual regalia following?"

entries.zh: 詢之無有。
entries.en: Upon inquiry there were none.
entries.literal: Upon inquiry there were none.

entries.zh: 宏贄曰：「大樹將顛，非一繩所維。
entries.en: Hongzan said, "When a great tree is about to topple, one rope cannot hold it up.
entries.literal: Hongzan said: "When a great tree is about to topple, one rope cannot hold it up.

entries.zh: 今以五十騎奔竄，無將相一人擁從，安能興復大計！
entries.en: Now with fifty horsemen fleeing in disorder and not a single general or minister in attendance, how can anyone undertake a plan to restore the dynasty!
entries.literal: Now with fifty horsemen fleeing in disorder, without a single general or minister attending—how can one undertake a plan to restore the dynasty!

entries.zh: 所謂蛟龍失雲雨者也。
entries.en: This is what people mean when they speak of a dragon deprived of clouds and rain.
entries.literal: This is what is called a dragon deprived of clouds and rain.

entries.zh: 今六軍將士總在潞邸矣，公縱以戚藩念舊，無奈之何！」
entries.en: Now the officers and soldiers of the Six Armies are all at the Prince of Lu's residence. Though you may, by reason of kinship and old frontier ties, wish otherwise, nothing can be done!"
entries.literal: Now the Six Armies' officers and soldiers are all at the Prince of Lu's residence; though you may by reason of kinship and old ties on the frontier wish otherwise, nothing can be done!"

entries.zh: 遂與宏贄同謁於驛亭，宣坐謀之。
entries.en: Thereupon he and Hongzan together waited upon the Emperor at the post station and invited him to sit and deliberate.
entries.literal: Thereupon he and Hongzan together waited upon him at the post station and invited him to sit and deliberate.

entries.zh: 敬瑭以宏贄所陳以聞，弓箭庫使沙守榮、奔洪進前謂敬瑭曰：「主上即明宗愛子，公即明宗愛婿，富貴既同受，休戚合共之。
entries.en: Jingtang reported what Hongzan had said. Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin, commissioners of the Bow-and-Arrow Store, stepped forward and said to Jingtang, "The sovereign is Mingzong's beloved son, and you are Mingzong's beloved son-in-law. You have shared fortune alike—glory and peril ought to be borne together.
entries.literal: Jingtang reported what Hongzan had stated. Bow-and-arrow Store commissioners Sha Shourong and Ben Hongjin stepped forward and said to Jingtang: "The sovereign is Mingzong's beloved son; you are Mingzong's beloved son-in-law; you have shared fortune alike—glory and peril should be borne together.

entries.zh: 今謀於戚藩，欲期安復，翻索從臣、國寶，欲以此為辭，為賊算天子耶！」
entries.en: Now you plot with a frontier kinsman, hoping for safe restoration, yet turn about to demand attending ministers and national treasures, intending to use this as a pretext—are you scheming against the sovereign on the traitor's behalf!"
entries.literal: Now you plot with a frontier kinsman, hoping for safe restoration, yet turn about to demand attending ministers and national treasures—intending to use this as a pretext: are you calculating against the sovereign for the traitor's sake!"

entries.zh: 乃抽佩刀刺敬瑭，敬瑭親將陳暉捍之，守榮與暉單戰而死，洪進亦自刎。
entries.en: They then drew their girdle daggers to stab Jingtang. Chen Hui, Jingtang's personal guard, parried them. Shourong and Hui fought one-on-one and died, and Hongjin cut his own throat.
entries.literal: They then drew their girdle daggers to stab Jingtang; Jingtang's personal guard Chen Hui parried them; Shourong and Hui fought one-on-one and died; Hongjin also cut his own throat.

entries.zh: 是日，敬瑭盡誅帝之從騎五十餘輩，獨留帝於驛，乃馳騎趨洛。
entries.en: That day Jingtang had all fifty-odd of the Emperor's attending horsemen executed, left the Emperor alone at the post station, and galloped toward Luoyang.
entries.literal: That day Jingtang had all fifty-odd of the Emperor's attending horsemen executed, kept the Emperor alone at the post station, and galloped toward Luoyang.

entries.zh: 四月三日，潞王入洛。
entries.en: On the third day of the fourth month the Prince of Lu entered Luoyang.
entries.literal: On the third day of the fourth month the Prince of Lu entered Luoyang.

entries.zh: 五日，即位。
entries.en: On the fifth day he took the throne.
entries.literal: On the fifth day he took the throne.

entries.zh: 七日，廢帝為鄂王。
entries.en: On the seventh day the Emperor was demoted to Prince of E.
entries.literal: On the seventh day the Emperor was demoted to Prince of E.

entries.zh: 遣弘贄子殿直王巒之衛州，時宏贄已奉帝幸州廨。
entries.en: He dispatched Hongzhi's son, Palace Guard Wang Luan, to Weizhou; by then Hongzhi had already escorted the Emperor to the prefectural offices.
entries.literal: He dispatched Hongzan's son, Palace Guard Wang Luan, to Weizhou; by then Hongzan had already escorted the Emperor to the prefectural offices.

entries.zh: 九日，巒至，帝遇鴆而崩，時年二十一。
entries.en: On the ninth day Luan arrived; the Emperor was given poisoned wine and died, aged twenty-one.
entries.literal: On the ninth day Luan arrived; the Emperor met poisoned wine and died, aged twenty-one.

entries.zh: 是日辰時，白虹貫日。
entries.en: That day at the chen hour a white rainbow pierced the sun.
entries.literal: That day at the chen hour a white rainbow pierced the sun.

entries.zh: 皇后孔氏在宮中，及王巒回，即日與其四子並遇害。
entries.en: Empress Kong was in the palace; when Wang Luan returned, that same day she and her four sons were all killed.
entries.literal: Empress Kong was in the palace; when Wang Luan returned, that same day she and her four sons were all killed.

entries.zh: 晉高祖即位，諡曰閔，與秦王及末帝子重吉並葬於徽陵域中，封才數尺，路人觀者悲之。
entries.en: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, he was given the posthumous title Min. He was buried together with the Prince of Qin and the Last Emperor's son Chongji within the precinct of Huiling Mausoleum. The mound was only a few feet high, and passersby who saw it were moved to grief.
entries.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, he was given the posthumous title Min; he was buried together with the Prince of Qin and the Last Emperor's son Chongji within the precinct of Huiling Mausoleum, the mound only a few feet high, and passersby who saw it were moved to grief.

entries.zh: 閔帝，諱從厚，小字菩薩奴，明宗第三子也。
entries.en: Emperor Min, whose taboo name was Conghou and childhood name Pusainu, was the third son of Mingzong.
entries.literal: Emperor Min, taboo name Conghou, childhood name Pusainu, was Mingzong's third son.

entries.zh: 母昭懿皇后夏氏，以天祐十一年歲在甲戌，十一月二十八日庚申，生帝於晉陽舊第。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Zhao-yi of the Xia clan. In the eleventh year of Tianyou, the jiaxu year, on gengshen, the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month, the future Emperor was born at the old family residence in Jinyang.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Zhao-yi née Xia; in the eleventh year of Tianyou, year jiaxu, on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month, gengshen, the Emperor was born at the old residence in Jinyang.

entries.zh: 帝髫齔好讀《春秋》，略通大義，貌類明宗，尤鍾愛。
entries.en: From boyhood he loved reading the Spring and Autumn Annals and had some grasp of its larger meaning. He looked like Mingzong, who cherished him above the rest.
entries.literal: From childhood the Emperor loved reading the Spring and Autumn Annals, had some grasp of its great meaning, resembled Mingzong in appearance, and was especially cherished.

entries.zh: 六月甲子朔，新州上言，契丹入寇。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on jiazi, the first of the month, Xin Prefecture reported a Khitan invasion.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, the first of the month, Xin Prefecture reported that the Khitan had invaded.

entries.zh: 乙丑，有司上言，宣憲皇太后陵請以順從為名，從之。
entries.en: On yichou the relevant offices reported that Empress Dowager Xuanxian's tomb should be named Shuncong. Approved.
entries.literal: On yichou, the relevant offices memorialized that the tomb of Empress Dowager Xuanxian should be named Shuncong. Granted.

entries.zh: 振武奏，契丹二萬騎在黑榆林。
entries.en: Zhenwu reported twenty thousand Khitan horsemen at Heiyulin.
entries.literal: Zhenwu reported that twenty thousand Khitan horsemen were at Heiyulin.

entries.zh: 丁卯，以太子少保致仕朱漢賓卒廢朝。
entries.en: On dingmao court was suspended for the death of Zhu Hanbin, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: On dingmao, court was suspended for the death of Zhu Hanbin, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 壬申，命史官修撰明宗實錄。
entries.en: On renshen the court ordered the historiographers to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Mingzong.
entries.literal: On renshen, the court ordered the historiographers to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Mingzong.

entries.zh: 契丹寇應州。
entries.en: The Khitan raided Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: The Khitan raided Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以新州節度使楊漢賓為同州節度使，以前晉州節度使翟璋為新州節度使。
entries.en: Yang Hanbin, Xin Prefecture military commissioner, was made Tong Prefecture military commissioner; Zhai Zhang, former Jin Prefecture military commissioner, was made Xin Prefecture military commissioner.
entries.literal: Yang Hanbin, military commissioner of Xin Prefecture, was made military commissioner of Tong Prefecture; Zhai Zhang, former military commissioner of Jin Prefecture, was made military commissioner of Xin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚辰，北面招討使趙德鈞奏，行營馬步軍都虞候、定州節度使楊光遠，行營排陣使、邢州節度使安審琦帥本軍至易州，見進軍追襲契丹次。
entries.en: On gengchen Zhao Dejun, northern expedition commissioner, reported that Yang Guangyuan, camp horse-and-foot chief adjutant and Ding Prefecture military commissioner, and An Shenqi, camp battle-formation commissioner and Xing Prefecture military commissioner, led their armies to Yi Prefecture and found the advancing force about to pursue the Khitan further.
entries.literal: On gengchen, Zhao Dejun, northern expedition commissioner, memorialized that Yang Guangyuan, chief adjutant of the camp horse-and-foot army and military commissioner of Ding Prefecture, and An Shenqi, battle-formation commissioner of the camp and military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, led their armies to Yi Prefecture and saw the advancing troops in pursuit of the Khitan at the next stop.

entries.zh: 河東節度使石敬瑭奏，邊軍乏芻糧，其安重榮巡邊兵士欲移振武就糧。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang, Hedong military commissioner, reported that border troops lacked fodder and grain and that soldiers under An Chongrong's border patrol wished to move to Zhenwu for provisions.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang, military commissioner of Hedong, memorialized that the border armies lacked fodder and grain, and that the soldiers of An Chongrong's border-patrol force wished to move to Zhenwu to obtain provisions.

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: Granted.

entries.zh: 尋又奏，懷、孟租稅，請指揮於忻、代州輸納。
entries.en: He soon memorialized again, asking that Huai and Meng rent and tax be directed for delivery at Xin and Dai Prefectures.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized again, requesting that the rent and tax of Huai and Meng be directed for delivery at Xin and Dai Prefectures.

entries.zh: 朝廷以邊儲不給，詔河東戶民積粟處，量事抄借，仍於鎮州支絹五萬匹，送河東充博采之直。
entries.en: Because border stores were insufficient, an edict ordered grain requisitioned wherever Hedong households had stores, and fifty thousand bolts of silk were disbursed at Zhen Prefecture and sent to Hedong as payment for procurement.
entries.literal: Because border stores were insufficient, the court issued an edict that wherever households in Hedong had stored grain, grain should be requisitioned as circumstances required, and furthermore fifty thousand bolts of silk were disbursed at Zhen Prefecture and sent to Hedong as payment for procurement.

entries.zh: 是月，北面轉運副使劉福配鎮州百姓車子一千五百乘，運糧至代州。
entries.en: That month Liu Fu, Northern Front deputy transport commissioner, assigned fifteen hundred civilian carts from Zhen Prefecture to haul grain to Dai Prefecture.
entries.literal: That month, Liu Fu, deputy transport commissioner of the Northern Front, assigned fifteen hundred civilian carts from Zhen Prefecture to transport grain to Dai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 時水旱民饑，河北諸州困於飛挽，逃潰者甚眾，軍前使者繼至，督促糧運，由是生靈谘怨。
entries.en: At the time drought and flood had left the people hungry; Hebei prefectures were strained by urgent grain transport; deserters were very numerous; envoys from the front kept arriving to press for grain—whereupon the people complained bitterly.
entries.literal: At the time drought and flood had caused famine among the people; the prefectures of Hebei were distressed by urgent grain transport; deserters were very numerous; envoys from the army front arrived in succession urging grain transport—thereby the common people complained bitterly.

entries.zh: 辛巳，詔諸州府署醫博士。
entries.en: On xinsi an edict ordered all prefectures and districts to establish posts for medical doctors.
entries.literal: On xinsi, an edict ordered all prefectures and districts to establish posts for medical doctors.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以前許州節度使李從昶為右龍武統軍，以前彰國軍節度使沙彥珣為右神武統軍。
entries.en: On bingxu Li Congchang, former Xu Prefecture military commissioner, was made commander of the Right Longwu Army; Sha Yanxun, former Zhangguo military commissioner, was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
entries.literal: On bingxu, Li Congchang, former military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, was made commander of the Right Longwu Army; Sha Yanxun, former military commissioner of the Zhangguo Army, was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

entries.zh: 秋七月丙申，石敬瑭奏，斬挾馬都指揮使李暉等三十六人，以謀亂故也。
entries.en: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingshen Shi Jingtang reported that he had executed the horse-guard commander Li Hui and thirty-five others for plotting rebellion.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingshen, Shi Jingtang memorialized that he had executed Li Hui and thirty-five others, commanders of the horse-guarding corps, for plotting rebellion.

entries.zh: 時敬瑭以兵屯忻州，一日，軍士喧噪，遽呼萬歲，乃斬暉等以止之。
entries.en: At the time Jingtang had troops at Xin Prefecture; one day the soldiers raised a clamor and suddenly shouted "Long live!"; he then executed Hui and the others to stop it.
entries.literal: At the time Jingtang had troops stationed at Xin Prefecture; one day the soldiers raised a clamor and suddenly shouted "Long live!"; he then executed Hui and the others to stop it.

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》：契丹屢攻北邊，時石敬瑭將大兵屯忻州，潞王遣使賜軍士夏衣，傳詔撫諭，軍士呼萬歲者數四。
entries.en: (The 《Chronicle of the Khitan State》 records: The Khitan repeatedly attacked the northern border. At the time Shi Jingtang had a large army at Xin Prefecture; the Prince of Lu sent an envoy to bestow summer garments on the soldiers and transmitted an edict of consolation—the soldiers shouted "Long live!" four times.
entries.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Khitan State》 records: The Khitan repeatedly attacked the northern border. At the time Shi Jingtang had a large army stationed at Xin Prefecture; the Prince of Lu sent an envoy to bestow summer garments on the soldiers and transmitted an edict of consolation and reassurance—the soldiers shouted "Long live!" four times.

entries.zh: 敬瑭懼，幕僚段希堯請誅其倡者，敬瑭命劉知遠斬三十六人以殉。
entries.en: Jingtang was afraid; his staff officer Duan Xiyao urged executing the ringleaders; Jingtang ordered Liu Zhiyuan to behead thirty-six men as a warning.
entries.literal: Jingtang was afraid; his staff officer Duan Xiyao requested executing the ringleaders; Jingtang ordered Liu Zhiyuan to behead thirty-six men as a warning.

entries.zh: 潞王聞，益疑之。）〉
entries.en: When the Prince of Lu heard of it, he grew even more suspicious of Jingtang.)〉
entries.literal: When the Prince of Lu heard of it, he grew even more suspicious of Jingtang.)〉

entries.zh: 御史中丞盧損奏：「準天成二年七月敕，每月首、十五日入閣，罷五日起居。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Lu Sun reported: "According to the edict of the seventh month of the second year of Tiancheng, on the first and fifteenth of each month enter the Hall of Affairs, abolishing the fifth-day audience.
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Lu Sun memorialized: "According to the edict of the seventh month of the second year of Tiancheng, on the first and fifteenth of each month enter the Hall of Affairs, abolishing the fifth-day audience.

entries.zh: 臣以為中旬排仗，有勞聖躬，請隻以月首入閣，五日起居依舊。
entries.en: Your subject considers the mid-month guard formation burdensome to the Emperor; we ask to enter the Hall only at the month's beginning, with the fifth-day audience unchanged.
entries.literal: Your subject considers the mid-month formation of guards burdensome to the imperial person; we request entering the Hall only at the month's beginning, with the fifth-day audience remaining as before.

entries.zh: 又準天成三年五月、長興二年七月敕，許諸州節度使帶使相歲薦僚屬五人，餘薦三人，防禦、團練使薦二人，今乞行厘革。
entries.en: Furthermore, under edicts of the fifth month of the third year of Tiancheng and the seventh month of the second year of Changxing, military commissioners with vice regent titles could recommend five subordinates annually, others three, and defense and training commissioners two—we now ask for reform.
entries.literal: Furthermore, according to edicts of the fifth month of the third year of Tiancheng and the seventh month of the second year of Changxing, military commissioners bearing the vice regent title were permitted to recommend five subordinates annually, others three, and defense and training commissioners two—we now request reform.

entries.zh: 又長興二年八月敕，州縣佐官差充馬步判官，仍同一任，乞行止絕，依舊衙前選補。」
entries.en: Also under the edict of the eighth month of the second year of Changxing, county and district aides were assigned as horse-and-foot reviewing secretaries within the same term—we ask that this be ended and selection restored from yamen runners."
entries.literal: Also according to the edict of the eighth month of the second year of Changxing, county and district aides were assigned as horse-and-foot reviewing secretaries within the same term—we request this be terminated and restored to selection from yamen runners."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「今後藩臣帶使相許薦三人，餘薦二人，直屬京防禦、團練使薦一人，餘並從之。」
entries.en: An edict stated: "Henceforth frontier officials with vice regent titles may recommend three persons, others two; defense and training commissioners directly under the capital may recommend one—the rest also approved."
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Henceforth frontier officials bearing the vice regent title may recommend three persons, others two; defense and training commissioners directly under the capital may recommend one—the remainder all granted."

entries.zh: 丁酉，回紇可汗仁美遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On dingyou Kaghan Renmei of the Uyghurs sent envoys with tribute goods.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Kaghan Renmei of the Uyghurs dispatched envoys presenting tribute goods.

entries.zh: 西京弓弩指揮使任漢權奏，六月二十一日與川軍戰於金州之漢陰，王師不利，其部下兵士除傷痍外，已至鳳翔。
entries.en: Ren Hanquan, Western Capital crossbow commander, reported that on the twenty-first day of the sixth month he fought Sichuan troops at Hanyin in Jin Prefecture; the imperial army fared poorly, and his subordinates, aside from the wounded, had already reached Fengxiang.
entries.literal: Ren Hanquan, commander of the crossbow corps of the Western Capital, memorialized that on the twenty-first day of the sixth month he fought Sichuan troops at Hanyin in Jin Prefecture; the imperial army fared poorly, and his subordinate soldiers, aside from the wounded, had already reached Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 先是，盩厔鎮將劉贇引軍入川界，為蜀將全師鬱所敗。
entries.en: Previously Liu Yun, Zhouzhi garrison commander, had led troops into Sichuan and was defeated by the Shu general Quan Shiyu.
entries.literal: Previously, Liu Yun, garrison commander of Zhouzhi, had led troops into Sichuan territory and was defeated by Quan Shiyu, a Shu general.

entries.zh: 金州都監崔處訥重傷，諸州屯兵潰散。
entries.en: Cui Chune, Jin Prefecture garrison supervisor, was severely wounded, and garrison troops across the prefectures scattered in rout.
entries.literal: Cui Chune, garrison supervisor of Jin Prefecture, was severely wounded, and the garrison troops of the various prefectures scattered in rout.

entries.zh: 金州防禦使馬全節收合州兵，固守獲全。
entries.en: Ma Quanjie, Jin Prefecture defense commissioner, gathered the prefecture's troops, held firm, and preserved the prefecture intact.
entries.literal: Ma Quanjie, defense commissioner of Jin Prefecture, gathered the prefecture's troops and held firm, preserving the prefecture intact.

entries.zh: 以樞密使劉延皓為天雄軍節度使。
entries.en: Liu Yanhao, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, was made Tianxiong Army military commissioner.
entries.literal: Liu Yanhao, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.

entries.zh: 甲辰，以右神武統軍沙彥珣權知雲州。
entries.en: On jiachen Sha Yanxun, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made acting prefect of Yun Prefecture.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Sha Yanxun, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made acting prefect of Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 乙巳，以徐州節度使張敬達充北面行營副總管。
entries.en: On yisi Zhang Jingda, Xu Prefecture military commissioner, was assigned as deputy overall commander of the Northern Front camp.
entries.literal: On yisi, Zhang Jingda, military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, was assigned as deputy overall commander of the Northern Front camp.

entries.zh: 時契丹入邊，石敬瑭屢請益兵，朝廷軍士多在北鄙，俄聞忻州諸軍呼噪，帝不悅，乃命敬達為北軍之副，以減敬瑭之權也。
entries.en: At the time the Khitan had crossed the border; Shi Jingtang repeatedly asked for reinforcements; most court troops were on the northern frontier; soon word came that the Xin Prefecture armies were raising a clamor; the Emperor was displeased and assigned Jingda as deputy to the northern armies to reduce Jingtang's authority.
entries.literal: At the time the Khitan had entered the border; Shi Jingtang repeatedly requested additional troops; most of the court's soldiers were on the northern frontier; soon word came that the armies at Xin Prefecture were raising a clamor; the Emperor was displeased and therefore assigned Jingda as deputy to the northern armies, to reduce Jingtang's authority.

entries.zh: 丁巳，宰臣盧文紀等上疏，其略曰：
entries.en: On dingsi Chief Counselor Lu Wenji and others submitted a memorial, the gist of which read:
entries.literal: On dingsi, Chief Counselor Lu Wenji and others submitted a memorial, the gist of which read:

entries.zh: 冬十月丁卯，幸崇道宮、甘泉亭。
entries.en: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao the Emperor visited the Chongdao Palace and Sweet Spring Pavilion.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao, the Emperor visited the Chongdao Palace and Sweet Spring Pavilion.

entries.zh: 己巳，以左衛上將軍李頃為左領軍上將軍。
entries.en: On jisi Li Qing, General of the Left Guard, was made General-in-chief of the Left Leading Army.
entries.literal: On jisi, Li Qing, General of the Left Guard, was made General-in-chief of the Left Leading Army.

entries.zh: 北面行營總管石敬瑭奏，自代州歸鎮。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang, Northern Front camp overall commander, reported that he had returned from Dai Prefecture to his command.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang, overall commander of the Northern Front camp, memorialized that he had returned from Dai Prefecture to his command.

entries.zh: 庚午，以晉州節度使張溫卒廢朝。
entries.en: On gengwu court was suspended for the death of Zhang Wen, Jin Prefecture military commissioner.
entries.literal: On gengwu, court was suspended for the death of Zhang Wen, military commissioner of Jin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 甲戌，幸趙延壽、張延朗第。
entries.en: On jiaxu the Emperor visited the residences of Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Yanlang.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, the Emperor visited the residences of Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Yanlang.

entries.zh: 丁丑，以端明殿學士、兵部侍郎李專美為秘書監，充宣徽北院使。
entries.en: On dingchou Li Zhuanmei, Duanming Hall academician and Vice Minister of War, was made Director of the Secretariat and Northern Bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: On dingchou, Li Zhuanmei, Academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of War, was made Director of the Secretariat and assigned as Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 庚寅，以左諫議大夫唐汭為左散騎常侍。
entries.en: On gengyin Tang Rui, Left Remonstrance Counselor, was made Left Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: On gengyin, Tang Rui, Left Remonstrance Counselor, was made Left Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 清泰二年春正月丙申朔，帝御明堂殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the first day of the first month of the second year of Qingtai, the Emperor took the Hall of Bright Clarity to receive the New Year's court congratulations, with guards and ceremonial escort according to custom.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qingtai, spring, first month, on the bingshen day, the first of the month, the Emperor presided in the Hall of Bright Clarity to receive court congratulations, with guards and honors as prescribed.

entries.zh: 乙巳，中書門下奏：「遇千春節，凡刑獄公事奏覆，候次月施行。
entries.en: On yisi the Secretariat and Chancellery reported: "For the Thousand Spring Festival, all criminal and official matters under review should wait until the following month before taking effect.
entries.literal: On yisi, the Secretariat-Chancellery memorialized: "When the Thousand Spring Festival falls, all criminal cases and official business submitted for review shall await implementation the following month.

entries.zh: 今後請重係者即候次月，輕係者即節前奏覆決遣。」
entries.en: Henceforth we ask that serious cases wait until the month after, while minor detainees be reviewed and decided before the festival."
entries.literal: Hereafter we request that heavily detained prisoners wait until the following month, while lightly detained ones be submitted for review and judgment before the festival."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: Granted.

entries.zh: 戊申，宗正寺奏：「北京、應州、曹州諸陵，望差本州府長官朝拜。
entries.en: On wushen the Court of Imperial Clan submitted: "For the imperial tombs in the Northern Capital, Yingzhou, and Cao Prefecture, we propose that the prefectural governors of each jurisdiction be assigned to pay court.
entries.literal: On wushen, the Court of Imperial Clan memorialized: "For the imperial tombs at Beijing, Ying Prefecture, and Cao Prefecture, we hope to dispatch the chief officials of each prefecture to perform obeisance.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載宗正寺原奏云：北京永興、長寧、建極三陵，應州遂、衍、奕三陵，準曹州溫陵例，下本州府官朝拜。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 quotes the original memorial: the three Northern Capital tombs Yongxing, Changning, and Jianji; the three Yingzhou tombs Sui, Yan, and Yi—following the Wen Tomb precedent at Cao Prefecture, local prefectural officials should be charged with attendance.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records the Court of Imperial Clan's original memorial as follows: The three tombs Yongxing, Changning, and Jianji at Beijing; the three tombs Sui, Yan, and Yi at Ying Prefecture—following the precedent of Wen Tomb at Cao Prefecture, order the officials of the local prefectures to perform obeisance.)〉

entries.zh: 雍、坤、和、徽四陵，差太常宗正卿朝拜。」
entries.en: For the Yong, Kun, He, and Hui tombs, the Vice Minister of Rites and the Court of Imperial Clan director should be assigned to attend."
entries.literal: For the four tombs Yong, Kun, He, and Hui, dispatch the Vice Minister of Rites and the Court of Imperial Clan director to perform obeisance."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: Granted.

entries.zh: 己酉，北京奏，光祿卿致仕周元豹卒。
entries.en: On jiyou the Northern Capital reported the death of Zhou Yuanbao, former Director of the Directorate of Foodstuffs.
entries.literal: On jiyou, Beijing reported that Zhou Yuanbao, retired Director of the Directorate of Foodstuffs, had died.

entries.zh: 庚申，鄴都進天王甲。
entries.en: On gengshen the capital at Ye presented suits of Heavenly King armor.
entries.literal: On gengshen, the capital at Ye presented Heavenly King armor.

entries.zh: 帝在藩時，有相士言帝如毗沙天王，帝知之，竊喜。
entries.en: While the Emperor was still a prince in his fief, a physiognomancer said he resembled the Guardian King Vaisravana; knowing this, he was quietly pleased.
entries.literal: When the Emperor was still a prince, a physiognomancer said the Emperor resembled the Heavenly King Vaisravana; the Emperor knew of this and secretly rejoiced.

entries.zh: 及即位，選軍士之魁偉者，被以天王甲，俾居宿衛，因詔諸道造此甲而進之。
entries.en: After his enthronement he chose the tallest soldiers, outfitted them as Heavenly Kings, and placed them in the palace guard; he also ordered every circuit to forge such armor and send it in.
entries.literal: Upon accession he selected the tallest and strongest soldiers, clothed them in Heavenly King armor, and had them serve in the palace guard; he then ordered all circuits to manufacture such armor and present it.

entries.zh: 三司奏，添征蠶鹽錢及增曲價。
entries.en: The fiscal offices reported a plan to increase the silk-and-salt tax and raise liquor prices.
entries.literal: The Three Departments memorialized to add a levy on silk-and-salt money and to raise the price of yeast liquor.

entries.zh: 先是曲斤八十文，增至一百五十文。
entries.en: Liquor had formerly been eighty cash per jin; it was now raised to one hundred fifty.
entries.literal: Previously yeast liquor was eighty cash per jin; it was increased to one hundred fifty cash.

entries.zh: 乙丑，雲州節度使張溫移鎮晉州，以西京留守安重霸為雲州節度使。
entries.en: On yichou Zhang Wen was moved from Yunzhou to Jinzhou, and An Chongba, Western Capital intendant, was made Yunzhou military commissioner.
entries.literal: On yichou, Zhang Wen, military commissioner of Yun Prefecture, was transferred to Jin Prefecture; An Chongba, garrison commander of the Western Capital, became military commissioner of Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 克讓，武皇之仲弟也。
entries.en: Ke Rang was Li Keyong's second younger brother.
entries.literal: Ke Rang was the Martial Emperor's second younger brother.

entries.zh: 少善騎射，以勇悍聞。
entries.en: From youth he was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and his reputation rested on bold, ferocious fighting.
entries.literal: In youth he excelled at mounted archery and was known for fierce courage.

entries.zh: 咸通中，從討龐勳，以功為振武都校。
entries.en: In the Xiantong era he took part in the suppression of Pang Xun and, for his service, was appointed metropolitan commandant of Zhenwu.
entries.literal: During the Xiantong period he followed the campaign against Pang Xun and, for merit, was made metropolitan commandant of Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 乾符中，王仙芝陷荊、襄，朝廷征兵，克讓率師奉詔，賊平，以功授金吾將軍，留宿衛。
entries.en: In the Qianfu era, after Wang Xianzhi overran Jing and Xiang, the court mobilized troops. Ke Rang led his forces as ordered, and when the rebels were crushed he was made general of the Golden Guard and kept on palace guard duty.
entries.literal: During Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi seized Jing and Xiang. The court raised troops; Ke Rang led his army in obedience to the edict. When the bandits were pacified, he was appointed general of the Golden Guard and remained on palace night duty.

entries.zh: 初，懿祖歸朝，憲宗賜宅於親仁坊，自長慶以來，相次一人典衛兵。
entries.en: When the Virtuous Ancestor (Yizu) first submitted to the Tang court, Emperor Xianzong granted the family a residence in Qinren Ward. From the Changqing reign onward, a member of the clan in each generation held command of the palace guard.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Founding Ancestor returned to court allegiance, Emperor Xianzong granted a residence in Qinren Ward. From the Changqing era onward, one after another held command of the guard troops.

entries.zh: 武皇之起雲中，殺段文楚，朝議罪之，命加兵於我，懼，將逃歸，天子詔巡使王處存夜圍親仁坊捕克讓。
entries.en: When Li Keyong rose in Yunzhong and killed Duan Wenchu, the court condemned him and ordered troops sent against the clan. Fearing arrest, he prepared to flee north, and the emperor ordered the commissioner Wang Chucun to surround Qinren Ward by night and capture Ke Rang.
entries.literal: When the Martial Emperor rose in Yunzhong and killed Duan Wenchu, court opinion condemned him and ordered additional troops against us. In fear, about to flee home, the Son of Heaven ordered the circuit commissioner Wang Chucun to surround Qinren Ward by night and seize Ke Rang.

entries.zh: 詰旦兵合，克讓與紀綱何相溫、安文寬、石的曆十餘騎彎弧躍馬，突圍而出。
entries.en: At daybreak the encircling force closed in. Ke Rang, with his officers He Xiangwen, An Wenkuan, Shi Deli, and a dozen horsemen, strung their bows, spurred their mounts, and charged out of the trap.
entries.literal: At dawn the troops closed in. Ke Rang, with his commanders He Xiangwen, An Wenkuan, Shi Deli, and more than ten riders, bent their bows, spurred their horses, and broke through the encirclement.

entries.zh: 官軍數千人追之，比至渭橋，死者數百。
entries.en: Several thousand government troops gave chase, and by the time the pursuit reached Wei Bridge, several hundred men lay dead.
entries.literal: Several thousand government troops pursued them; by the time they reached Wei Bridge, several hundred had been killed.

entries.zh: 克讓自夏陽掠船而濟，歸於雁門。
entries.en: Ke Rang commandeered boats at Xiayang, crossed the river, and made his way back to Yanmen.
entries.literal: Ke Rang seized boats at Xiayang and crossed the river, returning to Yanmen.

entries.zh: 明年，武皇昭雪，克讓復入宿衛。
entries.en: The following year, after Li Keyong was cleared of the charges against him, Ke Rang returned to palace guard service.
entries.literal: The next year, after the Martial Emperor was cleared of blame, Ke Rang again entered palace night duty.

entries.zh: 黃巢犯闕，僖宗幸蜀，克讓時守潼關，為賊所敗，以部下六七騎伏於南山佛寺，夜為山僧所害。
entries.en: When Huang Chao stormed the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Ke Rang was holding Tong Pass. Routed by the rebels, he took refuge with only six or seven riders in a temple on South Mountain, where mountain monks killed him that night.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Ke Rang was then defending Tong Pass. Defeated by the rebels, he hid with six or seven horsemen of his command in a Buddhist temple on South Mountain, and that night was killed by mountain monks.

entries.zh: 五年正月，武皇疾篤，克寧等侍疾，垂泣辭訣。
entries.en: In the first month of the fifth year Li Keyong fell gravely ill. Ke Ning and the others kept vigil at his bedside, weeping as they bade him farewell.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the Martial Emperor's illness was grave. Ke Ning and the others attended his sickbed, weeping as they took leave.

entries.zh: 克寧曰：「王萬一不諱，後事何屬？」
entries.en: Ke Ning said, "If anything should happen to you, my lord, who is to take charge of what follows?"
entries.literal: Ke Ning said, "If Your Majesty should meet with misfortune, to whom should later affairs belong?"

entries.zh: 因召莊宗侍側，謂克寧、張承業曰：「亞子累公等。」
entries.en: He then had Emperor Zhuangzong brought to his side and said to Ke Ning and Zhang Chengye, "Yazi will be a burden on you all."
entries.literal: He then summoned Emperor Zhuangzong to attend at his side and said to Ke Ning and Zhang Chengye, "Yazi burdens you all."

entries.zh: 言終棄代。
entries.en: With those words he died.
entries.literal: When he had finished speaking he passed from this generation.

entries.zh: 將發哀，克寧紀綱軍府，中外無嘩。
entries.en: As mourning was proclaimed, Ke Ning took command of the military government, and neither within the yamen nor outside it was there any disturbance.
entries.literal: When mourning was about to be proclaimed, Ke Ning commanded the military government, and within and without there was no uproar.

entries.zh: 初，武皇獎勵軍戎，多畜庶孽，衣服禮秩如嫡者六七輩，比之嗣王，年齒又長，各有部曲，朝夕聚謀，皆欲為亂。
entries.en: Li Keyong had long rewarded his officers by raising many sons by concubines. Six or seven of them were dressed and honored like legitimate heirs. They were older than the designated successor and each commanded his own following. Day and night they met to plot rebellion.
entries.literal: Earlier the Martial Emperor, rewarding military service, had raised many sons by concubines. Six or seven were treated in dress and ritual rank like legitimate heirs. Compared with the heir, they were also older in years. Each had his own following; morning and evening they gathered to plot, all wishing to make trouble.

entries.zh: 莊宗英察，懼及於禍，將嗣位，讓克寧曰：「兒年孤稚，未通庶政，雖承遺命，恐未能彈壓大事。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was sharp-witted and feared for his life. As he was about to succeed, he offered the position to Ke Ning, saying, "I am young and alone, with no experience of government. Though I have my father's last command, I doubt I can hold the great affairs together.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was keen and perceptive and feared disaster. About to succeed to the throne, he yielded to Ke Ning, saying, "Your servant is young and alone, ignorant of common administration. Though I receive the final command, I fear I cannot suppress great affairs.

entries.zh: 季父勳德俱高，眾情推伏，且請製置軍府，候兒有立，聽季父處分。」
entries.en: Your merit and standing are high, and everyone looks to you. Please take charge of the military government for now. When I am fit to rule, I will leave everything to you, uncle."
entries.literal: Uncle's merit and virtue are both high, and public sentiment defers to you. I beg you to take charge of the military government. When your servant is established, let Uncle decide as he will."

entries.zh: 克寧曰：「亡兄遺命，屬在我兒，孰敢異議者！
entries.en: Ke Ning replied, "My late brother's last command placed everything in my nephew's hands. Who would dare object!
entries.literal: Ke Ning said, "My late brother's final command entrusted affairs to my son. Who would dare raise objection!

entries.zh: 兒但嗣世，中外之事，何憂不辦。」
entries.en: Nephew, take the succession. Affairs within and without the realm will be managed—have no fear of that."
entries.literal: Son, simply succeed to the inheritance. As for affairs within and without, what worry that they cannot be managed."

entries.zh: 視事之日，率先拜賀。
entries.en: On the day Zhuangzong took office, Ke Ning was the first to bow in congratulation.
entries.literal: On the day he assumed office, Ke Ning was first to bow in congratulation.

entries.zh: 莊宗嗣位，軍民政事，一切委之，權柄既重，趣向者多附之。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong succeeded, he entrusted all military and civil affairs to Ke Ning. As Ke Ning's power grew, ambitious men flocked to his side.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded, military and civil affairs were wholly entrusted to him. Once his authority was weighty, many who sought advancement attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 李存顥者，以陰計幹克寧曰：「兄亡弟及，古今舊事，委父拜侄，理所未安，富貴功名，當宜自立，天與不取，後悔無及。」
entries.en: Li Cunhao secretly urged Ke Ning, saying, "When the elder brother dies the younger brother succeeds—that is the old way of the world. For an uncle to bow to his nephew is unnatural. You should seize fortune and rank for yourself. If heaven offers and you refuse, you will regret it when it is too late."
entries.literal: Li Cunhao, by secret stratagem, importuned Ke Ning, saying, "When the elder brother dies the younger succeeds—an ancient precedent. For an uncle to yield to a nephew and bow to him is by reason unsettling. Wealth, honor, and achievement should be seized for oneself. Heaven gives and one does not take—later there will be no remorse in time."

entries.zh: 克寧曰：「公毋得不祥之言，
entries.en: Ke Ning said, "Do not speak such ill-omened words!
entries.literal: Ke Ning said, "Sir, do not speak such ill-omened words!

entries.zh: 我家世立功三代，父慈子孝，天下知名，苟吾兄山河有托，我亦何求！
entries.en: Our house has served with distinction for three generations, father and sons loving and filial, known throughout the realm. If my brother's heir holds the realm in trust, what more could I want!
entries.literal: In our house merit has been achieved for three generations; father is kind and sons filial, renowned throughout the realm. If my brother has the realm entrusted to him, what more do I seek!

entries.zh: 公無復言，必斬爾首以徇。」
entries.en: Say no more of this, or I shall behead you as a warning to others."
entries.literal: Sir, speak no more of this, or I shall certainly behead you as a warning."

entries.zh: 克寧雖慈愛因心，而日為凶徒惑亂。
entries.en: Though Ke Ning was by nature loving and kind, day by day the conspirators led him further astray.
entries.literal: Though Ke Ning was by nature loving and kind, day by day he was confused and led astray by wicked men.

entries.zh: 群凶之妻復以此言幹克寧妻孟夫人，說激百端，夫人懼事泄及禍，屢讓克寧，由是愈惑。
entries.en: The conspirators' wives used the same arguments on Ke Ning's wife, Lady Meng, pressing her from every angle. Fearing exposure and ruin, she repeatedly urged Ke Ning to act, and he grew only more unsettled.
entries.literal: The wives of the wicked men again used these words to importune Lady Meng, Ke Ning's wife, urging her with every sort of argument. The lady feared the affair would leak out and bring disaster, and repeatedly reproached Ke Ning, whereby he became all the more confused.

entries.zh: 會克寧因事殺都虞候李存質，又請兼領大同節度，以蔚、朔為屬郡，又數怒監軍張承業、李存璋；
entries.en: Ke Ning then killed the chief controller Li Cunzhi on a pretext, asked to take the Datong commission as well with Wei and Shuo as subordinate prefectures, and repeatedly provoked the army supervisors Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang;
entries.literal: Then Ke Ning, on a pretext, killed the chief controller Li Cunzhi, also requested to hold concurrently the military commission of Datong with Wei and Shuo as subordinate prefectures, and repeatedly angered the army supervisors Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang;

entries.zh: 由是知其有貳。
entries.en: and from this they knew he was turning disloyal.
entries.literal: thereby they knew he was disloyal.

entries.zh: 近臣史敬鎔素與存顥善，盡知其事。
entries.en: The close attendant Shi Jingrong was an old friend of Cunhao's and knew the whole plot.
entries.literal: The close attendant Shi Jingrong had long been on good terms with Cunhao and knew the whole affair.

entries.zh: 敬鎔告貞簡太后曰：「存顥與管內太保陰圖叛亂，俟嗣王過其第即擒之，並太后子母，欲送於汴州。
entries.en: Jingrong told Empress Dowager Zhenjian, "Cunhao and the circuit grand guardian are secretly plotting rebellion. They mean to seize the heir when he passes their residence, and send you and your son to Bianzhou as well.
entries.literal: Jingrong reported to Empress Dowager Zhenjian, saying, "Cunhao and the circuit grand guardian within the command are secretly plotting rebellion. When the heir passes their residence they will seize him, and together with the Empress Dowager mother and son they intend to send them to Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 竊發有日矣。」
entries.en: The rising is only days away."
entries.literal: Their secret rising is only days away."

entries.zh: 莊宗召張承業、李存璋謂曰：「季父所為如此，無猶子之情，骨肉不可自相魚肉，吾即避路，則禍亂不作矣。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong summoned Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang and said, "My uncle has acted as though he felt no bond between us. Kin must not tear one another apart. I will step aside at once, and the realm will be spared this disaster."
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong summoned Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang and said, "Uncle's conduct is such that he has no feeling of an uncle toward his nephew. Flesh and bone must not devour one another. I shall at once yield the way, and then calamity and disorder will not arise."

entries.zh: 承業曰：「老夫親承遺托，言猶在耳。
entries.en: Chengye replied, "I received your father's last charge in person, and his words are still in my ears.
entries.literal: Chengye said, "This old man personally received the final entrustment; the words are still in my ears.

entries.zh: 存顥輩欲以太原降賊，王乃何路求生？
entries.en: Cunhao and his fellows mean to hand Taiyuan over to the enemy. What path to safety remains for you, my lord?
entries.literal: Cunhao and his fellows wish to surrender Taiyuan to the rebels. By what road, Your Majesty, will you seek to live?

entries.zh: 不即討除，亡無日矣。」
entries.en: Unless you strike at once, ruin will come within days."
entries.literal: If you do not immediately suppress and eliminate them, destruction will come within days."

entries.zh: 因令吳珙、存璋為之備。
entries.en: He then ordered Wu Gong and Cunzhang to prepare.
entries.literal: He then ordered Wu Gong and Cunzhang to make preparations.

entries.zh: 二月二十日，會諸將於府第，擒存顥、克寧於坐。
entries.en: On the twentieth day of the second month he assembled his generals at the residence and seized Cunhao and Ke Ning where they sat.
entries.literal: On the twentieth day of the second month he assembled the generals at the prefectural residence and seized Cunhao and Ke Ning in their seats.

entries.zh: 莊宗垂泣數之曰：「兒初以軍府讓季父，季父不忍棄先人遺命。
entries.en: Zhuangzong wept as he rebuked them, saying, "I first offered the military government to you, uncle, and you would not set aside my father's last command.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong, weeping, reproached them, saying, "Your servant at first yielded the military government to Uncle. Uncle could not bear to abandon our forefather's final command.

entries.zh: 今已事定，復欲以兒子母投畀豺虎，季父何忍此心！」
entries.en: Now that all is settled, you would cast me and my mother to the wolves. Uncle, how could you bring yourself to this!"
entries.literal: Now that affairs are settled, you again wish to cast your servant and his mother to wolves and tigers. Uncle, how can you bear such a heart!"

entries.zh: 克寧泣對曰：「蓋讒夫交構，吾復何言！」
entries.en: Ke Ning wept in reply, "Slanderers set us at odds. What more can I say!"
entries.literal: Ke Ning wept in reply, saying, "It is all slanderers weaving plots together. What more can I say!"

entries.zh: 是日，與存顥俱伏法。
entries.en: That day he and Cunhao were both executed.
entries.literal: That day he and Cunhao were both executed according to law.

entries.zh: 克寧仁而無斷，故及於禍。
entries.en: Ke Ning was kind-hearted but indecisive, and so came to ruin.
entries.literal: Ke Ning was benevolent but lacked resolution, and therefore met with disaster.

entries.zh: 〈（案《新唐書·宰相世係表》：嗣昭，國昌有子四人：克恭、克儉、克用、克柔。
entries.en: (According to the 《New Book of Tang·Tables of Chancellor Lineages》: Sizhao—Guochang had four sons: Ke Gong, Ke Jian, Ke Yong, and Ke Rou.
entries.literal: (According to the 《New Book of Tang·Tables of Chancellor Lineages》: Sizhao—Guochang had four sons: Ke Gong, Ke Jian, Ke Yong, and Ke Rou.

entries.zh: 薛史《李嗣昭傳》云：武皇母弟代州刺史克柔之假子也。
entries.en: The Xue History 《Biography of Li Sizhao》 says he was the adopted son of Li Keyong's younger uterine brother Ke Rou, prefect of Daizhou.
entries.literal: The Xue History 《Biography of Li Sizhao》 says: He was the adopted son of the Martial Emperor's younger brother by the same mother, Ke Rou, prefect of Daizhou.

entries.zh: 是克柔為武皇母弟。
entries.en: Thus Ke Rou was Li Keyong's younger uterine brother.
entries.literal: Thus Ke Rou was the Martial Emperor's younger brother by the same mother.

entries.zh: 《新唐書·沙陀傳》：武皇有弟克勤，《通鑒》引《紀年錄》有兄克儉，而薛史俱無傳，疑有闕文。）〉
entries.en: The 《New Book of Tang·Biography of the Shatuo》 records a younger brother Ke Qin. The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 cites the 《Chronicle Record》 as mentioning an elder brother Ke Jian, yet the Xue History has biographies for neither; text may be missing.)〉
entries.literal: The 《New Book of Tang·Biography of the Shatuo》: The Martial Emperor had a younger brother Ke Qin. The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 cites the 《Chronicle Record》 as having an elder brother Ke Jian, yet the Xue History has biographies for neither; it is suspected that text is missing.)〉

entries.zh: 史臣曰：昔武皇發跡於陰山，莊宗肇基於河朔，雖奄有天下，而享國日淺，眷言枝屬，空秀棣華，固未及推帝堯敦敘之恩，廣成王封建之義。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: The Martial Emperor rose from the Yin Mountains and Emperor Zhuangzong founded his rule in Hebei. Though they briefly held the realm, their dynasties were short-lived. Their kinsmen bloomed like catalpa blossoms yet bore no fruit—they never attained Emperor Yao's generous ordering of kin or broadly extended King Cheng's principles of enfeoffment.
entries.literal: The historiographer remarks: In former times the Martial Emperor rose from the Yin Mountains and Emperor Zhuangzong founded his rule in Hebei. Though they briefly held all under Heaven, their enjoyment of the realm was brief. Turning affection to the branch kin, the flowering of the catalpa alone was empty show. They indeed did not reach the point of extending Emperor Yao's generous ordering of kin, or of broadly extending King Cheng's principle of enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 自克讓而下，不獲就魯、衛之封，懋間、平之德也。
entries.en: From Ke Rang downward, none received fiefs like the states of Lu and Wei, nor did they cultivate the virtue of the Princes of Hejian and Dongping.
entries.literal: From Ke Rang downward, they did not obtain enfeoffment like Lu and Wei, nor did they display the virtue of Jian and Ping (the Princes of Hejian and Dongping).

entries.zh: 況夭橫相繼，亦良可悲哉！
entries.en: To make matters worse, violent early deaths followed one after another—a truly lamentable fate!
entries.literal: Moreover, untimely violent deaths followed one upon another—truly a matter for deep grief!

entries.zh: 克讓既死，紀綱渾進通冒刃獲免，歸於黃巢。
entries.en: After Ke Rang's death, his officer Hun Jintong fought through the blades and survived, then went over to Huang Chao's side.
entries.literal: After Ke Rang died, his commander Hun Jintong braved the blades and escaped, going over to Huang Chao.

entries.zh: 中和二年冬，武皇入關討賊，屯沙苑。
entries.en: In the winter of Zhonghe 2, Li Keyong marched through the passes against the rebels and encamped at Shayuan.
entries.literal: In the winter of the second year of Zhonghe, the Martial Emperor entered the passes to attack the rebels and encamped at Shayuan.

entries.zh: 黃巢遣使米重威齎賂修好，因送渾進通至，兼擒送害克讓僧十人。
entries.en: Huang Chao sent Mi Chongwei with gifts to sue for peace, returned Hun Jintong with the embassy, and also delivered up the ten monks who had murdered Ke Rang.
entries.literal: Huang Chao sent the envoy Mi Chongwei bearing gifts to seek peace, and with him sent Hun Jintong back, together with the ten monks who had killed Ke Rang, seized and delivered up.

entries.zh: 武皇燔偽詔，還其使，盡誅諸僧，為克讓發哀行服，悲慟久之。
entries.en: Li Keyong burned Huang Chao's forged edict, sent the envoy away, had all the monks executed, and for Ke Rang observed mourning and wore funeral dress, grieving for a long while.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor burned the false edict, sent the envoy back, executed all the monks, and for Ke Rang held mourning and wore mourning garments, grieving deeply for a long time.

entries.zh: 克修，字崇遠，武皇從父弟也。
entries.en: Ke Xiu, styled Chongyuan, was Li Keyong's younger cousin.
entries.literal: Ke Xiu, styled Chongyuan, was the Martial Emperor's younger cousin.

entries.zh: 父德成，初為天寧軍使，從獻祖討龐勳，以功授朔州刺史。
entries.en: His father Decheng had first served as military commissioner of Tianning. He followed the Offering Ancestor against Pang Xun and, for his service, was made prefect of Shuozhou.
entries.literal: His father Decheng was first military commissioner of Tianning. He followed the Offering Ancestor in the campaign against Pang Xun and, for merit, was appointed prefect of Shuozhou.

entries.zh: 克修少便弓馬，從父征討，所至立功，武皇節制雁門，以克修為奉誠軍使，從入關為前鋒，破黃揆於華陰，敗尚讓於梁田坡，蹙黃巢於光順門，每戰皆捷，勇懾諸軍。
entries.en: Ke Xiu was skilled with bow and horse from youth. On his father's campaigns he distinguished himself wherever he fought. When Li Keyong took command of Yanmen, he appointed Ke Xiu commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. Marching into the passes as vanguard, Ke Xiu defeated Huang Kui at Huayin, routed Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and drove Huang Chao back at Guangshun Gate. He won every engagement, and his boldness overawed the other armies.
entries.literal: Ke Xiu from youth was adept with bow and horse. Following his father on campaigns, wherever he went he achieved merit. When the Martial Emperor held military authority over Yanmen, he made Ke Xiu commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. Following him into the passes as vanguard, he defeated Huang Kui at Huayin, routed Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and pressed Huang Chao at Guangshun Gate. In every battle he was victorious, and his courage awed all the armies.

entries.zh: 賊平，以功檢校刑部尚書，為左營軍使。
entries.en: After the rebels were crushed, he was made acting minister of justice and commander of the Left Camp Army for his achievements.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for merit he was made acting minister of justice and commander of the Left Camp Army.

entries.zh: 其年十月，潞州牙將安居受來乞師，請復昭義軍，武皇遣大將賀公雅、李筠、安金俊等以兵從。
entries.en: In the tenth month of that year, the Lu garrison officer An Jushou came to request aid in restoring the Zhaoyi command. Li Keyong sent the senior generals He Gongya, Li Jun, An Jinjun, and others with an army in support.
entries.literal: That year in the tenth month, the Lu prefecture garrison officer An Jushou came to request troops, asking to restore the Zhaoyi army. The Martial Emperor sent the great generals He Gongya, Li Jun, An Jinjun, and others with troops to follow.

entries.zh: 與孟方立戰於銅鞮，不利，武皇乃令克修將兵繼進。
entries.en: The allied force fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi without success, so Li Keyong ordered Ke Xiu to advance with reinforcements.
entries.literal: They fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi with an unfavorable outcome, and the Martial Emperor then ordered Ke Xiu to lead troops forward in succession.

entries.zh: 是月，平潞州，斬其刺史李殷銳，乃表克修為昭義節度使。
entries.en: That month Luzhou was taken, its prefect Li Yinrui was executed, and Ke Xiu was recommended for appointment as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: That month they pacified Luzhou, beheaded its prefect Li Yinrui, and then memorialized to appoint Ke Xiu military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 光啟二年九月，克修出師山東，收復邢、洺。
entries.en: In the ninth month of Guangqi 2, Ke Xiu took the field east of the Taihang range and recovered Xing and Ming.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Guangqi, Ke Xiu marched east of the mountains and recovered Xing and Ming.

entries.zh: 十一月，拔故鎮。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he took Guzhen.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he captured Guzhen.

entries.zh: 孟方立遣將呂臻來援，戰於焦崗，大敗之，擒呂臻，俘斬萬計，進拔武安、臨洺諸屬縣，乘勝進圍邢州。
entries.en: Meng Fangli sent Lü Zhen to the rescue. Ke Xiu met him at Jiaogang and won a crushing victory, capturing Lü Zhen and killing or taking prisoner tens of thousands. He then seized Wu'an, Linming, and the other subordinate counties and, riding the momentum, laid siege to Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Meng Fangli sent the general Lü Zhen to relieve him. They fought at Jiaogang and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Lü Zhen. Captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands. Advancing, they took Wu'an, Linming, and other subordinate counties, and pressing the victory moved to besiege Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 方立求援於鎮州，王鎔出師三萬援之，克修軍退。
entries.en: Fangli appealed to Zhenzhou for help. Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army fell back.
entries.literal: Fangli sought aid from Zhenzhou; Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army withdrew.

entries.zh: 及李罕之來歸，武皇授以澤州刺史，與克修合勢進攻河陽，連歲出師，以苦懷、孟。
entries.en: When Li Hanzhi defected to Li Keyong, he was made prefect of Zezhou and joined Ke Xiu in a combined offensive against Heyang. Campaigning year after year, they wore down the Huai and Meng factions.
entries.literal: When Li Hanzhi came over to our side, the Martial Emperor appointed him prefect of Zezhou. Together with Ke Xiu he combined forces to attack Heyang, campaigning year after year to wear down Huai and Meng.

entries.zh: 文德元年十月，孟方立遣將奚忠信將兵三萬襲我遼州，克修設伏於遼之東山，大敗賊軍，擒忠信以獻。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Wende 1, Meng Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men to raid Liaozhou. Ke Xiu laid an ambush on East Mountain and routed the enemy, capturing Zhongxin and sending him to headquarters.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Wende, Meng Fangli sent the general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to raid our Liaozhou. Ke Xiu set an ambush on East Mountain of Liao and inflicted a great defeat on the rebel army, capturing Zhongxin and presenting him.

entries.zh: 龍紀元年，武皇大舉以伐邢、洺，及班師，因撫封於上黨。
entries.en: In Longji 1, Li Keyong mounted a major campaign against Xing and Ming. When the army returned, he rewarded and enfeoffed his followers at Shangdang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longji, the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign against Xing and Ming. When the army returned, he therefore bestowed rewards and enfeoffments at Shangdang.

entries.zh: 克修性儉嗇，不事華靡，供帳饔膳，品數簡陋。
entries.en: Ke Xiu was frugal by nature and shunned display. His quarters and table were spare and plain.
entries.literal: Ke Xiu by nature was frugal and sparing, not given to luxury. His furnishings and meals were few and plain in kind and number.

entries.zh: 武皇怒其菲薄，笞而詬之，克修慚憤發疾；
entries.en: Li Keyong, angry at his austerity, had him flogged and berated him. Ke Xiu, mortified and embittered, fell ill;
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor, angered at his meagerness, flogged and reviled him. Ke Xiu, ashamed and resentful, fell ill;

entries.zh: 明年三月，卒於潞之府第，時年三十一。
entries.en: and in the third month of the following year he died at the Lu prefectural residence, aged thirty-one.
entries.literal: in the third month of the following year he died in the prefectural residence at Lu, aged thirty-one.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，追贈太師。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to the throne, Ke Xiu was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 克寧，武皇之季弟也。
entries.en: Ke Ning was Li Keyong's youngest brother.
entries.literal: Ke Ning was the Martial Emperor's youngest brother.

entries.zh: 初從起雲中，為奉誠軍使，赫連鐸之攻黃花城也，克寧奉武皇及諸弟登城，血戰三日，力盡備竭，殺賊萬計。
entries.en: He had followed Li Keyong from the first rising in Yunzhong and served as commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. When Helian Duo attacked Huanghua Fort, Ke Ning helped Li Keyong and his brothers onto the walls. For three days they fought hand to hand until strength and supplies were spent, killing rebels by the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: From the first he followed the rise in Yunzhong and was commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. When Helian Duo attacked Huanghua Fort, Ke Ning attended the Martial Emperor and his brothers onto the walls. For three days they fought in blood; strength and supplies were exhausted, and rebels slain numbered in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 燕軍之攻蔚州，克寧昆仲嬰城拒敵，晝夜輟寢食者旬餘。
entries.en: When the Yan army besieged Weizhou, Ke Ning and his brothers held the city and went more than ten days and nights with scarcely any sleep or food.
entries.literal: When the Yan army attacked Weizhou, Ke Ning and his brothers held the city and resisted the enemy, going more than ten days and nights without sleep or food.

entries.zh: 後從達靼入關，逐黃寇。
entries.en: Later he marched through the passes with the Tatar allies and drove off Huang Chao's forces.
entries.literal: Later he followed the Tatars into the passes and drove off the Huang bandits.

entries.zh: 凡征行無不衛從，於昆弟之間，最推仁孝，小心恭謹，武皇尤友愛之。
entries.en: On every campaign he marched at Li Keyong's side. Among the brothers he was the most noted for kindness and filial devotion, careful and deferential in manner, and Li Keyong cherished him above the rest.
entries.literal: On every campaign he was never absent as escort. Among the brothers he was most esteemed for benevolence and filial piety, careful and reverent, and the Martial Emperor especially cherished him.

entries.zh: 及鎮太原，授遼州刺史，累至雲州防禦使。
entries.en: When Li Keyong held Taiyuan, Ke Ning was made prefect of Liaozhou and later promoted to defender of Yunzhou.
entries.literal: When he held Taiyuan he was appointed prefect of Liaozhou and was promoted in succession to defender of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 乾寧初，改忻州刺史，從入關討王行瑜，充馬步軍都將，以功授檢校司徒。
entries.en: Early in the Qianning era he was made prefect of Xinzhou. He followed Li Keyong through the passes against Wang Xingyu as commander-in-chief of horse and foot and, for his service, was appointed acting minister of education.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he was transferred to prefect of Xinzhou. Following the entry into the passes to attack Wang Xingyu, he served as commander-in-chief of horse and foot and, for merit, was appointed acting minister of education.

entries.zh: 天祐初，授內外都製置、管內蕃漢都知兵馬使、檢校太保，充振武節度使，凡軍政皆決於克寧。
entries.en: Early in the Tianyou era he was made overall commissioner for inner and outer affairs, commander of all Tangut and Chinese forces in the circuit, acting grand guardian, and military commissioner of Zhenwu. Military and civil affairs alike were left to Ke Ning's decision.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was appointed overall commissioner for inner and outer affairs, commander of all Tangut and Chinese military forces within the circuit, acting grand guardian, and military commissioner of Zhenwu. All military and civil affairs were decided by Ke Ning.

entries.zh: 克恭，武皇之諸弟也。
entries.en: Ke Gong was one of Li Keyong's younger brothers.
entries.literal: Ke Gong was one of the Martial Emperor's younger brothers.

entries.zh: 龍紀中，為決勝軍使。
entries.en: During the Longji era he served as commissioner of the Decisive Victory Army.
entries.literal: During Longji he was commissioner of the Decisive Victory Army.

entries.zh: 大順初，潞帥李克修卒，克恭代為昭義節度使。
entries.en: Early in the Dashun era, after the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, Ke Gong succeeded him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dazhun, the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, and Ke Gong replaced him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 性驕橫不法，未閑軍政。
entries.en: He was arrogant, lawless, and wholly unversed in military administration.
entries.literal: By nature he was arrogant, overbearing, and lawless, and unversed in military administration.

entries.zh: 潞人素便克修之簡正，惡克恭之恣縱，又以克修非罪暴卒，人士離心。
entries.en: The people of Lu had long valued Ke Xiu's plain, upright rule and resented Ke Gong's excesses. Ke Xiu's sudden death, though he was innocent of wrongdoing, also alienated the gentry and commoners.
entries.literal: The people of Lu had long been accustomed to Ke Xiu's simplicity and rectitude and hated Ke Gong's wanton indulgence. Moreover, because Ke Xiu had died violently though guiltless, officials and commoners lost heart.

entries.zh: 時武皇初定邢、洺三州，將有事於河朔，大搜軍實。
entries.en: Li Keyong had just secured Xing, Ming, and the third prefecture and was preparing for operations in Hebei, so he made a sweeping levy of military supplies.
entries.literal: At the time the Martial Emperor had newly pacified the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and another, was about to undertake operations in Hebei, and made a great levy of military stores.

entries.zh: 潞州有後院軍，兵之雄勁者，克恭選其五百人獻於武皇，軍使安居受惜其兵。
entries.en: Lu maintained a Rear Court Army of its toughest troops. Ke Gong selected five hundred of them and sent them to Li Keyong. The army commissioner An Jushou resented losing his best men.
entries.literal: Lu had a Rear Court Army of the strongest troops. Ke Gong selected five hundred of them and presented them to the Martial Emperor. The army commissioner An Jushou regretted the loss of his troops.

entries.zh: 不悅。
entries.en: He was deeply displeased.
entries.literal: He was displeased.

entries.zh: 克恭令裨校李元審、安建、紀綱、馮霸部送太原，行次銅鞮縣，馮霸劫眾謀叛，殺都將劉杲、縣令戴勞謙，循山而南，比及沁水，有眾三千。
entries.en: Ke Gong ordered the subordinate officers Li Yuanshen, An Jian, the escort officers, and Feng Ba to march the detachment to Taiyuan. At Tongdi county Feng Ba incited a mutiny, killed the commander Liu Gao and the magistrate Dai Laoqian, and led his men south along the mountains until, by the time they reached Qinshui, he had three thousand followers.
entries.literal: Ke Gong ordered the subordinate officers Li Yuanshen, An Jian, the commanders, and Feng Ba to escort them to Taiyuan. When they reached Tongdi county, Feng Ba incited the troops to rebel, killed the commander Liu Gao and the magistrate Dai Laoqian, followed the mountains southward, and by the time they reached Qinshui had three thousand followers.

entries.zh: 武皇令李元審將兵擊之，與霸戰於沁水，不利，元審戰傷，收軍於潞。
entries.en: Li Keyong ordered Li Yuanshen to attack them. Yuanshen fought Feng Ba at Qinshui without success, was wounded, and withdrew to Lu.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor ordered Li Yuanshen to lead troops against him. He fought Feng Ba at Qinshui with an unfavorable outcome; Yuanshen was wounded in battle and withdrew the army to Lu.

entries.zh: 五月十五日，克恭視元審於孔目吏劉崇之第。
entries.en: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month Ke Gong went to visit the wounded Yuanshen at the home of the clerical officer Liu Chong.
entries.literal: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month, Ke Gong visited Yuanshen at the residence of the clerical officer Liu Chong.

entries.zh: 是日，州將安居受引兵仗攻克恭，因風縱火，克恭、元審並遇害，州民推居受為留後。
entries.en: That same day the prefectural officer An Jushou led armed men against Ke Gong, set fires with the wind at his back, and killed both Ke Gong and Yuanshen. The people of the prefecture made Jushou acting commissioner.
entries.literal: That day the prefectural officer An Jushou led armed troops to attack and overcome Ke Gong. Taking advantage of the wind he set fires. Ke Gong and Yuanshen were both killed. The people of the prefecture installed Jushou as acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 初，孟方立之亂，居受以澤、潞歸於武皇，至是孟遷以邢、洺納降，復任為牙將，居受懼其圖己，乃叛，殺克恭以結汴人。
entries.en: During Meng Fangli's rebellion Jushou had surrendered Ze and Lu to Li Keyong. Now Meng Qian surrendered Xing and Ming and was reappointed a garrison officer. Fearing that Meng Qian would move against him, Jushou rebelled, killed Ke Gong, and sought an alliance with the Liang.
entries.literal: Earlier, during Meng Fangli's rebellion, Jushou had surrendered Ze and Lu to the Martial Emperor. Now Meng Qian surrendered Xing and Ming and was reappointed a garrison officer. Jushou feared he would plot against him, therefore rebelled and killed Ke Gong to ally with the Bian.

entries.zh: 居受遣人召馮霸於沁水，霸不受命。
entries.en: Jushou sent men to summon Feng Ba at Qinshui, but Feng Ba refused to obey.
entries.literal: Jushou sent men to summon Feng Ba at Qinshui, but Ba refused the order.

entries.zh: 居受懼，將奔歸朝廷，至長子，為野人所殺，傳首馮霸軍。
entries.en: Terrified, Jushou set out to flee to the Tang court. At Changzi he was killed by local bandits, and his head was sent to Feng Ba's camp.
entries.literal: Jushou was afraid and was about to flee back to the court. When he reached Changzi he was killed by local bandits, and his head was sent to Feng Ba's army.

entries.zh: 霸乃引軍據潞州，自稱留後，求援於汴。
entries.en: Feng Ba then seized Luzhou, declared himself acting commissioner, and appealed to the Liang for help.
entries.literal: Ba then led his army to occupy Luzhou, styled himself acting commissioner, and sought aid from Bian.

entries.zh: 武皇令康君立討之，汴將葛從周來援霸。
entries.en: Li Keyong ordered Kang Junli to suppress him. The Liang general Ge Congzhou marched to Feng Ba's relief.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor ordered Kang Junli to attack him. The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to relieve Ba.

entries.zh: 九月，李存孝急攻潞州，汴軍夜遁，獲霸等誅之，武皇乃以康君立為昭義節度使。
entries.en: In the ninth month Li Cunxiao pressed the attack on Luzhou. The Liang army fled by night, Feng Ba and his fellows were captured and executed, and Li Keyong appointed Kang Junli military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Li Cunxiao pressed the attack on Luzhou. The Bian army fled by night. Ba and the others were captured and executed, and the Martial Emperor then appointed Kang Junli military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 嗣肱，少有膽略，屢立戰功，夾城之役，從周德威為前鋒。
entries.en: Sigu showed daring and strategic sense from youth and won repeated distinction in battle. In the Jiacheng campaign he served under Zhou Dewei as vanguard.
entries.literal: Sigu from youth had daring and resourcefulness and repeatedly achieved military merit. In the Jiacheng campaign he followed Zhou Dewei as vanguard.

entries.zh: 時兄嗣弼為昭義副使，與嗣昭守城，兄弟內外奮戰，忠力威壯，感動三軍。
entries.en: His elder brother Sibi was then deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi and, with Sizhao, held the city. The brothers fought fiercely inside and out, their loyalty and prowess so imposing that they stirred the whole army.
entries.literal: At the time his elder brother Sibi was deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi; with Sizhao he defended the city. The brothers fought fiercely within and without, their loyalty and strength majestic and inspiring, moving all three armies.

entries.zh: 潞圍既解，以功授檢校左僕射，入為三城巡檢，知衙內事。
entries.en: After the siege of Lu was raised, he was made acting left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat for his service. He entered the capital as inspector of the Three Cities and took charge of inner yamen affairs.
entries.literal: When the siege of Lu was lifted, for merit he was appointed acting left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat. He entered the capital as inspector of the Three Cities and managed affairs within the yamen.

entries.zh: 天祐七年，周德威援靈、夏，党項阻道，音驛不通。
entries.en: In Tianyou 7, Zhou Dewei marched to relieve Ling and Xia. The Tangut blocked the route, and no word came through the courier network.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei went to relieve Ling and Xia. The Tangut blocked the road, and courier communications ceased.

entries.zh: 嗣肱奉命自麟州渡河，應接德威，與党項轉戰數十里，合德威軍。
entries.en: Sigu was ordered to cross from Linzhou and link up with Dewei. After fighting the Tangut over several tens of li, he joined Dewei's force.
entries.literal: Sigu received orders to cross the river from Linzhou and link up with Dewei. Fighting the Tangut over several tens of li, he joined Dewei's army.

entries.zh: 柏鄉之戰，嗣肱為馬步都虞候。
entries.en: At Baixiang, Sigu served as chief controller of horse and foot.
entries.literal: In the battle of Baixiang, Sigu served as chief controller of horse and foot.

entries.zh: 明年，從莊宗會朱友謙於猗氏，改教練使，與存審援河中，敗汴軍於胡壁堡，獲將龐讓。
entries.en: The following year he accompanied Emperor Zhuangzong to meet Zhu Youqian at Yishi and was made training commissioner. With Cunshen he marched to relieve Hezhong, defeated the Liang army at Hubi Fort, and captured the general Pang Rang.
entries.literal: The next year he followed Emperor Zhuangzong to meet Zhu Youqian at Yishi, was transferred to training commissioner, and with Cunshen went to relieve Hezhong, defeating the Bian army at Hubi Fort and capturing the general Pang Rang.

entries.zh: 十年，與存審屯趙州，擊汴人於觀津。
entries.en: In the tenth year he encamped at Zhaozhou with Cunshen and attacked the Liang forces at Guanjin.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he encamped at Zhaozhou with Cunshen and struck the Bian troops at Guanjin.

entries.zh: 時梁祖新屠棗強，其將賀德倫急攻蓚縣，率師五萬合勢營於蓚之西。
entries.en: The Liang founder had just slaughtered the population of Zaoqiang. His general He Delun was pressing the attack on Suo county and had brought fifty thousand men to encamp west of the city in a combined force.
entries.literal: At the time the Liang founder had newly massacred Zaoqiang. His general He Delun pressed the attack on Suo county and led fifty thousand men in combined strength to encamp west of Suo.

entries.zh: 嗣肱自下博率騎三百，薄晚與梁之樵芻者相雜，日既晡，入梁軍營門，諸騎相合，大噪，弧矢星發，虓闞馳突。
entries.en: Sigu led three hundred horsemen from Xiabo. Near dusk he mixed in with Liang men out gathering firewood and fodder. In the late afternoon he rode through the Liang camp gate. His horsemen closed up, raised a deafening uproar, loosed arrows in a storm, and charged roaring through the encampment.
entries.literal: Sigu led three hundred horsemen from Xiabo. Toward evening he mingled with the Liang foragers gathering firewood and fodder. After the sun had passed mid-afternoon he entered the Liang army's camp gate. The horsemen converged, raised a great clamor, arrows flew like stars, and with fierce shouts they charged and broke through.

entries.zh: 汴人不知所為，營中擾，既暝，斂騎而退。
entries.en: The Liang troops did not know what had hit them, and the camp fell into chaos. After dark he gathered his riders and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Bian men did not know what to do; the camp was thrown into disorder. When night fell, he gathered his riders and withdrew.

entries.zh: 是夜，梁祖燒營而遁，解蓚縣之圍。
entries.en: That night the Liang founder burned his camp and fled, lifting the siege of Suo.
entries.literal: That night the Liang founder burned his camp and fled, lifting the siege of Suo county.

entries.zh: 以功特授蔚州刺史、雁門以北都知兵馬使。
entries.en: For this exploit he was specially appointed prefect of Weizhou and commander of all forces north of Yanmen.
entries.literal: For merit he was specially appointed prefect of Weizhou and commander of all military forces north of Yanmen.

entries.zh: 從平劉守光。
entries.en: He took part in the campaign that brought down Liu Shouguang.
entries.literal: He followed in the pacification of Liu Shouguang.

entries.zh: 十二年，改應州刺史，累遷澤、代二州刺史、石嶺以北都知兵馬使。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he was made prefect of Yingzhou and was later promoted in turn to prefect of Ze and Dai and commander of all forces north of Shiling Pass.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou, and was promoted in succession to prefect of Ze and Dai and commander of all military forces north of Shiling.

entries.zh: 十九年，新州刺史王鬱叛入契丹。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year Wang Yu, prefect of Xinzhou, rebelled and defected to the Khitan.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, Wang Yu, prefect of Xinzhou, rebelled and went over to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 嗣肱進兵定媯、儒、武等三州，授山北都團練使。
entries.en: Sigu advanced and pacified Gui, Ru, and Wu, and was appointed regimental commissioner of the Northern Mountains.
entries.literal: Sigu advanced his troops and pacified the three prefectures of Gui, Ru, and Wu, and was appointed regimental commissioner of the Northern Mountains.

entries.zh: 二十年春，卒於新州，時年四十五。
entries.en: In the spring of the twentieth year he died at Xinzhou, aged forty-five.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he died at Xinzhou, aged forty-five.

entries.zh: 永王存霸，武皇子，莊宗第二弟，同光三年封。
entries.en: Prince Yong Cunba, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's second younger brother, received his princely title in Tongguang 3.
entries.literal: Prince Yong Cunba, son of the Martial Emperor, Emperor Zhuangzong's second younger brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

entries.zh: 莊宗敗，為軍卒所殺。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, he was killed by common soldiers.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, he was killed by soldiers.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：存霸曆昭義、天平、河中三軍節度使，居京師食俸祿而已。
entries.en: (The Ouyang History records that Cunba had served in turn as military commissioner of the Zhao-Yi, Tianping, and Hezhong circuits, living in the capital on stipend alone.
entries.literal: (The Ouyang History states: Cunba successively held the posts of military commissioner of the Zhao-Yi, Tianping, and Hezhong armies, residing in the capital and drawing salary only.

entries.zh: 趙在禮反，乃遣存霸於河中，莊宗再幸汜水，徙存霸北京留守。
entries.en: When Zhao Zaili rose in revolt, Cunba was dispatched to Hezhong. Zhuangzong returned to Si River a second time and reassigned Cunba as Protector of the Northern Capital.
entries.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, Cunba was sent to Hezhong; Emperor Zhuangzong again visited Si River and transferred Cunba to be Northern Capital Protector.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》云：李紹榮欲奔河中就永王存霸，從兵稍散，存霸亦率眾千人棄鎮奔晉陽。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Mirror adds that Li Shaorong meant to flee to Hezhong to reach Prince Yong Cunba, but his followers slowly melted away, and Cunba too abandoned his command with a thousand men and fled to Jinyang.
entries.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror states: Li Shaorong wished to flee to Hezhong to join Prince Yong Cunba; his followers gradually dispersed, and Cunba also led a thousand men in abandoning his post and fleeing to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 又云：存霸至晉陽，從兵逃散俱盡，存霸削髮僧服謁李彥超：「願為山僧，幸垂庇護。」
entries.en: The text goes on to say that by the time Cunba reached Jinyang every one of his followers had deserted him. He shaved his head, put on monastic robes, and visited Li Yanchao, saying, "I wish only to be a mountain monk; please grant me your protection."
entries.literal: It also states: When Cunba reached Jinyang his followers had all fled and scattered. Cunba shaved his head, donned monk's robes, and called on Li Yanchao: "I wish to be a mountain monk; I beg your protection."

entries.zh: 軍士爭欲殺之，彥超曰：「六相公來，當奏取進止。」
entries.en: The troops clamored to kill him, but Li Yanchao said, "The Sixth Lord has arrived; I must submit a report and await instructions."
entries.literal: The soldiers competed to kill him. Li Yanchao said: "The Sixth Lord has come; I should memorialize and await orders."

entries.zh: 軍士不聽，殺之於府門之碑下。）〉
entries.en: The soldiers refused to wait and killed him at the stele before the prefectural gate.)〉
entries.literal: The soldiers would not listen and killed him below the stele at the government gate.)〉

entries.zh: 邕王存美，武皇子，莊宗第三弟，同光三年封。
entries.en: Prince of Yong Cunmei, a son of the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong's third younger brother, received his title in Tongguang 3.
entries.literal: Prince Yong Cunmei, son of the Martial Emperor, Emperor Zhuangzong's third younger brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

entries.zh: 莊宗敗，不知所終。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, his fate was never learned.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, his end was unknown.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：存美以病風偏枯得免，居於晉陽。）〉
entries.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror notes that Cunmei was spared because wind sickness had left him half-paralyzed, and he remained at Jinyang.)〉
entries.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: Cunmei, because he suffered hemiplegia from wind disease, was spared and lived at Jinyang.)〉

entries.zh: 薛王存禮，武皇子，同光三年封。
entries.en: Prince Xue Cunli, a son of the Martial Emperor, was enfeoffed in Tongguang 3.
entries.literal: Prince Xue Cunli, son of the Martial Emperor, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

entries.zh: 莊宗敗，不知所終。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, his fate was never learned.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, his end was unknown.

entries.zh: 睦王存乂，莊宗第五弟，同光三所封。
entries.en: Prince Mu Cunyi, Zhuangzong's fifth younger brother, was enfeoffed in Tongguang 3.
entries.literal: Prince Mu Cunyi, Emperor Zhuangzong's fifth younger brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

entries.zh: 〈（案，以下原闕。）〉
entries.en: (Note: the original text below this point is missing.)〉
entries.literal: (Examination shows the original text is missing below.)〉

entries.zh: 曆鄜州節度使，後以郭崇韜婿為莊宗所殺。
entries.en: He had served as military commissioner of Fuzhou and was later executed by Zhuangzong for being Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.
entries.literal: He successively served as military commissioner of Fuzhou and was later killed by Emperor Zhuangzong because he was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：莊宗異母弟存乂，以郭崇韜女婿伏誅。
entries.en: (Beimeng Suoyan records that Cunyi, Zhuangzong's half-brother, was put to death for being married to Guo Chongtao's daughter.
