entries.literal: (Beimeng Suoyan states: Cunyi, Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brother by a different mother, was executed because he was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.

entries.zh: 先是，郭崇韜既誅之後，朝野駭惋，議論紛然。
entries.en: After Guo Chongtao's execution, the court and the streets alike were shaken with horror and regret, and debate raged on every side.
entries.literal: Earlier, after Guo Chongtao had been executed, court and commoners alike were shaken and aggrieved, and opinion was in uproar.

entries.zh: 莊宗令閹人察訪外事，言存乂於諸將坐上訴郭氏之無罪，其言怨望。
entries.en: Zhuangzong sent eunuchs to spy on affairs beyond the palace, and they reported that seated among the generals Cunyi had argued for the Guo family's innocence in tones full of resentment.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong ordered eunuchs to investigate external affairs, and they reported that at a gathering of generals Cunyi, seated among them, pleaded Guo's innocence, speaking with resentment.

entries.zh: 又於妖術人楊千郎家飲酒聚會，攘臂而泣。
entries.en: He had also been seen drinking with friends at the home of the wonder-worker Yang Qianlang, where he rolled up his sleeves and wept aloud.
entries.literal: Furthermore, at drinking gatherings at the house of the sorcerer Yang Qianlang he rolled up his sleeves and wept.

entries.zh: 楊千郎者，魏州賤民，自言得墨子術於婦翁，能役使陰物，帽下召食物果實之類。
entries.en: Yang Qianlang was a common man of Weizhou who claimed to have learned Mozi's techniques from his father-in-law and could command spirits of the yin realm: food, fruit, and other provisions would appear from under his cap.
entries.literal: Yang Qianlang was a lowly man of Weizhou who claimed to have received Mozi's arts from his wife's father and could command yin spirits; beneath his hat he could summon food and fruit and the like.

entries.zh: 又蒱爪博必勝，人有拳握之物，以法必取。
entries.en: In finger-wrestling and dice games he never lost, and whatever a man clenched in his fist, Yang could always draw forth by his arts.
entries.literal: Furthermore, in finger-guessing and gambling games he was sure to win; if someone held something clenched in his fist, by his arts he was sure to take it.

entries.zh: 又說煉丹乾汞，易人形，破扃鑰。
entries.en: He also boasted of alchemical mastery over cinnabar and mercury, of changing a man's shape, and of opening any lock.
entries.literal: He also claimed to refine cinnabar with heated mercury, change human form, and break locks.

entries.zh: 貴要間神奇之，官至尚書郎，賜紫，其妻出入宮禁，承恩用事。
entries.en: The great and powerful marveled at him. He rose to Gentleman of the Secretariat, was granted the purple robe, and his wife moved freely through the inner palace, enjoying imperial favor and real power.
entries.literal: Among the great and influential he was regarded as miraculous; he reached the office of Gentleman of the Secretariat and was granted purple robes; his wife entered and left the palace precincts, enjoying favor and wielding influence.

entries.zh: 皇弟存乂常朋淫於其家，至是與存乂並罹其禍。）〉
entries.en: Prince Cunyi was a habitual reveler at Yang's house; now Yang and Cunyi alike fell victim to the same purge.)〉
entries.literal: The imperial younger brother Cunyi often caroused licentiously at his house, and on this occasion together with Cunyi he fell into the calamity.)〉

entries.zh: 通王存確，莊宗第六弟，雅王存紀，莊宗第七弟，同光三年封。
entries.en: Prince Tong Cunque, Zhuangzong's sixth younger brother, and Prince Ya Cunji, his seventh, both received their titles in Tongguang 3.
entries.literal: Prince Tong Cunque, Emperor Zhuangzong's sixth younger brother, and Prince Ya Cunji, Emperor Zhuangzong's seventh younger brother, were enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

entries.zh: 莊宗敗，並為霍彥威所殺。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, both were killed by Huo Yanwei.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, both were killed by Huo Yanwei.

entries.zh: 〈（考《梁紀》，太祖有子廷鸞、落落；
entries.en: (Cross-checking the Liang Annals shows that Taizu had sons named Tingluan and Luoluo;
entries.literal: (Examining the Liang Annals, Taizu had sons Tingluan and Luoluo;

entries.zh: 《盧文進傳》，莊宗又有弟存矩。
entries.en: the biography of Lu Wenjin mentions another younger brother of Zhuangzong, Cunju;
entries.literal: in the biography of Lu Wenjin, Emperor Zhuangzong also had a younger brother Cunju.

entries.zh: 《薛史宗室傳》皆不載。）〉
entries.en: yet none of these appear in the imperial-family biographies of the Xue History.)〉
entries.literal: None of these are recorded in the Xue History's imperial family biographies.)〉

entries.zh: 申王存渥，莊宗第四弟，
entries.en: Prince Shen Cunwo, Zhuangzong's fourth younger brother,
entries.literal: Prince Shen Cunwo, Emperor Zhuangzong's fourth younger brother,

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》，存渥與存霸、存紀皆莊宗同母弟。）〉
entries.en: (The Ouyang History adds that Cunwo, like Cunba and Cunji, was Zhuangzong's uterine younger brother.)〉
entries.literal: (The Ouyang History [notes]: Cunwo, together with Cunba and Cunji, were all Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brothers by the same mother.)〉

entries.zh: 同光三年封。
entries.en: He received his princely title in Tongguang 3.
entries.literal: was enfeoffed in the third year of Tongguang.

entries.zh: 莊宗敗，與劉皇后同奔太原，為部下所殺。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong's defeat, he fled toward Taiyuan with Empress Liu and was killed by his own followers.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was defeated, he fled to Taiyuan together with Empress Liu and was killed by his subordinates.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：存渥至晉陽，李彥超不納，走至風穀，為其下所殺。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Comprehensive Mirror, Cunwo reached Jinyang but Li Yanchao refused him entry; fleeing as far as Feng Valley, he was killed by his own party.)〉
entries.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: When Cunwo reached Jinyang, Li Yanchao would not admit him; he fled to Feng Valley and was killed by his men.)〉

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌，莊宗子也。
entries.en: Prince Wei Jiji was a son of Zhuangzong.
entries.literal: Prince Wei Jiji was Emperor Zhuangzong's son.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以繼岌充北都留守；
entries.en: When Zhuangzong assumed the throne at Weizhou, he appointed Jiji Protector of the Northern Capital;
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Jiji was made Northern Capital Protector;

entries.zh: 及以鎮州為北都，又命為留守。
entries.en: when the seat of the Northern Capital was moved to Zhenzhou, Jiji was ordered to serve there again as Protector.
entries.literal: and when Zhenzhou was made the Northern Capital, he was again ordered to serve as Protector.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：三年九月二十三日，封為魏王。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of that year.)〉
entries.literal: (Five Dynasties Institutional Essentials: On the twenty-third day of the ninth month of the third year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.)〉

entries.zh: 三年，伐蜀，以繼岌為都統，郭崇韜為招討使。
entries.en: In Tongguang 3 the court marched against Shu, with Jiji as commander-in-chief and Guo Chongtao as campaign commissioner.
entries.literal: In the third year they campaigned against Shu; Jiji was made commander-in-chief and Guo Chongtao campaign commissioner.

entries.zh: 十月戊寅，至鳳州，武興軍節度使王承捷以鳳、興、文、扶四州降。
entries.en: On wuyin in the tenth month they reached Fengzhou, where Wang Chengjie, military commissioner of the Wuxing circuit, surrendered Feng, Xing, Wen, and Fu.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day of the tenth month they reached Fengzhou; Wang Chengjie, military commissioner of Wuxing Army, surrendered the four prefectures Feng, Xing, Wen, and Fu.

entries.zh: 甲申，至故鎮，康延孝收興州。
entries.en: On jiashen they reached Gu Town, and Kang Yanxiao took Xingzhou.
entries.literal: On the jiashen day they reached Gu Town; Kang Yanxiao recovered Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 時偽蜀主王衍率親軍五萬在利州，令步騎親軍三萬逆戰於三泉，康延孝、李嚴以勁騎三千犯之，蜀軍大敗，斬首五千級，餘皆奔潰。
entries.en: The Shu pretender Wang Yan was then at Lizhou with fifty thousand household troops. He sent thirty thousand foot and horse of his personal guard to meet the Tang advance at Sanquan. Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan charged with three thousand elite cavalry; the Shu force was shattered, five thousand heads were taken, and the survivors fled in disorder.
entries.literal: At that time the false Shu ruler Wang Yan led fifty thousand personal troops at Lizhou and ordered thirty thousand infantry and cavalry of his personal army to meet the attack at Sanquan. Kang Yanxiao and Li Yan struck them with three thousand crack horsemen; the Shu army was utterly defeated, five thousand heads were taken, and the rest all fled in rout.

entries.zh: 王衍聞其敗也，棄利州奔歸西川，斷吉柏津，浮梁而去。
entries.en: Hearing of the defeat, Wang Yan abandoned Lizhou and fled west into Shu, severing the Jibo crossing and escaping over a pontoon bridge.
entries.literal: When Wang Yan heard of the defeat, he abandoned Lizhou and fled back to western Shu, cutting the Jibo Ford and departing by pontoon bridge.

entries.zh: 己丑，繼岌至興州，偽蜀東川節度使宋光葆以梓、潼、劍、龍、普等州來降；
entries.en: On jichou Jiji reached Xingzhou, where Song Guangbao, the Dongchuan military commissioner of Shu, surrendered Zi, Tong, Jian, Long, Pu, and other prefectures;
entries.literal: On the jichou day Jiji reached Xingzhou; Song Guangbao, military commissioner of eastern Shu Dongchuan, came to surrender with the prefectures Zi, Tong, Jian, Long, Pu, and others;

entries.zh: 武定軍節度使王承肇以洋、蓬、壁三州符印降；
entries.en: Wang Chengzhao of the Wuding circuit submitted the seals of Yang, Peng, and Bi;
entries.literal: Wang Chengzhao, military commissioner of Wuding Army, surrendered with the seals of the three prefectures Yang, Peng, and Bi;

entries.zh: 興元節度使王宗威以梁、開、通、渠、麟等五州符印送降；
entries.en: Wang Zongwei of Xingyuan sent in the seals of Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin in submission;
entries.literal: Wang Zongwei, military commissioner of Xingyuan, sent the seals of the five prefectures Liang, Kai, Tong, Qu, and Lin in surrender;

entries.zh: 階州王承嶽納符印；
entries.en: Wang Chengyue of Jiezhou turned over his seals;
entries.literal: Wang Chengyue of Jiezhou presented the seals;

entries.zh: 秦州節度使王承休棄城而遁。
entries.en: and Wang Chengxu of Qinzhou abandoned his city and fled.
entries.literal: Wang Chengxu, military commissioner of Qinzhou, abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 辛丑，繼岌過利州。
entries.en: On xinchou Jiji passed through Lizhou.
entries.literal: On the xinchou day Jiji passed Lizhou.

entries.zh: 戊申，至劍州。
entries.en: On wushen they reached Jianzhou.
entries.literal: On the wushen day they reached Jianzhou.

entries.zh: 己酉，至綿州，王衍遣使上箋乞降。
entries.en: On jiyou they reached Mianzhou, where Wang Yan sent envoys with a written plea to surrender.
entries.literal: On the jiyou day they reached Mianzhou; Wang Yan sent envoys with a memorial begging to surrender.

entries.zh: 丁巳，入成都。
entries.en: On dingsi they entered Chengdu.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day they entered Chengdu.

entries.zh: 自興師出洛至定蜀，計七十五日，走丸之勢，前代所無。
entries.en: From the army's departure from Luoyang to the pacification of Shu took only seventy-five days—a speed like a ball rolling downhill, without precedent in earlier times.
entries.literal: From raising the army and leaving Luoyang to pacifying Shu, the total was seventy-five days—a momentum like a rolling pellet, unmatched in former ages.

entries.zh: 師回，至渭南，聞莊宗敗。
entries.en: On the march home the army reached Weinan and learned of Zhuangzong's defeat.
entries.literal: The army returned and, reaching Weinan, heard that Emperor Zhuangzong had been defeated.

entries.zh: 師徒潰散，自縊死。
entries.en: His force dissolved in panic, and he hanged himself.
entries.literal: The troops and followers scattered in rout, and he hanged himself.

entries.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》引《王氏見聞錄》云：後唐莊宗巴子魏王繼岌伐蜀，回軍在道，而有鄴都之變。
entries.en: (The Extensive Records of the Taiping, citing Wang's Records of Things Seen and Heard, relates that Zhuangzong's son Prince Wei Jiji marched against Shu and was already on the homeward road when the upheaval at Ye Capital broke out.
entries.literal: (Extensive Records of the Taiping cites Wang's Records of Things Seen and Heard: Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong's son Prince Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu; the army was on the road returning when the Ye Capital upheaval occurred.

entries.zh: 莊宗與劉後命內臣張漢賓齎急詔，所在催魏王歸闕。
entries.en: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu dispatched the palace eunuch Zhang Hanbin with an urgent edict ordering Prince Wei to return to court at once.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong and Empress Liu ordered the inner attendant Zhang Hanbin to carry an urgent edict, urging Prince Wei to return to the capital wherever he might be.

entries.zh: 張漢賓乘驛倍道急行，至興元西縣逢魏王，宣傳詔旨。
entries.en: Zhang Hanbin raced by post relay at top speed, met Prince Wei at Xixian in Xingyuan, and delivered the imperial command.
entries.literal: Zhang Hanbin rode the post relays at double speed and, reaching Xixian in Xingyuan, met Prince Wei and proclaimed the edict.

entries.zh: 王以本軍方討漢州，康延孝相次繼來，欲候之出山，以陳凱歌，漢賓督之。
entries.en: The prince's own force was still reducing Hanzhou, and Kang Yanxiao was following close behind; he wanted to wait until both columns had cleared the mountains to celebrate victory, but Hanbin pressed him onward.
entries.literal: The prince, because his own army was still campaigning at Hanzhou and Kang Yanxiao was coming in succession, wished to wait for them to emerge from the mountains so as to proclaim victory; Hanbin pressed him.

entries.zh: 有軍謀陳岷，比事梁，與漢賓熟，密問張曰：「天子改換，且是何人？」
entries.en: A staff officer named Chen Min, who had once served Liang and knew Hanbin well, asked him in private, "The throne has changed hands—who sits on it now?"
entries.literal: There was a military adviser Chen Min who had formerly served Liang and was on familiar terms with Hanbin; he secretly asked Zhang: "The Son of Heaven has been replaced—who is it now?"

entries.zh: 張色莊曰：「我嘗麵奉宣詔魏王，況大軍在行，談何容易。」
entries.en: Zhang's face hardened. "I received this edict in person to deliver to Prince Wei, and a great army is on the march—such talk is not to be bandied about lightly."
entries.literal: Zhang's expression grew stern: "I once received the edict face to face to proclaim it to Prince Wei; moreover the great army is on the march—how can such talk be lightly made?"

entries.zh: 陳岷曰：「久忝知聞，故敢諮問，兩日來有一信風，新人已即位矣，復何形跡。」
entries.en: Chen Min replied, "We have known each other a long time, which is why I dare ask. For two days reliable word has been blowing this way: the new man is already enthroned. Why keep up appearances?"
entries.literal: Chen Min said: "Having long enjoyed your acquaintance, I venture to inquire; for two days there has been a trustworthy wind—the new man has already taken the throne; what need for concealment?"

entries.zh: 張乃說：「來時聞李嗣源過河，未知近事。」
entries.en: Zhang then admitted, "When I set out I heard Li Siyuan had crossed the Yellow River, but I do not know what has happened since."
entries.literal: Zhang then said: "When I came I heard Li Siyuan had crossed the river; I do not know recent affairs."

entries.zh: 岷曰：「魏王且請盤桓，以觀其勢，未可前邁。」
entries.en: Chen said, "Prince Wei ought to hold where he is and watch how the situation develops. He must not press forward yet."
entries.literal: Chen said: "Prince Wei should please linger and observe how matters stand; he must not advance yet."

entries.zh: 張以莊宗命嚴，不敢遷延，督令進發，魏王至渭南遇害。）〉
entries.en: Bound by Zhuangzong's strict order, Zhang would not delay and drove the march forward; Prince Wei reached Weinan and was killed.)〉
entries.literal: Because Emperor Zhuangzong's command was strict, Zhang dared not delay and pressed for departure; Prince Wei reached Weinan and met disaster.)〉

entries.zh: 許王從益，明宗之幼子也。
entries.en: Prince Xu Congyi was Mingzong's youngest son.
entries.literal: Prince Xu Congyi was Emperor Mingzong's youngest son.

entries.zh: 宮嬪所生。
entries.en: He was born to a palace concubine.
entries.literal: He was born of a palace concubine.

entries.zh: 明宗命王淑妃母之，嘗謂左右曰：「惟此兒生於皇宮，故尤所鍾愛。」
entries.en: Mingzong appointed Consort Wang Shufei as his foster mother and once told his attendants, "Only this child was born in the palace itself, and so I cherish him above all."
entries.literal: Emperor Mingzong ordered Consort Wang Shufei to be his foster mother and once said to those around him: "Only this child was born within the imperial palace, and so I especially cherish him."

entries.zh: 長興末，封許王。
entries.en: At the end of the Changxing era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
entries.literal: At the end of Changxing he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.

entries.zh: 晉高祖即位，以皇后即其姊也，乃養從益於宮中。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, the empress being his elder sister, Congyi was raised in the palace.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, because the empress was his elder sister, Congyi was raised within the palace.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，以從益為二王後，改封郇國公，食邑三千戶。
entries.en: During Jin Tianfu he was made heir to the second princely rank, retitled Duke of Xun, with a fief of three thousand households.
entries.literal: During Tianfu of Jin, Congyi was made heir to the second prince rank, his title was changed to Duke of Xun, and his fief was three thousand households.

entries.zh: 其後與母歸洛陽。
entries.en: He later returned to Luoyang with his mother.
entries.literal: Afterward he returned to Luoyang with his mother.

entries.zh: 守陵開運末，契丹主至汴，以從益遙領曹州節度使，復封許王，與王妃尋歸西京。
entries.en: While guarding the imperial tombs in late Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler reached Bian. Congyi was given titular command of Caozhou, again enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and soon returned to the Western Capital with his consort.
entries.literal: While guarding the tombs at the end of Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler came to Bian; Congyi was made titular military commissioner of Caozhou at a distance, again enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and soon returned to the Western Capital with his princess consort.

entries.zh: 會契丹主死，其汴州節度使蕭翰謀歸北地，慮中原無主，軍民大亂，則己亦不得按轡徐歸矣；
entries.en: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north. He feared that with no ruler in the Central Plains and army and people in chaos, he himself could not withdraw at leisure;
entries.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north and feared that with no ruler in central China and army and people in great disorder, he himself would be unable to rein in his horse and withdraw at leisure;

entries.zh: 乃詐稱契丹主命，遣人迎從益於洛陽，令知南朝軍國事。
entries.en: so he falsely claimed the Khitan ruler's command, sent men to summon Congyi from Luoyang, and installed him to govern the southern court's military and civil affairs.
entries.literal: therefore he falsely claimed the Khitan ruler's command, sent men to welcome Congyi from Luoyang, and ordered him to manage the military and civil affairs of the southern court.

entries.zh: 從益與王妃逃於徽陵以避之，使者至，不得已而赴焉。
entries.en: Congyi and his consort fled to Huiling to escape the summons; when the envoys arrived, he had no choice but to go.
entries.literal: Congyi and his princess consort fled to Huiling to avoid this; when the envoys arrived, unable to refuse, he went to them.

entries.zh: 從益於崇元殿見群官。
entries.en: Congyi received the assembled officials in Chongyuan Hall.
entries.literal: Congyi received the assembled officials in Chongyuan Hall.

entries.zh: 蕭翰率蕃首列拜於殿上，群官趨於殿下，乃偽署王鬆為左丞相，趙上交為右丞相。
entries.en: Xiao Han led the Khitan chiefs in ranks bowing in the hall while the officials hurried to below the steps. He falsely appointed Wang Song Left Chancellor and Zhao Shangjiao Right Chancellor.
entries.literal: Xiao Han led the Khitan chiefs in ranks bowing in the hall; the officials hurried to below the steps, and he falsely appointed Wang Song as Left Chancellor and Zhao Shangjiao as Right Chancellor.

entries.zh: 李式、翟光鄴為樞密使，王景崇為宣徽使，餘官各有署置。
entries.en: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong palace commissioner, and the remaining posts were each filled.
entries.literal: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong was made palace commissioner, and the remaining offices were each filled.

entries.zh: 又以北來燕將劉祚為權侍衛使，充在京巡檢。
entries.en: The Yan general Liu Zuo, newly arrived from the north, was made acting commissioner of the Palace Guard and charged with capital patrol.
entries.literal: Furthermore the Yan general Liu Zuo, who had come from the north, was made acting commissioner of the Palace Guard and charged with patrol in the capital.

entries.zh: 翰北歸，從益餞於北郊。
entries.en: When Xiao Han marched north, Congyi gave him a farewell feast at the Northern Suburb.
entries.literal: When Han returned north, Congyi gave a farewell feast at the Northern Suburb.

entries.zh: 及漢高祖將離太原，從益召高行周、武行德欲拒漢高祖，行周等不從，且奏其事。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Han was about to march from Taiyuan, Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde to resist him. They refused and memorialized the court.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Han was about to leave Taiyuan, Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde, wishing to resist Gaozu of Han; Xingzhou and the others would not obey and moreover memorialized the matter.

entries.zh: 漢高祖怒，車駕將至闕，從益與王妃俱賜死於私第，時年十七；
entries.en: Gaozu of Han was enraged. As the imperial carriage neared the capital, Congyi and his consort were both ordered to die in their private residence. He was seventeen;
entries.literal: Gaozu of Han was angry; as the imperial carriage was about to reach the palace, Congyi and his princess consort were both granted death in their private residence; he was seventeen years old;

entries.zh: 時人哀之。
entries.en: and the people pitied him.
entries.literal: people of the time pitied him.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：漢高祖自太原起軍建號，至洛陽，會郭從義先入京師，受密旨殺王淑妃與許王從益。
entries.en: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties records that Gaozu of Han raised his army at Taiyuan and established his reign. Reaching Luoyang, he found Guo Congyi already in the capital with a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.
entries.literal: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu of Han raised an army at Taiyuan and established his reign; reaching Luoyang, he met Guo Congyi, who had entered the capital first and received a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.

entries.zh: 淑妃臨刑號泣曰：「吾家子母何罪，吾既為契丹所立，非敢與人爭國，何不且留吾兒，每年寒食，使持一盂飯灑明宗陵寢。」
entries.en: Facing execution the consort wept aloud, "What crime have mother and son committed? The Khitan installed me; I never sought to contend for the realm. Why not spare my son, so that each Cold Food he may bring one bowl of rice to Mingzong's tomb?"
entries.literal: Facing execution the consort wept aloud: "What crime have my household's mother and son committed? I was installed by the Khitan and did not dare contend for the realm with others—why not at least spare my son, so that each year at Cold Food he may bring one bowl of rice to pour at Emperor Mingzong's tomb?"

entries.zh: 聞者無不泣下。）〉
entries.en: All who heard wept.)〉
entries.literal: All who heard wept.)〉

entries.zh: 十六年，嗣昭代周德威權幽州軍府事。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year Sizhao took over from Zhou Dewei as acting administrator of the Youzhou military headquarters.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year Sizhao replaced Zhou Dewei in acting charge of the Youzhou military headquarters.

entries.zh: 九月，以李紹宏代，嗣昭出薊門，百姓號泣請留，截鞍惜別，嗣昭夜遁而歸。
entries.en: In the ninth month Li Shohong was appointed in his place. As Sizhao left through Jimen Gate, the people wept and begged him to stay, even cutting his saddle straps in their grief at parting. Sizhao stole away by night and returned.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Li Shohong was appointed to replace him; Sizhao went out through Jimen Gate. The people wept and begged him to stay, cutting his saddle in sorrow at parting; Sizhao slipped away by night and returned.

entries.zh: 十七年六月，嗣昭自德勝歸藩，莊宗帳餞於戚城。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year Sizhao returned to his circuit from Desheng, and Zhuangzong held a farewell feast for him at Qicheng.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year Sizhao returned to his circuit from Desheng; Emperor Zhuangzong held a farewell feast in his tent at Qicheng.

entries.zh: 莊宗酒酣，泣而言曰：「河朔生靈，十年饋挽，引領鶴望，俟破汴軍。
entries.en: Deep in his cups, Zhuangzong wept and said, "The people of Hebei have supplied us for ten years, craning their necks in hope, waiting for us to break the Bian army.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong was deep in wine, he wept and said, "The people of Hebei have supplied provisions for ten years, stretching their necks like cranes in longing, waiting for the Bian army to be broken.

entries.zh: 今兵賦不充，寇孽猶在，坐食軍賦，有愧蒸民。」
entries.en: Now our levies fall short, the enemy still stands, and we sit here consuming what they provide. I am ashamed before the people."
entries.literal: Now military levies are insufficient, the bandit scourge still remains, and we sit consuming army provisions—we are ashamed before the common people."

entries.zh: 嗣昭曰：「臣忝急難之地，每一念此，寢不安席。
entries.en: Sizhao said, "I hold a post in this hard-pressed land. Whenever I think of it, I cannot sleep at ease.
entries.literal: Sizhao said, "Your servant holds a post in this land of urgent peril; whenever I think of this, I cannot sleep peacefully on my mat.

entries.zh: 大王且持重謹守，惠養士民。
entries.en: Your Majesty should hold steady, guard carefully, and care for your officers and people.
entries.literal: Your Majesty should for now hold steady and guard carefully, nurturing officers and people with kindness.

entries.zh: 臣歸本藩，簡料兵賦，歲末春首，即舉眾復來。」
entries.en: I will return to my circuit, gather troops and supplies, and come back with my forces by the end of the year or early spring."
entries.literal: Your servant will return to his circuit, muster troops and levies, and at year's end or the start of spring will lead the host back again."

entries.zh: 莊宗離席拜送，如家人禮。
entries.en: Zhuangzong rose from his seat and bowed him off with the intimacy of family.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong left his seat and bowed in farewell, with the courtesy of family.

entries.zh: 是月，汴將劉鄩攻同州，朱友謙告急，嗣昭與李存審援之。
entries.en: That same month the Bian general Liu Xun attacked Tong Prefecture. Zhu Youqian sent an urgent appeal, and Sizhao went to his aid with Li Cunshen.
entries.literal: That month the Bian general Liu Xun attacked Tong Prefecture; Zhu Youqian reported urgently, and Sizhao with Li Cunshen went to his aid.

entries.zh: 九月，破汴軍於馮翊，乃班師。
entries.en: In the ninth month he defeated the Bian army at Fengyi and withdrew.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he defeated the Bian army at Fengyi and then withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 李嗣本，雁門人，本姓張。
entries.en: Li Siben was from Yanmen and was originally surnamed Zhang.
entries.literal: Li Siben was a man of Yanmen, originally surnamed Zhang.

entries.zh: 父準，銅冶鎮將。
entries.en: His father Zhun was commander of Tongye Garrison.
entries.literal: His father Zhun was commander of Tongye Garrison.

entries.zh: 嗣本少事武皇，為帳中紀綱，漸立戰功，得補軍校。
entries.en: Siben served the Martial Emperor from youth as a guard officer in his tent, gradually won distinction in battle, and was appointed a military cadet.
entries.literal: Siben in youth served the Martial Emperor as a guard officer in the tent, gradually achieved merit in battle, and was appointed a military cadet.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，從征李匡儔為前鋒，與燕人戰，得居庸關，以功為義兒軍使，因賜姓名。
entries.en: During the Qianning era he served as vanguard in the campaign against Li Kuangchou, fought the Yan forces, and took Juyong Pass. For this he was made commander of the adoptive-sons army and granted the Li surname and his given name.
entries.literal: During Qianning he followed the campaign against Li Kuangchou as vanguard, fought the Yan men, took Juyong Pass, and for his merit was made commander of the adoptive-sons army; he was thereupon granted the surname and given name.

entries.zh: 從討王行瑜，授檢校刑部尚書，改威遠、寧塞等軍使。
entries.en: He joined the campaign against Wang Xingyu and was appointed acting Minister of Justice, then made commander of the Weiyuan, Ningsai, and other armies.
entries.literal: He followed the punitive campaign against Wang Xingyu and was appointed acting Minister of Justice, then changed to commander of the Weiyuan, Ningsai, and other armies.

entries.zh: 五年，討羅宏信於魏州，嗣本為前鋒，師還，改馬軍都將。
entries.en: In the fifth year he campaigned against Luo Hongxin at Weizhou as vanguard. When the army returned he was made commander of the horse army.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he campaigned against Luo Hongxin at Weizhou; Siben was vanguard. When the army returned he was changed to commander of the horse army.

entries.zh: 從李嗣昭討王暉於雲州，論功加檢校司空。
entries.en: He followed Li Sizhao against Wang Hui at Yun Prefecture and was promoted to acting Minister of Works for his service.
entries.literal: He followed Li Sizhao in campaigning against Wang Hui at Yun Prefecture; for merit he was promoted to acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 汴將李思安之圍潞州也，從周德威軍於餘吾，嗣本率騎軍日與汴人轉鬥，前後獻俘千計，遷代州刺史。
entries.en: When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he served under Zhou Dewei at Yuyu. Siben led cavalry in daily skirmishes with the Bian, presented more than a thousand captives in all, and was made prefect of Dai.
entries.literal: When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he followed Zhou Dewei's army at Yuyu; Siben led cavalry daily in running battles with the Bian, presenting more than a thousand captives in all, and was transferred to prefect of Dai.

entries.zh: 六年，從攻晉、絳，為蕃漢副使都校。
entries.en: In the sixth year he joined the attack on Jin and Jiang as deputy commander of the mixed Tangut-Han forces.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he followed the attack on Jin and Jiang and was deputy commander of the mixed Tangut-Han forces.

entries.zh: 及武皇喪事有日，嗣本監護其事，改雲中防禦使、雲蔚應朔等州都知兵馬使，加特進、檢校太保。
entries.en: When the Martial Emperor's funeral drew near, Siben supervised the arrangements. He was made defender of Yunzhong and overall commander of troops for Yun, Wei, Ying, Shuo, and other prefectures, with special advancement and the acting rank of Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: When the Martial Emperor's funeral was near, Siben supervised the arrangements; he was changed to defender of Yunzhong and overall commander of troops for Yun, Wei, Ying, Shuo, and other prefectures, with special advancement and acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 九年，周德威討劉守光，嗣本率代北諸軍、生熟吐渾，收山後八軍，得納降軍使盧文進、武州刺史高行珪以獻。
entries.en: In the ninth year Zhou Dewei campaigned against Liu Shouguang. Siben led the northern Dai armies and Tuyuhun forces, recovered the eight armies beyond the mountains, and presented the surrendered commander Lu Wenjin and Wu prefect Gao Xinggui.
entries.literal: In the ninth year Zhou Dewei campaigned against Liu Shouguang; Siben led the armies of northern Dai and raw and seasoned Tuyuhun, recovered the eight armies beyond the mountains, and presented the surrendered commander Lu Wenjin and the prefect of Wu Gao Xinggui.

entries.zh: 幽州平，論功授振武節度使，號「威信可汗」。
entries.en: When Youzhou was pacified, he was rewarded with the post of military commissioner of Zhenwu and styled "Trustworthy and Worthy Khan."
entries.literal: When Youzhou was pacified, for merit he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu and styled "Trustworthy and Worthy Khan."

entries.zh: 十二年，莊宗定魏博，劉鄩據莘縣，命嗣本入太原巡守都城，十三年，從破劉鄩於故元城，收洺、磁、衛三郡。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong secured Weibo while Liu Xun held Shen County. Siben was ordered into Taiyuan to guard the capital. In the thirteenth year he helped defeat Liu Xun at Old Yuancheng and recovered Ming, Ci, and Wei.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Emperor Zhuangzong secured Weibo; Liu Xun held Shen County, and Siben was ordered into Taiyuan to patrol and guard the capital. In the thirteenth year he followed the defeat of Liu Xun at Old Yuancheng and recovered the three commanderies of Ming, Ci, and Wei.

entries.zh: 六月，還鎮振武。
entries.en: In the sixth month he returned to his post at Zhenwu.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he returned to his post at Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 八月，契丹阿保機傾塞犯邊，其眾三十萬攻振武，嗣本嬰城拒戰者累日。
entries.en: In the eighth month the Khitan ruler Abaoji invaded in force with three hundred thousand men against Zhenwu. Siben held the city and fought for many days.
entries.literal: In the eighth month the Khitan Abaoji poured across the frontier in invasion; his host of three hundred thousand attacked Zhenwu, and Siben held the city and resisted in battle for many days.

entries.zh: 契丹為火車地道，晝夜急攻，城中兵少，禦備罄竭，城陷，嗣本舉族入契丹。
entries.en: The Khitan used fire carts and tunneling and attacked day and night without pause. The garrison was small, defenses were exhausted, the city fell, and Siben took his whole clan into Khitan territory.
entries.literal: The Khitan used fire carts and tunneling, attacking urgently day and night; troops in the city were few, defenses exhausted, the city fell, and Siben led his whole clan into Khitan territory.

entries.zh: 有子八人，四人陷於幕庭。
entries.en: He had eight sons, four of whom were lost in the Khitan court.
entries.literal: He had eight sons; four were lost in the Khitan court.

entries.zh: 嗣本性剛烈，有節義，善戰多謀，然治郡民，頗傷苛急，人以此少之也。
entries.en: Siben was stern and principled, skilled in battle and full of stratagems. Yet in governing his prefecture he was harsh, and for that people thought less of him.
entries.literal: Siben by nature was stern and fierce, possessed integrity and righteousness, was skilled in battle and full of stratagems; yet in governing prefectural people he was rather harsh and severe, and for this people thought less of him.

entries.zh: 李嗣恩，本姓駱。
entries.en: Li Si'en was originally surnamed Luo.
entries.literal: Li Si'en was originally surnamed Luo.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：嗣恩本吐谷渾部人。）〉
entries.en: (The Ouyang History records that Si'en was originally from the Tuyuhun people.)
entries.literal: (The Ouyang History: Si'en was originally a man of the Tuyuhun tribe.)

entries.zh: 年十五，能騎射，侍武皇於振武；
entries.en: At fifteen he could ride and shoot and attended the Martial Emperor at Zhenwu;
entries.literal: At fifteen he could ride and shoot and attended the Martial Emperor at Zhenwu;

entries.zh: 及鎮太原，補鐵林軍小校。
entries.en: when the emperor took charge at Taiyuan, he was appointed a junior officer in the Iron Forest Army.
entries.literal: when the emperor took up his post at Taiyuan, he was appointed a junior officer of the Iron Forest Army.

entries.zh: 從征王行瑜，奉表獻捷，加檢校散騎常侍，漸轉突陣指揮使，賜姓名。
entries.en: He joined the campaign against Wang Xingyu, reported victory to court, was promoted to acting Regular Attendant, became commander of the shock-assault formation, and was granted the Li surname and his given name.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Wang Xingyu, presented a memorial reporting victory, was promoted to acting Regular Attendant, gradually became commander of the shock-assault formation, and was granted the surname and given name.

entries.zh: 天祐四年，逐康懷英於河西，解汾州之圍，加檢校司空，充左廂馬軍都將。
entries.en: In Tianyou 4 he drove Kang Huaiying from Hexi, lifted the siege of Fen Prefecture, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and made commander of the left wing of the horse army.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou he drove Kang Huaiying from Hexi, relieved the siege of Fen Prefecture, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and served as commander of the left wing of the horse army.

entries.zh: 戰王景仁有功，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: He fought Wang Jingren with distinction and was promoted to acting Minister of Education.
entries.literal: Fighting Wang Jingren he achieved merit and was promoted to acting Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 救河中府，與梁人接戰，應弦斃者甚眾，而槊中其口；
entries.en: Relieving Hezhong, he fought the Liang in battle. Many fell to his arrows, but a spear struck him in the mouth;
entries.literal: Relieving Hezhong Prefecture, he engaged the Liang in battle; many fell to his arrows, but a spear struck his mouth;

entries.zh: 及退，莊宗親視其傷，深加慰勉，轉內衙馬步都將、遼州刺史。
entries.en: when he withdrew Zhuangzong personally inspected his wound and comforted him warmly. He was made commander of the inner guard horse and foot forces and prefect of Liao.
entries.literal: when he withdrew, Emperor Zhuangzong personally inspected his wound and greatly comforted and encouraged him; he was transferred to commander of the inner guard horse and foot forces and prefect of Liao.

entries.zh: 十二年，從莊宗入魏，擊劉鄩有功，轉天雄軍都指揮使。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he followed Zhuangzong into Wei, fought Liu Xun with distinction, and was made overall commander of the Tianxiong army.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Emperor Zhuangzong into Wei, struck Liu Xun with merit, and was transferred to overall commander of the Tianxiong army.

entries.zh: 劉鄩之北趣樂平也，嗣恩襲之，倍程先入晉陽。
entries.en: When Liu Xun marched north toward Leping, Si'en struck at him, forced the pace, and entered Jinyang ahead of him.
entries.literal: When Liu Xun marched north toward Leping, Si'en struck him, doubled the pace, and entered Jinyang first.

entries.zh: 時城中無備，得嗣恩兵至，人百其勇，鄩聞其先過，乃遁。
entries.en: The city was unprepared. When Si'en's troops arrived, every man fought as if he were worth a hundred. Xun, hearing that Si'en had passed him, fled.
entries.literal: At that time the city had no preparations; when Si'en's troops arrived, each man was a hundred times braver; Xun, hearing he had passed ahead, then fled.

entries.zh: 莘之戰，以功轉代州刺史，充石嶺關以北都知兵馬使，稍遷振武節度使。
entries.en: At the battle of Shen he was rewarded with the post of prefect of Dai and overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was later promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.
entries.literal: At the battle of Shen, for merit he was transferred to prefect of Dai, served as overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was gradually promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 十五年，追赴行在，卒於太原。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was summoned urgently to the imperial camp and died at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned in haste to the imperial camp and died at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 天成初，明宗敦念舊勳，詔贈太尉。
entries.en: Early in the Tiancheng era Emperor Mingzong, mindful of old service, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Emperor Mingzong recalled his old merit and issued an edict posthumously honoring him as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 李嗣昭，字益光，武皇母弟代州刺史克柔之假子也。
entries.en: Li Sizhao, whose courtesy name was Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, prefect of Dai and younger full brother of the Martial Emperor.
entries.literal: Li Sizhao, courtesy name Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, prefect of Dai Prefecture and younger full brother of the Martial Emperor.

entries.zh: 小字進通，不知族姓所出。
entries.en: He was also known in youth as Jintong, but his original clan and surname are unknown.
entries.literal: His childhood name was Jintong; his clan and surname of origin are unknown.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》作本姓韓氏，汾州大穀縣民家子。）〉
entries.en: (The Ouyang History records that he was originally surnamed Han and came from a common family in Dagu County, Fen Prefecture.)
entries.literal: (The Ouyang History states that his original surname was Han and that he was the son of a common household in Dagu County, Fen Prefecture.)

entries.zh: 少事克柔，頗謹願，雖形貌眇小，而精悍有膽略，沉毅不群。
entries.en: As a youth he served Kerou with dutiful steadiness. Though slight in build, he was sharp, courageous, and unusually composed.
entries.literal: In youth he served Kerou and was quite dutiful and compliant; though small in stature, he was keen and bold in spirit, deep and resolute, and unlike others.

entries.zh: 初嗜酒好樂，武皇微伸儆戒，乃終身不飲。
entries.en: He had once been fond of wine and music, but after the Martial Emperor gently admonished him, he never drank again for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: At first he loved wine and music; the Martial Emperor gave him a mild warning, and thereafter he never drank for the rest of his life.

entries.zh: 少從征伐，精練軍機。
entries.en: He took the field from an early age and became thoroughly skilled in military operations.
entries.literal: From youth he followed campaigns and became thoroughly versed in military affairs.

entries.zh: 乾寧初，王珂、王珙爭帥河中，珙引陝州之軍攻珂，珂求救於武皇，乃令嗣昭將兵援之，敗珙軍於猗氏，獲賊將李璠等。
entries.en: Early in the Qianning era, Wang Ke and Wang Gong fought over command of Hezhong. Gong brought Shaan troops against Ke, who appealed to the Martial Emperor. Sizhao was sent to his aid, defeated Gong at Yishi, and captured the rebel general Li Fan and others.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianning, Wang Ke and Wang Gong contended for command of Hezhong; Gong brought troops from Shaan Prefecture to attack Ke. Ke sought rescue from the Martial Emperor, who then ordered Sizhao to lead troops to aid him. He defeated Gong's army at Yishi and captured the rebel generals Li Fan and others.

entries.zh: 四年，改衙內都將，復援河中，敗汴軍於胡壁堡，擒汴將滑禮，以功加檢校僕射。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was made commander of the inner guard, returned to aid Hezhong, routed Bian forces at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and for his service was promoted to acting Vice Director.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to commander-in-chief of the inner guard, again aided Hezhong, defeated Bian troops at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and for his merit was promoted to acting Vice Director.

entries.zh: 及王珂請婚武皇，武皇以女妻之；
entries.en: When Wang Ke sought a marriage alliance with the Martial Emperor, the latter gave him his daughter in marriage;
entries.literal: When Wang Ke requested marriage with the Martial Emperor, the Martial Emperor gave him his daughter as wife;

entries.zh: 珂赴禮於太原，以嗣昭權典河中留後事。
entries.en: Ke traveled to Taiyuan for the wedding, and Sizhao was left in charge of Hezhong as acting military governor.
entries.literal: Ke went to Taiyuan for the wedding rites, and Sizhao was appointed to administer the acting military governorship of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 大順二年三月，邢州節度使安知建叛入汴軍，武皇令存孝定邢、洺，因授之節鉞。
entries.en: In the third month of the second year of Dashun, Xingzhou commissioner An Zhijian defected to the Bian army. The Martial Emperor sent Cunxiao to secure Xing and Ming and invested him with the commissioner's regalia.
entries.literal: In the third month of the second year of Dashun, An Zhijian, military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, rebelled and entered the Bian army; the Martial Emperor ordered Cunxiao to pacify Xing and Ming and thereby invested him with commission and regalia.

entries.zh: 時幽州李匡威與鎮州王鎔屢弱中山，將中分其疆土。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Wang Rong of Zhen were then repeatedly pressing Zhongshan and meant to partition its territory between them.
entries.literal: At that time Li Kuangwei of Youzhou and Wang Rong of Zhen repeatedly weakened Zhongshan and intended to divide its territory between them.

entries.zh: 定州王處存求援於武皇；
entries.en: Wang Chucun of Ding Prefecture appealed to the Martial Emperor for help;
entries.literal: Wang Chucun of Ding Prefecture sought aid from the Martial Emperor;

entries.zh: 武皇命存孝侵鎮、趙之南鄙，又令李存信、李存審率師出井陘以會之，並軍攻臨城、柏鄉。
entries.en: who ordered Cunxiao to harry the southern marches of Zhen and Zhao while Li Cunxin and Li Cunshen marched through Jingxing Pass to join him. The united forces attacked Lincheng and Baixiang.
entries.literal: the Martial Emperor ordered Cunxiao to raid the southern borders of Zhen and Zhao, and also ordered Li Cunxin and Li Cunshen to lead armies out through Jingxing Pass to join him; the combined armies attacked Lincheng and Baixiang.

entries.zh: 李匡威救至，且議旋師。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei came to their relief, and the commanders began discussing withdrawal.
entries.literal: Li Kuangwei arrived to rescue them, and there was discussion of withdrawing the army.

entries.zh: 李存信與存孝不協，因構於武皇，言存孝望風退衄，無心擊賊，恐有私盟也。
entries.en: Li Cunxin, at odds with Cunxiao, slandered him to the Martial Emperor, claiming he shrank from battle, lacked zeal against the enemy, and may have struck a private bargain.
entries.literal: Li Cunxin was not in accord with Cunxiao and therefore framed him before the Martial Emperor, saying Cunxiao shrank back at sight of the wind, had no heart to strike the enemy, and perhaps had a private alliance.

entries.zh: 存孝知之，自恃戰功，鬱鬱不平，因致書通王鎔，又歸款於汴。
entries.en: When Cunxiao learned of this, confident in his battle record yet bitterly aggrieved, he opened correspondence with Wang Rong and also offered his allegiance to Bian.
entries.literal: Cunxiao learned of it; relying on his battle merit, he was depressed and resentful, and therefore sent letters to open relations with Wang Rong and also submitted allegiance to Bian.

entries.zh: 明年，武皇自出井陘，將逼真定，存孝面見王鎔陳軍機。
entries.en: The following year the Martial Emperor marched in person through Jingxing Pass toward Zhending. Cunxiao met Wang Rong in person to discuss strategy.
entries.literal: The next year the Martial Emperor himself came out through Jingxing Pass, about to press close to Zhending; Cunxiao met Wang Rong face to face and laid out military plans.

entries.zh: 武皇暴怒，誅先獲汴將安康八方旋師。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor flew into a rage, executed the captured Bian officer An Kang, and turned the army homeward.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor was violently angry, executed the Bian general An Kang who had been captured earlier, and wheeled the army back.

entries.zh: 七月，復出師討存孝，自縛馬關東下，攻平山，渡滹水，擊鎮州四關城。
entries.en: In the seventh month he marched out again against Cunxiao, descending east from Fuma Pass, taking Pingshan, crossing the Hutuo, and assaulting the four garrison towns of Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he again led out the army to attack Cunxiao, descending east from Fuma Pass, attacking Pingshan, crossing Hutuo River, and striking the four pass cities of Zhen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 王鎔懼，遣使乞平，請以兵三萬助擊存孝，許之。
entries.en: Wang Rong, alarmed, sued for peace and offered thirty thousand men to help crush Cunxiao. The Martial Emperor agreed.
entries.literal: Wang Rong was afraid, sent envoys begging peace, and asked to aid with thirty thousand troops in attacking Cunxiao; this was granted.

entries.zh: 《新唐書》：王鎔失幽州助，因乞盟，進幣五十萬，歸糧二十萬，請出兵助討存孝。
entries.en: The 《New Tang History》 adds that, having lost Youzhou's support, Wang Rong sought alliance, sent five hundred thousand in tribute goods, returned two hundred thousand in grain, and asked to join the campaign against Cunxiao.
entries.literal: 《New Tang History》: Wang Rong had lost Youzhou's aid, and therefore begged alliance, presenting five hundred thousand in goods, returning two hundred thousand in grain, and requesting troops to help attack Cunxiao.

entries.zh: 武皇蒐於欒城。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor mustered his forces at Luancheng.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor held a grand review at Luancheng.

entries.zh: 李存信屯琉璃陂。
entries.en: Li Cunxin camped at Liuli Marsh.
entries.literal: Li Cunxin encamped at Liuli Marsh.

entries.zh: 九月，存孝夜犯存信營，奉誠軍使孫考老被獲，存信軍亂。
entries.en: In the ninth month Cunxiao struck Cunxin's camp at night, captured the Fengcheng commissioner Sun Kaolao, and threw Cunxin's army into chaos.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Cunxiao raided Cunxin's camp by night; the Fengcheng army commissioner Sun Kaolao was captured and Cunxin's army fell into disorder.

entries.zh: 武皇進攻邢州，深溝高壘以環之，旋為存孝衝突，溝塹不成。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor invested Xingzhou with deep trenches and high ramparts, but Cunxiao repeatedly broke through the works and the encirclement could not be finished.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor advanced to attack Xing Prefecture, digging deep trenches and raising high ramparts to encircle it, but was soon broken through by Cunxiao and the trenches and ditches could not be completed.

entries.zh: 有軍校袁奉韜者，密令人謂存孝曰：「大王俟塹成即歸太原，如塹壘未成，恐無歸志。
entries.en: An officer named Yuan Fengtao secretly sent word to Cunxiao: "The Prince will return to Taiyuan once the siege works are complete; if the ramparts are not finished, he may not intend to go home at all.
entries.literal: There was an army officer, Yuan Fengtao, who secretly sent someone to tell Cunxiao: "The Prince will return to Taiyuan once the trench is complete; if the fortifications are not finished, he may have no thought of returning.

entries.zh: 尚書所畏惟大王耳，料諸將孰出尚書右。
entries.en: The Inspector-General fears you alone. Which of his commanders could stand above him?
entries.literal: The Inspector-General fears only you; consider which of the generals could surpass the Inspector-General.

entries.zh: 王若西歸，雖限以黃河，亦可浮渡，況咫尺之洫，安能阻尚書鋒銳哉！」
entries.en: If the Prince withdraws westward, the Yellow River alone cannot stop him—and how could this ditch at your very feet check his spearhead?"
entries.literal: If the Prince returns west, though limited by the Yellow River, he can still cross by floating; how much less can this moat within arm's reach block the Inspector-General's sharp advance!"

entries.zh: 存孝然之，縱兵成塹。
entries.en: Cunxiao believed him and let the besiegers finish the works.
entries.literal: Cunxiao agreed and allowed his troops to complete the trench.

entries.zh: 居旬日，深溝高壘，飛走不能及，由是存孝至敗，城中食盡。
entries.en: Within ten days the trenches and ramparts were complete; not even birds could pass. Cunxiao was thereby brought to ruin as the city's provisions ran out.
entries.literal: Within ten days deep trenches and high ramparts were complete; neither bird nor beast could cross them, and thereby Cunxiao came to defeat as food in the city was exhausted.

entries.zh: 乾寧元年三月，存孝登城首罪，泣訴於武皇曰：「兒蒙王深恩，位至將帥，苟非讒慝離間，曷欲捨父子之深恩，附仇讎之黨！
entries.en: In the third month of the first year of Qianning, Cunxiao mounted the wall to confess his guilt and wept before the Martial Emperor: "I owed you deep kindness and rose to command armies. Had slanderers not driven us apart, why would I ever have forsaken a father's bond to join your enemies?!
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Qianning, Cunxiao ascended the wall to confess guilt, weeping as he appealed to the Martial Emperor: "Your son received the Prince's deep favor and rose to command armies; if not for slanderous villains sowing discord, how would he wish to abandon the deep bond of father and son and attach himself to a party of enemies!

entries.zh: 兒雖褊狹設計，實存信構陷至此，若得生見王面，一言而死，誠所甘心。」
entries.en: Whatever schemes I devised, it was Cunxin who brought me to this pass. If I might see your face once more and speak a single word before I die, I would accept that gladly."
entries.literal: Though your son devised narrow schemes, in truth it was Cunxin who framed him to this point; if he could see the Prince's face alive, to die after one word would truly be what his heart desires."

entries.zh: 武皇愍之，遣劉太妃入城慰勞。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor was moved and sent Consort Liu into the city to comfort him.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor pitied him and sent Consort Liu into the city to comfort him.

entries.zh: 太妃引來謁見，存孝泥首請罪曰：「兒立微勞，本無顯過，但被人中傷，申明無路，迷昧至此！」
entries.en: She brought him to audience. Cunxiao prostrated himself and pleaded: "I earned only modest merit and committed no grave offense, yet I was struck down by slander with no way to clear my name, and in my confusion came to this!"
entries.literal: The Consort brought him to audience; Cunxiao pressed his forehead to the earth begging pardon: "Your son established slight merit and originally had no glaring fault, but was wounded by others in the middle; he had no road to clear himself and in confusion came to this!"

entries.zh: 武皇叱之曰：「爾與王鎔書狀，罪我萬端，亦存信教耶！」
entries.en: The Martial Emperor thundered at him: "Your letters to Wang Rong heaped ten thousand charges upon me—did Cunxin dictate those as well?!"
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor rebuked him: "Your letters to Wang Rong accused me in ten thousand ways—was that also Cunxin's teaching!"

entries.zh: 縶歸太原，車裂於市。
entries.en: He was bound, taken to Taiyuan, and torn apart by chariots in the marketplace.
entries.literal: He was bound and returned to Taiyuan and torn apart by chariots in the market.

entries.zh: 然武皇深惜其才。
entries.en: Yet the Martial Emperor deeply regretted his talent.
entries.literal: Yet the Martial Emperor deeply regretted his talent.

entries.zh: 存孝每臨大敵，被重鎧橐弓坐槊，僕人以二騎從，陣中易騎，輕捷如飛，獨舞鐵□，挺身陷陣，萬人辟易，蓋古張遼、甘寧之比也。
entries.en: Whenever Cunxiao met a major foe he donned heavy armor, bow slung as he rode spear in hand, with two spare mounts led behind him. In the press of battle he changed horses mid-charge, light as flight, wielding his iron spear alone as he drove into the enemy line until ten thousand men shrank back—worthy, indeed, of comparison with Zhang Liao and Gan Ning of old.
entries.literal: Whenever Cunxiao faced a great enemy he wore heavy armor, carried his bow seated on his spear, with servants following on two horses; in battle he changed mounts, swift as flight, alone brandishing an iron spear, plunging bodily into the ranks so that ten thousand men gave way—he may be compared to the ancients Zhang Liao and Gan Ning.

entries.zh: 存孝死，武皇不視事旬日，私憾諸將久之。
entries.en: After Cunxiao's death the Martial Emperor neglected state business for ten days and long harbored private resentment toward his generals.
entries.literal: When Cunxiao died the Martial Emperor did not attend to affairs for ten days and privately resented the generals for a long time.

entries.zh: 李存信，本姓張，父君政，回鶻部人也。
entries.en: Li Cunxin was originally surnamed Zhang; his father Junzheng came from the Uighur tribes.
entries.literal: Li Cunxin, original surname Zhang, father Junzheng, was a man of the Uighur tribes.

entries.zh: 大中初，隨懷化郡王李思忠內附，因家雲中之合羅川。
entries.en: In the early Dazhong reign he accompanied the Prince of Huaihua, Li Sizhong, in coming over to Tang territory, and his family then settled at Heluo River in Yunzhong.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era he followed the Prince of Huaihua, Li Sizhong, in submitting to the interior, and thereby made his home at Heluo River in Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 存信通黠多數，會四夷語，別六蕃書，善戰，識兵勢。
entries.en: Cunxin was clever, shrewd, and skilled at reckoning; he knew the languages of the frontier peoples, could read the six foreign scripts, fought well, and understood how armies should be deployed.
entries.literal: Cunxin was clever and cunning and good at calculation; he knew the languages of the four barbarians, could distinguish the scripts of the six foreign peoples, excelled in battle, and understood military situations.

entries.zh: 初為獻祖親信，從武皇入關平賊，始補軍職，賜姓名。
entries.en: He first served as a trusted intimate of the Ancestor of Offerings, then followed the Martial Emperor through the passes to suppress rebels, received his first military appointment, and was granted the surname and name Li Cunxin.
entries.literal: At first he was a trusted intimate of the Ancestor of Offerings; he followed the Martial Emperor in entering the passes to pacify rebels, was first given a military post, and was granted the surname and personal name.

entries.zh: 大順中，累遷至馬步都校，與李存孝擊張浚軍於平陽。
entries.en: During the Dashun era he rose to commander of cavalry and infantry and, together with Li Cunxiao, attacked Zhang Jun's forces at Pingyang.
entries.literal: In the Dashun era he was repeatedly promoted to commander of horse and foot, and with Li Cunxiao struck Zhang Jun's army at Pingyang.

entries.zh: 時存孝驍勇冠絕，軍中皆下之，惟存信與爭功，由是相惡，有同水火。
entries.en: Cunxiao's martial prowess was then unmatched in the army, and all deferred to him—except Cunxin, who vied with him for credit. From this they grew mutually hostile, irreconcilable as fire and water.
entries.literal: At that time Cunxiao's fierce bravery was unmatched; everyone in the army looked up to him, but only Cunxin competed with him for merit, and thereby they came to hate each other like fire and water.

entries.zh: 及平定潞州，存孝以功望領節度，既而康君立授旄鉞，存孝怒，大剽潞民，燒邑屋，言發流涕，疑存信擯己故也。
entries.en: After Luzhou was pacified, Cunxiao expected the governorship for his achievements, but Kang Junli received the commission instead. Enraged, he looted the people of Lu, burned settlements, and wept openly as he spoke, convinced that Cunxin had turned the Martial Emperor against him.
entries.literal: When Luzhou was pacified, Cunxiao by merit expected to receive the military commission, but then Kang Junli was awarded the banner and axe; Cunxiao was enraged, plundered the people of Lu heavily, burned town houses, spoke with tears streaming, and suspected that Cunxin had slandered him.

entries.zh: 明年，存孝得邢、洺，武皇與之節鉞。
entries.en: The following year Cunxiao took Xing and Ming prefectures, and the Martial Emperor invested him with command and regalia.
entries.literal: The next year Cunxiao obtained Xing and Ming, and the Martial Emperor gave him the commission and regalia.

entries.zh: 存孝慮存信離間，欲立大功以勝之，屢請兵於武皇，請兼併鎮、冀，存信間之，不時許。
entries.en: Fearing Cunxin's intrigues, Cunxiao sought outstanding victories to outshine him. He repeatedly asked the Martial Emperor for reinforcements and permission to seize Zhen and Ji, but Cunxin obstructed him and the requests went unapproved.
entries.literal: Cunxiao feared Cunxin's sowing discord and wished to establish great merit to surpass him; he repeatedly requested troops from the Martial Emperor and asked to annex Zhen and Ji, but Cunxin intervened and permission was not granted in timely fashion.

entries.zh: 大順二年，武皇大舉略地山東，以存信為蕃漢馬步都校，存孝聞之怒，武皇令存質代之，存孝乃謀叛。
entries.en: In the second year of Dashun, the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign east of the mountains and appointed Cunxin commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot. Cunxiao flew into a rage. The Martial Emperor sent Cunzhi to take the post in his place, whereupon Cunxiao began plotting rebellion.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dashun, the Martial Emperor made a great expedition to seize territory in Shandong, appointing Cunxin as commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot; when Cunxiao heard of it he was angry; the Martial Emperor had Cunzhi replace him, and Cunxiao then plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 既誅，以存信為蕃漢都校。
entries.en: After Cunxiao was put to death, Cunxin was appointed overall commander of barbarian and Han forces.
entries.literal: After he was executed, Cunxin was made commander of barbarian and Han forces.

entries.zh: 從討李匡儔，降赫連鐸、白義誠，以功檢校右僕射，從入關討王行瑜，加檢校司空，領郴州刺史。
entries.en: He campaigned against Li Kuangchou, accepted the surrenders of Helian Duo and Bai Yicheng, and was made acting Right Vice Director for his service. He then marched through the passes against Wang Xingyu, was promoted acting Minister of Works, and was given Chen Prefecture.
entries.literal: He followed in attacking Li Kuangchou, received the surrender of Helian Duo and Bai Yicheng, and by merit was made acting Right Vice Director; he followed in entering the passes to attack Wang Xingyu, was further made acting Minister of Works, and held the post of prefect of Chen.

entries.zh: 王鎔，其先回鶻部人也。
entries.en: Wang Rong's ancestors were of the Uighur tribes.
entries.literal: Wang Rong, his ancestors were men of the Uighur tribes.

entries.zh: 遠祖沒諾幹，唐至德中，事鎮州節度使王武俊為騎將。
entries.en: His distant ancestor Mo Nuogan served as a cavalry commander under Wang Wujun, military governor of Zhenzhou, during the Zhide reign of Tang.
entries.literal: A remote ancestor, Mo Nuogan, during the Zhide era of Tang served the Zhenzhou military governor Wang Wujun as a mounted commander.

entries.zh: 武俊嘉其勇幹，畜為假子，號王五哥，其後子孫以王為氏。
entries.en: Wujun admired his courage and competence, took him as an adoptive son, and called him Fifth Brother Wang; his descendants thereafter adopted Wang as their clan surname.
entries.literal: Wujun admired his courage and ability, raised him as an adopted son, and called him Fifth Brother Wang; later generations took Wang as their surname.

entries.zh: 四代祖廷湊，事鎮帥王承宗為牙將。
entries.en: His fourth-generation ancestor Tingcou served the military governor of Zhen, Wang Chengzong, as a guard officer.
entries.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Tingcou served the Zhen commander Wang Chengzong as a guard officer.

entries.zh: 長慶初，承宗卒，穆宗命田宏正為成德軍節度使。
entries.en: In the early Changqing reign Chengzong died, and Emperor Muzong appointed Tian Hongzheng military governor of the Chengde army.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing era Chengzong died, and Muzong appointed Tian Hongzheng as military governor of the Chengde army.

entries.zh: 既而鎮人殺宏正，推廷湊為留後，朝廷不能制，因以旄鉞授之。
entries.en: Soon afterward the garrison of Zhen killed Hongzheng and installed Tingcou as acting governor. The court could not restrain them and therefore granted him the insignia of command.
entries.literal: Soon afterward the men of Zhen killed Hongzheng and elevated Tingcou as acting governor; the court could not control them and therefore invested him with the commander's banner and axe.

entries.zh: 廷湊卒，子元逵尚文宗女壽安公主。
entries.en: When Tingcou died, his son Yuankui married Princess Shou'an, a daughter of Emperor Wenzong.
entries.literal: When Tingcou died, his son Yuankui married Princess Shou'an, daughter of Emperor Wenzong.

entries.zh: 元逵卒，子紹鼎立。
entries.en: When Yuankui died, his son Shaoding succeeded him.
entries.literal: When Yuankui died, his son Shaoding succeeded.

entries.zh: 紹鼎卒，子景崇立。
entries.en: When Shaoding died, his son Jingchong succeeded him.
entries.literal: When Shaoding died, his son Jingchong succeeded.

entries.zh: 皆世襲鎮州節度使，並前史有傳。
entries.en: Each in turn inherited the post of military governor of Zhenzhou, and all have biographies in earlier histories.
entries.literal: All inherited the post of Zhenzhou military governor, and each has a biography in earlier histories.

entries.zh: 景崇位至太尉、中書令，封常山王，中和二年卒。
entries.en: Jingchong rose to Grand Preceptor and Director of the Chancellery, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan, and died in the second year of the Zhonghe era.
entries.literal: Jingchong rose to Grand Preceptor and Director of the Chancellery, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan, and died in the second year of Zhonghe.

entries.zh: 鎔即景崇之子也，年十歲，三軍推襲父位。
entries.en: Rong was Jingchong's son. At the age of ten the three armies installed him in his father's place.
entries.literal: Rong was Jingchong's son; at the age of ten the three armies elevated him to succeed his father.

entries.zh: 大順中，武皇將李存孝既平邢、洺，因獻謀於武皇，欲兼並鎮、定，乃連年出師以擾鎮之屬邑。
entries.en: During the Dashun era the Martial Emperor's general Li Cunxiao, having pacified Xing and Ming, proposed to the Martial Emperor that Zhen and Ding be seized together, and for years thereafter led campaigns harassing the counties under Zhen.
entries.literal: In the Dashun era the Martial Emperor's general Li Cunxiao, having pacified Xing and Ming, offered a plan to the Martial Emperor to annex Zhen and Ding, and thereafter for years led campaigns to harass Zhen's subordinate counties.

entries.zh: 鎔苦之，遣使求救於幽州。
entries.en: Rong was hard pressed and sent envoys to Youzhou seeking aid.
entries.literal: Rong was hard pressed by this and sent envoys to Youzhou seeking rescue.

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》云：時天子蒙塵，九州鼎沸，河東節度使李克用虎視山東，方謀吞據。
entries.en: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 states: At that time the emperor was in exile and the realm seethed; Li Keyong, military governor of Hedong, eyed Shandong like a tiger and was plotting to seize it.
entries.literal: (The Old Book of Tang says: At that time the Son of Heaven was in exile, the Nine Provinces seethed, and the Hedong military governor Li Keyong eyed Shandong like a tiger, plotting annexation.

entries.zh: 鎔以重賂結納，請以修和好。
entries.en: Rong sought alliance through lavish gifts and asked to restore friendly relations.
entries.literal: Rong sought alliance through heavy bribes and requested restored good relations.

entries.zh: 晉軍討孟方立於邢州，鎔常奉以芻糧。
entries.en: When the Jin army attacked Meng Fangli at Xingzhou, Rong regularly supplied them with fodder and provisions.
entries.literal: When the Jin army attacked Meng Fangli at Xingzhou, Rong regularly supplied fodder and grain.

entries.zh: 及方立平，晉將李存孝侵鎔於南部，鎔求援於幽州。）〉
entries.en: After Fangli was defeated, the Jin general Li Cunxiao raided Rong's southern territories, and Rong again sought aid from Youzhou.) 〉
entries.literal: When Fangli was pacified, the Jin general Li Cunxiao raided Rong in the south, and Rong sought aid from Youzhou.) 〉

entries.zh: 自是燕帥李匡威頻歲出軍，以為鎔援。
entries.en: Thereafter the Yan commander Li Kuangwei marched out year after year to aid Rong.
entries.literal: From then on the Yan commander Li Kuangwei for years led armies out as Rong's support.

entries.zh: 時匡威兵勢方盛，以鎔衝弱，將有窺圖之志。
entries.en: Kuangwei's forces were then at their strongest, and seeing Rong young and vulnerable, he began to contemplate seizing his domain.
entries.literal: At that time Kuangwei's military power was at its height; seeing Rong young and weak, he was about to harbor designs of encroachment.

entries.zh: 天祐八年冬十二月，鎔自西山回，宿於鶻營莊，將歸府第，希蒙勸之佗所。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter in the eighth year of Tianyou Rong returned from the western mountains and lodged at Gueying Manor. About to return to headquarters, he was urged by Ximeng to go elsewhere.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the eighth year of Tianyou Rong returned from the western mountains, lodged at Gueying Manor, was about to return to headquarters, and Ximeng urged him elsewhere.

entries.zh: 宦者李宏規謂鎔曰：「方今晉王親當矢石，櫛沐風雨，王殫供軍之租賦，為不急之遊盤，世道未夷，人心多梗，久虛府第，遠出遊從，如樂禍之徒，翻然起變，拒門不納，則王欲何歸！」
entries.en: The eunuch Li Honggui told Rong: "The Prince of Jin now personally faces arrows and braves storms, while Your Highness exhausts supply revenues on frivolous excursions. The world is unsettled and hearts are restless. Headquarters has long stood empty, and you roam far afield—if troublemakers rise and bar the gates, where will Your Highness go!"
entries.literal: The eunuch Li Honggui said to Rong, "At present the Prince of Jin personally faces arrows and stones, bathes in wind and rain, while Your Highness exhausts supply revenues for the army on unurgent excursions and play. The age is not yet settled, hearts are restless, headquarters has long stood empty, and you go far on excursions—if men who delight in trouble suddenly rise in revolt and refuse you at the gate, where will Your Highness go!"

entries.zh: 鎔懼，促歸。
entries.en: Rong was afraid and hastened back.
entries.literal: Rong was afraid and hastened back.

entries.zh: 希蒙譖宏規專作威福，多蓄猜防，鎔由是復無歸誌。
entries.en: Ximeng slandered Honggui for arrogantly wielding power and harboring suspicion, and Rong therefore lost the will to return again.
entries.literal: Ximeng slandered Honggui for arrogantly wielding power and favor and harboring much suspicion and guard; Rong therefore again lost the will to return.

entries.zh: 宏規聞之怒，使親事偏將蘇漢衡率兵擐甲遽至鎔前，抽戈謂鎔曰：「軍人在外已久，願從王歸。」
entries.en: Honggui heard this and grew angry. He sent his aide, the partial commander Su Hanheng, with armored troops rushing to Rong, drew his blade, and said: "The soldiers abroad have been away long and wish to follow Your Highness home."
entries.literal: Honggui heard this and was angry; he sent his aide, the partial commander Su Hanheng, to lead armored troops rushing before Rong, drew his blade and said to Rong, "The soldiers abroad have been long away and wish to follow Your Highness home."

entries.zh: 宏規進曰：「石希蒙說王遊從，勞弊士庶，又結構陰邪，將為大逆。
entries.en: Honggui stepped forward and said, "Shi Ximeng urged Your Highness on excursions, exhausting officials and commoners, and moreover plotted wicked treachery that would become great rebellion.
entries.literal: Honggui stepped forward and said, "Shi Ximeng urged Your Highness on excursions, exhausting officials and commoners, and moreover plotted wicked treachery that would become great rebellion.

entries.zh: 臣已偵視情狀不虛，請王殺之，以除禍本。」
entries.en: I have investigated and found this to be true. I beg Your Highness to kill him and remove the root of the disaster."
entries.literal: Your servant has investigated and found the situation is not false; I beg Your Highness to kill him and remove the root of disaster."

entries.zh: 鎔不聽。
entries.en: Rong would not listen.
entries.literal: Rong would not listen.

entries.zh: 宏規因命軍士聚噪，斬希蒙首抵於前。
entries.en: Honggui therefore ordered the soldiers to raise a clamor, beheaded Ximeng, and presented his head before Rong.
entries.literal: Honggui therefore ordered the soldiers to gather in clamor, beheaded Ximeng, and presented his head before Rong.

entries.zh: 鎔大恐，遂歸。
entries.en: Rong was greatly frightened and returned.
entries.literal: Rong was greatly frightened and therefore returned.

entries.zh: 是日，令其子昭祚與張文禮以兵圍李宏規及行軍司馬李藹宅，並族誅之，詿誤者凡數十家。
entries.en: That day he ordered his son Zhaozhuo and Zhang Wenli to surround the residences of Li Honggui and the campaign secretary Li Ai with troops, executed their entire clans, and implicated several dozen households by error.
entries.literal: That day he ordered his son Zhaozhuo and Zhang Wenli to surround with troops the residences of Li Honggui and the campaign secretary Li Ai, executed their entire clans, and those implicated by error numbered several tens of households.

entries.zh: 又殺蘇漢衡，收部下偏將下獄，窮其反狀，親軍皆恐，復不時給賜，眾益懼。
entries.en: He also killed Su Hanheng, imprisoned his subordinate partial commanders, and exhaustively investigated their rebellion. The personal guard was terrified, rewards were no longer given on time, and fear spread among the troops.
entries.literal: He also killed Su Hanheng, seized his subordinate partial commanders and imprisoned them, exhaustively investigated their rebellion, and the personal guard all feared; moreover rewards were not given in timely fashion, and the masses grew still more afraid.

entries.zh: 文禮因其反側，密諭之曰：「王此夕將坑爾曹，宜自圖之。」
entries.en: Wenli, taking advantage of their restlessness, secretly told them, "The prince intends to bury you all alive tonight. You should plan for yourselves."
entries.literal: Wenli, taking advantage of their restlessness, secretly instructed them, saying, "The prince tonight intends to bury you all alive; you should plan for yourselves."

entries.zh: 眾皆掩泣相謂曰：「王待我如是，我等焉能效忠？」
entries.en: All wept and said to one another, "The prince treats us like this—how can we still serve him loyally?"
entries.literal: All covered their faces weeping and said to one another, "The prince treats us like this—how can we still serve him loyally?"

entries.zh: 是夜，親事軍十餘人，自子城西門逾垣而入，鎔方焚香受籙，軍士二人突入，斷其首，袖之而出，遂焚其府第，煙焰亙天，兵士大亂。
entries.en: That night more than ten personal guard soldiers climbed over the wall from the Zicheng West Gate. Rong was burning incense and receiving talismans when two soldiers burst in, severed his head, tucked it in their sleeves, and fled. They then burned his mansion; smoke and flames filled the sky and the army fell into chaos.
entries.literal: That night more than ten personal guard soldiers entered over the wall from the Zicheng West Gate; Rong was just burning incense and receiving talismans when two soldiers burst in, severed his head, tucked it in their sleeves and went out, then burned his mansion; smoke and flames filled the sky and the soldiers fell into great disorder.

entries.zh: 鎔姬妾數百，皆赴水投火而死。
entries.en: Rong's several hundred concubines all drowned themselves or threw themselves into the fire and died.
entries.literal: Rong's several hundred concubines all rushed into water or threw themselves into fire and died.

entries.zh: 軍校有張友順者，率軍人至張文禮之第，請為留後。
entries.en: An army officer named Zhang Youshun led soldiers to Zhang Wenli's residence and asked that he be made acting governor.
entries.literal: Among the army officers was one Zhang Youshun, who led soldiers to Zhang Wenli's residence and requested that he be made acting governor.

entries.zh: 遂盡殺王氏之族。
entries.en: They then slaughtered the entire Wang clan.
entries.literal: They then killed the entire Wang clan.

entries.zh: 鎔於昭宗朝賜號敦睦保定久大功臣，位至成德軍節度使、守太師、中書令、趙王，梁祖加尚書令。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong, Rong was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Lasting Concord, Preservation, and Endurance, rose to military governor of the Chengde army, Grand Preceptor, Director of the Chancellery, and Prince of Zhao; the Founding Emperor of Liang later added Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, Rong was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Lasting Concord, Preservation, and Endurance, rose to military governor of the Chengde army, Grand Preceptor, Director of the Chancellery, and Prince of Zhao; the Founding Emperor of Liang added Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 初，鎔之遇害，不獲其屍，及莊宗攻下鎮州，鎔之舊人於所焚府第灰間方得鎔之殘骸。
entries.en: When Rong was killed his corpse could not be recovered. After Zhuangzong captured Zhenzhou, Rong's old retainers found his remains among the ashes of the burned mansion.
entries.literal: At first when Rong met disaster his corpse could not be recovered; when Zhuangzong captured Zhenzhou, Rong's old retainers found his remains among the ashes of the burned mansion.

entries.zh: 莊宗命幕客致祭，葬於王氏故塋。
entries.en: Zhuangzong ordered his staff to perform sacrifices and buried him in the Wang family ancestral tomb.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong ordered his staff to perform sacrifices and buried him in the Wang family ancestral tomb.

entries.zh: 鎔長子昭祚，亂之翌日，張文禮索之，斬於軍門。
entries.en: Rong's eldest son Zhaozhuo was demanded by Zhang Wenli the day after the uprising and beheaded at the army gate.
entries.literal: Rong's eldest son Zhaozhuo, on the day after the uprising, was demanded by Zhang Wenli and beheaded at the army gate.

entries.zh: 次子昭誨。
entries.en: His second son was Zhaohui.
entries.literal: The second son was Zhaohui.

entries.zh: 當鎔被禍之夕，昭誨為軍人攜出府第，置之地穴十餘日，乃髡其發，被以僧衣。
entries.en: On the night Rong was killed, soldiers carried Zhaohui out of the mansion, hid him in an underground pit for more than ten days, then shaved his head and dressed him in monk's robes.
entries.literal: On the night Rong met disaster, Zhaohui was carried out of the mansion by soldiers, placed in an underground pit for more than ten days, then had his hair shaved and was clothed in monk's robes.

entries.zh: 屬湖南綱官李震南還，軍士以昭誨托於震，震置之茶褚中。
entries.en: When Li Zhen, transport officer for Hunan, was returning south, the soldiers entrusted Zhaohui to him, and Zhen hid him in a tea crate.
entries.literal: It happened that Li Zhen, transport officer for Hunan, was returning south; the soldiers entrusted Zhaohui to Zhen, and Zhen placed him in a tea crate.

entries.zh: 既至湖湘，乃令依南嶽寺僧習業，歲給其費。
entries.en: Once he reached Hunan he had Zhaohui study under the monks of Nanyue Temple and provided his expenses each year.
entries.literal: Once he reached Hunan he had him study under the monks of Nanyue Temple and provided his expenses each year.

entries.zh: 昭誨年長思歸，震即齎送而還。
entries.en: When Zhaohui grew older and longed to return home, Zhen escorted him back.
entries.literal: When Zhaohui grew older and longed to return, Zhen escorted him back.

entries.zh: 時鎔故將符習為汴州節度使，會昭誨來投，即表其事曰：「故趙王王鎔小男昭誨，年十餘歲遇禍，為人所匿免，今尚為僧，名崇隱，謹令赴闕。」
entries.en: At that time Rong's former general Fu Xi was military governor of Bianzhou. When Zhaohui came to seek refuge, he memorialized: "The late Prince of Zhao Wang Rong's younger son Zhaohui, barely in his teens when disaster struck, was hidden and spared. He is still a monk named Chongyin, and I respectfully send him to court."
entries.literal: At that time Rong's former general Fu Xi was military governor of Bianzhou; when Zhaohui came to seek refuge he memorialized the matter, saying, "The late Prince of Zhao Wang Rong's younger son Zhaohui, more than ten years old when disaster struck, was hidden and spared by others; he is still a monk named Chongyin, and I respectfully send him to court."

entries.zh: 明宗賜衣一襲，令脫僧服。
entries.en: Emperor Mingzong granted him a suit of clothing and ordered him to remove his monk's robes.
entries.literal: Emperor Mingzong granted him one suit of clothing and ordered him to remove his monk's robes.

entries.zh: 頃之，昭誨稱前成德軍中軍使、檢校太傅，詣中書陳狀，特授朝議大夫、檢校考功郎中、司農少卿，賜金紫。
entries.en: Before long Zhaohui claimed his former title of central army commander of the Chengde army and Honorary Grand Mentor, petitioned the Secretariat, and was specially appointed Grand Master for Discussion, Honorary Director of the Bureau of Merit, and Vice Minister of Agriculture, with gold and purple robes.
entries.literal: Before long Zhaohui claimed his former title of central army commander of the Chengde army and Honorary Grand Mentor, went to the Secretariat to state his case, and was specially appointed Grand Master for Discussion, Honorary Director of the Bureau of Merit, and Vice Minister of Agriculture, with gold and purple robes.

entries.zh: 符習因以女妻之。
entries.en: Fu Xi therefore married his daughter to him.
entries.literal: Fu Xi therefore gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 其後，累曆少列，周顯德中，遷少府監。
entries.en: Thereafter he rose through junior court ranks, and in the Xiande era of Zhou was promoted to Director of the Palace Workshops.
entries.literal: Thereafter he rose through junior court ranks, and in the Xiande era of Zhou was promoted to Director of the Palace Workshops.

entries.zh: 景福二年春，匡威率精騎數萬，再來赴援，會匡威弟匡儔奪據兄位，匡威退無歸路，鎔乃延入府第，館於寶壽佛寺。
entries.en: In the spring of the second year of Jingfu, Kuangwei led tens of thousands of elite cavalry to aid Rong once more. His younger brother Kuangchou had meanwhile seized his place, leaving Kuangwei nowhere to return. Rong therefore welcomed him into his mansion and lodged him at Baoshou Buddhist Temple.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jingfu, Kuangwei led tens of thousands of elite cavalry to come again in aid; it happened that Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou seized his elder brother's position, and with no road of retreat Kuangwei was received by Rong into his mansion and lodged at Baoshou Buddhist Temple.

entries.zh: 鎔以匡威因己而失國，又感其援助之力，事之如父。
entries.en: Because Kuangwei had lost his domain on Rong's account and because Rong was deeply grateful for his aid, Rong treated him like a father.
entries.literal: Rong, because Kuangwei had lost his state on his account and was moved by the power of his aid, treated him like a father.

entries.zh: 五月，鎔謁匡威於其館，匡威陰遣部下伏甲劫鎔，抱持之。
entries.en: In the fifth month Rong visited Kuangwei at his quarters. Kuangwei secretly ordered his men to lie in wait in armor and seize Rong, holding him fast.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Rong visited Kuangwei at his lodging; Kuangwei secretly ordered his subordinates to lie in ambush in armor and seize Rong, holding him fast.

entries.zh: 鎔曰：「公戒部人勿造次。
entries.en: Rong said, "Sir, restrain your men from rash action.
entries.literal: Rong said, "Sir, restrain your men from rash action.

entries.zh: 吾國為晉人所侵，垂將覆滅，賴公濟援之力，幸而獲存。
entries.en: My realm has been invaded by the Jin and was nearly destroyed; only through your rescue have we survived.
entries.literal: My state has been invaded by the men of Jin and was on the verge of destruction; relying on the power of your rescue, by good fortune it has survived.

entries.zh: 今日之事，本所甘心。」
entries.en: What happens today I accept willingly."
entries.literal: What happens today is what I willingly accept."

entries.zh: 即並轡歸府舍。
entries.en: Then they rode side by side back toward the headquarters.
entries.literal: Then side by side on horseback they returned to the mansion.

entries.zh: 鎔軍拒之，竟殺匡威。
entries.en: Rong's troops resisted, and in the end they killed Kuangwei.
entries.literal: Rong's army resisted and in the end killed Kuangwei.

entries.zh: 鎔本疏瘦，時年始十七，當與匡威並轡之時，電雨驟作，屋瓦皆飛。
entries.en: Rong was slight and thin by nature and was then only seventeen. As he rode beside Kuangwei, a sudden thunderstorm broke and roof tiles flew from the buildings.
entries.literal: Rong was by nature slight and thin; he was then only seventeen. When he was riding side by side with Kuangwei, sudden thunder and rain broke out and roof tiles flew everywhere.

entries.zh: 有一人於缺垣中望見鎔，鎔就之，遽挾於馬上，肩之而去。
entries.en: A man glimpsed Rong through a broken wall. Rong went to him, and the man swiftly lifted him onto a horse and carried him away on his shoulders.
entries.literal: A man saw Rong through a broken wall; Rong went to him, and he swiftly lifted him onto the horse and carried him off on his shoulders.

entries.zh: 翌日，鎔但覺項痛頭偏，蓋因為有力者所挾，不勝其苦故也。
