entries.en: The next day Rong's neck ached and his head was tilted to one side, apparently from being gripped too forcefully by a strong man.
entries.literal: The next day Rong felt only pain in his neck and his head tilted to one side—apparently because he had been gripped by a man of strength and could not bear the pain.

entries.zh: 既而訪之，則曰墨君和，乃鼓刀之士也，遂厚賞之。
entries.en: When Rong inquired afterward, the man was Mo Junhe, a butcher by trade, and Rong rewarded him generously.
entries.literal: When he inquired afterward, the man was named Mo Junhe, a butcher by trade, and Rong richly rewarded him.

entries.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》引《劉氏耳目記》云：真定墨君和，幼名三旺。
entries.en: (The 《Taiping Guangji》 cites the 《Liu Family Ear-and-Eye Record》: Mo Junhe of Zhending, childhood name Sanwang.
entries.literal: (The Taiping Guangji cites the Liu Family Ear-and-Eye Record, which says: Mo Junhe of Zhending, childhood name Sanwang.

entries.zh: 眉目棱岸，肌膚若鐵，年十五六。
entries.en: His features were sharp and angular, his skin like iron; he was fifteen or sixteen.
entries.literal: His brows and eyes were angular, his skin like iron; he was fifteen or sixteen years old.

entries.zh: 趙王鎔初即位，曾見之，悅而問曰：「此中何得昆侖兒也？」
entries.en: When Prince Zhao Rong first took the throne he saw him and, delighted, asked, "How does such a Kunlun boy come to be here?"
entries.literal: When Prince Zhao Rong first took the throne he once saw him, was pleased, and asked, "How does such a Kunlun boy come to be here?"

entries.zh: 問其姓，與形質相應，即呼為墨昆侖，因以皂衣賜之。
entries.en: When he learned his surname and found it matched his appearance, he called him Ink Kunlun and gave him black robes.
entries.literal: When he asked his surname and it matched his appearance, he called him Ink Kunlun and therefore gave him black robes.

entries.zh: 是時，常山縣邑屢為并州中軍所侵掠，趙之將卒疲於戰敵。
entries.en: At that time the counties of Changshan suffered repeated raids from Bingzhou's central army, and Zhao's officers and soldiers were worn down by fighting.
entries.literal: At that time the counties of Changshan were repeatedly raided by the central army of Bingzhou, and the Zhao generals and soldiers were worn out by battle.

entries.zh: 告急於燕王，李匡威率師五萬來救之。
entries.en: Rong urgently appealed to the Prince of Yan, and Li Kuangwei led fifty thousand troops to the rescue.
entries.literal: He reported urgency to the Prince of Yan, and Li Kuangwei led an army of fifty thousand to rescue him.

entries.zh: 並人攻陷數城。
entries.en: The Bing forces had already captured several cities.
entries.literal: The men of Bing had already captured several cities.

entries.zh: 燕王聞之，躬領五萬騎徑與晉師戰於元氏，晉師敗績。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yan heard this, he personally led fifty thousand cavalry to meet the Jin army head-on at Yuanshi and defeated them.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yan heard this, he personally led fifty thousand cavalry straight to battle the Jin army at Yuanshi, and the Jin army was defeated.

entries.zh: 趙王感燕王之德，椎牛灑酒，大犒於稾城，輦金二十萬以謝之。
entries.en: Grateful for the Prince of Yan's aid, Prince Zhao slaughtered cattle and poured libations, hosted a grand feast at Gaocheng, and sent two hundred thousand in gold as thanks.
entries.literal: Prince Zhao, grateful for the Prince of Yan's virtue, slaughtered cattle and poured libations, held a great feast at Gaocheng, and sent two hundred thousand in gold to thank him.

entries.zh: 燕王歸國，比及境上，為其弟匡儔所拒，趙人以其有德於我，遂營東圃以居之。
entries.en: On his return the Prince of Yan was blocked at the border by his brother Kuangchou. Because the Zhao people felt indebted to him, they built the Eastern Garden for his residence.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yan returned to his state, but when he reached the border he was blocked by his younger brother Kuangchou; because the Zhao people felt he had shown them virtue, they built the Eastern Garden for his residence.

entries.zh: 燕王自以失國，又見趙王之幼，乃圖之。
entries.en: Having lost his realm and seeing Prince Zhao's youth, the Prince of Yan then plotted against him.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yan, having lost his state and seeing Prince Zhao young, then plotted against him.

entries.zh: 遂伏甲俟趙王，旦至，即使擒之。
entries.en: He concealed armed men and waited; at dawn when the prince arrived, he had him seized.
entries.literal: He then concealed soldiers in armor and waited for Prince Zhao; at dawn when he arrived, he had him seized at once.

entries.zh: 趙王請曰：「某承先代基構，主此山河，每被鄰寇侵漁，困於守備，賴大王武略，累挫戎鋒，獲保宗祧，實資恩力。
entries.en: Prince Zhao pleaded: "I inherited my ancestors' foundation and hold this domain. Constantly harassed by neighboring enemies and hard pressed in defense, I rely on Your Highness's military prowess, which has repeatedly turned back the enemy and preserved my ancestral rites. I owe this entirely to your gracious aid.
entries.literal: Prince Zhao pleaded, "I have inherited the foundation laid by former generations and hold this land and rivers; repeatedly harassed by neighboring enemies and hard pressed in defense, I rely on Your Highness's martial strategy, which has repeatedly blunted the enemy's edge and preserved the ancestral rites—truly I owe this to your gracious power.

entries.zh: 顧惟幼懦，夙有卑誠，望不匆匆，可伸交讓。
entries.en: I am young and timid and have always meant you honor; I beg you not to rush matters, so that we may yield to one another.
entries.literal: I am only young and timid and have long held humble sincerity; I hope you will not be hasty, so that we may yield to one another.

entries.zh: 願與大王同歸衙署，即軍府必不拒違。」
entries.en: Let us return together to headquarters—the military prefecture will surely not refuse."
entries.literal: I wish to return with Your Highness together to headquarters; then the military prefecture will surely not refuse or disobey."

entries.zh: 燕王以為然，遂與趙王並轡而進。
entries.en: The Prince of Yan agreed and rode side by side with Prince Zhao as they went forward.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yan thought this right and therefore rode side by side with Prince Zhao as they advanced.

entries.zh: 俄有大風並黑雲起於城上，大雨雷電，至東角門內，有勇夫袒臂旁來，拳毆燕之介士，即挾負趙王逾垣而走，遂得歸公府。
entries.en: Suddenly fierce winds and black clouds rose above the city, followed by heavy rain and thunder. At the East Corner Gate a bare-armed brave man appeared, struck the Yan bodyguards, seized Prince Zhao, and carried him over the wall to escape back to the palace.
entries.literal: Soon fierce wind and black clouds rose above the city, with heavy rain and thunder; at the East Corner Gate a brave man came from the side with bare arms, struck the Yan bodyguards with his fists, then seized Prince Zhao and carried him over the wall and fled, and thus he was able to return to the palace.

entries.zh: 問其姓名，君和恐其難記，但言曰：「硯中之物。」
entries.en: Asked his name, Junhe, fearing it would be forgotten, simply said, "The thing in the inkstone."
entries.literal: When asked his name, Junhe, fearing it would be hard to remember, only said, "The thing in the inkstone."

entries.zh: 王心志之。
entries.en: The prince remembered this.
entries.literal: The prince kept it in mind.

entries.zh: 左右軍士既見主免難，遂逐燕王。
entries.en: Once the guards saw their lord safe, they drove off the Prince of Yan.
entries.literal: Once the guards saw their lord escape danger, they drove off the Prince of Yan.

entries.zh: 燕王退走於東圃，趙人圍而殺之。
entries.en: The Prince of Yan retreated to the Eastern Garden, where Zhao forces surrounded and killed him.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yan retreated to the Eastern Garden, and the Zhao men surrounded and killed him.

entries.zh: 趙王既免燕王之難，召墨生以千金賞之，兼賜上第一區，良田萬畝，仍恕其十死，奏授光祿大夫。）〉
entries.en: After escaping this danger, Prince Zhao summoned the Ink Scholar and rewarded him with a thousand gold pieces, a top residence, ten thousand mu of fertile fields, exemption from ten death sentences, and a memorial appointing him Grand Master for Splendorous Enjoyment.) 〉
entries.literal: After Prince Zhao escaped the Prince of Yan's peril, he summoned the Ink Scholar and rewarded him with a thousand in gold, also granting him a top residence and ten thousand mu of fertile fields, exempting him from ten death sentences, and memorializing to appoint him Grand Master for Splendorous Enjoyment.) 〉

entries.zh: 鎔既失燕軍之援，會武皇出師以逼真定，鎔遣使謝罪，出絹二十萬匹，及具牛酒犒軍，自是與鎔俱修好如初。
entries.en: Having lost Yan military support, Rong found the Martial Emperor marching toward Zhending. He sent envoys to apologize, offered two hundred thousand bolts of silk, and supplied cattle and wine to reward the army; from then on he and the Jin were reconciled as before.
entries.literal: Rong having lost Yan army support, it happened that the Martial Emperor led an expedition pressing toward Zhending; Rong sent envoys to apologize, offered two hundred thousand bolts of silk, and provided cattle and wine to reward the army; from then on he and Jin were reconciled as before.

entries.zh: 洎梁祖兼有山東，虎視天下，鎔卑辭厚禮，以通和好。
entries.en: Once the Founding Emperor of Liang controlled Shandong and eyed the realm, Rong used humble words and lavish gifts to maintain friendly relations.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor of Liang had taken all of Shandong and eyed the realm like a tiger, Rong used humble words and rich gifts to maintain good relations.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：羅紹威諷鎔絕太原，共尊全忠，鎔依違，全忠不悅。）〉
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Luo Shaowei urged Rong to break with Taiyuan and jointly honor Quanzhong; Rong wavered, and Quanzhong was displeased.) 〉
entries.literal: (The New Book of Tang: Luo Shaowei urged Rong to break with Taiyuan and jointly honor Quanzhong; Rong wavered, and Quanzhong was displeased.) 〉

entries.zh: 光化三年秋，梁祖將吞河朔，乃親征鎮、定，縱其軍燔鎮之關城。
entries.en: In the autumn of the third year of Guanghua the Founding Emperor of Liang planned to annex the Hebei region and personally campaigned against Zhen and Ding, while his troops burned Zhen's border fortresses.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Guanghua the Founding Emperor of Liang was about to swallow the Hebei region and therefore personally campaigned against Zhen and Ding, letting his army burn Zhen's border fortresses.

entries.zh: 鎔謂賓佐曰：「事急矣，謀其所向。」
entries.en: Rong told his staff, "The crisis is upon us—we must decide what to do."
entries.literal: Rong said to his staff, "The matter is urgent; let us plan where to turn."

entries.zh: 判官周式者，有口辯，出見梁祖。
entries.en: His secretary Zhou Shi was a skilled speaker and went out to meet the Founding Emperor of Liang.
entries.literal: The secretary Zhou Shi was eloquent in speech and went out to meet the Founding Emperor of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁祖盛怒，逆謂式曰：「王令公朋附並汾，違盟爽信，敝賦業已及此，期於無舍！」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor was furious and confronted Shi: "Lord Wang has allied with Bing and Fen, broken his treaty, and violated his word. My army has already reached your borders, and I intend to leave no quarter!"
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor was greatly angry and confronted Shi, saying, "Lord Wang has allied with Bing and Fen, broken the covenant and violated trust; my army has already reached here, and I intend to leave no quarter!"

entries.zh: 式曰：「公為唐室之桓、文，當以禮義而成霸業，反欲窮兵黷武，天下其謂公何！」
entries.en: Shi replied, "Your Lordship is the Huan and Wen of the Tang house and should establish hegemony through ritual and righteousness. Instead you wish to exhaust armies in ceaseless warfare—what will the realm say of you!"
entries.literal: Shi said, "Your Lordship is the Huan and Wen of the Tang house and should establish hegemony through ritual and righteousness; instead you wish to exhaust the armies in ceaseless warfare—what will the realm say of you!"

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：李嗣昭攻洺州，全忠自將擊走之，得鎔與嗣昭書，全忠怒，引軍攻鎔。
entries.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Li Sizhao attacked Mingzhou; Quanzhong personally led troops and drove him off, discovered letters between Rong and Sizhao, grew angry, and led an army against Rong.
entries.literal: (The New Book of Tang: Li Sizhao attacked Mingzhou; Quanzhong personally led troops and drove him off, obtained letters between Rong and Sizhao, was angry, and led an army to attack Rong.

entries.zh: 周式請見全忠，全忠即出書示式曰：「嗣昭在者，宜速遣。」
entries.en: Zhou Shi requested an audience; Quanzhong produced the letters and showed them to Shi, saying, "If Sizhao is present, send him away at once."
entries.literal: Zhou Shi requested an audience with Quanzhong; Quanzhong at once produced the letters and showed them to Shi, saying, "If Sizhao is present, he should be sent away at once."

entries.zh: 式曰：「王公所與和者，息人鋒鏑間耳。
entries.en: Shi replied, "Lord Wang's alliances were merely to silence weapons for a time.
entries.literal: Shi said, "What Lord Wang made peace over was merely to still weapons and blades for a time.

entries.zh: 況繼奉天子詔和解，能無一番紙墜北路乎？
entries.en: Moreover, having followed the Son of Heaven's decree for reconciliation, how could there not be occasional correspondence heading north?
entries.literal: Moreover, having followed the Son of Heaven's decree for reconciliation, how could there not be occasional letters falling toward the northern road?

entries.zh: 太原與趙本無恩，嗣昭庸肯入耶！」）〉
entries.en: Taiyuan and Zhao owe each other no favor—why would Sizhao enter at all!" ) 〉
entries.literal: Taiyuan and Zhao owe each other no favor—why would Sizhao be willing to enter!" ) 〉

entries.zh: 梁祖喜，引式袂而慰之曰：「前言戲之耳！」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor was pleased, took Shi's sleeve, and comforted him: "My earlier words were only in jest!"
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor was pleased, took Shi's sleeve and comforted him, saying, "My earlier words were only in jest!"

entries.zh: 即送牛酒貨幣以犒軍。
entries.en: He then sent cattle, wine, and goods to reward the army.
entries.literal: He then sent cattle, wine, and goods to reward the army.

entries.zh: 式請鎔子昭祚及大將梁公儒、李宏規子各一人往質於汴。
entries.en: Shi requested that Rong's son Zhaozhuo and one son each of the great generals Liang Gongru and Li Honggui be sent as hostages to Bian.
entries.literal: Shi requested that Rong's son Zhaozhuo and one son each of the great generals Liang Gongru and Li Honggui go as hostages to Bian.

entries.zh: 梁祖以女妻昭祚。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor of Liang married his daughter to Zhaozhuo.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor of Liang gave his daughter in marriage to Zhaozhuo.

entries.zh: 及梁祖稱帝，鎔不得已，行其正朔。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor of Liang declared himself emperor, Rong had no choice but to adopt his calendar.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor of Liang declared himself emperor, Rong had no choice but to adopt his calendar.

entries.zh: 其後梁祖常慮河朔悠久難製，會羅紹威卒，因欲除移鎮、定。
entries.en: Thereafter the Founding Emperor of Liang constantly worried that the Hebei provinces would long resist control. When Luo Shaowei died, he sought to replace the governors of Zhen and Ding.
entries.literal: Thereafter the Founding Emperor of Liang constantly worried that the Hebei region would long resist control; when Luo Shaowei died, he therefore sought to remove and replace the governors of Zhen and Ding.

entries.zh: 先遣親軍三千，分據鎔深、冀二郡，以鎮守為名。
entries.en: He first sent three thousand personal guards to occupy Rong's Shen and Ji prefectures, nominally to garrison them.
entries.literal: He first sent three thousand personal guards to occupy separately Rong's Shen and Ji prefectures, in the name of garrison defense.

entries.zh: 又遣大將王景仁、李思安率師七萬，營於柏鄉。
entries.en: He also dispatched the great generals Wang Jingren and Li Si'an with seventy thousand troops, encamped at Baixiang.
entries.literal: He also sent the great generals Wang Jingren and Li Si'an leading an army of seventy thousand, encamped at Baixiang.

entries.zh: 鎔遣使告急莊宗，莊宗命周德威率兵應之；
entries.en: Rong urgently appealed to Emperor Zhuangzong, who ordered Zhou Dewei to lead troops in response;
entries.literal: Rong sent envoys in urgent appeal to Emperor Zhuangzong; Zhuangzong ordered Zhou Dewei to lead troops in response;

entries.zh: 鎔復奉唐朝正朔，稱天祐七年。
entries.en: Rong again adopted the Tang calendar, dating his reign the seventh year of Tianyou.
entries.literal: Rong again adopted the Tang court calendar, dating it the seventh year of Tianyou.

entries.zh: 及破梁軍於高邑，我軍大振，自是遣大將王德明率三十七都從莊宗征伐，收燕降魏，皆預其功，然鎔未嘗親軍遠出。
entries.en: After the Liang army was defeated at Gaoyi our forces were greatly heartened. Thereafter the great general Wang Deming led thirty-seven commands in Zhuangzong's campaigns, sharing in the conquest of Yan and the submission of Wei, yet Rong never personally led armies far afield.
entries.literal: When the Liang army was defeated at Gaoyi our army was greatly heartened; from then on the great general Wang Deming led thirty-seven commands following Zhuangzong in campaigns, in conquering Yan and subduing Wei all sharing in the merit, yet Rong never personally led armies far afield.

entries.zh: 八年七月，鎔至承天軍，與莊宗合宴同盟，奉觴獻壽，以申感概。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the eighth year Rong came to Chengtian army, joined Zhuangzong in an allied feast, offered wine and birthday wishes, and expressed his gratitude.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year Rong came to Chengtian army, joined Zhuangzong in a allied feast, offered wine and birthday wishes, to express gratitude.

entries.zh: 莊宗以鎔父友，曲加敬異，為之聲歌，鎔亦報之，謂莊宗為四十六舅。
entries.en: Zhuangzong, considering Rong a friend of his father, showed him special respect and sang for him; Rong reciprocated, calling Zhuangzong his forty-sixth uncle.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong, considering Rong his father's friend, showed special respect and sang for him; Rong also responded, calling Zhuangzong his forty-sixth uncle.

entries.zh: 中飲，莊宗抽佩刀斷衿為盟，許女妻鎔子昭誨。
entries.en: Mid-feast Zhuangzong drew his sword and severed his collar in alliance, promising his daughter in marriage to Rong's son Zhaohui.
entries.literal: Mid-feast Zhuangzong drew his sword and severed his collar in alliance, promising his daughter in marriage to Rong's son Zhaohui.

entries.zh: 因茲堅附於莊宗矣。
entries.en: From this he was firmly bound to Zhuangzong.
entries.literal: From this he was firmly attached to Zhuangzong.

entries.zh: 鎔自幼聰悟，然仁而不武，征伐出於下，特以作藩數世。
entries.en: Rong was intelligent from youth, yet benevolent rather than martial; warfare was left to subordinates, and he held his post only because his clan had governed the frontier for generations.
entries.literal: Rong was intelligent from youth, yet benevolent and not martial; campaigns came from subordinates, sustained only because his clan had governed the frontier for generations.

entries.zh: 專製四州，高屏塵務，不親軍政，多以閹人秉權，出納決斷，悉聽所為。
entries.en: Controlling four prefectures, he shielded himself from mundane affairs and never personally handled military administration. Eunuchs mostly wielded power, and revenue and decisions were entirely at their discretion.
entries.literal: Controlling four prefectures exclusively, he screened himself from mundane affairs, did not personally handle military administration, mostly let eunuchs wield power, and revenue and decisions were entirely at their discretion.

entries.zh: 皆雕靡第舍，崇飾園池，植奇花異木，遞相誇尚。
entries.en: All built extravagant mansions and ornate gardens and ponds, planting exotic flowers and rare trees, each trying to outdo the other.
entries.literal: All built extravagant mansions, adorned gardens and ponds, planted exotic flowers and rare trees, each trying to outdo the other.

entries.zh: 人士皆裒衣博帶，高車大蓋，以事嬉遊，藩府之中，當時為盛。
entries.en: Officials wore loose robes and broad sashes, rode tall carriages with large canopies, and devoted themselves to amusement—the military prefecture was then at its most splendid.
entries.literal: Officials all wore loose robes and broad sashes, rode tall carriages with large canopies, and amused themselves in play; within the military prefecture it was then at its most splendid.

entries.zh: 鎔宴安既久，惑於左道，專求長生之要，常聚緇黃，合煉仙丹，或講說佛經，親受符籙。
entries.en: Long accustomed to ease, Rong became deluded by heterodox arts, obsessively seeking immortality. He constantly gathered monks and Taoists to refine elixirs, or expounded Buddhist sutras and personally received talismans.
entries.literal: Rong, long accustomed to ease, was deluded by heterodox ways, devoted solely to the essentials of longevity, constantly gathered monks and Taoists to refine elixirs, or expounded Buddhist sutras and personally received talismans.

entries.zh: 西山多佛寺，又有王母觀，鎔增置館宇，雕飾土木。
entries.en: The western mountains held many Buddhist temples and also the Queen Mother shrine; Rong added halls and lavishly ornamented the buildings.
entries.literal: The western mountains had many Buddhist temples and also the Queen Mother shrine; Rong added halls and lavishly ornamented the buildings.

entries.zh: 道士王若訥者，誘鎔登山臨水，訪求仙跡，每一出，數月方歸，百姓勞弊。
entries.en: The Taoist Wang Ruone seduced Rong to climb mountains and wade waters seeking immortal traces. Each excursion lasted months before he returned, exhausting the people.
entries.literal: The Taoist Wang Ruone seduced Rong to climb mountains and wade waters seeking traces of immortals; each outing lasted months before he returned, and the people were exhausted.

entries.zh: 王母觀石路既峻，不通輿馬，每登行，命仆妾數下人維錦繡牽持而上。
entries.en: The Queen Mother shrine's stone path was steep and impassable to chariots and horses. Whenever Rong climbed it, he had maids and servants hold brocade to pull him upward.
entries.literal: The stone path of the Queen Mother shrine was steep and impassable to chariots and horses; whenever he climbed he ordered maids and several servants to hold brocade and pull him upward.

entries.zh: 有閹人石希蒙者，奸寵用事，為鎔所嬖，恒與之臥起。
entries.en: A eunuch named Shi Ximeng wielded wicked favor and was beloved by Rong, constantly sharing bed and waking with him.
entries.literal: There was a eunuch named Shi Ximeng who wielded wicked favor in power, was beloved by Rong, and constantly shared bed and waking with him.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：王鎔據鎮、冀以稱王，治將數世；
entries.en: The historian says: Wang Rong held Zhen and Ji and styled himself king, ruling for nearly generations;
entries.literal: The historian says: Wang Rong held Zhen and Ji and styled himself king, ruling for nearly generations;

entries.zh: 處直分易、定以為帥，亦既重侯。
entries.en: Chuzhi held Yi and Ding as commander and was likewise a powerful regional lord.
entries.literal: Chuzhi divided Yi and Ding and became commander, also a heavy noble.

entries.zh: 一則惑佞臣而覆其宗，一則嬖孽子而失其國，其故何哉？
entries.en: One was deluded by sycophantic ministers and his clan was overthrown; one favored an illegitimate son and lost his state. What was the reason?
entries.literal: One was deluded by sycophantic ministers and his clan was overthrown; one favored an illegitimate son and lost his state—what was the reason?

entries.zh: 蓋富貴斯久，仁義不修，目眩於妖妍，耳惑於絲竹，故不能防奸於未兆，察禍於未萌，相繼敗亡，又誰咎也！
entries.en: Surely wealth and honor had lasted so long that benevolence and righteousness were neglected. Eyes were dazzled by seductive beauty and ears bewitched by music. They could not guard against treachery before signs appeared or discern disaster before it sprouted. Successive ruin followed—who else is to blame!
entries.literal: Surely wealth and honor had lasted so long that benevolence and righteousness were not cultivated; eyes were dazzled by seductive beauty and ears bewitched by string and bamboo—therefore they could not guard against treachery before signs appeared or discern disaster before it sprouted; successive ruin followed—who else is to blame!

entries.zh: 建瑭以父蔭少仕軍門。
entries.en: Jiantang entered military service young through his father's standing.
entries.literal: Jiantang, through his father's shadow, entered military service young.

entries.zh: 光化中，典昭德軍。
entries.en: During the Guanghua reign he commanded the Zhaode army.
entries.literal: During Guanghua he commanded the Zhaode army.

entries.zh: 與李嗣昭攻汾州，率先登城，擒叛將李瑭以獻，授檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: With Li Sizhao he attacked Fenzhou, was first over the wall, captured the rebel general Li Tang and presented him, and was appointed acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: With Li Sizhao he attacked Fenzhou, was first to scale the wall, captured the rebel general Li Tang and presented him, and was appointed acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 李思安之圍上黨也，建瑭為前鋒，與總管周德威赴援。
entries.en: When Li Si'an besieged Shangdang, Jiantang served as vanguard and marched with Commander Zhou Dewei to relieve the city.
entries.literal: When Li Si'an besieged Shangdang, Jiantang was vanguard and, with the commander-in-chief Zhou Dewei, went to the relief.

entries.zh: 時汴人夾城深固，援路斷絕，建瑭日引精騎，設伏擒生，夜犯汴營，驅斬千計，敵人不敢芻牧。
entries.en: The Bian army had ringed the city with a tight siege and cut every line of relief. Jiantang led elite cavalry out each day, laid ambushes to take prisoners, and struck Bian camps by night, killing and driving off thousands. The enemy no longer dared graze their horses or gather fodder.
entries.literal: At that time the Bian men had built a tight encirclement around the city and cut the relief route. Jiantang daily led picked horse, set ambushes to seize prisoners alive, and raided the Bian camps by night, driving off and killing men by the thousands; the enemy dared not graze or gather fodder.

entries.zh: 汴將王景仁營於柏鄉，建瑭與周德威先出井陘。
entries.en: The Bian general Wang Jingren encamped at Baixiang. Jiantang and Zhou Dewei marched out first through Jingxing Pass.
entries.literal: The Bian general Wang Jingren encamped at Baixiang; Jiantang and Zhou Dewei went out first through Jingxing Pass.

entries.zh: 高邑之戰，日已晡晚，汴軍有歸誌，建瑭督部落精騎先陷其陣，夾攻魏、滑之間，遂長驅追擊。
entries.en: At the battle of Gaoyi the afternoon was waning and the Bian army was ready to withdraw. Jiantang led tribal elite cavalry to smash their line first, struck them from both flanks between Wei and Hua, and then pursued them at length.
entries.literal: In the battle of Gaoyi the sun was already late in the afternoon and the Bian army showed signs of returning home. Jiantang led tribal picked horse to break their formation first, attacked from both sides between Wei and Hua, and then drove in long pursuit.

entries.zh: 夜入柏鄉，俘斬數千計，論功加檢校左僕射。
entries.en: They entered Baixiang by night, capturing and killing thousands. For his service he was promoted to acting Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: By night they entered Baixiang, capturing and killing several thousand; for merit he was advanced to acting Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 師還，留戍趙州。
entries.en: When the army marched home, he was left to garrison Zhaozhou.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was left to garrison Zhaozhou.

entries.zh: 汴將氏延賞數犯趙之南鄙，建瑭設伏柏鄉，獲延賞，獻之。
entries.en: The Bian general Shi Yanzhang repeatedly raided southern Zhao. Jiantang ambushed him at Baixiang, captured him, and presented him.
entries.literal: The Bian general Shi Yanzhang repeatedly raided the southern borders of Zhao; Jiantang set an ambush at Baixiang, captured Yanzhang, and presented him.

entries.zh: 十二年，魏博歸款，建瑭與符存審前軍屯魏縣。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Weibo submitted. Jiantang and Fu Cunshen marched ahead and encamped at Wei County.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Weibo submitted allegiance; Jiantang and Fu Cunshen advanced and encamped at Wei County.

entries.zh: 十三年，敗劉鄩於元城，收澶州，以建瑭為刺史、檢校司空、外衙騎軍都將。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he defeated Liu Yan at Yuancheng and recovered Chanzhou. Jiantang was made prefect, acting Minister of Works, and commander of the outer-office cavalry.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he defeated Liu Yan at Yuancheng and recovered Chanzhou; Jiantang was made prefect, acting Minister of Works, and commander of the outer-office mounted army.

entries.zh: 尋曆貝、相二州刺史，屯於德勝。
entries.en: He soon served in turn as prefect of Bei and Xiang and garrisoned at Desheng.
entries.literal: Soon he served in succession as prefect of Bei and Xiang and garrisoned at Desheng.

entries.zh: 十八年，與閻寶討張文禮，為馬軍都將。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he joined Yan Bao in the campaign against Zhang Wenli as commander of the horse army.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, with Yan Bao he campaigned against Zhang Wenli and served as commander of the horse army.

entries.zh: 八月，收趙州，獲刺史王鋋。
entries.en: In the eighth month he recovered Zhaozhou and captured Prefect Wang Rong.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he recovered Zhaozhou and captured the prefect Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 進逼鎮州，為流矢所中，卒於軍，時年四十六。
entries.en: As he pressed the attack on Zhenzhou, a stray arrow struck him and he died in camp at forty-six.
entries.literal: Advancing to press Zhenzhou, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the army, aged forty-six.

entries.zh: 史儼，代州雁門人。
entries.en: Shi Yan was from Yanmen in Daizhou.
entries.literal: Shi Yan was a man of Yanmen in Daizhou.

entries.zh: 以便騎射給事於武皇。
entries.en: He served the Martial Emperor as a mounted attendant skilled in riding and archery.
entries.literal: He served the Martial Emperor as a mounted attendant skilled in riding and shooting.

entries.zh: 為帳中親將，驍果絕眾，善擒生設伏，望塵揣敵，所向皆捷。
entries.en: He was an intimate general in headquarters, fiercer than any in the army, skilled at taking prisoners and laying ambushes. He could read the enemy from the dust on the horizon and won wherever he fought.
entries.literal: He was an intimate general in the tent, fierce and bold beyond the host, skilled at seizing prisoners alive and setting ambushes; seeing dust he could gauge the enemy, and wherever he went he prevailed.

entries.zh: 自武皇入定三輔，誅黃巢，每出師皆從。
entries.en: From the time the Martial Emperor secured the three capitals and killed Huang Chao, he followed on every campaign.
entries.literal: From the time the Martial Emperor settled the three auxiliaries and executed Huang Chao, he followed on every campaign.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，從討王行瑜，師次渭北，遣儼率五百騎護駕石門。
entries.en: During Qianning he joined the campaign against Wang Xingyu. When the army halted north of the Wei, Yan was sent with five hundred cavalry to escort the emperor at Shimen.
entries.literal: During Qianning he followed the campaign against Wang Xingyu. When the army halted north of the Wei, Yan was sent to lead five hundred horse to escort the carriage at Shimen.

entries.zh: 時京城大擾，士庶多散布南山。
entries.en: The capital was in turmoil, and officials and commoners had fled into the southern hills.
entries.literal: At that time the capital was in great turmoil and gentry and commoners had largely scattered to the southern hills.

entries.zh: 儼分騎警衛，比駕還京，盜賊不作，以功授檢校右散騎常侍，屯於三橋者累月，昭宗寵錫優異。
entries.en: Yan divided his cavalry for patrol and guard. By the time the emperor returned to the capital, banditry had ceased. For his service he was appointed acting Right Regular Attendant and garrisoned the Three Bridges for months, while Emperor Zhaozong showered him with exceptional favors.
entries.literal: Yan divided his horse for patrol and guard; by the time the carriage returned to the capital bandits did not act. For merit he was appointed acting Right Regular Attendant; he garrisoned at the Three Bridges for months, and Emperor Zhaozong favored him with exceptional gifts.

entries.zh: 明年，與李承嗣率騎渡河援兗、鄆。
entries.en: The following year he and Li Chengsi led cavalry across the river to relieve Yan and Yun.
entries.literal: The next year, with Li Chengsi he led horse across the river to relieve Yan and Yun.

entries.zh: 時汴軍雄盛，自青、徐、兗、鄆，柵壘相望。
entries.en: The Bian army was then at its height. From Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yun, stockades and ramparts stretched in an unbroken line.
entries.literal: At that time the Bian army was powerful; from Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yun, stockades and ramparts stood in sight of one another.

entries.zh: 儼與騎將安福順等，每以數千騎直犯營壘，左俘右斬，汴軍為之披靡。
entries.en: Yan and the cavalry commander An Fushun often led several thousand horsemen straight into enemy camps, taking prisoners on one flank and killing on the other until the Bian army broke before them.
entries.literal: Yan with the mounted commander An Fushun and others often took several thousand horse straight against the camps, capturing on the left and slaying on the right, and the Bian army was scattered before them.

entries.zh: 及朱瑾失守，與李承嗣等奔淮南。
entries.en: When Zhu Jin lost his territory, he fled with Li Chengsi and others to Huainan.
entries.literal: When Zhu Jin lost his position, he fled with Li Chengsi and others to Huainan.

entries.zh: 淮人比善水軍，不閑騎射，既得儼等，軍聲大振，尋挫汴軍於清口。
entries.en: The Huainan forces had excelled at naval warfare but were unskilled in cavalry. Once they had Yan and his men, their army's prestige soared, and they soon defeated the Bian army at Qingkou.
entries.literal: The Huai men had been skilled in naval warfare and unpracticed in mounted archery; once they obtained Yan and the others, their army's renown greatly rose, and soon they defeated the Bian army at Qingkou.

entries.zh: 其後並鍾傳，擒杜洪，削錢鏐，成行密之霸跡者，皆儼與承嗣之力也。
entries.en: Their later conquests of Zhong Chuan, capture of Du Hong, and reduction of Qian Liu—the steps by which Xingmi built his hegemony—owed to the strength of Yan and Chengsi.
entries.literal: Thereafter, in uniting Zhong Chuan, capturing Du Hong, and reducing Qian Liu—accomplishing Xingmi's path to hegemony—it was all through the strength of Yan and Chengsi.

entries.zh: 淮人館遇甚厚，妻孥第舍必推其甲，故儼等盡其死力。
entries.en: The Huainan court treated them lavishly, always giving their families the finest houses, and Yan and his companions repaid them with unstinting loyalty.
entries.literal: The Huai men lodged and treated them very generously, always giving their wives and children the finest houses, and therefore Yan and the others gave their utmost strength even unto death.

entries.zh: 〈（《十國春秋》云：儼累官滁州刺史。）〉
entries.en: (The Spring and Autumn of the Ten Kingdoms states that Yan eventually rose to prefect of Chuzhou.) 〉
entries.literal: (The Spring and Autumn of the Ten Kingdoms says: Yan rose in office to prefect of Chuzhou.) 〉

entries.zh: 天祐十三年，卒於廣陵。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Tianyou he died at Guangling.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianyou he died at Guangling.

entries.zh: 蓋寓，蔚州人。
entries.en: Gai Yu was from Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Gai Yu was a man of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 祖祚，父慶，世為州之牙將。
entries.en: His grandfather was Zuo and his father Qing; for generations the family had served as guard officers of the prefecture.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Zuo and his father Qing; for generations they had been guard officers of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 武皇起雲中，寓與康君立等推轂佐佑之，因為腹心。
entries.en: When the Martial Emperor rose in Yunzhong, Yu joined Kang Junli and others in raising and supporting him and became one of his closest confidants.
entries.literal: When the Martial Emperor rose in Yunzhong, Yu with Kang Junli and others supported and aided him, and thereby became his trusted core.

entries.zh: 武皇節制雁門，署職為都押牙，領嵐州刺史。
entries.en: When the Martial Emperor took command of Yanmen, Yu was appointed chief guard officer and prefect of Lanzhou.
entries.literal: When the Martial Emperor commanded Yanmen, Yu was appointed chief guard officer and acted as prefect of Lanzhou.

entries.zh: 洎移鎮太原，改左都押牙、檢校左僕射。
entries.en: When the Martial Emperor moved his headquarters to Taiyuan, Yu became left chief guard officer and acting Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: When he moved his garrison to Taiyuan, Yu was changed to left chief guard officer and acting Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 武皇與之決事，言無不從，凡出征伐，靡不衛從。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor consulted him on every decision and never refused his counsel. He accompanied him on every campaign.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor decided affairs with him and never rejected his words; on every campaign he never failed to attend and escort him.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：光啟二年，駕幸興元，大將蓋寓說克用曰：「 鑾輿播遷，天下皆歸咎於我，今不誅朱玫，黜李煴，無以自湔洗。」
entries.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: In the second year of Guangqi the emperor went to Xingyuan. Great general Gai Yu said to Li Keyong, "The imperial carriage has been driven into exile, and the realm blames us for it. Unless we execute Zhu Mei and remove Li Yun, we cannot clear our name."
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: In the second year of Guangqi the carriage went to Xingyuan. The great general Gai Yu said to Keyong, "The imperial carriage has been driven into exile, and the realm blames it all on us. If we do not now execute Zhu Mei and remove Li Yun, we cannot cleanse ourselves."

entries.zh: 克用從之。
entries.en: Li Keyong followed his advice.
entries.literal: Keyong followed this advice.

entries.zh: 又，《通鑒考異》引《紀年錄》云：偽使至太原，太祖詰其事狀，曰：「皆朱玫所為。」
entries.en: The Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror also cites the Chronicle Record: When a false envoy reached Taiyuan, the Founder questioned him about the affair and said, "Zhu Mei did it all."
entries.literal: Moreover, Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror cites the Chronicle Record: A false envoy reached Taiyuan. The Founder interrogated him on the facts and said, "It was all done by Zhu Mei."

entries.zh: 將斬之以徇，大將蓋寓等言云云。
entries.en: He was about to execute him as a warning when Great General Gai Yu and others spoke on his behalf, and so on.
entries.literal: He was about to behead him as a warning when the great general Gai Yu and others spoke, and so forth.

entries.zh: 太祖燔偽詔，械其使，馳檄喻諸鎮曰：「今月二十日，得襄王偽詔及朱玫文字，云：『田令孜脅遷鑾駕，播越梁、洋，行至半塗，六軍變擾，遂至蒼黃而晏駕，不知弑逆者何人。
entries.en: The Founder burned the false edict, put the envoy in fetters, and sent a rapid proclamation to the commands: "On the twentieth of this month I received the false edict of the Prince of Xiang and documents from Zhu Mei stating: 'Tian Lingzi coerced the removal of the imperial carriage into exile in Liang and Yang. Halfway on the road the Six Armies mutinied, and the emperor died in sudden confusion. No one knows who murdered him.
entries.literal: The Founder burned the false edict, put the envoy in fetters, and sent a rapid proclamation to instruct the various commands, saying, "On the twentieth of this month I received the false edict of the Prince of Xiang and documents from Zhu Mei, which state: 'Tian Lingzi coerced the removal of the imperial carriage, driving it into exile in Liang and Yang; halfway on the road the Six Armies muttered and were disturbed, until in sudden confusion the emperor passed away, and it is not known who committed regicide.

entries.zh: 永念丕基不可無主，昨四鎮藩後推朕纂承，已於正殿受冊畢，改元大赦者。』
entries.en: Mindful that the empire cannot be without a ruler, yesterday the four commands and frontier lords urged me to succeed. I have already received investiture in the main hall, changed the era, and proclaimed a great amnesty.'
entries.literal: Ever mindful that the great foundation cannot be without a lord, yesterday the four commands and frontier lords urged me to succeed, and I have already completed receiving the investiture in the main hall and proclaimed a change of era and great amnesty.'

entries.zh: 李煴出自贅疣，名汙藩邸，智昏菽麥，識昧機權。
entries.en: Li Yun is a mere excrescence on the imperial house. His name stains the princely residence. He cannot tell beans from wheat, nor grasp the moment's need.
entries.literal: Li Yun sprang from a mere excrescence, his name stained the princely residence, his wisdom was dimmer than beans and wheat, and his grasp of opportunity was lost.

entries.zh: 李符擄之以塞辭，朱玫賣之以為利。
entries.en: Li Fu seized him to pad empty proclamations; Zhu Mei sold him for profit.
entries.literal: Li Fu seized him to stuff out empty phrases; Zhu Mei sold him for profit.

entries.zh: 呂不韋之奇貨，可見奸邪；
entries.en: Like Lü Buwei's rare commodity, their treachery is plain to see;
entries.literal: Like Lü Buwei's rare commodity, their treachery is plain to see;

entries.zh: 蕭世誠之土囊，期於匪夕。
entries.en: like Xiao Shicheng's sack of earth, their end cannot be far off.
entries.literal: like Xiao Shicheng's sack of earth, their end is expected before many evenings pass.

entries.zh: 近者，當道徑差健步，奉表起居，行朝現住巴、梁，宿衛比無騷動。
entries.en: Recently the court dispatched swift runners with memorials on the emperor's health. The traveling court is at Ba and Liang, and the palace guard has not been disturbed.
entries.literal: Recently the authorities directly dispatched swift runners to present memorials on health and conduct; the traveling court now resides in Ba and Liang, and the palace guard has lately known no disturbance.

entries.zh: 而朱玫脅其孤騃，自號台衡，敢首亂階，明言晏駕，熒惑藩鎮，淩弱廟朝」云云。）〉
entries.en: Yet Zhu Mei coerced this foolish child, styled himself chief of the terrace, dared to lead rebellion, openly declared the emperor dead, deluded the frontier commands, and insulted the ancestral temple and court," and so forth.) 〉
entries.literal: Yet Zhu Mei coerced this foolish child, styled himself chief of the terrace, dared to lead the first step of rebellion, openly declared the emperor's death, deluded the frontier commands, and insulted the ancestral temple and court," and so forth.) 〉

entries.zh: 乾寧二年，從入關討王行瑜，特授檢校太保、開國侯，令邑一千戶，領容管觀察經略使。
entries.en: In the second year of Qianning he marched through the passes against Wang Xingyu and was specially appointed acting Grand Mentor and Marquis Who Founded the State with a fief of one thousand households, and made observation and pacification commissioner of Rong.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianning he followed through the passes to campaign against Wang Xingyu and was specially appointed acting Grand Mentor, Marquis Who Founded the State, with a fief of one thousand households, and made observation and pacification commissioner of Rong.

entries.zh: 光化初，車駕還京，授檢校太傅，封成陽郡公。
entries.en: Early in the Guanghua reign, when the emperor returned to the capital, he was appointed acting Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chengyang.
entries.literal: At the start of Guanghua, when the carriage returned to the capital, he was appointed acting Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chengyang commandery.

entries.zh: 寓性通黠，多智數，善揣人主情。
entries.en: Yu was quick-witted and shrewd, full of stratagems, and skilled at reading his lord's mind.
entries.literal: Yu by nature was quick and shrewd, full of stratagems, and skilled at gauging his lord's feelings.

entries.zh: 武皇性嚴急，左右難事，無委遇者，小有違忤，即置於法，惟寓承顏希旨，規其趨向，婉辭順意，以盡參裨。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor was stern and exacting. Those around him found him hard to serve, and none enjoyed his full trust. The slightest offense brought punishment. Only Yu read his mood, anticipated his wishes, and with gentle words guided him, serving as his closest adviser.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor's nature was stern and urgent; those around him found it hard to serve him, and none were fully entrusted. For the slightest offense they were punished by law. Only Yu met his expression and sought his intent, observed his inclinations, and with gentle words followed his wishes, fully assisting in counsel.

entries.zh: 武皇或暴怒將吏，事將不測，寓欲救止，必佯佐其怒以責之，武皇怡然釋之。
entries.en: When the Martial Emperor flew into a rage against an officer and the man's fate hung in the balance, Yu would feign to join the anger and reproach the victim, and the Martial Emperor would calmly relent.
entries.literal: When the Martial Emperor would fly into rage against generals and officers and the outcome was uncertain, if Yu wished to save and stop it he would feign joining the anger to reproach them, and the Martial Emperor would calmly release them.

entries.zh: 有所諫諍，必征近事以為喻，自武皇鎮撫太原，最推親信，中外將吏，無不景附，朝廷藩鄰，信使結托，先及武皇，次入寓門；
entries.en: When he remonstrated, he always cited recent events as examples. From the time the Martial Emperor secured Taiyuan, Yu was his most trusted intimate. Generals within and without looked to him with admiration. Envoys from court and neighboring commands sought him out—first the Martial Emperor, then Yu's door;
entries.literal: When he offered remonstrance he always cited recent events as analogies. From the time the Martial Emperor pacified and held Taiyuan, Yu was most trusted and intimate; generals and officers within and without none failed to admire and attach themselves to him. Court and neighboring commands bound themselves through envoys—first reaching the Martial Emperor, next entering Yu's gate;

entries.zh: 既總軍中大柄，其名振主，梁祖亦使奸人離間，暴揚於天下，言蓋寓已代李，聞者寒心，武皇略無疑間。
entries.en: and once he held the army's greatest authority, his name overshadowed even his lord's. The Founder of Liang sent agents to spread rumors through the realm that Gai Yu had already replaced Li Keyong. Men who heard it were chilled with fear, yet the Martial Emperor scarcely doubted him.
entries.literal: once he held the great authority of the army his name shook the ruler. The Founder of Liang also sent agents to sow division and spread it openly through the realm that Gai Yu had already replaced Li; those who heard it were chilled at heart, yet the Martial Emperor had hardly any doubt.

entries.zh: 初，武皇既平王行瑜，旋師渭北，暴雨六十日，諸將或請入覲，且云：「天顏咫尺，安得不行覲禮。」
entries.en: After the Martial Emperor had pacified Wang Xingyu, he turned his army north of the Wei. Rain poured for sixty days. Some generals asked to enter the capital for an audience, saying, "The emperor is within reach. How can we fail to pay our respects?"
entries.literal: Earlier, after the Martial Emperor had pacified Wang Xingyu, he turned his army north of the Wei. Rain poured for sixty days. Some generals requested an audience at court and said, "The imperial countenance is within arm's reach—how can we fail to perform the audience rite?"

entries.zh: 武皇意未決，寓白曰：「車駕自石門還京，寢未安席，比為行瑜兄弟驚駭乘輿，今京師未寧，奸宄流議，大王移兵渡渭，必恐復動宸情。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor hesitated. Yu said, "Since the emperor returned from Shimen to the capital, he has not yet rested secure on his throne. Wang Xingyu and his brothers have just terrified the court. The capital is not yet settled, and malicious talk circulates. If you cross the Wei with your army, you will surely alarm the throne again.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor's mind was not yet decided. Yu reported, "Since the carriage returned from Shimen to the capital, it has not yet rested secure on its seat. Lately the carriage was alarmed by Xingyu and his brothers. Now the capital is not yet settled and treacherous talk circulates. If the Great King moves his troops across the Wei, he will surely fear stirring the imperial heart again.

entries.zh: 君臣始終，不必朝覲，但歸藩守，姑務勤王，是忠臣之道也。」
entries.en: Loyalty does not require an audience. Return to your fief, guard it, and devote yourself to supporting the throne. That is the way of a loyal minister."
entries.literal: Between lord and minister from beginning to end, an audience is not necessary; only return to your fief and guard it, and for the moment devote yourself to supporting the throne—that is the way of a loyal minister."

entries.zh: 武皇笑曰：「蓋寓尚阻吾入覲，況天下人哉！」
entries.en: The Martial Emperor laughed and said, "Even Gai Yu blocks my going to court—how much more would the realm!"
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor laughed and said, "Even Gai Yu still blocks my entering for audience—how much more the people of the realm!"

entries.zh: 即日班師。
entries.en: That very day he withdrew the army.
entries.literal: That very day he withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 天祐二年三月，寓病篤，武皇日幸其第，手賜藥餌。
entries.en: In the third month of the second year of Tianyou Yu fell gravely ill. The Martial Emperor visited his house daily and personally sent him medicine.
entries.literal: In the third month of the second year of Tianyou Yu's illness was grave; the Martial Emperor daily visited his residence and personally bestowed medicines.

entries.zh: 初，寓家每事珍膳，窮極海陸，精於府饌，武皇非寓家年獻不食，每幸寓第，其往如歸，恩寵之洽，時我與比；
entries.en: Yu's household prepared delicacies from land and sea, cuisine fit for the palace. The Martial Emperor would eat no New Year's offering except from Yu's kitchen. Whenever he visited Yu's house he came as to his own home. None at the time could compare in favor;
entries.literal: Earlier, in every matter Yu's household prepared rare delicacies, exhausting land and sea, skilled in palace cuisine; the Martial Emperor would not eat what was not presented annually from Yu's house. Whenever he visited Yu's residence he went as though returning home. The fullness of favor and grace—at the time none could compare;

entries.zh: 及其卒也，哭之彌慟。
entries.en: and when Yu died he wept all the more bitterly.
entries.literal: when Yu died he wept all the more bitterly.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，追贈太師。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne he posthumously honored Yu as Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 伊廣，字言，
entries.en: Yi Guang, style name Yan,
entries.literal: Yi Guang, style name Yan,

entries.zh: 〈（原本闕一字。）〉
entries.en: (Originally one character is missing.) 〉
entries.literal: (Originally one character is missing.) 〉

entries.zh: 元和中右僕射慎之後。
entries.en: a descendant of Right Vice Director Shenzhi of the Yuanhe reign.
entries.literal: a descendant of Right Vice Director Shenzhi in the Yuanhe era.

entries.zh: 廣，中和末除授忻州刺史。
entries.en: Guang was appointed prefect of Xinzhou at the end of the Zhonghe reign.
entries.literal: Guang, at the end of Zhonghe, received appointment and commission as prefect of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 遇天下大亂，乃委質於武皇。
entries.en: When the empire fell into chaos he submitted to the Martial Emperor.
entries.literal: He met the great disorder of the realm and thereupon submitted his person to the Martial Emperor.

entries.zh: 廣襟情灑落，善占對，累曆右職，授汾州刺史。
entries.en: Guang was open and easy in manner and skilled at ready replies. He rose through successive staff posts and was appointed prefect of Fenzhou.
entries.literal: Guang's bearing was free and open; he was skilled in ready replies and rose through successive right-hand posts, and was appointed prefect of Fenzhou.

entries.zh: 時武皇主盟，諸侯景附，軍機締結，聘遺旁午，廣奉使稱旨，累遷至檢校司徒。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor then presided over the alliance, and lords flocked to him. Military affairs and diplomatic ties multiplied, and envoys with gifts crossed paths without cease. Guang served on missions to general approval and rose to acting Minister of Education.
entries.literal: At that time the Martial Emperor presided over the alliance; feudal lords admired and attached themselves; military affairs were bound together and envoys with gifts crossed unceasingly. Guang, on missions, met approval and rose in succession to acting Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 乾寧四年，從征劉仁恭，武皇之師不利於成安寨，廣歿於賊。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Qianning he joined the campaign against Liu Rengong. The Martial Emperor's army met defeat at Chengan stockade, and Guang died fighting the enemy.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Qianning he followed the campaign against Liu Rengong. The Martial Emperor's army met ill fortune at Chengan stockade, and Guang died at the hands of the bandits.

entries.zh: 史敬鎔，太原人。
entries.en: Shi Jingrong was from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Shi Jingrong was a man of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 事武皇為帳中綱紀，甚親任之。
entries.en: He served the Martial Emperor as steward of headquarters and enjoyed his deep trust.
entries.literal: He served the Martial Emperor as steward of the tent and was greatly trusted and employed.

entries.zh: 莊宗初嗣晉王位，李克寧陰構異圖，將害莊宗，事發有日矣，克寧密引敬鎔，以邪謀諭之。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong first succeeded to the Jin throne, Li Kening secretly plotted against him and was on the verge of acting. Kening secretly summoned Jingrong and tried to win him to the conspiracy.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong first succeeded to the Jin princedom, Li Kening secretly formed a different design and was about to harm Zhuangzong; the affair had a day to break forth. Kening secretly summoned Jingrong and instructed him with a treacherous plot.

entries.zh: 既而敬鎔白，貞簡太后惶駭，召張承業、李存璋等圖之。
entries.en: Jingrong then reported the plot. Empress Dowager Zhenjian was terrified and summoned Zhang Chengye, Li Cunzhang, and others to act against it.
entries.literal: Thereupon Jingrong reported it. Empress Dowager Zhenjian was alarmed and terrified and summoned Zhang Chengye, Li Cunzhang, and others to plot against it.

entries.zh: 克寧等伏誅，以功累曆郡。
entries.en: Kening and his conspirators were executed. For his service Jingrong rose through successive prefectural posts.
entries.literal: Kening and the others were executed in hiding, and for merit Jingrong rose through successive prefectures.

entries.zh: 同光初，為華州節度使，移鎮安州。
entries.en: Early in the Tongguang reign he was military governor of Huazhou, then transferred his headquarters to Anzhou.
entries.literal: At the start of Tongguang he was military governor of Huazhou and then moved his garrison to Anzhou.

entries.zh: 天成中，入為金吾上將軍。
entries.en: During the Tiancheng reign he entered the capital as general of the Golden Guards.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng he entered the capital as general of the Golden Guards.

entries.zh: 期年，復授鄧州，至鎮數月卒。
entries.en: A year later he was appointed to Dengzhou again. Several months after reaching his post he died.
entries.literal: After a full year he was again appointed to Dengzhou; several months after reaching his post he died.

entries.zh: 贈太尉。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 康君立，蔚州興唐人，世為邊豪。
entries.en: Kang Junli was from Xingtang in Yuzhou, and his family had been powerful border lords for generations.
entries.literal: Kang Junli was a man of Xingtang in Yuzhou; for generations his family had been frontier magnates.

entries.zh: 乾符中，為雲州牙校，事防禦使段文楚。
entries.en: During the Qianfu reign he was a guard officer at Yunzhou under Defense Commissioner Duan Wenchu.
entries.literal: During the Qianfu era he served as a guard officer at Yunzhou and attended the defense commissioner Duan Wenchu.

entries.zh: 時群盜起河南，天下將亂，代北仍歲阻饑，諸部豪傑，咸有嘯聚邀功之志。
entries.en: Bandit armies were rising south of the Yellow River, the empire was sliding toward chaos, and north of Dai famine struck year after year. Leaders in every tribe dreamed of rallying men and winning glory.
entries.literal: At that time bandit hosts rose south of the Yellow River, the realm was on the verge of disorder, and north of Dai suffered famine year after year; heroes of every tribe alike harbored the ambition to rally followers and win merit.

entries.zh: 會文楚稍削軍人儲給，戍兵谘怨。
entries.en: Wenchu had recently reduced the troops' stored provisions, and the garrison soldiers grumbled in anger.
entries.literal: It happened that Wenchu had lately cut the troops' stored rations, and the garrison soldiers murmured in resentment.

entries.zh: 君立與薛鐵山、程懷信、王行審、李存璋等謀曰：「段公懦人，難與共事。
entries.en: Junli plotted with Xue Tieshan, Cheng Huaixin, Wang Xingshen, Li Cunzhang, and others. "Lord Duan is a coward," they said. "We cannot serve under him.
entries.literal: Junli plotted with Xue Tieshan, Cheng Huaixin, Wang Xingshen, Li Cunzhang, and others, saying, "Lord Duan is a timid man and hard to serve with.

entries.zh: 方今四方雲擾，武威不振，丈夫不能於此時立功立事，非人豪也。
entries.en: The realm is in turmoil on every side and martial glory lies idle. A man who cannot win merit now is no true champion.
entries.literal: Now the four quarters are troubled as by storm clouds and martial prestige is not aroused; if a man cannot at such a time establish merit and achievement, he is no true hero.

entries.zh: 吾等雖權係部眾，然以雄勁聞於時者，莫若沙陀部，復又李振武父子勇冠諸軍，吾等合勢推之，則代北之地，旬月可定，功名富貴，事無不濟也。」
entries.en: We command only tribal bands, yet none in this age are fiercer than the Shatuo, and Li Zhenwu and his son outmatch every army. If we join forces and put them forward, we can secure the north of Dai within a month. Fame, wealth, and rank will all be within reach."
entries.literal: Although we are only leaders of tribal bands, of those famed in the age for fierce strength none surpass the Shatuo tribe; moreover, father and son Li Zhenwu are boldest among all armies. If we unite our strength and raise them up, the lands north of Dai can be settled within a month, and fame, merit, wealth, and rank—nothing will fail."

entries.zh: 君立等乃夜謁武皇言曰：「方今天下大亂，天子付將臣以邊事，歲偶饑荒，便削儲給，我等邊人，焉能守死！
entries.en: That night Junli and his companions went to the Martial Emperor. "The empire is in chaos," they said. "The throne leaves the frontier to its generals, yet a single year of famine is enough for them to cut our stores. How can border men die for that?
entries.literal: Junli and the others then visited the Martial Emperor by night and said, "The realm is in great disorder. The Son of Heaven has entrusted border affairs to generals and ministers; because of a year of famine they cut stored rations—how can we border people die in place!

entries.zh: 公家父子，素以威惠及五部，當共除虐帥，以謝邊人，孰敢異議者！」
entries.en: Your father and son have long ruled the five tribes with authority and grace. Join us in removing this cruel commander and answering the frontier. Who would dare object?"
entries.literal: Your house, father and son, have long shown authority and kindness to the five tribes. You should together remove the cruel commander to answer the border people—who would dare dissent!"

entries.zh: 武皇曰：「明天子在上，舉事當有朝典，公等勿輕議。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor replied, "The Son of Heaven still reigns. Any action must follow the laws of the court. Do not speak rashly.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor said, "The enlightened Son of Heaven sits above. Any undertaking must follow court statutes; do not speak lightly of such things.

entries.zh: 予家尊遠在振武，萬一相迫，俟予稟命。」
entries.en: My father is far away at Zhenwu. If you force the issue, wait until I have reported to him."
entries.literal: My honored father is far away at Zhenwu; if we are pressed, wait until I report for orders."

entries.zh: 君立等曰：「事機已泄，遲則變生，曷俟千里谘稟！」
entries.en: Junli and the others said, "The secret is out. Delay will bring disaster. Why wait for orders from a thousand li away?"
entries.literal: Junli and the others said, "The plot is already leaked; delay will bring change—why wait for consultation a thousand li away!"

entries.zh: 眾因聚噪，擁武皇。
entries.en: The men raised a clamor and pressed the Martial Emperor forward.
entries.literal: The crowd thereupon clamored together and pressed around the Martial Emperor.

entries.zh: 比及雲州，眾且萬人，師營鬥雞台，城中械文楚以應武皇之軍。
entries.en: By the time they reached Yunzhou they numbered nearly ten thousand. The army camped at the Cockfighting Terrace, and the city seized Wenchu in bonds to welcome the Martial Emperor's forces.
entries.literal: By the time they reached Yunzhou the host was nearly ten thousand strong. The army encamped at the Cockfighting Terrace; within the city Wenchu was put in fetters to answer the Martial Emperor's army.

entries.zh: 既收城，推武皇為大同軍防禦留後。
entries.en: After the city fell, they urged the Martial Emperor to become acting defense commissioner of the Datong army.
entries.literal: Once the city was taken, they urged the Martial Emperor to be acting defense commissioner of the Datong army.

entries.zh: 眾狀以聞，朝廷不悅，詔征兵來討。
entries.en: They reported the matter to court. The throne was displeased and ordered armies raised against them.
entries.literal: The host submitted a memorial to inform the court; the court was displeased and ordered troops levied to attack.

entries.zh: 俄而獻祖失振武，武皇失雲州。
entries.en: Soon the Ancestor of Offerings lost Zhenwu and the Martial Emperor lost Yunzhou.
entries.literal: Before long the Ancestor of Offerings lost Zhenwu and the Martial Emperor lost Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 朝廷命招討使李鈞、幽州李可舉加兵於武皇，攻武皇於蔚州。
entries.en: The court ordered Pacification Commissioner Li Jun and Li Keju of Youzhou to reinforce their armies and attack the Martial Emperor at Yuzhou.
entries.literal: The court ordered the pacification commissioner Li Jun and Li Keju of Youzhou to add troops against the Martial Emperor and attack him at Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 君立從擊可舉之師屢捷，及獻祖入達靼，君立保感義軍，武皇授雁門節度，以君立為左都押牙，從入關，逐黃孽，收長安。
entries.en: Junli followed the campaigns against Keju's army and won victory after victory. When the Ancestor of Offerings fled into the Tatar lands, Junli held the Ganyi army. The Martial Emperor received the Yanmen command, made Junli his left chief guard officer, marched with him through the passes, drove off Huang Chao, and recovered Chang'an.
entries.literal: Junli followed in striking Keju's army and won repeated victories. When the Ancestor of Offerings entered the Tatar lands, Junli held the Ganyi army; the Martial Emperor received the Yanmen command, appointed Junli left chief guard officer, followed him through the passes, drove off the Yellow remnant, and recovered Chang'an.

entries.zh: 武皇還鎮太原，授檢校工部尚書、先鋒軍使，
entries.en: When the Martial Emperor returned to Taiyuan, he appointed Junli acting Minister of Works and commander of the vanguard army,
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor returned to garrison Taiyuan and appointed him acting Minister of Works and vanguard army commander,

entries.zh: 七年，岐人攻靈夏，遣使來求助，德威渡河以應之；
entries.en: In the seventh year the Qi attacked Ling and Xia and sent envoys asking for aid. Dewei crossed the Yellow River to answer them.
entries.literal: In the seventh year the Qi people attacked Ling and Xia; they sent envoys to ask aid, and Dewei crossed the river to respond.

entries.zh: 師還，授蕃漢馬步總管。
entries.en: When the army returned he was appointed overall commander of tribal and Han horse and foot.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed overall commander of tribal and Han horse and foot.

entries.zh: 七年十一月，汴人據深、冀，汴將王景仁軍八萬次柏鄉，鎮州節度使王鎔來告難，帝遣德威率前軍出井陘，屯於趙州。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the seventh year the Bian held Shen and Ji. The Bian general Wang Jingren camped at Baixiang with eighty thousand men. Wang Rong, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, sent word that he was in peril. The emperor sent Dewei with the vanguard through Jingxing Pass to encamp at Zhaozhou.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year the Bian held Shen and Ji; the Bian general Wang Jingren with eighty thousand troops halted at Baixiang. Wang Rong, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, came to report distress; the emperor sent Dewei to lead the vanguard out through Jingxing Pass and encamp at Zhaozhou.

entries.zh: 十二月，帝親征。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the emperor took the field in person.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month the emperor personally campaigned.

entries.zh: 二十五日，進薄汴營，距柏鄉五里，營於野河上。
entries.en: On the twenty-fifth they pressed close to the Bian camp, five li from Baixiang, and pitched their tents on the Ye River.
entries.literal: On the twenty-fifth day they advanced close to the Bian camp, five li from Baixiang, and encamped on the Ye River.

entries.zh: 汴將韓率精兵三萬，鎧甲皆被繒綺，金銀炫曜，望之森然，我軍懼形於色。
entries.en: The Bian general Han led thirty thousand elite troops in armor draped with brocade, gold and silver glittering so that they looked terrifying from afar. Fear showed plainly on our men's faces.
entries.literal: The Bian general Han led thirty thousand elite troops; their armor was all draped in silk brocade, gold and silver dazzling, and seen from afar they looked grim; our army's fear showed on their faces.

entries.zh: 德威謂李存璋曰：「賊結陣而來，觀其形勢，誌不在戰，欲以兵甲耀威耳。
entries.en: Dewei told Li Cunzhang, "The enemy advances in battle order, but their intent is not to fight. They mean only to dazzle us with arms and armor.
entries.literal: Dewei said to Li Cunzhang, "The foe comes in formed array; judging their posture, their intent is not battle—they wish only to dazzle with arms and armor.

entries.zh: 我軍人乍見其來，謂其鋒不可當，此時不挫其銳，吾軍不振矣！」
entries.en: Our men, seeing them for the first time, think their charge cannot be stopped. If we do not blunt their pride now, our army will never recover its spirit!"
entries.literal: Our men, seeing them come all at once, say their edge cannot be withstood; if at this moment we do not blunt their keenness, our army will not be roused!"

entries.zh: 乃遣存璋諭諸軍曰：「爾見此賊軍否？
entries.en: He sent Cunzhang to rally the troops and asked, "Do you see this enemy host?
entries.literal: He then sent Cunzhang to instruct the armies, saying, "Do you see this bandit host?

entries.zh: 是汴州天武健兒，皆屠沽傭販，虛有表耳，縱被精甲，十不當一，擒獲足以為資。」
entries.en: They are the Heaven Martial guards of Bianzhou—nothing but butchers, peddlers, and hired hands. Their splendor is empty show. Fine armor or not, ten of them are not worth one of us. Capture them and you will profit."
entries.literal: They are the Heaven Martial stalwarts of Bianzhou—all butchers, peddlers, and hired sellers; their show is empty. Even if clad in fine armor, ten are not equal to one; capture them and that will be enough for profit."

entries.zh: 德威自率精騎擊其兩偏，左馳右決，出沒數四。
entries.en: Dewei himself led elite cavalry against both flanks, wheeling left and right and appearing and vanishing again and again.
entries.literal: Dewei himself led elite cavalry to strike both their flanks, charging left and breaking right, appearing and vanishing four or five times.

entries.zh: 是日，獲賊百餘人，賊渡河而退。
entries.en: That day they took more than a hundred prisoners, and the enemy crossed the river and withdrew.
entries.literal: That day they took more than a hundred of the foe; the bandits crossed the river and withdrew.

entries.zh: 德威謂莊宗曰：「賊驕氣充盛，宜按兵以待其衰。」
entries.en: Dewei told Emperor Zhuangzong, "The enemy's pride is at its height. We should hold our ground and wait for it to fade."
entries.literal: Dewei said to Emperor Zhuangzong, "The bandits' arrogant spirit is full; we should hold the army and wait for their decline."

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「我提孤軍，救難解紛，三鎮烏合之眾，利在速戰，卿欲持重，吾懼其不可使也。」
entries.en: The emperor replied, "I have brought a lone army to rescue allies in distress. These three prefectures' men are a mob gathered in haste; our advantage lies in swift battle. If you insist on caution, I fear the moment will pass us by."
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "I have led a lone army to rescue distress and settle strife; the three prefectures' crowd gathered like blackbirds—profit lies in swift battle. You wish to be weighty; I fear that cannot be applied."

entries.zh: 德威曰：「 鎮、定之士，長於守城，列陣野戰，素非便習。
entries.en: Dewei said, "The men of Zhen and Ding excel at defending walls. Fighting in open field arrays is not their strength.
entries.literal: Dewei said, "The men of Zhen and Ding excel at defending cities; to deploy in array for field battle is not their accustomed skill.

entries.zh: 我師破賊，惟恃騎軍，平田廣野，易為施功。
entries.en: To defeat the enemy we depend wholly on cavalry. On level plains and open country we can fight to our advantage.
entries.literal: Our army in defeating the bandits relies solely on cavalry; on level fields and broad wilds it is easy to exert force.

entries.zh: 今壓賊營，令彼見我虛實，則勝負未可必也。」
entries.en: If we press close to their camp and let them see our full strength, victory and defeat become uncertain."
entries.literal: Now we press on the bandit camp and let them see our strength and weakness; then victory and defeat cannot be certain."

entries.zh: 莊宗不悅，退臥帳中。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased and withdrew to his tent to lie down.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was displeased and withdrew to lie in his tent.

entries.zh: 德威患之，謂監軍張承業曰：「王欲速戰，將烏合之徒，欲當劇賊，所謂不量力也。
entries.en: Dewei was deeply troubled. He told army supervisor Zhang Chengye, "His Majesty wants a quick battle. He would pit a hastily gathered mob against a formidable foe. That is to misjudge one's strength.
entries.literal: Dewei was troubled by this and said to the army supervisor Zhang Chengye, "The king wishes swift battle, will take a mob gathered like blackbirds and meet fierce bandits—what is called not measuring one's strength.

entries.zh: 去賊咫尺，限此一渠水，彼若早夜以略彴渡之，吾族其為俘矣。
entries.en: We stand a foot from the enemy, with only this ditch between us. If they cross by night on light bridges, our whole army will be taken prisoner.
entries.literal: A mere foot from the bandits, with only this ditch between—if they cross by night on light bridges, our clans will be their captives.

entries.zh: 若退軍鄗邑，引賊離營，彼出則歸，復以輕騎掠其芻餉，不逾月，敗賊必矣。」
entries.en: If we withdraw to Gaoyi and lure them from their camp, we can strike when they advance and fall back when they retreat, then send light cavalry to raid their fodder and supplies. Within a month the enemy will surely be broken."
entries.literal: If we withdraw the army to Gaoyi, draw the bandits from camp, when they come out we return, and again with light cavalry raid their fodder and grain, within a month the defeated bandits are certain."

entries.zh: 承業入言，莊宗乃釋然。
entries.en: Chengye went in and spoke to the emperor, who then accepted the plan with relief.
entries.literal: Chengye entered and spoke; Emperor Zhuangzong then was relieved.

entries.zh: 德威得降人問之，曰「景仁下令造浮橋數日」，果如德威所料。
entries.en: Dewei questioned a prisoner, who said, "Jingren has ordered floating bridges built for several days"—just as Dewei had predicted.
entries.literal: Dewei questioned a surrendered man, who said, "Jingren has ordered floating bridges built for several days"—exactly as Dewei had foreseen.

entries.zh: 二十七日，乃退軍保鄗邑。
entries.en: On the twenty-seventh the army withdrew to Gaoyi.
entries.literal: On the twenty-seventh day they then withdrew the army to hold Gaoyi.

entries.zh: 周德威，字鎮遠，小字陽五，朔州馬邑人也。
entries.en: Zhou Dewei, whose courtesy name was Zhenyuan and childhood name Yangwu, was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.
entries.literal: Zhou Dewei, courtesy name Zhenyuan, childhood name Yangwu, was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.

entries.zh: 初事武皇為帳中騎督，驍勇，便騎射，膽氣智數皆過人。
entries.en: He first served Emperor Wu as captain of the guard cavalry. Fierce in battle and expert at mounted archery, he surpassed other men in courage, resolve, and cunning.
entries.literal: At first he served Emperor Wu as captain of the guard cavalry; he was fierce and brave, skilled at mounted archery, and in daring, spirit, and stratagem he surpassed other men.

entries.zh: 久在雲中，諳熟邊事，望煙塵之警，懸知兵勢。
entries.en: After long service at Yunzhong he knew the frontier inside out; from the dust of distant alarms he could read the enemy's movements at a glance.
entries.literal: Long stationed at Yunzhong, he was thoroughly versed in frontier affairs; at the sight of dust and smoke warnings he could foresee military dispositions.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，為鐵林軍使，武皇討王行瑜，以功加檢校左僕射，移內衙軍副。
entries.en: During the Qianning reign he was made commissioner of the Iron Forest Army. When Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Dewei was promoted for merit to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to deputy commander of the inner guard.
entries.literal: During the Qianning era he became commissioner of the Iron Forest Army; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, for merit he was given the additional title of acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to deputy commander of the inner guard.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜，字安時，代州雁門人也。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao, whose style name was Anshi, was a native of Yanmen in Dai Prefecture.
entries.literal: Guo Chongtao, style Anshi, was a man of Yanmen in Dai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父宏正。
entries.en: His father was Hongzheng.
entries.literal: His father was Hongzheng.

entries.zh: 崇韜初為李克修帳下親信。
entries.en: Chongtao began as a trusted confidant in Li Kexiu's personal entourage.
entries.literal: At first Chongtao served as a trusted intimate beneath Li Kexiu's command tent.

entries.zh: 克修鎮昭義，崇韜累典事務，以廉幹稱。
entries.en: While Kexiu held the Zhaoyi command, Chongtao repeatedly handled administrative affairs and earned a reputation for integrity and efficiency.
entries.literal: When Kexiu garrisoned Zhaoyi, Chongtao repeatedly managed affairs and was renowned for integrity and competence.

entries.zh: 克修卒，武皇用為典謁，奉使鳳翔稱旨，署教練使。
entries.en: After Kexiu's death, Emperor Wu appointed him Master of Ceremonies. On an embassy to Fengxiang he fulfilled his mission to the emperor's satisfaction and was made Training Commissioner.
entries.literal: When Kexiu died, Emperor Wu employed him as Master of Ceremonies; on a mission to Fengxiang he pleased the intent, and was appointed Training Commissioner.

entries.zh: 崇韜臨事機警，應對可觀。
entries.en: In handling affairs Chongtao was alert and resourceful, and his replies were impressive.
entries.literal: In attending to affairs Chongtao was quick-witted, and his responses were admirable.

entries.zh: 莊宗嗣位，尤器重之。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he placed exceptional trust in him.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne, he especially valued and trusted him.

entries.zh: 天祐十四年，用為中門副使，與孟知祥、李紹宏俱參機要。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year of Tianyou he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate and, together with Meng Zhixiang and Li Shaohong, shared in confidential state affairs.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianyou, he was employed as Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate, and together with Meng Zhixiang and Li Shaohong all participated in vital secrets.

entries.zh: 俄而紹宏出典幽州留事，知祥懇辭要職。
entries.en: Soon afterward Shaohong was sent to administer Youzhou as resident commissioner, and Zhixiang earnestly sought to relinquish his key post.
entries.literal: Before long Shaohong went out to govern Youzhou as resident commissioner; Zhixiang earnestly declined the vital post.

entries.zh: 先是，中門使吳珙、張虔厚忠而獲罪。
entries.en: Previously, the Inner Gate commissioners Wu Gong and Zhang Qianhou had been loyal men who nevertheless fell under accusation.
entries.literal: Earlier, Inner Gate Commissioners Wu Gong and Zhang Qianhou had been loyal yet incurred guilt.

entries.zh: 知祥懼，求為外任，妻矞華公主泣請於貞簡太后。
entries.en: Meng Zhixiang grew fearful and petitioned for a provincial assignment; his wife, Princess Yuhua, tearfully appealed to Empress Dowager Zhenjian.
entries.literal: Zhixiang feared, and sought an external assignment; his wife Princess Yuhua wept and begged Empress Dowager Zhenjian.

entries.zh: 莊宗謂知祥曰：「公欲避路，當舉其代。」
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong said to Meng Zhixiang, "If you wish to step aside, you must name your successor."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said to Zhixiang: "If you, sir, wish to yield the way, you ought to recommend your replacement."

entries.zh: 知祥因舉崇韜。
entries.en: Zhixiang thereupon nominated Guo Chongtao.
entries.literal: Zhixiang thereupon recommended Chongtao.

entries.zh: 乃署知祥為太原軍在城都虞候。
entries.en: The emperor then appointed Meng Zhixiang Chief Garrison Officer of the Taiyuan army stationed in the capital.
entries.literal: Thereupon he appointed Zhixiang Chief Garrison Officer of the Taiyuan Army within the city.

entries.zh: 自是崇韜專典機務，艱難戰伐，靡所不從。
entries.en: From then on Guo Chongtao alone directed state affairs, accompanying the emperor through every hardship and campaign.
entries.literal: From this Chongtao alone managed vital affairs; in hardship and warfare, nothing did he not follow.

entries.zh: 崇韜服勤盡節，佐佑王家，草昧艱難，功無與比，西平巴蜀，宣暢皇威，身死之日，夷夏冤之。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao had served with tireless loyalty, standing by the royal house through the founding struggle with achievements few could match. He subdued Ba and Shu in the west and carried imperial might to the frontiers. On the day he died, both Chinese and foreigners alike felt his end was unjust.
entries.literal: Chongtao served diligently and fulfilled his charge, supporting the royal house through the rough founding of the dynasty with achievements unmatched by any other. He pacified Ba and Shu in the west and spread imperial might abroad. On the day of his death, barbarian and Chinese alike mourned his injustice.

entries.zh: 然議者以崇韜功烈雖多，事權太重，不能處身量力，而聽小人誤計，欲取泰山之安，如急行避跡，其禍愈速。
entries.en: Yet critics noted that for all his achievements, Guo Chongtao wielded too much power and failed to measure himself against his place. He listened to petty men's bad counsel. Seeking security as unshakable as Mount Tai, he acted like a man fleeing in haste to cover his tracks—and brought ruin upon himself all the faster.
entries.literal: Yet commentators held that although Chongtao's achievements were many, his power was too great. Unable to measure himself and act within his means, he listened to petty men's mistaken schemes. Wishing to secure safety as firm as Mount Tai, he acted like one hurrying to hide his tracks—and his calamity came all the swifter.

entries.zh: 性復剛戾，遇事便發，既不知前代之成敗，又未體當時之物情，以天下為己任，孟浪之甚也。
entries.en: He was stubborn and explosive by nature, ignorant of the rise and fall of earlier dynasties and blind to the mood of his own day, yet he acted as though the realm rested on his shoulders alone—a recklessness bordering on arrogance.
entries.literal: His nature was moreover stubborn and harsh; he erupted at every turn. He neither understood the successes and failures of earlier ages nor grasped the temper of the times, yet took the realm upon himself—recklessness in the extreme.

entries.zh: 及權傾四海，車騎盈門，士人諂奉，漸別流品。
entries.en: Once his power eclipsed all others, his gates overflowed with visitors, scholars flattered him, and he began sorting men by pedigree and rank.
entries.literal: Once his power tilted the four seas, chariots and riders filled his gates, scholars fawned upon him, and he gradually sorted people by pedigree.

entries.zh: 同列豆盧革謂崇韜曰：「汾陽王代北人，徙家華陰，侍中世在雁門，得非祖德歟？」
entries.en: His colleague Doulu Ge said to Guo Chongtao, "The Prince of Fenyang came from northern Dai and moved his family to Huayin. Your family has roots in Yanmen for generations—surely this is ancestral grace?"
entries.literal: His colleague Doulu Ge said to Chongtao, "The Prince of Fenyang was a man of northern Dai who moved his family to Huayin. You, Lord Chancellor, have generations in Yanmen—is this not ancestral virtue?"

entries.zh: 崇韜應曰：「經亂失譜牒，先人嘗雲去汾陽王四世。」
entries.en: Guo Chongtao answered, "The genealogies were lost in the chaos, but our ancestors once said we were four generations from the Prince of Fenyang."
entries.literal: Chongtao replied, "Through the turmoil the genealogical records were lost, but our forebears once said we were four generations removed from the Prince of Fenyang."

entries.zh: 革曰：「故祖德也。」
entries.en: Doulu Ge said, "Then it is indeed ancestral merit."
entries.literal: Ge said, "So it is ancestral virtue after all."

entries.zh: 因是旌別流品，援引薄徒，委之心腹；
entries.en: Thereafter he ranked men by lineage, elevated low-born followers, and entrusted them with his innermost affairs;
entries.literal: From this he distinguished pedigree, promoted base companions, and entrusted them as his inner circle;

entries.zh: 佐命勳舊，一切鄙棄。
entries.en: and founding veterans who had shared the struggle he treated with open contempt.
entries.literal: the founding merit-holders and old companions he utterly despised and cast aside.

entries.zh: 舊僚有幹進者，崇韜謂之曰：「公雖代邸之舊，然家無門閥，深知公才技，不敢驟進者，慮名流嗤餘故也。」
entries.en: When an old colleague sought promotion, Guo Chongtao told him, "You are indeed an old companion from the Prince of Dai's camp, but your family lacks a great lineage. I know well what you can do, yet I dare not advance you hastily for fear the eminent would laugh at me."
entries.literal: When an old subordinate sought advancement, Chongtao told him, "Although you are an old companion from the Prince of Dai's household, your family has no great pedigree. Though I well know your talent and skill, I dare not advance you abruptly for fear the leading men would scorn me for it."

entries.zh: 及征蜀之行，於興平拜尚父子儀之墓。
entries.en: On the march into Shu, he paid his respects at Xingping at the tomb of the Honorary Prince of Guo, Ziyi.
entries.literal: On the expedition to Shu, at Xingping he paid respects at the tomb of the Honorary Prince of Guo, Ziyi.

entries.zh: 嘗從容白繼岌曰：「蜀平之後，王為太子，待千秋萬歲，神器在手，宜盡去宦官，優禮士族，不唯疏斥閹寺，騸馬不可復乘。」
entries.en: He once told Li Jiji in confidence, "When Shu is pacified you will be crown prince, and in the years to come, with the throne in your hand, you should purge the eunuchs and honor the scholar-official clans—not merely ostracize the palace eunuchs, but never again ride a gelded horse."
entries.literal: He once calmly told Jiji, "After Shu is pacified you will be crown prince, and when you reign for ten thousand years with the imperial regalia in hand, you should remove all eunuchs, honor the gentry families, not only cast out the palace eunuchs, but never again ride gelded horses."

entries.zh: 內則伶官巷伯，怒目切齒；
entries.en: Within the court, actor-officials and eunuchs gnashed their teeth in fury;
entries.literal: Within, the actor-officials and eunuchs glared and ground their teeth;

entries.zh: 外則舊僚宿將，戟手痛心。
