entries.en: without, veteran officers and old companions wrung their hands in outrage.
entries.literal: without, old subordinates and veteran generals pointed in accusation with anguished hearts.

entries.zh: 掇其族滅之禍，有自來矣。
entries.en: The disaster that wiped out his clan had been gathering long before.
entries.literal: That he brought upon himself the calamity of extermination of his clan had long been foreshadowed.

entries.zh: 復以諸子驕縱不法，既定蜀川，輦運珍貨，實於洛陽之第，籍沒之日，泥封尚濕。
entries.en: His sons, too, were arrogant and lawless. Once Shu was taken, cartloads of treasure were stored in the family's Luoyang mansion—on the day of confiscation the clay seals were still fresh.
entries.literal: Moreover his sons were arrogant, unrestrained, and lawless. Once Shu was secured, precious goods were carted and stored in his Luoyang mansion; on the day of confiscation the clay seals were still wet.

entries.zh: 雖莊宗季年為群小所惑，致功臣不保其終，亦崇韜自貽其災禍也。
entries.en: True, in his final years Emperor Zhuangzong was led astray by petty men, and many a meritorious minister failed to die in peace—but Guo Chongtao also made his own disaster.
entries.literal: Although in his final years Emperor Zhuangzong was deluded by petty men, causing meritorious ministers not to keep their ends, Chongtao also brought calamity upon himself.

entries.zh: 十八年，從征張文禮於鎮州。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he accompanied the campaign against Zhang Wenli at Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, he followed on campaign against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 契丹引眾至新樂，王師大恐，諸將鹹請退還魏州，莊宗猶豫未決。
entries.en: When the Khitans marched on Xinle, the imperial forces were gripped with fear. The generals unanimously urged a retreat to Weizhou, but Emperor Zhuangzong remained undecided.
entries.literal: The Khitans led their masses to Xinle; the imperial army was greatly afraid; the various generals all petitioned to withdraw back to Weizhou; Zhuangzong hesitated and had not decided.

entries.zh: 崇韜曰：「阿保機隻為王都所誘，本利貨財，非敦鄰好，苟前鋒小衄，遁走必矣。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao said, "Abaoji was lured here by Wang Du alone. He came for loot, not out of genuine alliance. If our vanguard inflicts even a minor defeat, he is certain to flee.
entries.literal: Chongtao said: "Abaoji came only because Wang Du enticed him; he originally sought profit in goods and wealth, not sincere neighborly goodwill. If the vanguard suffers a small setback, he will surely flee away.

entries.zh: 況我新破汴寇，威振北地，乘此驅攘，焉往不捷！
entries.en: And we have just crushed the Liang forces and now dominate the north. If we press this advantage, where can we fail to prevail?
entries.literal: Moreover we have newly broken the Bian bandits; our authority shakes the northern lands. Riding this to drive and scatter them—where would we go and not be victorious!

entries.zh: 且事之濟否，亦有天命。」
entries.en: Besides, whether we succeed also rests with Heaven's mandate."
entries.literal: Moreover whether affairs succeed or not also has the Mandate of Heaven."

entries.zh: 莊宗從之，王師果捷。
entries.en: The emperor took his advice, and the imperial army duly won the day.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong followed this; the imperial army indeed was victorious.

entries.zh: 明年，李存審收鎮州，遣崇韜閱其府庫，或以珍貨賂遺，一無所取，但市書籍而已。
entries.en: The following year, after Li Cunshen recovered Zhen Prefecture, he sent Guo Chongtao to inspect its treasury. Many offered him precious gifts, but he accepted nothing and bought only books.
entries.literal: The next year, Li Cunshen recovered Zhenzhou and dispatched Chongtao to inspect its treasury stores. Some tried to bribe him with precious goods; he took not one thing, but only purchased books.

entries.zh: 會客省使李嚴使西川回，言王衍可圖之狀，莊宗與崇韜議討伐之謀，方擇大將。
entries.en: About then Guest Affairs Commissioner Li Yan returned from his mission to the West River circuit and reported that Wang Yan's realm was ripe for conquest. Emperor Zhuangzong and Guo Chongtao debated the campaign and were still choosing a commander.
entries.literal: It happened that Guest Affairs Commissioner Li Yan returned from his mission to Xichuan, reporting that Wang Yan's situation made him vulnerable to attack. Zhuangzong and Chongtao discussed plans for an expedition and were just selecting a commander.

entries.zh: 時明宗為諸道兵馬總管當行，崇韜自以宦者相傾，欲立大功以製之，乃奏曰：「契丹犯邊，北面須藉大臣，全倚總管鎮禦。
entries.en: At the time Li Siyuan, as overall commander of the armies of all circuits, was slated to lead the campaign. Guo Chongtao, knowing the eunuchs were working against him, sought a great victory with which to restrain them. He memorialized: "The Khitans are raiding the frontier; the northern line must rest on a senior minister—the overall commander is needed there to hold the defense.
entries.literal: At the time Mingzong was overall commander of the armies of all circuits and was slated to lead the campaign. Chongtao, considering how the eunuchs were undermining him, wished to achieve a great victory to check them. He memorialized: "The Khitans are violating the border; the northern front must rely on a senior minister—the overall commander must fully depend on military defense there.

entries.zh: 臣伏念興聖宮使繼岌，德望日隆，大功未著，宜依故事，以親王為元帥，付以討伐之權，俾成其威望。」
entries.en: I reflect that the Director of the Xingsheng Palace, Li Jiji, grows daily in stature and reputation, yet has not won a great victory of his own. Precedent calls for an imperial prince as commander-in-chief, entrusted with the power of expedition, so that his authority may be established."
entries.literal: Your subject reflects that the Director of the Xingsheng Palace, Jiji, grows daily in virtue and reputation, yet has not yet displayed great achievement. According to precedent, a prince should serve as commander-in-chief, entrusted with authority for the expedition, so that his prestige may be established."

entries.zh: 莊宗方愛繼岌，即曰：「小兒幼稚，安能獨行，卿當擇其副。」
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong, who doted on Jiji, said at once: "The boy is still young. How could he go alone? You must choose his deputy."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong, who doted on Jiji, immediately said: "The boy is still young—how could he go alone? You must choose his deputy."

entries.zh: 崇韜未奏，莊宗曰：「無逾於卿者。」
entries.en: Before Guo Chongtao could answer, the emperor said: "There is no one better suited than you."
entries.literal: Before Chongtao could reply, Zhuangzong said: "No one surpasses you."

entries.zh: 乃以繼岌為都統，崇韜為招討使。
entries.en: Jiji was appointed overall commander, and Guo Chongtao Pacification Commissioner.
entries.literal: Thereupon Jiji was made overall commander and Chongtao was made Pacification Commissioner.

entries.zh: 是歲九月十八日，率親軍六萬，進討蜀川。
entries.en: That year, on the eighteenth day of the ninth month, he led sixty thousand imperial guards west against Shu.
entries.literal: That year, on the eighteenth day of the ninth month, he led sixty thousand of the imperial guard in an expedition against Shu.

entries.zh: 崇韜將發，奏曰：「臣以非才，謬當戎事，仗將士之忠力，憑陛下之威靈，庶幾克捷。
entries.en: As Guo Chongtao was about to depart, he memorialized: "I am unworthy and have been wrongly placed in command of war. Trusting in the loyalty and strength of the troops and in Your Majesty's august power, I hope we may prevail.
entries.literal: As Chongtao was about to depart, he memorialized: "Your subject, lacking talent, has been wrongly entrusted with military affairs. Relying on the loyalty and strength of officers and soldiers and on Your Majesty's august authority, I hope we may achieve victory.

entries.zh: 若西川平定，陛下擇帥，如信厚善謀，事君有節，則孟知祥有焉，望以蜀帥授之。
entries.en: If the West River circuit is pacified and Your Majesty chooses a governor—one loyal, trustworthy, prudent in counsel, and restrained in service—Meng Zhixiang is such a man. I ask that the Shu command be given to him.
entries.literal: If the western circuit is pacified and Your Majesty selects a commander—one who is trustworthy, generous, skilled in planning, and serves his lord with proper restraint—Meng Zhixiang is such a man. I hope he may be granted the Shu command.

entries.zh: 如宰輔闕人，張憲有披榛之勞，為人謹重而多識。
entries.en: If the chief ministers need filling, Zhang Xian cleared the thorns at the founding and is a man of gravity, prudence, and wide learning.
entries.literal: If the chief ministers lack a worthy candidate, Zhang Xian rendered service in clearing the path at the outset; he is prudent, grave, and widely knowledgeable.

entries.zh: 其次李琪、崔居儉，中朝士族，富有文學，可擇而任之。」
entries.en: Next are Li Qi and Cui Jujian, eminent clansmen of the central court, men of literary accomplishment who may be chosen and appointed."
entries.literal: Next are Li Qi and Cui Jujian, eminent clansmen of the central court, rich in literary skill—they may be selected and appointed."

entries.zh: 莊宗禦嘉慶殿，置酒宴征西諸將，舉酒屬崇韜曰：「繼岌未習軍政，卿久從吾戰伐，西面之事，屬之於卿。」
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong held court in the Jiaqing Hall and feasted the generals bound for the west. Raising his cup to Guo Chongtao, he said: "Jiji has not yet learned the arts of war. You have long marched at my side. The western campaign is yours to command."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong held court at the Jiaqing Hall, set out wine and feasted the generals of the western expedition. Raising his cup he addressed Chongtao: "Jiji is not yet versed in military affairs. You have long followed me in campaign. The western enterprise is entrusted to you."

entries.zh: 軍發，十月十九日入大散關，崇韜以馬箠指山險謂魏王曰：「朝廷興師十萬，已入此中，儻不成功，安有歸路？
entries.en: The army marched out. On the nineteenth day of the tenth month they entered Dasan Pass. Guo Chongtao pointed with his riding crop at the treacherous mountains and said to the Prince of Wei: "The court has sent a hundred thousand men into this trap. If we fail here, what road home remains?
entries.literal: The army set out. On the nineteenth day of the tenth month they entered Dasan Pass. Chongtao pointed with his riding crop at the perilous mountains and said to the Prince of Wei: "The court has raised an army of a hundred thousand and already entered these depths. If we do not succeed, what road of return remains?

entries.zh: 今岐下飛挽，才支旬日，必須先取鳳州，收其儲積，方濟吾事。」
entries.en: Supplies rushed up from beneath Qi will barely last ten days. We must take Fengzhou first and seize its stores, or our cause is lost."
entries.literal: Now supplies rushed from beneath Qi barely last ten days. We must first take Fengzhou and seize its stored provisions before our enterprise can succeed."

entries.zh: 乃令李嚴、康延孝先馳書檄，以諭偽鳳州節度使王承捷。
entries.en: He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanxiao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to summon the puppet Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie.
entries.literal: He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanxiao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to persuade the pseudo-Fengzhou Military Commissioner Wang Chengjie.

entries.zh: 及大軍至，承捷果以城降，得兵八千，軍儲四十萬。
entries.en: When the main army arrived, Chengjie surrendered the city as expected, yielding eight thousand troops and four hundred thousand units of provisions.
entries.literal: When the main army arrived, Chengjie duly surrendered the city, yielding eight thousand troops and four hundred thousand units of military stores.

entries.zh: 次至故鎮，偽命屯駐指揮使唐景思亦以城降，得兵四千。
entries.en: Next they reached Guzhen, where Tang Jingsi, the garrison commander appointed by the puppet court, also surrendered the city and yielded four thousand troops.
entries.literal: Next they reached Guzhen. Tang Jingsi, the garrison commander appointed by the pseudo-court, also surrendered the city, yielding four thousand troops.

entries.zh: 又下三泉，得軍儲三十餘萬。
entries.en: They then took Sanquan and obtained more than three hundred thousand units of provisions.
entries.literal: They then descended upon Sanquan and obtained more than three hundred thousand units of military stores.

entries.zh: 自是師無匱乏，軍聲大振。
entries.en: From then on the army lacked nothing, and its martial renown swelled.
entries.literal: From then on the army wanted for nothing, and its martial reputation greatly rose.

entries.zh: 其招懷製置，官吏補置，師行籌畫，軍書告諭，皆出於崇韜，繼岌承命而已。
entries.en: Recruitment and pacification, administrative arrangements, filling official posts, planning the march, and drafting orders and proclamations—all came from Guo Chongtao. Li Jiji merely received and carried out his commands.
entries.literal: Recruitment and pacification, administrative arrangements, filling official posts, planning the march, and drafting military orders and proclamations—all issued from Chongtao. Jiji merely received and carried out commands.

entries.zh: 莊宗令內官李廷安、李從襲、呂知柔為都統府紀綱，見崇韜幕府繁重，將吏輻輳，降人爭先賂遺，都統府唯大將省謁，牙門索然，由是大為詬恥。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong appointed the eunuchs Li Ting'an, Li Congxi, and Lü Zhirou as disciplinarians of the overall command headquarters. They saw Guo Chongtao's headquarters thronged with officers and clerks, with surrendered men vying to offer bribes, while the prince's own headquarters received only the chief generals on formal visits and its gate stood empty. They were deeply shamed.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong appointed the eunuchs Li Ting'an, Li Congxi, and Lü Zhirou as disciplinarians of the overall command headquarters. Seeing Chongtao's headquarters heavy with business, officers and clerks crowding in, and surrendered men vying to offer bribes, while the headquarters saw only the chief generals on formal visits and its gate stood empty—they were deeply shamed.

entries.zh: 及六軍使王宗弼歸款，行賂先招討府。
entries.en: When Wang Zongbi, commander of the Six Armies, came over to the Tang side, he sent bribes first to the Pacification Commissioner's headquarters.
entries.literal: When Wang Zongbi, commander of the Six Armies, submitted allegiance, he offered bribes first to the Pacification Commissioner's headquarters.

entries.zh: 王衍以成都降，崇韜居王宗弼之第。
entries.en: When Wang Yan surrendered Chengdu, Guo Chongtao took up residence in Wang Zongbi's mansion.
entries.literal: When Wang Yan surrendered Chengdu, Chongtao took up residence in Wang Zongbi's mansion.

entries.zh: 宗弼選王衍之妓妾珍玩以奉崇韜，求為蜀帥，崇韜許之。
entries.en: Zongbi selected Wang Yan's courtesans and treasures to present to Guo Chongtao and asked to be made governor of Shu; Chongtao agreed.
entries.literal: Zongbi selected Wang Yan's courtesans and precious objects to present to Chongtao, requesting appointment as Shu commander; Chongtao agreed.

entries.zh: 又與崇韜子廷誨謀，令蜀人列狀見魏王，請奏崇韜為蜀帥。
entries.en: He also plotted with Guo Chongtao's son Tinghui to have men of Shu submit collective petitions to the Prince of Wei asking that a memorial be sent appointing Guo Chongtao governor of Shu.
entries.literal: He also plotted with Chongtao's son Tinghui to have men of Shu submit collective petitions to the Prince of Wei requesting that a memorial be sent appointing Chongtao Shu commander.

entries.zh: 繼岌覽狀謂崇韜曰：「主上倚侍中如衡、華，安肯棄元老於蠻夷之地，況餘不敢議此。」
entries.en: Jiji read the petitions and said to Guo Chongtao: "His Majesty relies on you as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua—how would he cast a senior minister off into barbarian country? As for me, I dare not even speak of such a thing."
entries.literal: Jiji read the petitions and said to Chongtao: "His Majesty relies on you, Minister, as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua—how would he abandon a senior minister in barbarian lands? As for me, I dare not broach such a matter."

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王宗弼傳》：宗弼送款於魏王，乃還成都，盡輦內藏之寶貨，歸於其家。
entries.en: (Biography of Wang Zongbi in the Jiuguo Zhi: After Zongbi submitted allegiance to the Prince of Wei, he returned to Chengdu and carted off all the treasures of the inner treasury to his own house.
entries.literal: (Biography of Wang Zongbi in the Jiuguo Zhi: After Zongbi submitted allegiance to the Prince of Wei, he returned to Chengdu and transported all treasures of the inner treasury to his own home.

entries.zh: 魏王遣使征犒軍錢數千萬，宗弼輒靳之，魏王甚怒。
entries.en: The Prince of Wei sent envoys to levy several tens of millions in cash to reward the army, but Zongbi repeatedly refused, and the prince was furious.
entries.literal: The Prince of Wei sent envoys to levy several tens of millions in funds to reward the army; Zongbi consistently withheld them, and the Prince was greatly angered.

entries.zh: 及王師至，令其子承班齎衍玩用直百萬，獻於魏王，並賂郭崇韜，請以己為西川節度使。
entries.en: When the imperial army arrived, he had his son Chengbian bring Wang Yan's playthings worth a million in cash, present them to the Prince of Wei, and also bribe Guo Chongtao, asking to be made military commissioner of the West River circuit.
entries.literal: When the imperial army arrived, he had his son Chengbian bring playthings of Wang Yan worth a million in cash, present them to the Prince of Wei, and also bribe Guo Chongtao, requesting appointment as Military Commissioner of Xichuan.

entries.zh: 魏王曰：「此吾家之物，焉用獻為！」
entries.en: The Prince of Wei said: "These are things of my own house—why offer them as gifts!"
entries.literal: The Prince of Wei said: "These are possessions of my house—why present them as gifts!"

entries.zh: 魏王入城，翌日，數其不忠之罪，並其子斬之於市。）〉
entries.en: The day after the prince entered the city, he enumerated Zongbi's crimes of disloyalty and executed him and his son in the marketplace.)〉
entries.literal: The next day after the Prince entered the city, he enumerated his crimes of disloyalty and executed him and his son in the marketplace.)〉

entries.zh: 李從襲等謂繼岌曰：「郭公收蜀部人情，意在難測，王宜自備。」
entries.en: Li Congxi and the others said to Jiji: "Minister Guo has won over the people of Shu, and his intentions are hard to read. Your Highness should be on your guard."
entries.literal: Li Congxi and others said to Jiji: "Minister Guo has won the hearts of Shu; his intentions are hard to fathom. Your Highness should guard yourself."

entries.zh: 由是兩相猜察。
entries.en: From this mutual suspicion took hold between them.
entries.literal: From this the two sides mutually suspected and watched each other.

entries.zh: 莊宗令中官向延嗣齎詔至蜀，促班師，詔使至，崇韜不郊迎，延嗣憤憤。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to Shu with an edict ordering the army's return. When the imperial messenger arrived, Guo Chongtao failed to greet him with the customary ceremony at the city outskirts, and Yansi was incensed.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong ordered the eunuch Xiang Yansi to carry an edict to Shu urging withdrawal of the army. When the edict envoy arrived, Chongtao did not go out to meet him in the suburbs, and Yansi was furious.

entries.zh: 從襲謂之曰：「魏王，貴太子也，主上萬福，郭公專弄威柄，旁若無人。
entries.en: Li Congxi said to him, "The Prince of Wei is the heir apparent—while the emperor enjoys every blessing under heaven, Lord Guo wields power alone and carries himself as though the rest of us did not exist.
entries.literal: Congxi said to him, "The Prince of Wei is the precious heir apparent, and Our Lord enjoys ten thousand blessings, yet Lord Guo monopolizes power and acts as though no one else were present.

entries.zh: 昨令蜀人請己為帥，郭廷誨擁徒出入，貴擬王者，所與狎遊，無非軍中驍果，蜀中凶豪，晝夜妓樂歡宴，指天畫地，父子如此，可見其心。
entries.en: Just yesterday they had the people of Shu petition to make him regional commander. Guo Tinghui travels about surrounded by his own followers, carrying himself almost like a king. His companions are the army's boldest fighters and Shu's most dangerous ruffians. Day and night the two hold banquets of wine, music, and women, swearing reckless oaths with grand gestures—and from such conduct, father and son alike, their ambitions are plain.
entries.literal: Yesterday they had Shu people petition that he himself be made regional commander. Guo Tinghui goes in and out surrounded by retainers, his status rivaling that of royalty. Those with whom they carouse are none other than the army's fiercest fighters and Shu's violent magnates. Day and night they revel with music and courtesans, swearing oaths with pointed fingers—father and son conduct themselves thus; their intent is plain to see.

entries.zh: 今諸軍將校，無非郭氏之黨，魏王懸軍孤弱，一朝班師，必恐紛亂，吾屬莫知暴骨之所！」
entries.en: Every officer in the army now seems to belong to the Guo faction. The Prince of Wei is stranded far from home with only a slender force. Once we withdraw, chaos is all but certain—and we may never know where our bones will be left to rot!"
entries.literal: Now the officers of all armies are without exception partisans of the Guo clan. The Prince of Wei is left with an isolated army in enemy country—once withdrawal is ordered, turmoil is certain to follow, and we cannot know where our bones will lie unburied!"

entries.zh: 因相向垂涕。
entries.en: They broke down in tears as they faced one another.
entries.literal: Thereupon they wept facing each other.

entries.zh: 延嗣使還具奏，皇后泣告莊宗，乞保全繼岌。
entries.en: Yansi reported everything on his return. The empress wept before Emperor Zhuangzong and begged him to protect Li Jiji.
entries.literal: When Yansi returned from his mission he submitted a full report. The empress tearfully told Emperor Zhuangzong and begged that Jiji be kept safe.

entries.zh: 莊宗復閱蜀簿曰：「人言蜀中珠玉金銀，不知其數，何如是之微也！」
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong again reviewed the Shu account books and said, "Everyone says the pearls, jade, gold, and silver of Shu are beyond numbering—how can the tally be so small?"
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong again reviewed the Shu ledger and said, "People say the pearls, jade, gold, and silver of Shu are beyond counting—how can the amounts be so small!"

entries.zh: 延嗣奏曰：「臣問蜀人，知蜀中寶貨皆入崇韜之門，言崇韜得金萬兩，銀四十萬，名馬千匹，王衍愛妓六十，樂工百，犀玉帶百。
entries.en: Yansi reported, "I questioned people in Shu and learned that the region's treasures had all passed through Guo Chongtao's hands. They say he took ten thousand liang of gold, four hundred thousand of silver, a thousand fine horses, sixty of Wang Yan's favorite concubines, a hundred musicians, and a hundred rhinoceros-horn and jade belts.
entries.literal: Yansi memorialized, saying, "Your servant asked Shu people and learned that all precious goods of Shu entered Chongtao's household. It is said Chongtao obtained ten thousand liang of gold, four hundred thousand of silver, a thousand famous horses, sixty of Wang Yan's favorite courtesans, a hundred musicians, and a hundred rhinoceros-horn and jade belts.

entries.zh: 廷誨自有金銀十萬兩，犀玉帶五十，藝色絕妓七十，樂工七十，他財稱是。
entries.en: Guo Tinghui personally held a hundred thousand liang in gold and silver, fifty rhinoceros-horn and jade belts, seventy courtesans of rare beauty and talent, seventy musicians, and comparable riches besides.
entries.literal: Tinghui personally possessed a hundred thousand liang of gold and silver, fifty rhinoceros-horn and jade belts, seventy courtesans of exceptional skill and beauty, seventy musicians, and comparable other wealth.

entries.zh: 魏王府，蜀人賂遺不過遣匹馬而已。」
entries.en: As for the Prince of Wei's household, gifts from Shu amounted to little more than the loan of a horse."
entries.literal: At the Prince of Wei's residence, Shu people's gifts amounted to no more than the loan of a horse."

entries.zh: 莊宗初聞崇韜欲留蜀，心已不平，又聞全有蜀之妓樂珍玩，怒見顏色。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong had already resented the rumor that Guo Chongtao meant to stay in Shu; when he heard next that Chongtao had taken for himself all the region's courtesans, musicians, and treasures, his anger was plain on his face.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong first heard that Chongtao wished to remain in Shu, his heart was already displeased. When he further heard that Chongtao possessed all of Shu's courtesans, musicians, and treasures, anger showed in his countenance.

entries.zh: 即令中官馬彥珪馳入蜀視崇韜去就，如班師則已，如實遲留，則與繼岌圖之。
entries.en: He immediately dispatched the eunuch Ma Yan'gui to Shu to learn whether Guo Chongtao intended to withdraw. If Chongtao returned with the army, nothing more need be done; if he truly meant to linger, Yan'gui was to join Li Jiji in removing him.
entries.literal: He immediately ordered the eunuch Ma Yan'gui to ride posthaste into Shu to observe whether Chongtao would withdraw. If he withdrew with the army, that would be the end of it; if he truly delayed, then Yan'gui was to plot with Jiji against him.

entries.zh: 彥珪見皇后曰：「禍機之發，間不容發，何能數千里外復稟聖旨哉！」
entries.en: Ma Yan'gui told the empress, "When disaster is about to strike, not a moment can be wasted—how can we seek fresh orders from thousands of li away?"
entries.literal: Yan'gui saw the empress and said, "When calamity is about to break out, not a hair's breadth of time can be spared—how can one seek imperial edict again from thousands of li away!"

entries.zh: 皇后再言之，莊宗曰：「未知事之實否，詎可便令果決？」
entries.en: The empress pressed the point again. Emperor Zhuangzong said, "We do not yet know whether any of this is true—how can we order so fatal a step on hearsay alone?"
entries.literal: The empress spoke again, and Emperor Zhuangzong said, "We do not yet know whether the matter is true—how can we immediately order so decisive an act?"

entries.zh: 皇后乃自為教與繼岌，令殺崇韜。
entries.en: The empress then wrote her own order to Li Jiji commanding Guo Chongtao's death.
entries.literal: The empress then herself wrote an order to Jiji commanding that Chongtao be killed.

entries.zh: 時蜀土初平，山林多盜，孟知祥未至，崇韜令任圜、張筠分道招撫，慮師還後，部曲不寧，故歸期稍緩。
entries.en: Shu had only just been pacified; bandits still roamed the hills, and Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived. Guo Chongtao sent Ren Yuan and Zhang Jun along separate routes to win over and settle the countryside, fearing unrest among his followers once the army withdrew—hence the slight delay in their return.
entries.literal: At that time Shu had only recently been pacified, bandits were numerous in the mountains and forests, and Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived. Chongtao ordered Ren Yuan and Zhang Jun to pacify the people by separate routes, fearing that after the army returned his followers would not remain settled—therefore the date of return was slightly delayed.

entries.zh: 光允，光逢之弟也，
entries.en: Guangyun was Guangfeng's younger brother.
entries.literal: Guangyun was Guangfeng's younger brother.

entries.zh: （新舊《唐書》俱云：趙隱子三人，光逢、光裔、光允。
entries.en: (Both the Old and New Books of Tang state: Zhao Yin had three sons—Guangfeng, Guangyi, and Guangyun.
entries.literal: (Both the Old and New Books of Tang state: Zhao Yin had three sons—Guangfeng, Guangyi, and Guangyun.

entries.zh: 為後唐相者，光允也。
entries.en: The one who became chief minister under Later Tang was Guangyun.
entries.literal: The one who became chief minister under Later Tang was Guangyun.

entries.zh: 原本作光裔，係誤。）
entries.en: The original text had Guangyi, which was an error.)
entries.literal: The original text had Guangyi, which was an error.)

entries.zh: 俱以詞藝知名，亦登進士第。
entries.en: Both were renowned for literary talent and also passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: Both were renowned for literary talent and also passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: （《舊唐書》云：大順二年，進士登第。
entries.en: (According to the Old Book of Tang: in the second year of Dashun he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: (According to the Old Book of Tang: in the second year of Dashun he passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 天祐初，累官至駕部郎中。）
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianyou he rose through successive posts to director of the Bureau of Transport.)
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he rose through successive posts to director of the Bureau of Transport.)

entries.zh: 光允仕梁，曆清顯，伯仲之間，咸以方雅自高，北人聞其名者，皆望風欽重。
entries.en: Guangyun served Liang in prominent offices. Among the brothers each held himself aloof with refined reserve, and northerners who heard their names all revered them from afar.
entries.literal: Guangyun served Liang in prominent offices; among the brothers each held himself aloof with refined reserve, and northerners who heard their names all bowed to their reputation from afar.

entries.zh: 及莊宗平定汴、洛，時盧程以狂妄免，郭崇韜自勳臣拜，議者以為國朝典禮故實，須訪前代名家，咸曰光允有宰相器。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian and Luoyang, Lu Cheng was dismissed for arrogance and Guo Chongyao was appointed from among meritorious ministers. Commentators held that the dynasty's ritual and precedents required consulting celebrated masters of former ages, and all said Guangyun had the makings of a chief minister.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian and Luo, Lu Cheng was dismissed for arrogance and Guo Chongyao was appointed from among meritorious ministers. Commentators held that the dynasty's ritual and precedents required consulting celebrated masters of former ages, and all said Guangyun had the makings of a chief minister.

entries.zh: 薛廷珪、李琪當武皇為晉王時，嘗因為冊使至太原，故皆有宿望，當時咸謂宜處台司。
entries.en: Xue Tinggui and Li Qi, when the Martial Emperor was Prince of Jin, had once served as investiture envoys to Taiyuan and therefore both enjoyed longstanding reputation; at the time all said they were fit for the highest council posts.
entries.literal: Xue Tinggui and Li Qi, when the Martial Emperor was Prince of Jin, had once served as investiture envoys to Taiyuan and therefore both enjoyed longstanding reputation; at the time all said they were fit for the highest council posts.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜采言事者雲，廷珪朽老，浮華無相業；
entries.en: Guo Chongyao adopted the words of memorialists, saying Tinggui was decrepit and aged, showy without ministerial substance;
entries.literal: Guo Chongyao adopted the words of memorialists, saying Tinggui was decrepit and aged, showy without ministerial substance;

entries.zh: 琪雖文學高，傾險無士風，皆不可相，乃止。
entries.en: and though Qi's literary learning was high, he was treacherous without the bearing of a gentleman—neither could be made chief minister, and the matter was dropped.
entries.literal: and though Qi's literary learning was high, he was treacherous without the bearing of a gentleman—neither could be made chief minister, and the matter was dropped.

entries.zh: 同光元年十一月，光允與韋說並拜平章事。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tongguang, Guangyun and Wei Yue were jointly appointed grand councilors.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tongguang, Guangyun and Wei Yue were jointly appointed grand councilors.

entries.zh: 崔協，字思化。
entries.en: Cui Xie, whose style name was Sihua.
entries.literal: Cui Xie, style name Sihua.

entries.zh: 遠祖清河太守第二子寅，仕後魏為太子洗馬，因為清河小房，至唐朝盛為流品。
entries.en: A remote ancestor, Yin, second son of the prefect of Qinghe, served the Northern Wei as crown prince groom and founded the lesser branch of the Qinghe Cui clan, which by the Tang had become a leading family.
entries.literal: A remote ancestor, the second son Yin of the Qinghe prefect, served the Later Wei as Crown Prince Groom and thereby became the lesser branch of Qinghe; by the Tang dynasty this line flourished as a distinguished clan.

entries.zh: 曾祖邠，太常卿，祖瓘，吏部尚書。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Bin had been director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and his grandfather Guan minister of personnel.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Bin was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his grandfather Guan was Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 父彥融，楚州刺史。
entries.en: His father Yanrong had been prefect of Chu Prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Yanrong was prefect of Chu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 彥融素與崔蕘善，嘗為萬年令，蕘謁於縣，彥融未出，見案上有尺題，皆賂遺中貴人，蕘知其由徑，始惡其為人。
entries.en: Yanrong had long been friendly with Cui Rao. When Yanrong was magistrate of Wannian County, Rao called at the yamen before Yanrong had come out and saw on the desk a list of names—all gifts to inner attendants. Rao understood his methods and came to despise him.
entries.literal: Yanrong had long been on good terms with Cui Rao; he once served as magistrate of Wannian County. Rao called at the county office while Yanrong had not yet come out; he saw on the desk a list of names, all bribes to inner attendants. Rao knew his crooked ways and began to detest his character.

entries.zh: 及除司勳郎中，蕘為左丞，通刺不見，蕘謂曰：「郎中行止鄙雜，故未見。」
entries.en: When Yanrong was appointed director in the Bureau of Merit, Rao was left vice director. Yanrong sent a visiting card but was refused an audience. Rao said, "The director's conduct is vulgar and corrupt—that is why I will not receive him."
entries.literal: When Yanrong was appointed Director in the Bureau of Merit, Rao was Left Vice Director; Yanrong sent a visiting card but was not received. Rao said, "The Director's conduct is base and mixed—therefore I do not see him."

entries.zh: 宰相知之，改楚州刺史，卒於任。
entries.en: The chief minister learned of the affair and transferred Yanrong to prefect of Chu Prefecture, where he died in office.
entries.literal: The chief minister learned of it and transferred him to prefect of Chu Prefecture; he died in office.

entries.zh: 誡其子曰：「世世無忘蕘。」
entries.en: He admonished his sons: "Never forget Rao, generation after generation."
entries.literal: He admonished his sons, saying, "Generation after generation do not forget Rao."

entries.zh: 故其子弟常云「崔仇」。
entries.en: His descendants therefore often spoke of "the Cui feud."
entries.literal: Therefore his sons and younger relatives often spoke of "the Cui feud."

entries.zh: 臣伏思漢文帝時，欲人務農，乃募人入粟，得拜爵及贖罪，景帝亦如之。
entries.en: Your subject respectfully recalls that Emperor Wen of Han, wishing the people to devote themselves to farming, offered to ennoble men who contributed grain and to allow grain contributions to redeem crimes. Emperor Jing did the same.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully considers when Emperor Wen of Han, wishing people to devote to farming, then recruited people to enter grain, could be enfeoffed with noble rank and redeem crimes; Emperor Jing also was so.

entries.zh: 後漢安帝時，水旱不足，三公奏請，富人入粟，得關內侯及公卿以下散官。
entries.en: In Later Han, during the reign of Emperor An, when flood and drought left stores insufficient, the Three Excellencies memorialized that wealthy men who contributed grain might receive the rank of marquis within the passes or honorary posts of the Three Excellencies and ministers and below.
entries.literal: Later Han during Emperor An, flood drought insufficient, Three Excellencies memorialized request—wealthy entering grain could obtain within-the-passes marquis and various officials below Three Excellencies honorary posts.

entries.zh: 本朝乾元中，亦曾如此。
entries.en: In our dynasty, during the Qianyuan era, the same measure was once adopted.
entries.literal: In our dynasty during Qianyuan, also once was so.

entries.zh: 今陛下縱不欲入粟授官，願明降製旨下諸道，合差百姓轉倉之處，有能出力運官物到京師，五百石以上，白身授一初任州縣官，有官者依資遷授，欠選者便與放選。
entries.en: Even if Your Majesty does not wish to grant office for grain contributions, I ask that you clearly issue an edict to all circuits. Wherever the people are being conscripted to transfer grain, let it be announced that anyone who transports government goods to the capital at his own expense—for five hundred shi or more—a commoner shall receive an initial appointment as a county or prefecture official; an official shall be promoted according to qualification; and one awaiting appointment shall be granted selection at once.
entries.literal: Now though Your Majesty may not wish entering grain granting offices, wish clearly to descend edict to all circuits—places where common people are assigned to transfer granaries—if able to exert strength transporting government goods to capital, five hundred shi and above, white-bodied person granted first appointment county-prefecture official; if already has office, according to qualification transferred; those lacking selection then immediately granted selection.

entries.zh: 千石以上至萬石，不拘文武，明示賞酬。
entries.en: For one thousand shi up to ten thousand shi, without distinction between civil and military ranks, let rewards be clearly specified.
entries.literal: One thousand shi and above to ten thousand shi, not bound by civil or military, clearly show reward and remuneration.

entries.zh: 免令方春農人流散，斯亦救民轉倉贍軍之一術也。
entries.en: This would keep farmers from scattering at the height of spring planting, and it is one way to relieve the people while moving grain and supplying the army.
entries.literal: Avoid ordering in spring farming people to scatter and flee—this also is one technique of saving people through transfer granary supporting army.

entries.zh: 趙光逢，字延吉。
entries.en: Zhao Guangfeng, whose style name was Yanji.
entries.literal: Zhao Guangfeng, style name Yanji.

entries.zh: 曾祖植，嶺南節度使。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Zhi had served as military commissioner of Lingnan.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Zhi was Military Commissioner of Lingnan.

entries.zh: 祖存約，興元府推官。
entries.en: His grandfather Cunyue had been a legal officer in Xingyuan Prefecture.
entries.literal: His grandfather Cunyue was a legal officer of Xingyuan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父隱，右僕射。
entries.en: His father Yin had risen to the post of right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Yin was Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 光逢與弟光裔，皆以文學德行知名。
entries.en: Guangfeng and his younger brother Guangyi were both widely known for their scholarship and upright character.
entries.literal: Guangfeng and his younger brother Guangyi were both renowned for literary learning and moral conduct.

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：光裔，光啟三年進士擢第，累遷司勳郎中、弘文館學士，改膳部郎中、知制誥。
entries.en: (According to the 《Old Book of Tang》: Guangyi passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Guangqi reign, rose through the posts of director in the Bureau of Merit and academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was later made director of the Bureau of Provisions with charge of drafting imperial edicts.
entries.literal: (《Old Book of Tang》 states: Guangyi passed the civil service examination in the third year of Guangqi, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel and Academician of the Hongwen Institute, and was later changed to Director of the Bureau of Provisions, charged with drafting imperial edicts.)

entries.zh: 季述廢立之後，旅遊江表以避患，嶺南劉隱深禮之，奏為副使，因家嶺外。）〉
entries.en: After the coup in which Jishu deposed and enthroned emperors, he traveled south of the Yangtze to escape the turmoil. Liu Yin of Lingnan received him with great honor and had him appointed deputy commissioner, and he thereafter settled his family in the far south.)〉
entries.literal: After Jishu deposed and enthroned emperors, he traveled in the Jiangnan region to avoid calamity; Liu Yin of Lingnan treated him with deep courtesy, memorialized to appoint him as deputy commissioner, and thus he made his home beyond the mountains.)〉

entries.zh: 光逢幼嗜墳典，動守規檢，議者目之為「玉界尺」。
entries.en: From childhood Guangfeng was devoted to the classical canon and unfailingly observed propriety in his conduct, so that contemporaries dubbed him the "Jade Measuring Rod."
entries.literal: From youth Guangfeng loved the classics of antiquity, and in his conduct he always observed rules and restraint; commentators called him the "Jade Measuring Rod."

entries.zh: 僖宗朝，登進士第。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Xizong he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xizong he passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 逾月，辟度支巡官，曆官台省，內外兩製，俱有能名，轉尚書左丞、翰林承旨。
entries.en: A month later he was appointed an inspector in the Revenue Bureau. He served in the central ministries and in both the inner and outer drafting offices, earning a name for competence at each step, until he was promoted to left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat and Hanlin academician-in-attendance.
entries.literal: Within a month he was recruited as an inspector of the Revenue Bureau, served in offices of the central ministries, held posts in both inner and outer drafting bureaus, and in all gained a reputation for ability; he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.

entries.zh: 昭宗幸石門，光逢不從，昭宗遣內養戴知權詔赴行在，稱疾解官。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhaozong went to Shimen, Guangfeng refused to accompany him. The emperor sent the inner attendant Dai Zhiquan with an edict ordering him to join the traveling court, but Guangfeng pleaded illness and resigned his post.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong visited Shimen, Guangfeng did not follow; Zhaozong sent the inner attendant Dai Zhiquan with an edict summoning him to the traveling court, but he pleaded illness and resigned his office.

entries.zh: 駕在華州，拜御史中丞。
entries.en: While the court was at Hua Prefecture, he was appointed censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Hua Prefecture, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 時有道士許岩士、瞽者馬道殷出入禁庭，驟至列卿宮相，因此以左道求進者眾，光逢持憲紀治之，皆伏法，自是其徒頗息。
entries.en: At that time the Daoist Xu Yanshi and the blind diviner Ma Daoyin moved freely in and out of the inner palace and were suddenly elevated to the highest ministerial ranks. Many others therefore sought advancement through occult practices. Guangfeng enforced the law against them, and all were executed; after that such followers largely disappeared.
entries.literal: At the time the Daoist Xu Yanshi and the blind diviner Ma Daoyin came and went within the forbidden precincts and swiftly rose to ranks of chief ministers and palace attendants; because of this many sought advancement through heterodox ways. Guangfeng upheld the law and punished them; all were executed according to law, and from then on such followers largely ceased.

entries.zh: 改禮部侍郎、知貢舉。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice minister of rites with responsibility for the civil examinations.
entries.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Rites with charge of the civil examinations.

entries.zh: 光化中，王道浸衰，南北司為黨，光逢素惟慎靜，慮禍及己，因掛冠伊洛，屏絕交遊，凡五六年。
entries.en: During the Guanghua era the imperial order waned and the northern and southern offices formed rival factions. Guangfeng had always been cautious by nature and, fearing that disaster would overtake him, resigned and withdrew to the Yi-Luo region, cutting off all social ties for five or six years.
entries.literal: In the Guanghua era the royal way gradually declined and the northern and southern offices formed factions; Guangfeng had always been cautious and quiet, feared calamity reaching himself, and therefore hung up his official cap in the Yi and Luo region, cutting off social contact, for five or six years in all.

entries.zh: 門人柳璨登庸，除吏部侍郎、太常卿。
entries.en: When his protégé Liu Can came to power, Guangfeng was appointed vice minister of personnel and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: His student Liu Can rose to power, and Guangfeng was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 〈（《唐摭言》云：光化二年，趙光逢放柳璨及第，後三年不遷，時璨自內庭大拜，光逢始以左丞征入。）〉
entries.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》: In the second year of Guanghua, Zhao Guangfeng had passed Liu Can in the examinations, yet for three years received no promotion. Only when Liu Can was elevated from within the inner court was Guangfeng at last recalled as left vice director.)〉
entries.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》 states: In the second year of Guanghua, Zhao Guangfeng passed Liu Can in the examinations; for three years afterward he received no promotion. When Can was greatly promoted from within the inner court, Guangfeng was only then summoned back as Left Vice Director.)〉

entries.zh: 入梁為中書侍郎、平章事，累轉左僕射兼租庸使，上章求退，以太子太保致仕。
entries.en: Under the Liang he became vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor, was later promoted to left vice director while also serving as commissioner of land tax and corvée labor, submitted a memorial asking to retire, and was granted retirement with the title grand guardian of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Entering Liang he became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was repeatedly transferred to Left Vice Director and concurrently Commissioner of Land Tax and Corvée Labor, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and was granted retirement as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 梁末帝愛其才，征拜司空、平章事。
entries.en: The last emperor of Liang admired his talent and recalled him as minister of works and grand councilor.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang admired his talent and summoned him to be Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 無幾以疾辭，授司徒致仕。
entries.en: Before long he resigned on account of illness and was granted retirement with the title minister of education.
entries.literal: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness and was granted retirement as Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 〈（《唐摭言》云：光逢膺大用，居重地十餘歲，七表乞骸，守司空致仕。
entries.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》: Guangfeng held high office for more than ten years, submitted seven memorials requesting retirement, and finally retired while retaining the title minister of works.
entries.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Tang》 states: Guangfeng received great employment, dwelt in weighty posts for more than ten years, submitted seven memorials begging to leave office, and held retirement as Minister of Works.)

entries.zh: 居二年，復征拜上相。）〉
entries.en: Two years later he was summoned back and again appointed chief minister.)〉
entries.literal: After two years in retirement he was again summoned and appointed chief minister.)〉

entries.zh: 丁會，字道隱，壽州壽春人。
entries.en: Ding Hui, whose style name was Daoyin, came from Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.
entries.literal: Ding Hui, style name Daoyin, was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父季。
entries.en: His father was named Ji.
entries.literal: His father was Ji.

entries.zh: 會幼放蕩縱橫，不治農產，恒隨哀挽者學紼謳，尤嗜其聲。
entries.en: In youth Ding Hui was unruly and idle, neglected the family fields, and constantly trailed funeral parties to learn mourning dirges for the pall ropes; he loved their cadence above all else.
entries.literal: As a youth Hui was wild and unrestrained, did not tend the family farms, always followed funeral mourners to learn pall-rope dirges, and was especially fond of their sound.

entries.zh: 既長，遇亂，合雄兒為盜，有誌功名。
entries.en: When he came of age amid the chaos, he gathered bold companions and turned bandit, yet he burned to win a name in arms.
entries.literal: When grown he met turmoil, gathered bold fellows and became a bandit, and harbored ambition for meritorious achievement.

entries.zh: 黃巢渡淮，會從梁祖為部曲，梁祖鎮門，會曆都押衙。
entries.en: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai, Ding Hui entered the Liang Founder's personal command. After the Founder secured the capital, Hui rose to chief of the capital guard office.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai, Hui followed the Liang Founder as a soldier in his personal command; when the Founder held the capital gate, Hui rose through the post of chief capital guard officer.

entries.zh: 自梁祖誅宗權，並時溥，屠朱瑄，走朱瑾，會恒以兵從，多立奇功。
entries.en: From the Founder's execution of Qin Zongquan through his absorption of Shi Pu, the slaughter of Zhu Xuan, and the rout of Zhu Jin, Ding Hui marched at his side and won repeated striking victories.
entries.literal: From when the Founder executed Zongquan, annexed Shi Pu, slaughtered Zhu Xuan, and drove off Zhu Jin, Hui constantly followed with troops and established many brilliant achievements.

entries.zh: 文德中，表授懷州刺史，曆滑州留後、河陽節度使、檢校司徒。
entries.en: During the Wende reign he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai, then served as acting governor of Hua, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting Minister of the Masses.
entries.literal: In the Wende era he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai Prefecture, then served as acting governor of Hua Prefecture, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting minister of the masses.

entries.zh: 自河陽以疾致政於洛陽。
entries.en: He left Heyang on grounds of illness and retired to Luoyang.
entries.literal: From Heyang he retired because of illness and settled in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 梁祖季年猜忌，故將功大者多遭族滅，會陰有避禍之志，稱疾者累年。
entries.en: In his last years the Liang Founder grew suspicious, and veteran commanders of great merit were often wiped out to the last kinsman. Ding Hui quietly resolved to escape that fate and pleaded illness year after year.
entries.literal: In the Founder's declining years he grew suspicious; therefore old commanders of great merit were mostly exterminated by clan purge. Hui secretly harbored the wish to escape calamity and claimed illness for many years.

entries.zh: 天復元年，梁祖奄有河中、晉、絳，乃起會為昭義節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianfu, after the Founder seized Hedong, Jin, and Jiang, he recalled Ding Hui and made him military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianfu the Founder suddenly held Hedong, Jin, and Jiang, then summoned Hui back as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 昭宗幸洛陽，加同平章事。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhaozong came to Luoyang, Ding Hui was made a joint manager of government affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong visited Luoyang, Hui was made Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court.

entries.zh: 其年，昭宗遇弑，哀問至，會三軍縞素，流涕久之。
entries.en: That same year, when word came that Zhaozong had been murdered, Ding Hui's whole army put on white mourning and wept for a long while.
entries.literal: That year, when Zhaozong was assassinated, the tidings of mourning arrived; Hui's entire army donned white mourning and wept for a long time.

entries.zh: 時梁祖親討劉守文於滄州，駐軍於長蘆。
entries.en: The Liang Founder was then campaigning in person against Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and had encamped at Changlu.
entries.literal: At the time the Founder was personally campaigning against Liu Shouwen at Cang Prefecture and camped his army at Changlu.

entries.zh: 三年十二月，王師攻會，居旬日，會以潞州歸於武皇。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the third year the imperial army besieged him; within ten days Ding Hui surrendered Luzhou to the Martial Sovereign.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year the imperial army attacked Hui; within ten days Hui surrendered Luzhou to the Martial Sovereign.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：梁祖雄猜，疑忌功臣，忽謂敬翔曰：「吾夢丁會在前祗候，吾將乘馬欲出，圉人以馬就台，忽為丁會跨之以出，時夢中怒，叱喝數聲，因驚覺，甚惡之。」
entries.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Northern Dreams》: The Liang Founder was fierce, suspicious, and wary of his great commanders. One day he suddenly told Jing Xiang, "I dreamed that Ding Hui was waiting before me as I prepared to mount and ride out. The groom led the horse to the terrace, and in the dream Ding Hui vaulted onto it and rode out with me. I shouted at him in anger several times, then woke—and the omen filled me with loathing.")
entries.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Northern Dreams》 states: The Founder was fierce and suspicious and wary of meritorious commanders. Suddenly he said to Jing Xiang: "I dreamed Ding Hui was attending in front of me. I was about to mount my horse to go out when the groom brought the horse to the terrace. Suddenly Ding Hui straddled it and rode out with me. In the dream I grew angry and shouted several times, then awoke, and greatly detested it."

entries.zh: 是月，丁會舉潞州軍民歸河東矣。）〉
entries.en: That very month Ding Hui brought the army and people of Luzhou over to Hedong.)〉
entries.literal: That month Ding Hui led the Luzhou army and people over to Hedong.)〉

entries.zh: 引見，會泣曰：「臣非不能守潞，但以汴王篡弱唐祚，猜嫌舊將，臣雖蒙保薦之恩，而不忍相從，今所謂吐盜父之食以見王也。」
entries.en: When he was received in audience Ding Hui wept and said, "It is not that I could not hold Luzhou. The Prince of Bian has usurped and enfeebled the Tang house and now suspects every old commander. Though I owed him the grace of preservation, I could not bear to follow him further. What I do now is what they call vomiting out a robber father's food to show oneself before the true king."
entries.literal: When presented in audience Hui wept and said: "Your subject is not incapable of holding Luzhou, but because the Prince of Bian usurped and weakened the Tang succession and is suspicious of old commanders, though I received the grace of preservation I could not bear to follow him—what is now called vomiting what one's robber father fed one to show the king."

entries.zh: 武皇納之，賜甲第於太原，位在諸將上。
entries.en: The Martial Sovereign welcomed him, granted him a great mansion in Taiyuan, and ranked him above the other generals.
entries.literal: The Martial Sovereign accepted him, granted him a mansion in Taiyuan, and ranked him above the other generals.

entries.zh: 五年，汴將李思安圍潞州，以會為都招討使、檢校太尉。
entries.en: In the fifth year the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, and Ding Hui was made chief campaign commander with the acting rank of Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou; Hui was made chief campaign commander and acting grand commandant.

entries.zh: 閻寶，字瓊美，鄆州人。
entries.en: Yan Bao, whose style name was Qiongmei, came from Yun Prefecture.
entries.literal: Yan Bao, style name Qiongmei, was a native of Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父佐，海州刺史。
entries.en: His father Zuo had served as prefect of Hai Prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Zuo was prefect of Hai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 寶少事朱瑾為牙將，瑾之失守於兗也，寶與瑾將胡規、康懷英歸汴梁，皆擢任之。
entries.en: In youth Yan Bao served Zhu Jin as a guard officer. When Jin lost Yanzhou, Bao went with Jin's officers Hu Gui and Kang Huaiying to Bianliang, and the Liang court promoted them all.
entries.literal: In youth Bao served Zhu Jin as a guard officer; when Jin lost Yan Prefecture, Bao with Jin's generals Hu Gui and Kang Huaiying returned to Bianliang, and all were promoted and employed.

entries.zh: 自梁祖陳師河朔，爭霸關西，寶與葛從周、丁會、賀德倫、李思安各為大將，統兵四出，所至立功，曆洺、隨、宿、鄭四州刺史。
entries.en: From the Founder's campaigns in the Hebei north through his struggle for the northwest, Yan Bao stood with Ge Congzhou, Ding Hui, He Delun, and Li Si'an among the great commanders. They led armies on every front, won merit wherever they marched, and Yan Bao in turn held the prefectures of Ming, Sui, Su, and Zheng.
entries.literal: From when the Founder arrayed troops in the Hebei region and contended for supremacy in the Guanxi region, Bao with Ge Congzhou, Ding Hui, He Delun, and Li Si'an each served as great generals, commanded armies in four directions, won merit wherever they went, and served as prefect of Ming, Sui, Su, and Zheng prefectures.

entries.zh: 天祐六年，梁祖以寶為邢洺節度使、檢校太傅。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianyou the Liang Founder made Yan Bao military commissioner of Xing and Ming with the acting rank of Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianyou the Founder made Bao military commissioner of Xing and Ming and acting grand mentor.

entries.zh: 莊宗定魏博，十三年，攻相、衛、洺、磁，下之，寶獨保邢州，城孤援絕。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong secured Weibo, in the thirteenth year he took Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Ci. Yan Bao alone still held Xingzhou, his city isolated and his relief cut off.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong secured Weibo, in the thirteenth year he attacked Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Ci and took them; Bao alone held Xing Prefecture, the city isolated and reinforcements cut off.

entries.zh: 八月，寶以邢州降，莊宗嘉之，進位檢校太尉、同平章事，遙領天平軍節度使、東南面招討等使，待以賓禮，位在諸將上，每有謀畫，與之參決。
entries.en: In the eighth month Yan Bao surrendered Xingzhou. Zhuangzong praised him, raised him to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor, and gave him titular command of Tianping and the southeastern campaign, treating him as an honored guest and ranking him above the other generals. On every major plan Zhuangzong consulted him and followed his counsel.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Bao surrendered Xing Prefecture; Zhuangzong praised him, advanced him to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor, made him titular military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner, treated him with guest ceremony, ranked him above the other generals, and whenever there was planning consulted and decided with him.

entries.zh: 契丹之寇幽州也，周德威危急，寶與李存審從明宗擊契丹於幽州西北，解圍而還。
entries.en: When the Khitan besieged Youzhou and Zhou Dewei was hard pressed, Yan Bao and Li Cunshen followed Mingzong to strike the Khitan northwest of the city, broke the siege, and returned.
entries.literal: When the Khitan raided You Prefecture and Zhou Dewei was in peril, Bao with Li Cunshen followed Mingzong to strike the Khitan northwest of You Prefecture, lifted the siege, and returned.

entries.zh: 胡柳之役，諸軍逗撓，汴軍登無石山，其勢甚盛。
entries.en: At the battle of Huliu the allied armies hung back while the Bian forces took Wushi Mountain and gathered overwhelming strength.
entries.literal: At the battle of Huliu the armies hesitated and hung back; the Bian army climbed Wushi Mountain and their momentum was very strong.

entries.zh: 莊宗望之，畏其不敵，且欲保營。
entries.en: Zhuangzong looked on them, feared he could not prevail, and thought only of holding his camp.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong looked at them, feared he could not match them, and wished moreover to preserve the camp.

entries.zh: 寶進曰：「王深入敵境，偏師不利，王彥章騎軍已入濮州，山下唯列步兵，向晚皆有歸誌。
entries.en: Yan Bao stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty has marched deep into enemy country, and one wing has already faltered. Wang Yanzhang's cavalry has entered Puzhou; below the mountain they have posted only foot soldiers, and by evening every man will be thinking of home.
entries.literal: Bao advanced and said: "Your Majesty has penetrated deep into enemy territory; a detached force has met misfortune. Wang Yanzhang's cavalry has already entered Pu Prefecture; below the mountain they have only arrayed foot soldiers, and toward evening all will have the will to return.

entries.zh: 我盡銳擊之，敗走必矣。
entries.en: If we throw our best troops against them, they are sure to break and run.
entries.literal: If we strike them with all our elite troops, they will surely flee in defeat.

entries.zh: 今若引退，必為所乘，我軍未集，更聞賊勝，即不戰而自潰也。
entries.en: If we pull back now they will surely overtake us. Our forces are not yet fully assembled, and once the men hear the enemy has won they will scatter without a fight.
entries.literal: If we now withdraw we will surely be overtaken by them; our army is not yet gathered, and if we further hear the enemy has won, we will collapse without fighting.

entries.zh: 凡決勝料情，情勢已得，斷在不疑。
entries.en: Victory always turns on reading the moment aright; once the odds are in hand, the decisive thing is not to hesitate.
entries.literal: In all cases of deciding victory and gauging circumstances, once the situation and momentum are obtained, the decision lies in not hesitating.

entries.zh: 今王之成敗，在此一戰，若不決勝，設使餘眾渡河，河朔非王有也，王其勉之！」
entries.en: Your Majesty's fate now hangs on this single battle. If we fail to win it here, and the rest of their army crosses the river, the north will no longer be yours. Press the fight, sire!"
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty's success or failure lies in this one battle; if we do not decide victory, suppose the remaining masses cross the river—the Hebei north will not be Your Majesty's; Your Majesty must exert yourself!"

entries.zh: 莊宗聞之聳聽，曰：「微公幾失計。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong listened with rising attention and said, "Without you I would nearly have thrown the campaign away."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong heard and straightened to listen, saying: "Without you I would nearly have lost the plan."

entries.zh: 即引騎大噪，奮槊登山，大敗汴人。
entries.en: He at once led his cavalry forward with a great shout, drove his spears up the slope, and routed the Bian army.
entries.literal: He immediately led cavalry in great clamor, brandished spears and climbed the mountain, and greatly defeated the Bian men.

entries.zh: 十八年，張文禮殺王鎔叛，寶帥師進討。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong and rebelled; Yan Bao marched to suppress him.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and rebelled; Bao led troops forward to attack.

entries.zh: 八月，收趙州，進渡滹水，擒賊黨張友順以獻。
entries.en: In the eighth month he recovered Zhao Prefecture, crossed the Hutuo, and captured the rebel partisan Zhang Youshun for presentation to the throne.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he recovered Zhao Prefecture, advanced and crossed the Hutuo River, and captured the rebel partisan Zhang Youshun to present.

entries.zh: 九月，進逼真定，結營西南隅。
entries.en: In the ninth month he pressed Zhending and pitched camp at the city's southwest corner.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he advanced pressing Zhending and encamped at the southwest corner.

entries.zh: 掘塹柵以環之，決大悲寺漕渠以浸其郛。
entries.en: He dug trenches and palisades to ring the city and breached the Dabei Temple canal to flood the outer walls.
entries.literal: He dug moats and stockades to encircle it and breached the canal of Dabei Temple to flood the outer wall.

entries.zh: 十九年正月，契丹三十萬來援鎮州，前鋒至新樂，眾心憂之。
entries.en: In the first month of the nineteenth year three hundred thousand Khitan marched to relieve Zhenzhou; when their vanguard reached Xinle the army's spirits sank.
entries.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year three hundred thousand Khitan came to aid Zhen Prefecture; the vanguard reached Xinle and the army's hearts were anxious.

entries.zh: 寶見莊宗，指陳方略，軍情乃安。
entries.en: Yan Bao laid out his plan before Zhuangzong, and the army's morale steadied.
entries.literal: Bao saw Zhuangzong, pointed out and laid out strategy, and the army's mood then settled.

entries.zh: 敵退，加檢校侍中。
entries.en: After the enemy withdrew he was promoted to acting Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When the enemy withdrew he was advanced to acting palace attendant.

entries.zh: 三月，城中饑，王處瑾之眾出城求食，寶縱其出，伏兵截擊之。
entries.en: In the third month famine gripped the city. Wang Chujin's men came out to forage; Yan Bao let them leave the gates, then ambushed and cut them down.
entries.literal: In the third month the city was starving; Wang Chujin's masses went out of the city to seek food; Bao let them out and ambush troops intercepted and struck them.

entries.zh: 饑賊大至，諸軍未集，為賊年乘；
entries.en: The starving rebels came in force before the allied armies had fully gathered, and Yan Bao's men were overrun;
entries.literal: The starving enemy came in great numbers; the armies were not yet gathered and were overrun by the enemy;

entries.zh: 寶乃收軍退保趙州，因慚憤成疾，疽發背而卒，時年六十。
entries.en: Yan Bao drew his troops back to Zhao Prefecture. Shame and anger brought on illness; a carbuncle broke out between his shoulders and he died at the age of sixty.
entries.literal: Bao then gathered the army, withdrew to hold Zhao Prefecture, and because of shame and anger fell ill; a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, aged sixty.

entries.zh: 同光初，追贈太師；
entries.en: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously granted the honor of Grand Preceptor;
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously granted the honor of Grand Preceptor;

entries.zh: 晉天福中，追封太原郡王。
entries.en: and under Jin in the Tianfu era he was posthumously created Prince of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: in the Tianfu era of Jin he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 符習，趙州昭慶縣人。
entries.en: Fu Xi came from Zhaoqing County in Zhao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Fu Xi, a native of Zhaoqing County in Zhao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少從軍，事節度使王鎔，積功至列校。
entries.en: He entered the army young, served the Zhao military commissioner Wang Rong, and by steady merit rose to regimental commander.
entries.literal: In youth he entered the army, served Military Commissioner Wang Rong, and through accumulated merit rose to regimental commander.

entries.zh: 自莊宗經略河朔，與鎔連衡，常令習率師從莊宗征討。
entries.en: Once Zhuangzong began his campaigns in the Hebei north and allied with Wang Rong, he regularly ordered Fu Xi to lead Zhao troops on Zhuangzong's campaigns.
entries.literal: From when Zhuangzong planned the Hebei north and allied with Rong, he constantly ordered Xi to lead troops following Zhuangzong in campaigns.

entries.zh: 鎔為張文禮所害，時習在德勝寨，文禮上書請習等歸鎮。
entries.en: When Wang Rong was murdered by Zhang Wenli, Fu Xi was at Desheng Stockade. Wenli wrote asking Xi and his officers to return to Zhao.
entries.literal: When Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli, at the time Xi was at Desheng Stockade; Wenli sent a letter requesting Xi and others return to the commandery.

entries.zh: 習雨泣訴於莊宗曰：「臣本趙人，家世事王氏，故使嘗授臣一劍，俾臣平蕩凶寇。
entries.en: Fu Xi wept bitterly before Zhuangzong and said, "I am a man of Zhao. For generations my house served the Wang family. The late lord once gave me a sword and charged me to crush the murderers.
entries.literal: Xi wept in the rain and appealed to Zhuangzong, saying: "Your subject is originally a man of Zhao; for generations my family served the Wang house. The late lord once bestowed on your subject one sword, ordering your subject to pacify and sweep away the fierce bandits.

entries.zh: 自聞變故，徒懷冤憤，欲以自剄，無益於營魂。
entries.en: Since I heard what befell him I have lived only with outrage. I might cut my own throat, but that would do my dead lord's spirit no good.
entries.literal: Since hearing of the calamity I have only harbored grievance and rage, wishing to cut my own throat, which would be of no benefit to the late lord's spirit.

entries.zh: 且張文禮乃幽、滄叛將，趙王知人不盡，過意任使，致被反噬。
entries.en: Zhang Wenli was a turncoat from You and Cang. The Prince of Zhao misjudged him, trusted him too far, and was destroyed for it.
entries.literal: Moreover Zhang Wenli is a rebel general of You and Cang; the Prince of Zhao did not fully know men, excessively trusted and employed him, and thus was bitten in return.

entries.zh: 臣雖不武，願在霸府血戰而死，不能委身於凶首。」
entries.en: I am no great warrior, but I would rather die fighting in your service than submit to that murderer."
entries.literal: Though your subject is not martial, I wish to die fighting bloodily in the hegemon's court and cannot entrust my person to the murderous chief."

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「爾既懷舊君之愛，可復仇乎？
entries.en: Zhuangzong said, "If you still love your old master, will you take revenge?
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said: "Since you cherish love for your old lord, can you take revenge?

entries.zh: 吾當助爾。」
entries.en: I will help you do it."
entries.literal: I shall assist you."

entries.zh: 習等舉身投地，號慟感激，謝曰：「王必以故使輔翼之勞，雪其冤恥，臣不敢期師旅為助，但悉本軍可以誅其逆豎。」
entries.en: Fu Xi and his officers prostrated themselves, wept in gratitude, and said, "If Your Majesty will honor our late lord's service and avenge his death, I do not ask for a great host—only let my own Zhao troops strike down the traitor."
entries.literal: Xi and the others threw their bodies to the ground, wailed in grief with gratitude, and thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty will surely, because of the late lord's labor in assisting, wipe away his grievance and shame; your subject does not dare expect army support, only that the entire native army can execute the rebellious villain."

entries.zh: 莊宗即令閻寶、史建瑭助習討文禮，乃以習為成德軍兵馬留後。
entries.en: Zhuangzong at once ordered Yan Bao and Shi Jiantang to aid Fu Xi against Wenli and made Xi acting military governor of the Chengde army.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong immediately ordered Yan Bao and Shi Jiantang to assist Xi in attacking Wenli, and made Xi acting military governor of the Chengde army.

entries.zh: 及文禮誅，將正授節鉞，習不敢當其任，辭曰：「臣緣故使未葬，又無嗣息，臣合服斬縗，候臣禮制畢聽命。」
entries.en: After Wenli was killed, Zhuangzong was ready to grant Fu Xi the full commission, but Xi declined. "My late lord is still unburied and left no heir," he said. "I ought to wear the deepest mourning. When those rites are finished I will await your command."
entries.literal: When Wenli was executed and Xi was about to receive the formal commission of command, Xi did not dare undertake the post and declined, saying: "Because the late lord is not yet buried and there is no heir, your subject ought to wear the hemp of deepest mourning; when your subject's ritual obligations are finished I shall await orders."

entries.zh: 及莊宗兼領鎮州，乃割相、衛二州置義寧軍，以習為節度使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong also took charge of Zhenzhou, he carved out Xiang and Wei to form the Yining command and made Fu Xi its military commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong also took charge of Zhen Prefecture, he carved out Xiang and Wei prefectures to establish the Yining army and made Xi its military commissioner.

entries.zh: 習奏曰：「 魏博六州，見係霸府，不宜遽有割隸。
entries.en: Fu Xi memorialized, "The six prefectures of Weibo already belong to your hegemony and ought not be carved away so soon.
entries.literal: Xi memorialized, saying: "The six prefectures of Weibo are now tied to the hegemon's court and ought not suddenly to have territory carved away.

entries.zh: 但授臣河南一鎮，臣自攻取。」
entries.en: Grant me only one command south of the Yellow River, and I will take it myself."
entries.literal: Only grant your subject one commandery south of the river and your subject will seize it himself."

entries.zh: 乃授天平軍節度、東南面招討使。
entries.en: He was then made military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner.
entries.literal: He was then granted military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner.

entries.zh: 烏震，冀州信都人也。
entries.en: Wu Zhen came from Xindu in Ji Prefecture.
entries.literal: Wu Zhen, a native of Xindu in Ji Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少孤，自勤於鄉校。
entries.en: Orphaned young, he threw himself into study at the district school.
entries.literal: Orphaned in youth, he applied himself diligently at the district school.

entries.zh: 弱冠從軍，初為鎮州隊長，以功漸升部將，與符習從征於河上，頗得士心。
entries.en: At twenty he entered the army as a squad leader in Zhenzhou, rose by merit to section commander, marched with Fu Xi on the Yellow River campaigns, and won strong loyalty from his men.
entries.literal: At weak cap he entered the army, at first was squad leader of Zhen Prefecture, through merit gradually rose to section commander, followed Fu Xi in campaigns along the river, and greatly won the soldiers' hearts.

entries.zh: 聞張文禮弑王鎔，誌復主讎，雪泣請行。
entries.en: When he heard that Zhang Wenli had murdered Wang Rong, he vowed to avenge his lord, wept aloud, and begged to march.
entries.literal: When he heard Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, he resolved to avenge his lord, wept tears of grief, and requested to march.

entries.zh: 兵及恒陽，文禮執其母妻洎兒女十口誘之，不回，攻城日急。
entries.en: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and children—ten persons in all—to lure him back, but he would not turn aside, and the siege pressed harder day by day.
entries.literal: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and together with sons and daughters ten mouths to entice him, but he did not turn back; the siege of the city grew daily more urgent.

entries.zh: 文禮忿之，鹹割鼻斷腕，不絕於膚，放至軍門，觀者皆不忍正視。
entries.en: Wenli in his rage had them mutilated, noses cut and wrists severed, wound upon wound, then sent them to the camp gate. The onlookers could not bear to meet their eyes.
entries.literal: Wenli resented this; he had them all cut off their noses and sever their wrists, the wounds unceasing on their flesh, and released them to the army gate; onlookers could not bear to look straight at them.

entries.zh: 震一慟而止，憤激奮命，身先矢石。
entries.en: Wu Zhen choked back a single sob and drove on, burning with rage he threw himself into the assault and led the charge under arrow and stone.
entries.literal: Zhen gave one great grief and stopped, in furious zeal threw his life into the fight, and took the lead before arrows and stones.

entries.zh: 鎮州平，以功授震深、趙二州刺史。
entries.en: When Zhenzhou fell, Wu Zhen was rewarded with the prefectures of Shen and Zhao.
entries.literal: When Zhen Prefecture was pacified, by merit Zhen was granted the prefectures of Shen and Zhao.

entries.zh: 其性純質，以清直禦下，在河北獨有政聲，移易州刺史，兼北面水陸轉運、招撫等使。
entries.en: Plain and upright by nature, he governed his subordinates with integrity and alone in the Hebei north won a name for good rule. He was moved to Yizhou and made concurrent northern commissioner for water and land transport and pacification.
entries.literal: His nature was pure and plain; with integrity and uprightness he governed subordinates; in the Hebei north alone he had a reputation for good government; he was transferred to Yi Prefecture and concurrently made northern commissioner for water and land transport and pacification.

entries.zh: 契丹犯塞，漁陽路梗，震率師運糧，三入薊門，擢為河北道副招討，遙領宣州節度使，代房知溫軍於盧台。
entries.en: When the Khitan raided the frontier and the road to Yuyang was cut, Wu Zhen led grain convoys through Jimen three times. He was promoted to deputy Hebei campaign commissioner, given titular command of Xuanzhou, and sent to replace Fang Zhiwen at Lutai.
entries.literal: When the Khitan raided the frontier and the Yuyang route was blocked, Zhen led troops transporting grain, three times entered Jimen, was promoted to deputy campaign commissioner of the Hebei circuit, held titular military commissioner of Xuan Prefecture, and replaced Fang Zhiwen's army at Lutai.

entries.zh: 及至軍，會戍兵龍至所部鄴都奉節等軍數千人作亂，未及交印而遇害。
entries.en: When he reached camp, several thousand garrison troops of the Yedu Fengjie army under Long Zhi mutinied. He was killed before he could even take command.
entries.literal: When he reached the army, garrison troops under Long Zhi of the Yedu Fengjie and other armies, several thousand men, mutinied; before he could hand over the seal he met calamity.

entries.zh: 明宗聞之，廢朝一日，詔贈太傅。
entries.en: Mingzong suspended court for a day on hearing the news and by edict posthumously honored him as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When Mingzong heard of it he suspended court for one day and by edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 震略涉書史，尤嗜《左氏傳》，好為詩，善筆劄，凡郵亭佛寺，多有留題之跡。
entries.en: Wu Zhen had some learning in history, loved the Zuo Commentary above all, wrote poetry, and penned fine letters. Post stations and temples all over the north still bore his inscriptions.
entries.literal: Zhen had slight acquaintance with books and histories, especially loved the Zuo Commentary, delighted in composing poetry, was skilled at letters, and at every post station and Buddhist temple there were many traces of inscriptions he left.

entries.zh: 及其遇禍，燕、趙之士皆歎惜之。
entries.en: When he was killed, men of worth in Yan and Zhao mourned him.
entries.literal: When he met calamity, gentlemen of Yan and Zhao all sighed in regret.

entries.zh: 李紹文，鄆州人，本姓張，名從楚。
entries.en: Li Shaowen came from Yan Prefecture. His original surname was Zhang and his given name Congchu.
entries.literal: Li Shaowen, a native of Yan Prefecture, originally surnamed Zhang with the given name Congchu.

entries.zh: 少事朱瑄為帳下，瑄敗，歸於梁祖，為四鎮牙校，累典諸軍。
entries.en: In youth he served Zhu Xuan on his staff. When Xuan fell he entered the Liang Founder's service as an officer of the four commands and rose through repeated army commands.
entries.literal: In youth he served Zhu Xuan in his tent staff; when Xuan was defeated he returned to the Founder, became a guard officer of the four commands, and repeatedly held command of armies.

entries.zh: 天祐八年，從王景仁戰，敗於柏鄉，紹文與別將曹儒收殘眾，退保相州。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Tianyou he fought under Wang Jingren and was defeated at Bai Township. Li Shaowen and the officer Cao Ru gathered the survivors and fell back to Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Tianyou he followed Wang Jingren in battle, was defeated at Bai Township; Shaowen with the separate general Cao Ru gathered the remnant masses and withdrew to hold Xiang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 王師之攻魏州也，紹文率眾自黎陽將渡河。
entries.en: When the Tang army besieged Weizhou, Li Shaowen led his troops from Liyang to cross the river.
entries.literal: When the imperial army attacked Wei Prefecture, Shaowen led his masses from Liyang and was about to cross the river.

entries.zh: 時汴人大恐，河無舟楫，紹文懼為王師所逼，乃剽黎陽、臨河、內黃至魏州，歸於莊宗。
entries.en: The Bian army was in panic and the river had no boats. Fearing the Tang advance, Li Shaowen plundered his way from Liyang through Linhe and Neihuang to Weizhou and surrendered to Zhuangzong.
entries.literal: At the time Bian men were greatly afraid; the river had no boats; Shaowen feared being pressed by the imperial army, therefore raided Liyang, Linhe, and Neihuang to Wei Prefecture and returned to Zhuangzong.

entries.zh: 莊宗嘉納之，賜姓名，分其兩將三千人為左右匡霸軍旅，仍令紹文、曹儒分將之。
entries.en: Zhuangzong welcomed him, granted him the imperial surname and personal name, and formed his three thousand men and two officers into the Left and Right Support-the-Hegemon brigades under Shaowen and Cao Ru.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong praised and accepted him, granted the imperial surname and name, divided his two generals' three thousand men into left and right Support-the-Hegemon army brigades, and still ordered Shaowen and Cao Ru to divide command of them.

entries.zh: 從周德威討劉守光，進檢校司空，移將匡衛軍。
entries.en: He followed Zhou Dewei against Liu Shouguang, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and was given command of the Support-the-Guard army.
entries.literal: He followed Zhou Dewei in attacking Liu Shouguang, was advanced to acting minister of works, and was transferred to command the Support-the-Guard army.

entries.zh: 十二年，授博州刺史，預破劉鄩於故元城，曆貝、隰、代三郡刺史，領天雄軍馬步副都將，屯於德勝。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he was made prefect of Bo, helped defeat Liu Kun at the old Yuan City, served as prefect of Bei, Xi, and Dai, became deputy overall commander of the Tianxiong army, and encamped at Desheng.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was granted Bo Prefecture, took part in defeating Liu Kun at the old Yuan City, served as prefect of the three commanderies of Bei, Xi, and Dai, held the post of deputy overall commander of the Tianxiong army horse and foot, and encamped at Desheng.

entries.zh: 從閻寶討張文禮，為馬步軍都虞候。
entries.en: He followed Yan Bao against Zhang Wenli and was made overall adjutant of the horse and foot forces.
entries.literal: He followed Yan Bao in attacking Zhang Wenli and was made overall adjutant of the horse and foot army.

entries.zh: 明宗收鄆州，以紹文為右都押衙、馬步軍都將，從破王彥章於中都。
entries.en: When Mingzong took Yanzhou, Li Shaowen was made right chief capital guard officer and overall commander of the horse and foot forces, and helped break Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took Yan Prefecture, Shaowen was made right chief capital guard officer and overall commander of the horse and foot army, and followed in defeating Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu.

entries.zh: 同光中，曆徐、滑二鎮副使，知府事。
entries.en: During Tongguang he served as deputy commissioner of Xu and Hua and managed their civil affairs.
entries.literal: In the Tongguang era he served as deputy commissioner of the two commands of Xu and Hua and managed prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 三年，從郭崇韜討西川，為洋州節度留後，領鎮江軍節度。
entries.en: In the third year he followed Guo Chongtao into western Shu, was made acting military commissioner of Yang, and held titular command of the Zhenjiang army.
entries.literal: In the third year he followed Guo Chongtao in attacking western Shu, was made acting military commissioner of Yang Prefecture, and held titular military commissioner of the Zhenjiang army.

entries.zh: 天成初，為武信軍節度使，尋卒於鎮。
entries.en: Early in Tiancheng he was made military commissioner of Wuxin and soon died in office.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was military commissioner of the Wuxin army; soon he died at his command.

entries.zh: 李襲吉，自言左相林甫之後，父圖，為洛陽令，因家焉。
entries.en: Li Xiji claimed descent from the Left Chancellor Li Linfu. His father Tu served as magistrate of Luoyang, and the family made their home there.
entries.literal: Li Xiji claimed for himself that he was a descendant of Left Chancellor Li Linfu; his father Tu was magistrate of Luoyang, and the family settled there.

entries.zh: 襲吉乾符末應進士舉，遇亂，避地河中，依節度使李都，擢為鹽鐵判官。
entries.en: Near the end of the Qianfu reign Xiji entered the jinshi examinations, but with rebellion abroad he fled to Hezhong and entered the service of Military Commissioner Li Du, who raised him to salt-and-iron judge.
entries.literal: At the end of the Qianfu era Xiji sat for the jinshi examination; he encountered turmoil, fled to Hezhong, relied on Military Commissioner Li Du, and was promoted to salt-and-iron judge.

entries.zh: 及王重榮代，不喜文士，時喪亂之後，衣冠多逃難汾、晉間。
entries.en: When Wang Chongrong took his place, the new commissioner had little use for scholars; in the wake of the civil wars, men of the official class fled in droves to the Fen and Jin region.
entries.literal: When Wang Chongrong replaced him, he did not favor literary men; after the disorders of the age, gentry in official dress mostly fled for refuge between Fen and Jin.

entries.zh: 襲吉訪舊至太原，武皇署為府掾，出宰榆社。
entries.en: Xiji followed old ties to Taiyuan, where the Martial Emperor Li Keyong named him a headquarters aide and later sent him out to govern Yushe county.
entries.literal: Xiji, visiting old acquaintances, came to Taiyuan; the Martial Emperor appointed him a staff officer of the commandery and sent him out as magistrate of Yushe.

entries.zh: 光啟初，武皇遇難上源，記室歿焉，既歸鎮，辟掌奏者，多不如旨。
entries.en: Early in the Guangqi reign the Martial Emperor suffered the Shangyuan debacle, and his chief recorder died in the affair. Back in his headquarters he tried one memorialist after another, but few could satisfy him.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi era the Martial Emperor met disaster at Shangyuan and his recorder died there; after he returned to his command, those he recruited to manage memorials mostly failed to please him.

entries.zh: 或有薦襲吉能文，召試稱旨，即署為掌書記。
entries.en: Someone praised Xiji's literary gifts; summoned for a trial draft, he pleased the prince at once and was named chief secretary on the spot.
entries.literal: Someone recommended that Xiji was skilled at writing; he was summoned for a trial and pleased the ruler, and was immediately appointed chief secretary.

entries.zh: 襲吉博學多通，尤諳悉國朝近事，為文精意練實，動據典故，無所放縱，羽檄軍書，辭理宏健。
entries.en: Xiji was erudite and widely read, with a specialist's grasp of recent court history. His prose was tight and concrete, every line anchored in precedent, never florid; whether drafting battle orders or field reports, his style was vigorous and commanding.
entries.literal: Xiji was broadly learned and widely versed, especially well acquainted with recent affairs of the dynasty; in writing he refined his meaning and condensed substance, constantly citing precedents without license, and in urgent dispatches and military documents his rhetoric was grand and forceful.

entries.zh: 自武皇上源之難，與梁祖不協，乾寧末，劉仁恭負恩，其間論列是非，交相聘答者數百篇，警策之句，播在人口，文士稱之。
entries.en: From the Shangyuan crisis through the rupture with the Liang Founder and, late in Qianning, Liu Rengong's betrayal, Xiji drafted hundreds of letters debating blame and merit between the rival camps. His sharpest lines passed from mouth to mouth, and men of letters spoke of him with admiration.
entries.literal: From the Martial Emperor's Shangyuan disaster, through his breach with the Liang Founder and, at the end of Qianning, Liu Rengong's ingratitude, in the exchanges that argued right and wrong back and forth there were several hundred pieces; striking lines spread on people's lips, and literary men praised them.

entries.zh: 三年，遷節度副使，從討王行瑜，拜右諫議大夫。
entries.en: In the third year of his service he became deputy military commissioner, marched against Wang Xingyu, and received appointment as Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to deputy military commissioner, followed the campaign against Wang Xingyu, and was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

entries.zh: 及師還渭北，武皇不獲入覲，為武皇作違離表，中有警句云：「穴禽有翼，聽舜樂以猶來；
entries.en: When the army withdrew north of the Wei, the Martial Emperor was denied an imperial audience. Xiji wrote his master's petition of separation, with lines that ran: "Even a bird that nests in caves will spread its wings; hearing the music of Shun, it would still return;
entries.literal: When the army returned to the north of the Wei, the Martial Emperor could not gain an audience; Xiji drafted for him a memorial on being kept apart, containing striking lines that read: "The cave-dwelling bird has wings; hearing Shun's music it would still return;
